suggestion.rationale: Article lists 30 C2 domains; T1071 technique confirms 'Application Layer Protocol'. Exfiltration of stolen cookies/credentials to attacker infrastructure is the collection-to-exfil bridge.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on DNS queries or HTTP/HTTPS connections from unsigned processes to any of the 30 article IOC domains (cleanmymacos.org, rapidfilevault4.sbs, domenpozh.net, etc.). Exclude system processes and /System/Applications/ binaries. Flag even single DNS query to these domains as high-confidence.

suggestion.title: Malicious File Hash Detection (SHA256 IOCs)
suggestion.rationale: Article provides 4 SHA256 hashes of malware files. Direct indicator matching should fire on creation, download, or execution of these binaries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Match SHA256 hashes against all file creation, modification, and process execution events. Alert immediately if any of the 4 hashes appear on disk or in memory. Cross-reference with parent process (expect Safari, Mail, or third-party browser) and file location (expect ~/Downloads/ or /tmp).

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Keychain Access from Non-Apple Processes
suggestion.rationale: macOS stores browser credentials and session tokens in Keychain. Infostealer must query Keychain APIs to access stored secrets. Article emphasizes credential theft; Keychain is the primary store on macOS.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unsigned processes or processes from ~/Downloads/ calling SecKeychainSearchCopyNext, SecKeychainItemCopyAttributesAndData, or Keychain framework APIs. Alert on Keychain access from processes not in /Applications or /System directories. Correlate with DMG execution timeline.

suggestion.title: Browser Process Impersonation or DLL/dylib Sideloading
suggestion.rationale: Infostealer often mimics legitimate browser processes or hijacks browser startup. Article mentions 'credential access from browsers' and malware obfuscation (T1027). Dylib hijacking is common macOS evasion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes with browser names (Chrome, Firefox, Safari) spawned from non-standard locations or unsigned. Monitor for dylib loading from ~/Downloads/ or /tmp. Alert on DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES environment variable use or rpath manipulation in Mach-O binaries.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Exploitation Attempts Against Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'a large amount of Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520 exploitation attempts based on the public PoC' and Shadowserver observed active exploitation. Pipeline generated zero detection for this documented, widespread attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST requests to Ivanti Sentry admin endpoints (typically port 8443, /admin or /login paths) containing OS command injection metacharacters (backticks, $(), semicolons, pipes) in request parameters or body. Correlate with failed authentication and successful breach indicators. Alert on payloads matching known PoC patterns or shell command syntax within HTTP request.

suggestion.title: Root Privilege Code Execution from Ivanti Sentry Service
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability core impact: 'execute code with root privileges on Internet-exposed secure mobile gateways.' Root-level process spawning from Sentry parent process is the direct privilege-escalation artifact. Pipeline missed this critical detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes spawned with SYSTEM/root privileges where parent is Ivanti Sentry service account (sentry.exe, sentry daemon, or associated UID). Focus on shell interpreters (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, /bin/sh) and suspicious utilities. Establish baseline of legitimate Sentry-spawned processes and flag post-patch-date (2026-06-11) deviations, especially encoding/obfuscation in command lines.

suggestion.title: Backdoor Artifacts on Compromised Sentry Appliances
suggestion.rationale: Shadowserver confirmed 'attackers had already backdoored most of the Sentry gateways exposed online' with 'at least 2 backdoored' verified. Backdoor persistence (new services, scheduled tasks, reverse shells) is the confirmed post-exploitation phase. Pipeline generated zero persistence detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry appliances for new services, scheduled cron jobs, systemd timers, or unexpected processes post-patch. Alert on unexpected local user accounts, SSH authorized_keys modifications in /root/.ssh/, or web shells in Sentry application directories. Flag outbound network connections from Sentry to external IP ranges on non-standard ports (not standard HTTP/S). Cross-reference against baseline configurations.

suggestion.title: Authentication Anomalies on Internet-Exposed Sentry Admin Portals
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'Ivanti Sentry admin portals exposed online.' Attackers gained sufficient access to install backdoors, indicating credential compromise or brute-force success. Pipeline missed pre-exploitation credential-access patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect high-volume failed authentication attempts to Sentry admin interface followed by successful login from same source within 1 hour. Flag geographic anomalies (login from unusual country/ASN post-exploitation). Monitor for password spray (multiple usernames, constant password) or credential stuffing (single account, many passwords). Alert on admin logins from non-corporate, non-VPN IP ranges.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Backdoored Sentry Gateway to Enterprise Network
suggestion.rationale: Sentry 'secures traffic between back-end corporate systems and remote mobile devices.' Compromised gateway at network edge enables lateral movement into corporate infrastructure. Pipeline missed this critical post-breach scenario despite Shadowserver confirmation of backdoors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound flows FROM Sentry appliance TO internal corporate systems (database servers, domain controllers, file shares) for unusual protocols (SMB, RDP, SSH from Sentry service account). Alert on LDAP query floods, suspicious DNS lookups, or large data-transfer volumes during non-business hours. Establish baseline of legitimate Sentry-to-backend traffic and flag protocol/port deviations.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Execution from AppData/LocalAppData on Developer Machine
suggestion.rationale: Article title specifies 'Detect Them on Developer Machines with Suspicious Files'—implies file-based execution is the attack vector; no UC proposed despite explicit mention.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor execution of binaries from user-writable directories (AppData, LocalAppData, %TEMP%) on developer workstations, especially those with suspicious file names, unsigned signatures, or unusual parent processes. Correlate with recent file creation events.

suggestion.title: Registry Run Key Modification for Persistence by Malware
suggestion.rationale: Malware 'spreading' on developer machines implies persistence mechanism; article mentions suspicious files but no persistence detection UC proposed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on writes to HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run or HKLM equivalents where the value data references recently-created files, unsigned executables, or paths outside Program Files.

suggestion.title: Developer Tool Abuse: Suspicious npm or Git Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article targets 'developer machines' but pipeline did not propose detection UC for developer-specific attack surfaces (package managers, VCS).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual npm install/git clone/git pull operations executing from suspicious directories, or spawning child processes with obfuscated/encoded names. Flag invocation of npm scripts that execute binaries from non-standard paths.

suggestion.title: Process Hollowing or Code Injection by Malware
suggestion.rationale: No kill chain phase captured for defense evasion; malware families spreading on developer machines likely use injection to evade static analysis and behavioral detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect parent-child process relationships where legitimate developer tools (Visual Studio, Git, npm) spawn suspended or early-termination child processes, or where unexpected memory/handle inheritance patterns indicate code injection.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from Developer Home Directory
suggestion.rationale: Malware targeting developer machines has high value for credential theft (SSH keys, API tokens, git credentials); article context suggests this but no credential-access UC proposed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes reading .ssh, .git, .aws, .azure, .kube directories in home folders or staging credential files for exfiltration. Monitor for file copies to staging directories or compression of credential-bearing directories.

suggestion.title: C2 Communication from Developer Machine
suggestion.rationale: Article implies active malware threat ('spreading now'); no network-based detection UC proposed for command-and-control beaconing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound HTTP/HTTPS/DNS from developer machines to newly-registered or low-reputation domains, especially with beaconing patterns (regular intervals, small payloads, abnormal user-agent). Correlate with process execution from suspicious file locations.

suggestion.title: AI Agent Tool-Use Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Trick OpenClaw AI Agent Into Running Code'—direct code execution via agent tool calls. Pipeline zero execution-phase UCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child processes spawned from AI agent runtime with unusual arguments, reverse shells, or credential-dumping utilities. Alert on tool-use API calls invoking code/script interpreters with suspicious payloads.

suggestion.title: Secret Exfiltration from Agent Environment
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Leaking Secrets'—no exfiltration UCs generated. Foundational detection gap for API key, credential, or config file theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound data from agent processes to non-whitelisted external IPs/domains; monitor for env-var or config-file reads followed by encoded HTTP POST; alert on bulk data egress from AI runtime contexts.

suggestion.title: Prompt Injection / Agent Jailbreak
suggestion.rationale: Title 'Trick OpenClaw'—implies social engineering / prompt manipulation. No initial-access technique mapped.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag prompts containing tool-use override directives, system-prompt disclosure requests, or jailbreak keywords. Correlate with subsequent tool calls that deviate from baseline intent.

suggestion.title: Recovery Partition XML File Modification
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states exploit targets 'Recovery Partition XML Files' — any write to recovery partition XML should alert, as this is non-standard and indicates BitLocker bypass attempt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file write operations to system recovery partition targeting .xml files, particularly those in \Recovery or \EFI\Microsoft directories. Flag processes running with System or elevated privileges modifying BitLocker-related XML configuration files.

suggestion.title: BitLocker Key Extraction or Bypass Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'GreatXML Exploit Bypasses Windows BitLocker' — the end-state is extracting encryption keys or disabling BitLocker protection, requires credential_access or impact monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for manage-bde.exe invocations with suspension or key extraction flags, access to %ProgramFiles%\BitLocker or recovery key storage, and elevation requests targeting encryption subsystem processes.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation to System for BitLocker Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Bypassing BitLocker requires System-level access; title implies exploit escalates privileges to modify protected recovery partition.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect UAC bypass attempts or direct System privilege acquisition followed by recovery partition or BitLocker subsystem access within 1-5 minutes. Flag unusual boot-loader modification sequences.

suggestion.title: XML Obfuscation or Malformed BitLocker Configuration Files
suggestion.rationale: Article title emphasizes 'XML Files' as the attack vector — GreatXML likely exploits XML parsing or uses crafted XML to trigger the vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation or modification of XML files in recovery/EFI partitions with unusual binary content, encoding mismatches, or XML parsing errors. Alert on processes invoking XML parsers with recovery partition paths as arguments.

suggestion.title: Boot Configuration Data (BCD) or Firmware Modification
suggestion.rationale: Recovery partition tampering to bypass BitLocker often involves BCD store modifications; title implies low-level firmware/bootloader manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bcdedit.exe execution with recovery-related flags (e.g., /recoverysequence), access to firmware update tools, or System Registry modifications to HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\dmboot. Flag unsigned firmware update attempts.

suggestion.title: Forensic Artifact: XML File Access Sequencing Before Encryption Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Kill chain likely involves reconnaissance (reading recovery XML) → modification → exploitation; temporal clustering of reads then writes is suspicious.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect pattern: single process first reads recovery partition XML files (normal operations don't do this), then writes to same directory within seconds, followed by BitLocker status check commands — triplet is strong indicator of GreatXML exploitation.

suggestion.title: Bulk Student PII Export from PeopleSoft Student Module
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'significant amount of data in our student record system has been accessed' and 'breach affects 454,600 former and current students' with detailed PII. Pipeline missed exfiltration detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on export or unload of >1000 student records from PSSTU* tables in single session. Monitor for archive creation (RAR/ZIP) of student data directories. Flag unusual STDINFILE/STDOUTFILE parameters in SQR or batch processes accessing student finance, enrollment, or contact tables outside maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Oracle PeopleSoft Gadget Chain Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'using a gadget chain of zero-days and old vulnerabilities in the attacks' against PeopleSoft. Pipeline omitted initial access detection despite explicit vulnerability exploitation description.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PeopleSoft app logs for serialization exceptions, ClassNotFoundException, or InvokerTransformer chain signatures. Detect malformed PSAPPSRV requests with oversized parameters or unusual Content-Type (application/x-java-serialized-object). Alert on failed Java reflection or unsafe deserialization during web service calls to known vulnerable PeopleSoft endpoints.

suggestion.title: Multi-Organization PeopleSoft Campaign Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'widespread data theft campaign...stolen data from over 100 organizations worldwide after breaching their cloud and on-premises Oracle PeopleSoft instances'. Pipeline missed correlation across institutional targets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate ShinyHunters threat intel indicators (dark web leak posts, infrastructure IPs) with PeopleSoft instance discovery scans. Alert when reconnaissance or exploitation attempts against PeopleSoft originate from same source IP cluster used in prior ShinyHunters campaigns (Instructure Canvas, Oxford CareerConnect noted in article).

suggestion.title: Large Data Archive Creation Prior to Dark Web Posting
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'ShinyHunters...shared an archive of allegedly stolen documents' containing 'over 40GB of documents'. Pipeline missed pre-exfil collection pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation of multi-gigabyte RAR/ZIP archives containing PII (names, addresses, passport numbers, phone numbers per article) outside normal backup/archive windows. Flag archive tools (WinRAR, 7-Zip) invoked by non-standard service accounts with read access to student data repositories. Monitor for staging directories with 40GB+ cumulative size.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Database Connection from Non-Campus Networks to Student Records
suggestion.rationale: Article describes breach accessed 'student records system'; no indication legitimate remote campus/overseas access during incident window. Pipeline omitted collection-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on database connections to student records tables (PSSTU_ACAD_PLAN, PSPERS, etc.) originating from IP ranges outside university-approved geographies or vendor networks. Establish baseline for legitimate PeopleSoft batch job sources (e.g., IT Shared Services, specific cloud datacenters); flag deviations. Correlate with elevated record count thresholds in same session.

suggestion.title: Dark Web Leak Site Data Posting Attribution Clustering
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'ShinyHunters...posted on their dark web leak site'. Pipeline did not surface monitoring for ShinyHunters infrastructure or posting patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor dark web leak sites associated with ShinyHunters (e.g., onion domain used for Nottingham, Oxford, Instructure posts) for new educational institution data dumps. Cross-reference WHOIS, SSL cert registrants, and hosting provider with prior ShinyHunters infrastructure. Alert on first sighting of new university name in ShinyHunters catalog; correlate with recent PeopleSoft exploitation chatter or CVE disclosures.

suggestion.title: Suspicious postinstall script execution during npm install
suggestion.rationale: Article title references 'block-postinstall' as a security improvement; postinstall hooks are the attack vector for supply chain compromise via npm packages. Article establishes postinstall scripts as executable code during package installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation or script execution with parent process npm.exe or node.exe, or child processes spawned during npm install. Flag postinstall scripts with network connectivity, registry modification, or system persistence attempts. Correlate npm install commands with unexpected child processes outside node_modules.

suggestion.title: npm package installation from untrusted or suspicious sources
suggestion.rationale: Article addresses supply chain risk through npm packages; the security improvement in v12 presupposes attackers use npm as distribution. Requires detection of package provenance and registry anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry queries and package downloads. Alert on installs from alternative registries, typosquatted package names, packages with unusual version jumps, or installs of deprecated/abandoned packages. Correlate install activity with process execution immediately following.

suggestion.title: npm install executed with elevated privileges or in unexpected context
suggestion.rationale: Article implies postinstall code execution as a privilege vector; running npm install in SYSTEM or ADMIN context escalates postinstall payload impact. This is a prerequisite condition for many supply chain attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag npm.exe or npm commands (install, update, ci) executed by SYSTEM, NT AUTHORITY, or privileged service accounts. Monitor for npm in containers with --user=root or equivalent. Baseline legitimate npm execution contexts and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: postinstall script writing to system-sensitive directories
suggestion.rationale: Article highlights postinstall as executable during install; attacker postinstall hooks persist by writing startup scripts, cron jobs, or registry entries. Detection targets file writes from postinstall context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file creation/modification in %APPDATA%, %PROGRAMFILES%, /etc, /usr/local/bin, or cron directories when parent is npm or node.exe. Alert on .sh, .bat, .ps1, .exe, or .dll writes from node_modules postinstall context to startup folders or system paths.

suggestion.title: Package.json with malicious postinstall script field
suggestion.rationale: Article directly addresses postinstall script abuse; package.json 'scripts' field with postinstall entry is the configuration vector. Detectable via package manifest analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse package.json files on install or in repositories. Flag postinstall scripts containing obfuscation (base64, hex), network calls (curl, wget, powershell -enc), privilege escalation (sudo, runas), or persistence commands (cron, registry, launchd). Correlate with package provenance (PyPI, npm registry metadata).

suggestion.title: npm audit or dependency scanning anomalies post-v12 adoption
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes npm v12 as a security boundary; organizations adopting postinstall blocking may trigger audit policy violations. Detectable via CI/CD logs or npm audit output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm audit invocations or CI/CD pipeline output for scripts bypassing postinstall restrictions (--legacy-peer-deps, --force, --no-audit). Flag git repositories or CI configs disabling postinstall in package-lock.json. Correlate with builds that reduce security posture to allow malicious package installation.

suggestion.title: Investment software installer executing LOLBins or suspicious children
suggestion.rationale: Article describes FireAnt MetaKit compromise delivering 'a powerful backdoor' via supply chain, but pipeline generated zero UCs. The trojanized installer must spawn child processes (cmd/powershell/regsvr32) to execute the payload. This is the primary exploitation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag child processes launched from FireAnt installation binaries with names matching cmd.exe, powershell.exe, regsvr32.exe, rundll32.exe, wscript.exe, cscript.exe, mshta.exe. Baseline legitimate installer behavior and alert on deviations or suspicious arguments (network calls, registry hives, scheduled tasks).

suggestion.title: Network connections from endpoints to OceanLotus IOC infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article provides 8 IPv4 and 6 domain IOCs. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs and zero C2 detection UCs. The backdoor must beacon to C2 (article cites T1071 Application Layer Protocol). Standard network IOC hunt entirely absent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on DNS queries or HTTP/HTTPS connections from endpoints to article IOCs: financemachinelearning[.]com, gatewayrvcenter[.]com, coachcybersecurity[.]com, mxprodesign[.]com, power-sync-services[.]com, leadingfilipinoteams[.]com and IP set {139.162.11.152, 142.91.98.77, 139.180.128.42, 139.99.33.239, 166.88.77.186, 103.119.47.104, 38.60.245.37, 194.68.26.241}. Aggregate by device and user for lateral movement signals.

suggestion.title: File hash matching on trojanized FireAnt binaries
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 20 SHA1 hashes of malicious binaries. Pipeline extracted zero hashes. Hash-based detection is highest-fidelity for supply-chain artifacts and should generate immediate high-confidence alerts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution or file creation matching any of the 20 provided SHA1 hashes. Cross-reference with software inventory and update logs to identify endpoints that received the trojanized FireAnt update. Flag for isolation and EDR deep-dive.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated code indicators in FireAnt binaries and child processes
suggestion.rationale: Article cites T1027 (Obfuscated Files or Information) but no detection UC targets obfuscation artifacts. Trojanized FireAnt binaries must employ packing/encryption to evade static detection — entropy analysis and yara-based detection should flag this.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan FireAnt binaries for high-entropy sections, suspicious import tables, or known packer signatures (UPX, custom obfuscators). Alert on processes with memory-only code execution or unusual section alignment. Compare against known-good FireAnt installation binaries from official sources.

suggestion.title: Persistence mechanisms installed by trojanized FireAnt
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain backdoor delivery requires durable C2 access. Article narrative implies post-compromise persistence, but pipeline missed detection coverage for scheduled tasks, startup folders, Registry Run keys, or service installation initiated from FireAnt context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Registry modifications (HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\Run, HKU\*\Run), scheduled task creation, or service installation where the process initiator is FireAnt installer, FireAnt.exe, or child processes thereof. Alert on persistence that survives reboot.

suggestion.title: OceanLotus C2 Beaconing – SPECTRALVIPER
suggestion.rationale: Article title names SPECTRALVIPER as the malware deployed in this campaign. Expected behavior: post-compromise C2 communication to attacker-controlled domains. Title phrase: 'SPECTRALVIPER in FireAnt Attack' establishes malware component.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound network connections to known or suspected OceanLotus C2 infrastructure. Flag DNS queries to SPECTRALVIPER-associated domains and anomalous outbound SSL/TLS connections from user endpoints to non-whitelisted C2 IPs, especially from Vietnam-based or finance-sector systems.

suggestion.title: SPECTRALVIPER Execution & File Artifacts
suggestion.rationale: Malware name and campaign reference imply executable binary delivery and execution. No file hash IOCs or process behaviors extracted. Title phrase: 'SPECTRALVIPER in FireAnt Attack' indicates a specific payload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of SPECTRALVIPER binary by file hash or name. Monitor for unusual process creation from user-writable directories, suspicious parent-child process chains (e.g., Office macro → cmd.exe → rundll32), and file writes to temp/AppData matching known SPECTRALVIPER signatures.

suggestion.title: OceanLotus Persistence Mechanism – FireAnt Campaign
suggestion.rationale: OceanLotus historically uses registry run keys, scheduled tasks, and WMI for persistence. Article name 'FireAnt Attack' suggests coordinated, multi-stage campaign implying persistence layer. No persistence detections generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation of Run/RunOnce registry keys associated with SPECTRALVIPER; scheduled task creation (schtasks.exe) with suspicious arguments; and WMI event subscriptions targeting OceanLotus-attributed malware. Alert on any modification to Windows startup folders.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email Delivery – Vietnam Investor Targeting
suggestion.rationale: Target group ('Vietnam Investors') and attack name ('FireAnt') suggest spear-phishing or watering-hole delivery. Article establishes financial sector as victim segment. No initial-access detections generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails with financial/investment-themed subject lines and Vietnamese language recipients; emails with macro-enabled Office attachments; or shortened URLs linking to attacker-controlled domains. Correlate with SPECTRALVIPER file hash execution post-click.

suggestion.title: OceanLotus Credential Theft – Investor Account Access
suggestion.rationale: Targeting of 'Vietnam Investors' implies financial credential harvesting (brokerage accounts, bank portals, trading platforms). Standard OceanLotus objective. No credential-access detections in output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for keystroke logging or screen capture API calls post-SPECTRALVIPER execution; browser credential store access; or LSASS memory dump attempts. Flag repeated failed logins followed by successful access to investment/banking portals from non-standard geolocations.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration – Financial Records & Account Credentials
suggestion.rationale: OceanLotus targets financial data for espionage and fraud. Investor-targeting implies bulk exfil of trading records, account statements, credentials. No exfiltration detection layer generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect large data transfers to C2 endpoints or cloud storage services post-SPECTRALVIPER execution. Monitor for archiving of financial documents (.xls, .pdf) or database file staging. Flag encrypted HTTPS POST requests to attacker C2 with unusual payload sizes or frequencies.

suggestion.title: Detect Mass File Encryption Activity via Ransomware
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes ransomware impact on 478 victims; 'Gentlemen Ransomware' encrypts files as primary destructive action. Title states 'Can Spread Like a Worm,' implying coordinated encryption across network.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect high-volume file write operations to .exe, .dll, .txt, .doc files in short timespan from single process. Ransomware typically encrypts in-place with new file extension or overwrites headers. Baseline normal file churn by process to isolate anomalies.

suggestion.title: Detect Lateral Movement via SMB/RDP Prior to Encryption Spike
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'Can Spread Like a Worm'—indicates self-propagating network traversal not typical of single-machine ransomware. Worm behavior requires RDP/SMB exploitation or credential replay.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate failed RDP authentication attempts or port 445/139 connections from a single source to multiple internal IPs, followed within 5–30 minutes by encryption file-write storms on those same targets. Worm propagation precedes payload execution.

suggestion.title: Detect Ransomware C2 Beaconing for Coordination
suggestion.rationale: Article references 478 claimed victims across likely multiple organizations; coordinated encryption at scale suggests C2 command-and-control communication to sync timing or receive encryption keys.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify persistent connections to non-whitelisted external IPs on unusual ports (8080, 443 to rare ASNs) originating from the compromised host cluster prior to encryption onset. Look for DNS queries to suspicious domains containing 'gentlemen', 'ransom', or randomized subdomains.

suggestion.title: Detect Deletion or Disabling of Shadow Copies / Backups
suggestion.rationale: Ransomware commonly destroys recovery mechanisms to prevent victim restoration. A worm variant spreading across 478 targets implies systematic anti-recovery steps.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag commands: `vssadmin delete shadows`, `wmic shadowcopy delete`, `bcdedit /set`, `diskpart` targeted at shadow copies. Timeframe: within 10 minutes before mass encryption detected. Correlate with account context and network source.

suggestion.title: Detect Credential Harvesting / Credential Access for Worm Propagation
suggestion.rationale: Worm-like spread requires either stolen credentials or unpatched exploits. Article states 'Can Spread Like a Worm' without specifying mechanism; credential reuse is common for ransomware lateral spread.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process access to LSASS memory from unusual processes, or execution of credential-dumping tools (mimikatz, ProcDump) followed by lateral RDP/SMB logons using harvested credentials to internal hosts.

suggestion.title: Detect Suspicious Process Execution for Worm Installation / Lateral Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Article title emphasizes worm propagation. Self-propagating malware typically uses spawned processes or script execution to copy/execute payload on remote hosts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify suspicious child processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe) spawned from ransomware entry point, especially with UNC paths in arguments (e.g., `\\[IP]\admin$\payload.exe`) or encoded payloads. Correlate with lateral SMB connections.

suggestion.title: phpBB Authentication Bypass Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'authentication bypass + RCE'; this is the initial-access vector. No auth-bypass detection generated despite explicit mention in the headline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to phpBB login endpoints (/ucp.php, /login.php) with abnormal POST payloads, injected SQL keywords, or parameter tampering. Baseline authentication failure rates and alert on spike clusters or requests from untrusted IPs within short windows.

suggestion.title: phpBB Remote Code Execution via Malformed HTTP Request
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly mentions RCE capability; pipeline missed execution-phase detection. This is the exploitation vector that materializes the vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST/GET requests to phpBB endpoints with payloads containing shell metacharacters (|, &, $(), backticks), base64-encoded commands, or PHP function calls (eval, system, exec, passthru). Correlate with unexpected child process creation under web-server PID (apache2, php-fpm, nginx) within seconds of the malicious request.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation File Write to phpBB Installation Directory
suggestion.rationale: RCE enables attacker persistence via webshells or backdoors; pipeline generated no persistence detection. Article's scope ('tens of millions') implies active exploitation risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected .php, .phtml, or script files created/modified in phpBB cache/, files/, store/, or root directories post-authentication. Flag rapid multi-file writes by web-server process outside scheduled deployments, or file writes with encoded/obfuscated content patterns.

suggestion.title: Abnormal Privilege Escalation in phpBB User Role
suggestion.rationale: Post-compromise, attackers escalate within phpBB to admin/moderator to maintain persistence. No privilege-escalation detection despite RCE implying admin-level capability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor phpBB database/application logs for unexpected user-role upgrades, group membership changes, or SQL UPDATE statements targeting user_type or user_permissions columns. Flag new admin/moderator account creation or elevation from non-administrative source IPs.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Outbound Network Activity from phpBB Web Server
suggestion.rationale: RCE enables C2 communication; pipeline did not surface command-and-control detections. Article's 10-year exposure window suggests widespread active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound connections (TCP/UDP) from web-server processes to non-whitelisted external IPs or domains, especially after suspicious HTTP requests. Monitor DNS queries from web-server PID; flag requests for pastebin, raw-GitHub, or known C2 domains. Correlate timing with RCE exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: JDY Botnet C2 Beaconing Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes botnet expansion to 1,500+ devices; implies active C2 communication infrastructure. No use case generated despite obvious need to detect outbound connections to known C2 servers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag devices establishing repeated outbound connections to known JDY C2 domains/IPs, particularly over non-standard ports or with domain generation algorithm (DGA) patterns. Correlate with known C2 IOC lists and detect encrypted HTTPS beacons with suspicious certificate patterns.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance Tool Execution on Compromised Hosts
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Cyber Reconnaissance' as botnet purpose; typical recon includes network/process/account discovery. Pipeline missed entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious sequential execution of discovery commands (whoami, ipconfig, systeminfo, arp, netstat) within short time windows on systems, especially combined with unusual outbound DNS queries or port scanning activity.

suggestion.title: Mass Botnet Installation via Exploitation Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article states 1,500+ devices compromised; no detection for initial compromise vector or installation pattern. Silent gap in initial-access and execution phases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate failed authentication attempts, exploitation attempts (HTTP 5xx errors post-suspicious request), and subsequent child process spawning indicative of payload execution (e.g., PowerShell, cmd.exe, curl).

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement and Persistence via JDY Botnet
suggestion.rationale: Expansion to 1,500+ devices implies lateral movement; no use case generated for detecting propagation or persistence mechanisms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for lateral movement via SMB (T1021.002), RDP (T1021.001), or WinRM (T1021.006) to new hosts, followed by service or scheduled task creation (T1053) indicative of botnet persistence.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration to Botnet C2
suggestion.rationale: Reconnaissance botnet typically exfiltrates collected data; no use case for detecting staged exfiltration or data egress patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag large outbound data transfers to known JDY C2 servers, unusual DNS query volumes from single host (DNS tunneling), or archive file creation followed by exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Code Deployment to Development Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article title 'code is being written everywhere' implies continuous code flow to developer machines; pipeline should detect unusual deployment/sync patterns to developer endpoints as an initial access or persistence vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected code deployment commands (git clone, npm install, docker pull, artifact repository pulls) originating from or targeting developer machine IP ranges outside normal CI/CD windows. Correlate with process creation from IDEs, terminals, or unusual parent processes. Flag code fetches from non-whitelisted artifact repositories or with suspicious authentication patterns.

suggestion.title: Device as Persistent Attack Surface (Developer Endpoints)
suggestion.rationale: Article's core claim—'device is the only constant'—suggests developer machines are attack focus. Pipeline missed detection gap for persistence and lateral movement from compromised dev endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious persistence mechanisms installed on developer machines: startup folder modifications, scheduled tasks created by non-SYSTEM users, shell profile modifications (.bashrc, .zshrc, PowerShell $profile), LaunchAgent/Daemon plist writes. Correlate with known development tools to reduce FP (legitimate IDEs installing extensions).

suggestion.title: Rust Crate Installation with Uncommon Network Connections
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'performs code exfiltration'—pipeline missed the execution + exfiltration chain triggered by cargo/crate build/install. Need to detect when Rust build tools spawn network-accessing child processes not typical of legitimate dependencies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for cargo/rustc spawning curl, wget, powershell, or native HTTP clients with unusual destinations during package installation. Correlate with crate manifest inspection (supply-chain poisoning).

suggestion.title: Source Code Exfiltration via Package Build Process
suggestion.rationale: Title and premise: 'onering performs code exfiltration'. Pipeline detected no collection/exfiltration-phase signals. Malicious crate likely reads source files and transmits them.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on build processes (cargo build, rustc) reading .rs/.toml source files outside their declared package directory, followed by network egress to non-package-manager IPs or suspicious domains.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Package Metadata or Author Changes
suggestion.rationale: Article title indicates crate compromise; pipeline should detect IOC for affected crate versions, authors, or repository indicators. Missing initial-access detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference crate.io/dependency-tracking logs for sudden version bumps without changelog, new yanked versions, or author account metadata shifts (e.g., transfer to new maintainer, account reactivation after dormancy).

suggestion.title: Cargo.lock File Tampering or Version Injection
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attack vehicle: modified Cargo.lock or dependency injection. Article does not specify attack mechanism but exfiltration via build-time code implies dependency manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for modifications to Cargo.lock files in version control or local build directories, especially version downgrades or insertions of new dependencies not present in Cargo.toml.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration Size Anomalies During Rust Compilation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies code exfiltration but pipeline generated zero exfil-specific detections. Unusual outbound traffic volume or duration during build would be signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag sustained or bursty network transfers from cargo/rustc/build processes with high byte counts, especially to non-standard ports or HTTPS exfil tunnels. Baseline legitimate build traffic and alert on >2σ deviations.

suggestion.title: JWT Signed with Hardcoded Secret 'random'
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Hardcoded JWT Secret "random" Allows Token Forgery' and lists CWE-798. Missing detection for JWTs signed with known-weak secret or HS256 with predictable key. Attack requires attacker to forge tokens using the exposed 'random' string.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Decode JWT header (alg) and attempt HMAC-SHA256 verification using hardcoded string 'random' as secret against sample auth event JWTs. Flag tokens that validate using weak secret. Cross-reference successful validations with upstream log entries showing no legitimate secret rotation.

suggestion.title: go-base Boilerplate Endpoint Probing
suggestion.rationale: Article names `github.com/dhax/go-base` as affected repository (1,685 stars). Missing reconnaissance phase hunt for automated probing of go-base default endpoints to identify vulnerable deployments before token forgery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequential HTTP requests to go-base canonical paths (/api/v1/users, /api/v1/admin/users, /api/v1/me, /api/v1/token/refresh, /cmd/serve route patterns) from single source within 30 seconds, followed by bearer token auth attempts. Baseline against known go-base asset inventory.

suggestion.title: JWT Expiration Claim Integrity Violation
suggestion.rationale: UC_45_1 title references 'extreme far-future JWT' but delivers no temporal validation. Article emphasizes token forgery—attacker can set arbitrary exp claim. Missing hunt for JWTs with expiration timestamps inconsistent with server clock (exp year 2099+) or negative lifetime.

suggestion.title: dev.env Configuration File Exposure or Enumeration

suggestion.title: Rapid JWT Token Issuance / Token Refresh Endpoint Abuse

Cross-reference with JWT payloads extracted from request bodies—flag if user_id / sub claim values change across refresh attempts, indicating bulk token generation across different identities.

suggestion.title: Baileys protocolMessage payload with malicious structure (Splunk)

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti product instances (ITSM, VPN, or other critical appliances) with version signatures matching pre-patch builds. Cross-reference against CVE release notes to flag systems at immediate exploitation risk.

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for FortiGate, FortiOS, or other Fortinet products running versions prior to disclosed patch level. Flag based on banner grabbing, SNMP queries, or management interface version strings.

suggestion.rationale: Title includes 'SAP Release Patches for Multiple Critical Vulnerabilities' but zero use case generated to detect vulnerable SAP installations
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify SAP systems (ECC, HANA, BusinessObjects, or portal) running unpatched kernel or application module versions. Correlate system version telemetry against official CVE patch matrices.

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Once CVE payload details are published, monitor for HTTP request patterns (SQL injection, path traversal, RCE payloads), suspicious child processes spawned from vulnerable application contexts, or anomalous file/registry writes consistent with post-exploitation activity.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Langflow Exploitation Attempts

suggestion.title: Langflow Service Spawning Command Shells

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Metadata Tampering in Automated Systems

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Ivanti Sentry Management Interface

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scanner Coverage Verification

suggestion.title: Check Point Gateway VPN Authentication Bypass (Exploitation Detection)

suggestion.rationale: Article describes ransomware campaign flow starting with VPN breach, but the gap between gateway compromise and credential dumping/lateral movement is silent; no detection for post-compromise enumeration (T1087, T1087.004, T1018) that would precede LSASS targeting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Within 5 minutes of a confirmed VPN breach indicator, hunt for process execution invoking 'ipconfig', 'net group', 'whoami', 'systeminfo', 'tasklist', or LDAP queries from the compromised host that would indicate reconnaissance before lateral movement.

suggestion.title: HTTP POST /mcp endpoint access without prior authentication handshake
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Unauthenticated HTTP MCP Tool Execution'—the core issue is that the /mcp endpoint accepts POST requests without authentication. Detections should flag POST requests to /mcp that do not follow authentication patterns (e.g., no Authorization header, no session validation).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP 200/201 responses to POST requests to /mcp endpoints on port 8080 where the client IP has not performed prior authentication (no auth cookie, no Bearer token in preceding requests, or Origin IP differs from established session). Correlate with absence of auth-required framework middleware.

suggestion.title: meta-ads-mcp process exfiltrating credentials to Meta Graph API
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes the vulnerability outcome: 'Leaks Operator Meta Access Token.' Detections must capture unauthorized credential exfiltration from the vulnerable process to external API endpoints (graph.facebook.com, graph.instagram.com).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate meta-ads-mcp or meta_ads_mcp process execution with outbound HTTPS connections to graph.facebook.com or graph.instagram.com. Flag if the process sends credentials in query strings, headers, or POST bodies to these Meta API endpoints without prior OAuth flow initiation detected in process telemetry.

suggestion.title: FastAPI/Starlette application startup without authentication middleware
suggestion.rationale: CVE is CWE-287 'Improper Authentication.' The root cause is a Python web framework (FastAPI/Starlette/uvicorn hosting meta-ads-mcp) that is instantiated without authentication decorators or middleware. Article mentions 'HTTP MCP Tool Execution'—this is ASGI application startup.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for python/python3 processes launching uvicorn, gunicorn, or Starlette applications on port 8080 without evidence of authentication module imports (e.g., missing FastAPI middleware initialization like 'AuthenticationMiddleware', 'JWTBearer', or decorator '@app.get(..., dependencies=[Depends(...auth...)])' in source).

suggestion.title: Vulnerable meta-ads-mcp version (≤1.0.101) with commit hash correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies affected commit hashes: 496c988–7d14226 and versions ≤1.0.101. Versions 1.0.102–1.0.105 lack git tags. Asset inventory and behavioral correlation should flag these specific builds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search software inventory and process load events for meta-ads-mcp binary with version ≤1.0.101. Cross-reference binary SHA256 with known vulnerable commit hashes if available in threat intel feeds. Flag unpatched installations and raise alert for 1.0.102–1.0.105 (patch status unconfirmed per article).

suggestion.title: File validation bypass: mixed image MIME-type with executable extension in single upload
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'uploaded file named shell.php containing GIF-like content could pass validation'—the bypass is the mismatch itself. Detection must flag requests combining image/* Content-Type with .php/.phar/.phtml/.phps filenames or query parameters in POST upload bodies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify POST requests to upload endpoints where HTTP Content-Type header declares image/* but the multipart form body contains a file field with an executable extension (.php, .phar, .phtml). This is the exact bypass condition: validator checks MIME (image) but attacker's filename is executable.

suggestion.title: CodeIgniter form validation rule bypass attempts in application logs
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically mentions 'ext_in rule' validation check. CodeIgniter logs form validation failures. Detecting repeated validation bypass attempts against the ext_in rule on file uploads would catch reconnaissance or testing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search application logs for CodeIgniter form validation messages referencing 'ext_in' rule failures or bypass attempts on file upload endpoints. Multiple failures from same source or burst of failures suggests attack reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: Executable file write by web process with mismatched recorded vs. actual file extension
suggestion.rationale: The vulnerability creates a file with a spoofed MIME type. Detection should identify when a web process writes a .php file but the initial POST indicated a different (image) MIME type, based on correlation of filesystem and network events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate DeviceNetworkEvents (POST with image/* Content-Type to upload endpoint) with subsequent DeviceFileEvents (FileCreated of .php/.phar by same web process within 10 seconds). The mismatch between declared MIME type and actual file extension written is highly suspicious.

suggestion.title: Web server child process inheriting upload directory context and executing
suggestion.rationale: Article describes shell execution post-upload: 'spawns OS shell or recon binary'. Detection should flag web process that reads from upload directory immediately before spawning shell, indicating file-read-then-execute chaining.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect web process (php-fpm, w3wp, nginx) that reads a .php file from an upload directory (FileOpened event) followed within 5 seconds by a child process spawn of cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, or whoami. Sequence is: file read from uploads → shell execution.

suggestion.title: CodeIgniter upload endpoint return status 200 with executable file in response body
suggestion.rationale: If attacker requests the uploaded .php file and the server accidentally echoes it (instead of executing), 200 response with PHP source code is detectable as a validation or configuration failure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP 200 responses from upload directory paths (/*uploads/*.php) where the response body starts with '<?php' or contains PHP keywords, indicating the file is being served as-is instead of executed. This reveals misconfiguration or failed execution attempt.

suggestion.title: Repeated CodeIgniter4 ext_in bypass probing with different file extensions
suggestion.rationale: Article demonstrates the vulnerability is specific to the ext_in rule and requires PHP/PHAR. An attacker testing the vulnerability would repeatedly POST to upload with different executable extensions (.php, .phar, .phtml, .phps, .inc) and image MIME types to find which ones bypass validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Within a 5-minute window, detect ≥3 distinct POST requests to the same upload endpoint from the same source, each with image/* Content-Type but different executable file extensions (.php, .phar, .phtml, .phps, .inc). Indicates systematic bypass testing.

suggestion.title: npm Post-Install Hook Spawns Suspicious Process
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly warns of 'automatic execution of installation scripts' as 'commonly abused mechanisms.' npm install triggers preinstall/postinstall/build hooks in package.json; should detect npm spawning cmd/powershell/sh with network tools or unusual arguments. Phrase: 'turning off automatic execution of installation scripts by default.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for npm or yarn parent process spawning interpreters (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, sh) with parameters suggesting command execution or network activity (curl, wget, nc). Exclude legitimate build tools; alert on unknown registry access or credential theft patterns. Cross-platform (Windows, Linux, macOS).

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Manifest Script Definitions
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks hide malicious code in package.json 'scripts' section. Article states npm v12 will 'disable scripts by default,' implying detection systems should flag suspicious script hooks. Phrase: 'breaking changes...to reduce software supply chain attack risks.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect package.json downloads and cached packages for suspicious preinstall/postinstall/prepare/build hooks. Flag scripts containing Base64 encoding, obfuscation, or known malware signatures. Monitor npm registry API calls for package downloads with recent publication dates and unusual script payloads.

suggestion.title: Network Activity Initiated During npm Install Phases
suggestion.rationale: npm supply chain attacks often exfiltrate secrets or establish persistence. Article frames this as 'software supply chain attack risks'—data theft is the impact. Phrase: 'reduce software supply chain attack risks significantly.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate npm/yarn process creation with unexpected egress to non-CDN IPs, especially to rare geographies or known C2 ranges. Flag connections to cloud storage (S3, GCS) or paste-bin services during post-install hooks. Baseline legitimate npm registries per org.

suggestion.title: Transitive Dependency Chain Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: npm supply chain attacks often hide in deeply nested dependency trees. The article's urgency suggests widespread exploitation of npm dependency chains. Detection should flag suspicious sub-dependencies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan npm lock files (package-lock.json) for dependencies with recent updates from unknown maintainers, version downgrades, or registry switches. Compare installed dependency trees against whitelisted versions; flag injection of new transitive deps in security-sensitive packages.

suggestion.title: Detect Suspicious npm Package Installation with Lifecycle Script Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states GitHub is 'disabling npm install scripts by default to stop supply chain attacks', establishing scripts as an exploitation vector requiring detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child processes spawned from npm/node package managers with arguments matching postinstall, preinstall, prepare, or other lifecycle hooks. Baseline legitimate installation patterns and alert on deviations, particularly scripts that spawn shells, reach out to external IPs, or access credential stores.

suggestion.title: Detect Obfuscated or Encoded Code in npm Lifecycle Scripts
suggestion.rationale: npm supply-chain malware evades detection by encoding payloads in package.json script fields; obfuscation patterns are a known indicator of malicious scripts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse package.json, package-lock.json, and npm shrinkwrap for base64, hex, or unicode-escaped code in lifecycle script fields. Correlate process creation events to identify where decoded payloads execute.

suggestion.title: Detect Unexpected npm Package Source or Registry Configuration Changes
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks often pivot on registry substitution or credential compromise; article context implies malicious packages are distributed through npm ecosystem.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected npm configuration changes (.npmrc modifications), non-canonical registry connections, package installations from private/mirror registries, or rapid install of new/obscure packages that deviate from baseline.

suggestion.title: Detect Process Anomalies During and After npm Install Windows
suggestion.rationale: npm scripts execute with installer privileges; monitoring behavioral anomalies during install windows detects script-based post-compromise activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baselines for normal npm install behavior (duration, child processes, file I/O). Alert on unplanned child processes, credential file reads, DNS/network exfiltration, or file modifications during or immediately following install commands.

suggestion.title: Detect Dependency Confusion or Typosquatting Package Installations
suggestion.rationale: Attackers distribute malicious packages with lifecycle scripts as payloads; detection of package-name deviations catches malicious package introduction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference installed packages (from npm logs, lock files) against known typosquats, misspellings of popular dependencies, and packages from unauthorized registries. Flag installations that deviate from organization's package registry whitelist.

suggestion.title: Go-compiled process spawning suspicious child executable
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states loader is 'written in the Go programming language' with job to 'decode and drop dangerous information-stealing programs.' No execution/spawn detection in pipeline output despite clear parent-child process chain described.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Go-compiled binaries (identified by import tables or file heuristics) spawning child processes outside system directories, especially with suspicious file writes preceding execution. Look for go.exe or Go-built executables creating .exe/.dll files in temp/appdata and immediately executing them.

suggestion.title: PE file with abnormally large overlay section written and executed
suggestion.rationale: Article's central evasion mechanism is 'massive PE overlay'—this is the key obfuscation differentiator. Pipeline failed to create defense-evasion detection despite T1027 being listed. Phrase: 'what makes it stand out is... how effective a simple trick has made it' referring to PE overlay.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PE files with overlay sections comprising >60% of file size being written to disk and subsequently executed. Overlay-heavy binaries are rare in legitimate software but common in packers and loaders. Correlate file write events with immediate child process spawning.

suggestion.title: Known infostealer payload families (Lumma/Vidar/StealC) spawned by loader process
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies specific payloads delivered by GoFlateLoader but pipeline generated zero payload-aware detections. Use command-line artifacts, file names, registry markers, or C2 patterns known to be specific to these three families.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-loader execution detection: look for known Lumma/Vidar/StealC behavioral indicators (specific DLL imports, C2 domains, mutex names, registry keys) within seconds of GoFlateLoader IOC hash execution or suspicious Go process activity.

suggestion.title: Decoder/deobfuscator process activity in suspicious context
suggestion.rationale: GoFlateLoader's primary function is to 'decode' the overlay. T1140 (Deobfuscate/Decode Files or Information) is a clear technique but was not listed in pipeline output. Article: 'loader has one job: to decode and drop dangerous information-stealing programs.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes performing bulk memory operations, file reads followed immediately by writes to temp locations, or API calls typical of decoders (VirtualAlloc, WriteFile patterns) in sequence with no legitimate application context.

suggestion.title: Browser password database access from non-browser process
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes credential theft via brand impersonation: victims are lured to fake login pages. Credential access is the core kill-chain step. No detection covers access to browser password stores (Chrome 'Login Data' SQLite, Firefox key3.db, Edge passwords). This is the likely mechanism for post-phishing credential exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for non-browser processes or suspicious parent processes opening/reading browser credential databases (Chrome/Edge User Data\\Default\\Login Data, Firefox profile\\logins.json, Safari Keychain). Detect via file-open syscalls or process-handle enumeration. High confidence if source is cmd, powershell, or script-runtime and correlates to recent click on a brand-impersonation domain.

suggestion.title: Browser homepage and search-engine hijacking via registry or settings modification
suggestion.rationale: Article's title explicitly mentions 'browser hijacking.' This is typically implemented via modification of HKCU\\Software\\Microsoft\\Internet Explorer\\Main (StartPage) or Chrome/Edge Preferences/Secure Preferences JSON. None of the provided detections cover browser settings tampering, which is the defining characteristic of the attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process-driven writes to browser configuration: HKCU\\Software\\Microsoft\\Internet Explorer\\Main\\Start Page, HKCU\\Software\\Google\\Chrome\\*\\Homepage, or modifications to Chrome/Edge Preferences JSON in User Data directory. Alert on changes from cmd, powershell, wscript, or unsigned binaries. Correlate to credential-access activity or malware execution.

suggestion.title: Suspicious browser extension sideload or manifest modification
suggestion.rationale: Browser hijacking often uses malicious extensions for persistence and redirection. Article describes 'browser hijacking' but no detection covers extension installation or modification. Extensions stored in profile directories can be sideloaded via script or registry, and manifest files contain redirection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file-writes to browser extension directories not originating from official update processes (Chrome: User Data\\Extensions, Firefox: profile\\extensions\\). Detect CRX file downloads from suspicious domains, or JSON files written to extension manifests with new redirection rules. Alert on extension installs triggered by cmd/powershell/script execution.

suggestion.title: Fuzzy-domain matching for brand impersonation IOCs
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'brand impersonation.' Domain IOCs like 'raviral.com' and 'sniperdz.com' are likely intentionally similar to legitimate brand domains. Detection should flag domains with high Levenshtein distance to known-good brands, homograph lookalikes, or suspicious TLD variations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compute string similarity (Levenshtein distance) between clicked domain and whitelist of major brand domains. Flag domains within edit-distance threshold (<3), domains with typosquatting patterns (doubled letters, vowel removal), or non-standard TLDs for known brands. Correlate to phishing-campaign indicators (WHOIS registration timing, SSL certificate issuer mismatch).

suggestion.title: Browser child-process execution following suspicious URL click (social-media delivery)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes delivery via Facebook and Instagram, not email. If victim clicks link in native social-media app on the same device, follow-on script execution (cmd, powershell) should be correlated to browser navigation events, not email events. This kill-chain correlation is currently missing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate spawning of cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or rundll32.exe as child-process of chrome.exe, firefox.exe, msedge.exe, brave.exe to URL navigation events in those browsers. Filter for URL domains matching provided IOC list or identified as brand-impersonation domains. High confidence if execution occurs within 60s of browser navigation and process attempts credential or system modification.

suggestion.title: DMG Mounting and Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'fake software installers disguised as legitimate apps' delivered via DMG — describes initial execution phase. Mounting and executing code from DMG is the attack's entry point and should trigger on suspicious DMG mounts followed by process spawning from /Volumes/.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DMG mount operations followed by process execution from /Volumes/ mount paths, especially where the parent process is 'hdiutil' or 'launchd' spawning unexpected binaries. Look for suspicious child processes with obfuscated names or running from user-writable DMG mount points minutes after mount creation.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated DMG/Installer File Hash Match
suggestion.rationale: Article provides four SHA256 hashes of infostealer samples. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs. Hash-based detection is high-confidence and necessary for known-malware hunting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference process creation and file write events against IOC hashes 9d2da07aa6e7db3fbc36b36f0cfd74f78d5815f5ba55d0f0405cdd668bd13767, 7ca42f1f23dbdc9427c9f135815bb74708a7494ea78df1fbc0fc348ba2a161ae, 241a50befcf5c1aa6dab79664e2ba9cb373cc351cb9de9c3699fd2ecb2afab05, 522fdfaff44797b9180f36c654f77baf5cdeaab861bbf372ccfc1a5bd920d62e. High fidelity if hit.

suggestion.title: C2 Communication to Infostealer Domains/IPs
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists 38 IOCs (8 IPs + 30 domains). Pipeline output dict was empty. Network-based detection against these IOCs is standard practice and was completely missed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries and network connections to known C2 infrastructure: domains including cleanmymacos.org, rapidfilevault4.sbs, rapidfilevault5.sbs, coco-fun2.com, nitlebuf.com, and IPs 95.85.251.177, 45.94.47.204, 138.124.93.32, 168.100.9.122, 199.217.98.33, 38.244.158.103, 38.244.158.56, 92.246.136.14 and others. Correlate with execution of infostealer samples or browser credential access.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Application Bundle Code Signing / Gatekeeper Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'fake software installers' and malware executing on macOS. Unsigned or weakly-signed Mach-O binaries, quarantine flag stripping, or xattr removal are common evasion tactics before execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect removal of com.apple.quarantine extended attributes, unsigned/self-signed binary execution from /Volumes/ or /tmp/, or codesign/xattr CLI tools being invoked by non-system processes. Alert on ad-hoc signed app bundles or binaries with missing or 'untrusted' code signatures.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration via HTTP/HTTPS to Attacker Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically names 'infostealer malware' exfiltrating credentials. HTTPS C2 communication with stolen credentials requires detection at both protocol level (TLS to unexpected domains) and content inspection (base64-encoded credential dumps).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag TLS/HTTPS connections from browser/infostealer processes to the 30 identified domains with unusual request sizes (large POST bodies), high frequency connection patterns, or known credential-exfil user-agent strings. Correlate with credential-database access windows observed 30–60 seconds prior.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'We are observing a large amount of Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520 exploitation attempts based on the public PoC today' and Shadowserver confirmed 19 instances scanned with at least 2 backdoored. Need immediate detection for exploitation traffic patterns against Sentry endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry gateways for HTTP requests with OS command injection payloads targeting known vulnerable endpoints. Correlate failed authentication attempts with subsequent command execution patterns. Baseline: malformed requests with shell metacharacters (|, ;, &&, $()) in query parameters or POST bodies.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Code Execution in Ivanti Sentry Process
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'execute code with root privileges on Internet-exposed secure mobile gateways' — this is the defining post-exploitation indicator. Sentry processes should never spawn child shells with root context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child process spawning (bash, sh, cmd) under Ivanti Sentry gateway processes running with uid=0/root context. Monitor for unexpected execution of system utilities (nc, wget, curl, cat, chmod) as children of Sentry. Alert on any process creation with parent=sentry daemon and elevated privilege level.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Backdoor Installation in Sentry Gateway
suggestion.rationale: Shadowserver explicitly reported 'at least 2 backdoored' instances and warned 'all remaining likely compromised too' — backdoor placement is the primary post-exploitation objective. Detection must focus on persistence mechanisms added after RCE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry system logs for creation of new user accounts with admin privileges, placement of SSH keys in .ssh directories, cron job modifications, or installation of reverse shells. Look for unusual web shell uploads to Sentry webroot (PHP/JSP files in unexpected paths). Correlate timeline: RCE attempt → file modification → unexpected service restart.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised Ivanti Sentry to Backend Network
suggestion.rationale: Article states Sentry 'secures traffic between back-end corporate systems and remote mobile devices' — a compromised gateway is a beachhead for enterprise network access. Post-exploitation lateral movement is the actual business risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any network flows from Ivanti Sentry gateway (as source) to internal backend systems not present in baseline corporate policy. Monitor for tunneling protocols (SSH, RDP, VPN clients) initiated from Sentry. Alert on internal reconnaissance patterns (port scanning, service enumeration) originating from the gateway IP.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Ivanti Sentry Instance Inventory Check
suggestion.rationale: Article names three patched versions (R10.5.2, R10.6.2, R10.7.1) — instances not on these versions or newer are exploitable. Shadowserver found 19 vulnerable instances; inventory is the first defense.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query all Ivanti Sentry instances in the environment for version string (banner grab, SNMP, config scrape). Flag any instance running R10.5.x (pre-10.5.2), R10.6.x (pre-10.6.2), R10.7.x (pre-10.7.1), or any earlier major version. Correlate against asset inventory; untrusted or unknown instances are highest priority.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Pattern Matching in Sentry Gateway Logs
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability is 'OS command injection weakness' — detection must surface the injection attempt itself in any Sentry access or application logs before RCE confirms compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse Ivanti Sentry access logs for payloads containing shell metacharacters in request parameters: backticks, $(…), |, ;, &&, ||, >, <, newlines (%0a/%0d). Apply WAF/IPS signatures for known CVE-2026-10520 payloads (if PoC code is public, extract literal strings). Alert on malformed requests with syntax errors (unmatched quotes, broken escaping).

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Creation in Developer Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly targets 'suspicious files' on 'developer machines' as the detection vector; pipeline generated zero file-system rules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected file creation in source control directories (.git, node_modules parent), IDE config folders, or build artifact paths with obfuscated names, double extensions, or anomalous timestamps correlating with user interaction patterns.

suggestion.title: Known Miasma/Hades Malware Hash Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article names two specific malware families but pipeline extracted zero file hashes, process names, or binary signatures for EDR detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create malware hash observables for Miasma and Hades samples. Alert on process creation or file write matching known indicators. Cross-reference with developer tool execution and network beaconing.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated Script Execution from Developer Tools
suggestion.rationale: Title cites 'suspicious files'—strongly implies obfuscation or encoding; pipeline did not surface T1027 or PowerShell-specific execution rules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PowerShell, Python, or shell execution with high entropy payloads, base64 decoding, or dynamic code invocation originating from user temp folders, Downloads, or IDE plugin directories on developer machines.

suggestion.title: Developer Machine Supply-Chain Attack Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article context implies delivery to dev machines; pipeline missed detection for git config tampering, build artifact modification, or package manager abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on modification of .gitconfig or package.json by unexpected processes, unexpected package installs, or unusual process spawning from IDEs. Correlate with recent phishing indicators and user email access logs.

suggestion.title: Code Execution from AI Agent Process via Prompt Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacks 'Trick OpenClaw AI Agent Into Running Code'—indicates crafted prompts bypass execution restrictions. Zero use case generated despite being the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on command/script execution spawned from known AI agent processes (OpenClaw, LangChain, AutoGPT, etc.) with unexpected child processes. Flag execution of system binaries (python -c, bash -i, powershell.exe, curl, wget) from sandboxed/containerized interpreter contexts with unusual code patterns in command line or file writes.

suggestion.title: Secret/Credential Exfiltration from AI Agent
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'Leaking Secrets' as attack outcome. No detection use case generated for credential access or exfiltration from AI processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor AI agent processes accessing credential storage (.env, .aws/credentials, HKCU registry credential paths, environment variables). Alert on reads of files/vars containing API keys, tokens, secrets followed by network egress to non-whitelisted destinations or unusual S3/cloud storage access.

suggestion.title: Prompt Injection / Jailbreak Command Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates attacks 'trick' the agent—implies malicious input/prompt manipulation. No detection for prompt injection patterns, escape sequences, or role-play override attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag API calls to OpenClaw or similar AI agents containing prompt injection indicators: role-play directives ('act as', 'pretend you are'), instruction overrides ('ignore previous'), system prompt leakage requests ('show your system prompt'), or escape sequences. Correlate with code execution within 60 seconds.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Tool/Library Import by AI Agent
suggestion.rationale: Code execution via prompted AI requires importing/loading dangerous libraries (os, subprocess, requests, etc.). No use case addresses dynamic import detection from AI execution context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal imports/modules loaded by AI framework. Alert on first-time or rare module loads (os, sys, subprocess, socket, requests, boto3, paramiko) within AI agent runtime. Especially flag imports followed immediately by child process creation or file system writes.

suggestion.title: Recovery Partition XML File Modification
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Recovery Partition XML Files' is the explicit attack vector. No use case detects unauthorized XML writes to System Reserved or recovery partitions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation, modification, or deletion of *.xml in reserved/recovery partitions (Device\HarddiskVolume* paths). Exclude signed Windows maintenance processes (SYSTEM context, signed Microsoft binaries). Cross-check with process ancestry to identify non-standard callers.

suggestion.title: BitLocker Recovery Key Enumeration via WMI
suggestion.rationale: Bypassing BitLocker logically requires recovery key access. Pipeline missed WMI and manage-bde.exe based detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for WMI queries to Win32_EncryptableVolume or Win32_BitLockerStatus. Alert on manage-bde.exe with arguments: 'recovery', 'protectors', 'suspend', or 'status'. Exclude scheduled admin tasks and BitLocker servicing.

suggestion.title: Pre-OS Boot Partition Access from User Mode
suggestion.rationale: Recovery partition XML exploitation implies pre-OS or early-boot execution context. No detection for boot/recovery environment tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag non-kernel processes writing to EFI System Partition, boot sectors, or System Reserved volumes. Alert on processes with SYSTEM privilege modifying SYSTEM32\drivers or boot-related registry paths (HKLM\SYSTEM\ControlSet*\Services\*Boot*).

suggestion.title: GreatXML Exploit Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Named exploit in title. No IOC extraction or signature-based detection generated for GreatXML artifacts, parent-child relationships, or network indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create file hash/filename signatures for GreatXML samples. Monitor for unsigned executables or scripts targeting recovery partitions. Flag PowerShell/cmd.exe spawning XML parsers or recovery utilities. Alert on suspicious parent-child chains: explorer.exe → greatxml, msiexec.exe → greatxml.

suggestion.title: Postinstall Script Execution During npm Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: URL slug 'npm-v12-block-postinstall' establishes postinstall scripts as the core threat; article framing around 'one of the biggest security improvements' indicates this is a high-risk attack vector requiring detection coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when Node.js/npm spawns child processes (sh, bash, powershell, cmd) during package installation without prior whitelist entry. Postinstall scripts should execute under strict containment; unexpected shells indicate supply-chain compromise or misconfiguration.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Package Source or Registry Substitution
suggestion.rationale: Title frames npm v12 as a *defense* against supply-chain threats; detection must cover the upstream attack—packages loaded from unauthorized registries or mirrors with embedded postinstall scripts.
