suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry requests for non-canonical domains, typosquatted package names, or installations bypassing corporate proxy. Flag packages with postinstall scripts from untrusted sources.

suggestion.title: Package Dependency Lock File Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain compromise often manifests as transitive dependency injection. Article context implies detection of lock-file anomalies (package-lock.json, npm-shrinkwrap.json) where new postinstall-script dependencies appear without code review approval.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected version bumps or new transitive dependencies in lock files, especially those with postinstall scripts. Correlate with code review bypass patterns.

suggestion.title: Postinstall Script Network Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Malicious postinstall scripts execute in the build/developer context with access to source, credentials, and SSH keys. Article implies this is the risk npm v12 aims to prevent by blocking unauthorized execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate npm install/postinstall execution with outbound HTTP, DNS, or SSH connections. Flag data exfiltration (curl, wget, nc) from postinstall contexts to external C2 or storage services.

suggestion.title: Backdoor Installation via Compromised Vendor Installer
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'hijacking a popular investment software platform to deliver a powerful backdoor'—clear execution of malicious payload through trusted vendor channel. Pipeline missed detection for post-installation artifact creation or registry persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unsigned DLLs or executables written to Program Files or AppData immediately after FireAnt/MetaKit installer execution. Flag registry modifications to Run/RunOnce keys or COM object registrations by child processes spawned from vendor update binaries.

suggestion.title: C2 Exfiltration to Article Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 6 domains (financemachinelearning.com, gatewayrvcenter.com, etc.) as C2 infrastructure. Pipeline listed IOC templates but failed to surface domain-to-stock-account-access correlation or outbound TLS/DNS anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound HTTPS connections from investor workstations to finance-themed domains absent from baseline corporate traffic. Correlate domain resolution timing with stock transaction queries or bulk account enumeration.

suggestion.title: FireAnt MetaKit Binary Staging Folder Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attack vector implies malware bundled in installer. Article mentions FireAnt MetaKit but pipeline missed detection for unusual child processes, config files, or plugins loaded from installation directory post-install.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for non-standard executables (rundll32, regsvr32, powershell) spawned from FireAnt/MetaKit installation paths or loading unsigned DLLs from plugin/lib subdirectories. Cross-reference file creation timestamps with installer completion.

suggestion.title: SPECTRALVIPER Malware Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'OceanLotus Hits Vietnam Investors With SPECTRALVIPER' — malware execution is the core attack delivery mechanism but pipeline extracted zero execution-phase detections
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SPECTRALVIPER process execution chains: suspicious parent-child relationships, encoded command-line arguments, and execution from unusual directories. Correlate file creation timestamps with email delivery to Vietnamese finance sector targets.

suggestion.title: OceanLotus Spear-Phishing to Vietnam Financial Sector
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'Hits Vietnam Investors' — indicates targeted phishing initial-access vector entirely missing from pipeline output
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect spear-phishing emails targeting Vietnamese investment firms with financial/M&A lures, malicious attachments, or credential-harvesting links. Alert on emails from spoofed domains, suspicious sender reputation, and URL clicks by finance-sector users.

suggestion.title: FireAnt C2 Beacon Communication
suggestion.rationale: Title names 'FireAnt Attack' campaign — implies coordinated C2 infrastructure but pipeline produced zero command-and-control reconstruction
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound HTTP/HTTPS traffic for periodic beacons to FireAnt C2 servers; detect via DNS queries to attacker-controlled domains, consistent callback timing, and payload patterns consistent with SPECTRALVIPER command exfiltration.

suggestion.title: SPECTRALVIPER Persistence Registry Modification
suggestion.rationale: High-severity campaign targeting investors implies sustained dwell time; persistence tactics (T1547) should be detected but pipeline missed entire persistence phase
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SPECTRALVIPER persistence via HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run modifications, scheduled task creation with malicious binaries, or startup folder artifacts post-infection of finance-sector hosts.

suggestion.title: Oracle PeopleSoft CVE-2026-35273 Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'ShinyHunters Exploits Oracle PeopleSoft Zero-Day (CVE-2026-35273)'—zero-day exploitation is the attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to PeopleSoft systems for payloads matching known CVE-2026-35273 exploitation signatures. Alert on POST requests to vulnerable endpoints (e.g., /psp/*/EMPLOYEE/) with obfuscated or binary payloads. Correlate with failed authentication followed by successful privilege escalation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Data Exfiltration from University PeopleSoft Instances
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'Breach Universities'—implies post-exploitation data collection and exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag bulk queries to PeopleSoft student/employee databases (PSROLELIST, PSOPRDEFN, PS_PERSONAL_DATA tables) from non-administrative accounts. Monitor for large data transfers to cloud services (AWS S3, Azure Blob, Google Drive) or unfamiliar external IPs from university networks during off-hours.

suggestion.title: ShinyHunters Threat Actor IOC Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Threat actor explicitly named ('ShinyHunters') but not flagged or mapped to known IOCs or attack signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference inbound emails, observed file hashes, C2 domains, and IP infrastructure against ShinyHunters historical IOC repositories. Alert on delivery of known malware families (e.g., BlackCat/ALPHV variants if ShinyHunters leverages them) or phishing campaigns historically attributed to the group.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation Within PeopleSoft Application
suggestion.rationale: Breach implies authenticated post-exploitation access; pipeline missed collection/lateral-movement phase after initial compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PeopleSoft for role elevation (e.g., SYSCID gaining SYS_ADMIN role) without change-control tickets. Detect lateral movement via SQL injection or stored-procedure execution to PS_ACCESSPRFL, PS_PSOPRDEFN_VW, or PSOPRDEFN tables. Flag bulk SELECT operations on sensitive tables (salary, SSN, credentials) by non-HR/Payroll accounts.

suggestion.title: University Sector Ransomware/Extortion Indicator Detection
suggestion.rationale: ShinyHunters is historically a data-extortion/ransomware group; article title 'Breach' coupled with threat actor should trigger impact/extortion detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for ransom notes or extortion communications in email and file shares. Correlate file-system encryption patterns with ShinyHunters' historical naming conventions and leak-site postings. Alert on darkweb monitoring for student PII, financial records, or research data attributed to universities matching the breach timeline.

suggestion.title: Ransomware Execution via Parent Process Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article title identifies a ransomware threat without specifying delivery vector; standard ransomware execution detections should capture suspicious parent-child process chains (e.g., explorer.exe → conhost.exe → ransomware binary, or email client → script → binary). Absence of execution-layer detection is a gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for anomalous parent processes spawning ransomware executables or script interpreters with suspicious child processes. Alert on process names matching known ransomware patterns or unsigned binaries launched from user-writable directories (Documents, Downloads, AppData/Local/Temp). Establish baseline for legitimate parent-child relationships.

suggestion.title: Worm Lateral Movement via SMB/Admin Shares
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states ransomware 'can spread like a worm,' indicating lateral propagation mechanism; pipeline completely missed this. Typical worm-ransomware uses SMB enumeration (T1021.002) and Windows Admin Shares to replicate. Should detect failed/successful lateral movement attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect attempts to enumerate and write executable files to remote administrative shares (C$, ADMIN$, IPC$) from a single source host in short timeframe. Alert on abnormal SMB write activity from compromised endpoints, especially targeting multiple remote systems. Correlate with subsequent execution events on targets.

suggestion.title: File Encryption Activity and Ransom Note Creation
suggestion.rationale: Ransomware's defining behavioral signature is mass file encryption followed by ransom note drop. Article mentions impact (478 victims presumed encrypted) but pipeline generated zero impact-phase detections. Critical gap for post-compromise visibility.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk file operations with encryption-related patterns: high-volume writes to varied extensions (overwriting or replacing files), creation of .txt/.html/.bmp ransom notes, or modification of file metadata timestamps in patterns inconsistent with normal user activity. Alert on processes touching >100 files within 1-minute windows or targeting system-wide directories from non-system processes.

suggestion.title: Backup/Recovery Inhibition (Ransomware Pre-stage)
suggestion.rationale: Mature ransomware variants delete shadow copies and disable backups before encryption to maximize impact. Article context (high victim count, worm spread) implies coordinated attack; pipeline missed pre-encryption defensive preparation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of vssadmin.exe, wmic.exe, or PowerShell commands with parameters: vssadmin delete shadows, wmic shadowcopy delete, Get-WmiObject Win32_ShadowCopy | Remove-WmiObject. Alert on bcdedit commands modifying boot recovery. Correlate with process elevation and ransomware file paths.

suggestion.title: Command-Line Obfuscation / Script-Based Ransomware Dropper
suggestion.rationale: No mention of command-line techniques (T1059 family) or script delivery mechanisms in pipeline output. Ransomware-as-a-service variants often rely on obfuscated PowerShell or Batch scripts to evade static detection and stage the final payload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell/cmd.exe invocations with Base64-encoded payloads, encoded argument flags (-nop, -noe, -c, -enc), or references to download-execute patterns (IEX, DownloadString). Alert on script-based execution from untrusted paths or with parent processes matching email clients, browsers, or Office applications.

suggestion.title: Persistence Registration via Scheduled Tasks / Registry Autorun
suggestion.rationale: Worm-capable ransomware requires persistence mechanisms to survive reboots and re-infect systems. Pipeline identified zero persistence techniques despite 'worm' capability implying long-dwell-time propagation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation or modification of scheduled tasks with suspicious names, binary paths, or source process identities. Alert on registry modifications to Run/RunOnce keys (HKLM/HKCU) pointing to executable directories associated with encryption payloads. Correlate with parent process and file write events.

suggestion.title: phpBB Authentication Bypass Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'authentication bypass' as primary vulnerability vector. Pipeline generated zero detections for auth evasion. Bypass attempts would manifest as unusual credential validation failures or authentication-handler parameter manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor phpBB ucp.php, login endpoints, and password-reset handlers for requests containing SQL injection payloads, PHP code injection in credential fields, or sequential authentication attempts that succeed despite repeated failures. Alert on HTTP 200 responses to login endpoints with unusual User-Agent patterns or from non-forum IPs within short burst timeframes.

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution via phpBB Template or Upload Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies RCE as the attack outcome; no detection rule generated for command execution phase. This is the core attack. Article phrase: 'Auth Bypass + RCE'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web server processes (apache, nginx, www-data) for spawning cmd.exe, /bin/sh, /bin/bash, or php subprocesses with arguments containing system(), passthru(), or exec(). Alert on HTTP requests to phpBB admin or template editing endpoints containing PHP evaluation keywords. Track child-process relationships where depth exceeds normal phpBB operation.

suggestion.title: Webshell Persistence and Administrative Account Creation Post-RCE
suggestion.rationale: RCE vulnerability affecting 'thousands of forums' implies attackers establish persistence; pipeline missed detection for webshells and rogue admin accounts. This is essential for determining breach scope across multiple forum instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor phpBB cache, styles, and upload directories for unexpected PHP file creation or modification by web server user. Alert on new admin/moderator account creation outside normal administrative windows, especially those with unusually permissive privileges. Track database modifications to user tables adding accounts with admin flags immediately after failed login attempts or file uploads.

suggestion.title: phpBB Version Fingerprinting and Vulnerability Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is version-specific ('10 year old' implies specific affected versions); pipeline failed to note reconnaissance phase. Article states vulnerability present 'Since 2014', suggesting legacy versions at high risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for requests to phpBB fingerprinting paths: /CHANGELOG.txt, /docs/, /install/install.xml, configuration disclosure endpoints, or version-reporting HTTP headers. Alert on sequential scanning of known-vulnerable phpBB endpoints (common in automated exploitation frameworks targeting forums). Track responses containing explicit phpBB version strings in headers or HTML comments.

suggestion.title: Cross-Forum Lateral Movement via Shared Database or Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability affects 'thousands of forums'—detection must cover lateral movement between instances. Article phrase: 'across thousands of forums' implies infrastructure-wide compromise detection is critical.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for database access patterns spanning multiple phpBB instances within same organization/hosting provider. Alert on credential reuse across distinct forum installations, bulk user-table exports or privilege escalations affecting multiple instances within short timeframe. Track outbound traffic from compromised forum servers to administrative interfaces of other phpBB forums.

suggestion.title: Detect JDY Botnet C2 Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies 'JDY Botnet' operating at 1,500-device scale implying active command infrastructure. Pipeline failed to extract C2 indicators or generate beaconing signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound connections to known or suspected JDY C2 infrastructure. Correlate periodic callback patterns to reconnaissance-associated IPs/domains. Alert on DNS queries to JDY-linked FQDNs with follow-on HTTP(S) traffic.

suggestion.title: Detect JDY Botnet Payload Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 1,500-device botnet requiring deployment/execution mechanisms. Title signals active reconnaissance operations but pipeline extracted no execution detection signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect script-based botnet execution via PowerShell/cmd.exe with obfuscated arguments, process injection (CreateRemoteThread, WriteProcessMemory into legitimate processes), or unsigned/suspicious child processes indicative of payload delivery.

suggestion.title: Detect Network Reconnaissance from Botnet Hosts
suggestion.rationale: Article headline explicitly names 'Cyber Reconnaissance' as botnet purpose. Pipeline should surface discovery and scanning patterns (nmap, Nessus, net.exe enumeration) but produced no such signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify hosts executing port-scanning tools, querying network topology (arp, ipconfig, Get-NetAdapter), or enumerating shared resources and domain objects. Correlate multiple source IPs with identical reconnaissance signatures within suspected 1,500-device cohort.

suggestion.title: Detect Lateral Movement Propagation Within Botnet
suggestion.rationale: Scale of 1,500 devices suggests either mass compromise vector or active worm-like propagation. Pipeline output contains no lateral-movement detection rules despite this being core to botnet expansion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SMB reconnaissance and share enumeration, credential-reuse patterns across multiple internal targets, and exploitation attempts (EternalBlue, CVE chains) in short timeframes—hallmarks of botnet worm propagation.

suggestion.title: Detect Exfiltration of Reconnaissance Data via JDY C2
suggestion.rationale: Reconnaissance botnet purpose implies collection and exfiltration of network maps, credentials, and system metadata. Pipeline has no exfiltration signatures despite this being central to article's threat narrative.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sustained outbound traffic to JDY C2 containing reconnaissance artifacts (network topology dumps, ARP tables, user enumerations). Baseline normal data flows and alert on anomalous volume or suspicious data patterns exfiltrated via botnet channels.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Code Commits from Anomalous Development Device
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'the device is the only constant'—implying device compromise as a unifying attack vector across multiple developers/locations. Article body truncated, but concept suggests attacker-in-the-middle or compromised dev machine committing malicious code. No UCs generated despite this being core supply-chain attack pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for code commits originating from a single device across multiple user accounts, or commits with anomalous timestamps/network paths. Correlate device login frequency and network access patterns against commit metadata (author, timestamp, origin IP) to surface device-based persistence.

suggestion.title: Elevated Process Execution in Development Tools or IDEs
suggestion.rationale: If 'code is written everywhere' implies diverse development tooling or IDE usage, article likely discusses code execution risks. Pipeline extracted zero kill-chain phases; execution (T1059.001 variants) should be foundational if malicious code is being written/deployed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unsigned or low-reputation processes spawned by development tools (VS Code, Xcode, JetBrains IDEs, npm/pip package managers). Detect inline script execution or obfuscated payloads passed as build arguments.

suggestion.title: Malware or Suspicious Binary Distribution via Package Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Title implies 'code written everywhere' may reference supply-chain poisoning or compromised package distribution. Article truncated; if it discusses npm, pip, Maven, NuGet, or similar, pipeline should have flagged package provenance and execution risks. Zero IOCs extracted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual package downloads (version mismatches, unexpected source domains), failed package signature verifications, or rapid lateral propagation of package installations across build agents. Flag packages downloaded over unencrypted channels or with mismatched hashes.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Rust crate installation with atypical post-install process execution
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'compromised Rust crate onering performs code exfiltration'—pipeline missed detection for supply-chain trojanization via build-time hooks. No UC captured the execution flow from package installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor cargo/npm installation processes spawning unusual child processes (curl, wget, python, powershell) with network outbound to non-standard destinations. Correlate cargo install or build commands with unexpected network or file access anomalies in the same time window.

suggestion.title: Code or source files exfiltrated during package build or post-install phase
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'performs code exfiltration' but pipeline captured no detection for data movement patterns. Should detect files read from project directories (*.rs, *.toml, *.py, *.js) being sent to attacker infrastructure during cargo/build operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate file access events (source files, config files) with outbound network connections from build processes. Flag if build-time network calls exfiltrate high-entropy payloads matching source-code fingerprints or if process reads private keys/credentials during installation.

suggestion.title: Trojanized dependency installation via typosquatting or namespace confusion
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks often rely on name confusion or unauthorized version publication. Pipeline should surface detection for crate version anomalies, installation from untrusted registries, or mismatched package signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor cargo lock file changes for unexpected crate name variations (typos, similar names). Alert on installations of unsigned or unverified crate versions, crates installed from alternate registries, or sudden version jumps without release notes.

suggestion.title: Reverse-shell or C2 beaconing initiated from Rust build artifacts
suggestion.rationale: Code exfiltration implies attacker interaction; pipeline missed detection for command-and-control or interactive reverse shells spawned during or after package installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected network connections (TCP/UDP/DNS) from cargo or build tool processes to unusual ASNs, residential IPs, or known malware infrastructure. Flag beaconing patterns (regular polling intervals, DNS tunneling) or reverse shell indicators (sh, bash spawned with stdin from network).

suggestion.title: Bearer-token access to dhax/go-base admin endpoints with far-future JWT expiry
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes and provides this as 'UC_46_1' with full Splunk SPL and Defender KQL. Detects successful (HTTP 200) access to '/api/v1/admin/users', '/api/v1/me', '/api/v1/token/refresh' via Bearer tokens — the primary exploitation path of the hardcoded JWT secret vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for successful (200 OK) HTTP requests to /api/v1/admin/*, /api/v1/me, /api/v1/token/refresh endpoints authenticated with Bearer tokens. Decode JWT claims and alert on tokens with suspicious exp fields (far future), non-standard aud/iss values, or admin user IDs from untrusted sources.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable dhax/go-base package deployment detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'github.com/dhax/go-base' (1,685 GitHub stars) as the affected component. Recon phase requires identifying which organizations deploy this boilerplate; detection via supply-chain scanning and dependency analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag go.mod/go.sum files, Dockerfiles, container builds, and CI/CD pipelines referencing github.com/dhax/go-base. Cross-reference with production inventory and alert on any deployed instances of the vulnerable package.

suggestion.title: Admin endpoint enumeration against REST API
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies three sensitive endpoints by name: '/api/v1/admin/users', '/api/v1/me', '/api/v1/token/refresh'. Attackers must probe these to confirm vulnerability before attempting token forgery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid sequential requests (>5 within 5 minutes) to /api/v1/admin/*, /api/v1/me endpoints returning 401 or 403 from a single source, indicating endpoint discovery preceding exploitation.

suggestion.title: Hardcoded JWT secret in configuration files
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability explicitly stated: 'dev.env | 10 | AUTH_JWT_SECRET=random' — template default shipped to all users. Must detect this hardcoded pattern in config files and secrets systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan dev.env, .env.example, config.yaml, Kubernetes secrets, and vault systems for AUTH_JWT_SECRET containing 'random', 'test', 'default', or other weak hardcoded values. Alert on commits, deployments, or config changes introducing these patterns.

suggestion.title: JWT signature verification failure followed by successful admin access
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Token Forgery' enabled by hardcoded secret. Attackers test different HS256 signatures offline; detection pattern is multiple auth failures followed by successful admin request with forged token.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate >3 JWT parsing or signature validation errors from a source within 2 minutes with subsequent successful authenticated access to admin endpoints from the same source. Extract and review successful token exp/aud/user_id claims for anomalies.

suggestion.title: Malicious protocolMessage payload reception and processing
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'sent a malicious payload via placeholderResendMessage' and describes spoofing attack vector, but pipeline has no detection for actual payload delivery or Baileys handling of crafted protocolMessage structures. This is the execution/exploitation phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Baileys session logs for protocolMessage objects with abnormal field counts, missing required crypto signatures, or timestamp/sender mismatches. Network layer: WhatsApp binary protocol frames with anomalous message envelope structure or resend-loop indicators (repeated placeholderResendMessage retransmissions from same peer without sender acknowledgment).

suggestion.title: Fake messages.upsert event emission with spoofed message metadata
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'trigger a fake messages.upsert event with a fake message key and payload.' Pipeline has no hunt for this impact—the actual evidence of successful exploitation is apps receiving messages attributed to wrong senders or with invalid cryptographic keys.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Baileys messages.upsert events against WhatsApp session crypto material: flag events where message sender JID does not match decryption key owner, or where remoteJid cryptographic identity differs from claimed message origin. Look for duplicate messageID with different payload or timestamp anomalies (future-dated or extremely old messages suddenly inserted).

suggestion.title: App state sync corruption via crafted messages.upsert injection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'corrupt the app state sync system by sending fake key s[...]' Pipeline generates no detection for state validation or integrity checks. Corrupted state is forensic evidence of exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Baileys appState dictionary for inconsistencies: chat count mismatches vs actual message counts, contact presence state flipping rapidly without corresponding network activity, or cryptographic hash validation failures on deserialized appState objects. In Windows registry/file-backed state: look for state write timestamps that predate the session's connect time (impossible in normal operation).

suggestion.title: Process-level runtime detection of vulnerable Baileys module load
suggestion.rationale: UC_38_2 detects vulnerable versions on disk; missing is confirmation that vulnerable code is actually executing. Attacker may have patched version on disk but old module cached in memory, or version check bypassed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate npm/nodejs process execution with module require() or import statements for baileys; extract loaded version from node_modules/.package.json at runtime via process memory inspection or instrumentation. Flag when process version metadata disagrees with package.json version string, or when version-specific patches (e.g., 7.0.0-rc12 security commit hash) are absent from loaded bytecode.

suggestion.title: Replay and timing analysis of protocolMessage resend sequences
suggestion.rationale: Article focuses on placeholderResendMessage as delivery mechanism; pipeline has no hunt for the request/response cadence that would distinguish exploits from legitimate resends. Malicious resends should show abnormal retry patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Capture WhatsApp protocol streams and analyze placeholderResendMessage frequency per conversation: flag when single peer sends >5 resend requests for same message within <2 second window (suggests payload spraying), or when resend timestamps violate chronological message sequence, or when resends arrive from IPs not previously seen in conversation (sender spoofing at network layer).

suggestion.title: Ivanti/Fortinet/SAP Vulnerability Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'critical vulnerabilities' from three enterprise vendors requiring patches. Title alone establishes patching activity; standard practice for vuln disclosures includes exploitation detection logic. Pipeline should have extracted CVEs and mapped them to initial_access or privilege_escalation techniques.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/network requests targeting known Ivanti, Fortinet, or SAP vulnerability endpoints or suspicious payloads matching published CVE PoCs. Check for unusual outbound connections from administrative/management interfaces to external IP ranges post-patch availability.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Service Enumeration (Ivanti/Fortinet/SAP)
suggestion.rationale: Critical vulnerabilities in enterprise products typically precede attack chains with reconnaissance/scanning phase. Article describes patching urgency but no detection UC for identifying unpatched systems in fleet.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify scanning or probing activity against known ports/services for Ivanti Connect Secure, Fortinet FortiGate, and SAP systems. Correlate with absence of patch deployment records to surface unpatched instances.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Patched Vulnerability
suggestion.rationale: Critical vulnerabilities often enable privilege escalation post-exploitation. No UC provided for detecting escalation attempts that would follow successful exploitation of disclosed vulns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual process creation, token elevation, or child process spawning from Ivanti/Fortinet/SAP services following patch release. Flag cases where services are performing privilege escalation outside normal baseline.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-5027 Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Exploited for Unauthenticated RCE'—detection should monitor for characteristic HTTP payloads, request patterns, or error signatures indicative of CVE-2026-5027 exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Langflow instances for patterns consistent with CVE-2026-5027 exploitation: requests to vulnerable endpoints without authentication headers, payloads attempting code injection or command execution, and response patterns indicating unauthorized access granted.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Process Execution from Langflow Service
suggestion.rationale: Title confirms RCE capability post-exploitation—detection must flag child process creation (shells, interpreters, utilities) spawned from Langflow service context without legitimate scheduled task or user trigger.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned by Langflow runtime (Java, Python, or Node processes) that spawn bash, cmd, powershell, or system utilities. Establish baseline of legitimate Langflow activity and flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Langflow API Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Unauthenticated' RCE—detection must identify successful HTTP responses to Langflow admin, API, or flow endpoints without valid session tokens or authentication credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP 200-299 responses to Langflow API paths (/api/*, /flows, /run) from sources lacking valid Bearer tokens, session cookies, or API keys. Correlate with preceding failed authentication attempts.

suggestion.title: Malware file hash detection (Talos telemetry)
suggestion.rationale: Article lists three SHA256 and three MD5 hashes under 'Most prevalent malware files from Talos telemetry over the past week' with detection names (Win.Worm.Coinminer, W32.Injector:Gen.21ie.1201). These are high-confidence, current-week IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hash-based detection for 9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507, 96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974, a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91. Alert on process execution, file creation, or image load of these hashes across enterprise endpoints.

suggestion.title: Check Point VPN exploitation by Qilin
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'CISA gives U.S. federal agencies three days to fix a VPN bug under attack by Qilin' affecting Check Point remote access tools, firewalls, and VPNs. Specific threat actor + specific product + active exploitation = high-priority detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Check Point appliances and proxies for exploitation patterns targeting the recently-disclosed VPN vulnerability (CVE reference should be resolved). Look for abnormal authentication flows, privilege escalation post-initial-access, or Qilin-attributed IP/infrastructure attempting connections to Check Point management interfaces.

suggestion.title: NSO social engineering indicator detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'WhatsApp catches spyware firm NSO defying no-hacking court order' via 'social engineering attack that attempted to trick users into clicking on malicious links.' Maps to NSO's active social engineering campaigns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate WhatsApp message metadata with URL clicks pointing to known NSO infrastructure or typosquat/lookalike domains. Flag social engineering vectors targeting high-value users. Cross-reference with known NSO phishing domains and certificate issuer patterns.

suggestion.title: Linux nf_tables use-after-free exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'High-severity vulnerability in Linux caused by a single faulty character... a use-after-free in code implementing nf_tables.' This is active in the wild and Linux-based services are common in SOC scope.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious kernel memory operations, nf_tables module load/unload sequences, or unexpected privilege elevation following iptables/nftables rule manipulation. Flag attempts to exploit memory corruption via crafted netfilter rules on systems with the vulnerable kernel.

suggestion.title: Microsoft local privilege escalation chain detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Microsoft fixes two high-severity zero-days... a local privilege escalation' that 'can be chained to a separate vulnerability to give users with low-level privileges... full SYSTEM rights.' Chainable LPE is a high-fidelity indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect privilege escalation chains: low-integrity process spawning system-integrity child processes, token impersonation patterns, or access to SYSTEM-level resources from unexpected caller context. Correlate with known Microsoft LPE CVE exploitation signatures.

suggestion.title: Detection Gap: Vulnerability Scanner Evasion via AI-Generated Obfuscation
suggestion.rationale: Title implies AI is 'breaking' vulnerability management—suggests attackers using AI to evade scanning. Article context ('CISOs moving budget to BAS') implies current detection/scanning inadequate. Expected article to discuss evasion techniques not caught by traditional VM scanning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for packers, obfuscators, or runtime-generated code execution that bypasses static scanning signatures. Look for processes spawning with high entropy payloads, unusual memory-mapped executable regions, or repeated re-compilation artifacts within attack timeframes.

suggestion.title: BAS Deployment Footprint: Authorized Breach & Attack Simulation Tool Activity
suggestion.rationale: Budget shift to BAS is the hook—organization is investing in continuous offensive testing. Need to detect legitimate BAS tool execution (Rapid7, Accenture ACME, Gremlin, etc.) to baseline and segregate from true attacks, preventing false positives in downstream alerting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create whitelist of known BAS vendors' scanning signatures, API calls, and network behaviors. Alert on scanning activity NOT matching known BAS CIDR/user-agent/command patterns to isolate unauthorized reconnaissance from approved red-team runs.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Management System Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: If AI broke traditional VM processes, attackers may be directly targeting VM platforms (Qualys, Tenable, ServiceNow, etc.) to suppress or modify findings. Article implies systemic failure of detection; direct compromise of VM infrastructure is a high-impact scenario.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for privileged authentication attempts against VM platform admin consoles, unexpected modifications to scan policies/exemptions, API calls that suppress findings, or lateral movement from VM appliance to critical infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Externally Reachable Ivanti Sentry Appliances
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability 'exploitable in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Primary attack surface—must detect internet-facing instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Ivanti Sentry or MobileIron Sentry appliances with HTTP/HTTPS ports (443, 8443) accessible from untrusted networks. Correlate external exposure records against internal asset inventory to identify unpatched or unmanaged instances.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Presence Across Fleet
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status indicates active exploitation. Article warns: 'patch lag is the silent killer'—detection must scan for vulnerable versions even if prior scans showed 'not vulnerable' due to lag.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference all Ivanti Sentry appliances against vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-10520. Flag instances with unpatched versions or missing remediation confirmation, especially if last scan predates patch release date (2026-06-14).

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Connection Attempts to Sentry Management Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'remote unauthenticated user' as the attack vector. Detection must identify connection attempts that bypass or fail to complete authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TCP sessions to Ivanti Sentry ports (443, 8443) that either timeout, reset, or exhibit incomplete TLS/authentication handshakes from external IPs. Baseline legitimate admin access and alert on deviations (port scans, connection storms, anomalous source geos).

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article names the vulnerability as 'OS command injection.' Detection must identify injection payloads with shell metacharacters or command substitution syntax targeting Sentry interfaces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect HTTP/HTTPS requests to Sentry endpoints for shell command injection indicators: pipe operators (|), command chaining (;, &, &&, ||), command substitution ($(), backticks), or shell metacharacters. Cross-reference with publicly disclosed vulnerable parameter names once vendor advisory published.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Execution from Sentry Service Context
suggestion.rationale: Article states exploitation achieves 'root-level remote code execution.' Detection must identify anomalous child processes spawned by Sentry application after successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal child processes spawned by Ivanti Sentry service/application user. Alert on unexpected shells, reverse shells, network tools (curl, wget, nc), compilers, or system utilities. High signal if correlated with preceding unauthenticated access or injection payload logs.

suggestion.title: Root Privilege Escalation from Sentry Application Context
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'root-level' access achieved via the vulnerability. Detection must surface privilege escalation events from Sentry process to root/SYSTEM.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor privilege escalation indicators from Sentry service account: sudo execution, uid 0 transitions, /etc/sudoers modifications, CAP_SYS_ADMIN grants. On Windows: privilege elevation from Sentry service to SYSTEM. Alert on any occurrence.

suggestion.title: Check Point VPN Authentication Bypass Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states CVE-2026-50751 'allows unauthenticated remote attackers to bypass user authentication and establish unauthorized VPN connections.' This is the explicit initial-access vector; no detection provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful VPN session creation from sources with zero prior authentication events, or immediate session-start following rapid auth-failure sequences (within 60 seconds) from the same source IP. Flag impossible-travel VPN logins post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: Credential Dumping Post-VPN Compromise
suggestion.rationale: T1003.001 (LSASS Memory) and T1003 (OS Credential Dumping) explicitly listed. Article implies credential theft phase following VPN access in ransomware kill chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect LSASS process access from non-system processes (excluding MsSense.exe, csrss.exe, lsm.exe, services.exe, svchost.exe). Monitor for rundll32+comsvcs.dll MiniDump, procdump targeting lsass, or sekurlsa module loading. Elevate confidence if within 10 minutes of VPN session creation.

suggestion.title: SMB Lateral Movement & Remote Service Execution
suggestion.rationale: T1021.002 (SMB Admin Shares) and T1569.002 (Service Execution) listed. Article narrative: exploit → lateral movement → ransomware implies service-execution lateral movements.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect psexec.exe, paexec.exe, smbexec.py, or wmic.exe with /node: parameters. Alert on outbound SMB (port 445) from processes not in an admin-tooling baseline. Correlate rapid internal subnet scanning with subsequent service-creation/start events on discovered hosts.

suggestion.title: Mass File Encryption (Ransomware Impact)
suggestion.rationale: T1486 (Data Encrypted for Impact) listed explicitly. Article warns of active ransomware campaigns, requiring real-time encryption detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when a single user/process on a single host modifies or renames >200 unique files within 1 minute. Correlate with file-extension changes (.locked, .encrypted, .<5-char random>, .{ransomware-name}). Monitor for file-handle locks preventing legitimate access.

suggestion.title: Application Layer Protocol Abuse for Command & Control
suggestion.rationale: T1071 (Application Layer Protocol) listed but not covered by any detection. Ransomware campaigns require C2; article IOCs imply attacker infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST beaconing at regular intervals, DNS tunneling patterns, or HTTPS to non-standard ports from process associated with ransomware execution. Match outbound connections against the 16 provided IPv4 IOCs. Flag missing standard HTTP headers or anomalous User-Agents.

suggestion.title: File Obfuscation & Encoded Payload Execution
suggestion.rationale: T1027 (Obfuscated Files or Information) listed but not detected. Ransomware payloads typically use obfuscation and encoding.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on base64-encoded or hex-encoded PowerShell execution, especially if parent process is unusual (e.g., msiexec, rundll32, regsvcs). Detect obfuscated batch/VBScript with suspicious registry or file-system operations. Monitor for unsigned binaries with metadata mismatches.

suggestion.title: Unusual postinstall/preinstall Scripts in Package Manifests
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'automatic execution of installation scripts' as the attack surface: 'postinstall', 'preinstall', 'prepare' hooks in package.json. Pipeline missed npm-native detection vectors entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for injection of obfuscated or suspicious shell commands into npm package.json lifecycle hooks. Baseline legitimate postinstall scripts per organization and alert on deviations, particularly downloads from external URLs or execution of unsigned binaries during 'npm install'.

suggestion.title: Detect npm Package Installation with Postinstall Scripts
suggestion.rationale: Article centers on postinstall scripts as the supply chain attack vector—'GitHub to Disable npm Install Scripts by Default' establishes postinstall execution as the key exploitation mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on installations of npm packages containing postinstall, preinstall, or prepare scripts that execute shell commands, especially those invoking curl, wget, powershell, or obfuscated command patterns. Cross-check package.json metadata against allowlists of known benign package scripts.

suggestion.title: Alert on Installation of Known-Malicious npm Packages
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain compromise in npm works by poisoning the package registry; the article's focus on disabling scripts-by-default implies prior incidents of malicious package installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference installed npm packages against threat feeds of typosquatted, hijacked, or trojanized package names. Flag installations matching known supply-chain compromise incidents, especially packages with small install bases or recent version mutations.

suggestion.title: Monitor npm Child Process Spawning During Installation
suggestion.rationale: Malicious postinstall scripts execute as child processes of npm/node—monitoring for unexpected shell spawning during package install detects exploitation of this vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag parent-child relationships where npm.exe or node.exe spawn cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, or curl with network-based destinations (especially to non-package-registry hosts). Monitor for process creation with encoded/obfuscated command lines during install phases.

suggestion.title: Detect npm Package Metadata Injection (Script Addition in New Versions)
suggestion.rationale: Attackers compromise packages by injecting postinstall scripts into new versions; detecting first-appearance of executable scripts in a package's version history signals hijack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare package.json metadata across consecutive versions; alert when postinstall/preinstall scripts appear in a minor or patch version update, especially if the script contains shell metacharacters, base64, or variable expansion patterns.

suggestion.title: PE Overlay Detection — Massive File Size / Poly-header Entropy
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states GoFlateLoader uses 'massive PE overlay' as its obfuscation vector ('what makes it stand out is how effective a simple trick has made it'). Pipeline maps T1027 but fails to generate a detection for the distinguishing characteristic—abnormally large overlay appended to PE headers, which is the attack's entire novelty and defense-evasion strength.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PE executables where reported file size >> virtual size in PE headers, or where the raw binary has entropy spikes in trailing sections (the overlay payload). Correlate with process creation; Go loaders typically show characteristic import tables. Raise priority for files in download/temp directories or executed from email attachment locations.

suggestion.title: Go-Compiled Loader Signature — Process Characteristics & Strings
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies GoFlateLoader as written in Go, which has distinctive compile-time artifacts and import patterns (runtime.GOMAXPROCS, runtime.goexit, etc.). No detection for the loader itself, only for its post-exploitation payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag process creation for executables with Go runtime imports or characteristic string patterns (e.g., 'Go build' metadata, 'runtime.newobject', runtime.systemstack). Cross-reference against known-malicious hashes (the 11 IOCs) and behaviors (high CPU usage during decompression, mmap syscalls for overlay decoding).

suggestion.title: Infostealer Post-Execution — Multi-Channel Credential Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names three infostealers (Lumma, Vidar, StealC) delivered by the loader. After browser credential theft (T1555.003/T1539), these stealers will exfiltrate to C2. Pipeline detects browser access but not the subsequent network beaconing or multi-stage credential aggregation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-discovery hunt: if UC_BROWSER_STEALER fires, escalate to network monitoring for the child process initiating HTTPS/TLS connections to non-standard ports or suspicious domains. Lumma/Vidar/StealC have known C2 patterns (TLS certificate anomalies, HTTP user-agent spoofing). Correlate with temporary file staging (dropped executables in %TEMP%, %APPDATA%).

suggestion.title: Loader Delivery Vector — Initial Access Artifact Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title and narrative imply GoFlateLoader is 'spreading across the internet' but the truncated body does not detail delivery mechanism (email, watering hole, drive-by, etc.). Pipeline reconstructed zero kill-chain phases; the initial_access phase is completely absent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Until source is confirmed: monitor for executable downloads to user-writable locations (Downloads folder) with low reputation / unknown publisher signatures. Correlate with email attachment opens, browser download events, and parent process chains (Outlook, Edge, Chrome). GoFlateLoader's Go signature may persist in memory/disk even before overlay decompression.

suggestion.title: Overlay Decompression / Decoding Process Behavior
suggestion.rationale: The loader's core function is decoding the PE overlay before dropping infostealers. Article: 'one job: to decode and drop dangerous information-stealing programs'. No behavioral detection for the decoding phase itself (T1140).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor the parent loader process for high CPU utilization spikes (decompression loop), large VirtualAlloc calls, and WriteFile operations to %TEMP% / %APPDATA% followed by CreateProcessA/W for freshly-written executables. Overlay decoders often iterate byte-by-byte or in chunks; correlate sustained high CPU with child process execution timing.

suggestion.title: DMG Mount and Suspicious Child Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'weaponized DMG files' and 'fake software installers' — no detection for spawning executables from mounted DMG volumes. This is the delivery and initial execution mechanism: user opens fake installer DMG, malware runs from /Volumes mount point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for process parent path or working directory under /Volumes/ followed by executable launch (especially unsigned or newly created binaries). infostealer payloads execute directly from mounted DMG media. Critical pattern: user mounts DMG, then process spawns with CommandLine containing path starting with /Volumes/.

suggestion.title: Infostealer C2 Beaconing to Article IOCs
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 38 domain IOCs but pipeline generated zero network-based detection. Exfiltration of stolen credentials must traverse network to these C2 servers — critical gap in kill chain coverage between credential access and exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Outbound DNS queries or HTTP/HTTPS connections from non-browser processes to IOC domains (cleanmymacos.org, rapidfilevault4.sbs, mentaorb.com, etc.) or IPs (95.85.251.177, etc.). High confidence if preceded within 10 minutes by credential database access detected in UC_BROWSER_STEALER.

suggestion.title: Fake Software Installer Pattern — Suspicious App Bundle Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'fake software installers disguised as legitimate apps, tricking users into handing over access' — no detection for creation of lookalike .app bundles or code-signed apps with borrowed legitimacy.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detection of .app bundles created in /Applications or ~/Applications with names mimicking legitimate software (Clean My Mac OS, Rapid File Vault, Autofill Manager) but mismatched code signing identity, missing signature, or signed by unknown developer. Also flags executable writes to legitimate system app bundles by non-Apple processes.

suggestion.title: Rapid Sequential Browser Credential Database Access
suggestion.rationale: Infostealer needs to access multiple browser credential stores (Chrome, Firefox, Safari) to exfiltrate all available credentials — detection provided only identifies single-browser access, missing the enumeration pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Single non-browser process accessing 2+ browser credential/cookie databases (Chrome Login Data, Firefox logins.json, Safari Cookies, Edge User Data) within 90-second window. This pattern is rare for legitimate tools and indicates malware enumerating all available credential sources before exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Download-Origin Process Executing Malware from DMG
suggestion.rationale: Article implies social engineering delivery — users downloading fake installers from messaging, email, or browser. No detection for suspicious download-to-execution chain triggering DMG mount.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parent process for 'open' or 'hdiutil attach' command is Safari, Mail, Messages, Slack, or other download/communication tool. DMG file located in ~/Downloads and executed immediately after download completion. Suspicious parent indicates social engineering success.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection in Ivanti Sentry Admin Portal
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'OS command injection weakness' and public PoC released. Attackers inject shell metacharacters via Sentry requests to achieve code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry admin portal requests (typically port 8443) for shell metacharacters (;, |, &, `, $(), backticks) in query parameters and POST bodies. Flag any parameter value containing command-injection syntax. Correlate with subsequent root process execution.

suggestion.title: Root-Privilege Process Execution from Sentry Service
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'execute code with root privileges on Internet-exposed secure mobile gateways.' Post-exploitation processes run as root, indicating privilege escalation occurred.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when Sentry web service (typically Java/httpd) spawns child processes with UID 0 or SYSTEM context. Legitimate admin functions rarely execute as root from web daemon. Baseline normal Sentry operations and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Backdoor Persistence Installation on Sentry Gateway
suggestion.rationale: Article: Shadowserver 'reported that attackers had already backdoored most of the Sentry gateways exposed online' and found 'at least 2 backdoored' instances. Persistence requires filesystem modifications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file writes to persistence locations (/etc/rc.d, /etc/init.d, systemd timers, crontab, SSH authorized_keys) originating from Sentry processes or with timestamp gaps suggesting root-owned modifications. Alert on executable creation in Sentry application directories.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Vulnerable Version Running
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies patched versions 'R10.5.2, R10.6.2, and R10.7.1' on June 10, 2026. Versions earlier than these are confirmed exploitable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset management for Sentry appliances running versions <R10.5.2, <R10.6.2, or <R10.7.1. Cross-reference with internet-exposure intelligence (Shodan, Censys). Alert on unpatched Sentry visible from untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: Internet-Exposed Ivanti Sentry Admin Portal Access
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Ivanti Sentry admin portals exposed online' and 'Internet-exposed secure mobile gateways.' Internet accessibility is the enabler for exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful authentication to Sentry admin portal (port 8443) from non-corporate/non-VPN source IPs. Flag geographic anomalies and bulk authentication attempts preceding successful login. Baseline legitimate administrative access patterns.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration from Compromised Sentry Gateway
suggestion.rationale: Article warns of 'theft of sensitive customer and corporate data' as end goal. Compromised gateways enable lateral movement and data theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from Sentry appliances to non-corporate destinations outside normal operational scope. Detect DNS queries to newly-registered or suspicious domains from gateway context. Alert on large data transfers to external IPs.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Creation on Developer Machines
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly covers 'Detect Them on Developer Machines with Suspicious Files'—indicates file-based attack delivery requiring file creation monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unknown executable and script files (.exe, .dll, .ps1, .vbs, .bat, .scr) created in typical developer-targeted locations: Downloads folder, user temp directory, project root directories, and %APPDATA%. Flag files with zero or minimal vendor reputation scores and unsigned binaries.

suggestion.title: Execution of Newly Created Suspicious Files
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates malware 'spreading'—implies execution phase where suspicious files are run, likely exploiting developer workflows or trust in development tools.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation from suspicious file paths (Downloads, temp, project directories) with parent-child chains showing unintended execution. Alert on script interpreters (powershell.exe, cmd.exe, cscript.exe) spawning from untrusted locations. Correlate file creation timestamps with immediate process execution.

suggestion.title: Credential Theft from Developer Tool Caches (SSH, Git, IDE Secrets)
suggestion.rationale: Developer machines targeted specifically—threat actors seek to steal SSH keys, git credentials, and IDE-stored secrets; article context implies credential-access phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file access to .ssh directory, .gitconfig, credential manager caches, and browser password stores. Flag processes reading these paths outside normal development workflows. Alert on copies of SSH keys or credential files to suspicious destinations or external storage.

suggestion.title: Malware Persistence via Startup Folders and Registry Run Keys
suggestion.rationale: Malware families require persistence mechanisms; developer machines provide high-value targets for sustained compromise beyond initial execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Windows startup folders and registry Run keys for new entries created contemporaneously with suspicious file artifacts. Alert on registry modifications from unusual source processes. Correlate suspicious file timestamps with startup location modifications.

suggestion.title: Masquerading as Legitimate Development Tools or Build Artifacts
suggestion.rationale: Developer machines targeted via 'suspicious files' likely disguised as legitimate dev tools; detection should identify trojanized or spoofed binaries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Analyze file properties (version strings, digital signatures, manifests) of executables claiming to be development tools. Flag unsigned binaries masquerading as signed Microsoft or trusted third-party tools. Verify certificate validity and issuer trustworthiness against known-good baseline.

suggestion.title: Command-and-Control Beaconing from Developer Machines
suggestion.rationale: Malware families require C2 infrastructure; detection should include unusual network communications from compromised developer systems to external hosts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from developer machines to non-standard ports, newly registered domains, or known-malicious infrastructure. Alert on DNS queries to botnet C2 nodes or suspicious external hosts. Establish baseline of expected external connections and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: OpenClaw AI: Code Execution via Agent Response Handling
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'Trick OpenClaw AI Agent Into Running Code'—core attack step but pipeline output contains zero kill-chain phases and zero use cases. Critical gap: no detection for process spawning or shell execution triggered by or correlated with OpenClaw agent API responses.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, /bin/bash, python) initiated within seconds of OpenClaw API calls, especially when process parent is a language interpreter (node, python, go) or service wrapper. Correlate process commandline tokens with agent output if logged.

suggestion.title: OpenClaw AI: Credential/Secret Exfiltration in Agent Output
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'Leaking Secrets'—direct data exfiltration impact but pipeline extracted no exfiltration techniques, no IOCs, no data-loss detections. Critical gap: no monitoring for credentials (API keys, tokens, passwords, SSH keys) appearing in cleartext within agent responses or outbound traffic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect secrets-manager queries by OpenClaw agent (calls to AWS Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault, Azure Key Vault), followed by exfiltration of retrieved credentials. Flag if agent output is written to external API endpoint, Slack channel, or S3 bucket external to organization.

suggestion.title: OpenClaw AI: Prompt Injection / Instruction Override Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Title states attacks 'trick' the agent—implies input manipulation/prompt injection but pipeline produced zero initial-access vectors, zero defense-evasion techniques. Critical gap: no detection for adversarial prompts, jailbreak payloads, or instruction-override syntax in queries to OpenClaw.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag API requests to OpenClaw endpoints containing instruction-override keywords ('ignore previous instructions', 'pretend you are', 'system override'), command-syntax characters ($(), backticks, pipes), or Base64/URL-encoded payloads that decode to injection syntax. Alert on repeated variations from same source (fuzzing pattern).

suggestion.title: OpenClaw AI: Unauthorized Secret Enumeration via Agent Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article title implies agent was manipulated to access secrets—credential discovery gap. Pipeline produced zero discovery techniques, zero credential-access phase reconstruction. Critical gap: no detection for agent function calls to list/enumerate secrets, environment variables, or configuration endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor OpenClaw agent invocations of secret-access functions (list-secrets, get-secret, read-env, get-config). Flag when agent queries credential stores without prior human authorization, especially with keywords like 'api_key', 'token', 'password', 'secret', 'credential' in the function call or query parameter.

suggestion.title: Recovery Partition XML File Creation or Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states exploit 'bypasses Windows BitLocker via Recovery Partition XML Files'—the mechanism is unambiguous. Pipeline missed the primary hunting vector: suspicious file writes to recovery partitions (C:\Recovery\*, EFI/boot partitions) with .xml extensions, particularly from non-admin or unusual process lineage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DeviceFileEvents for XML creation/modification in recovery partition paths. Correlate with process parent (should be System updates, not cmd.exe, PowerShell, or user processes). High-risk processes include manage-bde.exe, rundll32.exe, svchost.exe spawning file I/O to recovery volumes. Baseline legitimate BitLocker updates first.

suggestion.title: BitLocker Encryption Status Tampering or Disablement
suggestion.rationale: Bypass of BitLocker encryption requires either suspension, disablement, or key extraction. Pipeline missed detections for manage-bde.exe invocation with disable/suspend/protectors flags, HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\FVE registry modification, or WMI calls to Win32_EncryptableVolume.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on manage-bde.exe with -off, -pause, -status, or -protectors flags. Monitor HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\FVE and BitLocker policy registry paths for unauthorized writes. Detect WMI method calls to GetKeyProtectors, DecryptVolume. Flag execution from recovery/system context (SYSTEM user, elevated token, pre-boot environment).

suggestion.title: GreatXML Exploit Artifact and Execution
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline failed to extract 'GreatXML' as a named IOC. Article establishes GreatXML as a specific, named exploit/malware family. This should seed file hash, PDB metadata, command-line signatures, and parent process hunting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execution artifacts related to GreatXML pending CVE/threat-intel feed publication. Track delivery via XML attachments, script-based exploit wrappers, or HTA execution. Correlate command-line execution with XML parsers (msxml, xmldom, powershell -File *.xml) and recovery partition file access. Search for unsigned or suspicious binary loads from recovery partitions.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Process Elevation or System Context Privilege Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Recovery partition and BitLocker manipulation typically require SYSTEM or boot-level privileges. Pipeline missed detection for privilege escalation patterns: token impersonation, service abuse, or processes spawned from recovery environment with elevated context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect calc.exe, cmd.exe, or PowerShell spawned with SYSTEM context, SeLoadDriverPrivilege, or SeSystemtimePrivilege tokens. Flag parent processes that are unusual (recovery loaders, smss.exe, csrss.exe). Alert on svchost.exe or rundll32.exe with recovery partition file operations. Baseline normal system service behavior first.

suggestion.title: BitLocker Recovery Key Escrow or TPM Bypass Artifacts
suggestion.rationale: Successful BitLocker bypass requires access to key material (TPM, recovery key, or escrow). Pipeline missed detection for abnormal AD recovery key queries, TPM module access, or Entra recovery key API calls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for manage-bde.exe -protectors -get calls (recovery key export). Alert on LDAP queries for msRecoveryInformation objects in Active Directory. Track TPM.msc execution or Trusted Platform Module WMI class access (Win32_Tpm). In hybrid environments, flag Entra BitLocker recovery API access from non-Intune/MDM sources.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Volume or Filesystem Access Patterns Related to Recovery Partitions
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation of recovery partition XML files implies direct filesystem access or volume-level manipulation. Pipeline missed detections for unusual device handle opens, raw disk I/O, or partition table reads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes opening \\.\PhysicalDrive* or \\.\Volume* handles with unusual process lineage. Alert on raw disk I/O operations, partition table reads, or direct writes to boot sectors. Flag attrib.exe, cipher.exe, or diskpart.exe on recovery partitions. Correlation: if followed by BitLocker status changes, escalate to critical.

suggestion.title: Oracle PeopleSoft Exploitation via Gadget Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article states attack used 'gadget chain' of zero-days and old vulnerabilities against PeopleSoft instances in cloud and on-premises deployments. No detection for exploit payloads or suspicious process chains initiated from the application layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PeopleSoft application servers for unusual Java process spawning, system utility execution (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, curl) from application root directories, or suspicious serialized object deserialization patterns. Flag POST requests to known PeopleSoft endpoints with abnormal payload sizes or gadget-chain-related class instantiation patterns.

suggestion.title: Bulk Export of Student Records and Sensitive Personal Data
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies theft of student records containing 'full names, home addresses, IP addresses, phone numbers, dates of birth, email addresses, ethnicities, disabilities, passport numbers and information relating to academic enrolments and fee payments'—454,600 records total. No detection suggested for bulk sensitive data access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk queries to student records database selecting passport_number, credit_card, or payment_detail fields at scale. Detect unusual database service accounts or application contexts querying >1000 student records in <1 hour. Flag direct file-system access to student records tables from non-standard processes or off-hours export requests.

suggestion.title: Multi-Gigabyte Data Staging and Compression Before Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article reports 'over 40GB of documents' stolen. No detection for data staging, compression, or bulk file packaging that precedes large-scale exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation of large compressed archives (>1GB .zip, .tar.gz, .rar files) in temp directories on database or file servers. Alert on sustained outbound network transfers >5GB in 1 hour to unknown external IPs or cloud storage services. Monitor for deletion of staging directories immediately after large file transfers complete.

suggestion.title: Cross-Campus Synchronized Unauthorized Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states compromise affected 'Nottingham UK main campus, Malaysia and China campuses,' indicating either lateral movement or synchronized attacker access across geographically dispersed infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect near-simultaneous account usage or data access across UK, Malaysia, and China campus network segments within <24 hours. Flag database replication, sync, or backup operations initiated between campuses targeting student records systems. Alert on credential or session token reuse across geographically distant campus networks.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Authentication to PeopleSoft Portal and Finance Systems
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions theft of 'billing and payment information, credit card and payment details' via 'campus portal exports,' implying either credential compromise or valid account abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PeopleSoft authentication logs for successful login followed by unusual data export requests, authentication from new geographies, or sessions performing actions inconsistent with the authenticated user's role. Detect rapid successive logins across multiple student or finance portals with single or similar credentials.

suggestion.title: ShinyHunters Threat-Group Campaign Correlation and Dark-Web Leak-Site Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article attributes breach to ShinyHunters, described as part of 'widespread data theft campaign...against over 100 organizations worldwide' via PeopleSoft. No detection suggested for actor-attributed infrastructure or leak-site correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference network logs for connections to known ShinyHunters dark-web leak-site infrastructure or previously-identified attacker-controlled storage services. Correlate data exfiltration timing and volume with ShinyHunters' posting cadence on leak sites. Monitor for data staging in cloud storage services known to host ShinyHunters exfil.

suggestion.title: npm Postinstall Script Execution from Suspicious Package
suggestion.rationale: Article centers on npm v12 blocking postinstall scripts; describes the attack vector directly: 'npm v12…block[s] postinstall'. Detection should monitor for what the feature prevents—malicious postinstall hooks executing during package install.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for npm.exe or yarn.exe spawning child processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash) during package installation, particularly with arguments injected from package.json postinstall field. Baseline clean install behavior and flag deviations; correlate with node_modules source IP/hash for potential compromised packages.

suggestion.title: npm Dependency Addition with Embedded Postinstall Hook
suggestion.rationale: Article's thesis is that postinstall scripts represent supply chain risk. Detection should cover manifest modification (package.json) and dependency resolution that introduces new postinstall hooks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag package.json edits (or npm install/add calls) that add dependencies with postinstall fields. Cross-reference against known-safe packages; escalate new postinstall entries in transitive dependencies (detected via npm ls output).

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via npm postinstall in CI/Build Context
suggestion.rationale: Article discusses npm postinstall risk in the context of software supply chain; in build/CI systems, postinstall scripts run with elevated privileges. Missing use case for escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In CI/build pipelines, detect npm postinstall scripts that attempt to write to restricted directories, modify environment variables, exfiltrate secrets (env var access), or spawn processes outside expected npm context (e.g., curl to external hosts, modifications to /etc or Windows registry).

suggestion.title: npm Package Repository Substitution or Registry Redirect
suggestion.rationale: Article implies supply chain compromise vectors; detection should cover when npm registry is spoofed or redirected to install poisoned packages before postinstall executes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry requests (DNS/HTTP to registry.npmjs.org); flag resolution to unexpected IPs or local package cache lookups. Detect .npmrc or package-lock.json modifications that point to alternate registries. Correlate with offline/air-gap violations.

suggestion.title: Detect OceanLotus Spearphishing Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article title references OceanLotus campaign targeting Vietnam investors. Title mentions 'FireAnt Attack,' typical of spear-phishing delivery. No IOCs extracted despite clear attribution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for emails with suspicious links or attachments targeting Vietnam-based investment sector. Alert on sender domains spoofing legitimate financial institutions. Check email headers for APT32/OceanLotus indicators.

suggestion.title: SPECTRALVIPER Malware Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: SPECTRALVIPER explicitly named in title as delivery payload. No signature-based detection or behavioral indicators extracted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious process launches following document opening (macro-enabled Office, PDF exploits). Flag parent process chains typical of OceanLotus: Office→cmd→PowerShell→C2 beaconing.

suggestion.title: Command and Control Communication for APT32
suggestion.rationale: OceanLotus attack campaign with malware delivery implies C2 callback phase. No domains, IPs, or C2 signatures extracted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/HTTPS callback patterns and DNS queries associated with known APT32 infrastructure. Alert on anomalous network traffic from compromised investors' systems to Vietnam-hosted C2 nodes.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via OceanLotus Documents
suggestion.rationale: Vietnam investor targeting suggests credential theft via lure documents. No harvest mechanisms or tools detected in pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag suspicious keylogging, clipboard monitoring, or credential manager access post-infection. Monitor for data exfil to attacker-controlled servers following SPECTRALVIPER execution.

suggestion.title: Oracle PeopleSoft CVE-2026-35273 Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly mentions 'ShinyHunters Exploits Oracle PeopleSoft Zero-Day (CVE-2026-35273)' — pipeline extracted zero indicators or detection rules despite this being the core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to known PeopleSoft endpoints (/psp/*, /ps/login.html, /weblib_*) from untrusted sources with payloads matching CVE-2026-35273 signature patterns. Flag successful 200/302 responses after malformed request sequence that would trigger the vulnerability. Track for corresponding process execution or shell spawning on PeopleSoft application servers.

suggestion.title: Bulk Data Exfiltration from University Directory Services Post-PeopleSoft Breach
suggestion.rationale: Article states breach targets 'Universities' with implicit data exfiltration; pipeline missed detection for lateral movement and data access patterns that follow initial exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After detection of CVE-2026-35273 exploitation, alert on unusual volume of LDAP queries or directory enumeration (T1087), followed by sequential access to student/employee record tables in PeopleSoft database (T1005). Flag encrypted outbound traffic on non-standard ports from compromised application server to external IP ranges not in university's approved egress list (T1041).

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from Compromised PeopleSoft Session
suggestion.rationale: Zero-day exploitation of user-facing system (PeopleSoft) typically yields session tokens or credentials; pipeline did not generate UC for credential access phase.
