suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for in-memory credential dumping (mimikatz, secretsdump) on PeopleSoft application servers post-compromise. Track for unusual PSAPPSRV process spawning shell interpreters (cmd.exe, powershell.exe) with parent process inconsistent with normal application flow. Flag repeated failed authentication attempts using credentials exfiltrated from memory.

suggestion.title: ShinyHunters Infrastructure Command & Control Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'ShinyHunters' as threat actor; pipeline failed to map actor to known IOCs (IP ranges, domains, ASNs) or detect C2 patterns associated with this group.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference observed outbound connections from compromised university networks against ShinyHunters' known C2 infrastructure (historical domains, bulletproof hosters, IP ranges from prior campaigns). Flag DNS queries to domains hosting ShinyHunters droppers or staging servers; inspect for encrypted payloads on anomalous ports consistent with group's historical tooling.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion: PeopleSoft Web Server Log Tampering or Deletion
suggestion.rationale: Zero-day exploits typically include log-clearing steps to evade audit trails; pipeline did not generate UC for defense evasion despite this being standard APT tradecraft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected deletion or modification of PeopleSoft web server logs (IIS logs, Weblogic access logs) immediately following successful RCE indicators. Alert on authenticated deletion of log files by SYSTEM account or unexpected service account permissions escalation. Track for batch file execution (del *.log) or PowerShell log clearing invocations from PeopleSoft process context.

suggestion.title: Ransomware Worm Self-Propagation via SMB Share Enumeration and Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article headline: 'Can Spread Like a Worm'—direct statement of lateral-movement capability. Should trigger detections for share enumeration + binary write + execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious net view, net share, Get-SmbShare, or dir \\\* commands followed by executable writes to UNC paths (\\\\[IP]\\share\\*.exe). Detect rapid lateral share enumeration across non-adjacent subnets or sustained write activity to removable media (.\\?\\ paths) with executable extensions.

suggestion.title: Bulk File Encryption with Ransom Note Drop
suggestion.rationale: Ransomware designation implies file encryption and ransom artifact drop (RANSOM.txt, _GENTLEMEN_DECRYPT_*.txt). Core impact IOC missing entirely from pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for high-volume file writes with suspicious extensions (.gentlemen, .locked, .crypt, etc.) in user directories (Documents, Desktop, shared folders) in conjunction with ransom note file creation. Correlate with process spawned from TEMP, %APPDATA%, %ProgramData% with no signed publisher. Alert on >500 file modifications in <5 minutes.

suggestion.title: Email-Based Worm Distribution with Macro or Executable Payload
suggestion.rationale: Worm capability typically propagates via phishing email with infected attachments. Initial-access vector missing from pipeline reconstruction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk inbound emails with .exe, .scr, .zip, .jar, or macro-enabled Office attachments (especially to external domains or mass recipient counts). Correlate with attachment execution and subsequent outbound email with similar payloads to organizational distribution lists or contact lists.

suggestion.title: Gentlemen Ransom Site and Payment Infrastructure Access
suggestion.rationale: 478 victims implies operational ransom payment site and leak portal. No C2 or infrastructure IOCs extracted; critical gap for threat tracking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Block/alert on DNS resolutions and HTTP/HTTPS connections to Gentlemen ransom site domains, payment portals, and leak-data URLs. Flag users clicking external links in phishing emails that resolve to threat-actor infrastructure; correlate with VPN access, credential entry, or file-staging activity.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Scheduled Task or Registry Persistence for Ransomware Binary
suggestion.rationale: Self-propagating worm should establish persistence to survive reboot and maintain presence. No persistence IOCs or techniques identified by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect schtasks /create, New-ScheduledTask, or Registry modifications (HKCU\\Software\\Microsoft\\Windows\\Run, HKLM\\System\\CurrentControlSet\\Services) with unsigned binary references from TEMP or %APPDATA%. Monitor for Registry operations with \\Gentlemen\\, \\ransom\\, or suspicious service names immediately after suspicious process execution.

suggestion.title: Gentlemen Ransomware Process Execution and Memory Injection Behavior
suggestion.rationale: RaaS operators typically use code injection, process hollowing, or UAC bypass. No execution/evasion IOCs surfaced; standard ransomware TTP.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unsigned .exe or .dll execution from TEMP, Downloads, ProgramData, or %APPDATA%\\Local\\Temp with command lines containing obfuscated PowerShell (-enc, -nop), rundll32, or regsvr32 with suspicious DLL paths. Flag parent-child process chains (explorer → cmd → powershell → ransom binary) typical of worm dropper chains.

suggestion.title: phpBB Authentication Bypass Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article headline explicitly states 'Auth Bypass + RCE Since 2014' — authentication bypass is the primary attack surface. Article describes 10-year-old vulnerability, suggesting pattern-based detection is feasible.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor phpBB instances for malformed authentication requests to sensitive endpoints (admin panel, token validation functions). Look for POST requests with unusual parameter combinations or missing CSRF tokens that succeed when they should fail, indicating auth validation bypass.

suggestion.title: RCE Payload Execution Post-phpBB Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'RCE' as explicit outcome of vulnerability chain. Attacker gains code execution after auth bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-exploitation: monitor for PHP process spawning shell commands (cmd.exe, /bin/bash) immediately following phpBB authentication events. Detect eval() or system() calls in web server context with payloads from web request parameters.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable phpBB Installation Detection via Banner Grabbing
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability affects specific phpBB versions since 2014. Article implies version-dependent exposure requiring enumeration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify phpBB version via HTTP response headers (X-Powered-By, Server version strings) and phpBB login page footers. Flag instances with version numbers in known-vulnerable ranges (likely 3.0.x–3.1.x based on 10-year timeline). Alert on probes to /install or /admin paths on unpatched instances.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Compromised phpBB Admin Account
suggestion.rationale: RCE + auth bypass grants attacker legitimate admin credentials. Article's scope ('thousands of forums') implies multi-forum infrastructure compromise potential.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After phpBB RCE detection, hunt for admin account activity (user creation, config changes, database exports) outside normal admin login patterns. Detect admin-level API/database queries originating from the web process rather than legitimate admin sessions.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Persistence in phpBB Directory
suggestion.rationale: RCE vulnerability enables attacker to write persistent backdoor. Article describes 'critical' 10-year exposure, implying production instances have been compromised.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor phpBB directories (/ext/, /cache/, /store/) for .php file creation or modification outside of legitimate update windows. Flag .php files with suspicious entropy (packed/obfuscated code). Detect HTTP requests to newly created .php files within minutes of creation.

suggestion.title: Database Exfiltration Post-phpBB RCE
suggestion.rationale: RCE grants database access. 'Millions of users across thousands of forums' suggests credential/PII at scale. Article implies compromise severity warrants exfiltration hunting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-RCE: monitor for unexpected database query volume (mysqldump, bulk SELECT), large data transfers to external IPs from web server, or compressed archive creation/transfer in phpBB root. Detect PHP processes executing database client tools with output redirection.

suggestion.title: JDY Botnet C2 Beaconing Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes active botnet expansion to 1,500+ devices; botnets require command & control communication. No C2 detection use case was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound connections from endpoints to known or suspected JDY C2 infrastructure. Alert on repeated DNS queries to malicious domains and HTTP/HTTPS callbacks to attacker-controlled servers, especially during non-business hours or from unexpected internal subnets.

suggestion.title: Host-Based Reconnaissance Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states purpose is 'cyber reconnaissance' across 1,500+ compromised devices. No process-level detection for enumeration/scanning commands was created.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation chains from JDY-infected hosts: cmd.exe or powershell.exe spawning reconnaissance tools (net.exe, ipconfig, systeminfo, tasklist) or making anomalous network connections to multiple destinations on scanner-typical ports (139, 445, 22, 3389).

suggestion.title: Network Reconnaissance Traffic Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: 1,500 devices performing reconnaissance will generate detectable network patterns (port scanning, failed connections, sequential probing). No network-level detection was suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect hosts initiating repeated connection attempts to sequential IP addresses, reserved ports, or non-responsive addresses. Flag internal scanning activity originating from endpoints not typically authorized for network enumeration.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Post-Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Reconnaissance-capable botnet infrastructure typically leads to lateral movement and deeper compromise. No detection for post-discovery movement was surfaced.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Windows administrative share access (\\target\IPC$, C$) from hosts previously flagged for reconnaissance activity. Alert on credential use on multiple hosts in short timespan following network discovery phase.

suggestion.title: JDY Botnet File / Hash Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Named botnet families have associated malware samples, hashes, and file paths. No file-based IOC detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file creation/execution matching known JDY sample hashes or file paths. Trigger alerts on first-instance hash matches or suspicious writes to system directories and startup locations. Coordinate with endpoint detection & response to isolate host.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Code Commit from Unexpected Device
suggestion.rationale: Title establishes 'the device is the only constant' — implies need to baseline and alert on commits from unfamiliar endpoints, especially if outside normal dev network. Core to securing distributed code-writing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag code commits to production-critical repos from devices not previously associated with the committer's account, especially if geographically distant or on public networks. Correlate with failed authentication attempts to catch credential theft.

suggestion.title: Repository Credential Exfiltration via Developer Machine
suggestion.rationale: Article posits device as attack surface when 'code is written everywhere' — developers' machines become prime targets for credentials (PATs, SSH keys, API tokens). Article phrase implies widespread exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect exfiltration of .ssh, .git/config, or token-storage files from dev machines. Alert on credential-manager access followed by network beaconing to non-corporate IP. Look for batch enumeration of repo secrets.

suggestion.title: Supply-Chain Code Poisoning via Compromised Developer Commit
suggestion.rationale: If 'code is written everywhere' on diverse devices, a compromised dev machine introduces tainted code to the supply chain. Pipeline should detect: commits with unusual file additions (backdoors, miners), commits that bypass code review, or commits that alter build/deployment configs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for commits that add binaries to source control, introduce shell/script execution in build configs, or create new privileged accounts in Terraform/IaC files. Correlate with committer's location/device baseline. Alert if code-review is bypassed via privilege abuse.

suggestion.title: Anomalous CI/CD Pipeline Execution from Unknown Trigger
suggestion.rationale: Distributed code-writing implies CI/CD pipelines triggered from multiple locations/devices. Detect unauthorized or anomalous trigger points (manual runs from unusual accounts, environment variables modified by non-ops).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on CI/CD pipeline executions triggered by developer accounts outside normal business hours, or from devices/locations not previously associated with infrastructure personnel. Flag environment variable modifications in pipelines that alter deployment targets.

suggestion.title: Insider Threat: Developer Account Lateral Movement Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article's premise — device as constant across multiple environments — implies an insider or compromised dev could pivot across dev, staging, and production. Detect cross-environment access using same credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag developer accounts accessing production systems outside their normal role scope, especially if from a personal device. Correlate repo access (staging branch) with immediate production-environment login. Alert on service-account credential usage from dev machines.

suggestion.title: Secrets Committed to Repository by Unvetted Device
suggestion.rationale: When code is written everywhere on personal/unsecured devices, secrets (API keys, tokens, credentials) leak into repos. Article's framing implies this is a pervasive risk vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Real-time detection of secret patterns (AWS keys, private keys, tokens) in code commits. Alert if secrets are committed by accounts outside the application-team roster, or from devices that haven't previously committed. Auto-revoke exposed secrets within SLA.

suggestion.title: Malicious Rust Crate Installation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Compromised Rust crate onering performs code exfiltration'—attack vector is direct package installation; pipeline must detect cargo install/add commands referencing malicious crate.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on cargo install, cargo add, or cargo build commands explicitly referencing 'onering' crate. Monitor Cargo.toml for suspicious dependency additions from non-primary registries. Flag first-time installations of recently-published package versions.

suggestion.title: Code Exfiltration via Malicious Build Script Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states crate 'performs code exfiltration'—malicious Rust packages execute via build.rs scripts; pipeline should detect unauthorized egress during build phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor network connections initiated by rustc, cargo, or build.rs processes for large data transfers to non-whitelisted destinations. Alert on curl/wget/http POST from build directories. Flag DNS queries for geolocation or analytics services during compilation.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Process Execution from Rust Build Context
suggestion.rationale: Rust crate attacks execute via build.rs (Cargo build scripts) and proc macros; pipeline should detect child processes spawned with network capability from build phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes spawned during cargo build with command-line arguments containing network utilities (curl, wget, nc). Flag powershell/bash execution from build.rs context. Alert on proc_macro execution with file I/O or environment variable tampering.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Package Repository Integrity Violation
suggestion.rationale: Core attack: supply-chain compromise; pipeline should flag malicious crates via hash/version mismatch or installation from non-primary registries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Cargo.lock vs Cargo.toml mismatches. Alert on failed signature validation, fallback to alternative registries, or installation of unpinned dependency versions. Flag crates with unusual publish velocity or permissions (filesystem, network access).

suggestion.title: JWT Signing with Hardcoded Secret 'random'
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'AUTH_JWT_SECRET=random — template default shipped to all users' (dev.env line 10). Detection should identify JWTs cryptographically signed with this known weak secret or claims with impossible timestamps indicating forgery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag bearer tokens in requests where JWT signature validation against the literal string 'random' succeeds, or tokens with far-future exp claims paired with admin endpoint access. Alternatively, decode tokens and alert on aud/iss fields consistent with go-base boilerplate.

suggestion.title: Deployment of Vulnerable github.com/dhax/go-base Package
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 1,685-star boilerplate as CVE-2026-48031 vector. Supply-chain detection should flag go.mod/go.sum imports or container images bundling this package.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect go.mod files referencing github.com/dhax/go-base in source repos or deployed container images. Cross-check against known-vulnerable version range. Escalate if running instances are exposed to untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: Hardcoded Secrets in Dev Config Files
suggestion.rationale: Article describes AUTH_JWT_SECRET persisted in dev.env shipped with boilerplate. Should detect secrets (API keys, tokens, passphrases) committed to version control or baked into images.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify commits touching .env, config.yaml, or similar template files where secret variables are assigned templated/weak defaults (e.g., 'random', 'test', 'changeme'). Flag merges to main/prod branches.

suggestion.title: Admin Endpoint Access via Forged Credentials Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article's UC identifies /api/v1/admin/users as exploitation target. Should detect high-volume or anomalous admin access following initial token forgery, indicating lateral movement or data exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate bearer-token 200-status responses to admin endpoints with user entity behavior baselines. Alert if a source IP or account suddenly accesses /api/v1/admin/users multiple times in short windows, or at hours inconsistent with normal admin activity.

suggestion.title: Malicious protocolMessage payload delivery and processing
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker 'can be sent a malicious payload via the placeholderResendMessage' but pipeline provides no hunt for payload receipt or processing. This is the execution phase of the exploit.

Correlate with subsequent messages.upsert callbacks.

suggestion.title: Spoofed message detection via messages.upsert anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article states exploit 'trigger a fake messages.upsert event with a fake message key and payload' but no hunt covers event validation or signature consistency.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect messages.upsert events where the message key cryptographic fingerprint fails to match the message body hash, sender ID is not in authenticated contact list, or timestamp precedes the network packet arrival time by >1s.

suggestion.title: App state database corruption indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacker can 'corrupt the app state sync system' but provides no hunt for integrity anomalies in the backing store.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Baileys SQLite/JSON state store for write operations lacking corresponding incoming sync protocol messages, schema validation failures, or state rollback patterns without user action.

suggestion.title: Runtime Baileys version detection via process introspection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerable versions < 6.7.22 and < 7.0.0-rc12; file-based discovery alone misses patched source overwritten by unpatched runtime loads. Process heap can reveal actual loaded module version.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Extract Baileys package.json version string from running Node.js process memory or require() module cache. Compare against known vulnerable ranges independent of disk artifacts.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Attempt Detection for Ivanti/Fortinet/SAP Critical CVEs
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Multiple Critical Vulnerabilities' with patches released by three major vendors. Exploitation detection is the canonical use case for patch advisory articles—title phrase alone establishes need.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Privilege Escalation Activity

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-5027 Langflow Exploitation Attempt Detection

No hunt for identifying ransom notes, email templates, or communication with victims. Article phrase: 'compromise-and-extortion campaign...attributed to the notorious threat actor UNC6240, also known as ShinyHunters'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for newly created files matching ransom-note naming conventions (e.g., INSTRUCTIONS.txt, README.txt, _RESTORE_*.txt) on accessible shares. Monitor email for outbound communications to internal addresses mentioning 'restoration,' 'recovery,' or 'negotiation.' Check for file modifications in home directories or public shares.

suggestion.title: Coinminer Process Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article lists Win.Worm.Coinminer::1201 as most prevalent malware with SHA256 9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507 and filename VID001.exe. Requires both file-based and behavioral detection as worm spreads via multiple vectors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process execution matching hash 9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507 or filename VID001.exe. Correlate with sustained high CPU usage, crypto-mining pool C2 connections, or recursive worm-like process spawning patterns.

suggestion.title: Code Injector Variant Detection via Memory Behavior
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies W32.Injector:Gen.21ie.1201 (SHA256 96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974) as prevalent malware class requiring post-execution behavioral analysis since signature evasion is common.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for remote code injection into system processes (svchost.exe, lsass.exe, winlogon.exe) via CreateRemoteThread or NtWriteVirtualMemory APIs. Alert on suspicious unsigned DLL loads into privileged processes or memory writes followed by process resumption.

suggestion.title: VPN Exploit Post-Compromise Activity Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'CISA gives U.S. federal agencies three days to fix a VPN bug under attack by Qilin,' establishing active exploitation chain requiring behavioral detection since initial access will succeed on unpatched systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline VPN service process behavior. Alert on process spawning from VPN service context (especially cmd.exe, powershell.exe, whoami, net), lateral movement attempts (PsExec, WMI), or file encryption activity. Monitor for ransom note file creation.

suggestion.title: Social Engineering Attack Delivery via Messaging Apps
suggestion.rationale: Article reports 'WhatsApp catches spyware firm NSO defying no-hacking court order' with 'social engineering attack that attempted to trick users into clicking on malicious links,' requiring behavioral link-click detection and post-click investigation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for user clicks on obfuscated URLs, shortened links, or domains spoofing legitimate security alert pages (especially WhatsApp-themed) within messaging apps. Correlate clicks with subsequent login anomalies (unusual location, device, time) within 24 hours.

suggestion.title: Zero-Day Exploitation Behavioral Baseline Violations
suggestion.rationale: Article cites Talos blog on AI vulnerability discovery 'completely outpaced human patching capabilities' with zero-days exploited 'in minutes.' Signature-based detection is insufficient; behavioral baselines and anomaly detection are the primary defense.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Deploy EDR focused on post-exploitation behavioral anomalies: unexpected shell spawning (cmd.exe, powershell.exe from unusual parents), unusual child process chains, memory-based attacks, and unsigned module loading from unexpected directories. Flag deviations from baseline within minutes of unusual network activity to CVE-vulnerable services.

suggestion.title: AI-Generated False Negatives in Vulnerability Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly frames 'AI Broke Vulnerability Management' — suggests AI tools are systematically missing vulnerabilities or producing unreliable risk scores. Pipeline should detect discussion of failed detection mechanisms or unpatched flaws that escaped AI-powered scanners.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for vulnerability scanner output anomalies or security teams reporting discrepancies between AI risk ratings and actual exploit success. Look for patch delays following failed detection cycles or reclassification of vulnerabilities after initial misassessment.

suggestion.title: Exploit-of-Undetected-Vuln Post-VM Failure
suggestion.rationale: Title implies CISOs are shifting budget away from traditional VM due to AI tool failures. This suggests real exploits are succeeding against flaws the AI-driven systems missed. Pipeline should reconstruct exploitation chains targeting undetected vulnerabilities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful exploitation attempts with gaps between vulnerability inventory snapshots. Flag anomalous network connections or process executions on assets marked as compliant by AI scanning tools but later confirmed vulnerable.

suggestion.title: BAS (Breach & Attack Simulation) Traffic from New Tooling
suggestion.rationale: Article title mentions CISOs moving budget to BAS as an alternative. This implies BAS platforms may be deployed to compensate for VM failures. Pipeline should identify IOCs or network behaviors associated with BAS frameworks (e.g., Rapid7, Cymulate, Microsoft DART) and their legitimate scanning patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baselines for authorized BAS tool communications and scanning patterns. Alert on anomalous timing or scope changes in BAS sweeps, or cross-contamination where BAS-generated payloads escape containment and reach production systems.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Asset Exposure Hunt (CVE-2026-10520)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable'—foundational to initial access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances reachable from untrusted networks via port scanning and certificate/banner analysis. Correlate exposed instances against vulnerability scan data to flag unpatched deployments, especially those not protected by mTLS or restricted HTTPS noted in article.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload Detection in HTTP Logs
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector is explicitly 'OS command injection vulnerability'—HTTP request bodies/parameters must contain shell metacharacters (|, &, ;, backticks, $()) or command substitution patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints containing Unix/shell metacharacters or known command injection patterns. Baseline legitimate admin activity; flag both blocked and unblocked attempts to Sentry-specific paths.

suggestion.title: Root-level Process Spawning from Ivanti Sentry Daemon
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'root-level remote code execution' as outcome. Endpoint logs must show unexpected child processes (shells, scripts, network tools) spawned from Sentry processes with UID 0.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child process creation where parent is Ivanti Sentry (sentry daemon, Java/tomcat processes) running as root. Flag any interactive shells, interpreters, curl/wget, or reverse-shell payloads spawned this way.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Remediation Tracking
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status + federal patch due date (2026-06-14) makes this the highest remediation priority. Scanning output is the primary preventive control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset management and vulnerability scanners for Ivanti Sentry instances with CVE-2026-10520 confirmed present or unfixed. Escalate any unpatched asset beyond the federal due date immediately.

suggestion.title: Atypical External HTTP Requests to Sentry Admin Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'remote unauthenticated' exploitation path, meaning HTTP endpoints are directly exposed and probed. New external sources requesting admin/API paths warrant investigation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP/HTTPS requests from external/non-whitelisted sources to Ivanti Sentry admin, API, or management endpoints. Flag unusual user-agents, methods (PUT, DELETE), or request frequencies that deviate from baseline legitimate admin access.

suggestion.title: Access token exfiltration in HTTP response body from /mcp endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article title emphasizes 'Leaks Operator Meta Access Token' but all provided detections assume token exfil *after* reaching graph.facebook.com. The primary signal is the token appearing in the MCP response itself during unauthenticated request. Article phrase: 'Unauthenticated HTTP MCP Tool Execution Leaks Operator Meta Access Token.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect HTTP response bodies from processes listening on TCP 8080 (/mcp path) for patterns matching Meta access token format (long alphanumeric strings with underscores/hyphens, typically 100–200 chars). Alert on token-pattern in response paired with absent/empty Authorization header in request. This is the core vulnerability trigger.

suggestion.title: POST requests to /mcp without Authorization or Bearer token header
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is explicitly 'Unauthenticated' (CWE-287). No provided UC explicitly checks for absence of auth headers on /mcp requests. Legitimate MCP clients will include proper Authorization headers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP POST to */mcp* on port 8080 where Authorization header is missing or empty AND HTTP response code is 2xx. Baseline and alert on clean outliers from established MCP client patterns. This directly operationalizes the 'unauthenticated' vulnerability.

suggestion.title: Suspicious MCP tool invocation via JSON payload to /mcp endpoint
suggestion.rationale: MCP protocol exchanges tool-invocation instructions via JSON. Article mentions 'MCP Tool Execution' but no detection looks inside POST body for tool names or suspicious payloads. Token exfiltration happens via tool response.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse JSON in POST bodies to /mcp endpoint; extract 'tool', 'method', or 'action' fields. Alert on sensitive-data tools (e.g., 'get_access_token', 'list_credentials', 'export_config'). Requires HTTP body inspection capability.

suggestion.title: Lateral movement via stolen Meta access token into ad-account modification
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1098.001 (Account Manipulation: Additional Cloud Credentials) as follow-on technique. After stealing token via MCP vulnerability, attacker pivots to modify ad-account permissions or create new admins in victim's Meta workspace.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Meta Graph API calls for account-modification operations (add_admin, update_account_settings, modify_roles, create_campaign) initiated by unusual or service-account API clients. Correlate with previously-leaked access tokens or POST activity to /mcp endpoints.

suggestion.title: Child process spawning from PHP interpreter in web-writable directory
suggestion.rationale: Article describes uploaded shell.php executing—'uploaded file named `shell.php` containing GIF-like content' with implied command execution. The execution of the shell after upload (via T1059 / T1505.003) is the end-goal but not explicitly detected by the three provided UCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect php.exe, php-fpm, or httpd spawning child processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, etc.) where the parent process image or working directory is under /uploads/, /writable/, /avatar, or /public/uploads. Web shells typically spawn reverse shells or data-exfil tools immediately after instantiation.

suggestion.title: Validation rule bypass: file extension mismatch on write to upload directory
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability: 'checked the MIME-derived guessed extension instead of the client-provided filename extension.' This is a defense-evasion technique (T1036.008) where the attacker exploits the validation logic itself. Detecting the actual file write with mismatched MIME type and dangerous extension.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation events where the file extension (php, phtml, phar, inc, phps) is present in the filename AND the parent HTTP request Content-Type header indicated a benign type (image/*, text/plain). Requires correlation of HTTP traffic with file creation events within <2 seconds of POST.

suggestion.title: Repeated failed uploads followed by successful PHP-in-uploads access
suggestion.rationale: Attack flow: attacker tries variations of the bypass, some fail validation, then succeeds and accesses the shell. The article states bypass was achieved, implying previous attempts may have failed. Detecting the attack progression.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for sequences where POST to /upload* returns 4xx for multiple requests (validation reject), then a subsequent POST returns 2xx (bypass succeeds), followed within seconds by GET to the same upload directory path with .php extension and 2xx response. Three-event correlation suggests active exploitation.

suggestion.title: npm Install Script Execution from Untrusted Sources
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'will turn off automatic execution of installation scripts by default, one of the most commonly abused mechanisms in malicious [packages]' — directly identifies the attack vector: postinstall/preinstall/postuninstall hooks executing code during npm install.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for node/npm processes spawning shells (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash) or making unexpected network connections during package installation. Detect postinstall/preinstall script definitions in package manifests that invoke shell interpreters. Alert on script execution from ~/.npm cache or node_modules directories.

suggestion.title: npm Package Manifest Script Abuse Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes that installation scripts are 'commonly abused mechanisms' — need to detect and inspect package.json scripts before execution, especially in CI/CD pipelines.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag npm packages where postinstall/preinstall/postuninstall scripts contain shell metacharacters, network utilities (curl, wget, nc), or privilege escalation attempts. Correlate script changes in dependency updates with package publish dates and author reputation signals.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Typosquatting and Masquerading
suggestion.rationale: Article frames supply-chain risk as 'commonly abused mechanisms' — typosquatting is a primary npm attack vector used to deliver malicious install scripts to victim environments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for installations of packages with names similar to popular npm modules (typosquatting: 'lodash-utils' vs 'lodash', 'requests-http' vs 'request'). Alert on first-time-published packages installed in production environments. Track package version downgrades or unusual version jumps.

suggestion.title: npm Registry Authentication Anomaly and Account Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks often involve compromised maintainer accounts publishing malicious versions; article's context implies need to detect unauthorized package updates.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm package publishes from unusual IP addresses, geographic anomalies, or off-hours for known maintainers. Monitor for rapid version bumps without corresponding git commits. Alert on script changes in patch/minor versions (unusual engineering pattern).

suggestion.title: Execution of npm Install-Time Scripts
suggestion.rationale: Article title 'GitHub to Disable npm Install Scripts by Default' explicitly establishes that install/postinstall hooks currently execute and are weaponizable. Pipeline should detect when npm spawns postinstall/preinstall/prepare script interpreters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm.exe or node.exe spawning shell interpreters (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, sh) with arguments matching npm lifecycle hooks. Focus on unexpected child processes and unusual command arguments during install phases.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Source or Metadata
suggestion.rationale: Article subtitle identifies 'Supply Chain Attacks' targeting npm registry. Pipeline should detect installation of packages with suspicious provenance, reputation, or behavioral anomalies that indicate compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install logs for newly published packages, packages with abnormal version jumps, packages from unexpected registries, or packages whose dependencies deviate from historical baselines.

suggestion.title: Bypass of npm Script Execution Controls
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes GitHub's default-disable as a protective measure. Pipeline should detect attempts to override this via npm flags, environment variables, or config overrides (e.g., --legacy-peer-deps, ignore-scripts=false).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm invocations with flags that re-enable script execution or disable security checks. Monitor npm config commands targeting script execution policies, especially in automated contexts.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Child Process from npm Installation
suggestion.rationale: Threat model: npm scripts run arbitrary code. Pipeline should detect unexpected children (network utilities, file modifiers, shell re-invocations) spawned under npm process context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Build process trees from npm parent. Baseline should exclude only legitimate npm/node children. Flag: curl/wget, powershell -Download, file modification outside node_modules, privilege escalation attempts.

suggestion.title: Network Anomaly from npm Process
suggestion.rationale: Malicious npm scripts can exfiltrate data or reach C2. Pipeline should detect unexpected outbound connections from npm/node processes during installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound connections initiated by npm.exe/node.exe or their children during install phases. Flag unusual ports, residential IP targets, high-volume egress, or known C2 domains.

suggestion.title: PE Overlay Execution — Abnormal Section Alignment / Entropy Spike
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly emphasizes 'massive PE overlay' as the obfuscation mechanism, but no detection addresses overlay detection. Article states 'what makes it stand out is...how effective a simple trick has made it' referring to the PE overlay technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Go-compiled PE files with abnormal section sizes (e.g., .rsrc or .data sections vastly larger than expected) or raw overlay data appended after the certificate table. Monitor for execution of binaries with entropy analysis flagging high-entropy payload in overlay sections. Cross-correlate with Go binary signatures (common in GoFlateLoader samples).

suggestion.title: Loader → Payload Spawn Chain — Secondary Process from Obfuscated Parent
suggestion.rationale: Article describes loader's function as 'decode and drop dangerous information-stealing programs.' Pipeline lacks detection for the decode-then-execute behavior that distinguishes loader malware from single-stage infostealers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process spawning chains where a parent process (attributed to GoFlateLoader via hash or behavioral IOC) creates child processes matching Lumma, Vidar, or StealC MITRE pattern (rapid file writes to temp, followed by process creation with unusual command lines or unsigned binaries). Flag low-prevalence parent-child pairs where parent is not a known application (browser, Office, etc.).

suggestion.title: Go-compiled Binary Execution with Anomalous File I/O
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies GoFlateLoader as Go-based. Payloads (Lumma, Vidar, StealC) perform file I/O against browser credential stores. Pipeline did not suggest detection for Go runtime-specific indicators or rapid credential-store access from loader.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate process execution of Go-compiled binaries (Go runtime artifacts, specific IAT imports) with rapid sequential file access to Chrome/Firefox/Edge credential paths within seconds. Filter out browser processes. Alert on clusters of >3 credential-store file accesses within a 10-second window from non-browser parents.

suggestion.title: User Execution of Suspicious PE Overlay Binary
suggestion.rationale: Article does not explicitly state delivery method, but loaders are typically delivered via phishing/drive-by download. Users must execute GoFlateLoader for the chain to begin. No UC for detecting user-initiated execution of suspicious files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect user-initiated execution of recently-downloaded executables from Downloads or Desktop folders, where the binary is a Go-compiled PE with abnormal file size or overlay characteristics. Correlate with user click-through on email links or web-based download prompts. Alert if binary hash is not in known-good application manifests.

suggestion.title: Phishing credential submission to attacker-controlled domain
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes SniperDz as credential-harvesting platform ('credential theft', 'PhaaS toolkit'); pipeline missed detection for the actual harvest step. Should detect browser HTTP POST with form fields (email/password/ssn) submitted to IOC domains post-click.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate phishing-link click to HTTP POST requests with credential-like field names (username, password, email, ssn, card) to attacker IOC domains within 5-10 minutes. High-fidelity because legitimate users rarely submit credentials to unknown domains post-phishing click.

suggestion.title: Brand account compromise on social media (brand impersonation pattern)
suggestion.rationale: Article title and body highlight 'Brand Impersonation' as core attack objective, with distribution via 'Facebook and Instagram'. Pipeline did not surface account-creation or account-takeover detection for social platforms. Existing hunts focus on email/endpoint, missing social-media supply chain.
log_sources: Social media API logs / SIEM integrations
Threat intel feeds for brand/lookalike account discovery
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for new social media accounts using brand names/logos, particularly those posting phishing links or credential-harvesting content. Correlate account creation IP/device to known attacker infrastructure (IOC list). Alerts on multiple accounts registered to same email/phone/payment method.

suggestion.title: Browser hijacking artifacts (DNS redirect / proxy injection / homepage override)
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly mentions 'Browser Hijacking' but body is truncated; this attack vector is entirely undetected by the three reference hunts. Should monitor for browser settings tampering, proxy/PAC file injection, or DNS resolution anomalies consistent with traffic interception.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect registry writes to Internet Explorer/Edge homepage/search page settings, browser extension installations from unsigned sources, DNS config changes to non-ISP servers, or PAC file injection from suspicious paths. Correlate to phishing-click timeline.

suggestion.title: PowerShell encoded payload execution from browser context
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1059.001 (PowerShell) and T1059.005 (Visual Basic) but pipeline missed specific pattern: encoded/obfuscated PowerShell spawned within 60s of phishing click. This is signature behavior for PhaaS payload delivery (inline scripts or downloaded via IEX/Invoke-WebRequest).
log_sources: PowerShell Script Block Logging (Windows Event ID 4104)
Sysmon Event ID 1 (ProcessCreate with encoded command args)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect powershell.exe or pwsh.exe spawned from browser/email parent with encoded/obfuscated command arguments (base64, -enc flag, DownloadString, Invoke-Expression). High confidence if parent process is browser that received phishing link in preceding 120 seconds.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Command Injection Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'OS command injection weakness' being actively exploited against Internet-exposed instances. Need to detect malicious payload delivery at network/application layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry HTTP access logs for requests containing shell metacharacters (|, ;, $(), backticks, redirection operators) in parameter values. Legitimate administrative traffic to Sentry does not require these. Cross-correlate proxy and WAF logs for same indicators.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution from Sentry Service Account
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers achieve 'execute code with root privileges' via command injection. Must detect unexpected root-level child processes spawned from Sentry service during active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes spawned by Ivanti Sentry service accounts (Mobile_Iris, sentry, or similar) with unexpected parent processes or launching shells, scripting interpreters, or system utilities as root. Normal Sentry operation limited to specific maintenance tasks; anomalies indicate successful exploitation.

suggestion.title: Sentry Persistence Mechanism Detection (Backdoor Accounts/Cron/Startup)
suggestion.rationale: Shadowserver reported 'backdoored most of the Sentry gateways exposed online'. Persistence installation must be detected post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry instances for creation of new local user accounts, new cron/at scheduled jobs, modifications to /etc/rc.* or systemd startup files, and unexpected SSH key additions. Establish baseline of legitimate Sentry accounts; any new additions post-patch likely indicate attacker persistence installation.

suggestion.title: Internet-Exposed Ivanti Sentry Admin Portal Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Internet-exposed secure mobile gateways' as primary attack vector and misconfiguration enabling initial access to vulnerable versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Continuously monitor for Ivanti Sentry admin portals reachable from untrusted networks. Expected: Sentry accessible only from corporate networks and approved partners. Unexpected: admin interface responding to scans from public IP space, successful authentications from external origins, or service banners visible in external asset databases.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Reconnaissance Activity from Compromised Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article describes Sentry as 'entry point into targets' enterprise networks' enabling attacker access to corporate systems. Post-compromise reconnaissance must be detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor egress traffic from Sentry for scanning patterns: multiple connections to different IPs/ports in short timeframe, probing to unexpected internal subnets, or rapid failed connection attempts. Baseline normal Sentry traffic to authentication and backend systems. Post-compromise reconnaissance exhibits broad exploration inconsistent with normal operations.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Sensitive Data Access Following Sentry Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article states compromised gateway enables 'theft of sensitive customer and corporate data' from backend systems accessible via Sentry. Impact phase data access spikes must be detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Sentry compromise timestamp with spike in data access from systems typically accessed through gateway. Flag bulk exports, unusual service accounts accessing sensitive assets, large transfers to non-standard destinations, or access patterns inconsistent with normal mobile-device-mediated use.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Creation in Source Control Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes detection via 'suspicious files' on developer machines; malware targeting developers often stages payloads in .git, node_modules, or package manager caches. No UC was generated despite this being the article's core claim.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation or modification in .git/, node_modules/, .npm/, .cargo/, or .maven/ directories with file extensions not typical to those directories (e.g., .exe, .ps1, .sh in node_modules). Cross-reference with process parent (npm install, git clone) to baseline legitimate activity.

suggestion.title: Unsigned or Mismatched Code Signing on Developer Tools
suggestion.rationale: Miasma and Hades likely spread via trojanized or unsigned binaries. Article title references 'suspicious files' but no IOC extraction occurred. Developer machines are prime targets for signed-binary attacks or unsigned runner scripts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of files in developer tool paths (C:\Program Files\nodejs, %USERPROFILE%\AppData\npm, /usr/local/bin) that lack valid Microsoft or vendor signatures, or whose signature thumbprint changed between first and subsequent executions.

suggestion.title: PowerShell/CMD Invocation from Package Manager or Source Control Contexts
suggestion.rationale: Malware spreading via developer toolchains (npm, cargo, git hooks) would likely trigger shell interpretation. Pipeline missed command-execution indicator entirely despite 'suspicious files' emphasis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when powershell.exe, cmd.exe, or sh spawned as child of npm.cmd, node.exe, git.exe, or other package-manager processes with command lines containing Base64 encoding, environment variable obfuscation, or network connectivity patterns.

suggestion.title: Registry Persistence via Run Keys from Unexpected Parent Process
suggestion.rationale: Developer-machine malware must persist; no kill-chain phase captured persistence mechanisms. Article context suggests long-dwell threats but no persistence detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect registry writes to HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run or HKCU equivalents where the parent process is npm.cmd, node.exe, python.exe, or git.exe—processes not normally associated with registry modification for persistence.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Developer Machine to Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Developer machines infected with Miasma/Hades pose supply-chain risk to internal infrastructure. Article does not show this was extracted, but threat context implies post-compromise lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on SMB or RDP connections originating from developer machines to non-developer infrastructure (build servers, artifact repositories, CI/CD runners) initiated by unexpected processes or at unusual times.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Source Code or Credentials via Network from Developer Machine
suggestion.rationale: Developer machines host source code and secrets; no exfiltration detection mapped. Article's 'developer machines' context implies code or credential theft as end goal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk reads of .git, .ssh, .aws, or source files followed by outbound HTTPS/DNS to non-whitelisted domains, or compression of source directories followed by network transmission outside work hours.

suggestion.title: Code Execution from AI Agent Process Context
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacks 'trick OpenClaw AI Agent into running code'—direct RCE is the primary attack impact. Pipeline generated zero execution-phase detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect interpreter spawning (bash, sh, cmd, python, powershell) from AI agent parent process or with AI agent in execution context. Flag on unusual command arguments, encoded payloads, or parent-child relationships inconsistent with normal OpenClaw operation.

suggestion.title: Credential/Secret Access and Exfiltration from AI Agent
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'leaking secrets' but pipeline missed all credential-access and exfiltration-phase detection. No rules for environment variable reads, secret manager API calls, or data egress.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for secret/credential file access (e.g. ~/.ssh, /etc/passwd, cloud credential stores) originating from AI agent. Detect high-entropy or credential-formatted data exfiltration from agent network sockets or API calls.

suggestion.title: Prompt Injection / Adversarial Input to AI Agent
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: 'trick[ing] OpenClaw into...' implies malicious prompt injection. Pipeline has zero initial-access detections for adversarial AI prompts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor API calls to OpenClaw agent for prompt payloads containing: system instruction overrides, jailbreak keywords (e.g. 'ignore previous', 'as an AI you must'), code-execution directives in backticks or markup, or role-play attempts to escape guardrails. Flag anomalous token patterns or multi-stage prompt sequences.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Plugin/Tool Invocation by AI Agent
suggestion.rationale: Compromised AI agents may be tricked into invoking dangerous plugins (OS commands, file I/O, network). Article describes behavioral manipulation but pipeline missed function-call detection angle.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect plugin or tool invocations from OpenClaw that violate baseline: calls to OS-level tools (subprocess, exec, system), cross-service APIs, file-system access, or network I/O plugins when normal operation uses curated APIs only. Flag rapid/repeated plugin switching or deprecated/disabled plugins.

suggestion.title: Recovery Partition XML File Modification Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states exploit 'bypasses Windows BitLocker via Recovery Partition XML Files'—the primary attack surface. Pipeline failed to generate any detection baseline for this core vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious creation or modification of XML files in WinRE/recovery partition paths (\\?\GLOBALROOT\Device\HarddiskVolume*\Recovery, System Volume Information\Recovery). Alert on XML file writes from non-system processes (user-mode executables, scripts) or outside normal maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: BitLocker Encryption State Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Title states exploit 'bypasses Windows BitLocker'—directly indicates T1562.002 (Impair Defenses) phase. Pipeline produced no detection for encryption-state tampering, WMI calls to Win32_EncryptableVolume, or manage-bde.exe anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect WMI Win32_EncryptableVolume method calls, registry modifications under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\fvevol, or manage-bde.exe execution with suspend/disable flags outside maintenance. Correlate with unexpected recovery key queries or TPM bypass patterns.

suggestion.title: System Utility XML Parsing Baseline Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Attack mechanism centered on XML file exploitation in recovery partition; no detection use case captures XML parsing by msiexec.exe, powershell.exe, or rundll32.exe from non-standard paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on system utilities (msiexec.exe, powershell.exe, wscript.exe, rundll32.exe) executing with command lines referencing recovery partition paths or XML files in \\?\GLOBALROOT or System Volume Information. Baseline normal WinRE maintenance parsing and flag behavioral deviations.

suggestion.title: Elevated Recovery Partition File Access from User Process
suggestion.rationale: Exploiting recovery partition XML requires privilege escalation or SYSTEM-level access. Title emphasizes recovery partition as attack surface; pipeline did not surface privilege-boundary-crossing detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor non-SYSTEM, non-kernel-driver processes attempting file I/O on \\?\GLOBALROOT\Device\HarddiskVolume* or System Volume Information\Recovery.
