suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all installed LangGraph versions in Python environments across agents. Alert on versions matching published vulnerable ranges or security advisory thresholds.

suggestion.title: Deserialization Payload Detection in Agent Input
suggestion.rationale: RCE flaws in Python-based frameworks commonly stem from pickle/cloudpickle/YAML unsafe deserialization. Article title's 'flaw chain' suggests serialization as likely attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor LangGraph graph inputs and state objects for serialized payloads (pickle, cloudpickle, YAML, JSON) containing suspicious imports (os, subprocess, builtins) or exec/eval constructs.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized File Operations from Compromised Agent Process
suggestion.rationale: RCE typically manifests as file writes (shells, backdoors). Pipeline missed impact-phase detection for suspicious file IO.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation/modification from LangGraph/agent processes outside whitelisted directories. Flag writes to /tmp, startup paths, web-accessible directories, or system binaries.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Network Egress from Self-Hosted Agent
suggestion.rationale: Compromised agents could exfiltrate data or establish reverse shells. Article's 'remote code execution' scenario includes post-exploitation C2 or data theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor egress from agent host IPs to unexpected external IPs/ports, especially on high-numbered ports or to known C2 infrastructure. Baseline normal outbound connectivity first.

suggestion.title: Office RCE Exploitation — Process Crash and Memory Corruption Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'memory-safety flaws in the Word rendering engine and its integration with Outlook Classic' causing RCE. This is the primary exploitation mechanism but no use case was generated. Rendering engine crashes are the immediate indicator of exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Outlook (outlook.exe) and Word (winword.exe) processes for crashes, access violations, heap corruption exceptions, or abnormal terminations. Memory-safety vulnerabilities manifest as structured exception handling events. Correlate with recent document opens or email delivery timestamps to isolate exploitation from legitimate usage.

suggestion.title: Malicious Office Attachment Delivery and Exploitation Chain
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector flows through Office document delivery: external email with attachment → document open → rendering engine crash → code execution. Article describes this flow implicitly ('RCE vulnerabilities in Microsoft Outlook and Word') but no use case captures the complete chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequence: Office attachment (.docx, .doc, .xls, .ppt) from external sender → recipient opens document in Outlook/Word → process crash or abnormal child spawning within 5 seconds. Prioritize external/untrusted senders and correlate email delivery metadata with endpoint process telemetry.

suggestion.title: Command and Script Execution from Office Application Context
suggestion.rationale: RCE vulnerabilities enable arbitrary code execution post-exploitation. Article explicitly describes RCE capability but no detection proposed for command execution spawning—the attacker's primary goal once rendering engine is compromised.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag child processes spawned by Outlook or Word with high confidence: shell interpreters (cmd.exe, powershell.exe), scripting engines (cscript.exe, mshta.exe), execution utilities (rundll32.exe, regsvcs.exe), or LOLBins (certutil.exe, bitsadmin.exe). Office applications do not legitimately spawn these children under normal operation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Office Document File Characteristics and Payloads
suggestion.rationale: Memory-safety exploits in rendering engines require crafted malicious documents with specific payloads or malformed structure to trigger the vulnerability. Article attributes RCE to rendering engine flaws but pipeline generated no detection for document-level anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Office documents with suspicious characteristics: malformed document structure, unusual OLE objects, suspicious embedded fonts, ActiveX controls, VBA macros in unexpected files, or entropy anomalies. Cross-reference with email metadata (external sender, unusual recipient patterns, suspicious subject lines).

suggestion.title: Oracle PeopleSoft CVE-2026-35273 exploitation attempt detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'active compromise' via 'unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability.' No use case targets the initial-access exploit delivery despite this being the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST/GET requests to Oracle PeopleSoft URIs with malicious payloads (oversized parameters, SQL injection patterns, serialized Java objects). Correlate with unexpected process spawning (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash) from PeopleSoft application pools or psadmin services.

suggestion.title: Data exfiltration from compromised PeopleSoft databases
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'compromise-and-extortion campaign,' indicating attacker exfiltrated sensitive data before ransom demand. No detection covers data staging or bulk transfer phases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for large outbound data transfers (>100 MB) from PeopleSoft servers to the eight attacker IPs or azurenetfiles.net. Alert on SFTP/HTTP uploads of database backup files or archive formats from PSADMIN_USER or application service accounts.

suggestion.title: Command-and-control beaconing to ShinyHunters infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article lists eight tactical C2 IPs (142.11.200.186–190, 108.174.202.99, 176.120.22.24) and domain azurenetfiles.net. Pipeline recommends IOC hunting but generates no executable use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any network connections (outbound on common ports 80, 443, 8080, 8443) from PeopleSoft application servers to the eight C2 IPs or DNS queries resolving azurenetfiles.net. Correlate timing with process creation to identify the backdoor process.

suggestion.title: Post-exploitation credential harvesting from PeopleSoft
suggestion.rationale: Compromised PeopleSoft deployments grant access to HR/payroll databases with high-value credentials. Article describes multi-stage campaign implying credential abuse but no detection targets credential access techniques.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of credential-dumping tools (mimikatz, procdump, SQLDumper) or PowerShell scripts accessing HKLM registry, LSA, or SAM databases from PeopleSoft process contexts. Alert on LDAP queries enumerating domain users/groups from the compromised application server.

suggestion.title: Lateral movement from PeopleSoft to internal infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Post-RCE, attackers typically pivot using stolen credentials to adjacent HR/financial systems. Article omits lateral-movement detections despite describing a 'campaign' (implying multi-host compromise).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for RDP/SSH sessions originating from the PeopleSoft server to internal hosts, especially file servers and HR databases. Alert on scheduled task creation or WMI lateral execution from PSADMIN_USER or application service accounts.

suggestion.title: Account Hijacking via Social Engineering - Tchap
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'threat actor gained access to the Tchap platform using a compromised user account' and 'gained access to the platform following a social engineering attack.' This is the initial compromise vector and should trigger detection for anomalous authentication behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Tchap/Matrix sign-in events for impossible travel (geographic distance impossible within observed time delta between logins), new device authenticating with known user credentials, or sign-in from high-risk countries. Alert on concurrent sessions from geographically disparate locations within short window or failed login attempts preceding successful hijack.

suggestion.title: Bulk Public Channel Message Scraping
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attacker was able to steal all the data shared in public chat rooms, which are not encrypted' and 'scraped nearly 650,000 messages.' Single account accessing abnormally high volume of public room content in constrained timeframe.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline typical user API call patterns and message download rates per account. Alert on single Tchap account making 10x+ normal volume of public channel message fetch calls within hours. Flag programmatic bulk-download patterns (rapid successive API calls without interactive delay) from otherwise dormant accounts.

suggestion.title: Exposed Hardcoded LDAP Credentials in Artifact
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'hardcoded LDAP credentials leaked via a PowerShell script.' Exposed credentials represent immediate lateral movement and authentication risk to directory infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Extract credential strings from leaked PowerShell and cross-reference LDAP bind attempts post-breach. Monitor LDAP authentication log for binds using exposed credentials from atypical source IPs or during anomalous hours. Flag any successful LDAP authenticated sessions following credential exposure date.

suggestion.title: Multi-Gigabyte Exfiltration of Government Communications
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'stolen over 13.5GB of documents and media files shared by public servants.' Volume-based exfiltration detection should flag multi-GB transfers from single account within short period.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Tchap platform for abnormal outbound data transfer volumes. Alert when single account downloads or exports multi-gigabyte content within hours (baseline: typical user exports <100MB per day). Flag file transfers to suspicious IP ranges, anonymization services, or cloud storage buckets unaffiliated with user organization.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized PII Enumeration of Government Personnel
suggestion.rationale: Article: attacker 'collect[ed] the users' names and email addresses, as well as their avatar images and the public sector organization they work for' on 73,467 accounts. Bulk user metadata enumeration enables targeting of French government staff.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk directory queries returning user email, organization, photo/avatar metadata from public Tchap channels. Flag single account performing user profile enumeration across multiple government departments or organizations. Monitor for API calls requesting user lists from chat rooms without legitimate business context.

suggestion.title: Persistent Unauthorized Access from Compromised Account
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates compromised account remained active long enough to scrape 650k messages and exfiltrate 13.5GB before discovery, suggesting days or weeks of persistence. Account activity should deviate sharply from baseline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor compromised account for anomalies: activity outside user's typical hours, geographies inconsistent with historical pattern, high-volume API access without corresponding interactive logins, or access to data unrelated to user's job function. Alert on sessions with no human-interactive indicators but high programmatic activity volume.

suggestion.title: PAN-OS CVE-2026-0273 Management Interface Command Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'command injection vulnerability in PAN‑OS...allows authenticated administrators to execute arbitrary commands as root via the CLI or web management interface.' This is a direct execution vector requiring detection of injected CLI commands or abnormal web interface requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PAN-OS management interface (port 443, SSH) for authenticated sessions followed by unusual command syntax patterns (shell metacharacters, command separators) in CLI logs or HTTP request bodies. Correlate with unexpected process spawning from PAN-OS daemon (root-level mgmt processes).

suggestion.title: PAN-OS Root Privilege Execution via CVE-2026-0273
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'execute arbitrary commands as root'—the impact depends on detecting root-level process spawning from the management interface or CLI daemon, not typical admin user execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify root-owned processes spawned by PAN-OS management daemons (e.g., mgmt_svr, logd) with command lines containing shell syntax, scripts, or suspicious binaries. Cross-reference with management interface authentication logs within the preceding 30 seconds.

suggestion.title: PAN-OS CLI Privilege Escalation (CVE-2026-0272)
suggestion.rationale: Article calls out a separate 'CLI privilege escalation' CVE as distinct from the root command injection. This warrants detection of non-root-to-root transitions within CLI sessions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for CLI session escalation patterns: admin-level logins followed by privilege-check failures then successful root-level command execution, or use of `sudo`-like escalation methods in PAN-OS CLI transcript logs.

suggestion.title: Asset Inventory – Vulnerable PAN-OS Versions
suggestion.rationale: Article does not explicitly list affected versions, but names 'PA‑Series and VM‑Series' as targets. Detection requires asset inventory correlation against CVE-2026-0273, CVE-2026-0272, CVE-2026-0269 patch status.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset management for PAN-OS instances (PA/VM series) with OS version < [patched version, to be sourced from CVE details]. Flag systems that have not applied updates within 30 days of advisory release.

suggestion.title: Tunnel Traffic Disruption (CVE-2026-0269)
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'tunnel traffic denial‑of‑service bug' as a third CVE. Detection should monitor for abnormal tunnel state or traffic drop correlated with CLI/management activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PAN-OS tunnel interface status logs for state transitions (up→down) following management interface activity. Alert if tunnel DoS occurs without known maintenance windows or if preceded by authentication events from unexpected sources.

suggestion.title: AI-Assisted Obfuscated Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly mentions 'Attackers and Defenders Embrace AI'—implies adversaries are using AI to generate evasive command payloads or obfuscate execution. No use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for commands with high entropy, unusual escape sequences, or polymorphic payloads that indicate algorithmic obfuscation rather than hand-crafted scripts. Correlate suspicious process execution with parent processes known to support dynamic code generation (PowerShell, Python, node.exe).

suggestion.title: MDR / EDR Evasion Technique Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title implies attackers are evolving tactics to bypass MDR defenses. Pipeline should have surfaced detection logic for EDR/MDR-specific evasion (driver unload, API hooking circumvention, sensor disable attempts).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on attempts to disable, unload, or bypass EDR drivers; registry modifications targeting monitoring services; API call interception patterns; or suspicious WMI/WinRM activity that might indicate lateral movement to sensor-evasion infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via AI-Assisted Discovery
suggestion.rationale: AI-driven attack chains typically leverage automated target profiling and lateral movement. Title suggests this is a key evolution. No use case covers discovery+lateral movement automation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid sequential account/host discovery queries (AD queries, SMB enumeration, ARP scans) followed immediately by lateral movement attempts. Look for patterns suggesting algorithmic targeting rather than human reconnaissance cadence.

suggestion.title: Credential File Access During Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article states attack 'the moment a package is installed' to steal 'wallet keys, cloud credentials, SSH keys, developer secrets.' No detection for file reads of .ssh/, .aws/credentials, .config/solana/ during npm/pip operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file-read operations targeting .ssh/id_rsa*, .aws/credentials, .config/solana/, .gnupg/ when spawned from npm/yarn/python parent processes or node_modules/.bin/ directories.

suggestion.title: Network Exfiltration During Package Post-Install Phase
suggestion.rationale: Article IPs (77.90.185.225, 104.239.66.223) and domains (meet-fr.com, whiteshopify.replit.app) are likely C2 for credential exfiltration triggered by post-install scripts. No detection for outbound connections timed to package installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate npm/pip install process execution time with outbound connections to article IOCs within 30 seconds. Alert on DNS queries to meet-fr.com or whiteshopify.replit.app from developer machines during dev-tool activity.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Execution from node_modules or .venv
suggestion.rationale: Post-install scripts in malicious packages execute arbitrary code from package directories. Article: 'the moment a package is installed.' Missing detection for process spawning from .venv/bin or node_modules/.bin with suspicious patterns (encoding tools, curl, credential dumping).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child process creation where parent command-line contains node_modules/.bin/, .venv/bin/, or pip-installed script paths, with child processes being powershell, cmd, curl, certutil, or other credential-access utilities.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm/PyPI Package Installation Audit
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies '25 malicious packages' on npm and PyPI supply chains but package names not enumerated in excerpt. Missing detection correlates known malicious package names or registry metadata (author, version, timestamps) with installation logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If malicious package names are enumerated from full article source, alert on npm/pip install/update of those packages in package.json, package-lock.json, Pipfile, or pip-install logs.

suggestion.title: Coinminer Malware Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists Win.Worm.Coinminer::1201 with hash 9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507 and example filename VID001.exe in 'Most prevalent malware files from Talos telemetry over the past week'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execution of VID001.exe or file hash 9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507. Alert on cryptocurrency mining process behavior: sustained high CPU utilization, memory allocation patterns matching libcrypto, outbound connections to known mining pools on non-standard ports.

suggestion.title: Code Injector Malware Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article lists W32.Injector:Gen.21ie.1201 (MD5: aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9, SHA256: 96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974) as prevalent malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process injection via WriteProcessMemory/CreateRemoteThread combinations. Monitor for processes with mismatched command-line vs. image path. Alert on RWX page allocations and unpacking signatures (VirtualAlloc + memcpy to executable regions).

suggestion.title: Unencrypted Wireless Communication Interception
suggestion.rationale: Article demonstrates vulnerability of unencrypted channels: 'if you don't want people like my dad intercepting your comms, maybe stick to encrypted channels.' Walkie-talkie anecdote illustrates T1040 collection vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unencrypted protocol usage (plaintext HTTP, FTP, unencrypted DNS). Alert on packet capture tools (Wireshark, tcpdump) or network sniffing tool execution. Detect unencrypted wireless credentials and session tokens in network traffic.

suggestion.title: VPN Vulnerability Exploitation by Qilin
suggestion.rationale: Article headline: 'CISA gives U.S. federal agencies three days to fix a VPN bug under attack by Qilin.' Check Point remote access tools explicitly mentioned as attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Check Point VPN authentication logs for exploitation patterns (post-auth code execution). Alert on VPN access followed by immediate privilege escalation or lateral movement. Detect Qilin-attributed C2 IOCs post-VPN compromise.

suggestion.title: Social Engineering via Malicious Links in Chat Platforms
suggestion.rationale: Article states WhatsApp users were 'targeted in a social engineering attack that attempted to trick users into clicking on malicious links'—explicit T1566.002 phishing vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for URL clicks from WhatsApp/chat apps to known credential harvesting or exploit delivery domains. Detect rapid follow-up authentication attempts from compromised accounts. Alert on file downloads post-click (suspected payload delivery).

suggestion.title: Insecure Credential Storage in Personal Productivity Tools
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions storing passwords in unencrypted Memo function on personal devices: 'My dad, meanwhile, mostly used the Memo function to store his passwords'—represents T1187/weak credential management.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect plaintext password files in note-taking apps, memo applications, or text editors. Monitor for exfiltration of password-containing files. Alert when credentials discovered in unencrypted storage are later used in authentication events from unusual locations/IPs.

suggestion.title: Exploitation of AI-Deprioritized Vulnerabilities
suggestion.rationale: Article premise: 'AI broke vulnerability management'—attackers exploit gaps in AI-driven risk assessment. Pipeline missed detection for exploits targeting CVEs that AI systems underranked.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect exploitation attempts against CVEs scored low/medium by recent automated scans. Correlate severity underestimation with actual exploitation activity—process injection, service compromise, or command spawning from network services.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner Evasion and Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Article discusses circumvention of AI defenses; no use case captures scanner blinding through process termination, network isolation, or obfuscation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abrupt termination of scanner processes, blocking of scanner communications, or masquerading of exploitable artifacts to evade signature/ML-based detection. Baseline scanner execution cadence.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from False-Negative Assessment Systems
suggestion.rationale: Systems cleared by broken AI assessment become springboards for lateral movement. No use case bridges clean scan status to behavioral exploitation indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on lateral movement, privilege escalation, or persistence from systems with recent clean/low-risk AI assessments. Correlate temporal proximity between assessment and suspicious activity.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly calls out 'CVE-2026-10520 — match against your vulnerability scanner.' Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this clear instruction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Match vulnerability scanner output for Ivanti Sentry appliances with CVE-2026-10520 detected or unfixed. CISA due date 2026-06-14 creates enforcement urgency; flag any unpatched instances regardless of scanner confidence (patch lag is the silent killer).

suggestion.title: Externally Reachable Ivanti Sentry Appliance
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' This is the precondition for exploitation and a clear detection boundary.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Ivanti Sentry appliance network exposure via port scanning, cloud asset inventory, or passive DNS. Flag instances without mTLS (with EPMM) or restricted HTTPS access, as these allow external exploitation.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry OS Command Injection Execution
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user.' Should surface command injection patterns in HTTP requests or logs targeting Sentry appliance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP(S) traffic to Ivanti Sentry appliances for command injection syntax (shell metacharacters, process substitution, pipe chains) in request parameters. Look for payloads injected into Sentry API endpoints accessed from untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Root-Level Remote Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exploitation outcome: 'achieve root-level remote code execution.' Post-exploitation indicators such as root process creation, privilege escalation attempts, or system-level changes on Sentry appliance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry appliance process logs for unexpected root-owned child processes spawned from HTTP service accounts. Flag non-standard interpreters (sh, bash) with arguments suggesting command execution from remote input.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unmanaged State Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article notes vulnerability exploitable 'in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state.' Unmanaged state is a risk posture indicator separate from vulnerability presence; should trigger configuration audit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Ivanti Sentry appliances not enrolled in management systems (EPMM, Neurons for MDM) or without confirmed mTLS enforcement. Unmanaged state removes access controls that would otherwise prevent exploitation.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Service Anomaly - CISA KEV Timeline
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV due date 2026-06-14 is near-term; article emphasizes federal enforcement logic and patch velocity. Detection should correlate service availability or patching activity against deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry appliance service restarts, patch events, or availability drops approaching CISA due date. Sudden changes may indicate hurried remediation or attacker disruption post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: npm install script execution by unusual process parent
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'npm install scripts' as attack vector. Pipeline should flag execution of arbitrary code during npm install phase (preinstall/postinstall hooks) as primary detection opportunity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned from npm/Node.js with parent process not in expected npm/build automation. Baseline legitimate preinstall/postinstall scripts; flag obfuscated commands, network I/O, or privilege escalation attempts.

suggestion.title: Malicious package.json install script injection
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attack mode described in title requires initial injection of malicious scripts into package.json. Detection should flag scripts with suspicious payloads (curl, wget, base64, powershell) added to preinstall/postinstall fields.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for package.json edits that add or modify install scripts. Flag scripts containing shell metacharacters, network utilities, or data exfiltration patterns. Correlate with commits from low-trust or external contributors.

suggestion.title: npm package metadata tampering in registry
suggestion.rationale: Article references GitHub's defensive measure against compromised npm packages. Detection should identify when legitimate packages receive new versions with malicious install scripts—indicator of registry account compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry publish API calls for unexpected script field updates to popular packages. Alert on version bumps that introduce new preinstall/postinstall scripts; correlate with unusual npm account login patterns.

suggestion.title: Suspicious node_modules extraction to sensitive paths
suggestion.rationale: Install scripts execute during package extraction. Detection should identify extraction to non-standard or sensitive directories, indicating attacker intent to persist or escalate.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unexpected node_modules extraction outside project directories or into system paths. Alert if install-script execution occurs followed by writes to /etc, /usr/local/bin, or registry paths.

suggestion.title: npm install with unsuspected network exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Malicious install scripts often exfiltrate data post-compromise. Detection should correlate npm install execution with unexpected outbound connections to non-CDN destinations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: During npm install phases, alert on outbound HTTP/HTTPS/DNS from npm or child processes to non-npm-registry IPs. Flag if connections attempt to compress, encrypt, or tunnel data.

suggestion.title: npm package downgrade or version pinning to older vulnerable release
suggestion.rationale: Attackers may inject malicious scripts into legacy versions. Detection should flag unexpected package downgrades or explicit pinning to pre-disclosure versions during dependency resolution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm install/update commands that resolve to older package versions than available. Flag package-lock.json modifications that pin to versions known to have security issues or suspicious script content.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Ivanti Sentry RCE Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'attackers are now targeting a recently patched maximum-severity flaw' enabling 'code execution with root privileges' via 'OS command injection weakness.' Shadowserver confirmed active backdooring of exposed instances within 24 hours of patch release. Pipeline produced zero detection for exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST/GET requests to Ivanti Sentry admin portals containing shell metacharacters (|, ;, &, $(), backticks) in parameters or payloads. Monitor for HTTP 200 responses followed by unexpected process execution on appliance. Look for command injection patterns in known vulnerable URL paths.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Ivanti Sentry Version Running
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies patched versions 'R10.5.2, R10.6.2, and R10.7.1' released on patch day. Shadowserver found vulnerable instances still online post-patch. Detection must identify systems running affected versions (R10.5.0–R10.5.1, R10.6.0–R10.6.1, R10.7.0) to prevent further exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory or network discovery tools for Ivanti Sentry appliances reporting firmware versions < R10.5.2, < R10.6.2, or < R10.7.1. Correlate with Internet-exposed appliances detected by perimeter scanning. Flag as immediate patch-required.

suggestion.title: Backdoor Persistence on Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Shadowserver reported 'most of the Sentry gateways exposed online' were 'backdoored' within hours. Article notes attackers 'enable theft of sensitive customer and corporate data.' Pipeline failed to map persistence phase of kill chain despite explicit backdoor mention.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry appliance logs and OS-level events for unauthorized admin account creation or privilege escalation. Detect unexpected web shells or backdoor scripts in appliance directories. Flag new scheduled tasks or cron jobs added post-exploitation window.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Ivanti Sentry to Enterprise Network
suggestion.rationale: Article states Sentry is a 'security gateway appliance [that] secures traffic between back-end corporate systems and remote mobile devices' and that attackers use Sentry flaws 'to breach targets' enterprise networks.' Compromised appliances become pivot points but no detection coverage specified.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal traffic flows from Ivanti Sentry appliance to internal network. Alert on new internal IP ranges contacted, unusual protocols (RDP, WinRM, SSH) from Sentry to backend systems, or large data transfers to external destinations via Sentry.

suggestion.title: Internet-Exposed Ivanti Sentry Admin Portal Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly references 'Ivanti Sentry admin portals exposed online' shown in Shadowserver screenshots, a prerequisite for successful exploitation. No detection use case for admin portal exposure or anomalous remote access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry admin portal logins (typically HTTPS on port 8443 or 9443) for geographic anomalies, rapid failed attempts, or logins from non-corporate IP ranges. Correlate successful logins with subsequent command execution or new account creation.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via Compromised Sentry Gateway
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'hackers often target Ivanti security flaws because they provide an entry point into targets' enterprise networks, enabling the theft of sensitive customer and corporate data.' No detection logic for exfiltration phase despite explicit mention.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound data volume and protocols from Ivanti Sentry appliance. Alert on encrypted tunnels (SSH, VPN) from Sentry to external IPs, large HTTP POST requests to public cloud storage, or unusual DNS query patterns indicative of DNS tunneling.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Execution on Developer Machines
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly promises detection guidance: 'Detect Them on Developer Machines with Suspicious Files.' No use case was generated for file-based detection of Miasma/Hades.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for suspicious files being executed from user-writable locations (Downloads, Temp, AppData) on developer workstations. Correlate file creation events with process execution, focusing on files with mismatched signatures or obfuscated content indicative of Miasma/Hades staging.

suggestion.title: Miasma/Hades Malware Family IOC Matching
suggestion.rationale: Article is titled '[HIGH] Miasma and Hades Are Spreading Now' but zero IOCs were extracted. Pipeline should have identified malware family indicators, filenames, or hashes associated with these families.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain intelligence feeds for Miasma and Hades family indicators (file hashes, registry paths, C2 domains). Alert on any file/network event matching known malware signatures, especially when file operations occur in %USERPROFILE% or common development directories.

suggestion.title: Developer Workstation Compromise Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article focus is on developer machines as targets; no use case was generated for detecting the initial compromise or persistence mechanisms specific to dev environments (IDE plugins, package managers, build tools).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious modifications to developer-related startup locations (Visual Studio extensions, npm/NuGet caches, Git hooks, IDE configuration). Detect unusual process chains spawning from these locations, especially with network connections.

suggestion.title: AI Agent Unauthorized Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Trick OpenClaw AI Agent Into Running Code'—the pipeline failed to generate any detection for this core attack vector. Must detect anomalous subprocess/shell invocations from agent runtime.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Process.ParentProcessName matching AI agent runtime patterns (Python, Node.js interpreters spawned by agent frameworks) executing unusual child processes (bash, cmd.exe, PowerShell). Alert on first-time execution of interpreters or shell commands by AI agent processes.

suggestion.title: AI Agent Credential/Secret Access and Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly mentions 'Leaking Secrets'—no use case generated for detection of AI agents accessing credential stores, environment variables, or files outside their intended context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on AI agent processes accessing credential paths (/root/.ssh, $CREDENTIAL_PATH, credential managers, .env files) or making unexpected cloud API calls to list/read secrets. Correlate process context with agent tool definitions to identify unauthorized access.

suggestion.title: Prompt Injection / Agent Jailbreak Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'New Attacks' against agents—likely prompt injection or jailbreak vectors that cause behavior deviation. Pipeline missed the initial-access phase entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor agent input/prompt logs for injection patterns (backtick escaping, role-play instructions, 'ignore previous instructions'). Alert on agent tool-call sequences that deviate from expected policy (e.g., agent invoking exec/shell tools without explicit user request, accessing secrets outside declared tool scope).

suggestion.title: Sensitive File/Secret Read by AI Agent
suggestion.rationale: 'Leaking Secrets' requires detection of file system access to sensitive paths. The pipeline did not propose any file-access or secret-scanning use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on AI agent processes (by parent PID or process name matching agent frameworks) reading files in sensitive directories: /etc/passwd, /root, configuration/secrets folders, cloud credential directories. Establish baseline of expected file reads per agent type and alert on deviation.

suggestion.title: Agent Behavior Anomaly - Tool Invocation Outside Policy
suggestion.rationale: Attacks 'trick' the agent into running code—implies tool/function calls occur outside the agent's intended behavior policy. No detection hypothesis addresses agent tool-call anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Model the expected tool-call sequence and arguments per agent workflow. Alert on: (1) invocation of dangerous tools (exec, eval, shell) when not declared in agent's tool manifest, (2) arguments to file I/O tools pointing to /etc or credential paths, (3) high cardinality in tool invocation chains within a single session.

suggestion.title: Recovery Partition XML File Modification Detected
suggestion.rationale: Article directly states attack vector is 'Recovery Partition XML Files.' Pipeline generated zero UCs despite this being the core technical mechanism. No detection logic whatsoever for the named attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor writes to system recovery partition paths (typically \\?\Volume{GUID}\, EFI partitions) targeting XML files. Alert on any process outside System/TrustedInstaller context opening recovery partition files with write access. Correlate with BitLocker service process activity.

suggestion.title: BitLocker Protection Status Bypass or Disablement
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Bypasses Windows BitLocker.' Pipeline generated no impact-phase UC despite bypass being the stated outcome.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for manage-bde.exe execution with -status, -off, -protectors parameters. Alert on Event ID 4656/4657 indicating changes to BitLocker object permissions or encryption status changes. Detect TPM-related WMI queries or UEFI/firmware access attempts.

suggestion.title: GreatXML Exploit Process Execution or Payload Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Article title names 'GreatXML Exploit' as the specific threat. Pipeline failed to generate any UC for detecting this exploit's code execution, staging, or delivery mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for processes named or attributed to 'GreatXML' or variants. Detect XML parsing libraries (System.Xml, msxml) loaded by non-system processes targeting recovery partition or firmware paths. Alert on unusual child processes spawned from XML-processing contexts with SYSTEM privileges.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Recovery Partition Access
suggestion.rationale: Exploit requires unauthorized access to protected recovery partition—a classic privilege escalation vector. Pipeline generated no UC for detecting this elevation technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any process spawning with elevated token integrity (High/System) immediately after accessing recovery partition or BitLocker configuration files. Detect token impersonation patterns where low-privilege process acquires recovery partition handles.

suggestion.title: Suspicious XML Parsing Against BitLocker Metadata
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector specifically targets 'XML Files' in recovery partition. No UC generated for detecting XML processing logic targeting BitLocker structures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for XML parsing utility execution (powershell.exe with -EncodedCommand, msbuild.exe, cscript.exe) with file paths pointing to System32\drivers or recovery mount points. Detect suspicious XML schema validation or transformation patterns targeting BitLocker recovery keys.

suggestion.title: PeopleSoft Gadget Chain Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attack vector: 'using a gadget chain of zero-days and old vulnerabilities in the attacks' against PeopleSoft. No detection use case generated despite this being the initial access pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PeopleSoft application server logs and network traffic for serialized Java object payloads in HTTP requests, unusual servlet access patterns, and exploitation signatures consistent with known PeopleSoft gadget chains (e.g., commons-beanutils chains).

suggestion.title: Bulk Student Records Export from PeopleSoft
suggestion.rationale: Article documents theft of '40GB of documents containing student finance data, billing and payment information' plus personal identifiers. This represents massive collection phase that should trigger DLP alerts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unusually large exports from PSSTU, PSFIN, and PSPYRL tables (student, finance, payroll modules). Correlate volume >10k records, off-hours timing, and service account usage. Flag cross-campus data consolidation within short time window.

suggestion.title: Educational Institution Data Posted to Known Dark Web Leak Site
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'In a post on their dark web leak site, the cybercrime group claims to have stolen over 40GB of documents.' ShinyHunters leak site is known infrastructure for educational data sales. Dark web monitoring gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain automated monitoring of ShinyHunters dark web leak site (tor mirrors, mirrors of mirrors) for postings containing institution names, student record artifacts, or payment/finance data. Trigger incident response on new institutional data appearing within 48-72 hours of breach discovery.

suggestion.title: Cross-Campus PeopleSoft Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Article reveals attack spanned 'University of Nottingham and its Malaysia and China campuses.' Detection use case missing for geographically distributed lateral movement within federated PeopleSoft deployments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect single compromised credential or service account authenticating to PeopleSoft instances across geographically separated campuses (UK, Malaysia, China) within 24-hour window. Flag unusual inter-campus data queries or bulk transfers.

suggestion.title: Extraction of Passport Numbers and Disability Status from Educational Records
suggestion.rationale: Article lists harvested PII: 'passport numbers and information relating to academic enrolments... ethnicities, disabilities.' High-value identity theft indicators. Queries targeting these fields should have dedicated detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor queries to PeopleSoft personal data tables for fields containing PASSPORT_ID, ETHNIC_GROUP, DISABILITY_STATUS with bulk retrieval (>1000 records). Trigger on queries from unexpected user roles or outside normal business hours.

suggestion.title: Configuration Variance Analysis in PeopleSoft Attack Success Rate
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'the attack is not working on all systems, likely because successful exploitation depends on each instance's configuration.' Implies need to identify misconfigured PeopleSoft instances as vulnerability assessment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate known-vulnerable PeopleSoft configuration states (missing patch levels, weak servlet security, enabled debug modes) with exploitation attempts. Track which instance configuration variants are being targeted in attacks.

suggestion.title: Suspicious postinstall script execution during npm install
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly addresses npm v12 blocking postinstall scripts as a security feature. The implication is that postinstall script abuse was an attack vector. Pipeline missed the core detection: monitoring for postinstall script execution, particularly with network I/O, file writes, or privilege escalation. Phrase: 'block-postinstall' in URL indicates this is the central threat model.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm/node process spawning shell interpreters (cmd, powershell, bash) with parent process npm.exe or node.exe during package installation phases. Flag postinstall hooks that make outbound network connections, write to sensitive directories, or execute with elevated privileges.

suggestion.title: npm package with dangerous postinstall hook patterns
suggestion.rationale: npm v12 security improvement implies prior attacks used postinstall hooks to install malware, steal credentials, or establish persistence. Pipeline should surface detection for package.json or .npm-scripts patterns indicative of supply-chain compromise. Phrase: 'biggest security improvements in years' signals this addresses a widespread, known attack pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate npm package installation events with subsequent spawning of obfuscated or encoded script interpreters, child processes making C2 calls, or credential-access tools (secretsdump, mimikatz) launched within 10 seconds of npm install completing.

suggestion.title: npm registry dependency injection or typosquatting install
suggestion.rationale: Article context is npm v12 security feature (postinstall blocking). While the body lacks specific incident examples, npm supply-chain attacks often combine typosquatting with malicious postinstall scripts. Pipeline should have inferred this as the threat model from the title alone.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install commands for package names that are levenshtein-distance-close to popular libraries; cross-ref postinstall hook execution against known-good package hashes to detect substitution attacks.

suggestion.title: Investment software beacon to attacker-controlled domains
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'delivering a powerful backdoor' via compromised software; six domains and eight IPs provided as IOCs clearly represent C2 infrastructure. Legitimate financial software should never connect to 'financemachinelearning.com' or 'gatewayrvcenter.com'. Detection should catch backdoored software establishing command-and-control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when FireAnt.exe or Windows update processes connect to the six attacker-controlled domains (financemachinelearning.com, gatewayrvcenter.com, coachcybersecurity.com, mxprodesign.com, power-sync-services.com, leadingfilipinoteams.com) or eight IP addresses. Correlate with file-hash IOCs to confirm malicious variant of legitimate software.

suggestion.title: Malicious file hash executed from installer directory
suggestion.rationale: Twenty SHA1 hashes provided as high-fidelity IOCs but pipeline generated no file-based alert. These hashes represent malware components injected via supply-chain compromise that must be detected on disk or during execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Match any file execution or load event against the 20 provided SHA1 hashes. Since supply-chain attack, expect hashes to appear in %Temp%, %AppData%, or alongside legitimate FireAnt installation directory. Alert on first observation of any hash match with alert routing to incident response.

suggestion.title: Installer followed by suspicious reconnaissance behavior
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain backdoors typically perform post-exploitation reconnaissance. Article describes 'powerful backdoor' implying active threat actor hand-off after installation. Detection should catch installer spawning commands to enumerate system, network, or process state.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Within 5 minutes of setup.exe/update.exe execution, alert on child processes executing: ipconfig, nslookup, net.exe (view commands), tasklist, Get-WmiObject, wmic.exe, or systeminfo. Establish baseline of expected reconnaissance by legitimate installer; flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: Code-signed installer with invalid or suspicious signature timestamp
suggestion.rationale: Compromised software distribution implies attacker-modified installer. Signature validation may reveal revocation, expiration, or timestamp anomalies indicating substitution or post-compilation tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Check code signature validity of any setup.exe, installer.exe, or update.exe. Flag binaries with: expired certificates, revoked signatures, timestamps predating vendor release date, or Self-Signed certificates. Correlate signature anomalies with file hash IOCs to confirm malicious variant.

suggestion.title: Supply-Chain Update Server Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly documents 'OceanLotus compromised the update server of FireAnt Metakit…and replaced legitimate software updates with a malicious payload.' This is the primary initial-access vector for the broad-reach campaign; no detection rule addresses signed/unsigned binary anomalies or update-manifest tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor update infrastructure for file modifications outside maintenance windows, unsigned binaries released as legitimate updates, hash mismatches vs. published manifests, and distribution logs showing when malicious versions were deployed to clients.

suggestion.title: SPECTRALVIPER Backdoor Orchestration Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: SPECTRALVIPER is explicitly identified as 'latest backdoor, which includes orchestration capabilities' and deployed in both campaigns (mid-2024–2026 infrastructure compromise, Oct 2025–Mar 2026 supply-chain). No detection captures its C&C communication patterns despite 8+ months of persistent activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify periodic outbound connections from compromised hosts with uncommon destination ports, irregular packet symmetry, or payload obfuscation consistent with custom C&C protocols. Correlate traffic spikes with suspected SPECTRALVIPER deployment timestamps.

suggestion.title: DNS Tunneling Detection (Denis/SOUNDBITE)
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies Denis as 'implementing DNS tunneling for C&C communications.' This is a documented evasion technique and a signature indicator of this malware family, yet no detection rule was proposed for abnormal DNS query patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag endpoints with: high-frequency DNS queries in short intervals, unusually long or high-entropy subdomain names, or DNS queries to suspicious TLDs. Correlate query patterns against known Denis/SOUNDBITE indicators if available.

suggestion.title: ICMP-Based C&C Protocol Abuse (PHOREAL)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes PHOREAL as 'leveraging the ICMP protocol for C&C communications.' ICMP tunneling is rare in legitimate enterprise traffic and highly anomalous; no detection addresses this protocol-smuggling technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound ICMP echo requests (ping) in high volume or at regular intervals from user endpoints, asymmetric payload sizes inconsistent with standard ping, or ICMP traffic to external/suspicious destinations. Legitimate ping is infrequent from workstations.

suggestion.title: Proxy Bypass Evasion via WINDSHIELD
suggestion.rationale: Article notes WINDSHIELD 'features an interesting proxy bypass mechanism,' enabling direct C&C communication that evades network controls. No detection targets proxy-bypass tactics or anomalous direct-outbound connections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes establishing raw socket connections (WINSOCK direct calls) or outbound network traffic that bypasses configured proxy infrastructure. Monitor for registry/PAC-file tampering disabling proxy enforcement. Correlate with suspicious parent processes.

suggestion.title: Long-Duration Update-Infrastructure Persistence (Oct 2025–Mar 2026)
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain campaign maintained control of FireAnt Metakit's update system for ~5 months, distributing malicious updates periodically. No use case detects sustained compromise of update services or tracks historical update-distribution patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal update frequency and package size for FireAnt Metakit; flag deviations (new builds outside release cycles, unsigned packages, modified binaries). Review update-server access logs for unauthorized administrative activity or credential misuse during Oct 2025–Mar 2026 window.

suggestion.title: SPECTRALVIPER Process Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Malware family explicitly named in title as primary payload in 'FireAnt Attack'; typical OceanLotus campaigns deploy remote access or information-stealing malware, but no execution detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution of SPECTRALVIPER (if known hash/name available), or anomalous child processes from Office applications, script interpreters, or living-off-the-land binaries typical of OceanLotus post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: OceanLotus Spearphishing to Vietnam Investors
suggestion.rationale: Article subtitle identifies targeted geographic and sectoral victim group ('Vietnam Investors'), indicating spearphishing is delivery vector; no email-based initial-access detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails with Vietnam investor-targeting keywords, finance/investment sector impersonation, OceanLotus-known sender domains, or macro/executable attachments to Vietnam-based or Vietnam-targeting enterprise recipients.

suggestion.title: FireAnt Campaign C2 Beacon Detection
suggestion.rationale: Campaign name 'FireAnt' is explicitly stated in title; typical OceanLotus campaigns establish C2 post-exploitation, but no command-and-control detection rules were generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound connections from compromised systems to known or suspected OceanLotus C2 infrastructure, unusual DNS queries for dynamically-generated domains, or HTTP/S traffic with OceanLotus-attributed User-Agent strings or beacon patterns.

suggestion.title: OceanLotus Persistence Mechanism Detection
suggestion.rationale: No persistence detection suggested despite OceanLotus historically using registry modifications, scheduled tasks, and WMI event subscriptions for dwell-time; article describes targeted attack implying long-term access is objective.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect registry modifications to Run/RunOnce keys, creation of scheduled tasks with suspicious binaries, WMI consumer/subscription creation, or file write operations to Startup folders initiated by Office or script-interpreter processes.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from OceanLotus Beachhead
suggestion.rationale: OceanLotus historically pivots laterally post-compromise; article mentions investor targets (likely multi-user environments) but no lateral movement detection use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SMB traffic between investors' workstations, RDP connections from anomalous internal sources, or creation of scheduled tasks on remote systems via WMI, indicating post-exploit pivot activity.

suggestion.title: SPECTRALVIPER Malware Indicators Discovery
suggestion.rationale: No IOCs returned for SPECTRALVIPER; article should have surfaced file hashes, C2 domains, registry keys, or file paths; pipeline failed to extract malware-specific indicators needed for hardening.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If SPECTRALVIPER hashes/filenames become available post-publication, create hash-based and filename-pattern detections; meanwhile, hunt for dropped files in temp directories, AppData, or startup folders with recent creation times correlated to email delivery.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-35273 PeopleSoft Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'ShinyHunters Exploits Oracle PeopleSoft Zero-Day (CVE-2026-35273)' — this is the primary attack vector. Pipeline must have use case for inbound exploitation attempts against PeopleSoft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to Oracle PeopleSoft endpoints (default ports 8000–8001, paths /psc/*, /pt8/*) for POST requests with suspicious payloads, unusually-sized request bodies, or SQL metacharacters. Flag any exploitation attempts matching known CVE-2026-35273 proof-of-concept signatures.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Data Exfiltration from University PeopleSoft Databases
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'breach of universities' — ShinyHunters must have exfiltrated student/faculty/research data. Detection rule critical for post-exploitation evidence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk exports or unusual query volumes from PeopleSoft databases targeting student records, faculty data, or research repositories. Flag large file transfers (>100MB) to external destinations from compromised service accounts within 24–72 hours post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Compromised PeopleSoft Service Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation playbook dictates credential reuse for lateral movement within university networks. Pipeline should detect use of stolen PeopleSoft credentials against adjacent systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify logon events using PeopleSoft service-account credentials to access non-PeopleSoft systems (email, file shares, HR databases). Flag authentication from geographic locations inconsistent with university campus, or off-hours access patterns for batch service accounts.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance and Vulnerability Scanning of PeopleSoft Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article implies targeting of multiple universities — ShinyHunters must have performed prior enumeration to identify vulnerable PeopleSoft deployments. Detection rule should cover scanning phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect port scans or HTTP enumeration of PeopleSoft default ports/paths from external source IPs. Flag patterns of 404/403 HTTP responses to /psc/ or /pt8/* paths, indicating version-discovery or vulnerability-scanning activity.

suggestion.title: ShinyHunters Attribution Indicators and Malware Staging
suggestion.rationale: Article names threat actor 'ShinyHunters' but provides no behavioral or malware indicators. Pipeline should generate detection rules for any known ShinyHunters staging, C2 domains, or malware families historically used in PeopleSoft exploitation campaigns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If any malware families or C2 infrastructure are documented for ShinyHunters operations, detect command execution, file writes, or network beacons matching known indicators. Monitor for post-exploitation tools (e.g., webshells, reverse shells) staged on compromised PeopleSoft application servers.

suggestion.title: Suspicious GitHub/Developer Account Access Sale or Listing
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'GitHub access can be more than access to code. It may expose secrets, deployment scripts, package publishing logic, cloud credentials, internal documentation, and CI/CD workflows.' Underground posts offering GitHub developer access are early supply-chain warning signals.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub audit logs for unusual developer account access patterns, geographic anomalies in authentication, or patterns consistent with compromised OAuth tokens. Correlate with dark-web intelligence feeds reporting GitHub credential sales or developer identity leaks.

suggestion.title: OAuth Token / SaaS Integration Access Theft
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes: 'underground posts mentioning OAuth access, SaaS tools, environment variables, or developer platforms deserve attention' and cites Vercel incident where 'compromise involving a trusted third-party AI tool and OAuth-connected SaaS access can create a wider security concern.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on OAuth token issuance to unfamiliar third-party applications, especially AI tools or monitoring SaaS platforms. Flag SaaS integrations with elevated permissions (read secrets, CI/CD access) that sign in from non-standard ASNs or with token-refresh patterns anomalous to normal usage.

suggestion.title: Database Credentials and API Secrets in Leaked Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article documents Sportradar case: 'exposure of sensitive operational material such as database passwords, API key and secret pairs, Kafka credentials, and monitoring tokens.' This kind of leak 'can reveal how a vendor's systems are connected, which services and integrations are trusted.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search code repositories for hardcoded database connection strings, API keys, or Kafka/monitoring credentials using regex patterns or secret scanning. Cross-reference against dark-web intelligence reporting repository leaks tied to vendor names or supply-chain campaigns (e.g., TeamPCP, Sportradar).

suggestion.title: Malicious Package Update to Compromised npm Maintainer Account
suggestion.rationale: Article describes Shai-Hulud attack: 'compromised npm maintainer accounts and malicious package updates could be used to steal credentials, harvest CI/CD secrets, and propagate across repositor[ies].' This is a direct supply-chain execution vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm package update frequency and file-size deltas for popular libraries. Flag package updates signed by accounts with sudden login anomalies or from unexpected geographies. Correlate with behavioral signals: presence of credential-stealing code (process spawning curl/wget with env vars, file reads of CI/CD config).

suggestion.title: CI/CD Environment Variable and Secret Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article states threat actors 'steal developer secrets and infected trusted packages' and 'harvest CI/CD secrets,' specifically calling out the risk that 'environment variables' in leaked data expose system trust relationships.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process execution spawning credential-dumping tools within CI/CD pipeline containers or runners (e.g., env | curl, cat $CI_CONFIG | nc). Flag unusual cloud storage or S3 writes from build agents, or exfiltration of .env files to external IPs. Monitor for Base64-encoded environment variable dumps in network traffic.

suggestion.title: Unpatched or Compromised Scanning Tool (Trivy) Supply-Chain Trojan
suggestion.rationale: Article cites Sportradar attack involving 'a compromised Trivy scanner' that exposed database passwords and credentials. Tools like Trivy run with access to secrets and repositories—compromise grants attacker wholesale access to CI/CD pipelines.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor downloads and execution of Trivy/scanning tools for unexpected network egress (DNS queries to C2, HTTP POSTs to non-repo IPs). Validate binary signatures and hashes against upstream registries. Alert if Trivy executes with unusual arguments (e.g., -o exfil.json piped to curl) or spawns child processes (shells, credential-dumping utilities).

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Exploitation Attempt (CVE-2026-10520)

Flag requests from untrusted IPs to known vulnerable endpoint paths without mTLS/client certificate validation.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Command Execution Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states successful exploitation grants 'root-level remote code execution' but pipeline captured zero execution-phase detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious child processes spawned from Ivanti Sentry service/daemon processes (sentry, mobileironmanager) running with root/system privileges. Look for curl, wget, bash, sh, or reverse-shell patterns in command line arguments.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unmanaged State + External Reachability
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' No exposure/discovery detection generated.

Cross-reference against CMDB/asset management for 'managed=false' or 'unmanaged' state. Flag instances lacking mTLS mutual authentication or restricted HTTPS access policies.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Patch Deployment Verification
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies federal patch due 2026-06-14 and emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer,' but pipeline generated no compliance/patch-readiness detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners (Qualys, Nessus, Tenable) for unpatched Ivanti Sentry instances. Correlate against patch-deployment logs. Alert on assets still running vulnerable versions after federal due date 2026-06-14.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Authentication Bypass Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'remote unauthenticated user' access path, distinguishing from protected configurations (mTLS, restricted HTTPS). No authentication-anomaly detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry application logs for successful API/endpoint access without valid session tokens or mTLS client certificates. Track 401→200 sequences or requests bypassing authentication middleware. Flag access from non-internal IP ranges to admin or command-execution endpoints.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scanner Detection — Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE: CVE-2026-10520 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and recommends asset-exposure hunt via scanner baseline, but pipeline generated zero scanner-driven detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any vulnerability scanner match for CVE-2026-10520 affecting Ivanti Sentry products. CISA KEV status confirms active exploitation; prioritize unmanaged appliances and instances externally reachable per article guidance.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Network Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states exploitation succeeds 'where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable'—requires asset exposure hunt but pipeline did not generate network-reachability detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances (detect via HTTP/S headers, certificate CN, or service banners on ports 443, 8443) reachable from external networks. Flag any instances without mTLS or restricted HTTPS access restrictions (article notes these configurations mitigate).

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload Detection — Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector is 'OS command injection vulnerability' but pipeline generated zero payload-inspection use cases for injection patterns in Sentry request handling.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints for shell metacharacters (`;`, `|`, `$()`, backticks, `&`) in URL parameters, POST bodies, and headers. Flag requests from unauthenticated sources (article: 'remote unauthenticated user') attempting command chaining or substitution.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Root RCE Activity — Ivanti Sentry Process Spawning
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'root-level remote code execution' as outcome; pipeline should detect post-compromise child processes and privilege escalation but generated zero execution-phase detections.

Monitor for shell spawning (cmd.exe, /bin/bash) and outbound network connections from Sentry processes.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unmanaged State & Configuration Drift

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Ivanti Sentry API Access — Auth Bypass

Flag requests to sensitive paths (/api/*, /management/*) from external source IPs returning success without prior authenticated login.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scanning Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2026-10520 — match against your vulnerability scanner' yet zero UC generated to detect this CVE in asset inventory or scan results.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanning results and CMDB for Ivanti Sentry instances lacking patches published before 2026-06-14. Prioritize results flagged as externally reachable or in unmanaged enrollment state per article's exploitation preconditions.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Command Injection Exploitation Attempt

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry administrative interfaces for command-injection patterns (semicolons, pipes, backticks, $() substitution, escaped quotes) in URL parameters and POST bodies from unauthenticated sources.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Root Process Execution

suggestion.title: Unmanaged Sentry with External Accessibility Configuration Risk
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability only exploitable where 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable'; detection must hunt this risky infrastructure posture.

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation where parent is Ivanti Sentry process/service and child spawns with root/system privileges, especially shells (/bin/bash, /bin/sh, cmd.exe, powershell.exe). Establish baseline of legitimate Sentry-spawned processes; surface novelty. Correlate with CVE-2026-10520 exposure detection.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unmanaged State Inventory Audit

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset and vulnerability management systems for all Ivanti Sentry instances and cross-reference against enrollment state in EPMM, mTLS certificate store, and Neurons for MDM. Flag any Sentry appliance in 'unmanaged' state (not enrolled in protective controls per vendor documentation) as a high-risk exposure ready for exploitation.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Egress from Potentially Compromised Ivanti Sentry Appliance

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal outbound connectivity from Ivanti Sentry appliances (typically restricted to Ivanti cloud services, internal DNS, NTP, vendor updates). Alert on unexpected outbound connections to non-standard ports, untrusted ASNs, or domains outside vendor allow-lists. Correlate with CVE-2026-10520 exploitation indicators or known adversary infrastructure if available.

suggestion.title: Federal Patch Due Date Compliance Checkpoint

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After 2026-06-14, enumerate all Ivanti Sentry appliances and flag any running vulnerable versions of CVE-2026-10520 as critical compliance failure. Escalate immediately. Implement controls to prevent re-deployment of unpatched instances. This is both a detection and a compliance hunt.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Externally Reachable Ivanti Sentry Instances

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry instances listening on public-facing interfaces via vulnerability scanner or network reconnaissance. Baseline all externally reachable Sentry appliances and alert on new exposures or instances lacking mTLS/EPMM/restricted HTTPS protection.
