suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If EDR/process telemetry available from the Sentry appliance: detect unexpected child processes spawned from Sentry application context, particularly shell interpreters (bash, sh), credential tools, or persistence mechanisms. Baseline legitimate Sentry process trees; alert on deviations from established patterns.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry—Unauthenticated Exploit Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Detect authentication bypass or requests missing session validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP(S) requests to Sentry management ports (443, 8443) from external IPs lacking valid authentication tokens, session cookies, or credentials. Correlate unauthenticated requests with subsequent command-injection payloads.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry—OS Command Injection Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'OS command injection vulnerability.' Detect shell metacharacters and command separators in request parameters targeting known Sentry endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry request logs for injection patterns: shell metacharacters (`;`, `|`, `&`, `` ` ``), command substitution syntax, and path traversal in parameters. Alert on successful command execution (process spawn events tied to Sentry binary).

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry—Root-Level Process Spawning
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'root-level remote code execution.' Detect unexpected privilege escalation and root shell spawning from Sentry service context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect shell interpreters (bash, sh, cmd.exe) or system utilities spawned with root/SYSTEM privileges as children of Sentry process or via Sentry-initiated execution.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry—Externally Exposed Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'externally reachable' and 'unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Identify and inventory exposed Sentry appliances on internet-facing network perimeter.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Network scan for open Sentry management ports from untrusted zones. Cross-reference against management status (mTLS/EPMM active)—flag unmanaged appliances or those without restricted HTTPS protection.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry—Post-Compromise Lateral Movement to Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Sentry is MDM/EMM infrastructure. Compromised appliance can push payloads to enrolled endpoints or steal management credentials for further lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual deployment commands issued from Sentry to enrolled endpoints, mass policy changes, or credential exfiltration attempts from Sentry's managed endpoint database.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry—Disabled mTLS or Management State Downgrade
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access...makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors.' Detect disabling of these mitigations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on configuration changes disabling mTLS enforcement, switching to HTTP, or transitioning appliance state from managed to unmanaged—actions that re-expose this CVE despite patches.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner Detection: CVE-2026-10520 Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes CVE-2026-10520 as a CISA KEV entry (actively exploited). Primary detection vector is vulnerability scanner match; pipeline produced no use case for scanner output or asset-inventory correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Vulnerability scanner reports or asset-inventory systems flag Ivanti Sentry instances (product name or version string match) as vulnerable to CVE-2026-10520. Scope to externally-reachable assets; filter out if mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access via Neurons for MDM are confirmed controls.

suggestion.title: External Ivanti Sentry Appliance Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is exploitable 'in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable'—the external reachability is the critical precondition. Pipeline did not suggest network-based asset exposure detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances (port 8443 HTTPS or product-string fingerprint) reachable from untrusted networks. Validate against network segmentation policy; escalate if external exposure confirmed without compensating controls (mTLS, restricted access).

suggestion.title: Unexpected Command Execution from Ivanti Sentry Service
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow...remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution'—exploitation via T1059.001 should trigger process-execution detection. Pipeline generated no behavioral detection use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected child processes spawned by Ivanti Sentry service (e.g., sentry-related process names executing shell, bash, cmd.exe, powershell). Context: normal operation does not spawn shells; any shell spawn suggests command-injection exploitation in flight. Prioritize if process runs with elevated (root/SYSTEM) privileges.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry HTTP Exploitation Request Pattern
suggestion.rationale: OS command injection typically exploits via malformed HTTP parameters. Article does not specify injection vector detail, but pipeline should have generated detection for crafted HTTP requests to known Ivanti endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST/GET requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints (e.g., /admin, /api/*) containing shell metacharacters (|, ;, &&, `, $(), backticks) or command-injection payloads (e.g., 'id', 'whoami', 'nc', 'bash'). Ivanti Sentry typically uses HTTPS on port 8443; focus on unencrypted fallback or proxy inspection where applicable.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Privilege Escalation to Root
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'could allow...remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Detection of privilege escalation or root-level process spawning from Ivanti context is critical for post-compromise hunting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on UID/privilege-level changes to root (UID 0) or SYSTEM initiated by or related to Ivanti Sentry service. Scope to unexpected process parent-child chains (e.g., Ivanti service spawning sh/bash then setuid() or sudoedit). False-positive context: legitimate privilege escalation for service maintenance; correlate with exploitation indicators.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Ivanti Sentry Unauthenticated Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability exploitable by 'remote unauthenticated user' with 'endpoints externally reachable' — direct asset-exposure indicator. Article explicitly references template at `_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure`.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful unauthenticated connections to Ivanti Sentry ports (typically 443) from external sources. Baseline internal traffic; alert on new external source IPs connecting without authentication headers or session tokens. Cross-reference with asset inventory for Sentry appliances.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies vulnerability type as 'OS command injection' allowing 'root-level remote code execution' — executables pattern is clear from vulnerability class.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for shell metacharacters (pipe, semicolon, backtick, command substitution syntax) in HTTP request parameters sent to Sentry endpoints. Alert on successful command execution (exit code 0) from Sentry processes spawning child shells.

suggestion.title: Root-level Process Spawning from Sentry Appliance
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'root-level remote code execution' — any non-root process becoming root via Sentry indicates compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on privilege escalation events where Sentry service account (uid typically 1000-2000 range) executes commands as root (uid 0). Baseline legitimate Sentry-to-root transitions; alert on anomalous command patterns.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scan
suggestion.rationale: Article CVE identifier is primary IOC for CISA KEV tracking. Federal patch due date 2026-06-14 creates audit-critical detection timeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference vulnerability scanner output (Nessus, Qualys, Tenable) against CVE-2026-10520. Alert on any remaining unpatched Sentry instances post federal due date. Escalate based on external reachability flag.

suggestion.title: Sentry Appliance Unmanaged State Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'successfully exploited in cases where Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state' — unmanaged = no mTLS or restricted HTTPS; direct config-control signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert if Sentry appliances lose connection to EPMM or Neurons for MDM without approval ticket. Monitor for firewall rule changes permitting direct external access to Sentry ports. Flag any appliances without mTLS certificate pinning.

suggestion.title: Vishing calls targeting credential or facility access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'vishing' as attack vector but pipeline generated zero social-engineering detections. Vishing is documented initial-access technique for this campaign.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious inbound calls to security/finance roles requesting credentials or building access info, especially if followed by badge/network access anomalies within 24–48 hours. Correlate with successful phishing reports.

suggestion.title: Physical building access during staged data exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'physical intrusions' but zero badge/CCTV/access-log detections were generated. On-site presence enables direct data staging and USB exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate after-hours or weekend badge swipes to restricted data-center or executive floors with concurrent large file transfers. Flag tailgating reports or suspicious vendor activity during business hours preceding data theft.

suggestion.title: Bulk data collection and archive creation in staging directories
suggestion.rationale: Campaign involves 'data theft' but no file-operations or data-staging detections. Attackers must identify, gather, and prepare exfiltration—usually via archive/compression.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk write operations (>500 MB in <1 hour), .zip/.rar/.7z creation in uncommon paths, directory traversal patterns accessing Finance/HR/Executive shares, and process execution (WinRAR, 7-Zip, tar) from user profiles.

suggestion.title: High-volume data exfiltration over public infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Data-theft-extortion campaigns require exfil; title says 'data theft' but pipeline missed egress detections. No IOCs for C2, upload sites, or anomalous network flows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for large sustained uploads to free file-sharing sites (Dropbox, Mega, OneDrive personal), unusual HTTPS egress to non-approved cloud storage, or SSH/FTP from user endpoints. Baseline and alert on deviation.

suggestion.title: Ransom demand and threat-actor extortion communication
suggestion.rationale: Article subtitle is 'extortion campaign' but zero detections for ransom emails, data-leak announcements, or victim-shaming posts. This is critical for impact and response.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for inbound emails referencing stolen data, demands, or deadline threats. Cross-reference sender domains (spoofed or newly registered). Scan dark-web forums, Tor sites, and leak aggregators for victim name or industry vertical.

suggestion.title: Lateral movement post-physical or vishing access
suggestion.rationale: Once on-site or credentialed, attacker moves to data targets. No detection for SMB reconnaissance, share enumeration, or credential reuse across systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag rapid SMB connection attempts to multiple hosts, net view / dir commands on network shares, pass-the-hash indicators, and failed/successful RDP attempts from single user source post-vishing window.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Ivanti Sentry Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Anything in CISA KEV is *currently* being exploited' and recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt'. Pipeline ignored this explicit guidance. Scanners must check for Ivanti Sentry appliances exposed to untrusted networks regardless of patch status ('patch lag is the silent killer').
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory scan for Ivanti Sentry appliances across network perimeter. Validate appliances are not externally reachable on default ports (443/tcp typical for web UI). Flag any instances without mTLS/EPMM enrollment or restricted HTTPS controls.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Remote Code Execution - Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution'. Pipeline failed to extract execution technique (T1059.001) or RCE detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry service account and process context for unexpected command execution (bash/sh spawning, /bin/sh -c patterns, perl/python exec calls). Root-level execution of shell commands from Sentry daemon is primary signal. Look for process lineage deviation from baseline.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged Ivanti Sentry Appliance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is 'successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable'. Pipeline missed the critical discovery/configuration validation phase that identifies exploitable assets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry instances not enrolled in EPMM management plane or lacking mTLS configured gateway. Validate HTTPS access restrictions are enforced. Cross-reference Sentry inventory against management system enrollment list; unmanaged appliances are high-risk exploitation targets.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Root Privilege Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'root-level remote code execution' as attack outcome. Pipeline ignored privilege escalation component and root-context execution indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation or command execution with UID 0 (root) originating from Ivanti Sentry service account or web service context. Monitor for elevation tricks or direct root spawning bypassing sudo. Anomalous root-level activity from Sentry process tree is exploitation signal.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry mTLS and HTTPS Restriction Configuration Audit
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors'. Pipeline failed to flag this as a compensating control requiring validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Verify all Ivanti Sentry appliances have mTLS configured and HTTPS access restricted to management network only. Audit Neurons for MDM policy enforcement. Non-compliant appliances (TLS disabled, HTTPS unrestricted) should escalate as critical misconfig and immediate patching requirement.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520 Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability successful 'in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Direct hunt needed to identify internet-exposed Sentry instances before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners and network telemetry for open ports associated with Ivanti Sentry (typically 9443, 8443). Cross-reference with external IP space (non-RFC1918). Alert on any Sentry appliance reachable from untrusted networks; mTLS + restricted HTTPS access reduce but do not eliminate risk.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Attack Against Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'OS command injection vulnerability' as the exploitation vector. Pipeline must detect payloads attempting shell metacharacter injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to Sentry endpoints containing shell metacharacters (`;`, `|`, `&`, `$()`, backticks, `&&`, `||`) in URL query parameters and POST body payloads. Filter on known Sentry endpoints (e.g., administration panels, API paths). High specificity expected; payload telemetry from recent CVE POCs should inform baseline.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution from Sentry Context
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could allow...root-level remote code execution.' Post-exploitation detection requires monitoring for privilege escalation to uid=0 from the Sentry process tree.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child process spawned from Sentry parent process (or child of Sentry-spawned shell) where effective UID (euid) = 0 or real UID (ruid) = 0. High-priority detection; legitimate Sentry operations rarely execute arbitrary code as root. Correlate with failed authentication logs to distinguish attack from configuration drift.

suggestion.title: Sentry Lateral Movement & C2 Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Once root RCE is achieved, attacker gains platform-level access to conduct lateral movement and command-and-control. Article's emphasis on 'unmanaged state' suggests post-breach network reconnaissance is likely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound connections from compromised Sentry appliance to unusual destinations (non-vendor infrastructure, known C2 domains, internal lateral-movement targets). Correlate with timestamps of failed Sentry authentication or web WAF alerts. Baseline normal Sentry traffic (vendor updates, MDM comms) to reduce noise.

suggestion.title: Sentry Scanning & Reconnaissance Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions exploitation succeeds in 'unmanaged state'—threat actors must first discover unmanaged Sentry appliances. Inbound reconnaissance signals should be monitored.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to Sentry endpoints from suspicious sources (datacenter IP ranges, VPN/proxy gateways, scanning services). Look for rapid scanning of multiple ports on suspected Sentry CIDR ranges or requests probing for version disclosure endpoints. Correlate with external threat intel on CVE-2026-10520 scanning campaigns.

suggestion.title: Disabled mTLS / EPMM Bypass Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access makes interfaces inaccessible.' Conversely, disabled mTLS or open HTTP interfaces indicate elevated risk posture.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit Sentry configurations for disabled mTLS, HTTP-fallback endpoints, or unrestricted HTTPS access. Alert on any recent changes disabling security controls. Cross-reference with network telemetry to confirm if non-EPMM endpoints are externally reachable. Configuration drift detection is lower-confidence but operationally critical for patch-planning.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Detection via Vulnerability Scanner
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Federal patch due: 2026-06-14' and 'CISA KEV only adds CVEs that have been observed exploited in the wild.' Minimum baseline: map CVE to scanner signatures and flag all unpatched instances before deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scanner detection of CVE-2026-10520 in Ivanti Sentry appliances. Prioritize unmanaged instances and route to remediation team with federal deadline context (2026-06-14).

suggestion.title: Externally Exposed Ivanti Sentry Appliance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Exposure is the prerequisite for exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances (including legacy MobileIron Sentry) externally reachable on management ports, lacking mTLS or restricted HTTPS controls. Cross-reference asset inventory with external port scan data and SSL certificate fingerprints.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'contains an OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Core vulnerability mechanism requires detection of injection payloads in requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to Ivanti Sentry management interfaces for OS command injection metacharacters (backticks, $(), &&, |, ;, \n) in URL parameters and POST bodies. Remote unauthenticated requests with these patterns are high-fidelity exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Root-Level Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'achieve root-level remote code execution.' Successful exploitation will spawn processes with elevated privileges; detect post-infection activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected process spawning from Ivanti Sentry service contexts (or root) shortly after exploitation window: unprivileged shells, network utilities (curl, nc, wget), persistence tools, or privilege escalation binaries.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unmanaged Configuration State Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible.' Absence of these controls indicates vulnerable configuration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances in unmanaged state: missing mTLS configuration, HTTPS not enforced, SSL certificate validation disabled, or management console explicitly showing 'unmanaged' status. Cross-check against external network reachability.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance: Ivanti Sentry Service Port Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires external network discovery. Article describes external reachability as prerequisite; should detect initial reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for scanning/probing activity targeting known Ivanti Sentry management ports from external sources (non-corporate ranges). Pattern: SYN scans, SSL banner grabs, or multiple failed connection attempts followed by successful handshake to known Sentry service ports.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable' — foundational detection for any pre-auth RCE. Pipeline zero use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry instances (product/service detection, certificate/banner grabbing) with external reachability or public DNS records. Cross-check asset inventory for unpatched instances and prioritize per CISA KEV due date 2026-06-14.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Sentry Administrative Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article defines attack as 'remote unauthenticated user' exploitation — requires hunt for authentication bypass or missing auth checks. Pre-auth exploitation is the critical signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP 200 or 404 responses to Sentry API/admin endpoints when no prior authentication event exists in session logs. Payload inspection for shell metacharacters (backtick, $(), |, ;) in request parameters indicates injection attempt.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation on Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names vulnerability type: 'OS command injection vulnerability' — exploitation manifests as shell commands injected into application parameters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry application logs and system logs for unexpected process spawn events or command-like patterns in parsed input fields. Look for stderr output from exec() or system() calls in application error logs; correlate with suspicious process tree (shell child processes from Sentry daemon).

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution from Sentry Service
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies outcome as 'root-level remote code execution' — this is privilege escalation. Attacker must spawn uid=0 processes post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag process creation events where parent process is Sentry service account (or related process) and child has uid=0 or root privilege. Anomalies: unexpected binary execution (/bin/bash, /bin/sh), network connections, or file writes from root-level Sentry-spawned processes.

suggestion.title: Sentry Misconfiguration: Missing mTLS or HTTPS Restriction
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists mitigations: 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible' — absence of these is a risk indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit Sentry appliance fleet configs for TLS cipher strength, mTLS enforcement status, and presence of Neurons for MDM. Flag instances with external reachability, unencrypted admin ports, or missing certificate pinning.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Publicly Exposed
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'externally reachable endpoints' as necessary precondition. Pipeline missed the foundational network exposure detection: Ivanti Sentry appliance accessible on public-facing network.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for inbound access to known Ivanti Sentry ports (typically 8443 for management UI) from external subnets. Flag any instances not behind restricted HTTPS/mTLS as described. Cross-reference against documented management network whitelist.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Presence
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies CVE-2026-10520 as the exploited vulnerability. Pipeline failed to emit vulnerability scanner-based detection. Federal patch due date (2026-06-14) drives urgency.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Match all Ivanti Sentry instances (product name variants: Sentry, MobileIron Sentry, Ivanti Sentry) against CVE-2026-10520. Alert on any presence, regardless of claimed patch status. Confirm patch application on active instances given patch lag is a known risk factor.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: 'OS command injection vulnerability'. Pipeline mapped no execution-phase detection. Article does not name specific injection payloads but exploitation must follow OS command syntax.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for suspicious URL parameters, POST bodies, or API payloads sent to Ivanti Sentry management endpoints containing shell metacharacters (|, ;, $(), backticks, &&, ||) or command keywords (bash, sh, cmd, powershell, whoami, id). Correlation with 401/403 responses followed by 200 suggests bypass attempt.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution from Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'root-level remote code execution'. Pipeline failed to emit privilege-escalation or post-exploitation detection. This is the impact—unauthorized root processes spawned from appliance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry service account (typically `root`, `sentry`, or `mobileion`) for spawned child processes. Flag any shell invocations (bash, sh, python, perl), reverse shells, or command-execution tools (ncat, curl, wget, socat) running with uid=0. Establish baseline of legitimate maintenance processes to tune FP.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Network Communication from Ivanti Sentry Appliance
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation behavior implied: compromised root-level process may reach out to attacker infrastructure. Article does not name C2, but RCE implies potential lateral movement or data exfil.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish egress baseline for Ivanti Sentry appliance (should be minimal: vendor updates, NTP, internal LDAP/AD). Flag outbound connections to non-allowlisted destinations, especially to IPs with low WHOIS reputation or high C2 prevalence scores. Monitor for DNS requests from appliance to newly-registered or suspicious domains.

suggestion.title: mTLS/Restricted HTTPS Bypass Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS' protects against exploitation. Pipeline missed detection of mTLS circumvention or HTTPS access policy violation from attacker-controlled source.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For Ivanti Sentry instances behind restricted HTTPS policies, detect access that bypasses mTLS validation (invalid/missing client certs), originates from outside authorized MDM/EPMM infrastructure, or uses protocol downgrade (HTTP instead of HTTPS). Flag Certificate Authority mismatches or cert pinning violations.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unauthenticated Admin Interface Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'remote unauthenticated user' can trigger RCE. Detection required for HTTP requests to Sentry admin/API endpoints from external IPs without valid authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP 200/302 responses to Sentry admin endpoints (/admin, /api/*, /settings) from untrusted external IPs with missing/invalid auth tokens. Baseline should exclude legitimate EPMM enrollment and Neurons MDM traffic.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection via HTTP Request Payloads to Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability as 'OS command injection'; attack uses shell metacharacters (|, ;, $()), backticks in HTTP parameters targeting Sentry request handlers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP requests containing unencoded or base64-encoded shell metacharacters in query strings/POST bodies to Sentry processes with subsequent child process spawning (bash, sh, cmd.exe). Flag requests with encoding evasion (hex, unicode escapes).

suggestion.title: Root-Level Child Process Execution from Sentry Service Account
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'root-level remote code execution'; Sentry spawning processes as uid=0 is abnormal and definitive of successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes spawned by Sentry daemons (sentry, java, python parent) running as root/uid=0 or SYSTEM, especially with non-standard command-line arguments. Exclude expected service restart scenarios.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Reachability and Unmanaged State Detection
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires two prerequisites from article: 'endpoints externally reachable' AND 'unmanaged state' (no EPMM/Neurons MDM). Detection identifies at-risk appliances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference asset inventory (Sentry appliances) with enrollment status (EPMM/Neurons for MDM) and external IP reachability scans. Alert on instances exposed to internet without MDM enrollment or mTLS proxy protection.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Patch Application Audit
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry with observed active exploitation; federal remediation due 2026-06-14. Standard vulnerability hunt for unpatched Sentry across fleet.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for Sentry instances with CVE-2026-10520 exposure. Cross-check against patch deployment logs and CMDB version records. Prioritize unmanaged and externally-reachable instances.

suggestion.title: HTTP Tunneling Command Payloads in Sentry Access Logs
suggestion.rationale: Article title references 'HTTP Tunneling'; suggests base64-encoded, gzip-compressed, or multi-part form payloads in HTTP requests to bypass input validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry HTTP access logs for requests with base64/hex-encoded bodies, chunked transfer encoding, multipart form data with binary blobs, or unusual Content-Encoding headers in admin endpoints. Correlate with command execution events.

suggestion.title: Detect Vulnerable Ivanti Sentry Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt—the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL' and identifies 'remote unauthenticated user' access as the attack vector. Pipeline generated zero asset-detection use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry instances by version, product banner, or CVE-2026-10520 vulnerability scanner hits on external IPs or public-facing networks. Correlate with absence of mTLS/EPMM enrollment or restricted HTTPS protection.

suggestion.title: Detect Command Injection Exploitation Against Sentry Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'OS command injection vulnerability...root-level remote code execution' but pipeline generated zero execution-phase use cases for detecting exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to Ivanti Sentry API and web endpoints for command-injection payloads (backticks, semicolons, pipes, shell metacharacters). Alert on unauthenticated requests with injection patterns against vulnerable Sentry versions.

suggestion.title: Detect Privileged Process Execution from Sentry Service Context
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly documents exploitation achieves 'root-level remote code execution' but pipeline generated zero post-exploitation process monitoring use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned with UID 0 (root) or SYSTEM privilege from Ivanti Sentry daemon processes or service account. Flag unexpected shell interpreters or system utilities executed from Sentry context.

suggestion.title: Detect Unmanaged Ivanti Sentry Appliance Configuration
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'vulnerability can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state.' Unmanaged state is a prerequisite for exploitability; absence of mTLS/EPMM enrollment enables attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate Ivanti Sentry appliances and verify enrollment in EPMM or Neurons for MDM. Alert on appliances in unmanaged state with external reachability. Audit for absence of mTLS certificates or restricted HTTPS policies.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable' — exposure is the attack surface prerequisite.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry instances (default ports 8443, 9443) with external network reachability or accessible from non-trusted networks. Flag unmanaged state indicators in device telemetry. Baseline internal-only access patterns.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Attack Pattern — Ivanti Sentry

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Ivanti Sentry Interfaces

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry application logs for API/endpoint access without valid session tokens or authentication headers. Flag any calls to administrative or management interfaces from IP addresses without prior authentication events.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Privilege Execution from Ivanti Sentry Service

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry appliance process logs for unexpected child processes spawned by Sentry service accounts running with root/system privileges. Alert on any privilege escalation from normally unprivileged web server process.

suggestion.title: External Ivanti Sentry Appliance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability requires 'endpoints externally reachable' in 'unmanaged state'. No external asset inventory hunt was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query DNS records, public IP databases, and passive DNS for Ivanti Sentry product signatures (appliance hostnames, default ports, HTTP banners). Correlate with internal asset inventory to flag externally-facing instances that should be behind firewall/VPN.

suggestion.title: Sentry OS Command Injection Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability' but pipeline provided no execution-phase detection. This is the core attack—spawning arbitrary commands.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry service processes for spawning shell interpreters (/bin/sh, cmd.exe) or unexpected child processes. Flag HTTP POST/PUT requests to Sentry endpoints immediately followed by process creation under the Sentry service account.

suggestion.title: Root Privilege Escalation from Sentry Service
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'root-level remote code execution' but no privilege-escalation detection was suggested. Root context is the impact indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Sentry service (typically non-root) spawning processes with uid=0 or running as SYSTEM. Cross-reference process execution timestamps with web server access logs to narrow suspicious windows.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline should surface scanner hits for this CISA KEV entry as a key hunt. None were included.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any vulnerability scanner or penetration test result flagging CVE-2026-10520 in Ivanti Sentry. Correlate scanner timestamps with process anomalies on matching assets to detect post-compromise activity.

suggestion.title: HTTP 401/403 Bypass Attempts to Sentry Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'remote unauthenticated' access, implying bypassing normal auth. Detection for unusual HTTP patterns to Sentry API endpoints was absent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal Sentry API traffic patterns. Alert on HTTP requests to known Sentry admin/API paths (e.g., /api/*, /admin/*) without authentication tokens or with atypical payloads (special characters, command separators), especially from external IPs.

suggestion.title: External Exposure Hunt — Ivanti Sentry Internet-Facing Instances

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry instances reachable from untrusted networks via port scanning, certificate chain analysis, or HTTP banner inspection. Flag instances WITHOUT mTLS or IP-restricted HTTPS gating as unmanaged/exposed. Cross-reference against asset inventory to surface instances not marked as internet-facing.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Match — Asset Inventory + Scanner

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag all Ivanti Sentry assets with CVE-2026-10520 findings in scanner results. Stratify by asset classification (externally reachable vs. internal). Enforce remediation tracking against 2026-06-14 federal due date; escalate unpatched internet-exposed instances to critical.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload Detection — Ivanti Sentry HTTP Logs

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry HTTP request logs for shell metacharacters (|, ;, &, `, $(), backticks) or common OS command injection patterns in unauthenticated endpoints. High confidence if originating from external IP + successful HTTP 200 response + absence of mTLS certificate chain validation.

suggestion.title: Root Process Spawned by Sentry Service (EDR Post-Exploit)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' EDR detection for unexpected privilege escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On systems running Ivanti Sentry, alert on root (uid=0) or SYSTEM processes spawned by or under the Sentry service parent (e.g., sentry → /bin/bash, cmd.exe, powershell). Filter out expected administrative activity; correlate with known external exposure and unpatched CVE-2026-10520 status.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Externally Reachable Ivanti Sentry (CVE-2026-10520)

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-10520 in Ivanti Sentry instances. Cross-correlate with network reachability scans to identify externally accessible instances. Flag instances lacking mTLS EPMM or restricted HTTPS through Neurons for MDM as unmitigated. Establish SLA for remediation by federal due date 2026-06-14.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempts (CVE-2026-10520)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Injection attack is the exploitation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry application and WAF logs for HTTP requests containing shell metacharacters (|, ;, &, `, $()), command substitution, or argument injection patterns. Focus on unauthenticated access attempts. Alert on any successful injection indicators (e.g., error messages from command injection, unexpected stdout in responses).

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner Coverage - CVE-2026-10520
suggestion.rationale: Article provides explicit hunt instruction: 'CVE-2026-10520 — match against your vulnerability scanner.' This is the canonical recommended detection method from CISA.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Activate/verify CVE-2026-10520 detection plugin in all vulnerability scanners (Nessus, Qualys, Rapid7, etc.). Ensure Ivanti Sentry instances in asset inventory are scanned. Correlate scan results with patch dates to identify remediation delays. Flag any 'not vulnerable' results on instances with update lag.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Code Execution Post-Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article states successful exploitation 'could allow remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Post-injection execution on Sentry host is the impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor process creation events on Ivanti Sentry appliances for unexpected child processes spawned by Sentry service accounts or root. Alert on command shells, scripting interpreters, or system utilities executed with root privileges from Sentry processes. Baseline legitimate Sentry-spawned processes to reduce FP.

suggestion.title: macOS Plist-based Artifact Modification for Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article title references 'tracks user menu selections' and is a 'new macOS Tahoe 26 artifact' — strongly suggests plist manipulation for persistence or state-tracking; no use case generated despite this being a classic macOS C2 or persistence vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ~/Library/Preferences/ and ~/Library/Application Support/ directories for plist file modifications, especially those related to macOS UI/menu state. Look for unexpected plist creation or modification timestamps that predate legitimate user activity, or plist files loaded at boot-time with suspicious origin.

suggestion.title: Workspace-scoped builder privilege escalation pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'workspace-scoped builders (`builder.apps` set but `builder.global` unset)' can escalate via the `/api/public/v1/roles/assign` endpoint. Pipeline did not generate any use case correlating role-scope detection with subsequent global privilege grant.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful POST to `/api/public/v1/roles/assign` from a user with workspace-scoped builder role (verified via prior profile queries or user enumeration) with subsequent audit logs showing `builder.global=true` or `admin.global=true` set on that user. Alert if workspace-scoped builder transitions to global scope within 10 minutes of API call.

suggestion.title: Request body field injection via roles/assign API
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'controller then spreads the request body into the SDK call' — this is a body-field-smuggling attack. No detection of unexpected or dangerous fields in the POST body.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag POST requests to `/api/public/v1/roles/assign` containing request body fields outside a whitelist (e.g., `builder`, `admin` objects with nested `global` or `apps` fields that bypass normal role assignment workflows). High-fidelity if paired with successful 200/201 response and evidence of privilege change in audit logs.

suggestion.title: Backdoored Login Binary Execution with Suspicious Network Callback
suggestion.rationale: Article describes backdoor embedded in 'Linux login software'—sshd, PAM, login daemon are prime targets. Phrase: 'backdoored login software' establishes malicious code execution during authentication phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sshd, login, or PAM processes initiating unexpected network connections to non-standard destinations, or login-related binaries executing child processes not in baseline. Flag modifications to /etc/pam.d/* or /etc/ssh/sshd_config_d/* outside change-control windows.

suggestion.title: Long-Duration Persistence: Unchanged Backdoor Across Software Versions
suggestion.rationale: Article headline 'hidden for nearly a decade' indicates the backdoor persisted through multiple software releases without re-infection. This is characteristic of supply-chain compromise, not runtime injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare binary hashes of login-related binaries against official upstream repositories across version deltas. Flag when identical malicious hash persists across multiple product versions or when binary modification timestamps predate vendor release dates.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration via Compromised Login Path
suggestion.rationale: Backdoored login software can intercept credentials before or after authentication. Article phrase: 'backdoored Linux login software' implies direct access to authentication flows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual processes attached to sshd or login parent processes (strace, gdb), or sshd processes reading from unexpected memory regions. Correlate with outbound HTTPS/DNS exfiltration to newly-registered or bulletproof-hosting IPs.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated PAM Module Injection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Linux login software may be backdoored via malicious PAM modules rather than binary replacement. Article refers to 'backdoored software'—could be dynamic injection at runtime.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate PAM modules in /lib/security/ and /lib64/security/ monthly; flag unsigned or newly-appeared .so files. Monitor pam-config or pam.conf modifications for entries pointing to non-standard paths or symlinks.

suggestion.title: Login Software Supply Chain: Binary Hash Deviation from Distro Baseline
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain backdoor (implied by 'nearly a decade' of secrecy) suggests either upstream compromise or repackaged binaries in update mirrors. Phrase: 'backdoored...software' targets production installs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hash all login binaries (sshd, login, su, sudo) against official distro repos and NVD signatures. Alert on mismatches; cross-reference package install logs with OS image builds to detect out-of-band modifications.

suggestion.title: Undetected Backdoor Persistence: Zero-Day or Signature Gap in Auth Stack
suggestion.rationale: Successful hiding 'for nearly a decade' implies bypass of known EDR/integrity-check mechanisms. Article establishes long evasion window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Deploy behavioral baselining on sshd and login: flag unusual syscall sequences, exception handling patterns, or resource allocation (memory, file descriptors) that deviate from clean vendor binaries. Use entropy analysis on executable sections.

suggestion.title: Cordova-plugin-inappbrowser vulnerable versions (3.1.0–6.0.0) on iOS devices
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies affected version range and patch version (6.0.1). This is the foundational asset-exposure hunt. Article body provides concrete Splunk/KQL (UC_100_2) that pipeline should have detected or generated independently.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for cordova-plugin-inappbrowser versions 3.1.0–6.0.0 on iOS devices. Join with device vulnerability records to confirm CVE-2026-47430 exposure. Prioritize devices in untrusted network zones or with history of loading external web content.

suggestion.title: WKScriptMessage callback ID injection in InAppBrowser context
suggestion.rationale: Article core mechanism: 'passes the id field from a WKScriptMessage body to commandDelegate sendPluginResult:callbackId: with no format validation' (CDVWKInAppBrowser.m:560–574). This is the actual attack vector, yet pipeline generated zero detections for malformed, non-numeric, or enumerated callback IDs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WKScriptMessage dispatch logs for 'id' field values that are non-numeric, contain unexpected characters, or do not match the host app's pending-callback registry. Detect rapid successive IDs suggesting callback enumeration or brute-forcing.

suggestion.title: Suspicious OAuth/credential grant following InAppBrowser activity
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies T1528 (Steal Application Access Token) and T1098.001 (Account Manipulation: Additional Cloud Credentials) as post-exploitation impacts. Article provides generic OAuth hunt (UC_OAUTH_ABUSE) but pipeline generated no use cases and no CVE-specific correlation tying InAppBrowser to credential events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate InAppBrowser or cordova-plugin-inappbrowser exploitation indicators with subsequent OAuth consent grants, permission-grant events, or new application credentials within 15 minutes on the same device/user. Escalate detections where InAppBrowser loaded remote/untrusted content immediately before credential event.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary Cordova callback execution from untrusted web context
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'arbitrary Cordova callback IDs can be dispatched without validation from InAppBrowser WebViews'—core privilege-boundary bypass. No detection suggested for unexpected callback origins or privilege-escalation implications despite T1548 (Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism) being listed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Instrument Cordova callback dispatch to log callback ID, origin context (in-app vs. InAppBrowser), and privilege level. Alert when callbacks triggering privileged operations (account modification, token access, permission elevation) are invoked from InAppBrowser WebView context with unregistered callback IDs or from untrusted content origins.

suggestion.title: Externally Reachable Ivanti Sentry Appliance
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability exploitable when 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' This is the primary exposure condition; any Sentry appliance accessible from untrusted networks is at immediate risk of active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for inbound traffic to Ivanti Sentry appliances (port 443, product identification in HTTP headers or TLS certs) originating from external/untrusted ASNs. Cross-reference against known internal Sentry IPs. Alert on any unauthenticated successful connection. The article notes mTLS/restricted HTTPS is protective, so absence of these controls is a gap.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection in Sentry Logs

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry API endpoints and request handlers for shell metacharacters (pipe, semicolon, backtick, $(), &&, ||) in parameters. Flag requests from unauthenticated sessions. Correlate with process execution events showing unexpected child processes spawned by Sentry daemon.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution on Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Detection must identify unexpected process spawns with elevated privilege context on the appliance.

suggestion.title: Sentry Appliance Configuration Gap (Unmanaged State)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability 'can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state.' Appliances lacking mTLS, EPMM integration, or restricted HTTPS are vulnerable; this is a configuration risk hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for Ivanti Sentry appliances; flag any missing mTLS configuration, lacking EPMM integration, or not enforcing restricted HTTPS access. Cross-reference against external-reachability scan data. These appliances are immediate remediation targets.

suggestion.title: Failed/Unusual Authentication Attempts on Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is exploitable by 'remote unauthenticated user,' implying brute-force or bypass attempts preceding injection. Sentry logs should show authentication anomalies from external sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry login endpoints for high-volume failed auth attempts from external IPs, repeated auth bypass attempts, or unusual HTTP status codes (401, 403 clusters). Flag any successful auth from unauthenticated or default credentials.

suggestion.title: Sentry Vulnerability Scanner Match (CVE-2026-10520)

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Daily hunt: cross-reference Ivanti Sentry instances in your environment against CVE-2026-10520 vulnerability data. Flag all instances running vulnerable versions (< patched release). Do NOT rely solely on scanner status; verify patch dates manually. Federal due date is 2026-06-14.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Network Exposure Hunt

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Ivanti Sentry instances responding on public IP ranges or DNS-resolvable to external FQDNs. Flag those lacking mTLS or HTTPS enforcement. Search for HTTP responses bearing Ivanti/MobileIron signatures or characteristic admin panel paths (/mifs, /api, /security).

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated OS Command Injection Detection

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints (especially /api/*, /mifs/*, /security/*) for command injection payloads. Watch for shell metacharacters (;, |, &, $(), backticks) in parameters, especially unauthenticated requests. Correlate with absence of authentication headers.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution on Sentry

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On Sentry appliances, monitor for unexpected child processes spawned by Sentry daemon (typically running under service account) executing as root or using setuid. Alert on shell invocations (bash, sh) or reverse shells originating from network interfaces.

suggestion.title: mTLS/HTTPS Enforcement Verification
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'The use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors.' Detection opportunity is verifying hardening in place.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Verify Sentry endpoints enforce mutual TLS (check certificate requirements, cipher suites) and restrict HTTP access. Alert if mTLS is disabled, HTTPS enforcement is removed, or endpoints downgrade to plaintext communication. Cross-reference with asset inventory.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Ivanti Sentry Inventory Gap

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Ivanti Sentry Externally Reachable
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states appliance vulnerability 'can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' This is the precondition for all exploitation; pipeline missed foundational asset-exposure hunt.

Query asset inventory for externally-exposed instances; cross-reference against firewall inbound rules. Alert on any new external exposure or removal of mTLS/EPMM restricting access (mentioned in article as protective controls).

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner: CVE-2026-10520 Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends 'CVE-2026-10520 — match against your vulnerability scanner' as a required hunt. Pipeline did not generate vulnerability scanner use case or correlate with patch-due-date (2026-06-14).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner findings for CVE-2026-10520 on all Ivanti Sentry instances. Prioritize findings on externally-reachable appliances. Flag instances remaining vulnerable >7 days post patch-release date (2026-06-14). Coordinate with patch-management team for immediate remediation of critical-severity RCE on externally-exposed assets.

suggestion.title: HTTP Command Injection Payload Detection

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry appliance for shell metacharacters (|, ;, &&, ||, $(), backticks, etc.) in query parameters and POST bodies. Alert on requests containing both benign parameter names and suspicious command injection patterns. Correlate with HTTP 200/500 responses indicating potential command execution or error-based exploitation.

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution: Root-Level Process Spawning
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Pipeline did not suggest detection of RCE artifacts (child process spawning, privilege escalation to UID 0).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual child processes spawned by Sentry application process (sh, bash, powershell, cmd.exe). Alert on process execution with UID 0 / SYSTEM privilege originating from Sentry application context. Correlate process-creation events with HTTP request logs to the appliance to establish exploitation chain.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Lateral Movement from Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article describes Sentry as an appliance managing endpoints; successful RCE grants pivot point for lateral movement. Pipeline did not suggest detection of outbound reconnaissance or credential abuse from compromised appliance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual outbound network connections from Sentry appliance to internal subnets, managed endpoints, or attacker infrastructure post-compromise. Alert on DNS queries from appliance to internal hosts, credential-spraying attempts, or port-scanning activity originating from compromised appliance. Track lateral movement patterns typical of post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: Patch Compliance Tracking: CVE-2026-10520 Remediation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Federal patch due: 2026-06-14' and notes 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Pipeline did not suggest compliance tracking or post-remediation verification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post patch-release (2026-06-14), verify all Ivanti Sentry appliances have been patched across the fleet. Query patch-management logs for deployment status; flag instances still running vulnerable versions >14 days after due-date. Alert on rollback attempts or patching failures on externally-exposed Sentry appliances.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in [`../_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure`]. Substitute this CVE wherever the template references `<CVE>`.' Baseline detection for any CISA KEV entry; directly cited in source.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all Ivanti Sentry appliances (product identification, version, exposure: external vs. internal). Flag instances lacking patches as of federal due date 2026-06-14. Prioritize appliances in 'unmanaged state' (no mTLS, no EPMM integration) as imminent compromise risk.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation to Sentry Management Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'contains an OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Pipeline failed to surface the execution phase—inbound requests with shell metacharacters targeting Sentry endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry management interface logs and HTTP proxies for requests containing OS command metacharacters (pipe, ampersand, semicolon, backtick, $(), etc.) in URI and request body. Correlate with successful HTTP responses (2xx, 3xx) to assess exploitation success.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Root Process Spawning from Sentry Services
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'achieve root-level remote code execution.' Successful exploitation will spawn processes at UID 0 from Sentry daemon contexts; pipeline omitted impact-phase detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned by Ivanti Sentry service accounts (mobileironsentryserver, sentry daemon, etc.) executing with UID 0 or EUID 0. Scope to unexpected binaries (shells, curl, wget, nc, dd, iptables).

suggestion.title: Sentry Configuration Regression: mTLS Disable, Unmanaged Transition
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable. The use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access makes interfaces inaccessible.' State transitions that remove protections are high-risk.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Identifier Match: CVE-2026-10520

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and asset inventory for Ivanti Sentry instances (any version) flagged with CVE-2026-10520 or unpatched Sentry appliances. Correlate against the federal remediation due date (2026-06-14). High-fidelity indicator of affected systems.

suggestion.title: Externally Reachable Sentry Appliance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is exploitable 'where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable'; this is the exposure condition enabling T1190

suggestion.title: Sentry OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempt

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound requests to Sentry endpoints for command injection patterns: semicolons, pipes, command substitution operators in POST/GET parameters. Expected FP: legitimate administrative scripts; test with benign input containing shell syntax.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Spawning from Sentry Context
suggestion.rationale: Article claims successful exploitation 'could allow... root-level remote code execution'; detect unexpected child processes spawned by Sentry daemon/service running as root
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation where parent is Sentry service/daemon (typically running as root on appliance) and child process is unexpected (bash, sh, curl, wget, nc, ncat). Baseline legitimate Sentry child processes and exclude from alerting.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged Sentry Appliance State Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability only exploitable 'where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state'; mitigated by 'mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access'—detect missing protective configurations
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit Sentry appliances for: (1) missing enrollment in EPMM/Neurons for MDM, (2) HTTPS listener without mTLS certificate requirement, (3) open inbound access from untrusted segments. Config baseline hunt; unmanaged + externally accessible = exploitable.

suggestion.title: Sentry Successful Authentication from Unauthenticated State

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry appliance logs for: successful root/admin operations without corresponding auth events, session creation from unexpected source IPs, privilege escalation events. High fidelity if Sentry auth is strictly logged and gating is enforced.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Externally Reachable Ivanti Sentry Appliance

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article describes OS command injection leading to root RCE — need detection for the command-injection vector itself, not just scanning.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged Ivanti Sentry Appliance Inventory Gap
