suggestion.title: Sentry OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability' requiring 'unauthenticated' access. Detection should focus on malformed/suspicious HTTP payloads to Sentry endpoints attempting to inject shell metacharacters (command separators, redirects, subshells).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to Ivanti Sentry endpoints for requests containing OS command injection patterns (;, |, &, $(), backticks, newlines, etc.) in query parameters, POST bodies, or headers. Correlate with 4xx responses (failed injection) and subsequent 2xx (successful exploitation). Alert on unauthenticated requests reaching vulnerable versions.

suggestion.title: Sentry Process Spawning Child Commands as Root
suggestion.rationale: Article states successful exploitation 'achieve[s] root-level remote code execution' via OS command injection. Post-exploitation detection should identify unusual child processes spawned from Sentry parent processes running under root context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag process creation events where Parent Process = Ivanti Sentry service/daemon, Parent User = root/SYSTEM, and Child Process contains command-line patterns inconsistent with legitimate Sentry operation (bash, sh, cmd, powershell, curl, wget, ncat). Baseline expected child processes for your Sentry deployment and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Sentry Service Network Connection Abnormality Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: After achieving RCE, attacker likely pivots or exfiltrates data. Article implies Sentry controls endpoint management, making compromised Sentry a springboard for lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for network connections initiated by Sentry service processes (normal = queries to Ivanti cloud, LDAP, internal PKI). Alert on outbound connections to external IPs, unusual ports (4444, 5555, 8888, common reverse-shell ports), or repeated connection attempts post-exploitation timeframe.

suggestion.title: Sentry Configuration/Log Tampering Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Root-level RCE implies ability to modify logs, disable auditing, or alter Sentry configuration. Detection should capture suspicious writes to Sentry directories or log rotation/clearing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file-system writes to Sentry installation directory, /var/log/sentry*, or configuration files (/etc/sentry*). Alert on deletion or truncation of log files, especially within minutes of exploitation-attempt timeframe. Track calls to log-rotation tools (logrotate, clear logs) initiated from non-standard processes.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Exposed Asset Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Core hunt is identifying exposed instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances listening on public IPs or accessible via external DNS. Cross-reference with asset inventory to surface unmanaged instances. Filter for those NOT behind mTLS/HTTPS restrictions per vendor guidance.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Attack Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Command injection is the exploitation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry processes for unusual child process spawning (shell interpreters, script engines) or encoded command patterns typical of injection payloads. Alert on command execution spawned by unauthenticated network requests.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Root-Level Privilege Escalation on Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability enables 'root-level remote code execution' from unauthenticated access, representing privilege escalation from no-auth context to root.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Sentry processes executing with root/SYSTEM privileges when spawned from network-facing daemons. Detect sudo or privilege-escalation calls lacking legitimate operational context.

suggestion.title: Sentry External Connectivity Configuration Deviation
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes vulnerability only exploitable when 'endpoints externally reachable.' Configuration changes enabling external access or disabling mitigations (mTLS, HTTPS restrictions) are precursors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry appliance network policies and firewall rules for changes increasing external accessibility. Alert if mTLS or HTTPS access controls are disabled or if appliance transitions from internal-only to externally-routable.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Confirmation Hunt
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV catalogs only 'vulnerabilities that have been observed exploited in the wild.' Confirm patch status and exposure across fleet, accounting for patch-lag risk windows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for Ivanti Sentry instances with CVE-2026-10520 unpatched. Investigate patched instances for exposure overlap—when they were externally reachable before patch application.

suggestion.title: Detect vishing campaign reconnaissance patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states UNC3753 'Used Vishing' as primary attack vector. Article phrases: 'vishing and physical intrusions.' Pipeline generated zero detection logic for phone-based social engineering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for statistically unusual inbound call volumes to specific departments or employee lists, followed within 24 hours by failed login attempts, credential submissions to fake portals, or authentication events from new geographic sources.

suggestion.title: Detect data collection following physical facility access anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Physical Intrusions' as attack method paired with 'Data Theft' objective. Phrase: 'Physical Intrusions in U.S. Data Theft.' Pipeline missed correlation between physical access and cyber exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk file collection from sensitive shares and unusual USB/removable media activity following unauthorized badge access, after-hours facility presence, or guest network connections in security-sensitive areas.

suggestion.title: Detect data exfiltration to attacker-controlled infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Data Theft Extortion Campaign'—central to extortion capability is confirmed exfiltration. Article states threat stole data for extortion leverage. Pipeline missed exfiltration detection use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect large-volume data transfers to non-whitelisted external cloud services, file-sharing platforms, or residential IP ranges, especially during off-hours or from compromised internal accounts with recent credential reuse indicators.

suggestion.title: Detect extortion threat communication and ransom messaging
suggestion.rationale: Campaign objective is 'Extortion'—article explicitly states threat demanded payment. Pipeline generated zero use cases for ransom-demand communication detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound emails containing keywords associated with data extortion (exfiltrated, leaked, ransom, encrypted, deadline, payment, proof-of-breach) paired with organization name references or specific data-set descriptions, or URLs to known extortion/leak-site infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: CVE-2026-10520 Ivanti Sentry Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'vulnerability can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable'—canonical first hunt per referenced template is asset inventory of vulnerable Sentry versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for CVE-2026-10520 matches against Ivanti Sentry appliances. Cross-reference against asset inventory to identify deployed instances, confirm version, verify patch status, and prioritize appliances marked unmanaged or with unknown management state.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation via Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution' via 'OS command injection'—detect injection payloads and spawned processes from Sentry context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry access logs for URL/parameter patterns indicative of command injection (shell metacharacters: backticks, $(), pipes, semicolons, command separators). Alert on unexpected child processes spawned by Sentry service processes, particularly shells (bash, sh, cmd.exe) or with privilege level elevated to root/SYSTEM.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged Sentry Appliance Configuration Audit
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exploitation requires 'Sentry appliance in an unmanaged state'—identify Sentry instances not enrolled in EPMM or Neurons for MDM management.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Sentry appliance configuration database (or via API) to enumerate all instances and verify enrollment status in EPMM or Neurons for MDM. Flag any with management_status = unmanaged, null, or unknown. Verify mTLS is enabled and HTTPS restrictions are active per mitigation controls.

suggestion.title: External Network Exposure of Sentry Management Interfaces
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'endpoints externally reachable' as prerequisite—audit and alert on Sentry appliances reachable from untrusted networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Conduct regular network reachability scans of Sentry appliances from external/WAN segments. Alert if Sentry default ports (443, 8443, admin interfaces) respond to external connection attempts. Verify firewall rules restrict inbound access to Sentry to trusted networks only.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Command Execution Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states exploitation results in 'root-level remote code execution'—detect commands executing with root privileges following injection attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes spawned with UID=0/SYSTEM integrity level that originate from Sentry processes or are triggered by Sentry request handlers. Correlate command injection detection signals with subsequent privilege-elevated process creation.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'CVE-2026-10520' as the canonical vulnerability indicator. Pipeline produced no IOCs or use cases despite this being a CISA KEV entry with active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability management platforms for any assets running Ivanti Sentry versions vulnerable to CVE-2026-10520. Cross-reference with exposed instances detected via network scanning.

suggestion.title: Externally Reachable Ivanti Sentry Appliance Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article states exploitation requires 'Sentry appliance in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Network exposure is the prerequisite for the attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Ivanti Sentry appliances (identify via HTTP headers, certificate CN, or known ports) accessible from untrusted networks without protective mTLS. Appliances not communicating with MDM/EPMM for >7 days likely in unmanaged state.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payloads in Sentry Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'OS command injection vulnerability'; exploitation requires sending injection payloads to the appliance. Article phrase: 'remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry appliance logs for unauthenticated requests containing command injection patterns: shell metacharacters (|, ;, $(), backticks, &&), executable names (bash, sh, cmd.exe), or common injection frameworks in URI parameters or POST bodies.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution Following Sentry Web Request
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies impact is 'root-level remote code execution'; successful exploitation results in arbitrary commands executing as UID 0. This is the post-exploitation detection point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate unauthenticated HTTP requests to Sentry endpoints with subsequent high-privilege process creation (UID 0) on the appliance. Flag process lineage: web server → shell → root-level command execution within 60 seconds of request.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged Sentry Appliance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state.' Unmanaged state is an enabled condition for attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Sentry appliances with no MDM (Neurons for MDM) or EPMM registration, no mTLS handshakes, or absent management heartbeats for ≥7 days. These systems lack the mitigating controls referenced in the article.

suggestion.title: mTLS/Restricted HTTPS Control Bypass Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates 'mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors'—implying attackers will attempt to circumvent these controls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for TLS handshake failures, certificate validation errors, or repeated HTTP (non-HTTPS) requests to Sentry endpoints. Flag protocol downgrade attempts, invalid client certificates, or bypass techniques targeting mTLS enforcement.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs: 'CVE-2026-10520 — match against your vulnerability scanner.' Pipeline generated zero use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag scanner findings reporting CVE-2026-10520 or Ivanti Sentry versions identified as vulnerable. Cross-reference with network segment data to confirm external reachability. Prioritize unmanaged appliances (those without mTLS/Neurons for MDM enrollment).

suggestion.title: External Ivanti Sentry Appliance Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability exploitable only 'where Sentry appliance is in unmanaged state with endpoints externally reachable.' External exposure is the requisite initial-access condition; no UC generated for this discovery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry instances (port 443/8443) with inbound routes from untrusted networks or public internet. Query asset management systems for Sentry appliances not restricted to internal-only access. Correlate with mTLS enrollment status—managed instances have restricted interfaces; flag unmanaged + exposed.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability allowing remote unauthenticated user' to execute code. Exploitation phase (T1059) entirely absent from pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry HTTP request logs for command injection payloads: shell metacharacters (;, |, &, $(), backticks) in URL parameters or POST bodies, particularly targeting known Sentry endpoints. Unauthenticated requests with injection signatures followed by process creation on the appliance are high-fidelity indicators.

suggestion.title: Root-level RCE from Sentry Service Process
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attackers 'achieve root-level remote code execution.' Privilege escalation phase (T1548) missing. Root RCE is the post-exploitation artifact; detection must look for service-to-root process elevation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag process creation events where Ivanti Sentry web service (non-root parent) spawns UID=0 child processes (shells, utilities). Monitor for unexpected commands (curl, wget, bash, python, nc) launched with root privileges from Sentry process context. Correlate temporal proximity with unauthenticated HTTP access.

suggestion.title: mTLS/HTTPS Restriction Configuration Verification
suggestion.rationale: Article notes mTLS and restricted HTTPS 'make interfaces inaccessible' to attackers—conversely, absence of these controls is a vulnerability condition. No defensive posture assessment UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit Ivanti Sentry configurations for mTLS enablement and HTTPS-only enforcement. Verify Sentry appliances are enrolled in Neurons for MDM. Flag any instances with deprecated HTTP endpoints, missing client certificate requirements, or permissive CORS policies. Correlate with external reachability data.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged Ivanti Sentry Appliance Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article states only 'unmanaged' appliances are exploitable; mTLS/Neurons enrollment protects. Identifying unmanaged instances is the foundational discovery hunt; pipeline output is blank.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query MDM/EMM platforms (Neurons for MDM) for Ivanti Sentry enrollment status. Cross-reference with asset inventory to identify unmanaged instances. Prioritize unmanaged + externally routable appliances. Confirm patch status against CVE-2026-10520 remediation timeline (federal due date 2026-06-14).

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Exposed to Unauthenticated External Access
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'endpoints externally reachable' and 'unmanaged state' as the vulnerability exposure surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on inbound connections to Ivanti Sentry default ports (443, 8443) from external networks. Flag Sentry instances not behind mTLS EPMM or Neurons for MDM gateway. Monitor for scanning/probing patterns from untrusted sources.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload in Sentry Request
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies 'OS command injection vulnerability' as the exploitation mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Sentry endpoints for shell metacharacters in parameters: ;, |, backticks, $(), newlines. High-fidelity: external source sends injection pattern and receives 200/302 response from vulnerable endpoint.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution from Ivanti Sentry Service
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'root-level remote code execution' — post-exploitation manifests as unexpected privileged child processes from web service.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag processes spawned from Ivanti Sentry service running as root (especially shell, file utilities, or network tools). Baseline: Sentry service typically runs unprivileged; root child processes = post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: Sentry Service Lateral Movement via Outbound Connection
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation behavior; attacker uses root RCE from appliance for internal reconnaissance, C2, or lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from Ivanti Sentry service to non-whitelisted destinations. Flag internal IP connections, high-entropy domains, or suspicious ASNs. Correlate with confirmed unpatched CVE-2026-10520 status.

suggestion.title: Missing mTLS Certificate in Direct Sentry Connection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS...makes interfaces inaccessible' — legitimate traffic includes these protections; absence indicates bypass or unprotected exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For Sentry instances expected behind mTLS/EPMM gateway: alert on requests missing mutual TLS certificates, requests arriving directly at Sentry port (bypass), or requests from IPs outside approved MDM infrastructure.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Version Detection via Scanner
suggestion.rationale: Article provides CVE-2026-10520 as the vulnerability identifier and is CISA KEV (federal agencies required to patch by 2026-06-14); baseline is vulnerability scanner coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory all Ivanti Sentry appliances and confirm patching status. Alert on exposed version banners, vulnerable version detection in unauthenticated API responses, or missing patches. Flag any externally reachable unpatched instances.

suggestion.title: AUR Package Repository Unauthorized Commit/Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 400+ packages hijacked; implies attacker injected malicious code into package sources. No UC for detecting unauthorized commits, version anomalies, or account takeover on AUR maintainer accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor AUR repository for unusual commits outside maintainer's typical workflow (new committer, unusual hours, large diffs to build scripts or PKGBUILD files). Alert on package version bumps without corresponding source hash changes. Detect compromised credentials via velocity (multiple packages modified in short window by single account).

suggestion.title: Package Installation with Malicious Execution
suggestion.rationale: Hijacked packages execute attacker code during install. No UC captures suspicious process spawning, file writes, or network activity during package decompression/build phase (T1059).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bash/sh processes spawned from /tmp/.pacman-* or similar AUR build directories executing unexpected binaries, writing to system paths, or making network calls. Baseline normal makepkg behavior and flag deviations (curl to C&C, iptables modifications, cron injections).

suggestion.title: Package Signature/Hash Integrity Mismatch Detection
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks often require compromising package checksums or signatures. No UC for verifying package integrity against known-good hashes or detecting signature validation bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package manager logs (pacman) for GPG signature verification failures, hash mismatches, or fallback to unsigned downloads. Flag packages downloaded from non-standard mirrors. Compare installed package checksums to upstream AUR repository values post-install.

suggestion.title: AUR Maintainer Account Compromise Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Hijacking 400+ packages implies either credential theft or account compromise at scale. No UC for detecting abnormal AUR login patterns, unusual geographic access, or MFA bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on AUR account logins from new/unusual IP ranges, velocity spikes in package uploads, logins at unusual hours compared to maintainer baseline, or MFA disable events. Cross-reference multiple maintainer accounts compromised within short timeframe.

suggestion.title: Post-Installation Persistence Mechanisms in Packages
suggestion.rationale: Hijacked packages likely establish persistence (cron, systemd, shell hooks). Article context implies packages affect user systems. No UC for detecting persistence installation during/after package install.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for cron jobs, systemd timers, or bashrc/profile modifications written by package installation. Flag packages that create scheduled tasks for non-standard intervals or modify user shell initialization after install. Alert on file writes to ~/.config or /etc during makepkg execution.

suggestion.title: AUR Package Mirror/Repository Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Attackers may have compromised AUR infrastructure or mirrors. No UC for detecting repository serving mismatched packages, unusual metadata, or serves different content to different clients.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare package hashes downloaded from different mirrors/times. Alert on CDN/mirror serving different package content for same version string. Monitor DNS for AUR domain hijacking or unusual NS/A record changes. Flag HTTP redirects to non-standard package mirrors.

suggestion.title: Forensic Artifact Creation or Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article title references 'New MacOS Tahoe 26 Artifact Discovered'—implies the artifact exists at a specific file path. Pipeline should detect writes to or creation of this artifact file (path not available due to missing article body).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation or modification of the macOS Tahoe 26 artifact file. Alert on processes accessing the artifact outside expected forensic tools. Detect bulk reads of artifact data that could indicate exfiltration of user activity records.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Access to Menu Interaction Artifact
suggestion.rationale: Article describes the artifact as 'tracks user menu selections across the operating system'—sensitive activity log. Detect non-privileged or non-expected process reads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag processes attempting to read the artifact file that are not system utilities, forensic tools, or the OS kernel. Monitor for repeated sequential reads that suggest data scraping for espionage.

suggestion.title: Artifact Exfiltration via Network I/O
suggestion.rationale: If threat actor learns of this artifact's forensic value (via article or research), they may attempt to steal accumulated user menu data. Pipeline should correlate artifact access with suspicious network outbound.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate high-frequency reads of the artifact file with unusual outbound network connections. Alert on compression or encoding of data read from artifact path followed by exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Workspace-scoped builder requests roles/assign endpoint before privilege grant
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'builderOrAdmin middleware passes any user who is a builder' but 'workspace-scoped builders (builder.apps set but builder.global unset)' should never be calling this endpoint. The middleware bypass is the vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any POST to /api/public/v1/roles/assign from a user whose audit log shows builder.global=false. The middleware bypass means workspace-scoped builders reach an endpoint they should not. Even non-200 responses are suspicious and warrant investigation.

suggestion.title: POST to roles/assign contains both app-level and global role fields
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'controller spreads request body into SDK call' — the SDK grants builder.global=true or admin privileges without re-validating scope. A workspace-scoped builder submitting global role fields is exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect POST bodies to /api/public/v1/roles/assign for presence of global-scope role assignments (builder.global, admin.global, admin role) from users without global privileges. Any POST body containing both app-scoped and global-scoped role fields is exploitation in progress.

suggestion.title: Admin or builder role grant to service account or newly-created user
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacker escalating 'workspace-scoped builder' to global admin—a privilege transition. Monitor for rapid admin grants to users with no prior admin API activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect admin or global builder role assignments to users with no prior API calls, no prior audit log presence, or accounts matching service-account naming patterns. Excludes planned onboarding (use context from ServiceNow/ITSM if available).

suggestion.title: Workspace-scoped builder queries self endpoint after successful roles/assign
suggestion.rationale: Article describes escalation to global admin. Post-exploitation, attacker would verify the privilege grant by calling /api/global/self or similar to confirm builder.global=true.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Chain detection: POST to /api/public/v1/roles/assign (200/201) immediately followed by GET to /api/global/self* or similar self-verification endpoint within 5 seconds, from the same user/IP. Attacker verifying successful privilege escalation.

suggestion.title: Lateral escalation: admin grants admin to other users in same workspace
suggestion.rationale: Article focuses on individual escalation but doesn't address lateral spread. Once attacker gains admin, they can use the same vulnerable endpoint to grant admin to other compromised accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequences where a newly-promoted admin (from roles/assign) immediately calls roles/assign themselves to promote other accounts. Multiple roles/assign POSTs from different users targeting the same workspace within 2 minutes suggests attacker spreading privileges laterally.

suggestion.title: IP or API key pivots after successful admin grant via roles/assign
suggestion.rationale: Article describes workspace-scoped builder exploit. After successful escalation, attacker may pivot to new IP or API key to obfuscate the attack chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect a successful POST to roles/assign (200/201) followed by audit/API log entries from a different source IP or API key, attributed to the same user or workspace, within 10 minutes. Suggests attacker using privilege escalation as a pivot point.

suggestion.title: Unsigned or Hash-Mismatched Authentication Binaries
suggestion.rationale: Article states backdoor 'backdoored Linux Login Software' — core attack vector is injection into /bin/login, sshd, or PAM libraries. 'Hide for nearly a decade' implies binaries evaded hash-based integrity checks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file modification events to /bin/login, /usr/bin/sshd, /lib/pam*, /etc/pam.d/* and hash mismatches against baseline or vendor manifests. Correlate mtime changes with missing audit logs or log deletion events.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Network Egress from sshd or login Process
suggestion.rationale: Backdoor persisting 'nearly a decade' requires command-and-control or systematic data exfiltration; authentication binaries should have zero expected outbound connections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline sshd and login processes for zero network egress. Alert on outbound connections initiated by these PIDs to any external IP or non-standard ports, especially over multi-year persistence windows.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Compromised Authentication Subsystem
suggestion.rationale: Article's 'backdoored Linux Login Software' directly handles UID/GID assignment during authentication; enables unauthorized privilege escalation without sudo/setuid.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor process creation with unexpected privilege levels spawned from sshd or login parent. Detect spawning of root shells (uid=0) from unprivileged source sessions or unusual child processes from authentication daemons.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Compromise: Malicious Package in OS Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Linux Login Software' backdoor with system-wide impact and decade-long evasion; implies infection at package distribution or source code level pre-deployment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track binary hashes of login/sshd packages against upstream vendor GPG signatures and SBOM metadata. Alert on unsigned packages, hash mismatches in installed vs. repository versions, or packages from unexpected mirrors.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via Intercepted Authentication Calls
suggestion.rationale: Compromised /bin/login or PAM library enables credential interception at kernel boundary; article's multi-year persistence implies active credential collection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for anomalous read/write syscalls from sshd/login to sensitive memory regions or files (/etc/shadow, /proc/*/mem). Detect function hooking or LD_PRELOAD patterns targeting libc credential functions.

suggestion.title: Kernel Module or eBPF Hook Enabling Multi-Year Evasion
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'hide for nearly a decade' — userland-only backdoor would be detected by package manager re-verification or OS updates. Implies kernel-level persistence or bootkit-style mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unsigned kernel modules loaded post-boot, eBPF programs attached to security-sensitive hooks, or processes that map kernel memory. Detect hidden processes via discrepancies between /proc enumeration and netstat/ps output.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Detection — Ivanti Sentry Scanning Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names CVE-2026-10520 as CISA KEV (actively exploited in the wild) with federal remediation deadline 2026-06-14. Pipeline must trigger on scanner matches and patch compliance gaps. Cite: 'CVE-2026-10520...Vendor: Ivanti, Product: Sentry. Federal patch due: 2026-06-14.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when vulnerability scans detect Ivanti Sentry product instances or CVE-2026-10520 matches in environment. Cross-reference against federal patch deadline (2026-06-14) and escalate any overdue assets as high-priority due to known active exploitation.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability only exploitable when appliance is 'in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Article explicitly states mTLS or HTTPS-only access renders interfaces 'inaccessible to external actors.' Cite: 'externally reachable' and 'mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access...makes interfaces inaccessible.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry instances listening on public-facing IP addresses (0.0.0.0 or internet-routable) without mTLS certificate enforcement or HTTPS-only access policies. Cross-check for EPMM enrollment status and Neurons for MDM registration; flag unmanaged instances as immediately exploitable.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload Detection — Ivanti Sentry Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector is 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Need behavioral detection for injection payloads. Cite: 'OS command injection vulnerability...remote unauthenticated user.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints containing shell metacharacters (backticks, $(), pipes, semicolons, &&, ||) or OS command payloads. Prioritize unauthenticated endpoints and known-vulnerable URI patterns. Establish baseline of legitimate requests to reduce false positives.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution from Ivanti Sentry Service Context
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability explicitly achieves 'root-level remote code execution.' Need post-exploitation detection for unexpected child processes spawned under root privileges originating from Ivanti service or Sentry-port network connections. Cite: 'root-level remote code execution.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when processes spawn with root/SYSTEM privileges from Ivanti Sentry daemon processes or from network connections arriving on Sentry service ports. Flag unexpected interactive shells (/bin/bash, /bin/sh), reverse-shell patterns, or system utilities (curl, wget, python, perl, nc) executed as root in Sentry context.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Management Plane Control Verification
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'unmanaged state' and absent 'mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access' as preconditions for successful exploitation. Configuration audits must verify protective controls are in place. Cite: 'unmanaged state' and 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access...makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Verify Ivanti Sentry instances are enrolled in EPMM (Enterprise Platform Mobility Management) or Neurons for MDM with valid mTLS certificates installed. Alert on any instances in 'unmanaged' state (missing MDM agent, absent policy enforcement, or lack of HTTPS-only access controls on management plane).

suggestion.title: Detect Internet-Exposed Ivanti Sentry Appliances
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Asset discovery/CMDB hunt is the primary control.

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert whenever Qualys, Nessus, or other vulnerability scanners flag CVE-2026-10520 in asset discovery. Include affected asset inventory, vulnerable versions, federal remediation deadline, and correlation with externally reachable instances.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload Detection Against Ivanti Sentry Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'OS command injection vulnerability' as the exploitation vector leading to root RCE. Direct payload detection on exposed Sentry endpoints captures exploitation in progress.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound HTTP traffic to Ivanti Sentry API/web endpoints for command injection signatures: shell metacharacters (backticks, $(), command substitution), Unix command separators (|, ;, &, &&, ||), base64-encoded payloads, and common payload prefixes (/bin/sh, exec, system). Flag POST/GET parameters destined for backend command execution contexts.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article confirms successful exploitation achieves 'root-level remote code execution' — post-exploitation detection captures actual command execution activity on compromised Sentry appliance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry appliance process execution logs for unexpected root-privilege spawns, especially shell interpreters (/bin/sh, /bin/bash, /bin/ksh), system utilities (curl, wget, nc, socat), scripting languages (python, perl, ruby), and reverse shell indicators. Baseline expected Sentry daemon processes and alert on anomalous deviations.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged Ivanti Sentry Configuration Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exploitability depends on 'unmanaged state' appliances; mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS mitigates. Identify configuration gaps in management frameworks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference Ivanti Sentry asset inventory against MDM enrollment records and EPMM management console. Flag instances absent from EPMM, lacking valid mTLS certificates, or not protected by restricted HTTPS firewall rules. Correlate with CVE-2026-10520 vulnerability scanner findings.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Asset Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability exploitable 'in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Asset-exposure hunt is canonical for any CISA KEV. Pipeline produced zero UCs despite article recommending this hunt by name.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for external HTTP/HTTPS connections to Ivanti Sentry appliances (detect via fingerprint or certificate CN='Sentry'). Correlate with asset inventory to identify unmanaged instances. Leverage SHODAN/Censys queries for external surface mapping.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unauthenticated OS Command Injection Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'remote unauthenticated user' achieving 'root-level remote code execution' via 'OS command injection vulnerability.' Core exploitation pattern entirely absent from pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for shell metacharacters (pipes, semicolons, backticks, $()) in Sentry API/web requests from unauthenticated sources. Correlate with root process spawning or command execution logs on Sentry appliance.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Root-Level Code Execution Post-Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'could allow...achieve root-level remote code execution.' Post-exploitation detection for privilege escalation outcome missing entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unexpected processes spawned by Sentry service account running with UID 0 or in SYSTEM context. Detect execution of shell, compiler, or lateral-movement tools (ssh, nc, wget) post-command-injection indicators.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged Ivanti Sentry Appliance Inventory Gap
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state.' Detection should include inventory/configuration assessment, not just network traffic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory and EPMM/MDM enrollment logs for Ivanti Sentry instances. Flag appliances NOT listed as managed via mTLS+EPMM or with restricted HTTPS access per article's mitigation.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article's IOC section explicitly states 'CVE-2026-10520 — match against your vulnerability scanner.' Pipeline extracted zero IOCs; this is the minimum extractable signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-10520 against Ivanti Sentry inventory. Flag any host showing vulnerable version. Cross-reference with external-reachability and management-state indicators.

suggestion.title: Exposed Ivanti Sentry Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability requires 'endpoints externally reachable'—need baseline of exposed Sentry appliances; article further specifies mitigation via mTLS or restricted HTTPS, implying most exposures can be rapidly identified.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate Ivanti Sentry instances exposed on public internet via port scanning, certificate transparency logs, or asset management systems. Cross-reference hostnames against known vulnerable versions prior to patch deadline (2026-06-14).

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article names vulnerability as 'OS command injection'—attackers will inject shell metacharacters (;, |, $(), backticks) into HTTP parameters to achieve RCE. This is the attack mechanism and must be detected pre-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints containing shell metacharacters in query parameters or POST bodies. Baseline normal traffic pre-patch; alert on injection-like patterns originating from external IPs to vulnerable appliances.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unauthenticated Administrative Access
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'remote unauthenticated user'—the exploit requires zero credentials. Flag unauthenticated HTTP requests reaching sensitive Sentry endpoints (config, API, command execution).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of authenticated vs. unauthenticated Sentry requests. Alert on HTTP requests lacking expected authentication tokens/headers (Authorization, X-Auth, etc.) targeting administrative endpoints or command execution paths.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Root Remote Code Execution Success Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'root-level remote code execution' as outcome—successful exploitation produces observable post-execution artifacts (unexpected privileged processes, file creation as root, privilege-escalation logs).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Sentry process (or parent Java process) spawning shell interpreters (/bin/bash, /bin/sh, /bin/zsh) with arguments; file creation/modification by root originating from Sentry service context; privilege-escalation logs correlated temporally with HTTP access to Sentry endpoints.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Patch Compliance Audit
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies Federal patch due date 2026-06-14 (CISA KEV mandatory for federal agencies). Version disclosure in HTTP headers and SSL certificates enables rapid compliance verification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner output for Ivanti Sentry version ≤ [last vulnerable version]. Inspect HTTP Server headers and SSL certificate issuer strings for version strings. Identify all unpatched systems post 2026-06-14 for escalation.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'CISA KEV entry. The U.S. federal "Known Exploited Vulnerabilities" catalog only adds CVEs that have been **observed exploited in the wild**. Federal civilian agencies are required to remediate by the published due date (2026-06-14).' Core hunt for patched vs. vulnerable instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for Ivanti Sentry product with CVE-2026-10520 match. Return all instances with version < patched release. Priority: instances marked 'unmanaged' or lacking mTLS/restricted HTTPS enrollment.

suggestion.title: Externally Reachable Ivanti Sentry Appliance Network Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'vulnerability can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' mTLS or restricted HTTPS mitigates. Requires network scan + traffic inspection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances reachable from untrusted networks (WAN, DMZ, Internet). Flag instances NOT protected by mTLS or HTTPS access restrictions (detect via TLS cert subject, HTTP headers, EPMM/Neurons MDM enrollment status). Correlate with vulnerability inventory to identify unpatched + exposed instances.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempt — Sentry Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'contains an OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Requires HTTP/HTTPS request inspection for injection patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to Ivanti Sentry administrative endpoints (e.g., /api/, /admin/, /management/) for OS command metacharacters: semicolons, pipes (|), backticks (``), command substitution ($(...)), cmd.exe, /bin/bash, sh, exec patterns. Alert on unauthenticated requests containing these payloads. Baseline: filter known legitimate traffic.

suggestion.title: Root Process Execution from Ivanti Sentry Service Parent
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Post-exploitation detection: Sentry process (Java/Node parent) spawning unexpected root-owned children indicates successful RCE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor process creation events where Ivanti Sentry service (typically running as sentry/non-root user) spawns child processes with UID=0 (root) or SYSTEM privileges. Flag bash, sh, PowerShell, cmd.exe, or reverse-shell executables as children of Sentry JVM/Node process. Alert on process trees indicating post-RCE lateral movement or data exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unmanaged or Unenrolled Appliance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'vulnerability can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state.' mTLS and EPMM/Neurons MDM enrollment provides visibility and control. Requires configuration + enrollment audit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query EPMM (Ivanti MDM) or Neurons for MDM agent enrollment logs for Sentry appliances NOT reporting management status or with agent health = 'unenrolled' / 'unmanaged'. Cross-reference with network exposure scan. Unmanaged appliances with external reachability are immediate remediation priority.

suggestion.title: Sentry Appliance External Network Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'endpoints externally reachable' as prerequisite for vulnerability exploitation; pipeline failed to generate asset-exposure hunt, which is canonical for publicly-accessible critical appliances
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all Ivanti Sentry and MobileIron Sentry appliances with external network accessibility via asset inventory correlation, public scanning (SHODAN/Censys), and network flow analysis. Prioritize unmanaged instances and those without mTLS/restricted HTTPS protections mentioned in article.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level RCE' via 'OS command injection vulnerability'; pipeline missed execution-phase detection for the core attack vector
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry service processes for spawned shell commands (bash, sh, /bin/sh, cmd.exe) without preceding authentication audit trail. Alert on process creation from Sentry daemons containing shell metacharacters (pipes, backticks, substitution) in command line, especially execution with elevated UID.

suggestion.title: Root-level Code Execution from Sentry Service Process
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'root-level remote code execution' as attack outcome; pipeline did not generate privilege-escalation detection for unauthenticated service-to-root code execution
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation where parent is Sentry service daemon and child executes with UID=0 (root) without intervening sudo/su audit event. Flag this pattern as direct RCE exploitation, not legitimate service operation, particularly when paired with unexpected command execution.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Unpatched Sentry Inventory Against Federal Due Date
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV designation confirms active exploitation; pipeline generated no vulnerability-based hunt. Proactive scan-based detection required to close exposure window before federal remediation deadline 2026-06-14
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Nessus/Tenable/Qualys for CVE-2026-10520 detections across all Ivanti Sentry appliances. Cross-reference with asset inventory and patch management. Escalate any remaining unpatched instances post-deadline as imminent breach risk.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' No application-layer attack detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints containing shell metacharacters (;, |, &, $(), backticks) in URL parameters or POST bodies. Correlate with unauthenticated request patterns. Cross-reference process execution events for shell spawning from Ivanti service accounts.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Root-Level Process Execution from Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'root-level remote code execution' as endpoint; no privilege escalation detection use case was generated despite explicit elevation observable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation where parent is Ivanti Sentry service and child runs with uid=0 or exhibits privilege elevation (setuid boundary crossing). Alert on shell interpreters (bash, sh, zsh) spawned from java or Ivanti application processes.

suggestion.title: Externally Exposed Ivanti Sentry Network Presence
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'endpoints externally reachable' as precondition; no network exposure or asset inventory detection was suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Ivanti Sentry appliances (identified by HTTP headers, certificate CN, banner) with inbound rules from 0.0.0.0/0. Cross-reference vulnerability scanner results for Ivanti Sentry instances against network firewall policy to identify uncontrolled exposure post-patch deadline (2026-06-14).

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unmanaged State Vulnerability Scan Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability only present 'where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state' and references protection via 'mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM.' No management state validation detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when vulnerability scanners report Ivanti Sentry vulnerable to CVE-2026-10520 AND the appliance is not registered with EPMM/Neurons OR mTLS certificate enrollment has failed. Escalate if scan timestamp is post 2026-06-14 (patch due date).

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Vulnerable Version Presence — Patch Deadline Breach
suggestion.rationale: Article is a CISA KEV entry with explicit 'Federal patch due: 2026-06-14.' No post-deadline vulnerability persistence detection was suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when Ivanti Sentry instances matching vulnerable version patterns for CVE-2026-10520 are detected in scans dated after 2026-06-14. Correlate with network exposure and lack of mTLS/Neurons enrollment to score criticality.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unauthenticated POST/GET Request Command Execution Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'remote unauthenticated user' can exploit. No detection for authentication bypass or unauthenticated exploitation was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry that lack valid authentication headers (Authorization, session cookie, OAuth token) yet trigger application error responses or command output. Flag unauthenticated requests that return shell errors, command output, or file listing artifacts.

suggestion.title: Internet-Facing Ivanti Sentry Appliance Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability affects appliances 'in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable'—canonical initial-access indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for Ivanti Sentry service fingerprints (port 8443, /sentry endpoints, application banners) reachable from the internet. Cross-reference external exposure against internal asset inventory; flag any Sentry instance marked 'unmanaged' or lacking mTLS/HTTPS restrictions.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated HTTP Access to Sentry Management Interfaces
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'remote unauthenticated user' exploitation path. Detect missing or invalid authentication tokens in requests to Sentry endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry appliance logs for HTTP(S) requests without valid session cookies or authentication headers. Flag successful access or 200/302 responses to protected endpoints when no prior authentication occurred.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload Detection in HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'OS command injection vulnerability'—the exploitation mechanism. Detect shell metacharacters and command syntax in HTTP request parameters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search HTTP requests to Sentry endpoints for shell metacharacters (`;|&$(){}[]<>"'`), command substitution syntax (`$(...)`, backticks), or pipe-chained commands. Correlate with HTTP 200 responses or subsequent system activity from the Sentry process.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Spawning from Sentry Service Account
suggestion.rationale: Article promises 'root-level remote code execution.' Detect child processes created with elevated privileges (UID 0 / SYSTEM) from Sentry-related processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate Sentry process trees (parent/child relationships, user context). Alert on any child process spawned from Sentry with effective UID=0 (Linux) or running as SYSTEM (Windows), or unexpected process names (shells, utilities) under Sentry context.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Sentry Service Account
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation grants root privileges; detect sudoers abuse, setuid binaries modified/executed by Sentry, or capability transitions to UID 0.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor sudo logs for entries run by Sentry service user. Search audit logs for sudoers file modifications, setuid binary execution, or uid/gid transitions from Sentry's user ID to root (UID 0). Alert if these occur during or shortly after unauthenticated HTTP access.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Network Egress from Compromised Sentry Appliance
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation, attacker may pivot or exfiltrate data. Detect unexpected outbound network connections from Sentry processes outside baseline operational profile.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for Sentry appliance network behavior (allowed destinations, protocols, ports). Alert on unexpected outbound connections from Sentry processes to non-whitelisted external IPs, dynamic DNS, or non-standard ports.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry — Unmanaged Appliance Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'vulnerability can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Foundational detection — identify internet-exposed instances lacking mTLS/EPMM enrollment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances reachable from untrusted networks on known management ports, cross-correlated with vulnerability-scanner data and MDM enrollment records. Flag any lacking mTLS certificates or EPMM/Neurons for MDM enrollment markers.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry — OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'OS command injection vulnerability' as the exploitation vector. Detect injection payloads in Sentry requests before RCE execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/API traffic to Ivanti Sentry endpoints for shell metacharacters, command separators, or encoded payloads indicative of command injection (e.g., semicolons, pipes, backticks, bash -c patterns in query parameters or POST bodies).

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry — Suspicious Root-Level Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states impact is 'root-level remote code execution.' Post-exploitation, unexpected processes with root privileges spawned from the Sentry service account are the execution footprint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned by Ivanti Sentry service processes (or the appliance OS kernel) with root/SYSTEM context, especially unexpected shells (bash, sh, cmd.exe), network tools (wget, curl, nc), or privilege-escalation utilities.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry — mTLS/EPMM Protection Bypass or Misconfiguration
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible.' Detect when these mitigations are absent or circumvented.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances lacking valid mTLS client certificates or EPMM-issued certificates on inbound connections. Correlate network access logs with MDM enrollment records to flag externally-reachable instances with missing enrollment.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 — Vulnerability Scanner Asset Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends: 'match against your vulnerability scanner.' Standard IOC correlation for asset identification and patch-status tracking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Ivanti Sentry appliances flagged as vulnerable for CVE-2026-10520 in scan output with patch-deployment logs. Alert on any unpatched or missing-remediation status beyond the federal due date (2026-06-14).

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Public Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is 'exploitable in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' This is an asset-discovery problem masquerading as a vulnerability—detect/enumerate publicly accessible Sentry instances before compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Ivanti Sentry appliances reachable from the internet on default ports (typically 443, 8443). Cross-reference with vulnerability scan data for CVE-2026-10520 presence and confirmation of absence of mTLS/restricted HTTPS mitigations mentioned in article.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Exploitation Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'OS command injection vulnerability.' Pipeline must generate signature for exploitation attempts—malformed requests to Sentry endpoints containing shell metacharacters or command separators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry access logs (or upstream WAF/IDS) for requests containing shell metacharacters (|, ;, &, `, $(), etc.) in parameters targeting Sentry API/web endpoints. High fidelity indicator of active exploitation attempts against CVE-2026-10520.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Post-Exploitation Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability achieves 'root-level remote code execution.' Pipeline must surface detection for attacker activity post-compromise—unusual process spawning or shell commands executed with Sentry service account or root context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected shell processes (bash, sh, /bin/sh) spawned by Sentry daemons or initiated from Sentry contexts. Baseline normal administrative activity; flag deviations. RCE exploitation will manifest as privileged command execution originating from network-accessible Sentry components.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unprotected Interface Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article notes vulnerability is mitigated by 'mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM.' Identify at-risk Sentry deployments lacking these protections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit Ivanti Sentry appliances for absence of mTLS certificates, lack of EPMM configuration, or unrestricted HTTPS access. Cross-reference exposed systems from asset hunt; flag those without documented mTLS or Neurons hardening as critical-priority targets for patching.

suggestion.title: Externally Reachable Ivanti Sentry Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'vulnerability can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable'—foundational attack prerequisite.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan asset inventory for Ivanti Sentry (MobileIron Sentry) appliances with external-facing HTTPS listeners (port 443). Flag instances not protected by mTLS certificate validation or restricted network access policies. Cross-reference against network segmentation baselines.

suggestion.title: Command Injection Exploitation Attempts Against Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution'—exploitation is the execution phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Sentry endpoints for command injection syntax: shell metacharacters (|, &, ;, $(), backticks), command separators (&&, ||), redirection operators (>, <), and base64/hex-encoded shell commands. Alert on external/unauthenticated requests containing these patterns.

suggestion.title: Root-Privilege Process Spawn from Sentry Service Context
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation outcome: 'root-level remote code execution'—successful compromise manifests as unexpected SYSTEM/root process spawning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes created by Ivanti Sentry service principal (e.g., sentry.jar, sentry process, MobileIron services) running as root/SYSTEM when not part of documented patch/upgrade procedures. Flag bash, sh, powershell, cmd.exe spawned this way.

suggestion.title: Missing or Disabled mTLS/Restricted HTTPS Controls on Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article mitigation statement: 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors'—absence of these controls enables attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit Sentry appliances for lack of enforced mTLS client certificate validation on external-facing endpoints. Monitor for configuration changes disabling or weakening certificate pinning. Flag any certificate validation bypass attempts.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated HTTP 200 Responses on Sentry Admin/API Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Exploit requirement: 'remote unauthenticated user'—successful exploitation includes successful auth bypass, detectable via access logs showing sensitive endpoints responding without session validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP 200 responses to Sentry administrative or API endpoints (/admin, /api, /config, /status, /management) from external IP sources without established authentication session or API token in request headers. Baseline legitimate administrative access.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scanner False Negatives
suggestion.rationale: Article guidance: 'Even if your scanners say not vulnerable because of patches, it's worth one quick check across your fleet—patch lag is the silent killer'—detects scanner coverage gaps.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare vulnerability scanner reports marking Sentry as patched against actual running Sentry version (via banner grab, admin panel, API query). Flag high-confidence mismatches where scanner version detection failed or patch was reported but service still running vulnerable code.

suggestion.title: Suspicious AUR Package Version Jump
suggestion.rationale: Article describes '400+ AUR Packages Hijacked,' implying rapid version changes or unexpected package updates. Detection needed for packages showing unexpected version increments or unusual source-code diffs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package manager (pacman) operations for rapid version bumps on AUR packages or unverified GPG signatures. Flag installations where source metadata (Git commit, maintainer signature) diverges from historical baseline. Correlate with package-source logs for unintended remote URLs.

suggestion.title: AUR Maintainer Account Compromise Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Hijacking 400+ packages implies compromised maintainer credentials or git.archlinux.org access. Article should detail account takeover mechanics but pipeline extracted nothing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unusual login patterns to AUR/Archlinux accounts (geographic anomalies, new devices, off-hours access). Correlate git.archlinux.org push events with non-standard committer IPs or new SSH keys. Monitor for bulk commits across unrelated packages by single account in short timeframe.

suggestion.title: Trojanized Binary Distribution via Package Manager
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain hijack implies malicious binaries packaged into AUR tarballs. No detection hypothesis generated for identifying compromised package contents (backdoors, shells, miners).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-package installation, monitor for unexpected child processes from package extraction directories or unexpected persistence mechanisms (cron, systemd, init scripts). Hash downloaded AUR tarballs and flag mismatches against upstream repository hashes. Detect unexpected network connections initiated by newly installed package binaries.

suggestion.title: Malicious Build Script Execution (PKGBUILD)
suggestion.rationale: AUR packages execute custom build scripts (PKGBUILD). Compromised packages would embed malicious commands in build() or install() functions—no detection generated for this vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor makepkg or bash execution of PKGBUILD files for suspicious command sequences: curl/wget to attacker infrastructure, chmod +s (privilege escalation), network listeners, shell bindings, or registry/cron modifications. Flag packages where build-time execution diverges from declared package purpose.

suggestion.title: Supply-Chain Artifact Tampering Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes hijacking; detection should cover Git commit spoofing, source-tarball replacement, or checksum mismatches in package metadata—none suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Validate AUR package manifests (PKGBUILD md5sums, pgp signatures, upstream URLs) against known-good baseline. Alert on signature verification failures, conflicting committer metadata (author email mismatch, unsigned commits), or tarball SHA256 divergence from published checksums.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Access to macOS Tahoe 26 Menu Selection Artifact
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'new macOS Tahoe 26 forensic artifact that tracks user menu selections across the operating system'—baseline detection logic missing. Defenders need to monitor for unauthorized reads/writes to this artifact location.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes accessing the Tahoe 26 menu selection artifact outside normal forensic tools. Monitor for copy, exfiltration, or analysis of this artifact by unusual user contexts or processes.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via macOS Artifact Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Menu selection history across the system (implied by 'tracks user menu selections across the operating system') could reveal user behavior patterns and system state reconnaissance used in lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify non-standard tooling (shell scripts, custom binaries) that enumerate or parse the Tahoe 26 artifact to extract user preference/behavior intelligence for lateral movement planning.

suggestion.title: Budibase workspace-scoped builder used x-budibase-app-id header to bypass builderOrAdmin middleware
suggestion.rationale: Article states middleware 'passes any user who is a builder for the app id in the x-budibase-app-id header' and explicitly allows workspace-scoped builders. This header is the attack trigger — detect workspace-scoped users sending it to invoke global-privilege endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: User with workspace-scoped builder role (builder.global=false, builder.apps=[...]) sends HTTP request with x-budibase-app-id header to /api/public/v1/roles/assign. If response is 200/201 and subsequent audit shows builder.global or admin.global flipped to true, flag as successful authorization bypass and privilege escalation.

suggestion.title: Budibase request body spread to SDK escalates workspace role to global scope
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'controller spreads the request body into the SDK call, and the SDK grants builder.global=true' — this is a logic flaw where attacker-controlled JSON body fields directly map to privilege escalation. Detect when POST body contains builder.global or admin.global set to true from non-admin source.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: POST to /api/public/v1/roles/assign includes request body with JSON/form fields builder.global=true or admin.global=true. Source is authenticated but not already a global builder or admin. Response indicates success. Flag as parameter injection / privilege escalation attempt.

suggestion.title: Budibase chained privilege escalation: workspace builder → global builder → global admin
suggestion.rationale: After exploiting the endpoint to gain builder.global=true, attacker can loop and change admin.global=true. Article only describes first escalation; should detect if same user elevates roles twice in quick succession via same endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Same user makes 2+ successful POST requests to /api/public/v1/roles/assign within 5 minutes. First escalates builder.global false→true, second escalates admin.global false→true (or similar role chain). Indicates attacker chaining exploits to reach maximum privilege.

suggestion.title: Suspicious PAM/SSH Backdoor Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'Backdoored Linux Login Software' — implies PAM or SSH modifications to maintain persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected modifications to /etc/pam.d/, /usr/lib/security/pam_*.so, or /etc/ssh/sshd_config without authorized change control.
