suggestion.title: External Exposure Detection—Ivanti Sentry Management Interfaces
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable'—detection must identify Sentry appliances accessible from untrusted networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on inbound connections from external IPs to Ivanti Sentry appliances on known management ports (8080, 5556 typical defaults). Baseline expected external access and flag anomalies; correlate with asset inventory to identify shadow/unmanaged instances.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability'—HTTP or application logs will capture malicious input before OS-level execution occurs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for shell metacharacters (|, &, ;, $(, ), backticks, >, <, newline) in HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints, especially in URL parameters or POST bodies from external sources. Flag anomalous request patterns targeting known vulnerable paths.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Process Execution on Ivanti Sentry Appliances
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could allow...remote code execution'—post-exploitation, process logs on the Sentry appliance itself will show unauthorized command execution at OS level.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry appliance process logs for unexpected command execution or script invocations spawned from web service processes (nginx, Java, etc.). Establish baseline of normal Sentry operation and alert on execution outside expected patterns, especially with root context.

suggestion.title: Root-Context Process Spawning from Network Services
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies impact is 'root-level remote code execution'—detection must flag privilege anomalies where unprivileged service processes spawn root-context children.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when network-facing Sentry service processes (typically unprivileged) spawn child processes with root/system privilege context. Baseline expected privilege transitions and flag deviations; correlate with external connection logs to link to exploitation.

suggestion.title: Patch Compliance & Vulnerability Remediation Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article mandates 'Federal patch due: 2026-06-14'—continuous compliance monitoring is required to ensure organizations do not remain vulnerable past deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scheduled asset scan to identify any Ivanti Sentry instances still running vulnerable software versions post-remediation deadline. Trend patch application dates and flag systems approaching or exceeding due date without documented patch deployment.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scan Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE: CVE-2026-10520 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Pipeline produced zero detection use cases despite direct guidance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability management systems for CVE-2026-10520 findings. Correlate with asset inventory to identify unpatched Ivanti Sentry instances. Flag any instances not remediated by federal due date (2026-06-14) or organizational patch SLA.

suggestion.title: Externally Reachable Ivanti Sentry Without mTLS Protection
suggestion.rationale: Article states exploitation succeeds 'where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable' but is mitigated by 'mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access.' Detection must identify exposed instances lacking these controls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances accessible from external networks without mTLS enforcement (check EPMM integration status) or restricted HTTPS controls (check Neurons for MDM enrollment). Alert on any Sentry instances reachable from untrusted networks without documented mitigation controls in place.

suggestion.title: HTTP Command Injection Payloads Targeting Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user' — exploitation requires crafted HTTP requests with shell metacharacters. Pipeline missed execution-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to Ivanti Sentry for unauthenticated payloads containing shell metacharacters (;, |, &, &&, ||, `, $(...), $((...))). Alert on requests to known vulnerable endpoints (e.g., /api/*, /admin/*) from external IPs without valid authentication tokens. Correlate with geographic intelligence if available.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Execution from Ivanti Sentry Service
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'root-level remote code execution' — successful exploitation spawns processes with elevated privileges. Post-exploitation processes must be detected via endpoint telemetry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected processes spawned by the Sentry service account (sentry/ivanti user) or root context: (1) shell interpreters (/bin/bash, /bin/sh, cmd.exe) without maintenance windows, (2) processes accessing /etc/passwd, SSH keys, or credential stores, (3) network connections from Sentry-spawned processes to external IPs, (4) privilege escalation via sudo/su without legitimate job codes.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation from Unauthenticated to Root Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'remote unauthenticated user' achieving 'root-level remote code execution' — this is privilege escalation from guest to root, a critical indicator of successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track privilege escalation events where the initiating principal is unauthenticated, anonymous, or the Sentry service account, escalating to root/system privileges. Monitor sudoers file access, su/sudo invocations, and capability escalations originating from Sentry listening ports or process context.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Instances Without Mitigation Controls
suggestion.rationale: Article lists mitigations: 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM.' Preventive detection should identify instances where these controls are absent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query network and identity infrastructure to identify Ivanti Sentry appliances lacking both mTLS with EPMM integration AND restricted HTTPS with Neurons for MDM enrollment. Flag instances with open HTTP ports, no mTLS certificates, or MDM enrollment disabled. Cross-reference against documented vulnerability status.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure — CVE-2026-10520 Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'vulnerability can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable' and cites standard asset-exposure hunt template. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite template reference.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances via vulnerability scanner (product match CVE-2026-10520). Cross-correlate with network inventory to find externally-reachable instances lacking mTLS/EPMM or restricted HTTPS. Escalate against 2026-06-14 federal due date.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Attempt Detection — Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability' as attack vector for RCE. Pipeline missed T1059 execution technique entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry appliance HTTP endpoints for OS command injection patterns: shell metacharacters (|, ;, &&, ||, backtick, $()), null-byte injection, or command chaining in request parameters. Correlate with unauthenticated access attempts.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Spawning from Ivanti Sentry Service
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Pipeline missed privilege-escalation and post-exploitation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On Ivanti Sentry appliances, monitor for unexpected processes with root/UID-0 execution spawned from Sentry service processes. Indicates successful command-injection RCE exploitation.

suggestion.title: Sentry Configuration Compliance — mTLS and HTTPS Restrictions
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access' as primary mitigations. Pipeline should have generated configuration-verification UC but generated nothing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Verify Sentry fleet configurations: confirm mTLS enabled for EPMM connections and HTTPS access restricted to internal networks or VPN. Flag unmanaged instances (config mismatch with MDM baseline) as critical exposure.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Reachability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability exploitable 'where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Detecting exposed Sentry on external interfaces is the primary control boundary before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances (TLS port 443/8443 with characteristic HTTP headers or certificate fingerprints) reachable from untrusted networks. Correlate with asset inventory to flag unmanaged instances not protected by mTLS with EPMM.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution' via OS command injection. Direct exploitation attempts must be detected in HTTP logs or WAF alerts before successful RCE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints containing OS command metacharacters (pipes, semicolons, backticks, $() substitution syntax) in parameters. Alert on patterns consistent with shell command injection payloads prior to execution.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Root Command Execution Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability grants 'root-level remote code execution.' Post-exploitation detection must hunt for unexpected root-level process creation or arbitrary commands from the Sentry appliance context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected processes spawned with root/system privileges originating from Ivanti Sentry application context or child processes. Alert on anomalous command-line invocations (credential access, reconnaissance, persistence, exfiltration) outside baseline operations.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scanner Matching
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends 'CVE-2026-10520 — match against your vulnerability scanner.' Pipeline must surface this as primary IOC for inventory-based remediation tracking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner output (Nessus, Qualys, Rapid7, OpenVAS) and correlate against Ivanti Sentry asset inventory. Flag any systems reporting CVE-2026-10520 unpatched. Track remediation status against federal deadline 2026-06-14.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unmanaged State Configuration Audit
suggestion.rationale: Article notes vulnerability only exploitable 'in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state.' Unmanaged instances lack mTLS protection; configuration state is prerequisite for risk ranking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Ivanti management plane (EPMM, Neurons for MDM) to enumerate appliances and verify management status. Escalate unmanaged instances that are simultaneously externally reachable. Verify mTLS certificate enrollment for managed instances.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry mTLS/HTTPS Access Control Bypass Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access...makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors.' Disabling or bypassing these controls is a prerequisite attack step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry for TLS renegotiation failures, unencrypted HTTP traffic from external sources, or configuration changes disabling mTLS enforcement. Alert on connection attempts bypassing expected mutual TLS flows.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scanner Hit
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-10520 explicitly identified in article as the exploited vulnerability. Scanner detections are the earliest detection point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any scanner report detecting CVE-2026-10520 in Ivanti Sentry products. Prioritize externally-facing instances.

suggestion.title: Publicly Exposed Ivanti Sentry Instance
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' External asset exposure is the attack precondition.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Ivanti Sentry instances marked as public or accessible from untrusted networks in asset inventory or active network scan results.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload to Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'OS command injection vulnerability.' Exploitation attempts will include command injection metacharacters in HTTP requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect malformed requests with shell metacharacters (;, |, &&, backticks, $()) or command chaining patterns targeting Ivanti Sentry endpoints in WAF or proxy logs.

suggestion.title: Root Process Spawn from Ivanti Sentry Service
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'root-level remote code execution.' Successful exploitation manifests as unexpected shell processes spawned from Ivanti service context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on shell process creation (bash, sh, cmd.exe) spawned from or as child of Ivanti Sentry service processes with root or system privileges.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Network Egress from Ivanti Sentry Host
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation, attacker establishing reverse shell or C2 would trigger outbound connections from an appliance that should have minimal external connectivity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound connections from Ivanti Sentry host to non-whitelisted external IPs or domains, especially on uncommon ports or to known malware infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Service Account Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation pivoting would manifest as the Ivanti service account attempting authentication or connections to systems outside its normal communication profile.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for authentication attempts or network connections initiated by the Ivanti Sentry service account to hosts outside its baseline communication set.

suggestion.title: Externally Exposed Ivanti Sentry Unpatched Assets
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable'—detection must identify unpatched appliances accessible from internet.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for Ivanti Sentry systems missing patch CVE-2026-10520. Cross-reference with network exposure tools to identify appliances reachable from internet. Federal due date 2026-06-14 requires expedited remediation.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user'—detection must catch injection payloads targeting vulnerable endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints for shell metacharacters in request parameters (;, |, &, $(), backticks, newlines). Flag requests from external sources with injection patterns against known vulnerable URI paths.

suggestion.title: Root Privilege Code Execution Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'allow...achieve root-level remote code execution'—detection must identify successful RCE with elevated privileges on appliance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry appliances for process creation events spawned with root privileges from Sentry HTTP service accounts. Detect execution of reconnaissance commands (whoami, id, uname, ifconfig, netstat) as root following web service interaction.

suggestion.title: mTLS and MDM Protection Misconfiguration
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible'—detection must flag absent protective controls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances where mTLS enforcement is disabled, EPMM integration absent, or Neurons for MDM access controls are not enforced. These misconfigured systems are exploitable from external networks.

suggestion.title: JavaScript posting arbitrary WKScriptMessage callback IDs from web content
suggestion.rationale: Article states explicitly: 'Any web content loaded inside the InAppBrowser can fire any pending Cordova callback in the host app by posting a message whose `id` field' is unvalidated. This is the core exploitation vector but no UC detects the malicious message posting itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: iOS apps with cordova-plugin-inappbrowser (<6.0.1) where web content from untrusted/external origin posts WKScriptMessage with high-velocity `id` field values, numeric callback IDs not matching legitimate app-registered handlers, or sequential/dictionary-attack patterns against callback ID namespace.

suggestion.title: iOS apps opening dynamic/user-supplied URLs in InAppBrowser
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires web content to be loaded in InAppBrowser — article describes vulnerability as vector for 'any web content loaded inside.' Attacker must supply or redirect to malicious page; hunt for apps invoking InAppBrowser.open() with untrusted/dynamic URLs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: iOS applications invoking InAppBrowser.open() with user-controlled, query-param-derived, or redirect-capable URLs; particularly those accepting deeplinks or intents without URL whitelisting. Flag if target domain differs from app certificate bundle declared safe origins.

suggestion.title: InAppBrowser content loaded without Content-Security-Policy or from HTTP
suggestion.rationale: Article's attack surface is 'web content loaded inside the InAppBrowser' — if attacker can inject or redirect to arbitrary HTML, exploitation is trivial. Hunt for InAppBrowser loads lacking CSP, allowing inline scripts, or over unencrypted transport.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: iOS Cordova apps where InAppBrowser loads content from HTTP (unencrypted) endpoints, lacks CSP headers, or permits script-src 'unsafe-inline'. Cross-reference with vulnerable plugin version detection; flag combination of unpatched plugin + insecure content loading.

suggestion.title: Cordova callback enumeration or brute-force from web context
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability allowing 'arbitrary Cordova callback IDs' — successful exploitation requires knowledge of valid callback IDs. Hunt for web content attempting to enumerate, brute-force, or probe Cordova callback namespace.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: JavaScript code in InAppBrowser attempting to access cordova.exec(), window.__cordova__, or cordova.callbacks objects; repeated failed callback invocations with sequential or dictionary-based IDs; try/catch blocks iterating through callback ID ranges; error-message parsing to infer valid callback structure.

suggestion.title: Suspicious token/credential access following InAppBrowser navigation
suggestion.rationale: Article maps T1528 (Steal Application Access Token) and T1098.001 (Account Manipulation) — post-exploitation, attacker could invoke auth-related Cordova callbacks. Hunt for credential/token operations occurring after untrusted InAppBrowser page load without intervening user action.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cordova apps where authentication callbacks (oauth_callback, setCredential, auth_token_retrieve) or token-access operations occur within N seconds of InAppBrowser navigation to external URL, with vulnerable plugin version, and without explicit user interaction (tap, authentication dialog) in the interim.

suggestion.title: Cordova plugin version inventory for iOS InAppBrowser <6.0.1
suggestion.rationale: No hunt currently detects the plugin version at deployment time. Article explicitly requires <6.0.1 to be vulnerable; runtime asset inventory should surface all iOS apps with unpatched versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: iOS devices with installed apps containing cordova-plugin-inappbrowser versions matching 3.x–6.0.0 (vulnerable range). Correlate with MDM records to identify unpatched deployments; flag if app receives updates from enterprise store but remains on vulnerable version.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Externally Exposed Instances Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' SOC must identify externally facing instances before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances accessible from internet or untrusted networks via port 443/8443. Correlate with vulnerability scanner results showing CVE-2026-10520 or Sentry version < patch baseline (pre-2026-06-14). Use HTTP response fingerprints (Sentry/MobileIron headers) to confirm product identity.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'OS command injection vulnerability...could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Detection of exploitation attempts required before post-compromise activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST/GET to Ivanti Sentry API endpoints for command injection payloads: shell metacharacters (backticks, $(), |, &&), URL encoding variants, and command chaining syntax. Flag requests with unauthenticated user-agent and payload patterns matching known PoC exploits.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Root-Level Process Activity from Sentry Service
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'root-level remote code execution.' Successful exploitation spawns privileged child processes from Sentry appliance—essential for detecting lateral movement and data exfiltration post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected process execution (shells: bash/sh, utilities: curl/wget/nc) spawned by Sentry service processes running as root or app-privileged account. Correlate timing with exploit attempt detection. Flag interactive shell sessions or outbound network activity originating from Sentry context.

suggestion.title: Externally Exposed Ivanti Sentry Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability exploitable 'in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Asset exposure hunting is the canonical first-line detection for public-facing vulnapp.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry instances routable from untrusted networks via network scanning, certificate search (CN='Sentry'), HTTP fingerprinting (Sentry-specific headers/response patterns), or public exploit scanner datasets. Flag unmanaged instances (no EPMM/Neurons for MDM enrollment, mTLS disabled, unrestricted HTTPS access).

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload Detection Against Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article core attack: 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' HTTP request payloads containing shell metacharacters, command substitution, or common binaries are direct execution indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Sentry admin/API endpoints for command injection payloads: backticks, $(), pipes, semicolons, command separators (&&, ||, |), and common OS commands (whoami, id, curl, wget, bash, sh, nc). Correlate with unauthenticated source IPs.

suggestion.title: Child Process Spawning from Ivanti Sentry Root Context
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation delivers 'root-level remote code execution.' Post-injection, Sentry process spawns shell or arbitrary binaries as root—this is the execution phase artifact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected child processes spawned from Ivanti Sentry service (parent: sentry, java, or platform-native daemon) with UID=0. Baseline legitimate Sentry children; alert on new process names (bash, sh, nc, curl, wget, python, perl) or suspicious command-line arguments.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation to Root from Application Context
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'root-level remote code execution.' This is privilege escalation; detection should capture uid transitions from Sentry service user to root/UID 0.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for uid/gid changes from Sentry service process (typically non-root) to 0. Flag sudo calls without prior sudo -l entry, unauthorized setuid binary execution from Sentry context, or capability escalation (cap_sys_admin).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Exploit Attempt Fingerprint Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry with federal remediation deadline (2026-06-14). Public exploit frameworks and mass-scanner botnets will probe for this CVE; detection of PoC patterns is a high-confidence indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests matching known CVE-2026-10520 PoC exploit signatures (specific URI paths, parameter names, User-Agent strings from public exploits). Correlate against Shodan/Censys scanner fingerprints and known botnet IP ranges targeting Sentry.

suggestion.title: Sentry Configuration Drift to Unmanaged State
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability exploitable only when 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state.' Configuration detection is a preventive control; flag instances dropping out of EPMM/Neurons management.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Sentry configuration API or enrollment database to detect loss of mTLS enrollment, disabled Neurons for MDM integration, or public HTTPS access without IP restrictions. Alert on appliances unmanaged >N days or recently downgraded from managed to unmanaged state.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Asset discovery and exposure assessment are the foundational hunt. The article recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' as the primary detection method.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate Ivanti Sentry instances across internal and external IP ranges via port scanning (typically 8443), DNS passive enumeration, and SSL certificate lookups. Flag instances without mTLS (per article: 'use of mTLS with EPMM...makes interfaces inaccessible') or restricted HTTPS access, or flagged as unmanaged in MDM enrollment records.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scanner Alerts
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends 'CVE: CVE-2026-10520' as explicit scan target. Pipeline must extract and operationalize the CVE identifier as a vulnerability IOC against scanner output. Federal due date 2026-06-14 is the remediation deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any vulnerability scanner result flagging CVE-2026-10520 in Ivanti Sentry instances, regardless of scanner confidence. Correlate with asset inventory to prioritize external instances. Escalate if scan is post-federal due date (2026-06-14).

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload Detection — Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Detection must identify the exploitation technique itself: command injection payloads (backticks, $(…), pipes, command separators).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP request bodies to Ivanti Sentry appliances for OS command injection patterns: backticks, `$(…)`, `|`, `||`, `&&`, `;`, newlines in parameter values. Correlate with 200 responses and subsequent process execution events on Sentry appliances. Flag unauthenticated requests (no session cookie) containing injection payloads.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unmanaged Instance Identification
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies unmanaged status as the critical vulnerability precondition: 'vulnerability can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state.' Detection must surface appliances not enrolled in EPMM or lacking mTLS protection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query EPMM and Sentry enrollment databases for instances with 'unmanaged' status. Cross-reference with mTLS certificate inventory (article: 'use of mTLS with EPMM…makes interfaces inaccessible'). Flag any unmanaged appliance with external routing or public DNS A/AAAA records.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Code Execution from Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'root-level remote code execution' — post-exploitation detection must capture high-privilege shell spawning and system-level commands from Sentry processes, indicating successful exploitation and privilege escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on shell spawning (/bin/bash, /bin/sh, cmd.exe) with parent process owned by Sentry service accounts AND executed as root/SYSTEM. Flag unusual child processes (network tools: curl, wget; persistence mechanisms: crontab, systemctl). Sentry often runs with elevated privileges as a management appliance.

suggestion.title: Network Scanning for Exposed Ivanti Sentry Ports
suggestion.rationale: Discovery phase preceding exploitation of public-facing appliance. Article mentions external reachability as the vulnerability condition; detection should identify reconnaissance probes targeting Sentry appliances before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect network scanning activity targeting Ivanti Sentry default ports (8443 HTTPS, 443, or custom ports) from external IPs: SYN flood patterns, sequential port increments, version-grab requests (GET / without authentication). Follow-up with command-injection payload detection.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Unauthenticated RCE requires public internet visibility.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory and port scans for Ivanti Sentry listening on tcp/443 or tcp/8443 reachable from untrusted networks. Cross-reference against managed state flags and patch status. Flag unmanaged instances as exploitation-ready.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Command Injection Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'OS command injection vulnerability...allow[s] a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Exploitation involves shell metacharacters or command substitution in HTTP requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry HTTP request logs for payloads containing shell syntax: pipes (|), command chaining (&, ;, &&, ||), command substitution ($(...), backticks), or environment variable expansion ($VAR). Alert on requests from unauthenticated sources or unusual User-Agent patterns.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Root Process Execution Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'root-level remote code execution.' Successful exploitation spawns processes running as UID=0 from the Sentry application context, abnormal for standard operation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On Sentry appliances (Java/Tomcat base), alert on child processes with UID=0 spawned from Sentry parent process (e.g., /bin/bash, /bin/sh, system binaries invoked post-injection). Correlate with HTTP access logs to the same timestamp.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Patch Compliance by Federal Due Date
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Federal patch due: 2026-06-14.' CISA KEV requires federal civilian agencies to remediate by this date; implies active exploitation pressure and audit/regulatory scrutiny.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Generate inventory of all Ivanti Sentry instances (product/version discovery). Flag any instance not patched or exception-documented by 2026-06-14. Cross-reference with external exposure scans to identify highest-risk unpatched systems.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Restricted Access Configuration Validation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors.' Detection should confirm deployment of these mitigations where unpatched instances exist.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For Sentry instances not yet patched, verify mTLS enforcement (certificate pinning, mutual auth), restricted firewall rules, and Neurons MDM integration. Flag instances with none of these controls as exploitable regardless of patch status.

suggestion.title: AUR Package Maintainer Account Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article documents hijack of 400+ AUR packages; implies initial compromise of maintainer credentials or repository trust. Title explicitly mentions 'packages hijacked'—requires account takeover or session compromise detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual AUR repository access patterns, failed authentication attempts against package maintainer accounts, geographic anomalies in Git commits, or SSH key usage from new locations. Correlate with published package update timestamps.

suggestion.title: Malicious Post-Installation Script Execution from AUR Packages
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain compromise via AUR typically leverages PKGBUILD post-install hooks to execute attacker code during package installation. Article describes 'hijacked packages'—these must contain execution payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected shell or binary execution spawned from pacman/makepkg processes. Flag suspicious network connections immediately after AUR package installation. Monitor for creation of systemd timers, cron jobs, or rc.local modifications by package post-install scripts.

suggestion.title: AUR Package Dependency Tree Manipulation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Compromised AUR packages often inject malicious dependencies. The phrase '400+ packages' suggests lateral spread through the dependency graph, not isolated attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PKGBUILD file modifications for new or unexpected dependency declarations. Flag packages where dependency versions suddenly change or depend on newly-created packages. Cross-reference package update metadata against Git commit history.

suggestion.title: Suspicious AUR Repository Metadata Changes
suggestion.rationale: Hijacking 400+ packages requires modifying package metadata, maintainer assignments, or build outputs. 'Atomic Arch Campaign' implies coordinated modification across multiple packages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline AUR package metadata (build timestamps, maintainer signatures, source URLs). Alert on bulk changes to PKGBUILD files, signature mismatches, or orphaned package re-assignment to new accounts. Monitor Git logs for bulk commits with unusual authorship.

suggestion.title: Supply-Chain Poisoning: Binary Hash Mismatch Detection
suggestion.rationale: Compromised packages likely have payload binaries that differ from legitimate upstream sources. Title confirms package hijacking—binaries will not match published checksums.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain checksums of all installed AUR packages. Flag when downloaded or installed binaries have hashes that deviate from published manifests. Correlate with package version metadata.

suggestion.title: Post-Install Hook Execution Anomalies in Linux Package Management

suggestion.title: Custom Binary Launching SSH Sessions via HTTP POST Parameters

suggestion.title: Splunk Process Child Spawning from RCE

suggestion.title: Splunk Instance Discovery via Port Scanning

suggestion.title: Session Token / Authentication Bypass Indicators

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor AUR for: login anomalies on maintainer accounts, package uploads from non-standard IPs, rapid version bumps without corresponding git history, or uploads of packages previously owned by different maintainers.

suggestion.title: Post-Installation Command Execution from Compromised Packages
suggestion.rationale: Campaign nature and scale suggest persistent backdoor delivery. Should detect arbitrary code execution during package installation—'PKGBUILD scripts executing unexpected binaries.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag package post-install scripts containing curl/wget/nc spawning network processes, shell escapes, privilege escalation attempts, or writes to system-wide startup locations (cron, systemd, etc.).

suggestion.title: C2 Beaconing from Infected Package Systems
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attack affecting 400+ systems likely results in widespread malware deployment. Critical severity suggests active command-and-control infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate systems with recent AUR package installations against C2 signature—outbound connections to non-standard ports, DGA-pattern domains, or beaconing to confirmed malicious infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Supply-Chain Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Scale of attack (400+ packages) suggests ecosystem-wide infection. Should detect reconnaissance and lateral movement from compromised client systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on systems with compromised AUR packages performing SSH/RDP scanning, network enumeration (whoami, id, arp, hostname), LDAP queries, or mass-credential attempts against internal infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Attack Campaign Tracking - Atomic Arch Attribution
suggestion.rationale: Article names campaign 'Atomic Arch'—pipeline should maintain threat-actor playbook correlations, group indicators by campaign, and track ecosystem-wide impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain campaign-level SIEM dashboards aggregating: affected package names, compromised maintainer accounts, C2 infrastructure, affected user systems, and remediation metrics. Cross-reference against community advisories and mirror integrity checks.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Access to macOS Tahoe 26 Menu Selection Artifact
suggestion.rationale: Article describes artifact that 'tracks user menu selections across the operating system'—forensic artifact is a detective's signal and an adversary's persistence footprint. Pipeline missed opportunity to detect access to the artifact location itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file system access, reads, or modifications to macOS Tahoe 26 user menu artifact locations (typically library/caches or forensic-artifact-specific paths). Baseline normal access patterns and alert on out-of-band reads by non-system processes or at unusual times.

suggestion.title: Anomalous macOS Tahoe 26 Menu Selection Behavior Change
suggestion.rationale: Artifact 'tracks user menu selections'—abnormal patterns in historical menu activity could indicate lateral movement, privilege escalation, or user-account compromise. Pipeline failed to propose behavioral detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of typical user menu selections per user/machine. Alert on statistically significant deviations (new menu items accessed, timing anomalies, rapid sequential selections). Useful for detecting automated lateral-movement discovery or reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: Forensic Artifact Timestamp Manipulation on macOS Tahoe 26
suggestion.rationale: Forensic artifacts are attack-surface for anti-forensics. Article introduces new artifact—pipeline should have proposed detection of tampering with its metadata or access timestamps to evade forensic analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for direct writes, deletions, or timestamp modifications to macOS Tahoe 26 menu artifact files. Correlate with tools like touch, SetFile, or low-level file-system calls. Alert on mismatches between file-creation time and system boot time.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is exploitable 'in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Requires network-layer detection of exposed appliances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances reachable from untrusted networks lacking mTLS/firewall-based access controls. Query firewall/proxy logs for inbound connections to Sentry default ports (443, 8443, 8004) from external IP ranges. Flag appliances in 'unmanaged' state per MDM inventory.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry OS Command Injection Attack Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is 'OS command injection' enabling 'root-level remote code execution.' Article describes injection attack vector but pipeline missed execution-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints for shell metacharacters (backticks, $(), pipes, semicolons, &&) and command substitution patterns. Correlate with process creation events from Sentry service context spawning shells (/bin/bash, /bin/sh, python, curl with -c flags). Baseline legitimate service process tree and alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unauthenticated Root Access
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'remote unauthenticated user' achieving 'root-level' execution. Detection gap for post-exploitation privilege indicators and unauth API abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation events where parent process is an HTTP handler/Sentry service and spawned process runs as root/uid=0. Monitor for privilege escalation within Sentry service context (setuid, sudo, direct root spawning). Baseline expected Sentry-spawned processes and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Configuration Baseline Drift
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'unmanaged state' as exploitation precondition. Requires detection for appliances deviating from hardened config (missing mTLS, exposed interfaces, firewall rules disabled).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Sentry appliance configs for: (1) mTLS disabled or misconfigured, (2) HTTPS access controls absent/permissive, (3) Unmanaged state flag in MDM, (4) Public routing to admin interfaces. Compare against hardened baseline. Correlate missing mTLS + unmanaged + external routing = exploitation risk.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Suspicious Policy Deployment Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Successful root RCE on Sentry creates lateral movement risk into managed endpoints. Article describes Sentry's MDM/EPMM function but pipeline missed detection for malicious policy push.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor policy push/deployment events from Ivanti Sentry to endpoints for timing correlation with exploitation windows. Flag policy changes introducing persistence mechanisms, C2 endpoints, or credential theft. Correlate source Sentry appliance patch status (CVE-2026-10520 vulnerable) with downstream endpoint compromise signals.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Default Credentials / Weak Auth Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article notes unauthenticated access pathway. Detection for credential-based attacks and weak auth on appliance APIs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry admin APIs for high-frequency failed auth attempts followed by successful admin-level API calls without session tokens. Alert on logins using default/weak credentials (admin/admin, root/root patterns). Flag successful API calls from external IP ranges without corresponding login event.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names CVE-2026-10520 as the vulnerability and notes federal patch due date of 2026-06-14. Pipeline generated zero IOC or detection coverage for this actively exploited vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners for Ivanti Sentry appliances matching CVE-2026-10520. Cross-reference patch management logs for unpatched instances after 2026-06-14 deadline. Correlate against asset inventory to identify exposed appliances still at risk of exploitation.

suggestion.title: External Ivanti Sentry Network Exposure Baseline
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability exploitable only when 'endpoints externally reachable' and 'in an unmanaged state' — conditional risk factors requiring network-layer detection that pipeline completely omitted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline HTTPS and management ports of Ivanti Sentry appliances. Alert on new external network exposure (inbound from untrusted CIDR ranges). Cross-reference against configurations to identify appliances lacking mTLS protection or restricted HTTPS access mentioned as mitigations in the article.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Attack Detection on Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability' as the exploitation mechanism — the actual attack vector. Pipeline missed execution-phase detection for command injection payloads (T1059.001) entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to Ivanti Sentry management interfaces for command injection syntax (pipes, semicolons, backticks, command substitution, shell metacharacters) in query parameters and POST bodies. Alert on payloads attempting to inject system commands into fields that should be controlled application input.

suggestion.title: Successful Remote Code Execution on Ivanti Sentry (Root Privilege)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability achieves 'root-level remote code execution' — privilege escalation and impact phase signals completely absent from pipeline output despite being central to threat profile.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on root-level process execution on Ivanti Sentry appliances following unauthenticated inbound requests. Look for unexpected privilege escalation, sudo/su events with system commands, or root-spawned child processes immediately after web requests from external sources.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Sentry appliance...with its endpoints externally reachable' enables exploitation. Asset exposure is the detection gate before exploitation becomes viable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for Ivanti Sentry appliances on public internet via banner-detection on port 8443 (or SSL/TLS certificate CN matching). Correlate against organization's asset inventory to identify unaccounted externally-reachable instances.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry OS Command Injection Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Detection must target injection payloads before successful RCE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints for OS command injection patterns (backticks, $(), semicolon-delimited commands, pipe operators) in request parameters. Flag requests from unauthenticated sessions with suspicious payloads.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Post-Exploitation Root Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article: vulnerability 'could allow...root-level remote code execution.' Detection should trigger on unexpected shell/command execution at root privilege on Sentry appliances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bash/sh/command spawning as root or SYSTEM on Ivanti Sentry appliances, especially if parent process is a web service (Tomcat, httpd). Correlate with prior external network access.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unmanaged Deployment Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'vulnerability...can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state.' Identifies high-risk deployments before exploitation occurs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query MDM/EPMM enrollment status for all Ivanti Sentry appliances. Flag devices not enrolled or lacking mTLS configuration as critically exploitable per article risk factors.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scan Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names CVE-2026-10520 and states 'patch lag is the silent killer' with federal due date 2026-06-14. Must detect unpatched instances across fleet inventory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for CVE-2026-10520 matches on Ivanti Sentry products. Cross-reference with asset registry to identify unpatched instances. Flag any appliances past federal due date without patches applied.

suggestion.title: Externally Reachable Ivanti Sentry Appliance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'vulnerability can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Network exposure is the precondition for exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry instances with public IP addresses, externally routable interfaces, or lacking WAF/mTLS protection mentioned in article. Prioritize unmanaged appliances (those not configured with mTLS via EPMM or restricted HTTPS as article states).

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Attack Attempts on Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability mechanism: 'contains an OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user.' Must detect attack delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry HTTP/HTTPS endpoints for unauthenticated requests with command injection metacharacters (;, |, &, `, $()) in parameters. Alert on payloads attempting shell command syntax in request paths or POST bodies.

suggestion.title: Root-Level RCE Post-Exploitation Detection on Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article states successful exploitation achieves 'root-level remote code execution.' Must detect execution phase after injection succeeds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected process creation or command execution spawned by Sentry process running as root/SYSTEM. Look for unusual binaries, network connections, or privilege escalation attempts originating from compromised Sentry appliance.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged vs. Managed Sentry Risk Posture
suggestion.rationale: Article provides risk differentiation: unmanaged appliances are vulnerable, but 'mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors.' Inventory gap on management status.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit all Ivanti Sentry appliances for management status: identify any not enrolled in EPMM, lacking mTLS configuration, or without restricted HTTPS access. Unmanaged instances are exploitable; managed instances are protected.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry - Unauthenticated Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 'remote unauthenticated user' achieves 'root-level remote code execution' via OS command injection. Zero detection UC for identifying exploitation attempts despite explicit attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry appliances for unauthenticated HTTP/HTTPS requests containing shell metacharacters or command injection patterns (backticks, $(), semicolons, pipes, &&, ||) in request parameters or POST bodies. Filter by external source IPs. Alert on requests to administrative or API endpoints from non-management subnets.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry - Post-Exploitation Process Activity Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'root-level remote code execution' as impact but no behavioral detection for successful exploitation post-injection. Successful RCE spawns arbitrary processes under root context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for legitimate Sentry service process activity. Alert on anomalous process creation (bash, sh, cmd.exe, PowerShell, wget, curl, netcat) from Sentry service principal or root user. Correlate temporal proximity to inbound exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry - At-Risk Appliance Inventory Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability exploitable only 'where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable' and 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access makes interfaces inaccessible.' Identifies clear preconditions; no inventory-based detection provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Asset discovery hunt: identify all Ivanti Sentry instances lacking (a) mTLS with EPMM, (b) Neurons for MDM, or (c) restricted HTTPS access. Confirm external reachability via perimeter network scans. Flag as immediately exploitable; prioritize for emergency patching before 2026-06-14 federal deadline.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry - Abnormal Egress Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Successful root RCE typically enables callback, lateral movement, or data exfiltration. Article does not describe post-exploitation behavior but threat actor motivation with root access is clear; no UC for C2 or exfil patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline outbound connections from Ivanti Sentry appliances (vendor updates, NTP, DNS only). Alert on unexpected external egress, especially to non-standard ports, P2P addresses, or known C2 infrastructure. Correlate timing with inbound exploitation window.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry - CVE-2026-10520 Patch Status Compliance
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry with explicit federal remediation deadline. Article states 'Federal patch due: 2026-06-14'; no compliance or patch verification UC provided despite regulatory deadline and active exploitation status.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query patch management and vulnerability scanning systems for unpatched Ivanti Sentry appliances. Flag any unpatched instances found after the federal due date. Post-deadline, correlate unpatched appliances against incident logs; unpatched status + inbound exploitation traffic = probable compromise.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520 Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'OS command injection vulnerability' enabling 'remote unauthenticated' exploitation; requires detection of injection payloads in HTTP parameters targeting Sentry endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry interfaces (ports 443, 5000-5001, 8443) for OS command injection metacharacters in parameters: $(command), `command`, |, ;, &&, || in request payloads. Correlate with known vulnerable endpoint patterns (e.g., /api/*, /admin/*, mobile management interfaces) and external source IPs.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Post-Exploitation: Root Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'root-level remote code execution' — successful exploitation manifests as root-owned process spawning from Sentry web service context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On Linux appliances running Ivanti Sentry, detect child processes spawned with UID 0 (root) from web service parent processes (httpd, nginx, Sentry daemon). Flag first-time-seen system utilities (curl, wget, bash, sh, nc, ncat) invoked at root level from network-accessible service context.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Asset Exposure: Externally Reachable Unmanaged Appliances
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'can be successfully exploited in cases where Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with endpoints externally reachable' — critical precondition requiring asset inventory hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query for Ivanti Sentry services listening on internet-facing addresses (ports 443, 5000, 5001, 8443) via netstat/ss or network telemetry. Identify instances not enrolled in EPMM/Neurons MDM (mentioned as mitigating control). Cross-reference with vulnerability scanner to determine patch status relative to CVE-2026-10520 fixed versions.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Authentication Spike — Exploitation Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Pre-exploitation, attackers probe unmanaged appliances for access points; spikes in failed auth attempts and unusual request patterns precede successful injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry access logs for sustained elevated request rates from single source IP, unusual User-Agent strings, rapid endpoint enumeration (404 spike), or failed authentication attempts against admin/API paths. Correlate timing with subsequent successful exploitation.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Privilege Escalation: Unexpected Root Process Lineage
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'root-level' achievement; detect anomalous privilege escalation paths distinct from normal service restarts or maintenance operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag processes gaining root privileges through mechanisms other than expected service restart or sudo rules (e.g., capability-based escalation, exploit-driven escalation). On Sentry appliances, baseline normal root-spawning patterns and alert on deviations, especially if preceded by inbound network requests to web service ports.

suggestion.title: Exposed Ivanti Sentry Instance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability requires 'endpoints externally reachable' and affects 'unmanaged state' appliances. Detecting exposed instances is the canonical initial-access hunt for this CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for externally accessible Ivanti Sentry instances on default ports (8443 typical). Fingerprint via HTTP headers, certificate CN, or known URI patterns (/api/v1/, /system/). Cross-reference against asset inventory to identify unmanaged deployments missing mTLS or restricted HTTPS.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Command Injection Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article defines attack vector as 'OS command injection vulnerability'—requires detection of malicious payloads targeting injection points. Pipeline omitted execution-phase detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry API endpoints for shell metacharacters (|, &, ;, `, $, >>, <) and common injection patterns in query strings and POST bodies. Flag requests with command substitution syntax or encoded variants targeting known vulnerable parameters.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Remote Code Execution—Sentry Process Execution Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'root-level remote code execution' achievable via injection. Post-exploitation detection requires process execution monitoring on Sentry hosts, absent from use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected process execution spawned by Sentry daemons with SYSTEM/root privileges (e.g., bash, sh, cmd.exe child processes from Java/appliance processes). Correlate with HTTP request events to confirm remote trigger.

suggestion.title: Sentry Patch Status / Configuration Audit
suggestion.rationale: Article notes mTLS and restricted HTTPS access mitigate exploitation. Detection should include proactive configuration checks to identify at-risk deployments (unmanaged, exposed, no mTLS), not just reactive incident response.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for Ivanti Sentry instances lacking mTLS, restricted HTTPS ingress, or management enrollment. Cross-reference vulnerability scanner results against CVE-2026-10520. Flag any unpatched instances in unmanaged state.

suggestion.title: Sentry Authentication Bypass / Unauthenticated Access Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'remote unauthenticated user'—attack does not require valid credentials. Detection should flag unauthenticated API calls to sensitive Sentry endpoints (command injection targets).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to Sentry API endpoints without valid session tokens, client certs, or API keys. Particularly sensitive: requests to parameter/config/system endpoints originating from untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Reverse Shell / Outbound Command-and-Control Post-RCE
suggestion.rationale: Once RCE is achieved, attacker would establish persistence. Article does not detail post-exploitation, but command-injection RCE typically leads to reverse shell or data exfiltration. Should detect anomalous outbound connections from Sentry appliance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound TCP/UDP connections from Sentry appliance to non-whitelisted external IPs/domains, especially on high-numbered ports. Flag DNS queries for dynamic domains or suspicious FQDN patterns from Sentry host.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution' via 'OS command injection vulnerability'—clear initial-access signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to Ivanti Sentry services for command injection patterns (shell metacharacters: semicolons, pipes, backticks, $(…) substitution) in request payloads. Alert if requests originate from untrusted networks and appliance is marked unmanaged.

suggestion.title: Root Process Spawning from Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly promises 'root-level remote code execution'—privilege escalation to root is the exploitation outcome.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes spawned by Ivanti Sentry service accounts or daemons running as root, especially shell interpreters (/bin/bash, /bin/sh, /usr/bin/python) spawning unexpected commands or opening reverse shells.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged Ivanti Sentry Inventory Exposure Check
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable'—explicit conditional for exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset database for Ivanti Sentry instances (product name or version from CMDB) flagged as 'unmanaged' or lacking MDM enrollment. Cross-check against network perimeter scans to confirm external reachability; alert on externally-exposed unmanaged instances without mTLS or restricted HTTPS.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry mTLS / Restricted HTTPS Configuration Gap
suggestion.rationale: Article notes mitigation: 'The use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors'—absence of these controls is a finding.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit Ivanti Sentry configurations for presence of mTLS enforcement and HTTPS access restrictions. Flag instances exposed to external networks lacking these controls as high-risk. Verify certificate pinning and client-certificate requirements are enabled.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Patch Compliance for Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV with federal patch due date 2026-06-14 mandates scan-based remediation tracking; article explicitly references standard asset-exposure template.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-10520 across all Ivanti Sentry instances. Alert on unpatched instances with external exposure. Correlate with MDM enrollment state; prioritize remediation for unmanaged appliances by 2026-06-14 federal deadline.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Service Restart or Behavioral Anomaly Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: OS command injection execution suggests attacker may modify service state, configurations, or spawn child processes inconsistent with baseline behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline behavior for Ivanti Sentry process trees (normal parent-child relationships, spawned interpreters, network connections). Alert on deviations: unexpected child processes, shell spawning, outbound network connections to non-whitelisted IPs, or rapid service restarts after HTTP requests from untrusted sources.

suggestion.title: AI-Generated Phishing Email Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'AI Phishing' as the attack vector. No detection logic was generated despite this being the core threat. Requires behavioral indicators: unusual sender reputation history, high-entropy subject lines, mismatched sender domain TLDs, and rapid email volume spikes from new senders.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails with AI-generated characteristics: novel sender+subject+body combinations, grammatically perfect with subtle anomalies (overuse of filler phrases), or rapid variant generation from lookalike domains. Flag if recipient is in credential-sensitive group (Finance, HR, Executive).

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via Phishing Landing Page
suggestion.rationale: Article discusses phishing volume crushing SOCs, implying high-velocity credential theft. No credential-access detection suggested. Typical AI phishing campaigns serve fake login portals or credential forms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound connections to lookalike or newly registered domains mimicking legitimate services (e.g., *.office365-verify.com, *.paypal-secure.io). Correlate with email gateway blocks and user reports to identify phishing landing pages receiving credential submissions.

suggestion.title: Malicious Attachment Execution Post-Phishing Click
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'alert volume' burden; typical phishing campaigns attach malware (Office macros, scripts). Pipeline did not suggest execution-phase detections despite implied breach chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Office documents (DOCX, XLSX) opened from email attachment paths executing child processes: WScript.exe, PowerShell, cmd.exe, or LOLBins (mshta.exe, regsvcs.exe). Flag if parent process is WINWORD.EXE or EXCEL.EXE and child runs in %TEMP% or %APPDATA%.

suggestion.title: SOC Alert Fatigue Exploitation (Defense Evasion)

Correlate with security team alert queue depth to identify potential saturation attacks.

suggestion.title: Link-Based Phishing with Redirect Chains
suggestion.rationale: AI phishing often uses URL shorteners and redirect chains to evade URL filtering. Article does not describe this tactic explicitly but is standard in high-volume campaigns. Pipeline should suggest detection for indirect delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails with shortened URLs or multi-hop redirects (bitly, tinyurl, *.bit.do). Monitor proxy for redirect chains exceeding 2 hops before landing on credential-collection or malware-hosting domain. Flag if final domain registered <30 days and shares TLD with legitimate service.

suggestion.title: Bulk Phishing Campaign Indicators (Email Gateway Patterns)
suggestion.rationale: Article focuses on 'alert volume' from phishing—inherently implies bulk distribution. No detection suggested for characteristic mass-mail patterns: SMTP relay abuse, sender spoofing variants, content reuse.

Correlate with external threat feeds for known phishing templates.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520 Asset Exposure Hunt

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated RCE Exploitation Pattern — Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution' via OS command injection. Core attack surface requires exploitation signature.

suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly flags vulnerability success depends on 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state' — requires continuous configuration posture assessment.

suggestion.rationale: Article states appliance vulnerability manifests 'in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Detection requires identifying exposed instances before exploitation.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry OS Command Injection Exploitation

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Root-Level Process Execution Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies threat outcome is 'achieve root-level remote code execution.' Requires detection of post-exploitation command execution on the appliance itself.
