suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for ssh/sshd/scp binary hash mismatches or binary replacement events. Alert on creation of local credential logs in unusual paths. Detect SSH process modifications that don't correspond to package manager updates.

suggestion.title: GS-Netcat Reverse Shell C2 Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'deployed a modified GS-Netcat reverse shell disguised as a legitimate system component that connected to a hardcoded relay domain, providing encrypted remote shell access.' Achieved persistence via systemd service or startup script.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for GS-Netcat process signatures and obfuscated reverse shell patterns. Monitor systemd service files for suspicious reverse shell commands. Alert on processes masquerading as legitimate components that establish outbound C2 connections to relay domains.

suggestion.title: SOCKS5 Proxy Masquerading as System Service
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'custom SOCKS5 proxy for network traffic tunneling... ran as a daemon masquerading as smbd -D, using different filenames and ports on each host.' Enables pivot from internet-facing to air-gapped network.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SOCKS5 listening ports on internet-facing servers. Alert on processes spoofing 'smbd -D' that actually bind to network sockets. Monitor sustained port forwarding or dynamic proxy creation from compromised internet-facing hosts.

suggestion.title: Nginx Proxy Chaining to Isolated Network
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'modified the configuration of a compromised internet-facing Nginx server to proxy specially crafted requests to a compromised backend server.' Backend Nginx forwards to FastCGI, creating HTTP→SSH bridge into air-gapped network.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor nginx.conf for proxy_pass directives to internal FastCGI or SSH endpoints. Alert on HTTP POST requests with SSH-like parameters (hostname, username, command). Detect unusual request forwarding chains between internet-facing and internal Nginx instances.

suggestion.title: FastCGI-Initiated SSH to Internal Systems
suggestion.rationale: Article details the attack vector: 'The FastCGI wrapper acted as an execution bridge, processing requests and launching a custom binary named uptime... established SSH connections to systems within the isolated critical infrastructure network using parameters supplied in HTTP POST requests.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on fcgiwrap or FastCGI processes spawning SSH/scp binaries. Correlate HTTP POST request content with subsequent SSH connection parameters. Detect SSH connections initiated by web server UIDs (www-data, nginx, etc.).

suggestion.title: Exploit Attempt on Splunk REST/Web API Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article title establishes unauthenticated RCE via Splunk endpoint; without article text, assumed exploitation vector is HTTP(S) request to vulnerable endpoint (likely /api/* or /en-US/* paths common in Splunk web interface).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to Splunk instances with POST/GET to /api/* or /en-US/* paths containing unusual parameters or command sequences. Flag requests without Authentication headers or valid session tokens to critical Splunk endpoints.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Code Execution via Splunk Process
suggestion.rationale: Article premise is unauthenticated code execution; need detection for spawned processes from splunkd or splunk-web processes indicating successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned by splunkd.exe, splunk-web.exe, or python.exe in Splunk context with unexpected command-line arguments (bash, cmd, powershell, curl, wget) or network operations.

suggestion.title: Splunk Configuration Injection or Deployment Client Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Critical unauthenticated RCE likely exploits Splunk config parsing or deployment mechanisms; detection should cover malicious conf file modifications or deployment client reaching unexpected C2.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor modifications to /etc/system/local/* or $SPLUNK_HOME/etc/deployment-client/deploymentclient.conf with unexpected target serverRepositories pointing to attacker C2 or conf files containing embedded commands.

suggestion.title: AUR Package Metadata Tampering Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 400+ packages hijacked; implies malicious PKGBUILD modifications or unauthorized metadata changes. No UC generated despite this being the core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected changes to AUR package .git history (commit author/timestamp anomalies, forced pushes from non-maintainer IPs, or batched updates outside normal maintenance windows). Cross-reference with maintainer account logins; flag modifications without corresponding auth events. Alert on package metadata changes preceding new releases.

suggestion.title: Malicious Installation Script Execution Post-AUR Install
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain hijack injects code into PKGBUILD/install scripts; article mentions packages but no detection for script execution phase. 'What the "Atomic Arch" Campaign Means' implies actual payload delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: During pacman -S or yay -S post-installation hooks, detect spawned shell processes with network I/O or file creation outside expected package scope. Flag if /tmp or /var/tmp writes correlate with immediate DNS lookups to non-repo domains or curl/wget to external hosts during package install.

suggestion.title: AUR Maintainer Account Compromise via Weak Auth or Phishing
suggestion.rationale: 400+ packages compromised suggests either mass maintainer account takeover or single vulnerability. Article likely describes auth mechanism but no UC for detecting account compromise prior to package modification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on AUR login from new IP geolocation within 24 hours of mass package updates. Flag multiple failed login attempts followed by successful auth from unusual client (e.g., curl vs. web UI). Monitor for new SSH keys added to maintainer accounts without corresponding audit trail or maintainer confirmation email.

suggestion.title: Package Repository Mirror Sync Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 400+ hijacked packages entering distribution; no UC for detecting abnormal sync patterns or mirror-level tampering indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sync operations that introduce packages with mismatched GPG signatures or timestamps predating maintainer commits. Alert if a single sync cycle pushes >100 package updates from non-vetted maintainers or if package size increases anomalously (payloaded binary bloat).

suggestion.title: Post-Installation Network Beaconing to C2 Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Hijacked packages likely include persistence or exfiltration payloads; article implies ongoing compromise but no UC for detecting C2 callbacks or data exfil post-install.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate package installation (pacman/yay process) with subsequent DNS queries or HTTP/HTTPS connections to non-whitelisted domains. Flag if outbound traffic originates from package-installed paths (/opt, /usr/local/bin, systemd services spawned by package) within 10 minutes of install completion.

suggestion.title: Bulk AUR Package Download/Installation Surge from Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Campaign compromises many packages; detecting mass installation attempts flags either automated testing of exploit or opportunistic infection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert if a single endpoint installs >5 AUR packages within 30 minutes or if pacman/yay logs show batch installations of packages flagged as compromised in threat intel feeds. Cross-reference against user baseline (non-developers, systems with no history of AUR installs).

suggestion.title: macOS Tahoe 26 Artifact File Access
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'new macOS Tahoe 26 forensic artifact that tracks user menu selections across the operating system.' Any exfiltration requires prior artifact file access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file opens or reads of macOS Tahoe 26 artifact locations by non-system processes. Alert on stat(), open(), or mmap() syscalls against artifact paths followed by suspicious process behavior (network egress, archive creation, memory access patterns indicating data staging).

suggestion.title: Tahoe 26 Artifact Deletion or Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Forensic artifact is a 'digital intent' record—attackers will attempt deletion/modification to cover tracks, matching adversarial practice of anti-forensics.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unexpected deletion, truncation, or modification of Tahoe 26 artifact storage locations on macOS. Detect invocations of rm, shred, unlink, or file truncation APIs against known artifact directories. Correlate with shell execution or suspicious process chains.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Tahoe 26 Menu Selection Data
suggestion.rationale: Artifact's stated function is to track user selections; the collected menu data is the attacker's target for intelligence gathering ('Tracing Digital Intent').
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate file access to Tahoe 26 artifact with subsequent suspicious network activity. Detect compression (tar, zip, gzip) or encoding of artifact data followed by connections to non-standard ports or known C2 infrastructure. Monitor for data exfiltration to cloud storage or file-sharing services.

suggestion.title: Phishing email impersonating AI vendors with credential CTA
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states AI brands used as social engineering bait. No detection UC for emails spoofing ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, or other AI platforms requesting verification or urgent action.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails claiming to be from major AI vendors with sender domain mismatches or lookalike domains. Trigger on urgency language + credential verification CTA + link to non-canonical domain. Correlate to phishing campaigns targeting specific organization.

suggestion.title: AiTM proxy credential interception and MFA token theft
suggestion.rationale: Keywords explicitly flag 'Adversary-in-the-middle' attacks; article focuses on credential theft via AiTM proxies. No detection UC for real-time token interception or MFA bypass signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect failed auth + immediate successful auth from different IP (credential replay). Look for MFA completion in <5 seconds post-submission (token reuse). Correlate impossible travel: phishing email open IP + subsequent sign-in from distant geography within 10 minutes.

suggestion.title: Post-compromise account abuse with stolen credentials
suggestion.rationale: Credential theft is stated attack goal; no UC for detection of compromised account activity patterns post-harvest.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sign-ins with compromised creds: impossible travel, anomalous client apps (legacy auth protocols), suspicious mailbox/file-share access immediately after phishing event, email forwarding rules created post-compromise.

suggestion.title: Lookalike domain registration targeting AI platforms
suggestion.rationale: Social engineering via AI brand impersonation requires attacker infrastructure (phishing domains). No IOC extraction of typosquatted AI vendor domains suggests infrastructure not mapped.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for domains similar to OpenAI, Anthropic, Google AI, Microsoft AI (Copilot) with edit-distance typos (openai-securelogin.com, claude-verify.net). Alert on user clicks to these domains from phishing emails. High-confidence alert if credential submission detected.

suggestion.title: Suspicious email URL clicks to external credential-submission endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Credential theft campaigns involve convincing users to enter passwords on attacker-controlled pages. No UC for phishing link + credential submission detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect email URL clicks to non-corporate endpoints followed by suspicious network activity (POST to external login/auth endpoints). Correlate phishing email receipt + link click + subsequent account compromise or MFA alert.

suggestion.title: Forced authentication via malicious redirects or NTLM relay
suggestion.rationale: AiTM campaigns often force credential submission. T1187 (Forced Authentication) is central to AiTM attacks but unmapped by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect NTLM authentication requests to attacker-controlled infrastructure within email-forwarding/URL-click session. Look for challenge-response auth to external IPs. Correlate to phishing campaigns.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Externally Reachable Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'vulnerability can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Baseline asset discovery is prerequisite for triage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances (product signatures, DNS patterns, open ports 443/8443) reachable from external networks. Flag appliances without mTLS (EPMM) or Neurons for MDM enrollment indicators. Cross-reference against patch inventory for CVE-2026-10520 remediation status.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry OS Command Injection Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Payload delivery is the primary attack vector requiring behavioral detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor unauthenticated HTTP requests to Sentry endpoints for OS command injection patterns: shell metacharacters (| ; & ` $() backticks), argument separators, or command substitution syntax in request paths, query strings, or POST bodies. Alert on repeated injection attempts from single sources.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unmanaged State Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors.' Absence of these mitigations identifies vulnerable configurations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query inventory for Sentry appliances lacking mTLS enforcement (certificate validation absence), EPMM agent enrollment, or Neurons for MDM integration. Correlate missing hardening with external network reachability to identify actively exploitable instances.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Root Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'achieve root-level remote code execution.' Post-exploitation indicators must capture process execution privilege escalation and unexpected root-context activity from Sentry services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on shell spawning (sh, bash, ksh) or reverse-shell payloads with UID=0 originating from Sentry daemon accounts. Flag unexpected network connections (outbound) or file modifications initiated from root-context Sentry processes. Monitor sudoers/privilege escalation logs for Sentry service privilege-climbing attempts.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Reconnaissance Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Article implies attacker reconnaissance phase: 'vulnerability can be successfully exploited...where the Sentry appliance is...externally reachable.' Scanning and probing precedes active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect mass HTTP requests to Sentry management paths (/admin, /ems/, /api/) from external IPs returning 401/403/200 in rapid succession. Alert on port scanning targeting typical Sentry ports (443, 8443, 8080) from single external source. Correlate with Shodan/Censys queries for Ivanti product fingerprints.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520: Ivanti Sentry External Exposure Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability exploitable only when 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Detection must identify exposed unpatched instances before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference network asset inventory against Ivanti Sentry product/version roster. Flag instances externally routable on management ports (443 typical) that lack documented mTLS or restricted HTTPS access. Correlate with patch-status records to isolate unmanaged devices.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520: OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Exploitation attempts must be detectable in application/HTTP logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry application and web-server logs for HTTP requests containing shell metacharacters ($(), backticks, pipes, semicolons) in URL parameters or POST bodies. Unauthenticated requests exhibiting these patterns should trigger immediate alert.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation: Root-Level RCE Privilege Confirmation
suggestion.rationale: Article warns of 'root-level remote code execution.' Post-compromise, attacker will execute commands at UID 0. Detection should hunt for shell spawning from Sentry processes with root privileges.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child process spawning (sh, bash, ksh) from Ivanti Sentry service account (typically non-root). If UID/GID reports as 0 in process context, or file modifications occur in /etc, /sys, /root—escalation confirmed.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Vulnerability Scanner Match (CVE-2026-10520)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2026-10520 — match against your vulnerability scanner' as the primary IOC, and template instructs 'Substitute this CVE wherever the template references <CVE>'. Pipeline extracted no IOCs or hunts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag assets matching CVE-2026-10520 in any vulnerability scanner output, focusing on Ivanti Sentry (formerly MobileIron Sentry). Cross-reference discovered instances against Federal remediation deadline of 2026-06-14. Prioritize any unpatched Sentry appliances exposed to the internet.

suggestion.title: External Exposure: Unmanaged Ivanti Sentry Appliances
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies attack prerequisite: 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' mTLS and restricted HTTPS negate the vulnerability, so exposure detection is critical.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify externally reachable Ivanti Sentry appliances via network reconnaissance (default Sentry service ports, HTTP banner matching Sentry/MobileIron strings, SSL certificate Subject/Issuer patterns). Cross-reference against asset inventory to find appliances NOT protected by mTLS (EPMM) or restricted HTTPS (Neurons for MDM). Unmanaged instances are highest risk.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Attempts Against Ivanti Sentry Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability mechanism is 'OS command injection' allowing 'root-level remote code execution.' Article describes execution technique but pipeline mapped only T1190 and generated no execution-phase hunts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/REST API requests to Ivanti Sentry for command injection payloads: shell metacharacters (backticks, $(), pipes, semicolons, &&, ||) in parameter values, URL-encoded variants, and path traversal sequences. Focus on unauthenticated endpoints. Correlate with process execution logs on the appliance to detect post-injection command spawning as root.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Process Execution and Privilege Escalation on Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article states the vulnerability 'could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution'—this is the impact that requires post-exploitation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for anomalous process spawning on Ivanti Sentry appliances: shell processes (bash, sh, cmd) launched by Java/Tomcat parent processes, child processes running as root initiated from network-facing services, commands containing shell metacharacters in appliance audit logs, and unexpected privilege escalation events.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' matching CVE-2026-10520 against vulnerability scanner. Pipeline produced no use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag all Ivanti Sentry instances in vulnerability management system with CVE-2026-10520 exposure. Correlate patch status against federal remediation deadline (2026-06-14). Prioritize unpatched + externally accessible instances as highest-risk.

suggestion.title: Externally Reachable Ivanti Sentry Appliance Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability exploitable 'where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Pipeline missed network-exposure hunting layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Ivanti Sentry management consoles accessible from untrusted networks (public IPs, non-corporate ranges). Cross-reference externally-facing instances against asset inventory to identify unmanaged appliances lacking mTLS or Neurons MDM restriction.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempts Against Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article describes core vulnerability mechanism as 'OS command injection vulnerability.' No behavioral detection mapped despite this being the exploitation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry API/web interfaces for malformed requests containing shell metacharacters (;, |, &&, `, $(), backticks) or command-separator patterns in parameters. Alert on systematic probing of known injection endpoints or public PoC payloads.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation: Unauthorized Root-Level Process Spawning on Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states impact as 'root-level remote code execution.' Pipeline missed privilege-escalation / impact-phase detection for post-exploitation activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On Ivanti Sentry appliances, detect unexpected processes spawned with root UID from Sentry service account, system binary modifications, or outbound network connections from Sentry processes to non-whitelisted destinations.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Security Posture: mTLS and Restricted Access Validation
suggestion.rationale: Article documents mitigations: 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible.' Pipeline should validate security controls preventing exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Verify all Sentry appliances enforce mTLS with EPMM or operate behind Neurons MDM with restricted HTTPS. Flag any appliance in 'unmanaged state' or with open management interfaces on public/untrusted networks as misconfigured and exploitable.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is exploitable 'when the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable'; federal patch due 2026-06-14 signals active exploitation in the wild.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for unauthenticated inbound connections to externally accessible Ivanti Sentry instances. Cross-reference asset inventory for Sentry appliances not enrolled in mTLS, EPMM, or Neurons for MDM. Flag unmanaged instances as exploitation-vulnerable.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Attack on Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'OS command injection vulnerability' as the exploitation vector leading to RCE; no use case exists to detect injection attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry appliance logs and endpoint telemetry for shell metacharacters (pipes, command separators, variable expansion) in HTTP request payloads targeting Sentry endpoints, followed by unexpected child process spawning from Sentry service accounts.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Code Execution on Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability enables 'root-level remote code execution'; privilege escalation to root is the attack outcome and should be detectable post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned with root/SYSTEM privileges under Sentry service context or originating from unauthenticated network listeners. Cross-correlate timing with command-injection detection to flag successful exploitation.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged Sentry Appliance Inventory Gap
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'unmanaged state' as the exploitation condition; mitigation explicitly mentions mTLS/EPMM/Neurons enrollment, implying need to detect unenrolled appliances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query MDM/management systems for Ivanti Sentry appliances with no mTLS certificate enrollment, no EPMM integration, and no Neurons for MDM registration. Flag absences as unmanaged exposure.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scanner Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies CVE-2026-10520 as the primary threat ID with federal remediation due 2026-06-14; scanner correlation is foundational for active-exploitation response.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate vulnerability scanner flags for CVE-2026-10520 against Ivanti Sentry inventory. Any positive match should trigger immediate isolation review and expedited patching, given CISA KEV active-exploitation status.

suggestion.title: Internet-Facing Ivanti Sentry Asset Inventory & Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly establishes prerequisite: 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Article itself cites the canonical asset-exposure template. Pipeline produced zero use cases despite the template reference.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for Ivanti Sentry instances exposed on standard ports (443, 8443, 8080) using product-specific signatures (SSL cert subjects, HTTP response banners, /admin path). Correlate asset inventory with vulnerability scanner to identify systems with CVE-2026-10520 vulnerability status. Flag any externally-reachable instances as critical prior to patch due date (2026-06-14).

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Pipeline missed detection for injection patterns (pipe, semicolon, backtick, command substitution) in HTTP requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt HTTP traffic to Ivanti Sentry endpoints for command-injection metacharacters (|, ;, &, $(), backticks, newlines) in query parameters or POST body. Establish baseline of legitimate Sentry API calls first. Alert on obfuscated or encoded variants targeting known vulnerable endpoints.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated RCE Post-Exploitation Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'remote unauthenticated' access leading to 'root-level' execution. Pipeline failed to propose detection for unexpected privileged process spawning or shell access from the Sentry service context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On Ivanti Sentry appliances, detect unexpected process creation (bash, sh, perl, python, curl, wget) spawned from the Sentry daemon user with root/UID-0 context. Baseline normal Sentry maintenance tasks. Alert on reverse shells, outbound connections, or filesystem modification by unexpected processes.

suggestion.title: mTLS & HTTPS Access Control Bypass Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article notes that mTLS and restricted HTTPS 'make interfaces inaccessible to external actors'—a stated control. Pipeline missed detection for attempts to circumvent these protections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for failed mTLS client certificate validation, TLS renegotiation attempts, or direct-to-IP access bypassing Neurons for MDM proxy. Track non-standard cipher suites or SSL/TLS version mismatches on Sentry ports. Alert on repeated failed certificate validation from external IPs.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner + Patch Compliance Validation
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and recommends fleet-wide patch verification. Pipeline must correlate vulnerability scanner results with CVE-2026-10520 for compliance tracking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for all Ivanti Sentry instances and cross-reference against CVE-2026-10520 patch status. Flag any systems with status 'vulnerable' or 'not assessed' as critical. Priority escalate systems with both vulnerability AND external network exposure. Validate patches installed after 2026-06-14 federal due date.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Exposed Asset Detection

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for CVE-2026-10520 across Ivanti Sentry deployments. Cross-reference scan results with external internet-facing asset data (Shodan, censys). Flag instances not protected by mTLS/EPMM connection or restricted HTTPS access, per article's stated mitigations.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempt

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry appliance web logs for HTTP requests containing shell metacharacters (|, ;, `, $(), backticks, newlines) in query parameters or POST bodies. Correlate with unauthenticated access to admin/system endpoints. Alert on 5xx errors following suspicious parameter submission.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Root Process Spawning from Web Service
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'root-level remote code execution' as impact but pipeline missed process-execution detection from compromised web context.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unmanaged State Configuration Detection

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Patch Compliance by Federal Due-Date
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies federal patch due-date 2026-06-14 and emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Pipeline missed compliance-based detection for this specific CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for all Ivanti Sentry deployments affected by CVE-2026-10520. Identify versions running pre-patch baseline per Ivanti advisory. Flag non-compliant systems with patch due-date 2026-06-14 passed, escalating to compliance/audit teams.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520 Externally Reachable Asset Exposure

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query firewall and network logs for inbound connections to Ivanti Sentry appliances (identify by IP/CIDR, banner fingerprint, or known management paths like /mobileironcore/) from non-corporate ASNs or untrusted networks. suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempt Against Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability...remote unauthenticated user' but pipeline generated no exploitation-detection UC. Shell metacharacters ($(), backticks, |, ;) in HTTP request payloads to Sentry endpoints are telltale exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse HTTP/HTTPS request payloads to Ivanti Sentry endpoints for OS command injection indicators: $(command), backticks, pipe (|), semicolon (;), &&, ||. Alert on suspicious parameters or POST bodies containing these metacharacters. Refine FP by excluding known MDM enrollment and mTLS client-cert negotiation traffic patterns.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged Ivanti Sentry Instances - Configuration Drift Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability only impacts appliances 'in an unmanaged state' and notes mitigations (mTLS, restricted HTTPS) that prevent exploitation. Pipeline generated no compliance or config-drift UC. Identifying unmanaged instances is prerequisite to prioritization.

Identify instances with HTTP (unencrypted) enabled, missing mTLS client certificate enforcement, or HTTPS bypass paths. Check for policy application lag (patch not deployed within 5 days of CISA due-date 2026-06-14).

suggestion.title: Root-level Process Spawning from Ivanti Sentry Service Context

suggestion.title: Detect externally reachable Ivanti Sentry appliances
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable'—this is the foundational attack precondition.

Alert on Sentry appliances lacking mTLS enforcement or restricted HTTPS channel validation.

suggestion.title: Detect unauthenticated access attempts to Sentry endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'remote unauthenticated user'—the vulnerability requires no valid credentials, making authentication-free requests direct exploitation signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry HTTP/HTTPS endpoint access for requests lacking valid auth headers, session tokens, or mTLS client certificates. Establish baseline of legitimate unauthenticated paths (login, health checks) and alert on unauthenticated access to /api, /admin, or /management routes.

suggestion.title: Detect OS command injection payloads to Sentry interfaces
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability type explicitly named: 'OS command injection'—shell metacharacters in request parameters are direct exploitation signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search HTTP request parameters and POST bodies destined for Sentry endpoints for Unix shell metacharacters (|, ;, &&, backticks, $(), command substitution). Correlate with HTTP 2xx responses or application error logs indicating command execution attempts.

suggestion.title: Detect anomalous root-level process spawning from Sentry service
suggestion.rationale: Impact explicitly stated: 'root-level remote code execution'—child processes spawned by Sentry daemon represent post-exploitation activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child processes under Sentry service contexts (ivanti-sentry, mobileiron-sentry daemons). Flag parent-child relationships missing from baseline, execution of interpreters (bash, sh, perl) from Sentry process, or spawning of network utilities (nc, curl, wget) with reversed or bind-shell patterns.

suggestion.title: Monitor unpatched Ivanti Sentry vulnerable to CVE-2026-10520
suggestion.rationale: Federal patch due date (2026-06-14) and CISA KEV designation indicate active wild exploitation—unpatched systems are direct compromise targets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner data for Ivanti Sentry versions vulnerable to CVE-2026-10520. Cross-reference asset inventory against patched version catalogs. Alert on systems remaining unpatched beyond federal due date or lacking patch-management enrollment.

suggestion.title: Detect mTLS enforcement bypass or misconfiguration on Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access makes interfaces inaccessible'—detecting bypass or absence of these controls is defensive priority.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for successful Sentry connections missing expected mTLS client certificates, plaintext protocol fallback, or HTTP-only access when HTTPS-only is enforced. Alert on connection sources outside known EPMM/MDM management plane networks accessing Sentry endpoints.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email with AI-Generated Content Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly addresses 'AI Phishing' campaigns; body presumably describes AI-crafted email characteristics that evade traditional filters. Pipeline extracted no use case despite this being the primary threat vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails with anthropomorphic phrasing patterns, unusual sender-domain mismatches, or authentication failures (SPF/DKIM) paired with low recipient trust scores. Correlate with user awareness training gaps to identify high-risk targets.

suggestion.title: SOC Alert Volume Spike from Phishing Campaign
suggestion.rationale: Core premise: 'Crushing SOCs with Alert Volume'—pipeline should detect sustained alert inflation from phishing infrastructure. No detection rule generated despite this being the stated operational impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline alert-per-user and alert-per-rule over 5-minute windows. Flag when Tier 1-assigned alert categories (phishing, suspicious sender) exceed 3σ above rolling 7-day mean. Correlate with email volume logs to separate noise from attack progression.

suggestion.title: Email Authentication Framework Bypass or Degradation
suggestion.rationale: AI phishing at scale often exploits SPF/DKIM misconfigurations or sender spoofing. Article implies recipient targeting; pipeline did not surface email-auth evasion as a detection vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on messages that fail SPF/DKIM/DMARC validation but bypass org policy filters, or claim internal-domain sender identity from external IP. Weight by recipient role (finance, HR, C-suite) to prioritize high-value phishing targets.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Email Sender Behavior from New Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Phishing campaigns typically originate from newly-spun or compromised sender domains. Title references scale ('crushing'); pipeline should flag bulk sender registration or first-contact phishing from unknown senders to target orgs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cluster emails by sender domain ASN/whois age. Flag domains registered <30 days ago sending >100 messages to org within 24h. Correlate domain reputation scores with payload analysis (URLs, attachment MIME types) to confirm phishing intent.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting Link Detection in Mass Email Campaign
suggestion.rationale: AI phishing typically embeds credential-capture URLs. Article discusses high-volume campaigns; pipeline should generate rules for common phishing-kit domains and obfuscation patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Extract URLs from email bodies; check against known phishing registrars, look-alike domains, and unicode/homograph variations. Flag clicks from suspicious URLs by users not normally visiting external auth pages. Correlate with downstream password-reset or MFA-bypass attempts.

suggestion.title: Tier 1 Alert Fatigue and Triage Bypass Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article's core claim: volume overwhelms Tier 1 capacity. Pipeline should map detection rules for alerts that bypass SOC SLAs or exceed analyst dwell-time budgets, signaling adversary pressure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track alert-close time SLA by rule and tier. Flag when phishing-class alerts show >50% SLA miss rate or >30min median dwell. Correlate with user complaints or escalation rates to identify triage collapse and potential account compromise during high-volume periods.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Exposure Detection

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Ivanti Sentry appliances (ports 8888-8890 typical, product headers, SSL certs) responding to external IPs. Cross-correlate with internal asset inventory to identify unregistered/unmanaged instances. Compare mTLS/EPMM protection status.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempts

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Root-Level Process Execution

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unmanaged Appliance State Audit
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability requires appliance in 'unmanaged state'—absence of mTLS/EPMM/MDM governance. Policy-driven audit complements real-time detection for cases where exposure existed but exploitation not yet observed.

suggestion.title: Disabled mTLS or Restricted HTTPS Policy Misconfiguration
suggestion.rationale: Article notes that 'mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible.' Detection should flag deployments where these mitigations are absent or disabled.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit Ivanti Sentry appliances for disabled mTLS enforcement, non-EPMM client acceptance on admin ports, or fallback to unencrypted protocols. Compare current config against baseline for policy drift.

suggestion.title: Patch Lag Post-Federal Due Date (2026-06-14)
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and sets Federal due date 2026-06-14 for remediation. Post-deadline, any unpatched Sentry is a critical exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post 2026-06-14, flag any Ivanti Sentry instance running a version older than the official patched release. Correlate against network exposure; alert on any unpatched instance with external reachability.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Ivanti Sentry External Accessibility
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable'. Primary attack vector is network exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for inbound network connections to known Ivanti Sentry ports/services from untrusted CIDR ranges. Flag any Sentry appliance responding on public IPs. Correlate with asset inventory to identify unmanaged instances.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection: Ivanti Sentry Request Payload Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution'. Payload intrusion detection required.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to Ivanti Sentry appliances for command injection patterns (shell metacharacters, backticks, $(), pipe chains in query strings or POST bodies). Alert on unauthenticated requests containing suspicious command syntax.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation: Root-Level Process Execution from Sentry Service
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'root-level remote code execution'. Endpoint logging needed to catch post-exploitation activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On Ivanti Sentry appliances, detect unexpected processes spawned by Sentry services running with root/SYSTEM privileges. Flag shell spawns, script execution, or privilege elevation attempts originating from Sentry daemons.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Version Identification: Ivanti Sentry Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies CVE-2026-10520 but does not list patched versions. Detection should identify unpatched Sentry instances via banner grab or version query.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for Ivanti Sentry appliances and extract version strings from HTTP headers or service banners. Cross-reference against CVE-2026-10520 vulnerability timeline to identify instances pre-dating the patch release (pre-2026-06-14).

suggestion.title: Configuration Bypass Detection: mTLS/Restriction Evasion Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible'. Detection should flag attempts to bypass these controls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for non-mTLS or unencrypted traffic to Sentry appliances in environments where mTLS is mandated. Flag direct HTTP (non-HTTPS) connections, certificate validation failures, or traffic from IPs not registered with EPMM/Neurons.

suggestion.title: Patch Verification: Ivanti Sentry Post-Remediation Scan
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Federal patch due: 2026-06-14'. Post-deadline, should verify all Sentry instances are patched.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-remediation deadline (2026-06-14), query all asset inventory and vulnerability scanners for Ivanti Sentry instances. Alert on any remaining unpatched or unknown-version Sentry appliances. Cross-check against patch release timestamps.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable cordova-plugin-inappbrowser Inventory (CVE-2026-47430)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies affected software, versions (3.1.0 ≤ v < 6.0.1), and platform (iOS). Pipeline generated zero asset-hunt use cases despite this being the primary detection foothold. Phrase: 'cordova-plugin-inappbrowser: iOS'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify iOS devices with cordova-plugin-inappbrowser versions in vulnerable range. Cross-correlate with app-usage logs to flag devices where InAppBrowser loads untrusted or user-controlled content. Escalate if IsInternetFacing=true or LoggedOnUsers include high-value accounts.

suggestion.title: Exploitation: InAppBrowser WKScriptMessage Callback Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article core vulnerability: 'passes the id field from WKScriptMessage body... with no format validation'. Pipeline missed the execution-layer detection despite explicit code path (CDVWKInAppBrowser.m:560–574).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cordova runtime for WKScriptMessages with id fields that deviate from expected callback ID patterns (numeric or UUID). Flag messages containing system-reserved callback prefixes ('exec', 'deviceexec', 'deviceready'). Correlation with vulnerable app version increases confidence.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation: OAuth Consent & Credential Grants After InAppBrowser
suggestion.rationale: Article maps T1528 (Steal Application Access Token) and T1098.001 (Account Manipulation) as direct impacts, but pipeline generated zero OAuth/token-abuse hunts. Phrase: 'fire any pending Cordova callback'—attacker-controlled callbacks can trigger auth flows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate InAppBrowser activity on vulnerable app + device with OAuth consent events, app role assignments, or delegated permission grants within 24h window. Alert if grant scope includes Mail.Read, Calendar.Read, or User.ReadWrite. High confidence if source app is on CVE-2026-47430 vulnerable version list.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance via Host Information Leakage
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1592.002 (Gather Victim Host Information: Software) as inferred technique. Pipeline failed to model reconnaissance flows despite callback dispatch enabling arbitrary host-info exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor InAppBrowser WebViews for repeated requests to callback ID enumeration or system-property inspection. Flag unusual network egress from vulnerable app immediately after InAppBrowser content load—may indicate device fingerprinting or credential-store enumeration.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL' and notes vulnerability is exploitable only 'where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances in vulnerability scanner inventory with CVE-2026-10520 exposure. Correlate with network flow data showing external HTTP/HTTPS inbound connections to appliance management ports. Prioritize systems not protected by mTLS or restricted HTTPS.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Reachability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states exploitation is only possible 'where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable' and that mTLS/restricted HTTPS makes it inaccessible — detection should verify these protective states.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Ivanti Sentry appliances (port 8080/8443 default) receiving external inbound traffic. Flag instances not behind mTLS termination proxy or without HTTPS access restrictions. Compare asset inventory against firewall rules to identify unmanaged exposure.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Web application logs would contain injection payloads or abnormal request patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for requests to Ivanti Sentry interfaces containing OS command injection metacharacters (;, |, $(), backticks, >&) or known payload patterns. Look for unauthenticated requests to endpoints handling command processing. Monitor for shell metacharacters in HTTP parameters.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Remote Code Execution Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'root-level remote code execution' as the outcome — post-exploitation detection should identify successful command execution on the appliance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry system/kernel logs for unexpected process spawning from web service processes or unusual privilege escalation to root. Look for parent-child process relationships indicating command execution chains. Baseline normal Sentry process behavior and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Presence Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' as primary recommendation. Should query vulnerability scanner output for CVE-2026-10520 findings on Ivanti Sentry appliances. This is the template pattern the article explicitly endorses.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when vulnerability scanner reports CVE-2026-10520 detection on any Ivanti Sentry appliance, especially in unmanaged state. Correlate with network-exposure telemetry to identify externally-reachable instances requiring urgent remediation.

suggestion.title: Externally Reachable Ivanti Sentry Appliance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exploitation prerequisite: 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' External network exposure is the gating condition for RCE risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry management interfaces (typical ports 8443, 8080) accessible from untrusted networks. Fingerprint via SSL certificate, HTTP banners, or known Sentry hostnames. Flag instances missing mTLS/EPMM enforced isolation.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload Detection in Sentry Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack mechanism: 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Direct exploitation requires execution-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt HTTP request logs to Ivanti Sentry endpoints for command injection payloads: backticks, $(), pipes, semicolons, or known gadget chains. Alert on requests originating from untrusted networks to vulnerable endpoints.

suggestion.title: Root-level Child Process Spawning from Sentry Service
suggestion.rationale: Article states impact: 'achieve root-level remote code execution.' Post-exploitation detection of successful privilege escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate unexpected child processes spawned with root context from Sentry service daemon with time-windows of external HTTP requests to vulnerable endpoints. Flag non-whitelisted binaries, reverse shells, or crypto-mining toolchains.

suggestion.title: Sentry Appliance Missing Security Boundary Configuration
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies security controls that mitigate: 'The use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors.' Absence of these controls indicates exploitable state.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Ivanti Sentry configuration or certificate stores to verify mTLS enforcement and EPMM integration are active. Alert on appliances with mTLS disabled, unencrypted HTTP endpoints enabled, or MDM isolation bypassed.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is exploitable only when 'endpoints externally reachable' and appliance is 'in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable'. External network exposure is the primary attack prerequisite.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Ivanti Sentry appliances accessible from internet-routable IP ranges on management ports (443, 8443, etc.). Flag any instance without the mTLS or restricted HTTPS mitigations mentioned in the article.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution'. Injection payloads in application traffic are the direct exploitation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints for command injection patterns (semicolons, pipes, backticks, command substitution syntax) in request parameters from unauthenticated sources.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Execution from Sentry Service Account
suggestion.rationale: Article states successful exploitation achieves 'root-level remote code execution'. Endpoint detection must flag anomalous process spawning from Ivanti service contexts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual child processes spawned by Ivanti Sentry service accounts with root/system privileges, especially interactive shells, network utilities (curl, wget, nc, bash), or privilege escalation tools.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article is CISA KEV entry with explicit CVE-2026-10520 identifier and federal patch deadline 2026-06-14. Vulnerability scanner alerting is the immediate detection vector for unexposed instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any vulnerability scanner detection of CVE-2026-10520 in Ivanti Sentry instances. Escalate to critical and enforce remediation by federal deadline (2026-06-14) or equivalent enterprise SLA.

suggestion.title: Network Segmentation Control Validation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies mitigations as 'mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors'. Detect instances without these controls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry instances allowing unauthenticated HTTPS access from internet-routable sources without upstream mTLS enforcement or WAF/proxy restrictions. Configuration and network segmentation audit required.

suggestion.title: PAM Module Replacement Detection
suggestion.rationale: Attackers 'replaced legitimate pam_unix.so modules with backdoored versions that accept hardcoded passwords and harvest user credentials' with 9 distinct variants. Direct hijack of authentication process.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file modifications to /lib64/security/pam_unix.so and /lib/security/pam_unix.so. Alert on unsigned or hash-mismatched PAM modules. Cross-reference FIM baselines with vendor signatures.

suggestion.title: OpenSSH Binary Trojanism
suggestion.rationale: Actors 'replaced OpenSSH components such as ssh, sshd, and scp with trojanized versions that captured credentials, logged commands entered during SSH sessions.' Persistence via authentication component hijacking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hash-verify /usr/bin/ssh, /usr/sbin/sshd, /usr/bin/scp against vendor signatures. Alert on binary modifications outside maintenance windows. Monitor for unexpected child processes spawned from SSH daemons.

suggestion.title: Systemd Service Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Reverse shell achieved 'persistence either via a malicious systemd service or through startup script modification.' No unit name provided indicates obfuscation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor /etc/systemd/system/ and /lib/systemd/system/ for new service units with obfuscated names. Alert on service EnableNow state before first user logon or with suspicious ExecStart pointing to non-standard paths.

suggestion.title: Nginx Proxy Modification for Internal Bridging
suggestion.rationale: Attackers 'modified the configuration of a compromised internet-facing Nginx server to proxy specially crafted requests to a compromised backend server' to establish access into air-gapped network. Config file became lateral-movement vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor /etc/nginx/nginx.conf and conf.d/ for new proxy_pass directives. Alert on proxy_pass pointing to private IP ranges or non-standard ports. Baseline config against last known-good or version-control snapshot.

suggestion.title: SOCKS5 Proxy Masquerading as Samba
suggestion.rationale: Custom SOCKS5 proxy 'ran as a daemon masquerading as smbd -D, using different filenames and ports on each host.' Process masquerading + network tunneling = evasion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for 'smbd' process names with suspicious parent processes or command lines. Monitor netstat/ss output for listening sockets opened by non-Samba processes. Flag inconsistencies between `ps` and `netstat` process listings.

suggestion.title: FastCGI-to-SSH Execution Bridge via HTTP
suggestion.rationale: Chained Nginx → FastCGI wrapper (fcgiwrap) → custom 'uptime' binary → SSH to establish 'a remote-execution path into the segregated environment via simple HTTP requests.' HTTP POST became pivot into air-gapped network.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web server access logs for HTTP POST requests with suspicious parameters. Alert on fcgiwrap process spawning SSH or shell processes. Flag HTTP requests triggering outbound SSH connections to internal/RFC1918 hosts.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated HTTP POST to Splunk Management Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article describes unauthenticated RCE; typical exploitation involves HTTP requests to unprotected Splunk API endpoints without valid credentials. No UC generated despite 'without authentication' being the core vulnerability vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP POST/GET requests to Splunk management ports (8089, 8000, 9997) from external IPs lacking valid session tokens, particularly with user-agent strings or request patterns matching known exploits. Baseline known administrative access and filter.

suggestion.title: Splunk Process Spawning Unexpected Child Process
suggestion.rationale: RCE implies successful code execution; article states 'attackers run code' but no detection for post-exploitation execution behavior. Missing UC for process-level detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when splunkd.exe or splunk process spawns cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, or other interpreters without known patch/update contexts. Establish baseline of legitimate child processes for Splunk.

suggestion.title: Splunk Outbound Network Connection to C2 Indicator
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation could involve data exfiltration or C2 callbacks from Splunk instance; article does not describe scope but RCE typically enables command & control. No network-based detection UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected outbound connections from Splunk processes to non-whitelisted external IPs/domains, especially on non-standard ports. Cross-reference with threat-intel feeds for known C2 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Splunk HTTP Request with Suspicious Encoding or Payload Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation of Splunk web interfaces typically involves injection or command patterns in query parameters or request bodies. Article mentions vulnerability but no payload-pattern detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to Splunk with URL-encoded or base64-encoded payloads, shell metacharacters (| ; & $ < >), or known Splunk RCE parameter names in query strings or POST bodies targeting management endpoints.

suggestion.title: Splunk Configuration File Modification Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Attackers gaining code execution often establish persistence via configuration or scheduled searches. Article does not specify post-compromise behavior but RCE scenarios warrant persistence detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected modifications to Splunk config files (props.conf, transforms.conf, inputs.conf) or creation of new scheduled searches/scripts, especially outside normal change-control windows.

suggestion.title: Failed Splunk Authentication Followed by Successful Unauthenticated Request
suggestion.rationale: Attack pattern: attacker probes authentication, then exploits unauthenticated endpoint. Pipeline missed the behavioral sequence inherent in 'without authentication' vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlation rule: detect sequences where the same source IP fails authentication attempts followed within minutes by successful API calls to known-vulnerable endpoints without valid session tokens.

suggestion.title: Detect Installation of Compromised AUR Packages
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 400+ AUR packages were hijacked; the pipeline missed the fundamental detection: monitoring for installation of known-compromised package versions from the affected Arch repository.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for pacman (Arch package manager) installation or build commands targeting package names in the confirmed compromised list. Alert on execution of code from ~/.cache/pacman/pkg or AUR build directories, particularly if timestamps indicate recent downloads post-campaign disclosure.

suggestion.title: Detect Anomalous Post-Installation Behavior from AUR Packages
suggestion.rationale: Hijacked packages likely contain malicious payloads; the pipeline missed detection of suspicious post-install behavior characteristic of supply-chain compromise: network callbacks, privilege escalation attempts, persistence mechanisms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate pacman install logs with subsequent suspicious process execution (bash, curl, wget, nc spawned from package extraction directories), outbound connections to non-standard ports, or modifications to dotfiles/cron jobs within 1 hour of package installation.

suggestion.title: Monitor AUR Repository Cache for Signature Mismatches
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions hijacked packages; the pipeline failed to suggest detection of cryptographic validation failures or repository cache anomalies that would indicate package tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit pacman.conf and AUR helper logs for disabled signature verification, or monitor /var/cache/pacman/pkg for files with timestamps inconsistent with published release dates. Flag any manual .pkg.tar.zst modifications post-download.

suggestion.title: Detect Privilege Escalation from Compromised Package Install Scripts
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain compromises frequently abuse PKGBUILD scripts and package pre/post-install hooks for privilege escalation; the pipeline did not suggest monitoring for unauthorized sudo execution or setuid calls during package installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sudo execution initiated from pacman hook processes (/var/lib/pacman) or on setuid/setgid flag changes to binaries in package directories during or immediately after pacman -S operations.

suggestion.title: Baseline AUR Build Directory Executable Modification
suggestion.rationale: Hijacked packages may introduce hidden executables or modify existing ones during build; the pipeline missed file integrity monitoring for AUR source/build artifacts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline hashes for commonly-installed AUR packages in ~/.cache/pacman/pkg and ~/.config/yay. Alert on unexpected new binaries or modified existing binaries (excluding expected version changes), especially those with suspiciously short creation-to-execution times.

suggestion.title: MacOS Tahoe 26 Artifact Access by Non-Forensic Tools
suggestion.rationale: Schema states artifact 'tracks user menu selections across the operating system.' Pipeline missed that threat actors may access this forensic artifact post-breach to reconstruct user behavior and timelines. No detection rules proposed for artifact access or exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor processes accessing the macOS Tahoe 26 artifact files (path not provided in article body) outside authorized forensic/MDM tools. Flag copy, read, or network transmission attempts. Correlate with lateral movement or dwell-time reconnaissance patterns to identify post-breach evidence gathering.

suggestion.title: MacOS Menu Selection Artifact Deletion or Clearing
suggestion.rationale: User menu-selection tracking implies temporal sequencing. Attackers may delete or truncate this artifact to disrupt post-incident timeline reconstruction and evade behavioral forensics.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on deletion, truncation, or modification of macOS Tahoe 26 artifact files. Compare deletion timestamps to known incident windows; unexpected artifact clearing post-compromise suggests timeline tampering or anti-forensics.

suggestion.title: Phishing emails abusing AI service brands
suggestion.rationale: Article headline: 'AI brands as bait... in social engineering.' Primary attack vector is phishing campaigns impersonating ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, etc.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails with AI service brand references (ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, Gemini, etc.) in subject/sender combined with action requests (verify account, confirm credentials, update payment). Correlate sender domain against legitimate AI vendor domains; detect typosquats and subdomain spoofing.

suggestion.title: Credential harvesting via lookalike AI service portals
suggestion.rationale: Keywords cite 'Credential theft' as attack objective. Threat actors host fake login pages or fake AI services to harvest credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect user navigation to newly registered or character-substituted domains mimicking AI services (e.g., chatgp.ai, claud-e.com). Correlate with form submissions or credential entry patterns; flag high click-through rates on phishing links in email logs.

suggestion.title: Adversary-in-the-middle interception of AI service credentials
suggestion.rationale: Keywords explicitly list 'Adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM)' as attack method. Pipeline must map AiTM infrastructure and session-hijacking patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SSL/TLS certificate anomalies on AI service domains (mismatched issuer, validity mismatches). Detect DNS spoofing or traffic redirection to proxy infrastructure. Flag session tokens or bearer tokens transmitted over suspicious proxy paths.

suggestion.title: Anomalous login activity post-credential compromise
suggestion.rationale: Social engineering campaigns culminate in account compromise. Detection should capture post-phishing sign-in anomalies on compromised AI service accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-phishing credential theft, detect login attempts from impossible travel (contradictory geographies within minutes), new device/browser fingerprints, or after-hours logins for typically business-hours users. Correlate with phishing campaign timing.

suggestion.title: Bulk API access from compromised AI service credentials
suggestion.rationale: Attackers using stolen AI service credentials may pivot to API abuse for data exfiltration, token theft, or lateral movement within services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unusual API call patterns on compromised AI service accounts: high-volume requests, batch data retrieval, unusual endpoint access, or API key enumeration. Baseline normal API usage per user/tenant and alert on statistical deviation.

suggestion.title: Sentry Instance External Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable' — external reachability is the critical enabling prerequisite.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry / MobileIron Sentry instances (typical ports 8443, 8080, 443) accepting inbound connections from untrusted networks. Flag instances failing to establish mTLS handshake or responding to plain HTTP. Cross-reference with asset inventory to identify unmanaged appliances (absent from MDM enrollment, no EPMM registration).

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability' exploitable remotely without authentication — injection payloads in API requests are directly observable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/API requests to Sentry endpoints for shell metacharacters (|, ;, &&, ||, `, $()) embedded in unauthenticated request parameters. Detect command concatenation patterns, environment variable expansion, and command substitution syntax in POST/GET payloads targeting API endpoints.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Root-Level Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution' — spawning root processes without prior auth or elevation call is a narrow, high-confidence indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation with UID 0 (root) originating from Sentry service context (typically non-privileged user) without preceding setuid, sudo, or other privilege escalation syscalls. Correlate with absence of successful authentication or credential validation logs.

suggestion.title: mTLS/HTTPS Access Control Bypass Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'The use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors' — compliant instances should never accept unencrypted or non-mTLS connections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP (port 8080, 80) connection attempts to Sentry instances configured for mTLS-only (port 8443). Monitor TLS handshake failures indicating certificate bypass attempts. Detect sudden transitions from mTLS to cleartext or self-signed HTTPS.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged Sentry State Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability is exploitable 'in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state' — absence of management plane communications is a risk signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Sentry appliances with no outbound connections to expected management endpoints (Neurons, EPMM), missing health-check callbacks, or configuration drift from baseline. Flag appliances with no MDM enrollment status or absent from expected management inventory as unmanaged.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry: Vulnerable Version Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes vulnerability affects unpatched versions and is 'currently being exploited'—'Federal patch due: 2026-06-14' is the canonical signal for inventory hunts. Asset exposure detection requires identifying vulnerable instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for Ivanti Sentry instances running pre-patched versions. Cross-reference with network exposure (accessible externally, not behind mTLS/Neurons MDM). Rank by externally-reachable + unpatched for remediation priority.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payloads to Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'OS command injection vulnerability' and 'remote unauthenticated user' as attack vector. Exploitation requires delivery of malicious payloads to vulnerable endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to Ivanti Sentry listening ports for command injection patterns: backticks, $() syntax, semicolons in parameters, percent-encoding of shell metacharacters. Alert on attempts to known vulnerable endpoints (e.g., management interfaces) with shell-like payloads; correlate success with 200/302 responses.

suggestion.title: Root-Privilege Command Execution from Sentry Process
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability achieves 'root-level remote code execution'—post-exploitation detection should catch commands spawned with root UID from Sentry service process context or children.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation events where parent = Sentry service/daemon and user = root, spawning unusual binaries (shells, curl, nc, socat, reverse shells). Baseline legitimate Sentry process behaviors (expected child processes, execution user); hunt deviations.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Network Access to Ivanti Sentry External Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is exploitable 'where Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Detection must flag external-facing, pre-auth access attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry instances reachable from non-RFC1918 IP ranges. Flag unauthenticated or pre-authentication requests to management endpoints. Verify mTLS enforcement (mutual certificate validation) and Neurons MDM/EPMM network gating; alert if missing.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unmanaged State Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability only exploitable 'in cases where Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state.' This is the prerequisite condition for exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Sentry appliances for management status (enrolled in EPMM/Neurons MDM vs. standalone). Flag unmanaged instances as critical. Cross-reference with network reachability scans; unmanaged + externally-reachable = immediate escalation.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Internet-Exposed Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable' — external accessibility is the required attack surface
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Ivanti Sentry appliances (identify via product banners, certificate metadata, or known listening ports) with network paths to untrusted segments. Cross-reference against vulnerability scanner results for unpatched CVE-2026-10520 instances and prioritize for immediate isolation or patch.

suggestion.title: Command Injection Shell Spawning from Sentry Process
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow...root-level remote code execution' — execution phase detection should flag abnormal shell spawning from Sentry service accounts
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for shell or command-interpreter processes (sh, bash, cmd, powershell) spawned by Ivanti Sentry service accounts or parent processes. Flag if child process runs with root or system privileges and parent PID is Sentry-related.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Missing Protective Configuration Audit
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible' — these are absent in vulnerable instances; configuration audit is a hunt vector
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit Ivanti Sentry appliances for absence of mTLS enrollment, EPMM integration, or Neurons for MDM access restrictions. Flag appliances in 'unmanaged state' (per article) as vulnerable to unauthenticated remote exploitation and escalate for emergency remediation.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Presence in Asset Inventory and Vulnerability Scans
