suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry appliances for HTTP requests containing command injection payloads (shell metacharacters, backticks, $(..)) targeting administrative or API endpoints. Correlate with abnormal response codes (200/500 sequences) and timeouts indicating successful injection.

suggestion.title: Externally-Reachable Ivanti Sentry in Unmanaged State
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability is exploitable only 'when the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Environmental exposure is the precondition for attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference Ivanti Sentry appliances without mTLS EPMM or restricted HTTPS (unmanaged) that are reachable from non-RFC-1918 IP space. Flag deviations from segmentation policy requiring HTTPS hardening.

suggestion.title: Root-Privilege Command Execution on Ivanti Sentry Appliance
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'root-level remote code execution' as the achieved impact. Post-exploitation detection must identify unexpected root-context commands on affected appliances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on root-privilege process spawning, file modifications, or shell command execution on Ivanti Sentry that originated from unauthenticated or non-administrative sessions. Focus on entry points (web interface, CLI) that require authentication.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unauthenticated Administrative Access
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability permits 'remote unauthenticated' exploitation, indicating authentication can be bypassed or bypassed entirely. Administrative operations without valid session tokens are anomalous.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect administrative or privileged operations on Ivanti Sentry appliances without corresponding valid authentication events (missing login records, invalid/expired sessions, missing MFA tokens).

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Outbound Communication from Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Root-level RCE on a management appliance creates vector for C2 establishment, data exfiltration, or lateral movement. Egress telemetry is critical for post-compromise detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound traffic from Ivanti Sentry appliances for anomalous destinations (unknown external IPs, high-entropy DNS queries, protocol misuse). Flag egress from unmanaged appliances especially. Correlate with post-exploitation RCE indicators.

suggestion.title: Externally-Reachable Ivanti Sentry Appliance Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' External reachability is the necessary precondition for exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all Ivanti Sentry and MobileIron Sentry (legacy) appliances via CMDB/asset inventory. Verify external reachability via port scan (default HTTPS ports) and SSL certificate fingerprinting. Flag instances: (1) in 'unmanaged' state per management console, (2) without mTLS mutual authentication, (3) accessible from untrusted networks, (4) not behind VPN or IP whitelist.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload Detection in Sentry Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability.' Exploit attempts will contain command substitution syntax in HTTP/HTTPS requests to Sentry API endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to known Ivanti Sentry URI patterns for command injection indicators: backticks, $(), ${}, semicolon chains, pipe operators, &&/|| logic, command substitution in parameter values. Correlate with vulnerability scanner status for CVE-2026-10520. Flag requests from any source to unpatched appliances.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Root-Level Process Execution from Sentry Service
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability achieves 'root-level remote code execution.' Post-exploitation detection must identify suspicious process spawning with root privileges from the Sentry appliance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry appliance process logs for unexpected command execution with root UID. Alert on: (1) shell spawns (bash, sh, zsh) from Sentry process, (2) suspicious binaries (curl, wget, nc, python, perl) executed as root, (3) network activity (outbound connections) initiated by root-level processes spawned post-exploit, (4) file creation/modification in system directories (sbin, etc) from Sentry context.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scanner Coverage Verification
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'patch lag is the silent killer' and sets federal remediation due date 2026-06-14. Proactive scanner coverage verification is required to confirm detection before exploitation window closes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners (Qualys, Nessus, Tenable, Rapid7) for CVE-2026-10520 detection results on all Sentry appliances. Alert on: (1) appliances missing from scan scope, (2) scan results >7 days old, (3) 'vulnerable' or 'unpatched' status, (4) appliances with unknown patch state, (5) scanner unable to reach asset. Escalate critical by federal due date.

suggestion.title: Ivanti EPMM Management State Audit
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'unmanaged state' as exploitation prerequisite; 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access' are mitigations. Detection must identify appliances not under active management control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Ivanti EPMM/UEM console for Sentry appliance state. Flag instances with state: 'unmanaged', 'disconnected', 'registration_failed', 'unenrolled', or last-heartbeat >24hrs. Cross-reference with network accessibility scan. Prioritize remediation: bring under management via EPMM enrollment or restrict network access via firewall/VPN.

suggestion.title: mTLS Configuration and TLS Mutual Authentication Verification
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'use of mTLS with EPMM...makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors.' Detection must confirm mTLS enforcement to exclude false-positive exploitability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For each Sentry appliance accessible from untrusted networks, verify: (1) mutual TLS enforced (bidirectional certificate validation), (2) HTTPS-only (no HTTP/cleartext fallback), (3) client certificate required and validated, (4) certificate pinning or CA whitelist implemented. Flag appliances accepting anonymous TLS or HTTP cleartext access from external sources.

suggestion.title: Asset Inventory: Ivanti Sentry Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable'—prerequisite for detecting exploitation is first identifying all Ivanti Sentry instances (including legacy MobileIron Sentry) in the network inventory and their exposure posture.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory, installed software catalogs, and vulnerability scanners for 'Ivanti Sentry' or 'MobileIron Sentry'. Flag instances with external IP binding, public DNS resolution, or confirmed external reachability. Identify those running without mTLS/HTTPS access controls.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Attempt: OS Command Injection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'OS command injection vulnerability' as the attack vector. Detect exploitation in-flight before RCE succeeds by monitoring for command-injection payloads targeting Ivanti Sentry endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to Ivanti Sentry instances for OS command-injection indicators: semicolons, pipes, backticks, $() subshells in query parameters or POST bodies. Flag payloads containing recon commands (whoami, id, cat, ls) or shell escape sequences.

suggestion.title: Execution: Process Spawning from Ivanti Service Context
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 'root-level remote code execution' outcome; successful exploitation manifests as unexpected process execution originating from the Ivanti service or its child processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect command-line process creation (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, sh) with parent process tied to Ivanti Sentry (java.exe, sentry process). High-confidence signal if child process executes immediately after inbound HTTP request to Sentry endpoint.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation: Root-Level Activity Post-Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly notes 'root-level remote code execution'—post-compromise indicator is unexpected SYSTEM/root-privileged activity spawned directly or indirectly from Ivanti Sentry context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag process execution with SYSTEM or root UID initiated by or parented through Ivanti Sentry service during or immediately after exploitation window. Correlate with process telemetry showing elevation attempts, setuid/sudo calls, or unexpected privileged binary execution.

suggestion.title: Command & Control: Post-Exploitation Outbound Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes external exposure and 'unmanaged state'—implies threat actor control post-RCE. Detect outbound C2 or data-exfiltration channels from compromised Ivanti instance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected outbound TCP/UDP connections and DNS queries initiated from Ivanti Sentry server post-exploitation. Flag non-standard ports, suspicious TLDs, known C2 domains, or connections to suspicious ASNs correlating with command-injection exploitation window.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scan Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes CISA KEV status and explicitly states 'it's worth one quick check across your fleet — patch lag is the silent killer.' Vulnerability scanning is the foundational detection for known-exploited CVEs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor vulnerability scanner outputs for any detection of CVE-2026-10520 on Ivanti Sentry appliances. Alert on any finding regardless of patch status, as CISA KEV entries are actively exploited and scanner inconsistencies are common.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Sentry Appliance Management Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution', establishing that exploitation requires no authentication credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS access logs to Sentry appliance management interfaces for requests without valid authentication tokens. Alert on any unauthenticated connections, particularly from external IP ranges.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution from Sentry Service
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'root-level remote code execution', indicating successful exploitation spawns processes as root from the Sentry service context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected process creation originating from Sentry service parent process. Flag non-system processes spawned with SYSTEM/root privileges, especially shell invocations (sh, bash, cmd).

suggestion.title: Internet-Exposed Ivanti Sentry Appliance Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies external reachability as mandatory prerequisite: 'unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable'. This configuration vulnerability enables exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Use internet-facing asset scans (Shodan, Censys) to identify Ivanti Sentry appliances accessible from external networks. Flag any with default or weak management interface configurations.

suggestion.title: Sentry Appliance Unmanaged State Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state', making configuration state critical for risk stratification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Ivanti Sentry management console for appliances in unmanaged state. Cross-reference with network exposure scans; any unmanaged + externally reachable = immediate remediation priority.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'OS command injection vulnerability' as the exploitation mechanism. Web traffic logs may capture injection attempts before successful RCE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP request payloads to Sentry endpoints for command injection patterns (;, |, &&, ||, `, $(), newlines in URL parameters). Flag any requests with these patterns to unauthenticated Sentry endpoints.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Internet Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is exploitable when 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable'—exposure to external networks is the root precondition for this vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry instances with external inbound connectivity on standard ports. Cross-reference against internal asset inventory to locate unmanaged Sentry appliances. Alert on any Sentry endpoint responding to external requests—indicates exploitable state.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Command Injection Exploit Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'OS command injection vulnerability' as the attack vector. Need telemetry-based detection for injection syntax in Sentry HTTP requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints for command injection syntax patterns (backticks, $(), pipes, semicolons in request parameters, URL-encoded equivalents). Flag requests with high entropy or shell metacharacters in unexpected fields, especially if followed by successful authentication or process spawning.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Post-Exploitation Process Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article confirms attackers 'achieve root-level remote code execution.' Detect post-exploitation commands via unexpected process spawning from Sentry service context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unusual child process creation from Ivanti Sentry parent process or service account (typically running as root), especially shell interpreters (bash, sh, cmd.exe) or network utilities (curl, wget, nc) spawned in that context. Look for UID 0 (root) processes spawned from Sentry service boundaries.

suggestion.title: Suspicious WKScriptMessage postMessage with crafted callback IDs
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'passes the id field from a WKScriptMessage body to commandDelegate sendPluginResult:callbackId: with no format validation.' Detection should target abnormal message patterns from InAppBrowser contexts with unexpected or malformed callback IDs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for WebView message posting patterns (JavaScript console, MitM proxies, app instrumentation) where message.id field contains unexpected characters, excessive length, or injection patterns (SQL/code injection-like syntax). Flag if originating from untrusted or newly-loaded domains within InAppBrowser context.

suggestion.title: InAppBrowser loading from suspicious or untrusted origins
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires attacker-controlled content in the WebView. Article states 'any web content loaded inside the InAppBrowser can fire any pending Cordova callback.' Hunt for InAppBrowser instantiation with unusual URLs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect InAppBrowser opens to file:// URLs, data: URLs, or domains flagged as malicious/compromised. Correlate with network inspection logs showing HTTP downgrade, certificate pinning bypass, or MitM indicators during InAppBrowser session establishment.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Exposure Scan
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is exploitable 'in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable' — foundational hunt for asset exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances (port 443, HTTPS certificate fingerprints, HTTP response banners) reachable from internet-routable sources. Cross-reference against internal asset inventory. CISA due-date priority: 2026-06-14.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability' and 'remote unauthenticated user' — requires detection of payload patterns in request logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for shell metacharacters (|, ;, &&, `, $(), backticks) or common command-injection patterns (whoami, id, cat, chmod) in HTTP parameters, headers, or POST bodies targeting Ivanti Sentry endpoints.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution on Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'root-level remote code execution' as the impact — successful exploitation will spawn processes under root context on the appliance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry appliance process logs for unexpected system commands (bash, sh, perl, python) executed with root privileges following HTTP requests from external sources.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry in Unmanaged State Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability requires 'unmanaged state with endpoints externally reachable' — mTLS or Neurons for MDM protect managed instances, so configuration audit is critical.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Ivanti Sentry appliance configuration to confirm EPMM registration, Neurons for MDM enrollment, and mTLS/restricted HTTPS enforcement. Unmanaged appliances should trigger immediate remediation workflow.

suggestion.title: Public-facing Ivanti Sentry asset detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable' — exposure is the prerequisite condition for exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate Ivanti Sentry / MobileIron Sentry instances accessible from untrusted networks. Use external asset inventory, passive DNS (*.sentry.ivanti.com lookups), port scanners, or cloud discovery. Flag those without mTLS and Neurons-for-MDM access controls.

suggestion.title: HTTP command injection payload to Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'OS command injection vulnerability' — the attack mechanism requires detecting malformed requests containing shell metacharacters or injection strings.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints (identify by asset scanning above) for command-injection payloads: backticks, $(), ||, &&, ;, | characters in query strings or POST bodies. Baseline benign traffic first; flag significant deviation.

suggestion.title: Root process spawning from Ivanti Sentry service
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'root-level remote code execution' — post-exploitation, RCE must manifest as privileged process creation on the appliance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On Ivanti Sentry appliances, detect unexpected root/SYSTEM process creation (especially shells: bash, sh, cmd.exe, powershell) spawning from the Sentry service or its parent. Correlate timing with suspicious HTTP requests within 1–2 minutes.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry mTLS and Neurons-for-MDM disabled
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible' — absence of these controls is a pre-exploitation risk indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan Ivanti Sentry appliances (management interface) to confirm mTLS is enabled and endpoint access is restricted via Neurons for MDM or equivalent. Flag instances with unencrypted HTTP, disabled mTLS, or unrestricted endpoint exposure.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry version & patch status baseline
suggestion.rationale: Article names product and federal patch deadline 2026-06-14 — standard vulnerability management requires inventory and status tracking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all Ivanti Sentry appliances via vulnerability scanner, service enumeration, or asset DB. Tag with version and CVE-2026-10520 patch status. Alert on unpatched instances or missing patch-date information. Report against federal deadline for audit readiness.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Exposed Asset Inventory & Patch Status
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable' — foundational hunt must identify Sentry instances on internet-facing infrastructure and their patch status relative to due date 2026-06-14.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and asset database for Ivanti Sentry/MobileIron Sentry instances. Filter for CVE-2026-10520 unpatched status or patch date prior to 2026-06-14. Cross-reference with firewall rules to confirm internet-facing access (public IP, no geo-fencing). Exclude instances protected by mTLS or HTTPS IP restrictions per vendor guidance.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection to Sentry Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution' — pipeline missed the actual exploitation vector: HTTP requests containing shell metacharacters to Sentry API/management endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints for command injection payloads: shell metacharacters (|, &, ;, $(), backticks, newlines) in request parameters, POST bodies, or headers. Alert on 200 responses (successful execution) or 500/502 (crash/error indicating exploitation attempt). Baseline against known-clean administrative traffic.

suggestion.title: Root-Context Process Spawning Post-RCE
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'root-level remote code execution' — successful exploitation will manifest as shell/command interpreter spawned from Sentry application process running as root/SYSTEM. Execution phase detection is entirely absent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation where parent is Ivanti Sentry service (e.g., ivanti_sentry, mobileironmanager, java process matching Sentry pattern) spawning shell interpreters (/bin/sh, /bin/bash, cmd.exe, powershell.exe) with UID/GID=0 (root) or SYSTEM. Cascade to monitor child process arguments for data exfil or lateral-move utilities (curl, wget, nc, ssh, scp).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Outbound Connections from Sentry Root Context
suggestion.rationale: Article describes unguarded root RCE with no mention of sandboxing — attacker will establish C2 or data exfil from compromised appliance. Post-exploitation network activity is undetected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound connections (TCP/UDP) originating from Ivanti Sentry appliance to non-whitelisted external IPs, especially to common C2 ports (443, 8080, 8443) or raw sockets. Monitor for DNS queries from Sentry context to suspicious/newly-registered domains or TLD patterns. Cross-reference against baseline of expected outbound (NTP, DNS, SNMP, patch servers).

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via mTLS/HTTPS Bypass Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible' — detection should include attempts to bypass these protective mechanisms or confirm they are absent in vulnerable configurations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for mTLS handshake failures or bypasses to Sentry endpoints: non-mTLS HTTP traffic to HTTPS-only ports, requests missing client certificates, or IPs outside trusted MDM/management ranges accessing Sentry APIs. Correlate with HTTP 4xx/5xx errors to identify exploitation attempts rejected by protective layers.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Configuration/Admin Endpoint Probing
suggestion.rationale: Article implies pre-exploit reconnaissance — attackers must confirm Sentry instance exists and is unprotected before attempting RCE. Pipeline missed reconnaissance use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect repeated HTTP GET/HEAD requests from external IPs to Ivanti Sentry known paths (/api/v1/system, /setup, /status, /admin, /console.jsp) returning 200 or 302 (confirming presence). Alert on spike in 401/403 responses to these endpoints—may indicate enumeration followed by exploitation. Baseline against known CI/monitoring tools.

suggestion.title: Malicious PAM Module Replacement Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers 'replaced legitimate pam_unix.so modules with backdoored versions that accept hardcoded passwords and harvest user credentials.' Nine distinct variants compiled separately suggests active exploitation. Core persistence mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor /lib64/security/pam_unix.so and /usr/lib*/security/pam_unix.so for unauthorized file modifications via file integrity monitoring (FIM). Alert on hash mismatches, unexpected file replacement, or modification timestamps outside known patching windows. Cross-correlate with PAM-related process execution anomalies.

suggestion.title: Trojanized OpenSSH Component Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'replaced OpenSSH components such as ssh, sshd, and scp with trojanized versions that captured credentials, logged commands entered during SSH sessions, and stored the collected data locally.' Direct evidence of credential interception at authentication layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: File integrity monitoring on /usr/bin/ssh, /usr/sbin/sshd, /usr/bin/scp for unauthorized replacements. Monitor for ssh/sshd binary hash deviations from baseline. Alert on suspicious file writes to paths containing locally-stored SSH logs or command histories in non-standard locations.

suggestion.title: SOCKS5 Proxy Masquerading as smbd Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'installed a custom SOCKS5 proxy for network traffic tunneling' that 'ran as a daemon masquerading as smbd -D, using different filenames and ports on each host.' Clear lateral movement and C2 indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for smbd processes with unusual command lines (daemon flags not matching known Samba configurations) or listening on non-standard ports. Alert on SOCKS5 proxy signatures in network traffic (IPv4 0x05 handshakes on non-1080 ports). Correlate process name masquerade with network tunneling signatures.

suggestion.title: Nginx Configuration Modification for Covert Proxying
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attackers 'modified the configuration of a compromised internet-facing Nginx server to proxy specially crafted requests to a compromised backend server' with FastCGI forwarding. Core lateral movement bridge into air-gapped network.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Nginx configuration files (nginx.conf, conf.d/*) for unauthorized proxy_pass directives pointing to internal IPs or unusual backend_server targets. Alert on modifications outside change-control windows. Correlate with HTTP POST requests to backend servers with suspicious parameters.

suggestion.title: FastCGI-based Remote Execution to Isolated Network
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly documents attackers using 'FastCGI process (fcgiwrap) listening on a separate port... processing requests and launching a custom binary named uptime' that 'established SSH connections to systems within the isolated critical infrastructure network using parameters supplied in HTTP POST requests.' This is the access vector into air-gapped segment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for fcgiwrap or FastCGI processes listening on ports outside 9000-9999 standard range. Alert on HTTP POST requests to Nginx backends with SSH parameters embedded. Watch for 'uptime' or similar masqueraded binaries spawning sshpass or ssh child processes. Correlate HTTP request timestamps with SSH connections to isolated segment.

suggestion.title: GS-Netcat Reverse Shell with Relay Domain C2
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'deployed a modified GS-Netcat reverse shell disguised as a legitimate system component that connected to a hardcoded relay domain, providing encrypted remote shell access.' Initial foothold and C2 channel.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for GS-Netcat process signatures or process masquerading with GS-Netcat behavioral fingerprint (encrypted reverse shell callback to hardcoded domain). Monitor for child processes spawning Unix shells from unexpected parent processes. Alert on DNS queries or connections to relay domains. File integrity checks on system components for GS-Netcat embedded code.

suggestion.title: Splunk Unauthenticated RCE Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Attackers Run Code Without Authentication'—core attack vector. Pipeline missed the foundational detection: unusual HTTP requests to Splunk endpoints attempting code execution or shell spawning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk instance for HTTP requests to known RCE endpoint paths (e.g., /admin/apps/, /api/) from non-authenticated sources or with suspicious payloads. Alert on 401 responses followed by process execution or port binding.

suggestion.title: Child Process Spawned by Splunk Services
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies code execution—attacker goal is to run arbitrary commands. Pipeline failed to suggest process-based detection for shell/command execution spawned from Splunk daemon.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when Splunk service (splunkd.exe, splunkd process) spawns cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, or sh without legitimate scheduled search context. Baseline benign children; flag new executes.

suggestion.title: Splunk Service Unexpected Network Connection Initiation
suggestion.rationale: Compromised Splunk instance typically establishes C2 or lateral-movement connections. Article emphasizes 'attackers run code'—follow-on activity detection critical.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections initiated by Splunk service to non-whitelisted IPs/ports. Flag connections to non-standard ports, residential IP ranges, or known C2 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Authentication Bypass to Splunk Admin Interface
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'without authentication'—detection must cover both the exploit itself and post-exploitation unauthorized admin access. Pipeline did not suggest auth-bypass or privilege-escalation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful admin-level API calls or configuration changes (e.g., adding users, enabling forwarding, modifying search permissions) without corresponding authentication log entry or from unexpected source IPs.

suggestion.title: Web Shell or Script Upload to Splunk Instance
suggestion.rationale: Persistent RCE typically requires backdoor placement. No detection suggested for suspicious file uploads to Splunk app directories or web-accessible paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk application directories (/opt/splunk/etc/apps/, /var/www/html/) for new .py, .sh, .php, or .jsp files created outside of deployment windows or by non-admin processes.

suggestion.title: Splunk Configuration or App Installation via Unauthenticated Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Without auth requirement, attacker can install malicious apps or modify configs. Pipeline missed detection for unauthorized cluster-manager API calls, app deployments, or server.conf modifications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST/PUT requests to /services/apps/local/ or cluster-manager endpoints with app tarballs or config payloads from IPs without prior successful authentication. Cross-reference against legitimate deployment schedules.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Execution Spawned by AUR Package Build
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 400+ hijacked AUR packages. During makepkg execution, malicious code in PKGBUILD scripts will spawn child processes (bash, curl, python). Article text: '400+ AUR Packages Hijacked'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag when makepkg or yay child processes execute bash/sh with network calls (curl, wget) or write to ~/.bashrc, ~/.zshrc, or /etc/profile.d/. Establish baseline for expected AUR package builds by package name.

suggestion.title: Persistence Injection via Shell Configuration from Package Manager Cache
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain compromises commonly achieve persistence via shell initialization files. Article implies code injection in build artifacts. Malicious PKGBUILD scripts will modify shell RC files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor modification of user shell initialization files (.bashrc, .zshrc, .profile, .bash_profile) by processes spawned from ~/.cache/yay/* or /var/cache/pacman/pkg. Alert on additions sourcing hidden files or containing one-liner payloads.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized AUR Repository Commit or Maintainer Account Activity
suggestion.rationale: 400+ packages hijacked implies repository credential compromise, account takeover, or impersonation of legitimate AUR maintainers. Article states: 'Atomic Arch Campaign' targeting AUR.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For internal AUR mirrors: alert on git commits from new IP addresses, geographically impossible login sequences, or push events that modify PKGBUILD, inject dependencies, or add binary files. Flag unusual update cadences per maintainer.

suggestion.title: Network Beaconing from Compromised AUR Package Process
suggestion.rationale: Hijacked packages likely execute C2 callbacks or exfiltration post-install. Attack vector implies malicious code establishment of outbound connections from unprivileged user context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate unexpected outbound connections from processes spawned by makepkg or initiated seconds-to-minutes after AUR package installation. Flag non-standard ports, non-HTTP protocols, or connections to unfamiliar ASNs.

suggestion.title: Installation of Known-Malicious AUR Package by Name or Checksum
suggestion.rationale: Once the affected packages are enumerated, detection must cover installed instances. Article is the canonical source: '400+ AUR Packages Hijacked' — package enumeration is necessary for inventory/remediation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain lookup of known-compromised package names and checksums. Alert when identified packages appear in /var/cache/pacman/pkg, pacman transaction logs, or when yay cache is accessed. Cross-reference with process execution trees.

suggestion.title: macOS Tahoe 26 Artifact Creation or Access
suggestion.rationale: Article title establishes discovery of new macOS forensic artifact. Pipeline generated zero detection logic. Article phrase: 'New MacOS Tahoe 26 Artifact Discovered'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for filesystem events on macOS artifact storage locations associated with Tahoe 26 artifact. Alert on processes accessing or enumerating forensic artifact databases or preference files that would reveal this newly-discovered collection vector.

suggestion.title: Menu Selection History Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates artifact 'tracks user menu selections across the operating system'—explicit collection activity. Pipeline missed this execution vector entirely. Article phrase: 'tracks user menu selections'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes (especially non-Apple, unsigned binaries) accessing macOS menu state databases or preference files. Monitor for forensic tools or scripts enumerating user interaction artifacts.

suggestion.title: Forensic Artifact Exfiltration

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempts — Sentry

Establish baseline of legitimate child processes; flag anomalies.

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to Ivanti Sentry endpoints (8443, 443) for command metacharacters in request parameters, POST bodies, headers: pipe (|), semicolon (;), backtick, $(), &&, ||, grave accents. Correlate with 200 responses or server errors (500) indicating command execution vs. baseline 403/401 auth failures.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution from Ivanti Sentry Service
suggestion.rationale: Article outcome: 'root-level remote code execution.' Successful exploitation manifests as elevated-privilege process spawn from Sentry service context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child processes spawned from Ivanti Sentry listening service (UID != 0 initially) that execute with UID=0 or EUID=0, or spawn /bin/sh, /bin/bash, or system utilities (whoami, id, curl, wget) with root privileges. Correlate with network ingestion events (failed auth logs preceding execution).

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Session Establishment to Ivanti Sentry APIs
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is 'exploitable by remote unauthenticated user.' Detection should capture unauthorized API access preceding command-injection attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry management/API endpoints for successful HTTP 200/302/session-cookie responses without preceding authentication events (login failures, no credentials in request). Baseline legitimate admin/MDM traffic and alert on anomalous source IPs, off-hours access, or rapid exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unpatched Version Confirmation Across Fleet
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'patch lag is the silent killer' with federal due date 2026-06-14. Continuous validation that vulnerable versions remain absent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner, CMDB, or package-management logs for Ivanti Sentry product family. Identify instances running versions prior to patched build for CVE-2026-10520. Alert on: unpatched instances still externally routable, patched versions with HTTPS access not using mTLS, or instances modified after patch date (potential re-exploitation attempts).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Non-mTLS Network Connections to Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies mTLS with EPMM or 'restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible.' Unencrypted or non-mTLS connections represent exploitation risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor network flows to Ivanti Sentry listening ports from external or untrusted networks. Identify connections using TLS v1.0/1.1 (weak), missing ALPN/EPMM indicators, or plaintext HTTP to port 8080/8888 variants. Baseline known MDM traffic (mTLS SigAlg, certificate pinning) and alert on non-conforming connections.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scan Detection — Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'match against your vulnerability scanner' and provides CVE-2026-10520 as template substitution; no use case generated for the canonical detection mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when vulnerability scanners report CVE-2026-10520 detected on any Ivanti Sentry appliance, particularly those on external-facing networks. Prioritize appliances with patch lag beyond the federal due date (2026-06-14).

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable' and calls out asset-exposure hunt as canonical; pipeline produced no network-based discovery use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for Ivanti Sentry products accessible on external-facing network interfaces or responding to public IP addresses. Correlate port scans and DNS data to identify externally discoverable instances of the product.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload Detection — Ivanti Sentry HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability' as exploitation method; no WAF or HTTP-log detection use case generated for injection payloads despite being the core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints for command injection indicators (backticks, $(), pipes, semicolons) in URL parameters and POST bodies, especially requests lacking valid authentication headers. Correlate with endpoint availability drops to identify successful exploitation.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Root Process Spawning — Ivanti Sentry Service
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies 'root-level remote code execution' as outcome; no detection use case for privilege elevation or post-exploitation process execution despite root privilege escalation being the attack's end goal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On Ivanti Sentry hosts, flag process creation events where the Sentry service or user account spawns shell interpreters (bash, sh) or system utilities while running as UID 0 (root). Correlate with recent failed HTTP authentication attempts to indicate post-exploitation activity.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unmanaged State Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability is 'successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state'; no use case generated for identifying unmanaged or misconfigured appliances despite being the explicit exploitation precondition.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare Ivanti Sentry inventory against management platform enrollment records. Alert on appliances not reporting to EPMM or Neurons MDM (which the article notes restrict access). Flag appliances missing recent policy pushes or configuration attestations as unmanaged and high-risk.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Remote OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempt

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry API and web endpoints for unauthenticated HTTP requests containing shell metacharacters (;, |, &, `, $()), command separators, or subprocess/exec patterns in query parameters or POST bodies. Trigger on unauthenticated requests to Sentry management endpoints combined with command-injection signatures.

suggestion.title: Externally-Reachable Unmanaged Ivanti Sentry Appliance Exposure

Cross-reference CMDB/MDM for 'unmanaged' state and absent mTLS/EPMM/Neurons restrictions. Escalate externally-routable instances running CVE-2026-10520 vulnerable versions.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation to Root via Sentry RCE

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry service account (sentry, _sentry, daemon) for spawning child processes with UID 0, interactive shell access, or modifications to /etc/sudoers, /etc/shadow, setuid binaries. Alert on credential-access or privilege-escalation tool invocation (sudo, su) from Sentry process context.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Patch Compliance and Vulnerability Status

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scans for Ivanti Sentry instances and verify patch status for CVE-2026-10520. Flag instances running vulnerable versions, especially past federal due date 2026-06-14. Escalate externally-facing unpatched Sentry appliances with highest priority.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry mTLS Configuration Bypass or Misconfiguration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors'—establishes baseline for failed mitigations and misconfigured controls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish TLS baseline for legitimate Sentry connections (expected client certificates, authorized CAs). Alert on HTTP (non-HTTPS) connections to Sentry interface, TLS downgrades, missing client certificates, or unauthenticated access from unexpected sources. Detect bypass or circumvention of mTLS/EPMM restrictions.

suggestion.title: InAppBrowser WKScriptMessage arbitrary callback dispatch (execution detection)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Any web content loaded inside the InAppBrowser can fire any pending Cordova callback in the host app by posting a message whose id field [has] no format validation.' This is the core attack mechanism—untrusted content triggers arbitrary app callbacks without validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: iOS apps using Cordova/InAppBrowser may expose callback dispatch events in logs or system traces. Look for rapid, out-of-order, or unexpected callback IDs being fired by WebView processes, especially when InAppBrowser is loading external or attacker-controlled content. Anomalies in callback timing or ID ranges could indicate exploitation.

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate InAppBrowser WebView activity (especially to external/untrusted origins detected via proxy or MDM) with subsequent token issuance, account grants, or authentication events from the same device within 5–30 minutes. Flag if grants occur to previously-unseen apps or from atypical IPs post-InAppBrowser activity.

Prioritize by user role, device internet exposure, and whether device is enrolled in MDM. Alert on install of 3.1.0–6.0.0 post-announcement of fix.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry—External Interface Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability requires 'endpoints externally reachable'—this is an explicit precondition for exploitation. Pipeline missed the asset-exposure hunt template reference in the body.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound traffic to Ivanti Sentry (known ports/interfaces) from untrusted networks. Correlate with internal asset inventory to identify externally-exposed Sentry appliances. Cross-reference against CVE-2026-10520 patch status.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry—Unmanaged Device State Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly notes exploit works when appliance is in 'unmanaged state'—this is a distinguishing vulnerability condition the pipeline ignored.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Ivanti Sentry appliances reporting unmanaged status to parent EPMM/Neurons for MDM systems. Flag unmanaged Sentry appliances with external network reachability as high-priority exposure.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry—OS Command Injection Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection' allowing 'root-level remote code execution'—pipeline failed to map the execution technique (command injection) and privilege escalation (root access) phases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry appliance logs and host process events for unexpected OS command execution, especially root-privileged processes spawned from web service contexts. Look for shell metacharacters in HTTP request parameters or unusual process chains involving system binaries.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry—Successful Authentication Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes vulnerability allows 'remote unauthenticated user' access—pipeline missed detection for authentication bypass or missing authentication checks on Sentry endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unauthenticated requests successfully reaching sensitive Ivanti Sentry endpoints or API calls. Flag HTTP 200/204 responses to endpoints typically requiring authentication, or absence of expected authentication headers in access logs.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry—mTLS/Secure Protocol Bypass Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article notes mitigation through 'mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS'—inverse detection: track direct unencrypted or unsecured protocol access to Sentry that bypasses these controls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline expected Sentry communication patterns (mTLS to EPMM, restricted HTTPS endpoints). Alert on direct HTTP connections, unvalidated TLS certificates, or protocol downgrades to Sentry management interfaces.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520: Ivanti Sentry Exposed to Untrusted Networks
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability applies when 'endpoints externally reachable' in 'unmanaged state.' This network exposure is the prerequisite for exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on inbound connections to Ivanti Sentry appliances (port 8443 standard) from non-corporate/non-allowlisted IP ranges. Cross-reference with patch status from vulnerability scanner to identify unpatched instances against 2026-06-14 deadline.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry: Command Injection Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'OS command injection' as the attack vector. HTTP requests containing shell metacharacters should be flagged on unauthenticated endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP/HTTPS requests to Sentry API/admin endpoints containing shell metacharacters (pipe, semicolon, backtick, $(), command substitution, quote escapes). Prioritize requests lacking authentication tokens.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry: Root-Level Process Spawning
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'root-level remote code execution' as the impact. Any shell or system binary spawned with UID=0 from Sentry context indicates successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes with UID=0 (root) created by the Sentry daemon, particularly shell interpreters (sh, bash, ksh), commands reaching external IPs, or reverse-shell indicators. Baseline legitimate admin actions first.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520: Failed Exploit Attempt Signatures
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status indicates active wild exploitation. Web server error logs should show HTTP 500/502 or application crashes from malformed injection attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP 500/502/503 errors or application crashes correlating with anomalous request patterns (e.g., requests with injection syntax followed by connection resets). Use as early warning of attack probing.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry: Unauthenticated Successful Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'remote unauthenticated user' capability. Access logs showing command execution without valid credentials are post-exploitation indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Sentry logs for successful command/request processing (HTTP 200, exit code 0) on vulnerable endpoints without authentication headers, session tokens, or valid API keys. Correlate with unusual user agents or automated tools.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Public Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability exploitable 'when the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable'—external reachability is the critical attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory Ivanti Sentry appliances via network scans or DNS records. Flag any instances with public-facing management interfaces (typically port 443) or reachable from untrusted networks. Cross-reference against patch status for CVE-2026-10520.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Command Injection Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability'—the attack mechanism is command payload injection into an unauthenticated request.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to externally-reachable Ivanti Sentry instances for command injection payloads (shell metacharacters: ;, |, &, $(, backticks, newlines in suspicious parameters). Ivanti Sentry logs should be analyzed for unauthenticated requests containing shell syntax.

suggestion.title: Root-level Code Execution Following Sentry Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker 'achieve root-level remote code execution'—post-exploitation process execution under root context is the impact marker.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry appliance process logs for unexpected root-level command execution, particularly spawning shell interpreters (sh, bash, python) or reverse shells immediately following failed/anomalous authentication attempts or HTTP requests with suspicious payloads.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unmanaged Appliance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article notes vulnerability exploitable specifically 'when the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state'—appliance configuration posture is a key risk factor.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for Ivanti Sentry instances missing expected management-plane connectivity (EPMM integration) or restricted HTTPS policies. Unmanaged appliances should be flagged for immediate remediation regardless of patch status.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article title and body directly reference CVE-2026-10520 as CISA KEV. Federal patch deadline 2026-06-14 is mandatory. Pipeline omitted basic vulnerability management use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-10520 detections against all assets running Ivanti Sentry. Flag any host with status 'unpatched' or version < [patched version]. Cross-reference against asset inventory for undocumented or rogue deployments.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Network Exposure—Internet-Facing Asset
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable' and attacker model assumes 'external actors.' This is network-layer initial access precondition.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Ivanti Sentry instances (port 8443, 9999, or banner-identified) reachable from untrusted networks (CIDR:0.0.0.0/0). Query threat-intel feeds (Censys, Shodan) for public exposure. Correlate with asset inventory to identify undocumented or misjudged network placements.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unauthenticated Command Injection Attack Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'remote unauthenticated user' exploitation via 'OS command injection.' T1059.001 execution vector and attack surface are explicit but unaddressed by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP(S) requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints (admin console, gateway endpoints) containing command injection payloads (semicolon, pipe, backtick, $(), command substitution syntax) sent without valid session/auth token. Look for 200-299 responses (success indicators) to suspicious requests.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Post-Exploitation RCE Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article claims 'root-level remote code execution.' Successful exploitation spawns unexpected process trees from Sentry daemon; pipeline missed T1548 privilege escalation and process-level execution detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for shell interpreter spawning (bash, sh, zsh, python) from Ivanti Sentry service accounts or daemon processes (MobileIronServer, sentry-gateway, etc.). Root-owned child processes from normally-unprivileged daemons indicate successful exploitation. Baseline normal behavior and alert on deviation.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Lateral Movement Post-RCE
suggestion.rationale: Root-level code execution on appliance enables lateral movement to domain-joined systems and internal services. Article doesn't restrict impact scope; post-exploitation pivot detection is missing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After identifying Sentry RCE, hunt for suspicious outbound connections from the appliance to internal infrastructure (LDAP, Kerberos, databases, management planes). Detect credential harvesting tools (secretsdump, mimikatz, ssh-keyscan) execution from Sentry process context. Monitor for lateral-move patterns: SMB/RPC connections, SSH pivots, or internal scan traffic.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry mTLS/Segmentation Bypass Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article notes mTLS and restricted HTTPS access as mitigations. Detection should validate that these controls are actually enforced; absence or misconfiguration leaves appliance vulnerable despite patch.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Verify mTLS enforcement on Ivanti Sentry endpoints via certificate pinning validation and mutual auth logs. Audit firewall rules and load-balancer policies to confirm restricted HTTPS access. Flag any Sentry endpoint accepting cleartext HTTP or missing mTLS checks. Alert on certificate validation bypass attempts.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2026-10520' and 'match against your vulnerability scanner.' Pipeline extracted zero IOCs despite this being the primary indicator. CISA KEV entries demand immediate scanner correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any scan result identifying Ivanti Sentry (product signature) with CVE-2026-10520 exposure. Escalate findings where appliances are externally routable or lack mTLS/restricted-HTTPS mitigation. Federal due date 2026-06-14 should trigger executive escalation.

suggestion.title: External Reachability of Ivanti Sentry Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article states exploit 'can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' This is the precondition; pipeline missed exposure hunting entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query network inventory and external scanning data for Ivanti Sentry (MobileIron Sentry) instances reachable from untrusted networks. Cross-reference with asset inventory to identify appliances NOT behind mTLS or restricted HTTPS. Flag unmanaged appliances with public network paths.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation in Web Logs
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'OS command injection vulnerability' as attack vector. Pipeline omits T1059 entirely despite this being the execution mechanism post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt Ivanti Sentry HTTP request logs and proxy records for command metacharacter payloads (`;|&$(){}<>[]`) in GET/POST parameters or headers targeting known vulnerable endpoints. Monitor for common RCE POC signatures. Alert on successful responses (200-302) following suspicious parameter injection.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Sentry Management Interfaces
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'remote unauthenticated user' achieves RCE. Pipeline should hunt for unauthenticated requests to Ivanti Sentry management paths, but generated no use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of authenticated vs. unauthenticated requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints (e.g., `/mobileironserver/admin`, `/endpoint_control/`). Alert on successful responses (status 200-302) to management endpoints from sources without prior authentication session. Correlate with IP geolocation and external scanning metadata.

suggestion.title: Root/System Privilege Process Spawning from Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article outcome: 'root-level remote code execution.' Pipeline omits privilege escalation detection. Arbitrary command execution at root is the exploit's impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor endpoint telemetry for processes spawned with root/SYSTEM privilege where parent process is Ivanti Sentry service account or binary. Establish clean baseline of legitimate root-spawned processes from Sentry. Flag anomalous child processes: shells (/bin/bash, /bin/sh, cmd.exe), network tools (curl, wget, nc), or persistence mechanisms.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Command Execution Behavior (RCE Confirmation)
suggestion.rationale: Once RCE achieved ('root-level remote code execution'), attacker runs arbitrary commands. Pipeline maps no post-exploitation hunting to detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-RCE, watch for reconnaissance and lateral-movement commands spawned from Sentry-rooted processes: id, whoami, uname, ps, getent, ssh, scp, wget, curl, iptables, cron modifications. Correlate command execution timeline with failed proxy/WAF alerts. Alert on credential dumping or persistence mechanisms (cron jobs, systemd services, SSH keys).

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk Web Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Attackers Run Code Without Authentication' — implies direct access to Splunk web interface endpoints (typically /en-US, /admin, etc.) without valid credentials. No detection use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Splunk web console endpoints from external/unauthenticated sources. Flag POST/PUT requests to admin or code-execution endpoints (e.g., /en-US/app/*, /admin/rest/*) where Splunk authentication token is absent or forged. Alert on rapid endpoint scanning followed by exploitation requests.

suggestion.title: Code Execution via Splunk Process Runtime
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'Run Code Without Authentication' — establishes execution channel. Article body truncated but vulnerability clearly enables arbitrary code execution. No use case for detecting spawned processes, reverse shells, or payload execution from Splunk runtime.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation events (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, sh, bash, python) spawned by Splunk runtime processes (splunkd.exe, mongod, python.exe running from SPLUNK_HOME). Flag unusual command-line arguments, network connections, or file operations from these child processes. Focus on non-standard interpreters or obfuscated commands.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Splunk Configuration or Script Injection
suggestion.rationale: Critical RCE in Splunk Enterprise likely exploits parsing of configuration, scripts, or query parameters. Article implies code execution path but no detection for malicious configuration writes or .conf file tampering is generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor writes to Splunk configuration directories ($SPLUNK_HOME/etc/, particularly app/*/local/, system/local/). Alert on .conf, .py, .sh files modified without documented deployment. Cross-reference with Splunk audit logs for any configuration changes sourced from unauthenticated requests or non-admin users.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Pattern: Splunk Vulnerable Version Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article is about a critical Splunk flaw but pipeline extracted no CVE ID, no affected versions, and no version-matching IOCs. Defenders need to identify vulnerable Splunk instances by version and patch status.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Splunk introspection logs or banner grabs for affected Splunk Enterprise versions (range TBD from CVE advisory). Cross-reference with network scans and process execution logs showing vulnerable Splunk daemons. Alert if vulnerable version is exposed on internet-facing ports or accessible from untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: Reverse Proxy / Web Service Layer Bypass Detection
suggestion.rationale: Unauthenticated access to Splunk web suggests auth bypass or path-traversal vector. No detection for requests that circumvent Splunk's authentication middleware or exploit authentication checks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Splunk endpoints for auth-bypass patterns: missing/null/forged auth headers, direct access to /admin/* or /api/* endpoints without prior successful login, or header-injection attempts. Flag requests with repeated 401/403 followed by successful code execution (200 with payload response).

suggestion.title: Suspicious AI Vendor Domain Registration & Phishing Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'AI brands as bait' and schema keywords include AiTM; implies threat actors registering/hosting lookalike domains (e.g., openai-verify.*, chatgpt-auth-*, claude-signin.*). Pipeline extracted zero IOCs despite article length suggesting domain enumeration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries and email links for lookalike AI vendor domains (e.g., Levenshtein distance < 2 from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Mistral). Flag registrations of AI-brand-containing domains with fast flux or short TTLs. Correlate with phishing report volume.

suggestion.title: AiTM Proxy Session Interception — Credential Capture
suggestion.rationale: Schema keyword 'Adversary-in-the-middle' is explicit. AiTM attacks intercept OAuth/SAML flows and harvest credentials/session tokens. Pipeline mapped zero kill-chain phases despite this being core to the article's threat model.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous sign-in patterns: auth sourced from infrastructure associated with credential-capture proxy operators (e.g., unusual geolocations, ISPs, SSL certificates issued to non-human entities). Flag browser-based AiTM indicators: referer headers pointing to attacker domains, session cookies stolen and replayed across different user-agents/IPs.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email with AI Tool Impersonation & Payload Redirect
suggestion.rationale: Core attack: using 'AI brands as bait' in social engineering. Article describes threat actors leveraging AI hype for lures. No phishing detection UC generated despite this being the stated attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails claiming to be from ChatGPT, Claude, or other AI platforms offering 'verification', 'account upgrade', 'trial access'. Flag emails with URLs redirecting to attacker-controlled phishing sites hosting AI vendor login pages. Monitor for macro-enabled docs or malware-laden attachments bundled with AI-themed social engineering.

suggestion.title: Token Theft & Replay — Harvested API Keys Reuse
suggestion.rationale: AiTM + credential theft pipeline likely results in stolen API keys or session tokens (e.g., OpenAI API keys, Anthropic tokens). Pipeline generated zero detection use cases for token replay or unusual API consumption patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag API token usage from non-standard IPs or geolocations relative to user baseline. Detect rapid token rotation or consumption spikes (e.g., bulk API calls to LLM endpoints). Monitor for tokens issued to AI services being replayed across multiple user identities or sessions.

suggestion.title: Domain Typosquatting & SSL Certificate Misuse for AI Services
suggestion.rationale: AiTM phishing requires hosting lookalike login pages. Article context ('AI brands as bait') implies certificate abuse. Zero IOCs extracted despite typical AiTM campaigns registering certificates for typosquatted domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for newly-issued SSL certificates with AI vendor names (OpenAI, Anthropic, Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini) registered to suspicious entities or via Let's Encrypt bulk issuance patterns. Flag certificates with mismatched Common Name/SAN fields. Correlate certificate issue date with phishing campaigns.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting Page Hosting — Infrastructure Fingerprinting
suggestion.rationale: AiTM attacks host credential-capture pages at attacker infrastructure. Pipeline should extract hosting IPs, ASNs, registrars as IOCs. Zero IOCs output indicates failure to parse article's likely inclusion of infrastructure indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify infrastructure hosting phishing pages by correlating ASN/registrar patterns, certificate issuer, and WHOIS privacy abuse. Detect clustering of typosquatted AI domains on same IP ranges or CDNs. Monitor for reverse-DNS mismatches and short-lived DNS records pointing to shared hosting.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: CVE-2026-10520 Ivanti Sentry Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs: 'CVE-2026-10520 — match against your vulnerability scanner.' Pipeline provided no IOC or use case for the canonical asset-exposure hunt despite providing the template reference.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any asset flagged by vulnerability scanner as vulnerable to CVE-2026-10520. Cross-correlate with network exposure (external IP, WAN-facing, unmanaged heartbeat status) to identify exploitable instances.

suggestion.title: Externally Reachable Ivanti Sentry Appliance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies prerequisite: 'This vulnerability can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' No detection for external network exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Sentry appliances (by banner, SSL cert subject, HTTP response headers) accessible from untrusted IP ranges. Flag any instance reachable from WAN or public-facing networks.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unmanaged State Indicator
suggestion.rationale: Article highlights 'the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state' as exploitation precondition. Unmanaged status is a critical risk signal absent from use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Sentry appliances missing heartbeat connectivity to EPMM or MDM console, or appliances with expired/invalid mTLS certificates. Combine with external-access signal.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempts on Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack vector: 'OS command injection vulnerability.' Execution-phase detection missing despite explicit description of injection mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry web/API endpoints for payloads containing shell metacharacters (;, |, &, backticks, $(), command substitution). Watch for suspicious process spawning from Sentry service daemon (running as root).

suggestion.title: Root-Level Post-Exploitation Activity from Sentry RCE
suggestion.rationale: Article confirms impact: 'achieve root-level remote code execution.' No post-exploitation detection for actions after successful injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After exploitation, monitor compromised Sentry appliance for root-level process creation, persistence mechanisms (cron/systemd modifications), lateral-movement scanning, or MDM/EPMM credential access.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Exposed / Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Detection must surface exposed Sentry instances before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances reachable from external IPs on management/API ports (typically 443). Cross-reference with configuration baseline to flag unmanaged instances not protected by mTLS or restricted HTTPS access.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Detect payloads in requests targeting Sentry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry endpoint logs for command injection payloads (shell metacharacters, backticks, pipes, semicolons in unexpected parameters). Flag if observed from unauthenticated context.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution from Sentry Service
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'achieve root-level remote code execution.' Successful exploitation will spawn privileged processes from Sentry service account or parent process.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal Sentry process trees. Alert when root/SYSTEM processes spawn from Sentry daemon without expected administrative activity (patching, restart). Correlate with HTTP request logs showing injection attempts.

suggestion.title: Sentry Appliance mTLS / EPMM Control Degradation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible.' Detect when protective controls are disabled or bypassed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry configuration for disablement or removal of mTLS enforcement, EPMM binding, or HTTP access restrictions. Alert on policy changes that expose endpoints without compensating controls.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged Sentry Instance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state' — state is a direct exploitation precondition. Inventory and baseline managed vs. unmanaged deployment modes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query MDM/EPMM console for Sentry instances NOT enrolled in centralized management. Cross-reference with firewall rules to identify which are externally reachable. Unmanaged + externally-routable = critical risk.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names CVE-2026-10520 as known-exploited in CISA KEV. 'Match against your vulnerability scanner' in Recommended hunts section means scanner data is the primary detection path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-10520 matches against Ivanti Sentry instances in your environment. Filter for positive findings (vulnerable systems) and cross-check against patch deployment records to identify lag. High-confidence discovery given CISA KEV status.

suggestion.title: Externally-Reachable Ivanti Sentry Appliance Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' This is the precondition for successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances (identify via asset inventory, DNS CNAME patterns, or certificate scanning) with inbound access from untrusted networks. Cross-check against mTLS/restricted HTTPS ingress rules; absence of protective controls + external reachability = high-risk exposure.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempt Against Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article describes the attack vector as 'OS command injection vulnerability' allowing 'unauthenticated' RCE. Exploitation requires command injection payloads in HTTP requests to Sentry endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry HTTP logs and WAF events for command injection patterns (shell metacharacters, backticks, command substitution syntax in URL paths/parameters). Look for unauthenticated requests (no session token) targeting known vulnerable endpoints. High baseline of exploitation attempts expected given KEV status.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution on Ivanti Sentry After External Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states successful exploitation 'could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Detection should focus on unexpected privilege escalation or root activity following external access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If Sentry appliance OS logs are accessible, correlate external HTTP requests from untrusted IPs with subsequent root-level process creation or privilege escalation events. Baseline normal Sentry operations first; any root spawning after external unauthenticated access is high-confidence exploitation indicator.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unmanaged State with External Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies unmanaged state as vulnerability precondition: 'can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state.' Detection should verify appliance management enrollment status.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Ivanti EPMM/Neurons management console or Sentry appliance status logs for enrolled vs. unmanaged appliances. Cross-reference unmanaged instances against network exposure findings from UC #2. Unmanaged + externally-reachable = critical risk tier requiring immediate remediation.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Reachability
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'exploitable in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable' — external network exposure is the gating condition for exploitation and the primary hunt vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan internet-facing infrastructure for Ivanti Sentry appliances. Identify port 443 banner signatures (Sentry/MobileIron), harvest certificate metadata, correlate with internal asset inventory. Flag any unaccounted appliances or those without mTLS/Neurons for MDM protection enabled.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Command Injection Payloads
