suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt HTTP requests to Sentry (endpoints: /mdsserver, /api, /admin) containing shell injection patterns: backticks, $(), semicolons, pipe operators, >, <, &&, || in parameter values. Correlate successful hits with subsequent process execution from Sentry service context.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution from Sentry Service
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'root-level remote code execution' as exploitation outcome — successful exploitation spawns child processes from Sentry daemon with UID 0 or equivalent elevated privilege.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor process creation where parent is Sentry service (sentry, mdm, or related daemon names). Flag unexpected child processes, especially interpreters (sh, bash, python) or network utilities (curl, wget, nc) executed with UID 0 or Sentry's effective privilege. Baseline against legitimate Sentry process trees.

suggestion.title: Sentry Appliance Unmanaged State Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability is exploitable only 'where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state' — configuration audit must confirm protective state (mTLS, Neurons for MDM) is active.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate Sentry appliance configuration: verify mTLS is enabled, confirm EPMM enrollment or Neurons for MDM is active, validate network ACLs restrict external access. Alert on appliances in 'unmanaged' state or with protective features disabled.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner Match: CVE-2026-10520 (Ivanti Sentry)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'match against your vulnerability scanner' for CVE-2026-10520. This is the baseline detection—any Ivanti Sentry asset should be scanned for this vulnerability, especially given CISA KEV status and active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any asset inventory record for Ivanti Sentry (vendor field matches 'Ivanti', product matches 'Sentry') that either (a) returns vulnerable status for CVE-2026-10520, or (b) has not been scanned in the past 7 days. Cross-reference with patch management to identify lag between patch availability (2026-06-14) and actual deployment.

suggestion.title: Network Exposure Hunt: Externally Accessible Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability is 'exploitable in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable' and describes it as a public-facing attack. Hunt for Ivanti Sentry instances on internet-routable IPs with exposed management ports.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances (fingerprint by service banner, SSL certificate product name, or known admin port ranges) accessible from untrusted networks (non-RFC1918 source IPs, non-corporate ASNs). Correlate with asset inventory to confirm unmanaged/exposed state. Alert on external connections to typical Sentry ports (443, 8443, etc.).

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation to Root: Ivanti Sentry Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability allows 'root-level remote code execution.' Post-exploitation detection should monitor for processes spawned by Ivanti Sentry services (typically non-root) that escalate to root UID, indicating successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor process creation where parent=ivanti sentry service process and child process uid=0 (root). Flag any child_process_name matching common command shells (bash, sh, cmd, powershell) spawned with escalated privileges. Correlate with network logs to confirm external source IP initiating the exploitation chain.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload Detection: Ivanti Sentry Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'OS command injection vulnerability' allowing remote unauthenticated exploitation. Detect malicious payloads attempting command injection against exposed Sentry endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect HTTP/HTTPS requests to known Ivanti Sentry endpoints for OS command injection patterns (shell metacharacters like pipes, semicolons, command substitution `$(...)` or `` `...` ``). suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'remote unauthenticated user' capability as requirement for exploitation — successful attacks bypass or exploit missing authentication controls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP/HTTPS requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints from external IP addresses that lack valid authentication tokens, session cookies, or mTLS client certificates; alert on repeated attempts with injection payloads.

suggestion.title: Malicious callback invocation from InAppBrowser WebView
suggestion.rationale: Article core vulnerability: 'passes the id field from a WKScriptMessage body to commandDelegate sendPluginResult:callbackId: with no format validation'. Attack requires JavaScript in the loaded web content to enumerate and invoke Cordova callbacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when InAppBrowser renders JavaScript that posts WKScriptMessage objects with id fields matching known Cordova callback patterns (auth, token, user-info, account). Baseline legitimate callback patterns per app; detect deviations and unknown callback IDs.

suggestion.title: Untrusted domain navigation in InAppBrowser
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability requires 'web content loaded inside the InAppBrowser' to execute malicious JavaScript. Initial access is user clicking a malicious link or redirect that opens in InAppBrowser outside the app's config.xml allowlist.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor InAppBrowser navigation (CFNetwork logs, MSEdge telemetry) to domains not in the app's Content Security Policy or Allow Intent URL allowlist. Flag newly-registered domains, high-velocity reputation changes, and redirects from trusted domains to untrusted ones.

suggestion.title: Account state change post-InAppBrowser callback
suggestion.rationale: Article maps T1098.001. Vulnerability enables arbitrary callback invocation, including those tied to account manipulation. Detect when account modification (password reset, MFA disable, credential addition) occurs immediately after InAppBrowser activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate InAppBrowser process events with downstream account attribute changes (Set-AzureADUser, Update-MgUser, credential grants). Flag high-risk modifications (MFA disable, secondary credential added, account delegation). Timeline: < 5 minutes between InAppBrowser event and account change.

suggestion.title: Token generation from InAppBrowser context
suggestion.rationale: Article maps T1528 (Steal Application Access Token). Vulnerability directly enables invocation of auth-related callbacks to extract tokens. Tokens issued immediately after InAppBrowser callback invocation are high-risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect OAuth token issuance (RefreshToken acquisition, access_token grant) originating from iOS device running vulnerable cordova-plugin-inappbrowser where the token request is preceded (within 2 minutes) by WKScriptMessage callback events or suspicious JavaScript execution.

suggestion.title: Cordova callback enumeration from web JavaScript
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation requires discovering what callbacks are available before invoking them. Article implies attacker-controlled code must enumerate: 'fire any pending Cordova callback' presupposes knowledge of which callbacks exist.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect JavaScript in untrusted InAppBrowser context attempting to enumerate or list Cordova plugin callbacks via reflection/introspection. Monitor for repeated failed callback invocations with incrementing ID patterns or known enumeration payloads.

suggestion.title: Externally Reachable Ivanti Sentry Appliance Inventory

This is the foundational asset-exposure hunt referenced in the article's own recommendations ('asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL') but pipeline produced no use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all Ivanti Sentry (formerly MobileIron Sentry) appliances reachable from external networks via DNS, asset inventory, or scanning. Flag instances showing unmanaged state configuration. Cross-reference with vulnerability scanner for patching status of CVE-2026-10520.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Sentry Management Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'remote unauthenticated user' exploitation. Pipeline should have surfaced network-based hunting for unauthenticated access attempts to Sentry management endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to known Ivanti Sentry management interface ports. Flag unauthenticated session access or 401/403 response patterns followed by successful authentication on externally reachable IPs. Correlate with known vulnerable versions.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Attack Attempts

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for shell metacharacters and command substitution patterns (semicolon, pipes, &&, $(), backticks) in HTTP request parameters sent to Ivanti Sentry management interface. Baseline normal legitimate traffic and flag deviations, particularly from external sources.

suggestion.title: Root-Privileged Process Execution from Sentry Context
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'root-level remote code execution' as impact. Pipeline should have generated post-exploitation detection for privilege escalation or command execution under root from Sentry process parent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation with SYSTEM/root privileges spawned from or under Sentry service account. Flag unexpected shell invocations (bash, sh, cmd.exe, powershell) or system utilities (curl, nc, dd) executing under elevated context from Sentry parent.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable' — external reachability is the required precondition for remote exploitation. This is the first detection layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry instances (typically port 4242/TCP) reachable from untrusted networks via firewall/WAF logs and network telemetry. Correlate externally routable IPs against CMDB to confirm Sentry appliances. High FP risk from intentional remote-access scenarios; require asset owner confirmation and mTLS/EPMM enrollment status.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Attempts to Ivanti Sentry Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies vulnerability as 'OS command injection' accessed via 'remote unauthenticated user' — HTTP/API requests should be monitored for injection metacharacters (pipes, semicolons, command substitution syntax).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound HTTP requests to Sentry endpoints for command injection patterns: shell metacharacters (|;&$()\`), URL/base64-encoded variants, and post-exploitation tools (ncat, curl). Alert on unauthenticated requests containing these patterns. FP risk from security scanners and legitimate admin tools; baseline approved traffic before alerting.

suggestion.title: Elevated-Privilege Process Spawning from Sentry Service

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation where parent is Ivanti Sentry service/daemon and child has root/SYSTEM ownership. Baseline normal Sentry operations (log rotation, service restarts). Alert on suspicious children: shells, reverse-shell utilities, credential dumpers, or lateral-movement tools. Critical finding if any process with root context spawned from Sentry after external network activity.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unmanaged State Detection

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query MDM/EPMM enrollment status for all Ivanti Sentry appliances. Cross-reference with external-exposure hunt. Flag systems marked externally-reachable AND not enrolled in mTLS/EPMM as critical-risk (unpatched + exposed + unprotected). Operationally, this is the highest-priority remediation list.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scanner Coverage

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file integrity of pam_unix.so and related PAM modules in /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/security/ and /lib64/ for hash mismatches against baseline packages. suggestion.title: SSH Binary Trojans (ssh, sshd, scp Replacement)

Monitor sshd for anomalous child processes, credential file access, or unusual environment variables. Detect SSH processes with command-line arguments inconsistent with normal authentication or session management.

suggestion.title: Systemd Service Persistence Implantation
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers achieved 'persistence either via a malicious systemd service or through startup script modification.' Systemd services persist across reboots and provide hands-off C2 execution.

Alert on systemd units spawning reverse shells, connecting to external IP addresses, or executing binaries from non-standard directories. Correlate with systemctl enable/start activity.

suggestion.title: SOCKS5 Proxy Masquerading as Samba Daemon

Alert on multiple distinct processes claiming smbd identity on different high-numbered ports. Correlate with SOCKS5 handshake signatures in network traffic; genuine Samba processes should match package baselines.

Alert on fcgiwrap spawning shell interpreters or system execution binaries. suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Validate file signatures of ssh, sshd, scp, ssh-keysign and other OpenSSH binaries against OS package manifests. Alert on unauthorized modifications to these binaries or mismatches in binary hashes. Monitor for unusual file creation events in SSH binary directories and correlate with unexpected SSH process behavior such as forking to credential-storage utilities.

suggestion.title: Suspicious SOCKS5 Proxy Service Masquerading as System Daemon
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'installed a custom SOCKS5 proxy for network traffic tunneling... The proxy ran as a daemon masquerading as 'smbd -D', using different filenames and ports on each host.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for unexpected SOCKS5 proxy processes (e.g., ss5, dante, custom SOCKS binaries) running on non-proxy systems. Alert on processes masquerading as system services (smbd -D, sshd, syslogd) that establish unexpected network listening sockets. Monitor for unusual port numbers and correlate with recent file creation or process execution anomalies on those hosts.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated HTTP POST to Splunk REST API Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'without authentication' code execution. Pipeline failed to generate detection for unauthenticated API exploitation, which is the core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST requests to Splunk REST API endpoints (e.g., /services/json/v1) from external sources lacking valid authentication headers or tokens. Baseline legitimate admin/API traffic and alert on anomalous patterns or error responses indicating exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Splunk Process Spawning System Commands
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes code execution capability; no detection use case addresses post-exploitation process activity. Unauthenticated RCE typically results in arbitrary command execution in target process context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor child processes spawned by Splunk daemon processes (splunkd.exe, splunk-python.exe) executing system commands (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, /bin/sh). Flag interactive shells or command execution outside scheduled maintenance windows and baseline Splunk operations.

suggestion.title: Anomalous HTTP Methods to Splunk Admin Console
suggestion.rationale: Critical unauthenticated vulnerability implies exploit delivery via HTTP verb (PUT/POST/DELETE). Pipeline generated no payload or HTTP-level detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PUT, DELETE, or POST requests to Splunk administrative endpoints (/en-US/app, /admin) from untrusted subnets without valid session cookies or authorization headers. Alert on requests containing encoded payloads or unusual request sizes.

suggestion.title: NSO Group Phishing Domain Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'NSO Group's New WhatsApp Phishing Attack.' Pipeline extracted zero IOCs despite threat actor and attack type both named in title.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries and HTTP traffic for domains impersonating WhatsApp or Meta login portals known to be used by NSO Group infrastructure. Cross-reference against Meta's disclosed IOCs and OSINT feeds documenting NSO campaigns.

suggestion.title: WhatsApp Account Compromise Post-Phishing
suggestion.rationale: Phishing campaign success would lead to credential theft and account takeover. Article describes active attack; should detect post-compromise behavioral anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on WhatsApp login from new device/geolocation immediately following credential entry on phishing page. Monitor for login storms or password spray patterns against Meta/WhatsApp properties within hours of phishing email delivery.

suggestion.title: NSO Spyware Installation Behavior (Post-Compromise)
suggestion.rationale: NSO Group historically leverages phishing as entry point to deploy Pegasus/other surveillance tools. Kill-chain should include post-exploitation execution phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-login, monitor for suspicious process execution, unsigned DLL loads, or file writes to mobile/app-level storage that could indicate spyware installation. Look for behavioral patterns consistent with Pegasus sandbox evasion (timing checks, geofencing, network exfiltration to known C2).

suggestion.title: Meta/WhatsApp Security Block Response Telemetry
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Meta Blocks NSO Group's...Attack.' Meta's defensive action is evidence of detection; should ingest Meta's published threat feed and alert correlations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest Meta's official threat intelligence disclosures and YARA/IOC feeds published post-incident. Cross-reference any domains/IPs/file hashes Meta identified as NSO-linked against internal email gateway, proxy, and network logs for matching activity within 30-day retrospective window.

suggestion.title: NSO Contempt Citation Artifacts (Litigation/Attribution)
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'Files Contempt Order,' indicating legal action and formal attribution. Court filings often contain IOCs and technical forensics not in press release.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor court databases and Meta's legal/security disclosures for supporting documents (amicus briefs, affidavits) that may contain additional IOCs (email addresses, domains, registrant details) not disclosed in public statements. Correlate with passive DNS and WHOIS history for infrastructure attribution.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner: CVE-2026-10520 Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and states CISA KEV requires 'one quick check across your fleet — patch lag is the silent killer.' Zero scanner-based detection UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when vulnerability scanner detects CVE-2026-10520 on any Ivanti Sentry instance. Correlate scanner findings with inventory to identify unpatched appliances, prioritize externally-facing instances without mTLS protection.

suggestion.title: Network Exposure: Internet-Facing Ivanti Sentry Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' This exposure condition is the primary enabler but generated no network-based detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt inbound connections to Ivanti Sentry from untrusted/internet ranges. Alert on externally-reachable Sentry appliances without documented mTLS (EPMM) or restricted HTTPS controls. Baseline by environment.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation Against Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' The execution technique (T1059.x) is the core attack vector but is absent from generated MITRE mappings and detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry application logs and web traffic for command injection payloads (shell metacharacters: backticks, `$()`, `;`, `|`, `||`, `&&` in request parameters). Alert on exploitation attempts, correlate with external network exposure.

suggestion.title: RCE Impact: Unexpected Privilege Escalation from Sentry Service
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'root-level remote code execution.' No detection for post-exploitation process execution with elevated privileges from Sentry context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected process creation under Ivanti Sentry service account with root/SYSTEM privileges. Flag shell interpreters (bash, sh, cmd, powershell) spawned from Sentry daemons. Requires baseline per environment.

suggestion.title: Configuration State: Unmanaged Sentry Appliance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'unmanaged state' as the critical precondition for exploitation: 'can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state.' No detection for identifying or alerting on unmanaged Sentry instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query MDM/EMM logs to identify Sentry appliances marked unmanaged or lacking active management enrollment. Cross-reference with external exposure data. Alert if unmanaged instances are internet-facing.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Ivanti Sentry Externally Reachable
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'exploitable in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Network exposure is the prerequisite for exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Ivanti Sentry appliances (port 443/8443, Sentry-specific HTTP response headers or certificate CN) responding to probes from external/untrusted ASNs or public IPs. Correlate with asset inventory to flag unpatched or out-of-compliance instances.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scan Match: CVE-2026-10520
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry requires tracking this specific CVE identifier. Detect vulnerability scanner results (Nessus, Qualys, Rapid7) reporting CVE-2026-10520 on Ivanti Sentry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scan reports containing CVE-2026-10520 or Ivanti Sentry instances with missing patches post-2026-06-14 federal due date. Prioritize internet-facing or DMZ assets.

suggestion.title: RCE Detection: Unexpected Child Process Under Sentry Service
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Detect shell/command process spawning from Sentry daemon.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bash, sh, or cmd.exe processes created by Ivanti Sentry service accounts or daemons, especially in root context. Look for shell metacharacters (|, ;, &, `) in web request logs to Sentry APIs immediately preceding process creation.

suggestion.title: External Unauthenticated Access Attempt to Sentry Admin Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'remote unauthenticated user.' Detect external requests to Ivanti Sentry admin/management endpoints lacking valid credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints (admin paths, API URIs) from external IPs returning 200/500 responses without prior successful authentication. Look for request bodies containing shell injection patterns in parameter values.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation: Root Process from Unprivileged Parent
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability result is 'root-level remote code execution'—process runs at highest privilege from initial foothold. Detect escalation in process tree.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Ivanti Sentry processes running as root when spawned by lower-privilege service parent without explicit privilege escalation syscalls (setuid, sudo, pkexec). Baseline normal process hierarchy first.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged State Detection: Sentry Lost Management Enrollment
suggestion.rationale: Article notes vulnerability is exploitable 'in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state.' mTLS and restricted HTTPS (enabled in managed state) block exploitation. Detect loss of management connection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of enrolled Sentry appliances via EPMM or Neurons for MDM management plane. Alert when appliance transitions offline/unmanaged or certificate/mTLS validation fails. Correlate state change with increased external HTTP/HTTPS probe traffic to that appliance.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry: Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article states appliance must be 'externally reachable' to be exploitable; standard asset-exposure hunt template referenced in article body.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry instances (CVE-2026-10520) that are externally reachable to the internet or untrusted networks. Cross-reference vulnerability scanner results against asset inventory and network segmentation controls. Flag instances in unmanaged state.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry: OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution'. No exploitation detection provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry appliance logs for suspicious OS command execution, shell metacharacters in HTTP parameters, or unexpected child processes spawned from service accounts. Look for injection payloads in request logs (shell redirects, command chaining operators).

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry: Post-Exploitation Root Access
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'root-level remote code execution' as impact; no post-exploitation detection provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unexpected root-level process execution on Ivanti Sentry appliances, especially from network-facing service accounts. Monitor for privilege escalation attempts or unexpected system-level changes post-initial compromise.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry: Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'CVE-2026-10520 — match against your vulnerability scanner'. Pipeline should generate scanner-based detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Automated alert: any Ivanti Sentry appliance flagged as vulnerable to CVE-2026-10520 by enterprise vulnerability scanner. Cross-correlate with patch management system to identify unpatched instances and escalate based on exposure (external vs. internal).

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry: Management Interface Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible'; detection of unprotected management interface is critical for this CVE's exploitability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Ivanti Sentry management interfaces (HTTPS ports) reachable from external networks or untrusted zones. Correlate with configuration audit to identify appliances NOT protected by mTLS or restricted HTTPS policies.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Ivanti Sentry Internet-Accessible Appliances
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' External accessibility is the exploitation precondition and must be detected immediately.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory Ivanti Sentry appliances (product family match) and flag any with public IP exposure or open ports (8443/8444/443) reachable from untrusted CIDRs. Cross-reference against vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-10520 presence.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Exploitation Pattern: OS Command Injection in Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability' leading to RCE. HTTP/HTTPS requests containing shell metacharacters targeting Sentry API endpoints are the exploitation signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints for payloads containing shell syntax: backticks, $(), pipes, semicolons, or command separators in URL parameters or POST bodies. Flag as high-severity if request receives 200-level response.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unauthenticated API Access
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'remote unauthenticated user' can exploit. Detection must flag API calls succeeding without valid authentication tokens on normally-protected endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP 200/201 responses to Sentry management or API endpoints when Authorization header is missing, malformed, or expired. Correlate with downstream shell command execution (DeviceProcessEvents) to confirm exploitation.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation: Root-Level Process Execution on Sentry Appliance
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'root-level remote code execution' achievable. Any shell spawned by Sentry service account or root is post-exploitation signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For Sentry appliances flagged as vulnerable (CVE-2026-10520) or exposed, alert on process creation by Sentry service user or root executing /bin/sh, /bin/bash, python, or wget. Correlate with failed authentication attempts or HTTP exploit patterns preceding the execution.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Appliance Internet Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable' as exploitation prerequisite. Asset inventory hunt required.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query external IP space against asset inventory to identify Ivanti Sentry appliances (product strings: 'Sentry', 'MobileIron Sentry') on standard ports (443/8443). Cross-reference with vulnerability scanner data for CVE-2026-10520 unpatched status.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated OS Command Injection to Sentry Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'remote unauthenticated user' exploiting 'OS command injection' as the attack vector—requires detection of pre-auth RCE attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP(S) requests to Sentry endpoints lacking valid session tokens for command injection payloads (shell metacharacters: pipe, semicolon, ampersand, command substitution syntax). Flag requests to /api/*, /admin/*, or management interfaces that attempt code execution without authentication.

suggestion.title: Root-Privilege Process Execution from Sentry Service
suggestion.rationale: Article states exploitation 'achieve[s] root-level remote code execution'—post-compromise detection on vulnerable appliance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On Ivanti Sentry appliances, alert on processes spawned by the Sentry daemon with root/system UID 0, especially shell interpreters (bash, sh) or network utilities indicative of reverse shell. Correlate timing with suspicious HTTP logs.

suggestion.title: Sentry Configuration Without mTLS or Restricted HTTPS
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM' as protective controls—gap analysis required.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit Sentry appliances for mTLS enforcement (mutual certificate requirement) and HTTPS origin restrictions. Appliances without these controls are vulnerable to unauthenticated exploitation; flag for immediate network segmentation or emergency patching.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Patch Compliance Scan
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies federal remediation deadline 2026-06-14 and emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer'—vulnerability management hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner output for any Ivanti Sentry instance flagged for CVE-2026-10520. Cross-reference with patch management records; any unpatched instance post-due-date represents active risk. Federal agencies must remediate by deadline; recommend same urgency across all organizations given CISA KEV status.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure Hunt — Ivanti Sentry Externally Reachable
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability is exploitable when 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable' — prerequisite for initial access is network exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate Ivanti Sentry / MobileIron Sentry appliances via port scanning (HTTP/HTTPS signatures), certificate metadata, or DNS. Flag instances routable from untrusted networks. Cross-reference with patch inventory; unpatched instances + external access = exploitable.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload Detection — Sentry Web Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is 'OS command injection vulnerability' allowing 'remote unauthenticated user' exploitation — must detect injection attempts targeting Sentry interfaces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry appliance web endpoints for HTTP requests containing shell metacharacters (;, |, &&, ``, $()) in query parameters, POST bodies, or headers. Flag requests that result in process spawning or unexpected command output in responses.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability enables 'root-level remote code execution' — must detect elevated command execution following successful injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry appliance host for root-owned processes spawned from web service accounts or network-originating context (parents: httpd, java, tomcat, etc.). Detect unexpected shell child processes (/bin/bash, /bin/sh, /bin/zsh) launched with UID=0.

suggestion.title: Absence of mTLS/EPMM Protective Controls — Configuration Audit
suggestion.rationale: Article states mTLS with EPMM and restricted HTTPS through Neurons for MDM 'makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors' — gap indicates unmitigated exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit Ivanti Sentry appliances for mTLS enforcement (client certificate requirement) and EPMM/Neurons for MDM enrollment. Flag instances accepting plaintext HTTP, TLS-without-client-cert, or non-enrolled status as unprotected against this CVE.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution' — no detection logic generated despite explicit vulnerability details. Article also references template at ../_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure for asset-exposure hunt with CVE substitution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound HTTP/HTTPS traffic to known Ivanti Sentry appliances for malformed requests, OS command metacharacters (backticks, $(), pipes, semicolons) in request parameters, or exploitation signatures targeting the Sentry API. Focus on externally-reachable instances per article condition 'endpoints externally reachable.'

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Ivanti Sentry Admin Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'remote unauthenticated user' and 'unmanaged state' — requires detection of authentication bypass or direct unauthenticated admin access attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP 200 or 302 responses to Ivanti Sentry admin endpoints (e.g., /admin, /api/admin, /mdm/admin) from unauthenticated sessions. Baseline on legitimate traffic; spike detection on failed authentication attempts followed by successful access without credential submission.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Pattern — Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability' as the attack vector — detection must look for injection syntax in HTTP payloads targeting Sentry endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints containing OS command injection metacharacters: $(command), `command`, |, ||, &, &&, ;, newline sequences in URL-decoded query/POST parameters. Correlate with response codes indicating successful execution (200, 302) vs. blocked (403, 400).

suggestion.title: Network Exposure of Ivanti Sentry Appliances
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable' — asset-exposure hunt required to identify at-risk inventory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query external asset discovery tools (Shodan, Censys) and internal asset inventory for Ivanti Sentry product instances with public IP routes or DNS resolution. Correlate with vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-10520 status. Flag instances marked 'unmanaged' or without mTLS/EPMM protection as per mitigation factors.

suggestion.title: Root-Level RCE Privilege Escalation — Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability yields 'root-level remote code execution' — post-exploitation detection required to catch successful privilege escalation once command injection is achieved.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry appliance process logs and system audit logs for unexpected root-owned process spawning, particularly child processes of web server / application processes. Flag commands executed as root that originate from HTTP request handlers or API parsers.

suggestion.title: mTLS Bypass or HTTPS Restriction Circumvention
suggestion.rationale: Article notes mitigation: 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible' — detection should flag attempts to bypass these controls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP (unencrypted) traffic to Ivanti Sentry instances configured for HTTPS-only or mTLS. Monitor for certificate validation failures, self-signed certificate use, or protocol downgrades on Sentry communication channels. Alert on traffic from non-EPMM/Neurons-MDM enrolled clients to Sentry.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability is exploitable when 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Detection avoids the need to wait for exploitation signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate Ivanti Sentry instances (product identification via HTTP headers, certificate CN, or configuration management data). Flag those missing mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM. Cross-reference against internal network scans to identify externally reachable instances.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry RCE Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is in CISA KEV (actively exploited in the wild). Need exploitation signature detection: 'remote unauthenticated user' sending OS command injection payloads to exposed endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST/GET requests to known Ivanti Sentry vulnerable endpoints (e.g., /unauthenticated-api paths if identifiable) containing shell metacharacters (;, |, &&, backticks, $()) or command injection patterns. Flag requests from external sources to management/configuration interfaces.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Root-Level Command Execution Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability' enabling 'root-level remote code execution.' Need behavioral detection of injected commands executing in root context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution originating from Sentry processes (e.g., Java process if Sentry is Java-based) spawning child shells with privilege level = root or uid=0. Track command line arguments for typical post-exploitation patterns (curl, wget, nc, /bin/sh -i).

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Missing Protective Controls Configuration
suggestion.rationale: Article cites mitigations that prevent exploitation: 'mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM.' Hunt for systems NOT configured with these controls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query MDM/EPMM enrollment and configuration data for Sentry instances. Flag systems that lack mTLS certificate pinning or HTTPS access restrictions. Review Neurons for MDM policies applied to Sentry; alert on instances with permissive network policies.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Public Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Detection must identify and flag externally-accessible instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for Ivanti Sentry appliances on standard management ports (8443, 8080) accessible from untrusted networks. Correlate external exposure with EPMM enrollment status and mTLS configuration to identify unprotected, unmanaged instances.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payloads Against Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability described as 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user' to execute arbitrary commands. Detection must identify command metacharacter patterns in HTTP requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry management endpoints containing shell metacharacters (|, ;, `, $(), &&, ||, \n) in parameters or POST bodies. Focus on unauthenticated requests and correlate with failed authentication indicators.

suggestion.title: Sentry Service Root-Level Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exploitation achieves 'root-level remote code execution.' Post-exploitation detection must flag unexpected shell spawning at root privilege from Sentry service context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On Ivanti Sentry appliances, detect /bin/sh, /bin/bash, or non-standard binaries spawned at root privilege level from Sentry daemon or web service parent processes. Flag any root-level execution outside maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Missing mTLS Protection on Sentry Management Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'The use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors,' indicating unprotected instances lack this critical control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry instances accepting management HTTPS connections without mutual TLS client certificate validation. Flag instances where port 8443 accepts connections from external IPs without mTLS enforcement.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Matching
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV designation confirms active in-the-wild exploitation. Detection must correlate vulnerability scanner findings against inventory to identify exploitable systems requiring emergency patching by federal deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference vulnerability scanner results identifying CVE-2026-10520 in Ivanti Sentry products against network exposure data and management enrollment status. Escalate any unpatched, exposed instances as critical given 2026-06-14 federal remediation deadline.

suggestion.title: Phishing emails impersonating AI companies
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'AI brands as bait' and keywords list 'Credential theft' — core social-engineering vector the pipeline ignored. Article premise is threat actors luring users via fake AI vendor emails/links.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails impersonating OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, or other high-profile AI vendors, especially those with lookalike domains, embedded login links, or credential-submission landing pages. Correlate email sender domain reputation, SPF/DKIM failures, and destination landing pages.

suggestion.title: AiTM proxy credential interception
suggestion.rationale: Keywords explicitly mention 'Adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM)' — a proxy-interception technique for harvesting credentials that should be central to detection strategy. Pipeline missed entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag authentication events where user logs in from new/suspicious geography immediately before account reuse from attacker-controlled infrastructure. Cross-reference SSL certificate issuance on lookalike AI domains. Monitor for unusual auth failures followed by success from different IP after proxy interception window.

suggestion.title: Credential submission to phishing landing pages hosting AI assets
suggestion.rationale: Article is about social engineering via AI hype — users are being redirected to fake login pages. Pipeline should detect the infrastructure hosting these pages and account-takeover patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate clicks on phishing links with failed logins to legitimate AI vendor domains within 10 minutes, followed by successful auth from attacker IP. Look for bulk clicks on lookalike domains from the same org, suggesting mass phishing campaign.

suggestion.title: Domain registration for AI brand impersonation
suggestion.rationale: Article discusses threat actors using 'AI brands as bait' — infrastructure discovery step. Typosquatting, lookalike domain registration should appear in IOC extraction and domain-monitoring rules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries and HTTP requests to domains closely resembling OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Claude, ChatGPT, etc. (character substitution, lookalike registrars). Cross-ref with SSL certs issued to suspicious registrants. Alert on bulk domain registration by single actor within 7 days.

suggestion.title: Abnormal auth after reported phishing campaign targeting AI brands
suggestion.rationale: Microsoft article likely attributes campaign to specific threat actor — pipeline should surface actor name and tie auth-risk signals to their known campaigns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For users who clicked known-bad AI phishing links (from threat intel), flag any successful authentication or low-risk login overrides within 24h. Escalate if account is in critical or high-value group. If user reset password after phishing click, correlate password-change timing with external IP login attempts.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Asset Exposure — Internet-Reachable Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mandates 'standard asset-exposure hunt' and states vulnerability affects 'unmanaged state with endpoints externally reachable.' Pipeline generated zero asset-discovery UCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query firewall/proxy logs and network telemetry for successful inbound HTTP(S) connections to known Ivanti Sentry service ports from untrusted IP ranges. Cross-reference against managed-asset inventory to identify unmanaged or misplaced instances.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload Detection — Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'OS command injection vulnerability' allowing 'remote unauthenticated user' RCE. No exploitation-attempt UC generated despite explicit remote code execution vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints for command-injection metacharacters (pipe, semicolon, backticks, $(), command substitution syntax) in query/POST parameters, especially from sessions with no prior authentication.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution from Sentry Service
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploit yields 'root-level remote code execution.' Post-exploitation process-creation detection entirely absent from pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes spawned with SYSTEM/root privileges originating from Ivanti Sentry service accounts or installation directories. Correlate with failed HTTP requests to Sentry endpoints to detect exploitation success.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Misconfiguration — Unmanaged / Unprotected State
suggestion.rationale: Article notes vulnerability only exploitable when 'unmanaged state' without 'mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access.' Configuration-risk UC missing entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query MDM/endpoint-management systems for Ivanti Sentry instances flagged as unmanaged or with external HTTPS access enabled but mTLS disabled. Flag misconfigurations as high-risk exposure.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised Sentry Appliance
suggestion.rationale: Root RCE on MDM appliance (network-critical asset) enables horizontal movement to managed devices. Post-exploitation lateral-movement detection missing.
