suggestion.title: External HTTP Requests to Ivanti Sentry with OS Command Injection Payloads
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 'remote unauthenticated user' exploits via 'OS command injection' on externally reachable appliances. Pipeline generated zero use cases; this is foundational initial-access detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/HTTPS requests to Sentry default ports (8443, 443) from external sources containing OS command injection payloads: backticks, $(), semicolons, pipes, or command-chaining operators in parameter values. Establish baseline of legitimate management IPs and flag all other external origins.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Command Execution on Ivanti Sentry Hosts Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'root-level remote code execution' but pipeline missed execution detection. Critical for catching post-exploitation activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On Sentry appliances, detect OS-level shell spawning (sh, bash, dash) initiated from HTTP request handlers, web service parent processes, or unexpected contexts. Flag uid=0 command execution chains triggered by inbound network activity rather than local maintenance.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged or Externally Exposed Ivanti Sentry Appliances
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability only exploitable 'in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable'—asset exposure is the prerequisite.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Sentry appliances accessible from untrusted networks via port scans or passive DNS. Cross-reference against management configurations: flag instances lacking mTLS certificate chains, disabled EPMM integration, or absent Neurons for MDM IP restrictions as immediately exploitable.

suggestion.title: HTTP Tunneling Abuse via Ivanti Sentry Interfaces
suggestion.rationale: Title and source mention 'HTTP tunneling vulnerability' but pipeline generated zero detections for tunnel abuse despite it being a core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous HTTP CONNECT method requests or binary streaming patterns through Sentry appliance interfaces. Look for long-lived connections with absence of standard application-layer handshakes, high data volume, or patterns inconsistent with authenticated MDM management traffic.

suggestion.title: Externally Accessible Ivanti Sentry Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable'—core exposure condition enabling exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Ivanti Sentry instances resolvable from external networks (non-RFC1918 sources connecting to TCP ports used by Sentry appliances). Cross-reference with asset inventory to identify unpatched instances past federal due date (2026-06-14). High-confidence if mTLS/HTTPS restrictions are not enforced per vendor guidance.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempt (CVE-2026-10520)
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability mechanism is explicitly 'OS command injection'—exploitation requires attacker to inject shell metacharacters into vulnerable parameter.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry HTTP request logs for shell metacharacters (pipe, semicolon, backtick, $(), &&, ||) in request parameters known to be vulnerable to injection. Baseline normal administrative API calls and alert on deviation. Correlation with 401/403 response codes indicates pre-auth exploitation attempt.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Root-Level Process Execution Post-Sentry Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'root-level remote code execution' as impact—successful exploitation should result in privileged process spawning from Sentry appliance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On Sentry appliances, monitor for unexpected root-level process creation outside normal application lifecycle (e.g., bash, sh, curl spawned from Sentry daemon/Java process). Correlate timing with command injection exploitation indicators. High-confidence alert if processes execute shell commands to external IP addresses.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner Detection: CVE-2026-10520
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status mandates rapid asset discovery. CVE-2026-10520 is the canonical indicator for vulnerability scanning and patch-status validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Run vulnerability scanner with CVE-2026-10520 signature against all identified Ivanti Sentry instances. Prioritize any systems flagged as vulnerable. Cross-reference with patch-management data to confirm remediation status. Flag instances still vulnerable as of federal due date (2026-06-14) for immediate escalation.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged Sentry Instance Configuration Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article distinguishes safe configurations ('mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access') from vulnerable ones ('unmanaged state'). Configuration review is critical control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit all Sentry appliances for mTLS enforcement and HTTPS access restrictions per vendor hardening guidance. Identify instances in 'unmanaged state' (no mTLS, no IP whitelisting, no HTTPS restrictions). These are immediate targets for CVE-2026-10520 exploitation. Cross-correlate with network exposure scanning to identify which unmanaged instances are internet-facing.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states CISA KEV entries are 'currently being exploited' and recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt.' Pipeline generated zero use cases despite direct guidance in article body.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner data for matches on CVE-2026-10520 against Ivanti Sentry appliances. CISA KEV status confirms active in-the-wild exploitation; scanner confirmation is high-confidence indicator for immediate remediation.

suggestion.title: Externally Reachable Ivanti Sentry Appliance Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability is only exploitable 'where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' External network exposure is the prerequisite condition.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference asset inventory for Ivanti Sentry appliances against network reachability data (external IP assignment, inbound firewall rules, DNS resolution). Flag unprotected instances lacking mTLS (EPMM) or Neurons for MDM restrictions as critical exposure.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload Detection on Sentry Interfaces
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability is 'OS command injection.' Article describes exploitation against 'remote unauthenticated user,' implying malicious requests target exposed interfaces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound HTTP/HTTPS traffic to externally exposed Ivanti Sentry appliances for OS command-injection patterns: backtick substitution, $(command) syntax, semicolon-delimited chains, pipe operators, or shell metacharacters in request parameters or headers.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Root-Level Post-Exploitation Activity
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation grants 'root-level remote code execution.' Detection of post-compromise activity signals successful breach.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor appliance logs or underlying OS for unexpected privilege escalation to root, suspicious process execution under privileged context, unauthorized configuration changes, or reverse-shell network connections correlated with exploitation window.

suggestion.title: PAM Module File Integrity Violation
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'replaced legitimate pam_unix.so modules with backdoored versions that accept hardcoded passwords and harvest user credentials. Sygnia identified nine distinct variants of the malicious PAM module, each compiled in a separate build environment.' Detectable via FIM and hash deviation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor /lib64/security/ and /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/security/ for modifications to pam_unix.so. Alert on mismatches between file hash and known-good baseline; flag multiple distinct variants of PAM modules compiled from different environments. Cross-correlate with privilege-account logins using hardcoded passwords.

suggestion.title: OpenSSH Binary Replacement Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'replaced OpenSSH components such as ssh, sshd, and scp with trojanized versions that captured credentials, logged commands entered during SSH sessions.' Trojanized binaries are high-confidence detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: File integrity monitoring on /usr/bin/ssh*, /usr/bin/sshd, /usr/bin/scp. Verify binary signatures against package manager database; detect unsigned or re-signed versions. Log command-line argument anomalies in SSH processes; alert if sshd spawns credential-stealing subprocesses.

suggestion.title: SOCKS5 Proxy Process Masquerading as smbd
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'custom SOCKS5 proxy... turned compromised servers into internal pivot points... running as a daemon masquerading as smbd -D, using different filenames and ports on each host.' Detectable via process anomaly detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process named 'smbd -D' with unexpected parent process or launched from non-standard Samba paths. Monitor for listening sockets on unusual ports with process masquerading. Correlate multiple 'smbd' instances with varying parent processes and ports across the same host or network.

suggestion.title: Nginx Proxy Chain to Internal SSH via FastCGI
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'modified the configuration of a compromised internet-facing Nginx server to proxy... requests to a compromised backend server... to a FastCGI process (fcgiwrap) listening on a separate port... custom binary named uptime... established SSH connections to systems within the isolated network using parameters supplied in HTTP POST requests.' Highly detectable via Nginx config audit and unusual HTTP-to-SSH chains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit Nginx configuration for proxy rules redirecting to internal RFC1918 addresses or FastCGI backends. Alert on fcgiwrap executing binaries named 'uptime' or other suspicious names. Monitor Nginx POST request parameters that flow into SSH command execution; track child processes of FastCGI spawning SSH sessions.

suggestion.title: GS-Netcat Reverse Shell Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'deployed a modified GS-Netcat reverse shell disguised as a legitimate system component that connected to a hardcoded relay domain, providing encrypted remote shell access. The shell achieved persistence either via a malicious systemd service or through startup script modification.' Signature detectable via process behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for GS-Netcat process names or strings; hunt for reverse shell spawning legitimate system component names. Monitor for outbound connections on unusual ports to hardcoded domains from low-privilege processes. Correlate systemd service creation or startup script modification with reverse shell execution.

suggestion.title: Systemd Service and Startup Script Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions: 'achieved persistence either via a malicious systemd service or through startup script modification.' Standard persistence vector with filesystem signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor /etc/systemd/system/ and /etc/rc*.d/ directories for suspicious unit files or scripts. Alert on services executing binaries from non-standard paths or with embedded C&C references. Validate that service executables match package inventory; flag services whose ExecStart points to adversary-controlled binaries.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Unauthenticated Access Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states flaw 'Lets Attackers Run Code Without Authentication' — implies direct web/API access to vulnerable endpoint without credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to known Splunk Enterprise vulnerable endpoints (e.g., /api/*, /en-US/app/*) originating from external IPs with no corresponding authentication tokens or session cookies. Flag 401/403 followed immediately by successful request as suspicious.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Remote Code Execution Payload
suggestion.rationale: Title core claim: vulnerability 'Lets Attackers Run Code' — implies payload injection or command injection mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk process spawn logs and search command logs for unusual spawned child processes (bash, powershell, cmd.exe) originating from splunkd or search processes. Correlate with unauthenticated web access in same time window.

suggestion.title: Splunk Configuration Parameter Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: RCE vulnerabilities in Splunk historically target search parameters, eval functions, or custom script execution — would appear in search queries or config modifications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag search queries or saved searches containing dangerous eval() functions, custom commands, or untrusted macro evaluation. Alert on any search execution without corresponding user authentication context.

suggestion.title: Splunk REST API Abuse — Unauthenticated Data Access
suggestion.rationale: Unauthenticated access implies API endpoints accessible without tokens; likely vectors for credential theft or sensitive data exfiltration from search results.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor /services/search/jobs or /services/saved/searches endpoints for requests lacking Authorization header. Track volume and scope of data returned in response; alert if queries target sensitive indexes or return credential material.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Privilege Escalation via Unsecured Configuration
suggestion.rationale: Unauthenticated RCE often chains into privilege escalation within the Splunk process or host; critical for lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After detecting unauthenticated command execution, monitor for Splunk process spawning higher-privilege processes (SYSTEM, root). Watch for changes to Splunk configuration files (inputs.conf, outputs.conf) made outside of authenticated admin sessions.

suggestion.title: Splunk Data Exfiltration via Malicious Search Jobs
suggestion.rationale: Successful RCE in SIEM enables attacker to extract raw logs or modify alert routing — critical impact for lateral movement or cover-up.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for search jobs executed without authentication that query sensitive indexes, return unusually large result sets, or output to external systems (syslog, HTTP, cloud storage). Correlate with unexpected outbound connections from Splunk host.

suggestion.title: Kernel Exploit Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'One-Character Linux Kernel Flaw Enables Local Root Access' and 'Exploits Now Public' — attackers will execute exploit code against vulnerable kernel. Pipeline missed straightforward execution-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual process execution with kernel syscall patterns characteristic of LPE exploits (ptrace, ioctl, mmap with executable flags, or direct /dev/mem access). Correlate with processes spawning unexpected child processes running as root.

suggestion.title: Unprivileged Process Gaining Root Privileges
suggestion.rationale: Core impact described: 'Local Root Access' achieved via kernel flaw. Should detect privilege boundary violations — unprivileged user/process suddenly executing code as root.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when a process spawned by low-privilege user (UID > 1000) subsequently executes commands with effective UID 0 (root) without intermediate sudo/su calls with valid authentication.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Kernel Module or Driver Loading
suggestion.rationale: Kernel LPE exploits frequently load modules or interact with kernel drivers directly. Article confirms kernel-level attack but pipeline generated no detection for kernel code loading anomalies.
log_sources: Sysmon (11: FileCreate, 13: RegistryEvent for loadable kernel modules)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected insmod, modprobe, or direct /sys/module writes by non-root or build-tools. Flag kernel module loads outside scheduled maintenance windows or from /tmp, /home directories.

suggestion.title: Direct Kernel Memory Access Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Kernel exploits typically require reading/writing kernel memory. Detection gap: no use case for /dev/mem, /dev/kmem, or kptr_restrict bypasses despite article describing kernel-level vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any process opening /dev/mem or /dev/kmem for writing, or accessing /proc/kcore. Monitor for mmap() calls with RWX flags targeting high memory addresses where kernel space resides.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Go Module Typosquatting Upload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack mechanism: 'bad actors create and upload harmful software packages to online libraries using names very similar to popular ones.' Malicious github.com/botdb-go/bolt was near-identical to github.com/boltdb/bolt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Go Module Proxy for newly registered package names with high string similarity (Levenshtein distance <3) to established popular packages. Alert on version schemes diverging from upstream, e.g., 1.3.1 appearing as first version for a typosquat copy. Cross-reference against known typosquatting blocklists.

suggestion.title: Go Module Source/Hash Mismatch Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article exploited caching where 'Go Module Mirror's indefinite caching of modules kicked in, and that cached the backdored module.' Requires detecting when module names resolve inconsistently across repository sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: During build time, compare resolved module hashes and source repositories against authoritative Go Module Proxy and GitHub upstream. Flag when the same module identifier resolves to differing commit hashes or when cached versions diverge from upstream.

suggestion.title: Command-and-Control Communication from Go Applications
suggestion.rationale: Article states backdoor 'allows hackers to remotely control infected computers through a server that sends them commands i.e. via a command and control server.' Any process importing malicious BoltDB v1.3.1 would execute this callback.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline outbound network behavior for services known to use BoltDB or similar Go database packages. Alert on unexpected egress to non-standard ports, foreign IPs, or domains with C2 signatures. Monitor for encoded command channels in HTTP/DNS that deviate from application's normal communication patterns.

suggestion.title: Bulk Dependency Update to Compromised Package Version
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation occurred when 'we now wish to update our systems to the latest dependencies, which led developers to update the version that stayed in the system for 3 years.' Coordinated version-pinning campaigns can indicate supply chain weaponization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for synchronized dependency version updates across multiple projects to the same package:version combination, especially if version doesn't match upstream stable releases. Correlate timing against public supply-chain disclosures; versions released shortly before CVE disclosure warrant elevated scrutiny.

suggestion.title: Package Repository Name Collision with Legitimate Package
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: 'The malicious Go Module Mirror's was named github.com/botdb-go/bolt, similar to the original one i.e. github.com/boltdb/bolt.' Requires detecting near-duplicate package registrations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Implement package-name collision detection across Go registries: flag new package registrations with names within edit-distance 2 of established packages, differing only by single character, character transposition, or subdomain change. Correlate with known software supply chain attack patterns.

suggestion.title: Indefinite Module Cache Serving After Upstream Revocation
suggestion.rationale: Persistence mechanism: 'The Module was cached on Go Module Proxy, which continued to serve clients' even after GitHub removal. Detection requires identifying when cache layer violates upstream trust state.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare Go Module Proxy cache hit logs against upstream repository revocation/deletion records. Alert when applications request modules that have been delisted from authoritative sources but are still served from cache. Implement hash verification on all cached module returns.

suggestion.title: Detect externally-reachable Ivanti Sentry appliances
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable'—external exposure is the necessary condition for exploitation. This is the canonical asset-exposure hunt that should run once per quarter.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for listening ports on Ivanti Sentry appliances (default HTTPS 8443, 443) reachable from untrusted networks. Correlate with unpatched asset inventory filtered to CVE-2026-10520. Check whether mTLS or Neurons-for-MDM restrictions are configured in control-plane logs.

suggestion.title: Detect unauthenticated access attempts to Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution'—the attack requires no credentials, making unauthenticated session patterns a direct indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline Sentry authentication logs for failed login attempts, HTTP 401/403 responses, or API calls that bypass auth middleware. Alert on sequences of unauthenticated requests followed by successful command execution patterns in system logs.

suggestion.title: Monitor Ivanti Sentry for OS command injection payloads
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability'—payloads will contain shell metacharacters or command separators in HTTP parameters or request bodies targeting the vulnerable endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search Sentry HTTP/API logs for common OS command injection patterns (pipe, semicolon, backtick, $(…), &&, ||) in parameters historically associated with the vulnerable endpoint. Correlate with 5xx or crash responses indicating command execution attempts.

suggestion.title: Detect root-level process spawning from Ivanti Sentry service
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'root-level remote code execution'—successful exploitation results in processes spawned as root from the Sentry process tree. This is post-exploitation indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline the Sentry service process (java, python, or vendor-specific binary). Alert on unexpected child processes spawned with PPID=Sentry PID and execution context=root/SYSTEM, especially shell interpreters (bash, sh, cmd.exe, powershell).

suggestion.title: Audit Ivanti Sentry mTLS and EPMM/Neurons-for-MDM configuration
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible'—misconfigurations of these controls leave appliances exposed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Sentry configuration for mTLS cert pinning status, EPMM trust anchors, and Neurons-for-MDM HTTPS restriction flags. Alert if mTLS is disabled, EPMM certificate chain is broken, or MDM-restricted endpoints are accessible to non-MDM clients.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure - Ivanti Sentry Externally Accessible
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability exploitable 'in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' External reachability is the necessary condition enabling exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset databases and external exposure scanning systems (SHODAN, Censys) for Ivanti Sentry instances with public IPv4 addresses or inbound routes from untrusted networks. Baseline management interface ports (443, 8080, vendor-specific).

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload Detection - Ivanti Sentry Web Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'OS command injection vulnerability' accessible to 'remote unauthenticated user.' Attack surface is HTTP/HTTPS parameters to the management interface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to Ivanti Sentry endpoints (management dashboard, APIs) for payloads containing shell metacharacters: backticks, $(), command substitution, semicolons, pipes, &&, ||, newlines in parameter values.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged Ivanti Sentry Appliance Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes vulnerability conditional on appliance being 'in an unmanaged state.' Managed instances with mTLS/EPMM enrollment are protected; unmanaged instances are vulnerable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference Ivanti Sentry fleet against EMM/MDM management enrollment records. Identify instances not enrolled with EPMM, lacking mTLS configuration, or not subject to restricted HTTPS access controls.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Command Execution Post-Exploitation on Sentry Appliance
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies successful exploitation grants 'root-level remote code execution.' Anomalous privileged process spawning is a post-exploitation indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate root-owned processes on Ivanti Sentry appliances (system daemons, vendor services). Alert on unexpected root-owned child processes spawned from web server workers or unauthenticated application contexts.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry mTLS and Network Segmentation Baseline
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors.' Defensive verification that protective controls are active.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Verify Ivanti Sentry instances enforce client certificate validation (mTLS) or are restricted by IP/firewall policy. Alert on management interfaces without mutual TLS enabled or with overly-permissive HTTPS access rules.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Reachability Audit
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Requires asset discovery and network exposure mapping before exploitation occurs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Ivanti Sentry appliances (fingerprint via HTTP headers, SSL certificate CN, or known config endpoints) reachable from untrusted networks. Correlate exposed instances with vulnerability scanner—prioritize unmanaged appliances.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unauthenticated Admin Access Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Baseline legitimate auth patterns; alert on repeated unauthenticated API/console endpoint access from external sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry management interfaces for HTTP 401/403 responses or repeated auth failures from external IPs. Flag payload-bearing unauthenticated requests to /admin, /api, /console paths.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload Detection in Sentry Requests
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability is 'OS command injection.' Monitor for shell metacharacters (|, ;, &&, $(), backticks, >, <, newlines) in request parameters to Sentry management endpoints indicating injection attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints for command injection syntax: pipes, command substitution, redirection operators, encoded payloads. Flag high-entropy or suspicious parameter values in query strings or POST bodies.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Process Execution Under Sentry Service Context
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'achieve root-level remote code execution.' Successful RCE should spawn anomalous child processes (shells, reverse shells, network tools) under Sentry daemon or root privilege.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bash/sh/cmd/powershell spawned from Sentry service account or as root. Look for unexpected network tool execution (wget, curl, nc) or outbound connection establishment post-process-creation.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry mTLS & Restricted HTTPS Control Verification
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'The use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access...makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors.' Verify defensive mitigations are deployed on exposed instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for Ivanti Sentry instances; flag those WITHOUT mTLS configuration, client-certificate pinning, or IP whitelisting. Cross-reference externally routable appliances against security-control inventory.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Patch Compliance Timeline Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'Federal patch due: 2026-06-14.' Post-deadline unpatched instances are non-compliant. Track time-to-patch and flag stragglers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for CVE-2026-10520 matches on Ivanti Sentry assets. Generate patch-lag reports; flag instances unpatched >7 days post-deadline and escalate to asset owners.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability succeeds 'in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Requires network exposure inventory to identify at-risk instances before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate Ivanti Sentry instances from asset inventory and vulnerability scanners. Cross-reference with network exposure telemetry (external IPs, internet-facing ports). Flag instances reachable from untrusted networks without mTLS/EPMM or Neurons enrollment as immediate risk.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempt Against Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability' enabling 'remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Web/proxy logs must detect exploitation attempts against vulnerable endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints for shell metacharacters and command injection syntax (backticks, $(), $<>, semicolons, pipes, newlines) in parameters and POST bodies. High confidence if request originates from external IP to known-vulnerable Sentry version.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution from Ivanti Sentry Service
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation 'could allow' attacker to 'achieve root-level remote code execution.' Abnormal process spawning from Sentry service context with SYSTEM/UID-0 privileges indicates post-compromise activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation where parent process is Ivanti Sentry service (java.exe, sentry daemon, etc.) spawning shell, scripting engine, or known attack tools with elevated integrity. Baseline benign Sentry-spawned processes and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged Ivanti Sentry Inventory Gap
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability is mitigated by 'mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM.' Unmanaged instances (absent from management plane) cannot enforce these protections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference asset inventory for Ivanti Sentry instances against MDM enrollment database and mTLS certificate store for EPMM. Flag instances present in inventory but absent from management plane as 'unmanaged.' Prioritize by external exposure and days since last patch.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Ivanti Sentry Management Interfaces
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability requires 'remote unauthenticated user' access; article emphasizes this is only preventable through management controls (mTLS/Neurons). Unauthenticated successful connections to admin endpoints indicate exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry application logs for unauthenticated HTTP POST/GET requests to admin/API endpoints (typically /sentry/admin, /api/*). Baseline expected authentication flows. Flag unauthenticated parameter-manipulation attempts, particularly from external/untrusted source IPs.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Externally Reachable Ivanti Sentry Appliances
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' This is the prerequisite condition for exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry instances accessible from external (non-RFC1918) sources on typical management ports. Cross-reference with inventory to flag unmanaged deployments. Flag systems without mTLS or restricted HTTPS controls (mitigating factors per article).

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner Match: CVE-2026-10520 Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry requires rapid detection. Article identifies 'OS command injection vulnerability' allowing 'root-level remote code execution' with remote unauthenticated access. Federal patch deadline is 2026-06-14 (today).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan all Ivanti Sentry instances for CVE-2026-10520 using vendor patches or vulnerability scanner signatures. Prioritize unmanaged appliances and those with external reachability. Escalate any unpatched systems post-deadline.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation via Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability' as exploitation vector enabling RCE. This is the attack execution mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry process logs and system audit trails for suspicious shell command execution (sh, bash, cmd) spawned from Sentry service context. Look for injection payloads: shell metacharacters (|, ;, &, backticks) in request parameters or logs.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution from Sentry Context
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'root-level remote code execution' as impact. Post-compromise activity with elevated privileges from Sentry context is highly anomalous.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes spawned with root/SYSTEM privileges originating from Ivanti Sentry service or process tree. Alert on privilege escalation events, credential enumeration, or lateral movement from Sentry context.

suggestion.title: Network Segmentation Check: mTLS and HTTPS Restriction Controls
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability mitigated by 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors.' Absence of these controls indicates exploitable deployment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit all Ivanti Sentry deployments for presence of mTLS enforcement and HTTPS restrictions. Inventory appliances lacking these controls and correlate with external reachability assessment to identify exploitable instances.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Ivanti Sentry Unmanaged Instance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'vulnerability can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Pipeline missed the core condition for exploitability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Ivanti Sentry appliances accepting external connections without mTLS/Neurons for MDM protection. Monitor for reconnaissance targeting typical Sentry ports from external IP ranges. Correlate absence of expected EPMM enrollment signals.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Exploitation of Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution'—pipeline failed to detect auth bypass.

suggestion.title: Root-Privilege Process Spawning on Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Attack outcome: 'root-level remote code execution.' Post-exploitation, unexpected UID=0 processes spawned via HTTP handlers or Sentry service account are strong indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution with root/UID=0 context on Ivanti Sentry appliances, especially spawned by HTTP request handlers, Sentry daemons, or unprivileged service accounts. Baseline normal Sentry process behavior to reduce FP.

suggestion.title: mTLS/Restricted Access Control Bypass Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article describes mitigation: 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible.' Bypass attempts indicate attacker adaptation to controls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP→HTTPS protocol downgrade attempts, mTLS certificate mismatches, or port-hopping to reach Sentry on non-standard ports. Flag proxying/tunneling behavior that circumvents mTLS certificate pinning.

suggestion.title: Linux PAM Module Unauthorized Replacement or Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly details attackers replacing pam_unix.so with nine distinct backdoored variants: 'replaced legitimate pam_unix.so modules with backdoored versions that accept hardcoded passwords and harvest user credentials.' This is a critical persistence and credential-harvesting mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor /etc/pam.d/ directory and /lib/security/ for unauthorized file modifications and hash changes to pam_unix.so. Alert on PAM module replacement, unsigned variants, or config changes permitting hardcoded password acceptance. Correlate with logon and credential-harvest telemetry.

suggestion.title: Trojanized OpenSSH Binary Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Article describes replacement of ssh, sshd, scp with trojanized versions: 'replaced OpenSSH components such as ssh, sshd, and scp with trojanized versions that captured credentials, logged commands entered during SSH sessions, and stored the collected data locally for future retrieval.' Dual-purpose malware enabling persistence and credential exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SSH binary integrity via hash and signature verification. Alert on ssh/sshd/scp launched from unexpected paths, with unexpected parent processes, or with compilation timestamps inconsistent with OS baseline. Track SSH authentication anomalies and side-channel credential exfiltration.

suggestion.title: System Service Masquerading for Proxy/Tunneling
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The proxy ran as a daemon masquerading as 'smbd -D', using different filenames and ports on each host.' SOCKS5 proxy used for internal lateral movement while evading process-inspection controls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for processes claiming to be smbd or other service daemons with unexpected parent, binary path, or listening on non-standard ports. Alert on legitimate service names making outbound connections to internal networks or spawning child processes atypical for that service.

suggestion.title: Nginx Configuration Modification for Command Execution Relay
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'modified the configuration of a compromised internet-facing Nginx server to proxy specially crafted requests to a compromised backend server...forward requests to a FastCGI process (fcgiwrap) listening on a separate port. The FastCGI wrapper acted as an execution bridge, processing requests and launching a custom binary.' Converts web server into remote-execution bridge.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Nginx configuration files for unexpected proxy_pass directives pointing to internal FastCGI, localhost, or unusual ports. Alert on fcgiwrap process spawning or unexpected child execution. Track HTTP POST requests with SSH-like parameters. Correlate web server process spawning shell/SSH children.

suggestion.title: Systemd Service Creation for Reverse Shell Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'achieved persistence either via a malicious systemd service or through startup script modification.' Modified GS-Netcat reverse shell connected to hardcoded relay domain, maintaining persistence across password changes and session termination.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor /etc/systemd/system/ and /usr/lib/systemd/system/ for new or modified units. Alert on services spawning shell interpreters, reverse shells, or connecting to hardcoded external domains. Verify service legitimacy against package manifests and track enable/disable operations.

suggestion.title: HTTP POST Parameter-Driven SSH Tunnel to Isolated Network
suggestion.rationale: Article describes novel C2 mechanism: 'established SSH connections to systems within the isolated critical infrastructure network using parameters supplied in HTTP POST requests. By chaining these modifications, Velvet Ant established a remote-execution path into the segregated environment via simple HTTP requests.' Critical lateral movement into air-gapped networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect HTTP POST request bodies for SSH connection parameters (host, port, key, user). Alert on web server processes spawning SSH or establishing SSH outbound connections in response to HTTP requests. Track fcgiwrap or other FastCGI processes executing SSH or custom binaries. Correlate web server logs with network-egress SSH sessions.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Splunk Endpoint Access Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'Attackers Run Code Without Authentication'—core attack vector is bypassing auth to reach Splunk APIs. Pipeline missed the initial access detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk instances for HTTP requests to authenticated endpoints (e.g., /services/*, /api/*) from sources that do not have an active authenticated session. Track 401/403 followed by 200 responses in the same session, or direct 200s without prior auth handshake.

suggestion.title: Splunk Remote Code Execution via Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly mentions 'Run Code Without Authentication'—execution phase is the attack impact. No detection for this critical outcome.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected child processes spawned by splunkd.exe or splunk processes (e.g., cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash) without corresponding user login or scheduled task trigger. Monitor for process execution with parent=splunkd and grandparent not in expected whitelist.

suggestion.title: Abnormal Outbound Connections from Splunk Enterprise
suggestion.rationale: Successful RCE typically leads to C2 or data exfiltration. Pipeline missed post-exploitation behavior detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate outbound connections from splunkd and related processes. Flag connections to non-whitelisted external IPs, especially to known malicious infrastructure, or connections to unusual ports (reverse shells on 4444, 5555, 8888).

suggestion.title: Splunk Configuration or Knowledge Object Tampering
suggestion.rationale: RCE in Splunk could enable persistence through malicious configuration or searches. Article describes a flaw in 'Splunk Enterprise'—no detection for post-breach persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk audit logs for unexpected modifications to saved searches, dashboards, app configurations, or alert actions. Alert on creation of searches containing suspicious keywords (curl, wget, powershell, bash -i) or new scripted inputs from unauthenticated sources.

suggestion.title: CVE-Based Splunk Vulnerability Scanning Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article is about a critical Splunk flaw—no detection for reconnaissance or exploitation tools probing for the vulnerability. Attackers must discover Splunk instances first.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create signature-based detection for CVE-specific exploit payloads in HTTP requests to Splunk ports (8000, 8089). Monitor for characteristic URL patterns, malformed requests, or known PoC beacon traffic targeting Splunk endpoints.

suggestion.title: Privilege escalation via kernel flaw – root shell spawn
suggestion.rationale: Article headline: 'Enables Local Root Access' — privilege escalation from local unprivileged process to root is the core attack. No detection UC addresses privilege boundary crossing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unprivileged processes spawning child processes with euid=0 or elevated capabilities (CAP_SYS_MODULE, CAP_SYSADMIN). Detect UID/GID transitions without sudo/su/doas invocation. Alert on process parent is non-root but child runs as root.

suggestion.title: Suspicious kernel module operations post-exploit
suggestion.rationale: Kernel exploits commonly load malicious modules. Article does not detail post-exploitation behavior, but kernel-level persistence via module loading is high-signal indicator for this class of flaw.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor insmod/modprobe/rmmod execution from user-space processes, particularly if spawned by non-system accounts. Detect kernel module insertions that lack corresponding source in /lib/modules or are executed from /tmp, /var/tmp, or other attacker-writable locations.

suggestion.title: Abnormal syscall sequences indicating memory corruption
suggestion.rationale: One-character kernel vulnerabilities often rely on memory corruption. Article emphasizes 'one-character flaw' but pipeline did not generate detection for syscall anomalies that precede exploit success.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for syscall sequences involving mmap/mprotect/mremap followed by rapid ioctl or prctl calls with unusual arguments. Detect processes that cross memory boundaries or attempt to write to kernel address space (mmap with MAP_FIXED_NOREPLACE failures, bad return codes).

suggestion.title: Public exploit invocation – known-bad binary/payload patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Exploits Now Public' — pipeline should flag execution of known public PoC tools or malicious scripts associated with this CVE once identifiers are confirmed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Once CVE identifier is confirmed and exploit code is available, maintain hash/path indicators of public PoC binaries. Alert on execution of any matching binary or shell invocations that download/execute exploit payloads from known staging domains.

suggestion.title: Capability escalation – CAP_SYS_ADMIN or kernel-level capabilities
suggestion.rationale: Privilege escalation to root typically requires kernel capabilities. No detection rule addresses capability escalation, which is a natural side-effect of kernel exploits.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes gaining CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_SYS_MODULE, CAP_SYSLOG, or CAP_SYS_PTRACE without explicit setcap or privilege inheritance chain. Detect capability bounding set modifications (prctl PR_CAPBSET_DROP) that indicate post-exploit hardening evasion.

suggestion.title: Pre-exploitation enumeration – kernel version/config discovery
suggestion.rationale: Exploit success depends on target kernel version. Pipeline should flag processes enumerating /proc/version, uname -a, or kernel config files — common reconnaissance preceding kernel exploit execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unprivileged processes executing uname -r, cat /proc/version, or reading /boot/config-* and /proc/config.gz in rapid succession. Correlate with subsequent attempts to execute suspicious binaries or shell scripts — indicator of pre-exploit reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly establishes exposure condition: 'vulnerability can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Foundational detection is asset inventory mapped to exposure risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all Ivanti Sentry appliances in production. Cross-reference against firewall rules and proxy logs to confirm management interfaces (HTTPS, typically 443) are NOT accessible from untrusted networks. Flag appliances with public-facing DNS records or listening on external IP interfaces.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article prescribes 'CVE-2026-10520 — match against your vulnerability scanner' as the detection mechanism. CISA KEV entries require active vulnerability scanning as primary detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for CVE-2026-10520 findings. Prioritize unpatched and unknown-patch-status Ivanti Sentry instances. Correlate findings with asset exposure hunt to identify externally-reachable vulnerable appliances requiring emergency patching.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated HTTP Access to Sentry Management Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'remote unauthenticated user' can exploit, meaning the vulnerability does not require valid credentials. Detection should surface authentication-bypass or early-stage unauthenticated access to management endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP/HTTPS requests to Sentry management interfaces that lack valid session tokens, authentication headers, or pre-auth credentials. Flag requests to /admin, /sentry, /mdm, or /manage paths without authenticated context. Baseline expected authenticated request patterns first.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload in Sentry HTTP Parameters
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability root cause explicitly stated: 'OS command injection vulnerability.' Attackers inject shell metacharacters into application parameters. Detection should flag command-injection patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search Sentry ingress and application logs for shell metacharacters in HTTP request parameters: backticks, $(...), pipe, semicolon, &&, ||, newline-escape sequences. Prioritize requests from untrusted networks hitting Sentry before authentication boundary.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Root-Level Process Execution on Sentry Appliance Post-Access
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies outcome as 'root-level remote code execution.' Post-exploitation detection should surface unexpected process spawning as root on the Sentry host.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry process execution logs for unexpected child processes spawned from Sentry management services (e.g., Java application container, nginx, tomcat) running as root. Flag any deviation from baseline expected processes. Correlate process spawn with unauthenticated HTTP access from same source within 1-10 second window.

suggestion.title: Network Segmentation Validation: Sentry Management Interface mTLS and MDM Integration
suggestion.rationale: Article states protective controls: 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors.' Inverse: absence of mTLS or MDM integration indicates severe risk. Detection should validate protection is active.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Verify each Ivanti Sentry appliance enforces mTLS client-certificate validation and is integrated with EPMM or Neurons for MDM. Alert on Sentry instances with: mTLS disabled, TLS certificate pinning absent, MDM/EPMM integration unconfigured, or HTTPS ingress accessible without client-certificate requirement.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry - Asset Exposure Scope
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable' — this is the foundational precondition enabling exploitation. Pipeline must establish scope before hunting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry / MobileIron Sentry appliances running vulnerable versions (pre-patch) that are internet-routable (WAN-facing, non-RFC1918). Cross-reference with MDM status to surface unmanaged instances lacking mTLS/EPMM proxy protection.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry - OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly specifies 'OS command injection vulnerability' as the attack vector. Pipeline must detect injection payloads in HTTP requests to vulnerable endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests (GET/POST/PUT) to Sentry endpoints for shell metacharacters and command separators (;, |, &, backticks, $() syntax) in query parameters or POST bodies. Alert on command-injection payloads (id, whoami, cat, chmod, curl) especially from unauthenticated sources. Baseline: expect no such patterns against these endpoints.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry - Root-Level RCE Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes impact as 'root-level remote code execution' — post-injection, attackers execute commands with root privilege. Must detect RCE execution signals.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On Sentry appliances, detect shell interpreter spawning (bash, sh, python, perl) from web service processes or Sentry application processes with root UID. Flag unusual child processes, commands from /tmp, and post-compromise discovery patterns (whoami, ifconfig, netstat, ps aux).

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry - Suspicious Outbound Traffic from Appliance
suggestion.rationale: Full appliance RCE implies C2 establishment or data exfiltration. Article's 'root-level' access enables unrestricted network access from the compromised host.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound traffic from Sentry appliance IPs for anomalies: unexpected connections to external IPs, non-standard ports, suspicious DNS queries, beaconing patterns. Establish baseline of expected Sentry egress (vendor updates, MDM heartbeats) and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry - Weak mTLS / Unencrypted Access Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article notes mitigation: 'mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible' — detection should flag absence of these controls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Sentry instances without mTLS enforcement: plaintext HTTP on Sentry ports, TLS missing client-certificate validation, HTTP served on standard ports, external (non-proxy) direct connections from untrusted networks. Flag appliances not routed through Neurons/EPMM intermediary.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry - Persistence and Lateral Movement Post-RCE
suggestion.rationale: Root-level RCE enables persistence mechanisms (cron, SSH keys, user creation) and lateral movement into trusted networks. Article's uncontained compromise implies network-wide risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor compromised Sentry appliance for persistence: cron job creation, SSH authorized_keys modification, new user account creation, sudoers edits. Detect lateral movement: SSH connection attempts to internal hosts, SMB reconnaissance, password dumping from Sentry, network scanning from appliance IP range.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Network Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'endpoints externally reachable' is the prerequisite for exploitation. Pipeline missed the foundational asset-exposure hunt identifying Internet-facing Sentry appliances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances with external network reachability via asset inventory, public IP scans, or exposure scanning. Cross-reference against internal asset database to flag unexpected externally-reachable management interfaces.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Request to Ivanti Sentry Management Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'remote unauthenticated user' can exploit; pipeline missed detection for unauthenticated access attempts against Sentry endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry access logs for requests lacking valid authentication tokens or session identifiers. Alert on unauthenticated access to management endpoints, especially from external IP sources.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Pattern Execution on Sentry Appliance
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability' as the exploitation mechanism; pipeline missed detection for injection patterns in application or system logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search Ivanti Sentry logs for command injection patterns: backticks, $() substitution, pipe chains, semicolons, or shell metacharacters in request parameters. Alert on unexpected process spawning or shell invocations from Sentry processes.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520 Patch Compliance Audit
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Federal patch due: 2026-06-14' and warns 'patch lag is the silent killer'; pipeline missed vulnerability scan and patch-status detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner data for Ivanti Sentry instances not patched for CVE-2026-10520. Correlate patch dates against federal compliance due date (2026-06-14). Identify instances where patching status is unknown or conflicting between scanner and asset database.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Command Execution Post-Exploitation on Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could allow...root-level remote code execution'; pipeline missed post-exploitation detection for privilege escalation and RCE indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation or command execution events running under root context on Ivanti Sentry appliances, especially from external network sources. Monitor for unexpected privileged process spawning or system modification attempts.

suggestion.title: mTLS Bypass or Restricted HTTPS Access Circumvention Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access' as mitigations; pipeline missed detection for attempts to circumvent these controls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for TLS/SSL errors, certificate validation failures, or HTTP access attempts to endpoints that should enforce mTLS. Detect attempts to connect via non-HTTPS channels or without required client certificates.

suggestion.title: External Ivanti Sentry Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes vulnerability requires 'endpoints externally reachable'—necessary precondition for exploitation. Pipeline missed asset discovery detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances accessible from external networks. Query asset inventory for product=Ivanti Sentry and cross-reference with network segmentation policy. Prioritize unmanaged instances.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'OS command injection vulnerability' as the attack vector but pipeline generated no execution detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect shell metacharacters (pipe, semicolon, backtick), command substitution syntax ($(), $()), and operator chains in HTTP payloads targeting Ivanti Sentry. Flag obfuscated variants targeting known vulnerable endpoints.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Root Process from Ivanti Sentry Daemon
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability achieves 'root-level remote code execution' but pipeline missed post-exploitation process detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes spawned with root/SYSTEM privileges originating from Ivanti Sentry daemon processes. Baseline normal behavior and alert on unexpected children.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Assessment Alert
suggestion.rationale: Explicit CVE with federal remediation deadline (2026-06-14) should trigger scanner-result monitoring and patch-status validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-10520. Cross-reference with patch management to identify unpatched Ivanti Sentry instances. Escalate systems past federal due date.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Sentry appliance... with endpoints externally reachable' is the exploitation prerequisite. Detection must identify Sentry instances accessible from internet.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for externally reachable Ivanti Sentry appliances via DNS, certificate enumeration, or HTTP fingerprinting (Sentry default ports, response headers). Flag any exposed instance as critical regardless of patch status, given active wild exploitation.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload Detection — Ivanti Sentry Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability described as 'OS command injection' enabling RCE. Detection should identify inbound requests with shell metacharacters targeting Sentry interfaces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound HTTP(S) traffic to known Sentry endpoint patterns for payloads containing shell metacharacters (|, &, ;, $(), `, >, <) or command sequences. High fidelity in pre-patch environments.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Root-Privileged Process Spawning from Sentry Daemon
suggestion.rationale: Article confirms 'root-level remote code execution' is achievable post-exploitation. Processes spawned by Sentry service would inherit root context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes spawned by Sentry service (or descendants) running as root/SYSTEM, particularly unexpected command shells (/bin/sh, bash, cmd.exe, powershell) or network utilities (curl, wget, nc). Baseline legitimate Sentry behavior first, but new interpreter spawning is anomalous.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unmanaged State + External Reachability Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability exploitable only when 'in an unmanaged state with endpoints externally reachable.' Detection must correlate both conditions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference Sentry instances against management enrollment (EPMM/Neurons MDM status) and external accessibility logs. Alert any instance that is (1) not managed via mTLS/EPMM AND (2) externally reachable as critical exposure.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Ivanti Sentry Version Inventory Check
suggestion.rationale: Article references CVE-2026-10520 with federal due date 2026-06-14 (today). Detection must identify vulnerable Sentry versions in fleet.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for Ivanti Sentry instances. Identify versions matching vulnerable ranges for CVE-2026-10520 and alert with urgent priority given CISA KEV status and active exploitation.

suggestion.title: Defensive Control Validation — Sentry mTLS and Access Restrictions
suggestion.rationale: Article states mitigation: 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible.' Detection validates defensive posture.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit Sentry appliance configurations to confirm mTLS is enforced and EPMM/Neurons integration is active. Alert if mTLS is disabled, HTTPS is permissive, or endpoints allow unauthenticated access. Preventive control validation rather than attack detection.

suggestion.title: External Asset Exposure: Unmanaged Ivanti Sentry Appliances
suggestion.rationale: Article states appliances with 'endpoints externally reachable' are vulnerable. Asset exposure is the precondition for exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances exposed to the Internet on standard ports (443, 8443, or vendor-specific). Correlate external reachability with 'unmanaged state' indicators (lack of mTLS enrollment, no EPMM integration). Splunk: search for Sentry version/banner grabs from untrusted subnets.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation: Sentry Endpoint Attacks
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'OS command injection vulnerability.' Attackers will send payloads containing shell metacharacters (|, &&, ;, $(), etc.) to vulnerable endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints for command injection signatures: backticks, $(), semicolons, pipe characters, and common shell commands (bash, sh, nc, curl) in query strings or POST bodies. WAF/IDS rules for CVE-2026-10520 should trigger on payloads like `id`, `whoami`, command chaining.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution from Sentry Service Account
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'root-level remote code execution.' Successful exploitation will spawn processes running as root from the Sentry service account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes spawned by the Ivanti Sentry service account (typically `sentry`, `mobile`, or similar) that execute with UID=0 (root). High-fidelity indicators: child processes of Sentry daemons running unexpected shells, system utilities (bash, sh, nc, curl, wget), or reverse shells.

suggestion.title: Sentry Appliance Configuration: Unmanaged State Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article notes vulnerability occurs 'in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state.' Detection of unmanaged appliances reduces risk exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query CMDB/asset inventory for Ivanti Sentry appliances lacking mTLS enrollment with EPMM, or running without Neurons for MDM integration. Cross-check against network exposure reports; unmanaged + externally-reachable appliances are critical risk.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scan Positive on Exposed Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article maps to CVE-2026-10520. Vulnerability scanning is the first detection layer before exploitation occurs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scanner results flagging CVE-2026-10520 against any Ivanti Sentry instance. Critical severity + KEV status = immediate remediation requirement regardless of patch state (verify actual patch application in endpoint details).

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised Sentry to Network
suggestion.rationale: Root-level RCE on network appliance enables lateral movement. Article notes restricted access mitigates but doesn't eliminate exploitation post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-exploitation, monitor for network reconnaissance from the compromised Sentry appliance: port scans, DNS queries to internal hosts, SSH/RDP connection attempts to internal assets, or data exfiltration over non-standard ports.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Externally Reachable Ivanti Sentry Appliances
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable' as attack prerequisite. Article itself recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in templates.' This is the canonical KEV response.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory Ivanti Sentry appliances accessible from untrusted networks. Correlate with vulnerability scanner data for CVE-2026-10520 unpatched status. Flag instances without mTLS with EPMM or HTTPS-restricted access through Neurons for MDM.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Exploitation: OS Command Injection in HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'OS command injection vulnerability' as attack vector. Requires detection of injected shell syntax or encoded payloads in HTTP requests to vulnerable Sentry endpoints from unauthenticated sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to Ivanti Sentry endpoints for command injection signatures: shell metacharacters ($(, backticks, |, ;, &), command substitution, environment variable expansion, encoded payloads. Alert on unauthenticated request sources.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Root-Level Process Execution on Sentry Appliances
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Requires detection of root-context process spawning without prior authentication event—a privilege-escalation anomaly.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On Ivanti Sentry appliances, detect root-context command execution (bash, sh, /bin/sh, curl, wget, nc) spawned from web-service worker accounts or without corresponding authentication audit trail. Alert on any privilege-escalation path from unauthenticated to UID 0.

suggestion.title: Missing mTLS / HTTPS Protective Controls on Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article states mitigation requirement: 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors.' Configuration audit is prerequisite for risk quantification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Verify Ivanti Sentry instances enforce TLS 1.2+, valid mTLS certificates, and reject plaintext HTTP. Alert on cleartext traffic on Sentry ports (443, 8080), failed certificate validations, or non-approved internal IPs bypassing HTTPS.

suggestion.title: Patch Compliance: Unpatched CVE-2026-10520 Past Federal Due Date
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies federal patch due date of 2026-06-14 (today). CISA KEV entries demand immediate patch compliance verification; unpatched instances are active exploitation targets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vuln scanner for any Ivanti Sentry instance with CVE-2026-10520 status 'vulnerable,' 'unpatched,' or missing patch-date record post-2026-06-14. Escalate unmanaged instances and those with external routing.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scanner Match — Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry mandates scanner coverage. Article states federal due date 2026-06-14; detecting unpatched instances against this CVE is mandatory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner output for Ivanti Sentry instances positive on CVE-2026-10520. Correlate against patch-compliance logs to identify unpatched production appliances post-deadline.

suggestion.title: Externally Reachable Ivanti Sentry Management Interfaces
suggestion.rationale: Article states exploitation succeeds 'where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable'—external exposure is the precondition.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory Ivanti Sentry appliances and verify management ports are not routable from internet-origin networks. Flag inbound internet traffic to standard Sentry management ports as misconfiguration enabling exploit surface.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Sentry HTTPS Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'remote unauthenticated user' exploitation path. Access prior to valid session is anomalous for a management appliance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry access logs for HTTP 200/302 responses without preceding valid authentication. Pattern-hunt for unauthenticated enumeration (repeated 401 followed by successful requests).

suggestion.title: Shell Metacharacters in Sentry HTTP Request Payloads
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability.' Exploitation requires shell syntax (`;`, `|`, `$()`, backticks, `&&`) in request parameters or body.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints containing shell metacharacters (`;`, `$(`, backtick, `||`, `&&`) in URI-decoded query strings, POST bodies, or headers. Payload-agnostic approach catches command-injection attempts.

suggestion.title: Root Process Spawning from Ivanti Sentry Service
