suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'remote unauthenticated user' as attack vector. Pipeline missed UC to detect requests lacking valid authentication tokens to vulnerable interfaces—the necessary precondition for exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry management endpoints for HTTP/HTTPS requests without valid authentication credentials (missing auth headers, invalid tokens, no mTLS client cert). Baseline expected authenticated request volume; spike or unauthenticated 200-responses indicate attack attempt.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'OS command injection vulnerability' as exploitation mechanism. Pipeline did not generate UC for detecting shell metacharacters, command separators, or injection operators in requests to vulnerable endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect HTTP request bodies and query parameters sent to Ivanti Sentry for command-injection patterns: shell metacharacters (|, &, ;, $(), backticks), path traversal (../, ..\ ), and binary operators (>, <). Correlate suspicious payloads with response codes (success vs. error) to infer exploitation success.

suggestion.title: Root-Privilege Process Execution on Sentry Appliance
suggestion.rationale: Article guarantees outcome: 'root-level remote code execution.' Pipeline missed UC to detect post-exploitation process spawning with root UID (uid=0) on Sentry systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry appliances for unexpected process spawning with root UID (0), particularly children of web server or Sentry management service PIDs. Baseline normal root processes; alert on execution of shells (/bin/sh, /bin/bash), download utilities (curl, wget), or reverse-shell indicators.

suggestion.title: Sentry mTLS and HTTPS Enforcement Verification
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies controls: 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors.' No UC generated to verify these mitigations are present or detect their absence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Verify Ivanti Sentry management ports enforce mutual TLS (client certificate required) and reject plaintext HTTP. Alert on: cleartext traffic to management endpoints, TLS handshakes without client cert validation, or weak cipher suites. Missing mTLS leaves interfaces exploitable.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged Sentry Appliance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exploitation precondition: 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state.' Pipeline missed UC to identify appliances outside management domain or lacking management-plane connectivity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Ivanti Sentry instances from network inventory against MDM/management enrollment state. Flag appliances present in network scans but absent from management console. Unmanaged + externally routable + CVE-2026-10520 vulnerable version = critical exploitation risk.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email with Suspicious Link Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'AI Phishing'—core T1566.002 attack. Pipeline completely missed phishing-as-initial-access reconstruction. Should detect emails containing malicious or newly-registered domains before user interaction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Email gateway rules flagging messages with URLs on newly-registered domains, high-entropy subdomains, typosquatted hostnames, or mismatches in DMARC/SPF/DKIM. AI-generated phishing often shows unusual domain registration patterns (bulk registration, aged <30 days).

suggestion.title: Anomalous Email Volume from External Senders
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes campaigns 'crushing SOCs with alert volume'—implies bulk phishing. Pipeline missed statistical anomaly detection for mass-targeting campaigns. No detection for baseline-violation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of emails per sender/domain. Alert on >10x increase in single-domain volume, identical message bodies sent to >50 internal recipients, or botnet-like headers (multiple From addresses, generic templates).

suggestion.title: User Click-Through on Flagged Phishing Links
suggestion.rationale: Article's thesis is phishing 'crushing' SOCs—implies attacker success, meaning clicks occur. Pipeline missed credential-access validation: T1566.002 → user click → credential harvest. Should correlate gateway blocks with proxy logs for click-through indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference email gateway alerts (blocked/suspicious URLs) with proxy access logs. Detect users accessing URLs within minutes of receiving flagged emails. Spike in user clicks on URLs from phishing senders is high-confidence compromise signal.

suggestion.title: AI-Generated Text Patterns in Email Body
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly 'AI Phishing'—generative model artifacts are detectable (perfect grammar in social engineering, hallucinated company details, repetitive phrasing). Pipeline missed content-level analysis for T1566.001.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan email body for LLM signatures: perfectionist grammar paired with urgent tone, non-existent internal department names, phone numbers with wrong format for claimed company. Combine with sender reputation to flag AI-generated phishing with >80% confidence.

suggestion.title: Domain Reputation Decline for Spoofed Senders
suggestion.rationale: AI phishing campaigns often register look-alike domains or compromise legitimate sender infrastructure. Article's mention of volume suggests domain-based spoofing/typosquatting. Pipeline missed domain-reputation and DNS anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for newly-registered domains within edit-distance of legitimate partners/suppliers. Track DMARC/SPF fail rates per sender domain. Flag emails from domains with <30-day age, high entropy subdomains, or bulk registrations in same registrar.

suggestion.title: Alert Fatigue Signal: High False-Positive Rate in Email Gateway
suggestion.rationale: Article's core claim: phishing volume 'crushing' SOCs, implying alert overload and Tier 1 fatigue. Pipeline missed meta-detection: measure email gateway false-positive rate as leading indicator of successful phishing campaign. No alert-tuning use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track email gateway alert-to-quarantine ratio daily. Spike in volume of blocked emails without corresponding increase in confirmed threats indicates either tuning drift or attacker-induced false-positive spam. When Tier 1 alert volume >500/day, investigate gateway for misconfiguration or active phishing campaign.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Externally Exposed Appliance Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable' as exploitation prerequisite. Pipeline generated zero asset-exposure detection despite the template reference and clear network boundary violation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference Ivanti Sentry appliances (identified by product/version in asset inventory or network scanning) against MDM enrollment records (EPMM or Neurons for MDM). Flag unmanaged instances; correlate with external-facing interface logs to identify appliances reachable from untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection in Ivanti Sentry Requests
suggestion.rationale: Core exploitation vector: 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' No detection for command metacharacters, shell escapes, or backticks in Sentry request payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry web application logs and reverse-proxy/WAF logs for command injection signatures: shell metacharacters (`;`, `|`, `&`, `$()`, backticks), path traversal (`../`), OS command keywords in HTTP parameters targeting known vulnerable endpoints.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution from Sentry Service
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation achieves 'root-level remote code execution'—direct post-compromise execution indicator. Pipeline failed to surface detection for privilege escalation or root process spawning from Sentry service context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation events where parent is Ivanti Sentry service process and child runs as UID 0 (root) or SYSTEM. Flag execution of system utilities (sh, bash, curl, nc, python, perl) spawned from Sentry-owned process.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unauthenticated Access Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Attack requires 'remote unauthenticated user' access. Pipeline missed detection for authentication bypass or missing auth enforcement on Sentry endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry application logs for HTTP requests to known-vulnerable endpoints originating without valid session tokens, mTLS certificates, or pre-authentication. Flag pattern: POST/GET to Sentry admin/API endpoints + HTTP 200/RCE indicators without prior auth event.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'OS command injection vulnerability' allowing 'remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution'—this is the primary exploitation vector requiring detection on malicious payloads in HTTP traffic to exposed endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints for payloads containing shell metacharacters, command substitution syntax, or known OS command injection patterns. Correlate with failed authentication attempts to detect unauthenticated exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Externally Exposed Ivanti Sentry Appliance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly stipulates 'endpoints externally reachable' and 'unmanaged state' as exploitation prerequisite—asset discovery and exposure is the critical precursor enabling this RCE vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Ivanti Sentry or MobileIron Sentry product signatures on internet-facing IP addresses via port scanning or banner analysis. Prioritize systems lacking mTLS or restricted HTTPS per article's mitigation discussion.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Ivanti Sentry Admin Interface Access
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'remote unauthenticated user' exploitation—successful authentication bypass is the attack enabler and should be detected pre-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry administrative endpoints lacking prior authentication (no session token or established mTLS) originating from external IP ranges.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution on Ivanti Sentry Host
suggestion.rationale: Article outcome is explicitly 'root-level remote code execution'—post-exploitation detection of elevated privilege process spawning from compromised Sentry instance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry systems for process spawning with root (UID=0) privileges from Sentry application processes. Flag unexpected shell interpreters or scripting engines spawned with elevated privilege.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scanner Alert
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry indicates active exploitation; article mandates federal remediation by 2026-06-14. Vulnerability scanner detection is the earliest detection opportunity and aligns with article's recommended 'Standard asset-exposure hunt'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create alert when vulnerability scanner identifies CVE-2026-10520 on Ivanti Sentry instances. Cross-reference against patch inventory and escalate unpatched systems as critical given active exploitation.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability affects appliances 'with its endpoints externally reachable' and recommends 'standard asset-exposure hunt.' No UC generated despite explicit guidance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query for inbound HTTP/HTTPS traffic to known Ivanti Sentry ports (typically 8443, 9090) from untrusted networks. Cross-reference against asset inventory to identify which instances lack mTLS or restricted HTTPS access per 'Neurons for MDM' controls.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unmanaged State Configuration Audit
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'vulnerability can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state.' Pipeline did not generate configuration compliance UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit Sentry management state and enrollment status. Flag appliances not enrolled in EPMM or lacking mTLS enforcement. Query asset database for Sentry instances without 'Neurons for MDM' integration or with unrestricted HTTPS.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry OS Command Injection Exploitation (Post-Compromise)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'root-level remote code execution' via command injection. If Sentry logs capture pre/post-authentication activity, detection for suspicious command sequences should be modeled.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry appliance logs for unauthenticated HTTP requests containing shell metacharacters (|, ;, $(), backticks) in request parameters. Alert on successful execution indicated by outbound command activity or root process spawning if visibility exists.

suggestion.title: Malicious PAM Module Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers 'replaced legitimate pam_unix.so modules with backdoored versions' identifying 'nine distinct variants' compiled in separate environments. PAM modules are critical authentication components whose replacement enables universal credential harvesting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor /lib64/security/pam_unix.so and /lib/security/pam_unix.so for unexpected modifications via file integrity monitoring. Alert on hash mismatches, timestamp anomalies, or binary replacements from pam module directories. Detect recompiled PAM modules by tracking file creation in /lib*/security/ outside of package manager activity.

suggestion.title: Trojanized OpenSSH Executable Replacement
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'replaced OpenSSH components such as ssh, sshd, and scp with trojanized versions that captured credentials, logged commands entered during SSH sessions'. Each SSH session becomes a surveillance point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor /usr/bin/ssh, /usr/sbin/sshd, /usr/bin/scp for file hash mismatches or unexpected modifications. Alert on sshd/ssh binary rewrites outside of package management. Track unexpected spawning of OpenSSH binaries with non-standard arguments or from unusual process parents.

suggestion.title: Nginx FastCGI Air-Gap Bridge Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attackers 'modified the configuration of a compromised internet-facing Nginx server to proxy specially crafted requests' through 'FastCGI wrapper acted as an execution bridge, processing requests and launching a custom binary named uptime' that 'established SSH connections to systems within the isolated critical infrastructure network'. This is the air-gapped network bridge.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Nginx configuration files (/etc/nginx/nginx.conf, /etc/nginx/sites-*/) for unexpected fastcgi_pass directives or upstream definitions. Alert on HTTP requests forwarded to local FastCGI sockets with binary payloads or SSH-like parameters. Detect child processes spawned by fcgiwrap (especially ssh/scp) via process monitoring.

suggestion.title: SOCKS5 Proxy Daemon Masquerading
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'installed a custom SOCKS5 proxy' running 'as a daemon masquerading as 'smbd -D,' using different filenames and ports on each host' enabling access to non-directly-accessible internal systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SOCKS5 listening ports via unexpected high-numbered port listeners from non-standard processes. Alert on process execution showing 'smbd' masquerading with suspicious command lines or file paths. Monitor for multiple instances of daemons with varied names and ports on the same host, unusual for legitimate services.

suggestion.title: Malicious Systemd Service for Reverse Shell Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'achieved persistence either via a malicious systemd service or through startup script modification' maintaining the 'modified GS-Netcat reverse shell disguised as a legitimate system component' across reboots and session terminations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor /etc/systemd/system/ and /lib/systemd/system/ for unexpected new .service files or modifications to existing services. Alert on services with ExecStart directives containing shell commands, reverse shells, or network callbacks. Correlate service enablement with subsequent outbound network connections to hardcoded relay domains.

suggestion.title: Hardcoded Credential Embedded in Authentication Flow
suggestion.rationale: Article reveals backdoored PAM modules 'accept hardcoded passwords' and the FastCGI execution bridge 'established SSH connections to systems within the isolated critical infrastructure network using parameters supplied in HTTP POST requests'—indicating embedded or exfiltrated credentials in malicious binaries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor authentication logs for repeated SSH connections with identical usernames/passwords from the same source (hardcoded credentials vs. interactive login). Alert on authentication bypass attempts originating from HTTP handlers or FastCGI processes. Detect SSH key material or credential strings embedded in process memory via memory scanning or binary analysis.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated HTTP POST to Splunk Admin Port
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'without authentication'—the vulnerability is accessible via HTTP requests to Splunk's management API without valid credentials or tokens. This is the initial access vector and should trigger on any unauthenticated POST/GET to typical Splunk ports (8089, 8000, 9997) lacking bearer tokens or session cookies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Splunk management endpoints (8089, 8000) that lack Authorization headers, valid session cookies, or Bearer tokens. Correlate with 4xx responses if endpoint enforces auth post-vuln, or 2xx if pre-patch. Flag POST requests with code-like payloads in URL parameters or request body.

suggestion.title: Child Process Spawned by Splunkd with Suspicious Parent
suggestion.rationale: Title states attackers 'run code'—unauthenticated RCE will result in process creation. Detection must catch when splunkd.exe spawns cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or other execution shells, which is abnormal under routine Splunk operation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on splunkd.exe or Splunk service accounts spawning child processes including: cmd.exe, powershell.exe, sh, bash, perl, python, wget, curl, or obfuscated variants. Baseline legitimate Splunk-spawned processes (search agents, etc.) and exclude those; flag deviations.

suggestion.title: HTTP Request to Splunk Containing Code Execution Syntax
suggestion.rationale: Unauthenticated RCE is delivered via HTTP payload. Detection should key on request content: presence of shell metacharacters, script tags, or code-execution keywords in parameters (cmd=, dispatch=, search=) to Splunk endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect HTTP/HTTPS requests to Splunk IP:port for URL parameters or POST body containing shell metacharacters (|, &, $(), backticks), script payloads, or base64-encoded commands. Alert on suspicious query strings like 'search=|system(...)', 'dispatch=...bash', or similar code-injection patterns.

suggestion.title: Splunk Service Initiating External Network Connection
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation, attackers may use the compromised Splunk instance for command and control or data exfiltration. Splunkd is typically inbound-only; outbound connections from the service are anomalous and should be flagged.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for network connections initiated by splunkd.exe or Splunk service accounts to external IPs (not internal infrastructure, not configured Splunk peers). Alert on connections to uncommon ports (not 8089, 9997, 514) or to IPs with low reputation scores.

suggestion.title: Rapid Unauthenticated Splunk Endpoint Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability scanners and exploitation frameworks will attempt multiple payloads against vulnerable Splunk instances. A pattern of repeated unauthenticated requests in short time windows indicates active exploitation or reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect 10+ unauthenticated requests to known-vulnerable Splunk endpoints (8089, 8000, /services/*, /admin/*) from the same source IP within a 5-minute window. Correlate with presence of exploitation signatures (code payloads, CVE identifiers in User-Agent or parameter names).

suggestion.title: Splunk Configuration or Input Modification by Unauthenticated User
suggestion.rationale: If the vulnerability allows not just code execution but also Splunk config or input modification, attackers could establish persistence. Detection should monitor Splunk audit logs or file integrity for unauthorized changes to inputs.conf, props.conf, or other critical config files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk audit logs (_audit index) for config changes originating from unauthenticated sessions or anonymous users. Alert on modifications to inputs.conf, props.conf, transforms.conf, or app configurations. Correlate with file integrity monitoring on $SPLUNK_HOME/etc directories.

suggestion.title: Kernel Privilege Escalation via Single-Byte Write
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'One-Character Linux Kernel Flaw Enables Local Root Access' — explicit privilege escalation vector; pipeline generated zero privilege-escalation detections despite critical severity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sudden uid/gid transitions from unprivileged to root without setuid/sudo, unusual capability additions (CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE), or privilege escalation syscalls (setuid, setresgid, prctl) triggered from non-standard execution paths. Correlate with heap/stack anomalies in dmesg.

suggestion.title: Exploit POC Execution and Compilation
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Exploits Now Public'; pipeline missed detection of exploit tool staging and execution from user-writable directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect gcc/clang compilation in /tmp, /var/tmp, or home directories; execution of shell scripts with exploit-related strings (kernel, pwn, exploit, CVE); or suspicious curl/wget to exploit repositories. Alert on rapid execve() of newly-compiled binaries followed by privilege escalation.

suggestion.title: Kernel Module Tampering Detection
suggestion.rationale: Kernel exploits commonly load malicious modules or trigger module load paths; pipeline failed to generate kernel-module monitoring use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor modprobe/insmod calls from unprivileged users or with paths outside /lib/modules; detect module loads from /tmp or world-writable locations. Alert on module load attempts that precede privilege escalation or kernel crashes.

suggestion.title: Kernel Crash and BUG_ON Spike Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Kernel exploits often trigger kernel panics or BUG assertions before achieving root; pipeline missed crash-log monitoring for post-exploitation forensics.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sudden increase in kernel OOPS, BUG, or panic messages in dmesg/kern.log. Correlate crash timing with process privilege escalation events. Flag crashes from unexpected processes or following local login attempts.

suggestion.title: Syscall Anomaly: Unusual Memory Access Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Single-character kernel flaw likely exploited via specific memory access or write syscall sequences; pipeline generated no syscall-level detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor audit logs for unusual mmap/mremap/mprotect sequences, or write syscalls to kernel memory ranges. Detect stack pivot patterns or ROP gadget execution signatures. Alert on processes that access /proc/mem or /dev/mem without privilege.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Root Shell Spawning
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'enables Local Root Access' — post-exploitation shell creation is the goal and should be detected; pipeline missed impact-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect spawning of /bin/bash, /bin/sh, or other shells with uid 0 from processes that did not start as root. Alert on setuid/capability escalation immediately followed by execve() of interactive shell. Monitor for non-interactive shells with interactive tty allocation (ptrace/pty hijacking).

suggestion.title: Go Typo-Squatted Package Import Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names attack vector: 'github.com/botdb-go/bolt, similar to the original one i.e. github.com/boltdb/bolt.' This is core initial access method—typo squatting in package name itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor go.mod and go.sum files for imports matching Levenshtein-distance patterns against known legitimate packages (especially high-value targets like boltdb, kubernetes, etc.). Correlate with package registry queries to confirm malicious variant presence. Alert on unexpected imports after dependency updates.

suggestion.title: Go Module Proxy Stale/Cached Malicious Package Serving
suggestion.rationale: Core persistence mechanism: 'Go Module Mirror's indefinite caching of modules kicked in, and that cached the backdored module... The Module was cached on Go Module Proxy, which continued to serve clients.' Package removed from GitHub but proxy continued serving for years.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when build systems or developers request Go modules from official proxies (pkg.go.dev, Go Module Proxy) that have been flagged in CVE/vulnerability databases or removed from origin repos. Track module pull timestamps against known removal/remediation dates. Monitor for version mismatches between declared and cached.

suggestion.title: Go Package Remote Code Execution via Backdoored Import
suggestion.rationale: Article states backdoor in version 1.3.1 'allows hackers to remotely control infected computers through a server that sends them commands.' Execution occurs on package import; need detection for process behavior post-import.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After go application startup, detect unexpected child processes spawned by go runtime (go.exe, go binary), outbound network connections to non-standard ports, or command execution via syscall patterns. Baseline normal Go app behavior per environment; alert on abnormal process spawning, DNS queries to known malware domains, or suspicious environment variable manipulation.

suggestion.title: Dependency Version Regression to Vulnerable/Backdoored Package
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'we now wish to update our systems to the latest dependencies, which led developers to update the version that stayed in the system for 3 years.' Developers updated to (or re-introduced) v1.3.1 thinking it was current, unaware of 3-year caching.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor go.mod/go.sum file changes in version control. Flag any updates to packages that appear in Go vulnerability database (GO-2025-3451 mentioned in article). Cross-reference dependency resolver logs against known malicious versions. Alert on downgrades or lateral moves to versions not in direct dependency chain.

suggestion.title: Outbound C2 Communication from Go Application Runtime
suggestion.rationale: Backdoor mechanism described: 'remotely control infected computers through a server that sends them commands i.e. via a command and control server.' Process is Go runtime; need network IOC correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate outbound network connections initiated by go.exe/go binary with C2 beacon patterns (periodic HTTP requests, DNS tunneling, non-standard ports, geolocation anomalies). Alert on connections to IPs/domains not in corporate whitelist. Use enrichment against known malware C2 infrastructure feeds. High priority if correlated with recent go.mod/go.sum changes.

suggestion.title: Go Module Repository Removal Followed by Continued Local Caching
suggestion.rationale: Article timeline: package removed from GitHub/Go proxy Feb 2025, but 'The Module was cached on Go Module Proxy, which continued to serve clients.' Detection should track removal-to-local-pull gaps.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference internal dependency resolve logs against Go package repository removal notices. Alert if build system pulls a module version within 90 days of its removal/remediation notification. Maintain list of withdrawn/backdoored modules and match against project go.sum files even if removal is old; any presence post-remediation indicates persistent compromise risk.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Appliance External Exposure Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article defines vulnerability window: 'unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Asset inventory precedes all exploitation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate Ivanti Sentry (formerly MobileIron Sentry) appliances on external-routable IPs. Flag instances lacking mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS through Neurons for MDM—these are in the vulnerable exposure window per article mitigation guidance.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation Against Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability explicitly permits 'remote unauthenticated user' exploitation via 'OS command injection.' Direct exploitation detection essential for active CISA KEV entry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry endpoints for unauthenticated HTTP requests containing OS command metacharacters (backticks, $(), pipes, semicolons, &&, ||) in URL/POST parameters. Correlate with successful authentication bypass or command output in response.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Post-Exploitation Process Execution on Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation achieves 'root-level remote code execution.' Early post-exploitation detection critical given severity and active wild exploitation (CISA KEV status).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline expected process tree from Sentry service accounts. Alert on unexpected process spawning from web service processes (Java, Python) with UID 0, shell invocations, or network connections initiated with root privileges.

suggestion.title: mTLS and Restricted HTTPS Protection Bypass Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies specific mitigations: 'Use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible.' Detect misconfiguration or circumvention attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit Sentry instances: flag any lacking mTLS enforcement on EPMM connections or HTTPS restriction to Neurons IP ranges. Alert on unauthorized access to Sentry interfaces from non-restricted sources or disabled certificate validation.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Command Injection in HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability' allowing 'remote unauthenticated user' exploitation. Pipeline generated no detections for injection attempts. Should hunt HTTP logs for command metacharacters (`;`, `|`, `&`, backticks, `$()`) in requests to Sentry endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for HTTP POST/GET requests to Ivanti Sentry appliance management interfaces containing OS command injection patterns (semicolons, pipes, command substitution syntax) in request parameters. Baseline clean traffic first; command metacharacters in parameters to unmanaged appliances should be rare.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation to Root from Web Service Process
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'root-level remote code execution' achievable via command injection. Pipeline missed the privilege-escalation phase entirely. After successful injection, process creation events showing web service spawning processes with root/SYSTEM privileges should be detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor process creation events where parent process is Ivanti Sentry service/web context and child process runs with UID 0 or SYSTEM privileges. Particularly suspicious if child process is bash, sh, PowerShell, or other shell spawned from Java/Python web process.

suggestion.title: External Reachability of Unmanaged Ivanti Sentry Appliances
suggestion.rationale: Article notes vulnerability 'successfully exploited in cases where Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with endpoints externally reachable.' Asset-exposure hunt needed. Pipeline provided only generic CVE scan instruction, no specific asset-posture detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate firewall/proxy logs showing inbound HTTP(S) traffic to Ivanti Sentry management ports (typically 8443, 443) from external (non-VPN, non-managed) sources. Cross-reference against MDM enrollment status; unmanaged appliances in external-facing network perimeter should trigger escalation.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance Traffic to Ivanti Sentry Default Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Pre-exploitation scanning of exposed appliances likely precedes active CVE-2026-10520 exploit attempts. Article describes 'externally reachable' endpoints as the vulnerability condition. Pipeline omitted reconnaissance detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequential HTTP requests to known Ivanti Sentry administrative/API paths (`/api/`, `/admin/`, `/login`) from external IP within short time window. Particularly suspicious if requests probe for version info or attempt default credentials.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Scanning Detection via Vulnerability Scanner Signatures
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes CISA KEV status (actively exploited) and audit requirement. Inbound scan attempts matching CVE-2026-10520 PoC signatures should be detected. Pipeline referenced vulnerability scanners in mitigation but provided no inbound-exploitation-attempt detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests matching known CVE-2026-10520 PoC payloads in request bodies/parameters. IDS/IPS rules from vendors (Snort, Suricata) should be deployed. Baseline: any external scan attempt against Ivanti Sentry appliance is suspicious.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry externally exposed asset hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' This is the gating condition for exploitation; finding exposed instances is the primary detective control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and network telemetry to identify Ivanti Sentry appliances with direct external inbound access on HTTP/HTTPS ports. Cross-reference against inventory to confirm absence of protective controls (mTLS, Neurons for MDM restricted access). Prioritize instances unpatched after federal due date 2026-06-14.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 OS command injection payload detection

suggestion.title: OpenSSH Binary Trojanization
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'replaced OpenSSH components such as ssh, sshd, and scp with trojanized versions that captured credentials, logged commands entered during SSH sessions.' No detection rule generated for OpenSSH binary replacement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect writes to /usr/bin/ssh, /usr/sbin/sshd, /usr/bin/scp outside normal package managers. Monitor compile timestamps of SSH binaries for anomalies versus OS patching schedules. Alert on sshd processes that exhibit unusual child process spawning or file write patterns (credential logging).

suggestion.title: Nginx Proxy Chain to Remote Execution Bridge
suggestion.rationale: Article describes critical technique: 'modified the configuration of a compromised internet-facing Nginx server to proxy specially crafted requests to a compromised backend server' whose Nginx then 'forward requests to a FastCGI process (fcgiwrap)' which 'launched a custom binary named uptime' to establish SSH into isolated network. This multi-stage proxy-to-execution chain for air-gap penetration completely absent from detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor nginx.conf and included configs for unexpected proxy_pass directives, especially chains targeting FastCGI backends on non-standard ports. Alert on fcgiwrap process spawning with custom binary execution (non-standard .so loading). Correlate HTTP POST traffic containing SSH parameters with subsequent SSH connection initiations from web server UIDs.

suggestion.title: SOCKS5 Proxy Masquerading as SMB Daemon
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'custom SOCKS5 proxy for network traffic tunneling' that 'ran as a daemon masquerading as smbd -D, using different filenames and ports on each host, turning compromised servers into internal pivot points.' No detection for this lateral-movement infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on smbd processes with command lines containing only '-D' flag or unusual arguments. Monitor smbd listening on high-numbered ports (>10000) inconsistent with SMB/CIFS. Detect smbd spawning network connections to non-Samba-standard destinations. Flag file system activity from smbd that doesn't match share definitions.

suggestion.title: GS-Netcat Reverse Shell with Systemd Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article states initial compromise deployed 'modified GS-Netcat reverse shell disguised as a legitimate system component' with 'persistence either via a malicious systemd service or through startup script modification.' No detection for modified reverse shells or their persistence mechanisms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GS-Netcat process creation using signature-based matching on known reverse shell indicators. Monitor /etc/systemd/system/ and /usr/lib/systemd/system/ for new service files created outside package manager. Alert on systemd services with ExecStart lines containing network tools (nc, ncat, bash -i, /dev/tcp). Monitor /etc/rc.local and /etc/init.d/ for injected network connection commands.

suggestion.title: Hardcoded Credential Acceptance and Auth Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'replaced legitimate pam_unix.so modules with backdoored versions that accept hardcoded passwords' enabling auth bypass where 'administrative activity became fully observable: every login; every command executed.' No detection for authentication flow manipulation or hardcoded credential acceptance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor authentication logs for successful logins immediately following multiple failed attempts on same account (hardcoded password acceptance after failures). Detect rapid-fire auth events with mixed success/failure patterns inconsistent with user behavior. Alert on command execution from accounts without corresponding interactive login events in auth logs. Flag sessions where user commands appear in logs but login/logout events are missing.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Splunk REST API Access Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'code execution without authentication' — core attack vector is bypassing auth. Detection must flag REST API calls (e.g., /services/*, /api/*) lacking valid auth headers or using malformed credentials to Splunk listener ports.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to Splunk service endpoints with missing Authorization header or HTTP 401 response, followed within 60 seconds by successful HTTP 200 request from same source IP to a privileged endpoint (e.g., /api/server/info, /api/apps/local).

suggestion.title: Child Process Execution Under Splunkd
suggestion.rationale: RCE vulnerability allows arbitrary code execution — must detect anomalous child processes spawned by splunkd.exe or Splunk Python/search processes outside normal search operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect spawning of shell interpreters (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, sh) or system utilities (whoami, ipconfig, curl) as children of splunkd.exe, python.exe (under Splunk), or splunk.exe. Exclude known scheduled searches and admin operations via whitelist.

suggestion.title: Unusual External Inbound Connection to Splunk Service Ports
suggestion.rationale: Critical RCE vulnerability will be actively exploited from external sources — detect external traffic to Splunk listener ports (8089, 8000, 9997) from non-baseline IPs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag inbound connections from external IPs to ports 8089 (Splunk indexer), 8000 (web UI), or 9997 (indexer peer) that are not in approved vendor/partner ranges. Correlate with HTTP GET/POST requests containing encoded payloads or shell syntax.

suggestion.title: Splunk Search Query Injection with OS Command Syntax
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation path likely involves injecting OS commands into search fields or API parameters — detect payloads containing shell metacharacters or command substitution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify search queries or REST API body payloads containing backticks, $(), pipes, semicolons, or common OS commands (cat, ls, whoami, curl, wget) passed to Splunk search endpoints. Alert especially on unauthenticated requests.

suggestion.title: Rapid Succession of Failed Auth + Successful Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Exploit workflow is: probe unauthenticated endpoint (fail), trigger RCE payload (succeed) — detection correlates auth failure/bypass with subsequent process or network anomaly.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP 401 responses to Splunk endpoints from a single source within 10 seconds of that source triggering DeviceProcessEvents (child process spawn) or DeviceNetworkEvents (outbound connection). Short time delta suggests automated exploit delivery.

suggestion.title: Linux Kernel Exploit Execution Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'One-Character Linux Kernel Flaw Enables Local Root Access' and 'Exploits Now Public'—pipeline must detect syscall patterns, kernel error messages, or process exits indicative of kernel exploit triggering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal syscalls (prctl, ioctl, mmap, userfaultfd) from low-privileged processes, kernel warnings/panics, or Oops messages. Correlate with process privilege escalation (uid 0 acquisition). High fidelity for public kernel exploits targeting known flaws.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Root Process Spawning from User Context
suggestion.rationale: 'Enables Local Root Access' is the attack outcome; detection should alert on processes gaining root UID without sudo/su authorization or credential use.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag processes where getuid() != 0 initially but child processes run with uid 0, or where EUID changes from non-zero to zero without setuid binary execution or PAM/sudo audit trails. Watch for kernel-stack-based privilege escalation patterns.

suggestion.title: Kernel Module Anomalies Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Kernel-level exploits may load unsigned modules or manipulate kernel memory; article confirms kernel as attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for insmod/modprobe calls, unsigned module loads, or anomalous entries in /sys/modules. Cross-reference with failed kernel signature verification events. High confidence indicator of post-exploitation persistence.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Kernel Memory Corruption Indicators
suggestion.rationale: 'One-character' flaw suggests memory safety issue (off-by-one, buffer overflow, logic error) typical of CVEs like userfaultfd, DirtyCOW variants, or stack corruption.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect segmentation faults, stack canary violations, heap corruption warnings, or CPU exceptions (SIGSEGV, SIGABRT) immediately preceding privilege escalation. Kernel logs should show address-space layout violations. Time-window correlation: crash → root spawn within <5s.

suggestion.title: Known Kernel Exploit Payload/IOC Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Exploits Now Public'; detection must include file hashes, process command-line signatures, or network IOCs of public PoC tools.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution of known kernel exploit PoCs (CVE-XXXX-XXXXX tools, e.g., public GitHub PoC repos); detect file writes to /tmp or /dev/shm followed by chmod +x and immediate execution. Hash-based detection of published exploit binaries.

suggestion.title: Typo-Squatted Go Package Download Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies the attack vector: 'The malicious Go Module Mirror's was named github.com/botdb-go/bolt, similar to the original one i.e. github.com/boltdb/bolt' — similarity-based package detection is the primary control for this threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor go get, go mod, and go.mod parsing for package names at small edit distance from known legitimate packages (e.g., boltdb→botdb-go). Alert on first-time resolution of lookalike variants, especially from non-canonical mirrors or with unsigned checksums.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Command & Control Communication from Go Application
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'This backdoor allows hackers to remotely control infected computers through a server that sends them commands' — outbound C2 callbacks from the backdoored module are observable kill-chain evidence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected HTTP/HTTPS callbacks from Go binaries to external non-organizational domains, particularly POST requests with command-like payloads, or keepalive patterns consistent with remote code injection awaiting instructions.

suggestion.title: Malicious Module Persistence via Package Cache Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article details the persistence mechanism: 'Go Module Mirror's indefinite caching of modules kicked in, and that cached the backdored module' — the cache served the malicious version for 3+ years after the original was reverted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Go module cache directories ($GOPATH/pkg/mod) for versions cached before a known removal date but accessed long after discovery. Flag timestamp inconsistencies where module metadata differs between local cache and canonical Go Proxy.

suggestion.title: Dependency Version Update to Unvetted or Suspicious Package
suggestion.rationale: Article observes: 'we now wish to update our systems to the latest dependencies, which led developers to update the version that stayed in the system for 3 years' — routine dependency bumps re-activated dormant malicious code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag go mod tidy or go get upgrade operations that pull versions not present in your baseline supply-chain graph, lack cryptographic signatures from known maintainers, or introduce packages with newly-created GitHub accounts/repos.

suggestion.title: Lookalike Package Mirror or Alternative Resolver Detection
suggestion.rationale: The typo-squatted name github.com/botdb-go/bolt vs github.com/boltdb/bolt demonstrates supply-chain misdirection. Article explains the mechanism: 'They hope people will mistakenly download and install these dangerous versions instead of the legitimate software'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Go build/module operations for resolver mismatches: go get commands where the canonical package (e.g., boltdb/bolt) is overshadowed by a near-homograph alternative (botdb-go/bolt), or where GOPROXY environment variable points to non-standard registries.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Unpatched Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Standard asset-exposure hunt against vulnerability scanner for CVE-2026-10520.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for Ivanti Sentry instances flagged with CVE-2026-10520, cross-reference patch status. Flag unpatched and externally reachable assets as critical. Compare against EPMM/MDM console to identify unmanaged instances.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Command Injection Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability' as the exploitation method. Application logs and HTTP access logs should be monitored for command injection patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry HTTP endpoints for shell metacharacters (`;`, `|`, `&&`, backticks, `$()`, `%(...)s`) in request parameters. Correlation with HTTP 200 responses to error responses indicates successful vs. failed injection attempts.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged Ivanti Sentry Instance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'vulnerability exploitable when appliance is in an unmanaged state.' Unmanaged state removes protective mTLS and firewall restrictions. Detection should identify Sentry appliances not reporting to EPMM/Neurons console.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query EPMM/Neurons management console for Sentry appliances with stale heartbeats or marked unmanaged. Identify network interfaces lacking mTLS enforcement. Flag as exploitable without remediation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Root-Level Process Spawning from Sentry Service
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation grants 'root-level remote code execution.' Post-exploitation detection should identify unexpected shell or command execution process spawning under Sentry service principal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry service process (typically privileged user/group) for unexpected child processes: /bin/bash, /bin/sh, cmd.exe, powershell.exe spawned as root or SYSTEM. High-fidelity post-compromise indicator.

suggestion.title: Sentry Interface Accessible Without mTLS Enforcement
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access...makes interfaces inaccessible.' Absence of mTLS or firewall restrictions on management interfaces is a precondition for exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan Ivanti Sentry management ports (443, 8443) for absence of mutual TLS. Cross-reference certificate inventory for Sentry instances without enforced mTLS on EPMM/Neurons connections. Identify appliances reachable from external networks without firewall restriction.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Internet Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'vulnerability can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' This is the canonical first-line detection—identify all Sentry instances exposed to untrusted networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Ivanti Sentry/MobileIron instances accessible from internet (port 8443, HTTP User-Agent, known URI paths). Correlate with asset inventory to flag unmanaged or unpatched instances. Alert if mTLS/restricted HTTPS fronting is not in place (per article: 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access...makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors').

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload Detection in HTTP Traffic
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is explicitly 'OS command injection'—payload delivery via HTTP requests containing shell metacharacters. Article does not provide exact parameter names but standard injection markers (;, |, &&, ||, backtick, $()) will be present in exploit attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to Sentry endpoints with shell metacharacters in query parameters or POST body: semicolons, pipes, logical operators (&&, ||), backticks, command substitution ($(...)), or newline injection attempts. Baseline Sentry's legitimate traffic (MDM enrollment, device sync) to filter benign requests.

suggestion.title: Root-Privilege Process Spawning from Sentry Service
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'root-level remote code execution'—successful exploitation will spawn arbitrary processes running as root/SYSTEM from Sentry service context. This is the privilege-escalation hallmark of the attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation where parent is Sentry/MobileIron service (sentry.jar, mobileironcore, or known Sentry daemon) spawning child processes with uid=0 (Linux) or LocalSystem (Windows), especially if child is shell, cmd.exe, bash, curl, wget, nc, or other utilities not expected in normal Sentry operation.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Patch Compliance Check
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV signals active exploitation. Article provides federal patch due date 2026-06-14 (overdue relative to article date 2026-06-11). Patch inventory is now a blocking detection requirement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and patch systems for Ivanti Sentry instances with CVE-2026-10520 unpatched. Flag any match as critical, especially if correlated with internet-accessible instances from exposure hunt. Track remediation SLA violation (due 2026-06-14); alert if unpatched instances remain.

suggestion.title: Sentry Service Crash and Abnormal Restart Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation activity via RCE (arbitrary root-level command execution) will likely cause service instability, crashes, or unexpected restarts—an operational detection signal of compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Sentry/MobileIron service crashes, unexpected restarts, or high-frequency restart patterns (e.g., >3 restarts in 1 hour). Correlate with OS command-injection attempts and root-privilege process spawning to confirm exploitation in progress.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure Hunt — Ivanti Sentry Externally Reachable
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable'—this is the primary attack surface for CVE-2026-10520 exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory and vulnerability scanners for Ivanti Sentry (including legacy 'MobileIron Sentry' naming) with external reachability to HTTP(S) management interfaces. Flag unmanaged instances with exposure on ports 443, 8443, or default admin interface ports.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempts — Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article defines attack mechanism: 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP request logs for command injection payloads targeting Ivanti Sentry endpoints (bash metacharacters: $(), backticks, pipes in URI parameters or POST bodies). Flag requests to vulnerable endpoints from external sources without prior authentication.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Administrative API Access — Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'remote unauthenticated user' accessing root-level administrative functions, indicating complete absence of authentication requirement on exposed endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to known Ivanti Sentry administrative endpoints originating from external IPs without authentication headers (missing Authorization, session tokens, or mTLS certificates). High-fidelity on HTTP 200 responses vs. expected 401/403.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Root-Level Process Execution — Sentry Appliances
suggestion.rationale: Article describes end-state: 'achieve root-level remote code execution'—successful exploitation results in privileged command execution detectable via process monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for uid=0 (root) process creation on Ivanti Sentry appliances following network connections from external IPs to vulnerable endpoints. Suspicious child processes: shell invocation (sh, bash), reverse shells, package managers. Baseline expected processes and alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Detection — Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes CISA KEV status with observed active exploitation in the wild and federal remediation deadline 2026-06-14—requires immediate vulnerability management action.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners and asset management systems for CVE-2026-10520 matches against 'Ivanti Sentry' (including legacy 'MobileIron Sentry'). Report all hits; patch-lag is common and deployed patches should be validated against running services.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged Sentry Appliance Inventory Gap — Missing mTLS or HTTPS Restriction
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors'—implies unmitigated instances are those without these controls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit all Ivanti Sentry appliances for management interface security configuration: identify and flag appliances lacking mTLS enforcement, HTTPS restriction, or EPMM/Neurons for MDM integration. These represent unmitigated attack surface.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Ivanti Sentry Admin Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'remote unauthenticated user' can trigger the vulnerability; this is the initial access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry admin/API endpoints from untrusted networks with successful responses when no valid authentication (session cookies, Bearer tokens, client certificates) is present. Alert on any external access to restricted admin paths.

suggestion.title: Command Injection Payload Detection in Sentry Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability'; requires inspection of web parameters for shell metacharacters (|, ;, &, $(), backticks).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Web application firewall or IDS rules detecting shell command syntax in request parameters or POST bodies targeting Sentry endpoints. Flag requests containing pipe, semicolon, ampersand, backticks, or command substitution syntax to Sentry paths.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Spawning from Sentry Service
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability enables 'root-level remote code execution'; post-compromise detection requires monitoring elevated-privilege process creation from Sentry context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor process creation where parent is Ivanti Sentry service and spawned process runs as SYSTEM/root with unexpected executable path or command-line. Baseline legitimate Sentry child processes; alert on bash, sh, cmd.exe, or powershell spawned as root from Sentry context.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unmanaged State Probing
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability only exploitable when 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state'; attackers would probe for this configuration prior to exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect external reconnaissance of Sentry configuration or status endpoints (/.../status, /.../config, /.../management, /.../health) from untrusted IPs. Alert on repeated failed attempts to access management interfaces or successful responses indicating unmanaged mode.

suggestion.title: Reverse Shell Activity from Sentry Process
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation of RCE typically involves shell spawning; article confirms root access is achievable, indicating attacker maintains interactive sessions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate short-lived shell process creation (bash, sh, powershell, cmd) as child of Sentry service with unexpected outbound network connections to non-standard ports. Alert on Sentry-spawned shell connecting to external IPs on ports >1024.

suggestion.title: External Ivanti Sentry Appliance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability only exploitable when 'externally reachable' — detection of internet-facing Sentry instances is critical prerequisite.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances exposed to internet via network scanning, certificate analysis, or service enumeration. Flag ports 443, 8080, or 8443 with Ivanti Sentry HTTP banners or X-Server headers. Cross-reference against internal asset inventory to alert on unexpected external exposure.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Attempt — Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability' as the core attack vector — detecting injection attempts is the primary exploitation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints for OS command metacharacters (pipes, backticks, command substitution, semicolons) in URL parameters or POST bodies. Alert on patterns targeting known vulnerable endpoints with payloads containing $(...)`, backticks, or shell command separators.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Ivanti Sentry Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability requires 'unauthenticated' access — detection of successful auth bypass or unauthenticated command execution is critical.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry appliance access logs for HTTP 200-OK responses to unauthenticated requests (missing Authorization header or invalid session tokens) reaching vulnerable endpoints. Flag any successful command execution from non-authenticated sessions.

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution from Sentry Appliance
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'root-level remote code execution' as the exploitation outcome — detecting post-exploitation process execution on the appliance itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry appliance or container host for unexpected child processes spawned from the Sentry service user (root or sentry_service). Alert on suspicious command patterns: curl/wget downloads, Python/bash with -c flags, reverse shells, or lateral-movement tools.

suggestion.title: mTLS/HTTPS Security Control Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access' prevents exploitation — detecting bypasses of these controls is essential.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry appliance network connections for unencrypted HTTP traffic to ports that should enforce HTTPS, or TLS handshakes lacking valid client certificates where mTLS is required. Flag connections from external, unmanaged, or untrusted endpoints.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Exploitation Activity Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status indicates active exploitation in the wild — rule-based signature detection for known attack patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Deploy IDS/WAF signatures for known CVE-2026-10520 exploitation payloads published in POCs and threat advisories. Alert on any matches regardless of patch status, as patch lag is common. Monitor for HTTP POST requests with malicious command injection payloads targeting /api/admin or /cmd endpoints.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Reachability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states explicitly: 'can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' External exposure is the attack prerequisite.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for Ivanti Sentry / MobileIron Sentry appliances accessible from external networks. Inventory all instances and flag those without mTLS + EPMM or Neurons for MDM restrictive controls. Cross-correlate with patch inventory for CVE-2026-10520 exposure.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation Against Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article core attack vector: 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Direct exploit pathway.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to exposed Ivanti Sentry interfaces for OS command injection patterns: shell metacharacters, backticks, $(), command substitution, pipe operators in query parameters or POST bodies. Flag unauthenticated requests with command execution indicators.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated RCE Against Sentry Appliance
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability explicitly requires no authentication: 'remote unauthenticated user.' Any successful code execution without valid session should alert.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any successful API/endpoint responses from Ivanti Sentry that indicate code execution (HTTP 200, command output in response body, status changes in appliance logs) without preceding valid authentication token or session cookie.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV mandates federal patch by 2026-06-14. Article explicitly references vulnerability scanning as primary hunt: 'CVE-2026-10520 — match against your vulnerability scanner.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Run Nessus/Qualys/native scanners for CVE-2026-10520 across enterprise. Flag positives regardless of patch status; patch lag is common. Correlate with network exposure data to identify externally-reachable instances as critical.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unmanaged State Configuration Audit
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability only exploitable 'in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state.' Configuration posture directly enables exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit all Ivanti Sentry appliances for management state (EPMM enrollment status, Neurons for MDM integration, mTLS configuration). Flag any instances in unmanaged state that are simultaneously network-exposed. Treat as critical finding requiring emergency remediation.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'remote unauthenticated user' exploiting 'OS command injection vulnerability.' This is the attack vector and should have a direct detection use case. No detection pattern was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry endpoints for unusual HTTP POST requests with command-like payloads, shell metacharacters, or known exploit patterns. Correlate with external access logs to confirm unauthenticated source. Flag any successful responses indicating code execution (200-range responses to malformed requests).

suggestion.title: Unexpected Root-level Process Spawning from Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability allows 'root-level remote code execution.' Post-exploitation detection should monitor for abnormal process execution originating from Sentry service context with elevated privileges.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes spawned with root privilege context by or from Ivanti Sentry daemon. Alert on shell interpreters (/bin/bash, /bin/sh, /bin/ksh) or non-standard binaries executed as root child processes of Sentry. Filter out expected administrative scripts.

suggestion.title: Exposed Unmanaged Ivanti Sentry Appliance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability is exploitable 'in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Requires asset and configuration scanning to identify exposed, unprotected instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for Ivanti Sentry appliances accessible on internet-facing IP space without mTLS or restrictive HTTPS controls. Cross-reference with endpoint management tools (EPMM, Neurons for MDM) to identify managed vs. unmanaged instances. Flag unmanaged externally-reachable instances as critical exposure.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Access Attempts to Ivanti Sentry Management Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article notes mTLS and HTTPS restrictions are mitigations, implying these interfaces are normal targets. Detection should monitor for access bypass or direct exploitation of management endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry management URLs (typically 443, sometimes 8443) from external IPs. Alert on requests lacking mTLS certificate validation or containing exploitation payloads (command injection syntax, SQLi patterns). Baseline legitimate administrative access first.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scanner Match & Patch Status
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'match against your vulnerability scanner' and emphasizes patch lag risk. Detection should combine vulnerability scan results with configuration data to confirm patch status.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-10520 matches. Correlate scanner alerts with patch management system to verify patches applied before federal due date (2026-06-14). Alert on unpatched instances with externally routable interfaces; prioritize unmanaged appliances.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Presence - Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'Substitute this CVE wherever the template references <CVE>: CVE-2026-10520' and recommends matching against vulnerability scanners. This basic inventory detection was entirely omitted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results, patch management logs, and asset inventory for Ivanti Sentry product presence with CVE-2026-10520 fingerprints (version checks, config patterns). Flag any unpatched instance as high-priority given CISA federal due date of 2026-06-14.

suggestion.title: Externally-Reachable Ivanti Sentry Appliance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is exploitable 'in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' No UC hunts for external network exposure, the primary precondition for active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound HTTPS traffic (ports 443, 8443, or custom) to Ivanti Sentry appliances from external ASNs. Cross-reference with asset inventory to identify instances without mTLS or restricted HTTPS controls mentioned as mitigations. Alert on any unprotected externally-reachable Sentry endpoint.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload Detection - Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability' as the exploit vector. No UC targets command-injection payloads or suspicious command syntax in requests to Sentry endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints for OS command-injection indicators: backticks, $(...), semicolons, pipes, or shell metacharacters in URL parameters, headers, or POST bodies. Flag requests containing command substitution or chaining operators as malicious.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution from Ivanti Sentry Service
