suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect HTTP request logs to Sentry appliances for command metacharacters (backticks, $(), |, ;, &&, ||) in POST/PUT parameters. Flag requests to known-vulnerable endpoints with injection indicators. High confidence if source is untrusted network.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Root-Level Process Execution on Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article states successful exploitation achieves 'root-level remote code execution.' Post-exploitation, attacker spawns processes with root privilege on the appliance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry appliance process logs (via auditd, syslog, or vendor API) for unexpected processes spawned by the vulnerable service daemon running as root. Baseline normal process spawning and alert on deviations, especially interactive shells (bash, sh) or reverse shells.

suggestion.title: Network Reconnaissance Against Sentry Ports
suggestion.rationale: Article implies attacker must first identify externally-reachable Sentry instances. Scanning or probing for open ports precedes exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag port scans or repeated connection attempts to typical Sentry listening ports from external IPs. Correlate with failed/rejected connections on Sentry appliances. High confidence if followed within hours by successful unauthenticated requests or injection payloads.

suggestion.title: Sentry Appliance Lateral Movement Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article notes mTLS/restricted HTTPS controls prevent external access but does not address east-west segmentation. A compromised Sentry in unmanaged state may pivot to internal assets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After RCE on Sentry, attacker may use root shell to scan internal networks or stage files. Monitor for anomalous outbound connections from Sentry appliance (port scans, file transfers, SSH/RDP probes) to internal subnets not in baseline communication pattern.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable' as exploitation precondition. Article also explicitly references 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' template. Pipeline should detect externally accessible Ivanti Sentry management interfaces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for inbound connections to Ivanti Sentry management ports (8443, 443) from untrusted external sources. Alert on external IPs successfully reaching Sentry management interfaces where access should be restricted to internal/VPN ranges.

suggestion.title: Command Injection Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is 'OS command injection' accessible to 'remote unauthenticated user'. Should detect suspicious command-like input to Sentry endpoints (shell metacharacters: pipe, semicolon, backtick, $(), etc.) indicating exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints for unencoded shell metacharacters or common encoding patterns (URL, HTML, Unicode) in parameters targeting likely vulnerable endpoints. Alert on payloads with command separators (;|&$).

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Process Execution on Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation achieves 'root-level remote code execution'. Should detect unexpected process execution spawned by Sentry processes with root/system privileges outside normal baseline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process execution where parent process is a Sentry service and child is unexpected (shells, curl, wget, nc, bash with network flags, reverse-shell indicators) executing with elevated privileges on Sentry appliances.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Sentry appliance provides MDM/endpoint management with internal network access. Compromised Sentry represents foothold for lateral movement. Should detect abnormal outbound connections from Sentry to internal network.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from Ivanti Sentry to internal IP ranges and suspicious ports (22, 3389, 5985, 5986, 135, 139) where Sentry should not normally initiate connections. Alert on connections to database, directory, or other sensitive internal systems.

suggestion.title: Mitigation Bypass – mTLS/HTTPS Restriction Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access makes interfaces inaccessible.' Post-exploitation attacker may disable these controls. Should detect configuration degradation of security settings.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on configuration changes to Ivanti Sentry that disable mTLS, weaken HTTPS restrictions, relax certificate validation, or broaden firewall rules for management interface access. Monitor for disabling of mutual TLS or changes to access control lists.

suggestion.title: AI-Generated Phishing Email Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly discusses 'AI phishing' as the threat driver. Pipeline should detect synthetic-generation indicators in email body structure, language patterns, and header anomalies per the article's core subject matter.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify inbound emails with unusual linguistic patterns (AI-generated markers), mismatched sender reputation vs. content urgency, or envelope-from/SMTP-auth misalignment indicative of spoofed AI-driven campaigns.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Email Alert Volume Spike
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly mentions 'crushing SOCs with alert volume.' Pipeline should correlate inbound email alert count spikes against baseline with sender reputation changes and authentication failures, directly addressing the reported overload mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for 300%+ surge in inbound email alerts in sliding 4-hour windows; correlate spikes with DMARC/SPF/DKIM failure counts and unique sender IPs to distinguish volume-based evasion from legitimate email storms.

suggestion.title: Email Authentication Bypass Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Phishing delivery depends on bypassing SPF/DKIM/DMARC. Article title implies modern phishing uses sophisticated sender spoofing. Pipeline should detect failed authentication combined with user engagement signals.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Trigger on emails where SPF=fail OR DKIM=fail OR DMARC=reject yet user clicked embedded links or opened attachments within 5 minutes of receipt, indicating phishing success despite auth failures.

suggestion.title: Post-Phishing Credential Access Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article focuses on phishing as initial access; should detect downstream compromise. Monitor for MFA bypass attempts, impossible-travel logins, or unusual credential usage after suspicious email receipt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate users who clicked phishing links in the past 24 hours with subsequent failed MFA challenges, password-spray patterns, or sign-ins from anomalous geographies or non-managed devices.

suggestion.title: Email Sandbox Evasion Detection
suggestion.rationale: AI-generated phishing implies sophisticated evasion of sandbox/detection engines. Pipeline should flag emails where attachments or URLs fail traditional detonation but succeed via user interaction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify emails where URL/attachment detonation returned 'clean' verdict yet recipient's endpoint shows execution/download anomalies (process creation, registry writes, DLL injection) within 10 minutes of email receipt.

suggestion.title: Tier 1 Alert Fatigue Metrics
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly mentions 'reduce Tier 1 Overload.' Pipeline should surface metrics-based detection of analyst alert-response degradation as a secondary threat indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for mean-time-to-response (MTTR) degradation >40% YoY, increase in auto-closed/dismissed alerts, or escalation-to-Tier-2 delays >2 hours, indicating alert-fatigue-driven detection failures.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution' via 'OS command injection'—exploitation attempts must be detected via suspicious request patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP/HTTPS requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints containing OS command injection metacharacters (pipes, semicolons, backticks, $() substitution, bash/cmd syntax) or documented exploit signatures. Correlate with external source IPs and failed authentication attempts.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Exposed Instance Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends asset-exposure hunt and explicitly states vulnerability is exploitable when appliance 'is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable'—must enumerate WAN-facing Sentry instances before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances exposed to untrusted networks via SSL certificate inspection, web server banners, admin interface fingerprinting, or vulnerability scanner results. Flag instances on internet-routable addresses lacking mTLS/EPMM protection.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Spawning from Ivanti Sentry Service
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'root-level remote code execution' through command injection—this manifests as the Sentry service spawning unexpected child processes with elevated privileges.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned by Ivanti Sentry service accounts (java, tomcat) with root/SYSTEM privileges, or spawning shell interpreters (bash, sh, cmd.exe, powershell.exe). Baseline legitimate Sentry child processes; flag command utilities and reverse shells.

suggestion.title: External Unauthenticated Access to Ivanti Sentry Web Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'externally reachable endpoints' as a precondition and 'external actors' accessing an unauthenticated interface—access from untrusted networks to Sentry ports (9443, 9090) is anomalous.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag successful HTTP(S) connections to known Ivanti Sentry ports from external/untrusted IP ranges without corresponding Ivanti authentication infrastructure upstream. Monitor failed login attempts and anomalous request patterns to /api/ or admin endpoints from outside corporate IP space.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Ivanti Sentry External Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states exploit succeeds 'where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable' — direct asset hunting requirement
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Ivanti Sentry instances accessible from untrusted networks. Correlate with CMDB to identify unmanaged appliances. Verify mTLS or restricted HTTPS access is deployed per article's mitigation notes.

suggestion.title: Command Injection Payload Detection: CVE-2026-10520
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability mechanism is 'OS command injection' — attack vector requires crafted requests; WAF/IDS should flag injection attempts to vulnerable endpoints
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP traffic to Ivanti Sentry for command injection payloads (shell metacharacters, command separators, backticks). Match against known CVE-2026-10520 exploit signatures.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Process Execution from Ivanti Sentry Service
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation grants 'root-level remote code execution' — post-compromise would show unexpected processes spawned from Sentry daemon context
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned from Ivanti Sentry services running with root or system privileges. Baseline normal process trees and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scan Match: CVE-2026-10520 Remediation Deadline
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry with federal remediation deadline 2026-06-14; critical patch urgency signal
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Run CVE-2026-10520 scans across all appliances. Escalate any positive matches to emergency remediation queue. Track patch deployment against federal deadline via ticketing system.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access Followed by RCE: Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Exploit is 'remote unauthenticated' — successful attacks execute code without authentication credentials in logs; signals auth bypass or injection success
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on RCE indicators (error messages, unexpected output, command execution logs) in Ivanti Sentry logs from sources that never authenticated. Correlate failed auth attempts with successful execution.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability is exploitable 'in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' This is the canonical CISA KEV hunt vector. Substitute CVE-2026-10520 into asset-exposure template.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners and asset inventory for Ivanti Sentry (or legacy MobileIron Sentry) appliances with unpatched CVE-2026-10520. Cross-reference with network exposure assessments (Internet-facing, lacks mTLS or restricted HTTPS controls via Neurons for MDM). Flag all unmanaged instances with external reachability.

suggestion.title: HTTP Command Injection Exploitation Attempt: Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability' exploitable by 'remote unauthenticated user.' Network-layer detection of payloads targeting Sentry endpoints with shell metacharacters or command substitution syntax.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to Ivanti Sentry appliance endpoints (admin console, API endpoints) for payloads containing shell metacharacters (backticks, $(), |, &, ;, >), command substitution patterns, or known OS command injection signatures. Correlate with HTTP 500 errors, parser exceptions, or timeouts indicating exploitation.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Process Execution from Ivanti Sentry Service Context
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability achieves 'root-level remote code execution.' Host telemetry should detect command execution spawned from Sentry service processes or running at root privilege.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, sh) with parent process or user context matching Ivanti Sentry services. Establish baseline of legitimate process spawning; flag shell or interactive interpreters, especially those with outbound network connections or file modification activity.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Appliance in Unmanaged State
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state' as prerequisite for exploitability. Configuration assessment should surface management state and correlate with external accessibility.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Ivanti Sentry management APIs or appliance config repositories to enumerate instances in unmanaged mode. Cross-reference against network access control lists; flag unmanaged appliances reachable from Internet-facing networks, DMZs, or untrusted VLANs.

suggestion.title: Network Scanning of Ivanti Sentry Web Interfaces
suggestion.rationale: Article states endpoints must be 'externally reachable' for exploitation; reconnaissance activity precedes successful exploitation. Monitor for scanning patterns targeting Sentry ports.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on rapid-fire GET requests to Ivanti Sentry HTTPS endpoints (typically 443, paths like /admin, /api, /health) from external sources. Flag varying User-Agent strings, connection attempts to multiple Sentry instances in sequence, or scanning tools (Nessus, OpenVAS, etc.) User-Agents.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Privilege Confirmation: Root Account Activity from Sentry Context
suggestion.rationale: Article outcome is 'root-level remote code execution'; host logs should show UID 0 or SYSTEM-level process creation following injection attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP command injection detection with subsequent process execution at UID 0 (root) or SYSTEM privilege. Flag new account creation, sudoers/shadow file access, or unexpected daemons spawned from Sentry service context at elevated privilege.

suggestion.title: WordPress Plugin File Integrity Deviation
suggestion.rationale: Article states plugins 'tampered' and 'scripts' modified with backdoors. Zero UC for file integrity monitoring of wp-content/plugins/ directory despite this being the primary attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on modifications to .php files in wp-content/plugins/ outside of package manager execution windows. Establish baseline of legitimate plugin directories per site and flag unauthorized changes to core plugin files. Correlate mtime changes with absence of corresponding WordPress plugin update activity.

suggestion.title: Suspicious PHP Process Spawning from Web Root
suggestion.rationale: Backdoors 'planted' in plugins execute via HTTP—implying process spawning from web-accessible directories. No UC for detecting PHP child processes or command execution initiated from WordPress plugin paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect php.exe or php-cgi spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or bash when parent process or working directory traces to wp-content/ or wp-admin/. Flag process execution with unusual command-line encoding (base64, hex escapes) or obfuscation patterns typical of PHP eval() payloads.

suggestion.title: Hidden WordPress Admin Account Registration
suggestion.rationale: Backdoors typically establish administrative persistence via rogue accounts. Article implies persistence mechanism ('hidden backdoors') but zero UC for post-compromise admin creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WordPress user creation events for accounts registered outside normal provisioning workflows. Flag simultaneous account creation and role escalation to Administrator. Detect programmatic user insertion via wp_usermeta table modifications or REST API /users endpoints from non-admin sources.

suggestion.title: Backdoor Command & Control Communication
suggestion.rationale: Hidden backdoors require communication channel to attacker infrastructure. Article implies offensive capability ('backdoors') but generated no C2 detection for network exfiltration or remote command receipt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound HTTP/HTTPS connections from php.exe processes in WordPress root, especially to unfamiliar domains or IPs with low reputation. Detect POST requests to suspicious endpoints from wp-content/ paths. Flag DNS queries for domains with no WHOIS registration history or known C2 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: WordPress Cron-Based Backdoor Persistence
suggestion.rationale: 'Hidden' backdoors often leverage WP-Cron for recurring execution without detection. No UC for scheduled task creation or cron-triggered malicious PHP.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor wp_cron entries for scheduled tasks executing PHP code from unexpected plugin directories. Flag base64-encoded payloads in cron callbacks. Detect cron events that spawn network connections or file modifications during low-traffic hours (suspicious timing for legitimate plugin activity).

suggestion.title: Malicious Code Injection into Plugin Loader Hooks
suggestion.rationale: Backdoors often hijack WordPress plugin initialization via action hooks or mu-plugins/ directory injection. Pipeline generated no detection for plugin loader-layer persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan wp-content/mu-plugins/ for unexplained PHP files or plugin header metadata. Monitor wp-config.php additions for require() statements pointing to suspicious paths. Flag obfuscated or eval()-based code added to plugin hooks via static analysis. Alert on plugin files with PHP comment-only headers (lack of legitimate plugin metadata).

suggestion.title: GlobalProtect VPN Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'active exploitation of PAN-OS GlobalProtect VPN Flaw'—a clear attack vector that must be detected at the perimeter. No use case was generated despite this being the primary attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GlobalProtect gateway logs for unusual HTTP request patterns, malformed SSL/TLS handshakes, or HTTP POST requests to admin endpoints with suspicious payloads. Flag requests with executable content-type headers or script injection markers targeting auth modules.

suggestion.title: Post-VPN-Compromise Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Active exploitation implies successful compromises and downstream movement into internal networks—article context strongly suggests lateral movement phase follows initial VPN breach, but no corresponding detection use case was created.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound connections from VPN-authenticated hosts to internal network ranges within minutes of authentication, especially to non-standard ports or to hosts not in baseline. Flag command-line execution of remote access tools or scripts on systems accessed over VPN.

suggestion.title: Suspicious GlobalProtect Authentication Patterns
suggestion.rationale: VPN compromise typically involves credential stuffing, brute-force, or session hijacking—article mentions 'active exploitation' suggesting ongoing access attempts. No use case addresses authentication anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GlobalProtect authentication logs for spike in failed login attempts, successful logins from new geographies within short timeframes, or logins to disabled/inactive accounts. Correlate with public IP geolocation changes within 5-minute windows.

suggestion.title: Known CVE Exploitation Signature Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article references a specific GlobalProtect VPN flaw (CVE number absent from provided body, but critical advisories carry specific CVE)—no use case was generated to detect exploitation payloads or known attack signatures for this vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create signature-based detection for known exploit payloads targeting the GlobalProtect gateway. Monitor for specific request patterns (path traversal, XXE, SSRF, RCE payloads) documented in CVE and Palo Alto security advisories.

suggestion.title: Detect Typo-Squatted Package Imports in Dependency Manifests
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies typo squatting as the initial access: 'github.com/botdb-go/bolt, similar to the original one i.e. github.com/boltdb/bolt.' Malicious package names differ by 1-2 characters from legitimate targets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor go.mod/go.sum and package resolution logs for package names with small Levenshtein distance (≤2 chars) to known-legitimate packages. Flag imports of packages with character substitutions (botdb vs boltdb) as potential supply-chain compromise.

suggestion.title: Detect Imports of Known-Malicious Package Versions
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies malicious package github.com/botdb-go/bolt v1.3.1 released Nov 2021, discovered Jan 30 2025, now in Go vulnerability database (GO-2025-3451) and Snyk advisory SNYK-GOLANG-GITHUBCOMBOLTDBGOBOLT-868841.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference all go module resolution logs against Go vuln DB and Snyk advisories. Alert on any resolution of github.com/botdb-go/bolt v1.3.1 or matching package names from affected registries.

suggestion.title: Detect C2 Communication from Compromised Systems with Malicious Package
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'This backdoor allows hackers to remotely control infected computers through a server that sends them commands i.e. via a command and control server.' Egress to C2 is the exploitation behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On systems with resolved github.com/botdb-go/bolt v1.3.1 in build artifacts or runtime, correlate with outbound connections to unknown domains, unusual DNS patterns, or encrypted tunneling from Go binaries initiated post-package installation.

suggestion.title: Monitor Go Module Proxy Cache Poisoning and Indefinite Caching Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article describes persistence: 'Go Module Mirror's indefinite caching of modules kicked in, and that cached the backdored module' for 3+ years. Cache abuse is the unique mechanism that kept malware alive after source removal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Go Module Proxy requests for typo-squatted package names and version serve-date anomalies (e.g., version served after removal from origin repo, or same version with multiple publish timestamps). Alert when a package is removed from origin but remains in cache.

suggestion.title: Detect Post-Compromise Process Execution and Lateral Movement from Backdoored Package
suggestion.rationale: Article reports 'Impacted thousands of organizations for over three years' with attacker capability to execute arbitrary commands. Systems with the malicious package active are compromised endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On hosts where github.com/botdb-go/bolt v1.3.1 is resolved at build or runtime, monitor for unexpected process spawning (shells, interpreters), elevation attempts, or lateral-movement indicators correlated with C2 communication timeline.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain: Monitor Upstream Registry for Masqueraded Package Names
suggestion.rationale: Article describes the attack surface: packages with names similar to legitimate ones uploaded to Go Module Proxy without automated name-collision detection. Infrastructure-layer detection needed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Go Module Proxy for newly-registered packages with Levenshtein distance <3 to high-value targets (boltdb, kubernetes, popular DB tools, etc.). Cross-reference suspicious registrations with Go vulnerability DB and security advisories within 48 hours of registration.

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify externally accessible Ivanti Sentry appliances via port scanning patterns, SSL certificate fingerprinting (MobileIron Sentry/Ivanti Sentry specific), or direct HTTP responses matching known appliance signatures. Correlate with vulnerability scanners confirming CVE-2026-10520 exposure.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry OS Command Injection Exploitation

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry appliance process logs for unexpected child processes spawned with root UID/SYSTEM privileges, unusual command execution paths, or privilege escalation indicators post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: HTTP Exploitation Attempt to Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article implies HTTP/HTTPS-based exploitation against unmanaged appliances. Web-layer logs should show injection payloads pre-execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP POST/GET to Ivanti Sentry endpoints with command-injection indicators: shell metacharacters in query strings, null-byte sequences, encoded payloads. Correlate requests from external IPs with process creation events on target host seconds later.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation to Root from Ivanti Service Account
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'achieve root-level remote code execution.' Privilege escalation from service context to root must be detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sudo invocation, setuid binary execution, or root-context process spawning from Ivanti service user. Look for unexpected parent-child process relationships with root as target.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'This vulnerability can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Asset exposure is the primary condition for risk; article explicitly recommends asset-exposure hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate Ivanti Sentry appliances externally visible via port scanning, certificate enumeration (HTTPS banners), or DNS/reverse-DNS. Cross-reference with asset inventory to surface unmanaged or unpatched instances. High-signal indicator for exploitation risk.

suggestion.title: Patch Compliance: Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520 Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'patch lag is the silent killer' and federal due-date is 2026-06-14. Pipeline should generate patch-tracking hunt correlating vulnerability scanner data against vendor-published patched versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest Ivanti Sentry instance versions from asset inventory. Cross-reference against vendor security bulletins for patched version threshold for CVE-2026-10520. Alert on vulnerable versions, especially post-federal-deadline instances.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection: Sentry Process Execution Baseline
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Exploitation requires shell or command execution; should detect abnormal process spawning from Sentry service.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal Ivanti Sentry process behavior (expected child processes, typical command patterns). Alert on shell spawning (sh/bash), reverse-shell indicators, or unexpected system commands executed from Sentry process context.

suggestion.title: Sentry Appliance Unmanaged State Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state.' Unmanaged state is a prerequisite for exploitation; mTLS with EPMM or Neurons for MDM mitigates. Should detect appliances lacking these protections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for Ivanti Sentry deployments. Cross-reference against EPMM enrollment and Neurons for MDM enrollment status. Flag appliances not enrolled in management, indicating unmitigated exposure.

suggestion.title: Sentry Exploitation Attempt: Network Signature Sweep
suggestion.rationale: Article describes remote, unauthenticated command-injection exploitation. Network-level detection (IDS/proxy inspection) should flag exploitation attempts targeting the vulnerable interface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Develop or monitor for network signatures targeting Ivanti Sentry interfaces. Alert on suspicious HTTP/HTTPS payloads containing shell metacharacters, command separators, or common injection patterns targeting Sentry endpoints.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scanner Positive
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2026-10520 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and emphasizes CISA KEV entries are currently exploited in the wild. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite directive and the CISA KEV status requiring immediate action.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Ivanti Sentry instances flagged with CVE-2026-10520 in scanner output. Alert on unpatched instances, particularly those not remediated by federal due date 2026-06-14; article emphasizes patch lag is 'the silent killer.'

suggestion.title: External Ivanti Sentry Appliance Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability exploitable 'in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Mitigation via mTLS and restricted HTTPS implies network-exposure detection is critical. Pipeline omitted asset-exposure hunt despite explicit recommendation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances (typical ports 8443 MDM, 443 web interface) reachable from untrusted networks. Cross-correlate with device inventory to flag unmanaged instances lacking mTLS enrollment with EPMM or restricted HTTPS through Neurons.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Execution on Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies vulnerability as 'OS command injection' enabling remote unauthenticated RCE. This execution technique is the attack centerpiece; pipeline captured no execution-layer detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry appliances for shell metacharacters, command substitution, or backticks in HTTP request payloads from external/unauthenticated sources. Detect unexpected shell process spawn from Sentry service account.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Command Execution on Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability achieves 'root-level remote code execution'—privilege escalation to root is the definitive impact. Pipeline failed to model this critical escalation stage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect root-level shell or process execution spawned from Ivanti Sentry daemon or web service context without corresponding authentication. Alert on UID 0 process creation from non-privileged service accounts.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unmanaged Configuration Baseline
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes vulnerability requires 'unmanaged state' appliance; mitigations (mTLS with EPMM, restricted HTTPS proxy) explicitly identify safe configurations. Pipeline omitted configuration-assessment detection identifying at-risk instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline Ivanti Sentry appliances with known-good mTLS + EPMM enrollment and Neurons proxy enrollment. Flag instances missing either control as 'unmanaged' and at risk for T1190 exploitation.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated HTTP Access to Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'remote unauthenticated user' can trigger exploitation—authentication bypass is a prerequisite condition. Pipeline omitted access-control violation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP/HTTPS requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints succeeding without valid authentication tokens or sessions. Baseline normal authenticated access patterns; surface spike in anonymous requests or 401→200 transitions.

suggestion.title: Externally accessible Ivanti Sentry appliances
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' This is the core attack precondition—must identify exposed instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify HTTP/HTTPS connections to known Ivanti Sentry management ports (8443, 9443, or custom) from external networks. Cross-reference with asset inventory to flag unmanaged appliances. Alert on repeated external probing to Sentry-like service signatures.

suggestion.title: OS command injection payloads in Sentry requests
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Direct exploitation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints for shell metacharacters (backticks, $(), pipes, semicolons, &&, ||) in query parameters and POST bodies. Profile normal request patterns; shell syntax in external requests to Sentry is high-fidelity indicator of exploitation.

suggestion.title: Root-level process spawning from Sentry service account
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'achieve root-level remote code execution.' Confirms privilege escalation to root is the attack outcome.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child processes running as UID 0 (root) spawned by Ivanti Sentry service account. Flag shell interpreters (bash, sh, python, perl) or reverse shells with root privileges from Sentry process context.

suggestion.title: Post-exploitation command execution from compromised Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Root-level RCE grants full system control. Monitor for attacker tooling and lateral movement commands post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious commands (curl, wget, nc, whoami, cron edits) executed by or from Sentry service context. Monitor for outbound network connections from appliance to non-whitelisted external IPs. Alert on DNS queries to malicious domains from Sentry.

suggestion.title: Sentry appliance missing protective mTLS or restricted access
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors.' Identifies defensive gaps that enable exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan Ivanti Sentry deployments for absence of mTLS enforcement, missing enrollment in EPMM/Neurons for MDM, or lack of network-level access controls. Appliances without these controls are exploitable per the article.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability exploitable 'in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Detection must identify exposed instances before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor network perimeter logs and DNS resolvers for external access to Ivanti Sentry default management ports (443, 8443). Alert on successful external connections from untrusted IPs. Cross-reference with asset inventory to identify misconfigured exposed appliances requiring immediate network segmentation.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scanner Matches
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'CVE-2026-10520 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and specifies federal patch due date 2026-06-14. Vulnerability detection is primary prevention control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate vulnerability scanner output (Nessus, Qualys, Rapid7) for Ivanti Sentry instances against known vulnerable versions. Flag any Sentry systems with CVE-2026-10520 exposure. Prioritize for emergency patching given federal deadline and active exploitation status.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Execution from Sentry Services
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is 'OS command injection' enabling remote code execution. Attack chain requires observing command interpreter spawning from Sentry process context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation where parent process is Sentry service/daemon. Alert on unusual child processes (shells, interpreters, net* utilities, reverse shells) spawned from Sentry. Baseline normal Sentry behavior and flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Code Execution from Sentry Process
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'root-level remote code execution' as impact. Detection must identify privilege-context anomalies in Sentry execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation events where Sentry service spawns processes with UID/GID 0. Alert immediately on any root-context child processes from Sentry. Review historical logs for post-exploitation cleanup or persistence mechanisms.

suggestion.title: mTLS/Restricted HTTPS Access Control Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article notes that 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible.' Detection should flag bypass attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for TLS handshake failures, certificate validation errors, or HTTP (non-HTTPS) access attempts to Sentry management interfaces. Alert on TLS downgrade attempts or suspicious renegotiations that could indicate control-bypass attempts.

suggestion.title: Browser extension spawning system interpreter
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'chrome_tabs plugin...interpolates...' with AppleScript injection. Need detection for when browser or browser extension process directly spawns osascript or jxa/JavaScript interpreters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect browser processes (chrome, brave, edge) or Anyquery plugin spawning osascript/jxa without user-initiated script execution. Parent process = browser, child = osascript. Filter for unexpected context (not debugging console, not user approval dialog).

suggestion.title: Anyquery plugin instantiation with shell metacharacters in URL parameter
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'via Unescaped URL in macOS Chrome Plugin' — detection should hunt for plugin loading with URLs containing shell delimiters (backticks, $(), semicolons, pipes, do shell script keywords).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Anyquery or chrome_tabs plugin process instantiation where command line or URL parameters contain AppleScript keywords (tell application, do shell script, end tell) or shell metacharacters. Can be detected in browser process logs or extension-specific logging.

suggestion.title: Mismatched AppleScript control flow (tell/end tell mismatch)
suggestion.rationale: The vulnerability specifically leverages 'mismatched tell blocks' to break out of intended script context. This is a lower-volume but very high-fidelity pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Osascript invocations where the count of 'tell application' opens exceeds 'end tell' closes by ≥1, or where 'end tell' appears before corresponding 'tell application' (out of order). High confidence indicator of intentional breakout attempt.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Externally Reachable Ivanti Sentry Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability is 'exploitable in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' This is the necessary precondition; asset discovery is the first detection priority.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory all Ivanti Sentry instances (port 443/8443 typical). Flag those without mTLS/EPMM enrollment or restricted HTTPS access. Cross-reference external IP geolocation against corporate data-center ranges. Query vulnerability scanner for CVE-2026-10520 detections in unpatched instances.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection in Unauthenticated Ivanti Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability' exploitable by 'remote unauthenticated user.' Detection must focus on malformed payloads with shell syntax against Ivanti endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to Ivanti Sentry management/API endpoints for requests containing shell metacharacters (backticks, $(), pipe, semicolon, &&, ||) in query parameters or POST bodies. Flag unauthenticated requests (missing Authorization header, invalid/null tokens). Correlate request timing with subsequent network anomalies.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Child Process from Ivanti Service Account
suggestion.rationale: Article states exploit 'could allow remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Privilege escalation from web service context to uid=0 is the post-exploitation signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor process creation where PPID is Ivanti Sentry service process (java, node, or appliance-specific daemon) and child process UID is 0 or runs as nt authority\system. Flag shell execution (/bin/bash, /bin/sh, cmd.exe, powershell.exe) spawned from web service context. Review for curl/wget/nc post-exploitation artifacts.

suggestion.title: Authentication Bypass to Ivanti Sentry Admin Functions
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability requires unauthenticated access to protected endpoints. Detection should flag requests that skip or defeat authentication controls on known Ivanti API/admin paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry protected paths (/api/*, /admin, /manage) that lack valid session tokens, Authorization headers, or use null/placeholder credentials. Correlate with command-injection payload detection. Alert on rapid sequential requests from single source to multiple protected endpoints.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scanner Hits
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly references CVE-2026-10520; scanner output is the direct control for confirming exposure, patch status, and urgency (federal due date 2026-06-14 is imminent).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner (Nessus, Qualys, Tenable) for CVE-2026-10520 matches. Prioritize Critical/High findings. Inventory unpatched Ivanti Sentry versions. Cross-reference with network segmentation rules to confirm external reachability. Validate whether affected instances have mTLS/EPMM protections enabled per article mitigation guidance.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Appliance Log Exploitation Signatures
suggestion.rationale: Article references native Ivanti Sentry appliance logs as detection source (no explicit format given, but standard for managed appliances). Logs should record exploitation attempts and injection failures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Collect Ivanti Sentry appliance event logs. Search for authentication failures on protected endpoints, malformed API requests, stack traces indicating command-injection exception handling, or access-denied errors from unauthenticated source IPs. Correlate with network detection events for timing and source alignment.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs asset-exposure hunt: 'CVE: CVE-2026-10520 — match against your vulnerability scanner'. Standard patch-status detection for federal compliance deadline (2026-06-14).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and asset inventory for Ivanti Sentry instances (product = 'Ivanti Sentry' OR 'MobileIron Sentry') missing CVE-2026-10520 patches. Cross-reference against federal due date 2026-06-14 for compliance and audit readiness.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged + Externally Reachable Ivanti Sentry Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exploitation requires both conditions: 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable'. Single-control detection is insufficient; requires correlation of EMM status + network exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Ivanti Sentry devices flagged as unmanaged in EMM/MDM systems against external network reachability (port 443, standard Sentry management ports). Flag appliances meeting both conditions as exploitable.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload Detection - Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability mechanism is 'OS command injection'. Web/API logs for Sentry endpoints must be scanned for command execution patterns (shell metacharacters, substitution operators) in request parameters and bodies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to Ivanti Sentry management interfaces for OS command injection indicators: backticks, `$()`, pipes, semicolons, command operators (|&, &&, ||) in URI query parameters and POST data. Unauthenticated requests are high-confidence signals given the flaw's unauthenticated nature.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Without mTLS or Restricted HTTPS
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies protective controls: 'The use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors'. Detect absence of both controls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit Ivanti Sentry appliance TLS configurations for lack of client-certificate authentication (mTLS) and network access policies permitting unrestricted HTTPS. Appliances without both protections are exploitable from the internet.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Root RCE Activity from Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation achieves 'root-level remote code execution'. Detect process spawning, privilege escalation, or shell activity originating from Sentry service context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected process creation, privilege escalation, or interactive shells executing under Ivanti Sentry service identity (typically running as root pre-exploitation or as privileged service account post-exploitation). Include file-system modifications, new user creation, or lateral-movement connections from the appliance.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Remote Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'remote unauthenticated user' exploiting 'externally reachable' Sentry appliances. Pipeline generated zero use cases for initial compromise despite explicit external access vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to externally exposed Ivanti Sentry management interfaces. Alert on requests from untrusted networks exhibiting exploitation patterns: suspicious parameter injection, URI path traversal indicators, or request patterns consistent with known Sentry exploits.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Attack in Ivanti Sentry HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'OS command injection vulnerability'—the execution mechanism. Pipeline omitted execution-phase detections and failed to surface T1059.001 command injection patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect HTTP request payloads to Ivanti Sentry endpoints for shell metacharacters (;, |, &, backticks, $(), newlines) and command substitution syntax. Flag encoded or obfuscated payloads attempting command injection through HTTP parameters.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution on Ivanti Sentry Appliance
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'root-level remote code execution' as the attack outcome. Pipeline generated no detections for post-exploitation process execution or privilege escalation indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected processes spawned with UID 0 (root context) on Ivanti Sentry appliances following exploitation attempts or HTTP anomalies. Correlate with command injection detection and baseline normal root activities.

suggestion.title: Externally Exposed Unmanaged Ivanti Sentry Asset Discovery

Cross-reference against internal asset management to identify unmanaged instances or those without mTLS/restricted HTTPS protections mentioned as mitigations.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'vulnerability can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Mandatory asset-exposure hunt for T1190 execution path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory all Ivanti Sentry instances (product names matching 'Sentry' + 'Ivanti'/'MobileIron') listening on external interfaces. Correlate against patch baseline for CVE-2026-10520. Flag any unpatched instance reachable from non-RFC1918 sources on default ports 8080/8443.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection – Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520
suggestion.rationale: Article core attack vector: 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Direct detection requirement for exploit attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints for shell metacharacters (pipes, semicolons, command substitution $(), &&, ||) in query params, POST bodies, headers. Correlate with process spawning (bash, sh, nc) from Sentry service account.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated RCE – Root Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'remote unauthenticated user' achieving 'root-level remote code execution.' Privilege escalation from unprivileged service account to root requires process-level detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Ivanti Sentry service processes spawning shell interpreters (bash/sh/zsh) or system commands with elevated privileges (UID 0/SYSTEM). Correlation: trigger only when immediately preceded by external HTTP request (unauthenticated exploit attempt).

suggestion.title: mTLS Bypass / Restricted Interface Evasion
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible.' Detection required to identify evasion of these mitigations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry endpoints for: (1) HTTP requests to interfaces that should enforce HTTPS-only, (2) mTLS handshake failures followed by successful unauthenticated access, (3) certificate anomalies (missing, self-signed, CN mismatch).

suggestion.title: CISA KEV Patch Compliance – CVE-2026-10520
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'anything in CISA KEV is currently being exploited…Even if your scanners say "not vulnerable" because of patches, it's worth one quick check.' Federal due date 2026-06-14 requires compliance tracking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Automated compliance check: flag all Ivanti Sentry instances that are (1) installed, (2) externally reachable, (3) unpatched as of 2026-06-14. Include instances where scanner reports 'not vulnerable' but version history indicates unpatched code—scanner lag is a known risk.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Asset Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Externally-reachable instances are the prerequisite attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry or MobileIron Sentry appliances with internet-routable IPs and HTTPS access from untrusted IP ranges. Flag appliances in unmanaged state without mTLS, EPMM enrollment, or Neurons for MDM integration that restricts external access.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Command Injection Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes: 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to exposed Sentry endpoints for command injection payloads (shell metacharacters: semicolons, backticks, $(), pipes) in URL parameters or POST bodies. Alert on unauthenticated requests containing execution patterns.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation: Privileged Process Spawning from Sentry Daemon
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'achieve root-level remote code execution.' Captures the privilege escalation/impact outcome of successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation where parent process is Ivanti Sentry service spawning child processes with root privileges (UID 0). Flag shell invocations (sh, bash, command, system) originating from Sentry context; correlate with external HTTP requests.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Patch Compliance and Vulnerability Tracking
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry with federal due date 2026-06-14; compliance detection and residual-risk tracking are essential for federal and regulated environments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all Ivanti Sentry appliances in production. Track CVE-2026-10520 vulnerability scanner findings. Alert on unpatched instances, especially those externally reachable. Monitor patch deployment against federal due date and flag post-deadline non-compliance.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unmanaged Appliance with External Reachability
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable'—this is the primary exposure condition.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances in unmanaged state with management interfaces accessible from untrusted networks. Monitor asset inventory for missing mTLS configuration or HTTPS restrictions. Prioritize appliances without VPN/IP whitelisting on management ports.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution'—the core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry API and web endpoints for command-injection payloads (backticks, $(...), semicolons, pipe characters) in HTTP requests from unauthenticated sources. Correlate with HTTP 5xx errors or application exceptions to flag exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Root-Level Process Execution from Sentry Service
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation directly grants 'root-level remote code execution'; any child process spawned by Sentry service running as root indicates successful compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes spawned by Sentry/sentry-api service running as root or SYSTEM. Baseline normal service behavior; flag unexpected system tools (sh, bash, curl, wget, python) invoked from Sentry context or working directories.

suggestion.title: Disabled or Downgraded mTLS/HTTPS Protection on Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible'—disabling these re-exposes the appliance to exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry appliance configuration changes for disabled mTLS enforcement, downgrade to plaintext HTTP, removal of IP restrictions, or modification of EPMM/Neurons integration settings that weaken access controls.

suggestion.title: Credential/API Key Extraction from Compromised Sentry Appliance
suggestion.rationale: Root-level RCE enables pivoting; Sentry appliances typically store credentials and API keys for downstream endpoint management—high-value targets for lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for extraction or enumeration of Sentry configuration files, credential stores, database files, or environment variables containing API tokens. Alert on authentication attempts using Sentry service account credentials on unrelated systems.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Ivanti Sentry Version Not Patched by Due Date
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies federal patch due-date 2026-06-14 and CISA KEV designation implies active wild exploitation—version inventory is the first detection layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory and vulnerability scans for Ivanti Sentry instances running versions prior to the published patch date or known-vulnerable versions. Cross-reference with network exposure data; flag externally-reachable vulnerable appliances for immediate escalation.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry internet-facing asset inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Detection of exposed Ivanti Sentry instances without mTLS or HTTPS restrictions is the prerequisite hunt for this CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for internet-routable Ivanti Sentry appliances (port 8443 or known Sentry service ports) with inbound connections from untrusted/external ASNs. Correlate with vulnerability scanner data to identify unpatched instances as of 2026-06-14.

suggestion.title: OS command injection attempts against Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user.' Detect HTTP POST/GET requests containing shell metacharacters or command-injection payloads targeting known Ivanti Sentry endpoint paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints containing shell command operators (;, |, &&, `, $, backticks) or known command-injection payloads. Baseline against legitimate administrative traffic and filter by destination port/path specific to Sentry.

suggestion.title: Process spawning from Ivanti Sentry service context
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'root-level remote code execution.' After command injection, the attacker executes OS commands in the context of the Ivanti Sentry process, which should not normally spawn child processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected parent processes matching Ivanti Sentry service names (ivanti-sentry, mobileIron-sentry, etc.) spawning cmd.exe, bash, sh, or PowerShell child processes. Establish baseline of legitimate administrative child processes; flag deviations as exploitation.

suggestion.title: Privilege escalation from Ivanti Sentry network service context
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'root-level remote code execution.' Detect privilege escalation techniques originating from the Ivanti Sentry service process, which typically runs as a service account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on privilege escalation events (sudo, UAC elevation, setuid, etc.) initiated by Ivanti Sentry service processes or their child processes. Cross-reference with failed authentication logs to identify exploitation attempts vs. legitimate administrative activity.

suggestion.title: Reverse shell or data exfiltration from Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'root-level remote code execution' implies post-exploitation impact. Detect C2 beacons or data exfiltration initiated from the compromised appliance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor network connections originating from Ivanti Sentry appliance IPs to suspicious external destinations (high-entropy domains, known C2 infrastructure, Tor exit nodes). Baseline against legitimate administrative outbound traffic.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry configuration tampering post-exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes appliance behavior in 'unmanaged state.' Post-exploitation, attacker may disable mTLS enforcement, weaken HTTPS restrictions, or modify enrollment policies to maintain access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on changes to Ivanti Sentry security settings (mTLS certificates, HTTPS policies, enrollment profiles, API access controls) without corresponding change-control ticket. Correlate with process-execution detections to identify attacker-initiated changes vs. legitimate administration.

suggestion.title: Externally Reachable Ivanti Sentry Appliance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Asset exposure is the primary detection vector for initial access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Ivanti Sentry appliances (via banner grab, asset inventory tags, or certificate fingerprinting) reachable from untrusted networks.
