suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected shell process spawning (bash, sh, cmd.exe) under the Ivanti Sentry service account, especially with root/SYSTEM privileges. Correlate with suspicious web server access logs from same time window.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Ivanti Sentry Instance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states CVE-2026-10520 'can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable' — asset exposure hunting is the foundational mitigation. Article references `_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure` directly.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all Ivanti Sentry instances (ports 443, 8443) in network traffic and asset inventory. Cross-reference against vulnerability scanner for CVE-2026-10520 presence. Alert on externally-reachable Sentry appliances. Correlate with absence of mTLS (EPMM) or restricted HTTPS controls.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation Payloads
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution' — exploitation attempts must be caught in request payloads and response anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to Ivanti Sentry endpoints for OS command metacharacters (pipe, semicolon, backticks, command substitution). Alert on anomalous parameter injection patterns. Review web server logs for 200/exec responses or error conditions following suspicious POST requests.

suggestion.title: Successful Unauthenticated RCE on Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'remote unauthenticated user' and 'root-level remote code execution' — successful exploitation should produce root-level process spawning or command output from Sentry without prior authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry appliance audit/syslog for root-level command execution or privilege escalation events. Alert on unexpected root processes spawned by network-facing Sentry daemons. Correlate with unauthenticated network connections.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Persistence from Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Once root RCE is achieved ('root-level remote code execution'), adversaries install persistence — cron jobs, backdoors, or reverse shells from the compromised appliance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for writes to /etc/cron*, /etc/init.d, /usr/lib, or ld.so.preload from Sentry processes. Alert on unexpected child processes (bash, sh, python, nc) spawned by Sentry network daemons. Monitor for outbound C2 connections or reverse shells from Sentry IPs.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Sentry MDM Channels
suggestion.rationale: Ivanti Sentry is endpoint management software (formerly MobileIron) — a compromised appliance can propagate to managed endpoints. Article mentions 'EPMM' (Ivanti Endpoint Manager Mobile) and 'Neurons for MDM', implying managed device population.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry-to-endpoint communication channels for anomalous commands or policy pushes. Alert on Sentry appliance pivoting to internal networks (scanning, credential collection). Track endpoint enrollment requests from compromised Sentry appliances.

suggestion.title: Patch Gap Analysis — CVE-2026-10520 Unpatched Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' with explicit federal due date (2026-06-14). Identifying unpatched versions is foundational risk quantification. Article's template explicitly instructs `Substitute this CVE wherever the template references <CVE>`.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for Ivanti Sentry appliances and extract version/build info from banner grabbing or management API. Query Nessus/Qualys/Rapid7 for CVE-2026-10520 matches. Alert on any unpatched instances post-2026-06-14 deadline. Track version drift across fleet.

suggestion.title: External Ivanti Sentry Appliance Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is exploitable 'in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable' — core attack surface detection missing entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for externally-reachable Ivanti Sentry appliances via port/service enumeration or certificate transparency lookups. Cross-reference with vulnerability scanner to identify instances unpatched for CVE-2026-10520 running in unmanaged state (no mTLS enrollment).

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Against Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'OS command injection vulnerability' as the attack mechanism — payload patterns attempting shell metacharacter injection should be detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry endpoints for shell metacharacters (|, ;, &&, backticks, $()) in HTTP request parameters/bodies. Alert on payloads containing command substitution syntax or pipeline operators targeting known vulnerable endpoints.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Code Execution from Ivanti Sentry Appliance
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes attackers achieve 'root-level remote code execution' — post-exploitation process activity from appliance should be hunted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for root-spawned processes on Ivanti Sentry appliances with suspicious command-line arguments, child processes indicative of post-exploitation (shells, tunneling tools), or unusual outbound network connections initiated by system-level processes.

suggestion.title: mTLS/HTTPS Restriction Bypass Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access' mitigates exploitation — attempts to bypass or validate these controls are missing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for TLS handshake failures, invalid certificate chains, or HTTP requests against Ivanti Sentry endpoints expecting mTLS. Flag connections from non-EPMM-enrolled endpoints or attempts bypassing HTTPS restriction layers.

suggestion.title: Post-Deadline Unpatched Sentry Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and federal due date 2026-06-14 — patching gap post-deadline is the primary risk indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query patch management for Ivanti Sentry appliances with CVE-2026-10520 unpatched after 2026-06-14 deadline. Correlate with network reachability scans to identify instances that are both vulnerable and externally accessible.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Externally Reachable — Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'vulnerability can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Pipeline missed baseline exposure hunt—critical for CISA KEV follow-up.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry instances (port scan, product identification) accessible from untrusted networks. Correlate with vulnerability scanner data confirming absence of patched version post-2026-06-14 deadline.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation — Ivanti Sentry RCE
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Pipeline failed to surface execution detection for injected shell commands.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry process lineage for unexpected shell spawning (sh, bash, cmd) or system command execution with high privilege context. Baseline normal Sentry CLI activity and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation to Root — Ivanti Sentry Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'achieve root-level remote code execution' — pipeline did not decompose the privilege escalation component of the RCE impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process execution under root context initiated from Ivanti Sentry service account or from network-facing service handlers. Flag UID/GID elevation anomalies correlated with CVE-2026-10520 exploitation window.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged Ivanti Sentry Configuration Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state' — this configuration prerequisite should be detected before exploitation occurs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Ivanti Sentry instances for unmanaged state flags in config; check absence of mTLS enrollment, EPMM integration, or Neurons for MDM policy enforcement. Cross-reference with network accessibility assessment.

suggestion.title: Typo-Squatted Go Module Import Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies attack vector: 'The malicious Go Module Mirror's was named github.com/botdb-go/bolt, similar to the original one i.e. github.com/boltdb/bolt.' Typo squatting is the entry point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor go.mod imports and package resolution for module names phonetically or orthographically similar to known popular packages. Flag imports of 'botdb-go/bolt' or single-character/prefix-swap variants of boltdb/bolt. Cross-reference against official Go registry.

suggestion.title: Installation of Malicious BoltDB v1.3.1
suggestion.rationale: Article names malicious artifact: 'The harmful version (1.3.1) was released on GitHub in November 2021' and 'developers to update the version that stayed in the system for 3 years.' Version 1.3.1 from botdb-go/bolt is forensically actionable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on installation or go.mod pinning of github.com/botdb-go/bolt version 1.3.1 or of boltdb/bolt v1.3.1 from non-canonical sources. Correlate against GO-2025-3451 and SNYK-GOLANG-GITHUBCOMBOLTDBGOBOLT-868841.

suggestion.title: C2 Backdoor Communication from BoltDB-Using Process
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'This backdoor allows hackers to remotely control infected computers through a server that sends them commands i.e. via a command and control server.' C2 communication is the explicit impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline BoltDB process network behavior. Flag unexpected outbound connections (HTTP/S, DNS queries) from processes importing malicious botdb-go/bolt. Monitor for beaconing patterns and unusual external domain resolution.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Compromise — Malicious Module Persistence via Proxy Cache
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies persistence mechanism: 'Go Module Mirror's indefinite caching of modules kicked in, and that cached the backdored module.' The module remained available for 3 years post-removal: 'Go Module Proxy, which continued to serve clients.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit local Go module caches and proxy logs for presence of archived botdb-go/bolt or revoked package versions. Flag go.mod/go.sum entries pinned to version 1.3.1 or checksums mismatched against official registries.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Dependency Resolution from Non-Canonical Go Registry
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'The malicious Go Module Mirror's was named github.com/botdb-go/bolt' implying it was hosted separately; attackers exploited 'how Go manages and caches its modules' — non-canonical source resolution is an anomaly.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Log and monitor Go build operations and module-fetch requests. Flag resolution of BoltDB or similar database-tool imports from repositories not on the official pkg.go.dev registry or unvetted mirrors.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Version Jump or Lateral Update to Malicious BoltDB
suggestion.rationale: Article highlights that 'we now wish to update our systems to the latest dependencies, which led developers to update the version that stayed in the system for 3 years' — update-driven activation is the reinfection vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor dependency update operations (go get -u, go mod tidy). Alert on updates to BoltDB variants that result in pulling v1.3.1 or other flagged versions. Correlate timestamp of update with deployment of C2 activity.

suggestion.title: Exposed Ivanti Sentry Appliance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability exploitable 'where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Network exposure to untrusted sources is the enabling precondition.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory Ivanti Sentry appliances and detect instances with external network reachability or missing mTLS/Neurons for MDM integration. Cross-reference unmanaged appliances against asset DB. Alert on inbound HTTPS to Sentry endpoints from untrusted source IPs.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Attack on Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'OS command injection vulnerability' enabling 'root-level remote code execution' from unauthenticated remote users. Core exploitation mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry process logs for shell spawning (sh, bash) from web service contexts or with suspicious parent-child relationships. Inspect HTTP request logs for injection payloads: pipe characters, semicolons, backticks, $() syntax in Sentry endpoint parameters.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation to Root on Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability enables 'root-level remote code execution.' Successful exploitation results in appliance-wide compromise with highest privilege level.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes executing with UID 0 (root) spawned from non-privileged service accounts or web application contexts on Ivanti Sentry. Monitor auditd/sudo logs for unexpected privilege transitions on vulnerable appliance versions.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged Ivanti Sentry Appliance Configuration
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability only 'successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state.' Unmanaged state directly enables exploitation path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit Ivanti Sentry fleet for management state. Flag instances missing EPMM/Neurons for MDM integration, unreporting to management server, or lacking expected management beacons. Correlate unmanaged + externally reachable = highest risk.

suggestion.title: Missing mTLS/HTTPS Restriction on Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors.' Absence of these controls leaves exploitation path open.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate Ivanti Sentry appliances and validate mTLS certificate configuration + Neurons for MDM enrollment. Identify instances configured for plaintext HTTP or without client certificate validation. Prioritize remediation of internet-exposed instances.

suggestion.title: Successful Unauthenticated Access to Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'remote unauthenticated user' can exploit. Detection of successful auth-bypass or unauthenticated successful requests indicates exploitation attempt or compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP 200/302 responses to Ivanti Sentry endpoints from external IPs without prior authentication events. Establish baseline of expected authenticated vs. unauthenticated access patterns. Flag deviations or successful requests without auth context.

suggestion.title: Sentry Appliance External Network Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability is exploitable when 'appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable' and mitigations include 'mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access.' This is the foundational asset-exposure hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances reachable from external/non-RFC1918 sources. Correlate with absence of mTLS enforcement, TLS certificate validation, or EPMM/Neurons MDM enrollment flags. Flag appliances in 'unmanaged state' (missing enrollment telemetry).

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempts to Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability explicitly named as 'OS command injection vulnerability.' No detection for the attack vector itself—shell metacharacters and encoded payloads in API requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP/REST API requests to Sentry services containing shell metacharacters (backticks, pipes, semicolons, &&, ||, $()) or URL-encoded variants (%24, %26, %7C, %3B) in query parameters, headers, or POST bodies. Baseline legitimate Sentry API calls and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution from Sentry Daemon
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'root-level remote code execution' as the impact. Post-exploitation detection should flag unexpected privileged process spawning from normally-limited Sentry service account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation with parent = Sentry service binary executing shell commands (cmd.exe, /bin/sh, /bin/bash) with SYSTEM/root privileges. Flag unexpected child processes: reverse shells, downloaders, lateral-movement tools. Monitor for execution binaries absent from baseline Sentry process tree.

suggestion.title: Sentry Appliance Enrollment and Configuration State Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'unmanaged state' as the prerequisite for exploitation. Detection should track absence of MDM enrollment, mTLS setup, or expected hardening telemetry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor fleet for Sentry appliances not enrolled in EPMM or Neurons for MDM. Alert on absence of mTLS certificate installation, disabled TLS enforcement, or unencrypted management interface (HTTP vs HTTPS). Correlate config gaps with external reachability findings.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised Sentry Appliance
suggestion.rationale: Successful RCE on a network appliance typically precedes lateral movement. Article does not describe, but post-compromise activity is a predictable detection opportunity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for scanning, brute-force (SMB, SSH), or credential-spraying originating from compromised Sentry appliance IP. Flag unexpected outbound connections to databases, credential stores, or non-whitelisted infrastructure. Alert on authentication failures followed by successful login from compromised appliance.

suggestion.title: Sentry Binary or Service Persistence Artifacts
suggestion.rationale: Root-level code execution enables attackable persistence mechanisms via binary modification, cron jobs, or systemd hijacking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthorized modifications to Sentry binaries, shared libraries, or startup scripts (setuid/setgid changes). Alert on unexpected cron jobs or systemd timers created under Sentry service account UID. Track Sentry service restarts with modified binary hashes or invalid signatures.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scanning — Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article directs: 'Standard asset-exposure hunt...Substitute this CVE wherever the template references <CVE>: CVE-2026-10520.' Pipeline ignored this direct guidance and generated no use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search vulnerability scanner inventory for Ivanti Sentry appliances flagged vulnerable to CVE-2026-10520. Cross-reference federal patch due-date (2026-06-14) to identify patch lag. Article notes patch absence even when scanner says 'not vulnerable' is worth checking—flag unpatched instances.

suggestion.title: Externally-Reachable Ivanti Sentry Appliance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is exploitable only 'in cases where Sentry appliance is in unmanaged state with endpoints externally reachable.' External exposure is the enabling condition; missing detection for this prerequisite.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate Ivanti Sentry appliances from inventory and correlate with network reachability data. Identify any instance with external (non-RFC1918) network paths to management interface. Flag as high-risk exposure; article notes mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS through Neurons for MDM mitigates—check if those controls exist.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated HTTP Requests to Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'remote unauthenticated user' can exploit. Detection must distinguish unauthenticated access attempts to Sentry appliances from legitimate authenticated traffic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS access logs to Ivanti Sentry appliance IPs for requests that lack valid authentication tokens/sessions. Baseline legitimate unauthenticated endpoints (e.g., status pages) to reduce false positives. Look for request patterns targeting known vulnerable functions or endpoints.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation of Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies vulnerability as 'OS command injection' enabling 'root-level remote code execution.' Pipeline missed the execution phase and command-level detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for shell/command interpreter processes spawned by Ivanti Sentry service account with root privileges (UID 0). Correlate process events with inbound HTTP traffic to Sentry appliance to detect exploitation in-flight. Look for sh, bash, python, or other interpreter spawns unlikely in normal Sentry operations.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Persistence on Compromised Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Root RCE capability (article's stated outcome) is typically weaponized for persistence. Detection should cover backdoor installation, scheduled task creation, or account creation post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt Ivanti Sentry appliance file system and cron/scheduled-task repositories for unauthorized entries created after suspected exploitation window. Ivanti logs should show admin or unusual account creation post-compromise. File modification timestamps on /etc/cron.d or appliance startup paths should be baseline-checked.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised Ivanti Sentry Appliance
suggestion.rationale: Root access on a network appliance (Sentry's typical role) enables pivot to internal assets. Article mentions mTLS and network controls—compromised Sentry can bypass those. Missing detection for east-west exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After root RCE on Ivanti Sentry is suspected, monitor for unusual outbound network traffic from appliance to internal subnets (connections to RFC1918 ranges not in baseline). Look for SSH, WinRM, LDAP queries, or other lateral movement protocols originating from Sentry with timing aligned to exploitation attempt.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Exposure Scan
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable' as the exploitation precondition. This is asset-exposure hunting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for inbound connections to Ivanti Sentry default ports (443, 8443) from external/untrusted ASNs or unexpected source IP ranges. Correlate with vulnerability scanner reports for CVE-2026-10520 to identify exposed instances requiring immediate mitigation.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploit Attempts Against Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'OS command injection vulnerability' allowing 'remote unauthenticated user' exploitation. Detection of injection payloads is critical.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints containing OS command metacharacters (backticks, pipe, semicolon, $(), &&, ||) in query parameters or POST bodies. Correlate with unauthenticated session context. High-signal indicators: attempts to invoke root-privileged utilities (sudo, chmod, iptables).

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation: Unexpected Process Execution from Sentry Service Account
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes that successful exploitation results in 'root-level remote code execution.' Detection of unexpected child processes from Sentry service is critical post-compromise indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation with parent=Sentry service (or Java/container runtime executing Sentry) spawning shells, curl/wget, or reverse shells. Flag any execution in root context; normal operation should be constrained. Suspicious children: bash, sh, nc, wget downloading payloads.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Service Restart or Anomalous Log Truncation
suggestion.rationale: Attackers exploiting root-level RCE often cover tracks by restarting services or clearing logs. Article implies data destruction capability via 'root-level' access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected Ivanti Sentry service restarts, especially during or immediately after external connection activity. Correlate with log file size reductions or deletion of application/system logs in Sentry directories (audit trail destruction). Cross-check service logs with Windows/Linux event logs for corroboration.

suggestion.title: mTLS Bypass or Restricted HTTPS Circumvention
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible' — detecting disable/bypass of these mitigations signals compromise of controls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry configuration or certificate logs for removal/modification of mTLS enforcement, HTTPS certificate pinning, or MDM policy restrictions. Alert on downgrade from mTLS to plaintext communication. Flag configuration changes to Sentry appliance outside of scheduled maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised Sentry to Downstream MDM/EPMM Systems
suggestion.rationale: Sentry is an endpoint management appliance with visibility into organizational mobile devices and management endpoints. Root-level compromise creates lateral movement pivot point to MDM/EPMM infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After detecting Ivanti Sentry compromise, hunt for outbound connections from Sentry to EPMM/MDM backends (MobileIron, VMware UEM, Microsoft Intune APIs) with suspicious payloads or authentication anomalies. Monitor for mass enrollment/unenrollment of mobile devices or policy push campaigns, which would indicate lateral movement exploitation.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520 Asset Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'vulnerability can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable'—core detection requirement is identifying exposed instances
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect externally accessible Ivanti Sentry instances through network scanning, SSL certificate discovery, or external service enumeration. Flag unmanaged Sentry deployments lacking mTLS/EPMM protection as high-risk.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user'—detect exploitation payloads in HTTP requests to Sentry endpoints
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints for shell metacharacters, command substitution syntax, or known CVE-2026-10520 payload indicators in query parameters or POST body.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Successful RCE Execution (Post-Exploitation)
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes exploitation 'achieve[s] root-level remote code execution'—detect successful exploitation through abnormal command execution patterns
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After successful exploitation, look for unusual process execution on Ivanti Sentry appliances, particularly commands executed with root/system privileges, shell spawning, or attempts to modify system configuration.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unmanaged State Configuration Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability exploitable 'in cases where Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state' and notes protection via 'mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access'—detect vulnerable configurations
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Sentry instances not enrolled in EPMM management or lacking mTLS certificate pinning. Check HTTPS access logs for absence of expected EPMM authentication headers or client certificate validation.

suggestion.title: Unpatched CVE-2026-10520 Ivanti Sentry Inventory Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states direct RCE risk via 'OS command injection vulnerability.' Pipeline must surface vulnerable product versions in scanners. No version bounds provided in article but federal patch-due date of 2026-06-14 anchors the urgency.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Ivanti Sentry appliances in vulnerability scanner output where version < patched release. Prioritize instances flagged as 'unmanaged' or those without mTLS/restricted HTTPS enforcement per vendor mitigation guidance.

suggestion.title: Externally Exposed Ivanti Sentry Appliances Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'vulnerability can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' External exposure is the enabling precondition—must hunt network presence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry instances with public/WAN-facing IP addresses or DNS entries. Cross-correlate with asset inventory to confirm unmanaged deployments. Flag absence of mTLS-EPMM or restricted Neurons-for-MDM configurations as high-risk.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payloads Against Sentry Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability' as the attack mechanism. Detection must capture malicious input patterns—shell metacharacters, command substitution—in traffic to Sentry services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic destined for Ivanti Sentry services for payloads containing command injection metacharacters: backticks, $(), |, ;, &&, ||, etc. Originating from external/untrusted sources is critical. Correlate with 401/403 errors indicating unauthenticated access attempts.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Command Execution from Sentry Process Context
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exploitation achieves 'root-level remote code execution.' Post-compromise detection must identify unexpected root-privilege commands spawned by or within the Sentry appliance context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On Ivanti Sentry appliances, alert on process creation where UID=0 (root), PPID traces to Sentry service, and child processes are unexpected binaries (bash, sh, curl, wget, nc, ncat). Inspect command line for encoded payloads or suspicious redirections.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement and Data Collection from Compromised Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Compromised unmanaged Sentry appliances (per article context) are internal infrastructure with network access. Detection must flag pivot attempts—outbound connections to unexpected destinations, credential-access tools, persistence mechanisms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from Sentry IPs to unexpected internal subnets or external IP ranges. Flag DNS queries from Sentry for C2 domains. Alert on execution of post-exploitation tools (impacket, ncat, systemd-analyze) from Sentry process tree.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerable Asset Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2026-10520' and recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt.' Vulnerability scanner and agent inventory are the baseline detection for any KEV entry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any Ivanti Sentry appliances in vulnerability scanner or endpoint inventory as matching CVE-2026-10520. Cross-reference inventory for version/patch status against Ivanti advisories. Asset is high-priority if exposed to untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: Externally Exposed Ivanti Sentry Appliances
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Public exposure is the prerequisite for exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry instances (port/service fingerprints, SSL certs, HTTP headers) with inbound access from untrusted IP ranges. Cross-reference against firewall/WAF rules; flag if reachable from internet without authentication enforcement or mTLS restrictions.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unmanaged State Configuration
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly restricts exploitability: 'This vulnerability can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state.' Appliances with EPMM/Neurons for MDM mTLS or restricted HTTPS are protected; unmanaged ones are exposed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Sentry configuration (via API or admin console logs) to identify appliances NOT enrolled in EPMM or Neurons for MDM. Flag unmanaged appliances, especially those also meeting 'externally reachable' criteria from previous hunt.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload Delivery to Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability.' Exploitation requires sending crafted payloads to trigger code execution. Web proxies, WAF, and IDS should log injection attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for HTTP requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints containing shell metacharacters (|, ;, $(), backticks, >, <, &) in URL params or POST bodies. Prioritize requests without authentication headers. IDS/WAF vendors may have Sentry-specific injection signatures.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution from Ivanti Sentry Service
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability allows 'root-level remote code execution.' Successful exploitation will spawn processes with root/SYSTEM privileges originating from the Sentry process or service account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor process creation events where parent is Ivanti Sentry service/daemon and child process runs as UID 0 (root). Unexpected shell spawning (sh, bash) from Sentry with elevated privileges is high-confidence exploitation.

suggestion.title: mTLS/Restricted HTTPS Bypass Attempts Against Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article states mitigations include 'mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access.' Adversaries may attempt to bypass these controls via direct HTTP, certificate spoofing, or HTTPS downgrade.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unencrypted HTTP requests to Sentry admin/API endpoints; flag HTTPS connections with invalid/expired certs or cert mismatches. Monitor for repeated connection attempts to Sentry after mTLS enforcement; patterns suggest bypass probing.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Ivanti Sentry (CVE-2026-10520)

suggestion.title: Malicious URL with embedded AppleScript syntax in browser navigation

suggestion.title: Detect OS Command Injection Exploitation on Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'OS command injection vulnerability' as the exploitation vector enabling RCE. No execution-phase detection suggested despite explicit attack mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry application request logs and process execution for shell metacharacters (pipe, backtick, $(), semicolon) in HTTP request parameters or unexpected child process spawns from Sentry daemon. Baseline benign application activity to distinguish exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Detect Root-Level RCE and Post-Exploitation Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'achieve root-level remote code execution.' Impact-phase detection absent despite explicit outcome statement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process execution with UID=0 or equivalent elevated context originating from Ivanti Sentry service accounts. Flag unexpected binary execution, script interpreters, or network utilities launched post-exploitation. Correlate timing with external network connections.

suggestion.title: Verify Unpatched Ivanti Sentry Despite Scanner False Negatives
suggestion.rationale: Article warns 'patch lag is the silent killer' and states 'Federal civilian agencies are required to remediate by the published due date.' No hunt for patch-gap false negatives generated despite explicit remediation deadline (2026-06-14).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for scanner false negatives: Ivanti Sentry instances reporting 'patched' in automated scans but actually vulnerable. Validate via banner grabs, version strings from application logs, or attempted exploitation patterns. Flag discrepancies for remediation verification.

suggestion.title: Network Exposure: Ivanti Sentry Appliance Internet-Facing
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability is exploitable 'in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' This is the precondition for attack — detection should hunt for exposed instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for inbound HTTPS/HTTP traffic to Ivanti Sentry appliances (identify via certificates, HTTP response headers 'Server: Sentry', or known Sentry endpoint paths). Correlate against internal asset inventory; flag endpoints with external routing and unmanaged enrollment status.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Attempt: OS Command Injection Payloads to Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability' allowing RCE. Detection should identify exploitation attempts targeting the command injection vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints for command injection patterns: backtick execution ($(...) or `...`), shell metacharacters (;, |, &, newlines), or common command substitution in query params, POST bodies, or headers. Flag requests from untrusted networks or lacking authentication tokens.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation: Root-Level Process Spawning from Sentry Service
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states capability to 'achieve root-level remote code execution.' Detection should identify successful exploitation by monitoring for unexpected privilege escalation and command execution under Sentry process context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On Ivanti Sentry appliances (Linux-based), identify child processes spawned by the Sentry service with effective UID 0 (root). Alert on suspicious process names (bash, sh, nc, curl spawned from Sentry daemon). Correlate with web access logs to Sentry endpoints within 5-10 second window.

suggestion.title: Configuration Audit: Sentry Missing mTLS/EPMM Enrollment
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability is *not* exploitable when 'The use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access' is in place. Detection should identify appliances lacking these mitigations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit Ivanti Sentry appliance enrollment status: flag instances in 'unmanaged' state, lacking mTLS certificate binding, not enrolled in EPMM (if expected), or running without HTTPS restriction ACLs. Parse Sentry config endpoints or agent-reported compliance status.

suggestion.title: Legacy Product Name Correlation: MobileIron Sentry Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'Ivanti Sentry (formerly known as MobileIron Sentry)' — legacy systems and unmanaged devices may still be tracked under old product name. Detection scope must include both names to avoid false negatives.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In asset inventory and vulnerability scanner output, correlate CVE-2026-10520 against both 'Ivanti Sentry' AND 'MobileIron Sentry' product names. Flag any instances identified under legacy name as high-priority remediation, as they may be shadow/unmanaged devices.

suggestion.title: External Exposure of Ivanti Sentry Management Interfaces
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes precondition: 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Externally reachable + unmanaged state = exploitable. Detection of this condition is foundational.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances reachable from external networks (validate against asset inventory, Shodan/Censys queries, external port scans). Cross-reference with vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-10520 presence. Flag instances without mTLS or restricted HTTPS access controls as immediately exploitable.

suggestion.title: Patch Compliance Gap for CVE-2026-10520
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes federal patch due date (2026-06-14, 3 days from publication). Explicitly states 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Patch status is the primary defense mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and patch management systems for Ivanti Sentry instances showing CVE-2026-10520 in 'not patched' status post-due-date (2026-06-14). Correlate patch deployment timestamps against federal due date. Alert on compliance gaps and escalate to remediation teams.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempts Against Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploitation vector: 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Direct detection of injection payloads in requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry HTTP logs and WAF for requests containing shell metacharacters (;, |, &, $(…), backticks, >, <) or known command injection payloads targeting API endpoints. Correlate with IDS/IPS alerts for 'command injection' signatures. Escalate on response codes 200/204 (successful execution) for incident investigation.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated API Access to Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies threat model: 'remote unauthenticated user' can exploit the vulnerability. Successful requests without authentication bypass built-in access controls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry API logs for HTTP 200/204 responses to unauthenticated requests (absent auth tokens, mTLS certs). Identify patterns: 401/403 attempts followed by successful 200 responses from same source IP, indicating auth bypass. Flag external source IPs with successful unauthenticated requests.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution on Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article describes successful exploitation outcome: 'achieve root-level remote code execution.' Detection of unexpected privileged processes indicates post-exploitation execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry host system and process logs for child processes spawned as root/SYSTEM from web server processes (e.g., Sentry web service). Alert on unexpected privileged process parents, modifications to /etc, /var, /opt directories. Correlate timing with web request logs to establish causality.

suggestion.title: Exposed Ivanti Sentry Appliance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable'—the attack surface prerequisite.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Asset exposure hunt: identify Ivanti Sentry instances (product identifier + common service ports) responding to external networks. Flag unmanaged appliances lacking mTLS or restricted HTTPS controls. Cross-reference against CVE-2026-10520 patch status.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Command Injection Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP(S) requests to Ivanti Sentry instances for command injection payloads (backticks, $(), pipes, semicolons in URL parameters or POST data) from external IPs. Correlate with unexpected process spawning or shell invocation on Sentry systems.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Root-Level Process Execution on Sentry Systems
suggestion.rationale: 'Root-level remote code execution' indicates privilege escalation as the impact condition.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry hosts for command execution with root/system privileges, especially unexpected shell spawning or interpreter invocation initiated from network interfaces. Any root-context process spawned from external network source is high fidelity.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Patch Compliance Hunting
suggestion.rationale: Federal patch due-date is 2026-06-14; article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and this is CISA KEV (active in-the-wild exploitation).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Continuous scanning for Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520 patch status across fleet. Prioritize externally-reachable unpatched instances. Alert on any systems past the federal due-date without compensating controls (mTLS, restricted HTTPS).

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states Sentry is 'exploitable in cases where the appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' No asset-exposure UC generated despite template reference in article.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Ivanti Sentry instances responding on public internet-facing IPs/ports. Cross-reference network discovery logs and YARA signatures against known Sentry HTTP/HTTPS response patterns. Prioritize unmanaged appliances lacking mTLS, EPMM, or Neurons MDM integration.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner Detection of CVE-2026-10520
suggestion.rationale: Article warns 'patch lag is the silent killer' and references checking scanners against CVE. No UC for detecting persistent vulnerability positives for this CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scanner results (Qualys, Tenable, etc.) reporting CVE-2026-10520 present on any Ivanti Sentry asset post-federal due date (2026-06-14). Escalate if scanner shows confidence match and patch is not applied.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempts on Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'OS command injection vulnerability' as attack vector. No UC for detecting exploitation attempts via malformed HTTP payloads to Sentry endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints for OS command injection patterns (backticks, $(), pipes, semicolons, command substitution). Cross-reference with WAF/proxy logs. Baseline against known maintenance traffic.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution Following Sentry Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'root-level remote code execution' as outcome. No UC for detecting post-exploitation activity such as unusual root-context commands spawned from Sentry service.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On Ivanti Sentry appliances, hunt for process execution showing root-context commands spawned from sentry service context: reverse shells, package managers (apt/yum), cryptominers, lateral movement tools, data exfiltration utilities.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Without Protective Controls
suggestion.rationale: Article notes mTLS, EPMM, and 'Neurons for MDM' restrict access and mitigate exploitation. No UC for identifying Sentry deployments lacking these protections despite exposure risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for Ivanti Sentry instances lacking documented mTLS, EPMM integration, or restricted access controls. Cross-reference with network telemetry showing inbound connectivity from untrusted subnets.

suggestion.title: Post-Patch Compliance for Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies federal patch due date of 2026-06-14 with active exploitation ongoing. No UC for compliance-based detection of unpatched systems post-deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-June-14-2026, generate daily report of Ivanti Sentry instances not patched against CVE-2026-10520. Escalate any instance unpatched 7+ days past deadline as mandatory incident; trigger IR workflow.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure Hunt: Externally-Reachable Ivanti Sentry Appliances
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability only exploitable 'in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable'—this is the foundational prerequisite for exploitation and requires immediate discovery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan external address space for Ivanti Sentry HTTPS services using banner identification. Cross-reference against asset management to identify unmanaged instances. Flag any Sentry appliance reachable from untrusted networks for immediate network segmentation and vulnerability assessment.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner Alert for CVE-2026-10520
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'match against your vulnerability scanner.' CISA KEV mandate requires rapid fleet-wide assessment; federal due date 2026-06-14 provides enforceable remediation timeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Generate high-priority alerts for Ivanti Sentry appliances identified as vulnerable to CVE-2026-10520 by automated scanners. Escalate if external-facing. Treat past-due-date findings (2026-06-14) as breach indicators requiring incident investigation.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Process Execution from Ivanti Sentry Service Context
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability...remote code execution'—attacker-supplied command execution via OS command injection requires T1059 detection at the endpoint level.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate child processes spawned by Ivanti Sentry daemon. Alert on anomalous spawning: reverse shells, scripting interpreters (bash, perl, python), data exfiltration tools, lateral movement utilities. Prioritize processes running with elevated privilege (root/SYSTEM).

suggestion.title: Root-Level Code Execution Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'achieve root-level remote code execution'—privilege escalation from unauthenticated network access to root is the direct attack outcome and requires privilege escalation technique detection (T1548).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag processes executing as root/SYSTEM originating from or parented by Ivanti Sentry services. Correlate Sentry appliance logs for exploit attempt patterns. Alert on root process creation triggered by network-accessible Sentry components.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Network Access to Ivanti Sentry Admin Interfaces
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'remote unauthenticated user'—exploitation requires no credentials, only network access. Unauthenticated access attempts are the primary external detection surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sentry appliance logs and external-facing network logs for sequences of unauthenticated requests from untrusted networks. Alert on HTTP 401/403 responses followed by exploitation indicators, command injection attempt patterns, or unexpected system behavior changes.

suggestion.title: Network Configuration Audit: Missing mTLS or Restricted HTTPS Access Controls
suggestion.rationale: Article notes that 'mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors'—absence of these mitigations enables external exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Ivanti Sentry appliances accepting inbound HTTPS without mutual TLS enabled. Verify EPMM or MDM Neurons integration status. Flag any externally-reachable Sentry instance without these controls for immediate network segmentation and prioritized patching.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Remote Code Execution Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution' and 'OS command injection vulnerability' but pipeline generated no detection for actual exploitation attempts targeting Sentry endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious HTTP POST/GET requests to Ivanti Sentry endpoints containing shell metacharacters, command separators, or base64-encoded payloads. Correlate with unexpected root-owned child processes (bash, sh, powershell) spawned from the Sentry application process or associated web server. Alert on requests from external sources to unmanaged appliances.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged Ivanti Sentry Appliance Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable,' establishing unmanaged + exposed as exploitation precondition.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all Ivanti Sentry/MobileIron Sentry appliances via asset inventory and network scanning. Cross-reference with internal management systems (EPMM, Neurons for MDM) to classify managed vs. unmanaged instances. Alert on unmanaged appliances that have inbound access from internet-facing segments or lack HTTPS/mTLS enforcement.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Vulnerable Version Detection and Patch Compliance
suggestion.rationale: Article instructs to 'match against your vulnerability scanner' for CVE-2026-10520 and emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer,' requiring inventory-based detection of vulnerable and unpatched instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate asset inventory with vulnerability scan data and patch management records. Identify Ivanti Sentry instances running unpatched versions affected by CVE-2026-10520. Flag systems past the federal due date (2026-06-14) without documented remediation; escalate to incident response if external-facing.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Root-Level Process Spawning from Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'root-level remote code execution' as the attack outcome, requiring detection of abnormal process execution under elevated privileges from the compromised appliance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child processes spawned by the Sentry application or underlying web server (e.g., tomcat, nginx) running with root or system privileges. Flag unexpected binaries (shells, compilers, script interpreters, network utilities) and correlate timing with HTTP requests. Unusual file modifications or deletions by Sentry process also suggests post-exploitation activity.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Configuration Hardening Verification
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors,' indicating need to verify protective configurations are in place.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Verify all externally-exposed Ivanti Sentry appliances enforce mTLS or restricted HTTPS access via authorized management channels. Detect HTTP (cleartext) connections to Sentry administrative interfaces. Flag appliances missing MDM/EPMM enrollment or lacking TLS certificate pinning. Alert on configuration rollback or removal of access restrictions.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Internet Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability affects appliances that are 'in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' External reachability is the primary risk condition—CISA KEV indicates active exploitation, making this the canonical initial-access hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for inbound HTTPS connections to known Ivanti Sentry management interface ports and paths from untrusted external networks. Cross-reference against asset inventory to identify unmanaged instances. Alert on scanning activity (high-volume connection attempts) and any successful connections from external IPs to Sentry appliances.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry OS Command Injection Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution.' Exploitation requires shell metacharacters in HTTP request parameters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on shell metacharacters (|, ;, &, $(, backticks) in HTTP request parameters to Ivanti Sentry endpoints, especially unauthenticated paths. Correlate suspicious parameter patterns with HTTP 200 responses (successful injection) or unusual process activity spawned on the appliance.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Root-Level Process Spawn Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation achieves 'root-level remote code execution'—post-exploitation will manifest as unexpected command execution at root privilege, distinguishing compromise from normal operation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate processes spawned by Ivanti Sentry service accounts. Alert on unexpected child processes at root/SYSTEM level, especially suspicious names (sh, bash, curl, wget, nc, python). Correlate with web request logs to identify triggering injection payloads.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scanner Confirmation
suggestion.rationale: Federal patch deadline is 2026-06-14 (imminent). Article warns 'patch lag is the silent killer'—organizations need to confirm scanners detect this CVE across all Sentry appliances to validate coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners to confirm CVE-2026-10520 detection rules are deployed and running against all discovered Ivanti Sentry instances. For any detected vulnerable appliances, validate remediation status and timeline against federal due date.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unmanaged State Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes vulnerability occurs specifically 'where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state'—unmanaged state is a distinct risk indicator independent of patch status, requiring configuration discovery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Ivanti management console or CMDB to identify appliances not enrolled in active management. Cross-reference unmanaged instances against network exposure scans. Alert on any unmanaged Sentry appliance reachable from untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability exploitable 'where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable.' Exposability is the prerequisite attack surface; no asset-exposure UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Ivanti Sentry appliances reachable from external networks via port scans, TLS certificate enumeration, HTTP header fingerprinting, or Shodan/Censys queries. Correlate externally-reachable instances against vulnerability scanning data to identify unpatched targets. Alert on Sentry instances without mTLS or HTTPS-only restrictions.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation on Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is 'OS command injection'—execution layer detection required but pipeline provided zero command-injection or process-execution use cases despite article explicitly naming the technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry appliance process logs for unexpected shell spawning (sh, bash) initiated by network requests. Detect shell metacharacters (|, &&, backticks, $(), command substitution) in HTTP request parameters targeting known vulnerable endpoints. Alert on child processes spawned by Sentry daemon with suspicious arguments (reverse shells, wget/curl payloads, system reconnaissance commands).

suggestion.title: Root-Level Privilege Escalation on Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'root-level remote code execution.' Privilege escalation from network-initiated process to root is the critical post-exploitation indicator; no such detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on privilege escalation on Ivanti Sentry where a network service (Sentry daemon) or its child process transitions from non-root to root UID. Monitor sudoers modifications, setuid abuse, and sudo/su invocations on appliances. Baseline normal Sentry privilege flows and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Reverse Shell or C2 Callback from Sentry RCE
suggestion.rationale: Successful root-level RCE implies post-exploitation callbacks (reverse shell, C2 check-in). Article describes impact as RCE but pipeline omitted command-and-control detection despite this being standard post-exploitation behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from Ivanti Sentry appliances to external IP addresses or domains. Flag unexpected DNS queries, reverse-shell protocols (bash -i >& /dev/tcp/...), and raw socket connections initiated by Sentry processes. Correlate against known C2 infrastructure and threat-intel feeds.

suggestion.title: Sentry Configuration Tampering – Removal of Security Controls
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes mTLS and HTTPS-only access prevent exploitation. Detection should flag when protective controls are disabled. Pipeline missed this pre-exploitation configuration-level detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti Sentry configuration files and logs for disabling or bypassing mTLS, EPMM integration, or HTTPS restrictions. Alert on transitions from 'managed' to 'unmanaged' state. Cross-reference configuration changes with network reachability changes.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Vulnerability Scanner Match (CVE-2026-10520)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies CVE-2026-10520 as the primary tracking indicator and references asset-exposure hunt template, but pipeline generated no concrete scanner detection use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and CMDB for Ivanti Sentry instances. Correlate against CVE-2026-10520 patch status. Flag unpatched or unknown-patch instances. Cross-reference with network exposure scans to identify externally accessible appliances.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged Ivanti Sentry with External Reachability Detection

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Ivanti Sentry appliances absent from MDM/EPMM enrollment or marked unmanaged. Correlate against network scans showing inbound internet access. Alert on Sentry instances with open ports (443, 8080, 8443) accessible from untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: OS Command Execution via Sentry Injection Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability' allowing 'root-level RCE'—T1059.001 is the execution technique. Post-compromise hunt for unexpected shell spawning completely absent from pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sh/bash spawning from Ivanti Sentry service processes or processes executing as root. Baseline normal Sentry command patterns. Flag deviations and post-compromise indicators (curl/wget outbound, reverse-shell one-liners, credential access).

suggestion.title: Anomalous HTTP(S) Access to Ivanti Sentry Management Interface
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires external network access to 'externally reachable' appliance; article establishes management interface as attack surface. No network-layer reconnaissance or exploitation detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on inbound HTTP(S) to typical Sentry ports (443, 8080, 8443) from external/untrusted IP ranges. Baseline administrative access. Flag source IP anomalies, failed authentication patterns, and connections from non-corporate network segments.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-10520 Vulnerability Scanner Match

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt vulnerability scan databases and patch-management systems for CVE-2026-10520 matches on Ivanti Sentry appliances. Identify systems reported vulnerable before federal due date 2026-06-14 as patch-lag risk.

suggestion.title: Externally Reachable Ivanti Sentry Appliance Detection

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempt Against Sentry

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt HTTP access logs to Ivanti Sentry management endpoints for command injection indicators: shell metacharacters (;, |, &, ``, $(), >>, <), escaped payloads (%20%7c, %3b), or common RCE patterns (whoami, id, cat /etc/passwd, curl callbacks). Unexpected root processes after HTTP requests to admin interfaces signal successful exploitation.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Unmanaged State Configuration Verification

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit Ivanti Sentry appliances for MDM/EPMM enrollment status and mTLS certificate validity. Flag appliances not enrolled or with expired/missing EPMM certificates as unmanaged and exploitable. Cross-check against network exposure (UC #2)—unmanaged + externally reachable = critical risk.

suggestion.title: Post-RCE Activity on Compromised Sentry Appliance (Lateral Movement / Persistence)

suggestion.title: Externally-Reachable Ivanti Sentry Appliance Exposure

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry OS Command Injection Payload Detection

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Spawning Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability achieves 'root-level remote code execution.' Successful exploitation manifests as SYSTEM/root processes spawning unusual children from Sentry services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On Ivanti Sentry appliances, detect process creation where parent is Sentry service (running as root) spawning shell interpreters, curl, wget, nc, or other execution tools with elevated privilege indicators.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry Deployment Configuration Audit
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors.' Misconfigured deployments lacking these controls are vulnerable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory all Ivanti Sentry instances and verify mTLS enforcement and EPMM/Neurons for MDM restrictions are active. Flag appliances in unmanaged state or with unrestricted external endpoint access as non-compliant.

suggestion.title: Ivanti Sentry External Accessibility Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability exists 'in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable' — need inventory of exposed instances before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Ivanti Sentry service ports (typically 443, 8443) externally reachable from internet-facing assets using network telemetry. Cross-reference with patch status from vulnerability scanner. Flag unmanaged Sentry instances or those not behind mTLS/restricted HTTPS as in the article's high-risk deployment.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Attempt to Ivanti Sentry
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user' — web server logs and WAF events should show exploitation attempts with shell metacharacters.
