suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate FileModified events on vite.config.* or vitest.config.* with child-process spawns of node.exe running 'vitest' or '@vitest/browser' within 0–10 seconds of the file write.

suggestion.title: Browser process with anomalous @vitest/@playwright node_modules image loads
suggestion.rationale: Article attack prerequisite: browser process must load @vitest/@playwright modules to execute malicious plugin code. Loading DLL/so/dylib from node_modules\@vitest or node_modules\vite by chrome/firefox/msedge is smoking-gun indicator. UC_4_8 in article; pipeline generated nothing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis:
Alert on ImageLoaded events where InitiatingProcessFileName is a browser binary (chrome.exe, firefox.exe, msedge.exe, brave.exe, chromium.exe, headless_shell.exe) and FolderPath contains 
ode_modules\@vitest, 
ode_modules\@playwright, or 
ode_modules\vitest.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Email Forwarding Rule Creation to External Recipient
suggestion.rationale: Article core: 'abused Google Workspace Rules to steal research and defense emails'—rule creation is the persistence/collection mechanism. Pipeline generated zero use cases for this primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Google Workspace for email forwarding rules created or modified targeting external domains, especially free email providers (Gmail, Outlook). Alert on rules that auto-forward, with high match rate (broad recipient scope) or rules created by previously dormant accounts.

suggestion.title: Rapid Bulk Email Rule Creation by Single User
suggestion.rationale: Systematic abuse implies multiple rules—article describes targeting 'research and defense emails' suggesting targeted filtering logic. Pipeline provided zero collection-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when single user creates 5+ email rules within 1 hour. Correlate rule creation with rule filter-text patterns matching org keywords (research, defense, lab, sensitive, classified). Baseline per-user rule creation frequency and flag outliers.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Login Before Email Rule Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Hackers must gain account access before abusing rules. Article implies credential compromise ('Chinese Hackers...abused') but pipeline missed initial access entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate anomalous logins (new geolocation, IP, device type, off-hours) to same account with rule creation within 24 hours. Flag impossible travel, MFA changes, or recovery email modifications preceding rule events. High confidence if login is outside normal user baseline.

suggestion.title: Email Rule Forwarding to Attacker-Controlled Inbox
suggestion.rationale: End-state: emails 'stolen'—requires exfiltration to attacker-controlled destination. Pipeline generated zero exfiltration-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SMTP forwarding destinations of emails matched by auto-forward rules. Alert on newly-registered domains, free email providers, or domains with no prior internal correspondence. Correlate forwarding rule creation timestamp with email volume spike to destination address.

suggestion.title: Targeting of Research/Defense Org Emails via Rule Filters
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'research and defense emails'—APT targeting high-value orgs/email patterns. Pipeline should surface org-specific collection detection but generated zero.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Build rule-creation detection triggering on filter-text containing research/defense keywords (research, defense, lab, classified, restricted, sensitive, mil, gov). High fidelity if rule targets known high-value org domains or employee distribution lists with security clearance/research roles.

suggestion.title: Chinese APT Email Rule Abuse Indicator Baseline
suggestion.rationale: Article attributes to 'Chinese Hackers'—pipeline must surface threat-actor context (APT40, APT41 TTPs) and campaign-specific detection. Zero threat context generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Build detection baseline for Chinese APT email rule abuse: targeting defense/research orgs, forwarding to free email destinations, targeting employee accounts with strategic access (C-suite, research leads, security), rule creation from VPN/high-risk geolocations.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Modification to Legitimate Developer Tool Executables
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'turning developer tools into malware delivery channels' — indicates compromise or replacement of legitimate tools (npm, python, git, maven, etc.) with malicious variants.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unsigned or hash-mismatched modifications to standard developer tool binaries (npm, pip, node, python, git, gradle, mvn). Detect tool executables with recent creation timestamps or loaded from non-standard installation paths. Cross-reference file hashes against official distributions.

suggestion.title: Developer Tool Process Establishing C2 Communication
suggestion.rationale: Weaponized dev tools delivering malware implies post-execution C2 callbacks; 'malware delivery' phase transitions to command-and-control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound network connections from developer tool processes (node.exe, python.exe, npm.cmd, mvn.exe, git.exe) to rare or malicious destinations. Flag connections to IPs with no corresponding DNS, to newly-registered domains, or to known C2 infrastructure. Alert on high-volume data exfiltration from dev tool processes.

suggestion.title: Malicious Package Installation via Compromised Package Manager
suggestion.rationale: Dev tools commonly fetch packages/dependencies from repositories; compromised or poisoned packages represent the actual 'malware delivery channel' described in title.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package manager network traffic (npm install, pip install, maven fetch) for downloads from suspicious sources or of packages with typosquatting names. Detect package installations that trigger unexpected child-process execution, file writes to system directories, or registry modifications during installation.

suggestion.title: Code Execution via Weaponized Developer Tool Build/Install Hooks
suggestion.rationale: npm, pip, cargo, and similar tools execute arbitrary code during dependency installation (lifecycle scripts, setup.py, build.rs); weaponized tools exploit this mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unexpected parent-child process relationships where package managers (npm, pip, python, node) spawn shells, interpreters, or system tools. Detect execution of scripts or binaries during package installation with obfuscated/encoded payloads, network requests, or credential access attempts.

suggestion.title: Download and Execution of Trojanized Developer Tool Distribution
suggestion.rationale: Attackers may host fake or modified versions of popular dev tools on phishing domains or compromised mirrors for direct download.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect downloads of developer tool installers from non-official sources (misspelled domains, HTTP instead of HTTPS, suspicious CDNs). Monitor for execution of dev tools immediately after download from suspicious URLs. Verify hash mismatches against official publisher checksums.

suggestion.title: LiteLLM Privilege Escalation - Configuration Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'low-privilege users take over servers' via vulnerability chain — this is explicit privilege escalation. Pipeline extracted zero mention of how escalation occurs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unprivileged process spawning with elevated capabilities, config file writes to LiteLLM installation directories by non-admin users, or sudoers/RBAC rule modifications originating from application service accounts.

suggestion.title: LiteLLM Exploitation - Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability chain implies multi-step exploit. Title offers no detail on execution vector — command injection, SSRF, or code injection. Pipeline provided zero detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect subprocess execution from LiteLLM gateway processes (unexpected child processes like shell, wget, curl), or network requests from gateway to internal resources inconsistent with LLM API calls.

suggestion.title: LiteLLM Gateway Persistence via Config Injection
suggestion.rationale: Server takeover implies persistent access — article title suggests attack chain but pipeline did not map to persistence techniques.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected modifications to LiteLLM config files (.env, litellm_config.yaml), service file rewrites, or new scheduled tasks / cron jobs executing within gateway service context.

suggestion.title: LiteLLM Gateway Reconnaissance - Service Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Low-priv user takeover typically requires discovery of gateway service details, running processes, environment variables. Pipeline found no reconnaissance phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for discovery commands (ps, env, config file reads, API introspection) executed by non-privileged accounts that normally do not run such commands.

suggestion.title: LiteLLM - Vulnerable Version in Use
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline extracted zero CVE identifiers or affected version ranges. Necessary for asset management and patch-readiness.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Asset query: identify systems running LiteLLM versions prior to the patched release. Cross-check against vulnerability advisories for exact version bounds.

suggestion.title: LiteLLM - Unauthorized Admin API Access
suggestion.rationale: Gateway takeover implies access to administrative APIs or management endpoints. Pipeline failed to map this attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect repeated /admin, /config, /users API calls from low-privilege user sessions; failed auth attempts followed by success; or API keys extracted from environment / config files.

suggestion.title: Suspicious binding.gyp Execution During npm Install
suggestion.rationale: Article title 'Wait, binding.gyp Can Do What?' directly signals unexpected capabilities in the binding.gyp build system. This is a primary attack surface for npm supply-chain attacks where build scripts execute arbitrary code during package installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Node.js or npm processes spawning unexpected child processes (bash, powershell, cmd) during package installation, especially with compilation-related arguments. Flag binding.gyp invocations with obfuscated or dynamic script content, network calls to non-package-repository endpoints, or file writes to sensitive locations outside node_modules.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Native Module Compilation via node-gyp
suggestion.rationale: Article is about npm's build system. node-gyp is the mechanism for compiling native modules; supply-chain attack would involve malicious native code compilation. Pipeline missed this core threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on node-gyp invocations with suspicious flags (--module-dir targeting system paths, --jobs exceeding CPU count, inline scripts), compilation of packages flagged as legitimate but with suspicious gyp hooks, or node-gyp output redirected to /dev/null or equivalent.

suggestion.title: npm Package with Malicious Build Phase Scripts
suggestion.rationale: binding.gyp attack vector relies on lifecycle script execution (install, prepare hooks). Pipeline should surface detection of packages with execute-before-index behavior or obfuscated build scripts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm package installation for packages declaring build/preinstall/postinstall scripts that decode/deobfuscate inline, invoke external tools in unusual sequences, or contain base64/gzip payloads. Flag discrepancies between published package.json and runtime execution.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability in 'Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager' exposed to authenticated remote attackers. First detection step must be inventory of which assets run this product and which are network-facing. No use case generated despite being canonical CISA KEV hunt pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for inbound HTTP/HTTPS traffic to known Cisco SD-WAN Manager default ports (443, 8443, 8453). Cross-reference asset inventory and vulnerability scanner output. Look for instances responding with Cisco SD-WAN Manager banners or certificate subject names containing 'SD-WAN'.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Exploitation: Directory Traversal Patterns in SD-WAN Manager Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'could allow an authenticated, remote attacker to create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem' via directory/path traversal. Exploitation would manifest as HTTP requests containing '../', '..\', percent-encoded variants, or absolute paths. No detection use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS request logs to Cisco SD-WAN Manager endpoints for path traversal payloads: '../' sequences, '..\' backslash variants, URL-encoded equivalents (%2e%2e), and absolute file paths (/etc/passwd, C:\Windows\, etc.). Flag requests attempting to read or write system-critical directories.

suggestion.title: File System Integrity: Unexpected File Creation/Modification on SD-WAN Manager Systems
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem.' Impact detection should monitor for suspicious file operations on affected hosts. Zero use cases generated for post-exploitation forensics or real-time file integrity monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor affected SD-WAN Manager systems for unexpected file creation or modification outside normal maintenance windows. Flag: (1) files written to system directories (/etc, /var, /system, C:\Windows, C:\Program Files), (2) creation of executable files in unexpected paths, (3) modification timestamps indicating out-of-band changes, (4) file ownership/permission changes.

suggestion.title: Authentication Anomaly: Successful Authentication to SD-WAN Manager by Unauthorized Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability requires 'authenticated' attacker. Exploitation chains likely depend on credential compromise, weak default credentials, or session hijacking. Article provides no guidance on where authentication occurs but implies standard web auth patterns. No detection for suspicious authentication events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SD-WAN Manager authentication logs for: (1) failed login spikes targeting service accounts or admin roles, (2) successful logins from anomalous source IPs or geographic locations, (3) authentication using default or weak credentials, (4) session tokens issued outside normal business hours or to unexpected users.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scan Match: CVE-2026-20262 Detection in Scanner Output
suggestion.rationale: Article cites 'CVE-2026-20262' explicitly and mandates federal patch by 2026-06-29. Simplest detection: direct scanner correlation. Pipeline produced no IOCs or use cases for vulnerability matching despite CISA KEV template recommending this.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate vulnerability scanner output (Nessus, Qualys, Rapid7) and software inventory tools (SCCM, CrowdStrike, EDR) for presence of Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager with version information. Flag any system matching CVE-2026-20262 vulnerability signature as CRITICAL and escalate to patch management with federal due date: 2026-06-29.

suggestion.title: HTTP Error Logging: 400/403/404 Patterns Indicating Directory Enum or Access Denied
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal and directory traversal exploits often generate HTTP error codes (403 Forbidden, 404 Not Found) when attackers probe non-existent paths or trigger access control checks. Article describes file overwrite capability implying filesystem access controls. Detection of probing activity precedes successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP response codes from SD-WAN Manager endpoints. Detect sequences of: (1) single source issuing 10+ requests to distinct filesystem paths within 5 minutes, (2) requests containing path traversal patterns followed by 403/404 responses, (3) rapid iteration over parameter values (e.g., ?file=../../../etc/passwd, ?file=../../../etc/shadow) with corresponding error codes.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20262 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'CVE-2026-20262 — match against your vulnerability scanner' but pipeline generated zero scanner-based detection logic. This is the minimum detection required for any CISA KEV entry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager asset flagged as vulnerable to CVE-2026-20262 in vulnerability scanner output. Correlate against patched inventory to identify patch-lag drift. Priority: systems showing NOT patched as of 2026-06-29 federal due date.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized File Write to SD-WAN Manager Filesystem
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker 'could allow an authenticated, remote attacker to create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem'. Pipeline missed file-creation/modification detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected file creation or modification events originating from Catalyst SD-WAN Manager web/API service accounts, especially in system directories or configuration paths. Flag path-traversal patterns (../, ..\) in request logs.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Authentication to Exposed SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'authenticated, remote attacker' — pipeline missed detection for suspicious login patterns to internet-exposed SD-WAN Managers. Credential compromise or session abuse are natural precursors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on failed/successful logins to Catalyst SD-WAN Manager from non-corporate IP ranges, especially around 2026-06-29 cutoff window. Correlate with vulnerability-scanning tool activity to detect active exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Payload Detection in SD-WAN Manager Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'directory or path traversal vulnerability' but pipeline missed detection for the actual payload signatures that trigger this flaw.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP/HTTPS requests to Catalyst SD-WAN Manager endpoints containing path-traversal patterns (../, %2e%2e, ..\, %252e%252e, etc.) regardless of success/failure response. Context: any hit post-publication date is likely reconnaissance or exploitation.

suggestion.title: Go Package Typo Squatting Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states malicious package named 'github.com/botdb-go/bolt' (vs legitimate 'github.com/boltdb/bolt') — 'names very similar to popular ones.' Pipeline missed detection for packages with editor distance <2 from known popular libraries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Go build system (go get, go mod) operations for package names within edit distance 2 of popular libraries. Flag downloads from non-standard mirrors; cross-reference against known typo-squatting IOCs and package name similarity databases.

suggestion.title: Go Module Proxy Cache Poisoning
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Go Module Mirror's indefinite caching of modules kicked in, and that cached the backdored module' even after removal. Pipeline missed persistence detection for stale/cached malicious packages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference Go module downloads against Go vulnerability database (GO-2025-3451) and upstream removal records. Alert when applications install package versions listed as malicious, indicating exploitation of stale module cache.

suggestion.title: Go Module Backdoor C2 Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article states backdoor 'allows hackers to remotely control infected computers through a server that sends them commands.' No C2 detection generated despite explicit remote-control capability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor network connections from Go processes or applications linked to boltdb for unexpected outbound HTTP/HTTPS to command servers. Alert on callbacks during module load, unusual connection patterns, or DNS queries to C2 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Go Dependency Version Integrity Mismatch
suggestion.rationale: Article notes malicious v1.3.1 remained in caches while 'developers to update the version that stayed in the system for 3 years.' Pipeline missed detection for version mismatches between declared and installed modules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare go.mod declared versions against installed binary modules and go.sum checksums. Flag where installed differs from declared or hash deviates, especially for packages flagged in Go vuln DB.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Go Module Proxy Configuration
suggestion.rationale: Backdoor persisted in Go Module Proxy despite removal. Pipeline missed detection for GOPROXY or go mod configuration pointing to unvetted proxies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GOPROXY environment variable, .config/go/env, and go.mod settings for non-standard module proxy URLs. Alert on resolution of packages from mirrors with documented security incidents, downtime, or removal records.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Internet Reachability
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes remote exploitation: 'authenticated, remote attacker' implies internet-exposed SD-WAN Manager instances. Pipeline must hunt for externally accessible instances before exploitation can occur.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager listening on internet-routable IPs (default ports 8443, 9443). Monitor inbound connections to these services from untrusted networks. Alert on successful authentication from non-whitelisted source IPs.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Attempt: CVE-2026-20262 Path Traversal Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'directory or path traversal vulnerability'—this is a URL/parameter manipulation attack pattern. Pipeline must detect traversal sequences (../, ..\\, encoded variants) in HTTP requests to SD-WAN Manager endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to Catalyst SD-WAN Manager for path traversal payloads: %2e%2e, ../, ..\, double-encoding, unicode variants in URI paths. Flag requests targeting system directories (/etc/, /var/, windows/system32, etc.).

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation: Suspicious File Write/Overwrite on SD-WAN Manager Host
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem.' This is the direct impact of successful exploitation and should trigger file integrity monitoring alerts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation/modification by SD-WAN Manager process (or running as its service account) in unexpected directories: system binaries, config directories outside normal update paths, web root directories. Correlate with failed authentication spikes immediately preceding writes.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scan Match: CVE-2026-20262 Detection in Nessus/Qualys/Rapid7
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV mandates rapid patching by 2026-06-29. Pipeline must surface all instances detected as vulnerable by standard scanners—this is the foundational compliance hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner output (Nessus, Qualys, Tenable.io, Rapid7) for CVE-2026-20262 detections. Correlate with asset inventory for Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager products. Flag any instance not confirmed patched or out-of-scope by security exception date.

suggestion.title: Authentication Anomaly: Elevated Failed Logins to SD-WAN Manager Before Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'authenticated, remote attacker'—exploitation likely requires credential compromise or brute force. Pipeline should detect credential stuffing/brute force as a prerequisite hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor authentication logs for Catalyst SD-WAN Manager for spike in failed login attempts from single source IP. Baseline normal login frequency per source; alert on 5+ failed attempts in 5 minutes. Correlate with successful login immediately following failed sequence.

suggestion.title: Patch Compliance: Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Version Inventory < Patched Version
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry with federal remediation date 2026-06-29. Pipeline must track software inventory versioning to measure patch currency across the fleet.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Generate automated inventory report of all Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances and their running versions. Flag any instance running version < patched version as non-compliant. Cross-reference with approved exceptions; escalate unexcepted non-compliance to patch management team.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly references standard asset-exposure hunt in template and cites 'KEV implies active exploitation against exposed assets.' No UC was generated despite this guidance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for publicly accessible Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances on default/known ports. Cross-reference against CVE-2026-20262 patch status. Monitor for exposed interfaces with 'Cisco Catalyst' or 'SD-WAN' in HTTPS certificate Subject. Article states patch due 2026-06-29—identify unpatched deployments before deadline.

suggestion.title: Directory Traversal Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'directory or path traversal vulnerability' as the core attack mechanism. No detection rule for traversal payloads (../, ..\, %2e%2e, etc.) in request paths against Catalyst SD-WAN Manager endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect path traversal patterns in HTTP requests to Catalyst SD-WAN Manager: sequences containing ../, encoded dots (%2e%2e), or absolute path prefixes in query/body parameters. Alert on 4xx responses following traversal attempts, or 200 responses with unusual latency (may indicate file system access).

suggestion.title: Unauthorized File Creation/Modification on Catalyst SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'could allow an authenticated, remote attacker to create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem.' No detection hypothesis for post-exploitation file system modification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Catalyst SD-WAN Manager host file system for suspicious file creation/modification in system directories, config paths, or web root. Flag files created/modified by the application process outside scheduled maintenance windows. Alert on overwrites of critical application binaries, config files, or startup scripts.

suggestion.title: Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Authentication Bypass / Post-Auth Exploit Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector is 'authenticated, remote attacker'—requires detection of credential abuse or session hijacking leading to exploitation. Article does not describe unauthenticated access, implying valid credentials or session are required.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal admin activity on Catalyst SD-WAN Manager (login frequency, IP ranges, time windows). Alert on anomalous authentications followed by file system operations or API calls targeting traversal parameters. Monitor for rapid API calls post-login indicative of automated exploitation.

suggestion.title: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Asset Exposure via CVE-2026-20262
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states CISA KEV status (actively exploited in wild) and directs: 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' with this CVE. No scanner or inventory detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory and vulnerability scanner for Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager versions prior to patch release (2026-06-29). Cross-reference with public IP exposure and authentication logs. Flag systems with no patch evidence post-advisory date.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Exploitation Attempts Against SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'directory or path traversal vulnerability.' Implies attacker must submit crafted requests. No web-log or HTTP-pattern detection coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt HTTP request logs to Catalyst SD-WAN Manager for path traversal sequences: ../, ..\, %2e%2e%2f, unicode/double-encoded variants targeting /etc/, /var/, /opt/ paths. Alert on 40x responses followed by successful HTTP 200, indicating directory bypass.

suggestion.title: File System Modification Post-Compromise on SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem.' Post-exploitation detection critical for breach detection. None generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline file creation/modification rates in /etc, /var, /opt, /tmp on Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances. Alert on suspicious overwrites to sudoers, SSH keys, cron jobs, or application binaries outside maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Authenticated Path Traversal Abuse on SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'authenticated, remote attacker.' Pipeline missed critical detection signal: post-auth path traversal differs from pre-auth and requires session correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful authentication events to Catalyst SD-WAN Manager with subsequent path-traversal HTTP patterns in session logs. Alert if traversal attempts appear in same session post-login, indicating active exploitation by authenticated user.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states the vulnerability 'could allow an authenticated, remote attacker' against an 'affected system' and notes 'KEV implies active exploitation against exposed assets' — indicating internet-facing deployment that should be hunted. Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' but pipeline generated zero use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for inbound traffic to Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager on default management ports (8443, 9443, 32768-32785) from external networks. Correlate with vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-20262 to identify exposure windows. Flag systems reporting vulnerable after federal patch due date 2026-06-29.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20262 Path Traversal Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies the vulnerability mechanism: 'directory or path traversal vulnerability' enabling file creation/overwriting. No detection for the exploitation pattern itself (path traversal payloads, unusual file paths) was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SD-WAN Manager application logs for HTTP request payloads containing path traversal sequences (../, ..\, percent-encoded variants %2e%2e%2f). Alert on traversal attempts targeting filesystem paths outside intended directories. Track response codes (200, 201, 204) following traversal requests.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized File Write on SD-WAN Manager Filesystem
suggestion.rationale: Article impact statement: 'create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem of an affected system' — post-exploitation file modification detection is missing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SD-WAN Manager file system for unexpected file creation or modification in web root, config, and system directories. Correlate file writes with failed/successful exploitation attempts by timestamp. Alert on files created under high-privilege paths (e.g., /etc, /var/www) by the application service account.

suggestion.title: SD-WAN Manager Vulnerability Scanner Hits for CVE-2026-20262
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states under Indicators of Compromise: 'CVE-2026-20262 — match against your vulnerability scanner' yet pipeline did not extract this IOC or recommend scanner correlation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any vulnerability scan result reporting CVE-2026-20262 present on Catalyst SD-WAN Manager assets. Cross-reference with patch deployment and system update logs. Escalate systems still vulnerable 7 days after federal remediation deadline (2026-06-29).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20262 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'match against your vulnerability scanner'; CVE is primary IOC for asset-exposure hunt template.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on CVE-2026-20262 hits from vulnerability scanner targeting Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager. CISA KEV status indicates active exploitation; prioritize by federal remediation due-date 2026-06-29.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager Internet-Facing Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'public-facing application' and 'KEV implies active exploitation against exposed assets'; asset-exposure template hunt is explicitly recommended.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify SD-WAN Manager instances with network paths to internet or untrusted subnets. Scan for open management ports; correlate with vulnerability scanner for dual exposure + vulnerable-version signals.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager Unauthorized File Overwrite
suggestion.rationale: Article core capability: 'create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem'; file manipulation is the direct attack impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SD-WAN Manager directories for unexpected file creation/modification. Alert on writes to executable or config paths, especially by service accounts or during off-hours.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager Authentication Followed by Directory Traversal
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'authenticated, remote attacker'; successful login followed by path-traversal attempts (../, ..\) indicates post-auth exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect successful SD-WAN Manager authentication followed by API/web requests containing path-traversal sequences (../, encoded variants) or directory-enumeration patterns in access logs.

suggestion.title: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Exposed to Internet (CVE-2026-20262)
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends 'standard asset-exposure hunt' and notes CISA KEV implies vulnerability is observed exploited against 'exposed assets'—exposure is the necessary entry point for T1190 exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners and network discovery tools for Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances reachable from the internet. Cross-reference with CVE-2026-20262 scanner matches and flag any unpatched versions. Escalate externally-facing instances with patch lag beyond 7 days as critical.

suggestion.title: Successful Authentication to Catalyst SD-WAN Preceding Filesystem Writes

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP/HTTPS requests to Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager endpoints containing path traversal sequences (../, ..\, %2e%2e, unicode encoding variants, ..%252f). Flag attempts to access system paths (/etc, /sys, /var, Windows\System32) through the vulnerability endpoint.

suggestion.title: Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Suspicious File Modifications Post-Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability allows attacker to 'create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem'—critical impact phase requiring post-exploitation file system monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Catalyst SD-WAN Manager service account and process for unexpected file creation/modification in config directories, binary paths, or system directories. Correlate with successful authentication and flag file overwrites within 10 minutes of first-seen or anomalous authentication source.

suggestion.title: Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Unusual Authentication Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Attack requires 'authenticated, remote attacker'—need detection of credential compromise or suspicious authentication behavior preceding exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful authentication to Catalyst SD-WAN Manager from new/unexpected IP addresses, especially with geographically impossible logins. Combine with baseline anomaly detection for authentication time, location, and volume patterns over 7-day baseline.

suggestion.title: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV implies active scanning/exploitation of exposed instances; need baseline of all externally accessible Catalyst instances with risk scoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory all Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances on network, validate they are appropriately segmented from untrusted networks, and identify any listening on default ports (443, 8443, or custom configured) externally. Cross-reference against network ACLs and firewall rules for unnecessary external exposure.

suggestion.title: CISA KEV Remediation Timeline Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies federal patch due date of 2026-06-29—deadline-driven hunt to identify systems still vulnerable at escalation points.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create automated alert 7 days before federal due date (2026-06-22) for all CVE-2026-20262 instances still in 'vulnerable' state. Flag any system where patch was available but not applied, with escalation workflow to ownership and compliance teams.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Internet-Facing Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes that 'authenticated, remote attacker' can 'create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem.' Exploitation requires network reachability—exposure hunt is the prerequisite. CISA KEV mandates due-date compliance (2026-06-29); asset enumeration drives patch priority.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for inbound connections to known SD-WAN Manager default ports (usually 8443 TCP) from external source IPs, or query asset inventory and public-IP scanners for hosts running Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager accessible from the internet.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20262 Vulnerability Scanner Detections
suggestion.rationale: Article directly states CVE-2026-20262 is in CISA KEV with federal patch due 2026-06-29. Vulnerability scanners and patch-management systems must report vulnerable instances. Pipeline recommended template substitution but produced no actual detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner output and patch management dashboards for CVE-2026-20262 matches in the last 7 days. Flag any system still showing vulnerable status post-2026-06-29 as remediation failure.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Operations on SD-WAN Manager Hosts
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability permits authenticated attacker to 'create a file or overwrite any file'—this is the exploitation mechanism. Unexpected file writes, especially to system/config directories or with unusual process parents, indicate active compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor hosts running SD-WAN Manager for unexpected file creation/modification in system directories (%windir%, /etc, /usr/bin, config directories). Flag writes where the file owner/permissions change unexpectedly or the creating process is not the SD-WAN Manager service itself.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Authentication to Cisco SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Attack path requires 'authenticated, remote attacker.' Credential compromise, default credentials, or brute force must precede exploitation. Monitor for authentication anomalies that surface attacker credential acquisition attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag failed authentication spikes (>5 failures in 5 minutes), logins from geographically impossible locations, logins to SD-WAN Manager from IPs not in corporate IP ranges, or after-hours access from new source IPs.

suggestion.title: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Service Process Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'create a file or overwrite any file'—if exploitation spawns child processes or uses the SD-WAN Manager process itself to execute binaries or scripts post-compromise, process lineage will diverge from baselines.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal child processes spawned by the SD-WAN Manager service (typically none or system utilities only). Alert on unexpected child processes, especially shells (cmd.exe, /bin/sh, powershell.exe) or network utilities (curl, wget, nslookup) spawned with the SD-WAN Manager as parent.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Post-SD-WAN Manager Compromise
suggestion.rationale: SD-WAN Manager is often a network hub with trust relationships to edge devices and upstream systems. File-write exploitation could lead to credential theft or persistence mechanisms enabling lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-CVE-2026-20262 detection, monitor for unusual outbound connections from the compromised SD-WAN Manager to internal infrastructure, credential reuse from that host to other systems, or lateral tool execution (psexec, wmiexec, ssh).

suggestion.title: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Internet Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article states CISA KEV implies 'active exploitation against exposed assets' and explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt.' Pipeline generated zero UCs despite this directive.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances (ports, web interfaces, management APIs) with inbound routes from untrusted networks. Cross-reference against vulnerability scanner for CVE-2026-20262. Alert on new external access to management interface.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Exploitation Against SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability as 'directory or path traversal' and attacker can 'create a file or overwrite any file'—exploitation attempts are the core threat. No UC addresses HTTP-layer path traversal patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Catalyst SD-WAN Manager access logs for requests containing path traversal payloads (../, %2e%2e, URL encoding variants, absolute paths). Flag requests to file-write endpoints with suspicious parameter values. Correlate multiple attempts from same source.

suggestion.title: Unexpected File Modifications on SD-WAN Manager Appliance
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attacker capability to 'overwrite any file on the filesystem'—this is a post-exploitation indicator. Pipeline missed impact-phase detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Catalyst SD-WAN Manager filesystem for file creation/modification outside scheduled maintenance windows, especially in system directories, config paths, or startup directories. Alert on modifications by unauthorized users or unexpected processes.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Authentication Activity on SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker must be 'authenticated, remote.' Pipeline did not generate UC for unusual auth patterns despite this requirement being explicit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on authentication attempts to Catalyst SD-WAN Manager from non-whitelisted source IPs, failed-then-success sequences, or off-hours access. Correlate successful authentications with subsequent file-access or system-modification events.

suggestion.title: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager CVE-2026-20262 Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-20262 explicitly named in article; CISA KEV catalog implies active exploitation. Federal due date 2026-06-29 requires inventory and patching tracking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all instances of Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager in fleet. Flag any version < patched baseline. Cross-reference with network exposure data to prioritize externally-accessible instances. Track patch compliance against federal due date.

suggestion.title: Directory Traversal Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'directory or path traversal vulnerability.' This is the attack vector; detectable via access logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Catalyst SD-WAN Manager API/web logs for path traversal patterns: ../, ..\ , %2e%2e%2f, unicode encoding, or directory escape attempts. Correlate with known CVE-2026-20262 exploitation PoC syntax if available.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Creation/Overwrite via Catalyst SD-WAN Process
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem.' File operations are the direct impact; detectable via file system monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file creation/modification events originating from Catalyst SD-WAN Manager process context (e.g., via API call flow). Flag writes to sensitive paths: /etc/, /bin/, C:\Windows\System32, /root/.ssh, credential stores. Establish baseline of legitimate Catalyst SD-WAN file operations.

suggestion.title: Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Child Process Execution Post-File Modification
suggestion.rationale: File overwrite capability could enable code execution if attacker writes scripts/binaries. Article's impact scope ('overwrite any file') includes executables.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate file creation/overwrite events in Catalyst SD-WAN context with subsequent unusual child process execution. Flag execution of new/unsigned binaries, shell commands, or scripts spawned shortly after CVE-2026-20262-related file ops.

suggestion.title: Credential Store Access Post-Path Traversal Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Arbitrary file overwrite capability creates risk of targeting credential stores, config files with secrets, or key material. Detectable via attempted access patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag access (read/write) to credential-storage paths following CVE-2026-20262 exploitation: /etc/shadow, /etc/passwd, C:\Windows\System32\config\SAM, .ssh directories, token files. Correlate timing with exploitation window.

suggestion.title: Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Authentication Anomaly Baseline Deviation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'authenticated, remote attacker'—authentication logs are available. Exploit prerequisites are: valid credential OR exposed unpatched instance. Monitor for abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of normal Catalyst SD-WAN Manager authentication patterns (source IPs, user accounts, time-of-day, request frequency). Flag authentication failures followed by success (brute-force signal), out-of-hours logins, or logins from unusual geolocations.

suggestion.title: Detect Initial Compromise via Identity Attack
suggestion.rationale: Keywords specify 'identity' as attack surface. Article describes attackers gaining 'access'—no UC generated for detecting credential compromise, password spray, or MFA bypass. Phrase: 'Attackers can move from access to exfiltration in 72 minutes' implies identity-based entry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on multiple failed login attempts followed by successful authentication from anomalous source (new IP, impossible travel). Flag MFA-bypass attempts or conditional-access policy violations preceding successful credential usage.

suggestion.title: Detect Lateral Movement Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: 72-minute timeline implies rapid lateral spread. Pipeline extracted zero use cases for detecting movement from initial compromise to target systems. Required to close detection gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid sequential remote session initiation (RDP, SSH, WinRM, SMB) from a single compromised source to 10+ targets within 2 hours. Correlate failed logons with successful lateral movement on high-risk accounts.

suggestion.title: Detect Data Staging and Compression Before Exfil
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 72-minute access-to-exfiltration window. Pipeline missed UC for detecting collection phase (file enumeration, compression) that precedes exfil. Phrase: '72 minutes' implies detection must catch pre-exfil staging.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid file-system enumeration on sensitive directories (HR, Finance, Engineering, R&D) post-compromise. Alert on: (1) bulk file-read operations on sensitive shares, then (2) compression or archiving tool execution (7z, RAR, WinRAR, tar).

suggestion.title: Detect Exfiltration Over Cloud Services
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'Managed XSIAM'—modern attacks use cloud-native exfil channels (OneDrive, SharePoint, cloud email). Pipeline generated zero UC for cloud-based data movement despite article context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous upload volume to OneDrive, Dropbox, or SharePoint from compromised user post-compromise (e.g., first-ever upload at 3 AM, 500+ files in 1 hour). Flag external sharing of sensitive files or creation of public-access links.

suggestion.title: Detect Time-Boxed Attack: Access-to-Exfil in 72 Hours
suggestion.rationale: Article's unique angle: attackers compress full attack cycle into 72 minutes/hours. Pipeline should generate a synthetic UC that correlates initial compromise detection to exfil event and measures dwell time. No such UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline: time from first sign of compromise (failed logons, process anomaly, file access) to data-egress event. Alert if exfiltration occurs within 72 hours of initial indicator. Correlate device compromise timestamp to first large egress (>100 MB) to non-standard destination.

suggestion.title: Detect Automated/Scripted Post-Compromise Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: 72-minute timeline implies automated tooling post-access. Article discusses 'AI-driven automation' (SOC-side), implying threat-side automation as well. Pipeline missed UC for rapid discovery/enumeration scripts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid execution of discovery commands (get-aduser, dsquery, net group, whoami, ipconfig) post-compromise. Flag scripted discovery via PowerShell or cmd loops, or enumeration of cloud-service users/groups via API calls.

suggestion.title: WebSocket upgrade to /__vitest_browser_api__ endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states the vulnerability is exposed via 'WebSocket RPC' and the endpoint `/__vitest_browser_api__` is the attack surface. This is the first observable event in the kill chain and must be detected before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP Upgrade requests to paths containing '__vitest_browser_api__' from external (non-loopback) sources. WebSocket handshake followed by abnormal frame activity (RPC calls to cdp()) indicates exploitation attempt. Baseline legitimate Vitest dev servers by IP/port pair and alert on new patterns.

suggestion.title: CDP method invocation via Vitest Browser RPC (cdp() calls)
suggestion.rationale: The article core finding: 'cdp() API...forwards raw Chrome DevTools Protocol methods...not gated by allowWrite/allowExec.' Detecting cdp() method calls themselves is the direct indicator of exploitation.
log_sources: Web proxy logs with payload inspection
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect WebSocket frames on /__vitest_browser_api__ connections for RPC method calls to 'cdp()' with parameters. High confidence if cdp() is called with file I/O methods (e.g., Filesystem.getDirectories, write operations). Requires proxy or agent-level visibility into RPC payload.

suggestion.title: Config file read/write from unprivileged browser process without privilege elevation
suggestion.rationale: Article states browsers 'can...overwrite config files' via CDP. Detection should flag when a browser process (chrome.exe, chromium.exe, firefox.exe, etc.) obtains read/write access to vite.config.*, vitest.config.* without a legitimate developer running the build explicitly.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when browser processes (chrome.exe, chromium.exe, msedge.exe, firefox.exe, brave.exe, headless_shell.exe, playwright.exe, opera.exe) create, modify, or write to vite.config.ts/js/mjs/mts or vitest.config.ts/js/mjs/mts WITHOUT an immediately preceding legitimate npm/yarn/pnpm/node process in the same parent process tree. Requires 5+ second lookback to establish legitimate dev context.

suggestion.title: Bypass attempt of allowWrite/allowExec controls via alternate API paths
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'allowWrite...allowExec' controls are ineffective because 'CDP is not gated by' them. Detections should look for attempts to invoke write/exec operations that bypass the stated control mechanisms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Vitest/Browser API logs for RPC calls that attempt write or exec operations when allowWrite=false/allowExec=false are configured. Flag cdp() calls with file write or process spawn methods as evasion attempts. Requires instrumentation of the Vitest Browser API layer.

suggestion.title: Unusual environment variable injection into Vitest or browser process startup
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions the vulnerability enables overwriting config; attackers may also inject env vars like NODE_OPTIONS or npm lifecycle hooks to trigger RCE. No detection rule was provided for env var-based bypasses.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when node.exe or npm/yarn is spawned with environment variables (NODE_OPTIONS, NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS, npm_config_*) that contain shell metacharacters, script paths, or exec placeholders. Cross-reference with preceding config file modifications to establish causal chain.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Email Forwarding Rule Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article title indicates 'abused Google Workspace Rules' to steal emails—the pipeline did not generate any detection for rule manipulation despite this being the core attack technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rapid creation of email forwarding rules or mail filters by non-admin accounts or during off-hours. Flag rules that forward emails to external domains or hide original messages after forwarding. Correlate rule creation with prior failed login attempts or credential-exposure indicators.

suggestion.title: Email Collection via Forwarding Rules Targeting Sensitive Keywords
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Research and Defense Emails' being stolen, implying rules targeting sensitive subject lines. Pipeline missed detection for keyword-based forwarding rules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect email rules filtering on keywords associated with research, defense, classified material, or sensitive projects. Look for rules that silently forward matched emails and suppress notifications. Identify destination external email accounts and compare against known corporate domains.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Email Rule Configuration in Google Workspace
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline generated no use case monitoring for rule creation patterns unique to compromise—article describes persistent data exfiltration implying stealthy rule setup.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on email rules marked as 'never show notification' or 'delete after sending' in combination with external forwarding. Baseline normal rule-creation frequency per user/department and flag statistical outliers within 30 minutes of account unlock or MFA override.

suggestion.title: Cross-Tenant Email Rule Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: If attack spans multiple organizations or research institutions, pipeline should detect lateral enumeration of tenant rules. No kill-chain phase maps enumeration or discovery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for repeated queries to email rules API or rule-listing commands by single account across multiple delegated mailboxes or shared calendars. Threshold: >5 unique mailboxes queried in <10 minutes.

suggestion.title: Credential-Access Followed by Email Rule Creation
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline did not map initial access (credential compromise) to persistence (rule creation). Article implies accounts were compromised before rules deployed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful login from new IP/device/geo with email rule creation within 5-60 minutes. Flag if the rule-creator account differs from the login account (lateral movement via shared service account).

suggestion.title: Suspicious External Email Forwarding Destination Reputation
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates emails forwarded to attacker-controlled external address. Pipeline should check forward-destination domain age, registration details, and threat-intel associations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Extract external email addresses from forwarding rules and cross-reference against domain-registration databases (WHOIS age <90 days), DNS sinkhole lists, and passive DNS records. Flag domains not associated with organization's known vendors or subsidiaries.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Developer Tool Download from Untrusted Source
suggestion.rationale: Article states hackers are 'turning developer tools into malware delivery channels'—implies compromised or spoofed downloads of IDEs, compilers, build tools, or package managers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on downloads of common developer tools (Visual Studio, JetBrains IDEs, Gradle, Maven, npm) from non-canonical domains (not official mirrors, CDNs, or package registries). Correlate with process execution of installer files from unusual paths or with parent processes consistent with malware downloaders.

suggestion.title: Code Execution via Compromised IDE or Build System
suggestion.rationale: Developer tools inherently execute arbitrary code during builds/editing. Article implies malware injected into these tools to achieve execution on developer machines.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child processes spawned by known developer tools (devenv.exe, idea.exe, gradle.bat, mvn.cmd) that are unusual or unsigned. Flag execution of scripting interpreters (powershell.exe, cmd.exe, python.exe) with parent process being a build tool or IDE, especially with persistence-indicative registry/file modifications.

suggestion.title: Malware Signature in Developer Tool Update or Plugin
suggestion.rationale: Article describes tools 'turned into malware delivery'—implies payload embedded in tool binaries or extensions that auto-execute during update cycles.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Yara/hash IOCs for known malware signatures in developer tool directories (.vs, .idea, node_modules, Maven cache, gradle cache). Trigger on unexpected files in tool installation paths with high entropy or non-standard extensions. Monitor plugin/extension install logs for suspicious sources.

suggestion.title: Command and Control Communication from Developer Tool Process
suggestion.rationale: Once malware executes via dev tools, it must exfiltrate or receive commands. Article implies attacker command channels post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate network activity for developer tools (package registry lookups, compiler symbol downloads). Alert on unexpected DNS queries or HTTP(S) connections from IDE or build-tool processes to unknown or known malicious C2 domains. Correlate with process lineage showing tool process spawning network utilities.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Poisoning via Compromised Package or Repository
suggestion.rationale: Developer tools integrate deeply with package managers and repositories. Article implies North Korean threat actors compromised this supply chain to distribute malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package manager logs (npm, pip, Maven, NuGet) for downloads of unsigned or misaligned dependencies. Alert on package metadata mismatches (version number downgrades, unexpected publishers). Correlate tool download events with subsequent malicious process behavior on systems that consumed those packages.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Post-Install Script Execution from npm Module
suggestion.rationale: Article title indicates binding.gyp (npm GYP build system) vulnerabilities; binding.gyp files contain post-install hooks that execute arbitrary code during 'npm install'. No detection rule was generated despite this being core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or bash spawned as children of npm.exe/node.exe processes during install phases. Flag for unusual working directories (node_modules), suspicious command-line arguments (curl, certutil, echo with base64), or parent processes with path containing .npm cache.

suggestion.title: Untrusted Registry Access During npm Install
suggestion.rationale: binding.gyp exploits are delivered via supply chain (malicious packages in npm registry or typosquatted packages). Pipeline missed initial-access phase completely: 'Exploring npm's Weirdest Build System' implies unsafe registry mechanics.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate npm registry queries (registry.npmjs.org, registry.yarnpkg.com). Flag anomalous registries, new registry configurations in .npmrc, DNS lookups to suspicious domains during install, or install activity from non-standard user accounts.

suggestion.title: binding.gyp File Injection or Modification
suggestion.rationale: Attacker-controlled packages can inject or modify binding.gyp in installed node_modules to execute malicious build steps. No file-system IOC or file-modification detection suggested despite this being core persistence mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for binding.gyp creation/modification in node_modules directories with timestamps correlating to npm install or update operations. Flag suspicious metadata: file size deviations from public package baseline, modification by non-npm-installer processes, or execution of binding.gyp from non-standard paths.

suggestion.title: High-Entropy or Obfuscated Payload in binding.gyp Script Blocks
suggestion.rationale: Malicious binding.gyp can hide payloads in GYP variables, conditions, or shell script blocks. Article explores 'what binding.gyp can do'—implying abuse cases; no content inspection logic generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On npm install, extract binding.gyp from all downloaded packages. Scan for high-entropy strings in action blocks, base64-encoded payloads, hexadecimal literals, or shell metacharacters (pipes, redirects, backticks) in variables. Flag presence of eval(), exec(), or child_process.spawn() calls.

suggestion.title: Unusual Network Activity Initiated from npm Post-Install Context
suggestion.rationale: Post-install scripts in binding.gyp can reach out to C2, exfiltration, or secondary-payload servers. No command-and-control or exfiltration phase covered despite critical severity and npm being a common supply-chain vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of npm install network dependencies (npmjs.org, github.com, node source mirrors). Alert on outbound connections from npm/node processes to non-registry IPs, residential proxies, dynamic DNS, or C2-typical ports (8080, 4444, 5555, 9001). Correlate with process timeline from install start.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'allows an authenticated, remote attacker' targeting a public-facing application (T1190). The article's template guidance explicitly references 'asset-exposure hunt' as the canonical first detection step. Discovery of exposed instances precedes exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances reachable from untrusted networks via proxy/WAF logs on standard SD-WAN Manager ports. Cross-reference with asset inventory to flag internet-facing deployments. Correlate with vulnerability scan results to identify exploitation targets.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20262 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly instructs: 'CVE-2026-20262 — match against your vulnerability scanner'. Federal patch deadline 2026-06-29 mandates rapid identification. This is the primary mechanism for locating vulnerable systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan all Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager systems for CVE-2026-20262 presence. Flag systems running unpatched versions. Cross-reference vulnerability results with network-exposure data to identify systems accessible from the internet (active targets).

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Request Detection on SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is explicitly classified as 'directory or path traversal vulnerability'. Exploitation manifests as malformed HTTP requests containing traversal sequences (.., encoded variants, unicode bypass).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to SD-WAN Manager administrative endpoints for path traversal indicators (../, %2e%2e, unicode normalization bypass). Baseline normal request patterns from authorized admin IPs. Alert on both successful and failed traversal attempts from any source.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Creation or Modification on SD-WAN Manager Systems
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability permits 'create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem of an affected system'. Post-exploitation, file operations on compromised systems should trigger alerts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SD-WAN Manager systems for unexpected file creation or overwrites, particularly in system directories (bin/, etc/, usr/, var/) and web-accessible paths. Correlate file operations with prior authentication and path traversal events. Establish baseline for normal administrative write activity.

suggestion.title: Authentication Events to Vulnerable SD-WAN Manager Services
suggestion.rationale: Attack chain requires 'authenticated, remote attacker'. Tracking authentication events enables early response when correlated with subsequent exploitation attempts or file operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline expected authentication patterns for SD-WAN Manager (users, times, source IPs, roles). Alert on brute-force attempts, successful logins from unexpected geographies, off-hours access, or privilege-escalation activity post-authentication. Correlate with known-compromised-credential feeds.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20262 Vulnerability Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'CISA KEV entry. The U.S. federal Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog only adds CVEs that have been observed exploited in the wild.' This is the foundational detection — asset inventory matching against Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager versions vulnerable to CVE-2026-20262.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query CMDB or vulnerability scanner for Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances. Identify version + patch status vs. CVE-2026-20262 fix version. Flag unpatched or patch-lagged instances. Prioritize remediation against federal due date 2026-06-29.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Exploitation Attempts on SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'directory or path traversal vulnerability that could allow an authenticated, remote attacker to create a file or overwrite any file.' Detection should capture exploitation payload patterns in HTTP/API requests to Manager endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager for path traversal payloads: (.., %2e%2e, /, %2f, encoded traversal sequences). Baseline against legitimate admin traffic. Alert on attempts from non-admin IP ranges or outside business hours.

suggestion.title: SD-WAN Manager Unauthorized Filesystem Writes
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem of an affected system.' Post-exploitation filesystem activity should show anomalous file creation/modification by the SD-WAN Manager service account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SD-WAN Manager service account for file creation/modification outside expected directories. Flag writes to /etc, /var, /opt, config files, or binaries. Baseline against patch windows and legitimate admin activity.

suggestion.title: SD-WAN Manager Authentication Context Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'authenticated, remote attacker' — exploitation requires valid credentials or session compromise. Baseline authentication patterns to detect credential abuse or session hijacking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Profile normal SD-WAN Manager admin authentication (source IPs, time-of-day, frequency, service accounts). Alert on: failed-then-successful auth pairs, logins from unusual geolocations, rapid re-auth attempts, or service account access outside maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager Exposure Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'public-facing application' (T1190 implies external exposure). Map Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances to network exposure and validate whether they should be internet-accessible.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances and validate network access controls. Query firewall rules and egress logs for inbound access to Manager ports (typically 8443). Flag instances with overly permissive internet exposure or missing VPN/WAF gating.

suggestion.title: Patch Compliance Hunt: CVE-2026-20262 by Due Date
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Federal patch due: 2026-06-29. Federal civilian agencies are required to remediate by the published due date.' This is a compliance-tracking detection tied to explicit deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Daily sweep of patch management system for Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager CVE-2026-20262 status. Count: total instances, patched, unpatched, patch-pending. Alert if any instance remains unpatched with < 7 days to federal due date.

suggestion.title: Typosquatting Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes the attack vector: 'Malicious Go Module Mirror's was named github.com/botdb-go/bolt, similar to the original one i.e. github.com/boltdb/bolt' and 'Typo squatting attacks happen when bad actors create and upload harmful software packages to online libraries using names very similar to popular ones.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Go module imports of packages with edit-distance similarity (<3 characters) to known legitimate packages, particularly from newly created or low-reputation accounts.
