suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create automated alert/SOAR task when vulnerability scanners report CVE-2026-20262 on any Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager. Flag as critical. Enforce federal due date 2026-06-29 as binding SLA for agencies; enterprises should match for compliance.

suggestion.title: Directory Traversal Patterns Against SD-WAN Manager Web Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'directory or path traversal vulnerability that could allow an authenticated, remote attacker to create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem.' Zero detection logic present for this core exploit mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Catalyst SD-WAN Manager endpoints for traversal patterns: (../, ..\, %2e%2e/, %252e%252e%252f and URL-encoded variants). Correlate with authenticated sessions to the same endpoint. Prioritize requests targeting config, credential, or system-path resources.

suggestion.title: Unexpected File Writes by Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Process
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly specifies impact: 'create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem.' Pipeline did not map this to file-system monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file creation/modification events from Catalyst SD-WAN Manager service account or process context. Flag writes to atypical paths (Windows: System32, registry hives, Program Files outside install dir; Linux: /etc, /root, /sys, /proc). Correlate with preceding authenticated web requests showing traversal signatures.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Asset Inventory Flag
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Federal patch due: 2026-06-29' and emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Pipeline must translate CVE into asset-driven hunt: identify exposed/unpatched instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference asset inventory for Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances not patched against CVE-2026-20262. Flag any instance with end-of-life or patch date after 2026-06-29. Validate external exposure via network segmentation audits and firewall rules.

suggestion.title: Authentication Success Followed by Path Traversal Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'authenticated, remote attacker'—two-stage attack requiring valid credentials first. Pipeline missed this sequence correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect session chains: successful authentication to Catalyst SD-WAN Manager UI followed (within 5-10 min) by HTTP requests containing path traversal payloads from same source IP. This raises fidelity above traversal-only detections by enforcing the authentication prerequisite.

suggestion.title: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Vulnerable Instance Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'patch lag is the silent killer' and references 'standard asset-exposure hunt'; pipeline generated zero asset exposure UCs despite CRIT severity and active exploitation
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results and asset inventory for Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances. Flag software versions predating 2026-06-29 baseline. Cross-reference exposed instances against internal approved management networks.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Payload Detection in SD-WAN Manager HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'directory or path traversal vulnerability'; exploitation requires sending traversal payloads (../, ..\\, encoded variants) to bypass access controls
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to SD-WAN Manager for path traversal patterns: ../, ..\\, %2e%2e/, or Unicode normalization attempts. Alert on traversal sequences appearing in URL paths or POST parameters immediately after successful authentication.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized File Creation/Modification on SD-WAN Manager Host
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem of an affected system'; successful exploitation manifests as abnormal file system mutations
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation/modification events on SD-WAN Manager host in critical paths (/etc, /var, /home, system32) occurring within 60 minutes of remote authentication. Establish baseline for maintenance activities and exclude known update windows.

suggestion.title: Authentication Followed by Suspicious Command Execution on SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Overwritten files (e.g., to web root or cron/scheduler locations) can enable code execution; article describes file write capability without specifying attacker intent beyond file manipulation
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful remote authentication to SD-WAN Manager with unexpected process spawning, especially from non-standard working directories (/tmp, /var/tmp) or with encoded arguments typical of post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Network Access to Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV implies active external exploitation; article notes 'remote attacker'; SD-WAN Manager should have restricted access posture
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful authentication to SD-WAN Manager from non-approved geographic regions or external IP ranges. Flag rapid authentication attempts (10+ within 5 min) indicating credential brute-force or scanning.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager Configuration File Integrity Violation
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal coupled with file-overwrite capability threatens system configuration and persistence; attackers likely target config, license, or bootstrap files for long-term access
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish file-integrity baseline for SD-WAN Manager configuration directories. Alert on hash mismatches, ownership changes, or timestamp anomalies in config/license files outside of scheduled maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Local LLM Inference Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 'worm operates entirely on local, open-weight models'—must detect when model inference pipelines execute outside dev environments, read sensitive files, or spawn children with unexpected arguments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Python/bash processes invoking transformers, ollama, or llama.cpp libraries with parent processes outside development/data-science tooling. Alert on model initialization reading /etc/passwd, ~/.ssh, credential paths, or environment variables before inference.

suggestion.title: Model File Persistence and Self-Replication
suggestion.rationale: Core mechanic: worm replicates via model artifacts. Pipeline missed detection for code embedded in .safetensors/.onnx files, model copies to startup folders (.bashrc, site-packages), or model staging in /tmp with execute bits.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor suspicious writes to ~/.bashrc, ~/.profile, /etc/init.d, or /usr/local/lib with model-like filenames. Detect model files with embedded executable sections or model copies propagating to shared/startup directories with repeated identical writes across systems.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration via LLM Processing of Sensitive Data
suggestion.rationale: Worm likely routes credentials, secrets, PII through local model inference before exfil. Article's 'local operation' design suggests data stays on-machine but is processed maliciously—must detect model processes accessing credential stores.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when model inference processes open sensitive paths (SSH keys, /etc/shadow, browser cookies, vaults) immediately before model execution or network I/O. Flag model loading from untrusted remote sources followed by credential access.

suggestion.title: Model-Based C2 via Inference Output Injection
suggestion.rationale: Open-weight models running locally enable novel C2: feeding network traffic or logs as model input and executing output as commands. Pipeline must detect model inference → shell execution chains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect model inference processes reading sockets, DNS logs, or HTTP response bodies, with inference output piped directly to bash/powershell interpreters. Flag model processes with abnormal network reads followed by child spawning with non-standard arguments.

suggestion.title: Compromised Open-Weight Model Distribution Chain IOC
suggestion.rationale: Article references specific threat model type but pipeline extracted zero model names, versions, repository URLs, or researcher attribution. These are direct IOCs for blocking/monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HuggingFace, GitHub, ModelScope downloads of model files (.pt, .safetensors, .onnx, .bin) with unusual sizes, timestamps, or commit hashes. Correlate model downloads with immediate invocation of model-loading libraries. Flag model repo clones with atypical branch or version selectors.

suggestion.title: Cross-Host Worm Replication via SSH/RCP Transfer
suggestion.rationale: Worm must replicate across infrastructure. Pipeline missed detection for model artifacts staged in shared directories or transferred via SSH/SCP to peer systems with subsequent execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SCP/SSH transfers of model files to multiple hosts in short timeframes or staged writes to /tmp/shared followed by remote execution invocations. Alert on model payload appearing post-transfer with execution permissions and matching hash across 3+ systems.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Pattern Detection in SD-WAN Manager HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'directory or path traversal vulnerability' — must detect ../, %2e%2e%2f, and equivalent encoded traversal sequences in HTTP requests to Catalyst SD-WAN Manager endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager for traversal payloads in URI and query parameters. Alert on ../../../ chains, encoded dot-slash variants, and null-byte injection attempts. Baseline clean request profiles and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: File Creation/Modification Post-Authentication on SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker can 'create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem' — detect suspicious filesystem activity immediately following successful remote authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal file operations on Catalyst SD-WAN Manager host. Alert on file creation/modification in sensitive paths (etc/, opt/, root/, config/) or with anomalous extensions (shell scripts, symlinks) within 60s of successful remote auth.

suggestion.title: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Internet Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'authenticated, remote attacker' accessing the service, indicating exposure to untrusted networks. Baseline and continuously inventory instances on public-routable addresses.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for Catalyst SD-WAN Manager on typical ports (8443, 2222) from internet-routable IP space. Compare weekly against approved production baselines. Alert on any new public instance not in change control.

suggestion.title: Credential Spraying or Failed-to-Success Auth Pattern on SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates 'authenticated, remote attacker' — baseline normal authentication patterns and flag indicators of exploitation attempts (spraying, unusual geolocation, rapid success after failures).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline successful and failed auth rates to Catalyst SD-WAN Manager per source IP and user. Alert on credential spraying (≥5 failed in 5min), successful auth from unusual country/ASN, or transition from multiple failed to successful within 10 min.

suggestion.title: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Exposed Asset Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' for CVE-2026-20262 and notes 'Federal civilian agencies are required to remediate by published due date.' Pipeline generated no corresponding detection use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners and asset inventories for Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances with positive CVE-2026-20262 detections. Cross-reference with firewall rules and network segmentation data to identify internet-facing exposure. CISA KEV status guarantees active exploitation; any gap between scanner detections and patch status is high-priority.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Exploitation Attempts Against SD-WAN Manager Web Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is a 'directory or path traversal' type. No detection use case was generated for the exploitation vector itself, only asset exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Cisco SD-WAN Manager management endpoints for path traversal payloads: URL-encoded dot-slash sequences (%2e%2e, %252e%252e), unencoded ../ patterns, and attempts to traverse outside intended application directories. Correlate successful traversals with 200/201 responses vs. typical 404/403 error patterns to distinguish exploitation from normal 404 noise.

suggestion.title: File System Modification on SD-WAN Manager Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker can 'create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem of an affected system.' This is the impact phase, but zero post-exploitation detection use cases were generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file create/modify events in Cisco SD-WAN Manager installation directories, especially web-root, configuration, and system-critical paths (e.g., /opt/cisco/…, /var/www if exposed). Correlate timing with exploitation windows derived from WAF/proxy logs. Expected false positives: legitimate patch deployments, log rotation, application cache writes; baseline against vendor-documented write patterns.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Lateral Movement from Compromised SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article describes SD-WAN Manager as a network appliance with potential to become a beachhead. No detection use case addresses post-compromise network reconnaissance or lateral movement to other infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound network behavior from Cisco SD-WAN Manager hosts for anomalies: connections to infrastructure management planes, unexpected DNS queries, authentication attempts to other network appliances (routers, firewalls, DNS/DHCP servers), or traffic patterns inconsistent with normal SD-WAN function. Alert on any eastbound connections to internal subnets post-exploitation window.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Authentication and Privilege Escalation on SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability allows 'authenticated, remote attacker' actions. Pipeline missed detection for post-exploitation session hijacking, account creation, or privilege elevation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco SD-WAN Manager authentication logs for: successful logins from atypical geolocations/ASNs, rapid admin account creation, password changes on privileged accounts, and session anomalies (unusual duration, concurrent sessions, privilege escalation). Correlate with known exploitation windows and inbound path-traversal attempts from WAF/proxy logs to confirm causal linkage.

suggestion.title: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager - CVE-2026-20262 Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly requires 'match against your vulnerability scanner' for CVE-2026-20262; pipeline generated zero detection use case for this critical actively-exploited vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scanner detection of CVE-2026-20262 in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager. Cross-reference with CMDB to identify at-risk instances. Flag assets unpatched after federal due date (2026-06-29) for immediate escalation.

suggestion.title: Exposed Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Asset Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'Standard asset-exposure hunt'; pipeline missed template-based detection for externally accessible SD-WAN manager interfaces despite explicit guidance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for internet-accessible Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager management interfaces (typically port 8443) via network logs and scans. Identify unexpected external routes to management ports. Validate firewall ingress rules restrict to authorized administrative networks only.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized File Write Activity on Compromised SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article describes post-exploitation impact: 'create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem'; pipeline omitted impact-phase detection for file manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file creation and modification on Catalyst SD-WAN Manager systems. Alert on writes outside normal application directories, especially system/config paths. Correlate with authentication anomalies to establish exploitation context.

suggestion.title: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'match against your vulnerability scanner' and CVE-2026-20262 is the primary detection vector. Pipeline failed to instantiate the asset-exposure template.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scanner results detecting CVE-2026-20262 on any Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instance. Flag by vulnerable version range and establish remediation SLA matching federal due date (2026-06-29).

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager File System Overwrite/Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article core threat: 'create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem'. Pipeline failed to map impact phase or recognize file-modification behavioral signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file creation/modification events on Catalyst SD-WAN Manager systems with focus on sensitive paths (config dirs, binary paths, log directories). Baseline normal file-op patterns and alert on anomalous creation/overwrite especially post-authentication.

suggestion.title: Public Exposure of Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application) explicitly cited; article notes 'against exposed assets' implying network-facing vulnerability. Pipeline missed asset inventory recommendation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory all Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances and flag any exposed on public networks or accessible beyond intended administrative segments. Cross-reference with CVE-2026-20262 patch status.

suggestion.title: Authentication Event + File System Change Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'authenticated, remote attacker', establishing attack sequence: auth success → file operation. Pipeline did not reconstruct this execution pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful authentication to Catalyst SD-WAN Manager with subsequent file creation/modification events within narrow time window (minutes). Baseline legitimate admin activity first; flag sequences matching attacker-controlled file paths.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager Configuration Change Audit
suggestion.rationale: Overwriting files on filesystem may alter application config or bypass controls. Article threat model includes unauthorized file modification on 'affected system'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If Catalyst SD-WAN Manager maintains audit logs of config/file changes, flag unexpected modifications especially to authentication, policy, or system files. Compare checksums of critical binaries/configs against known-good baseline.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager CVE-2026-20262 Path-Traversal Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'allows an authenticated, remote attacker to create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem' — yet no detection rules for web-request-level exploitation patterns were generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for authenticated HTTP requests to Cisco SD-WAN Manager endpoints containing path-traversal sequences (../, ..\, %2e%2e, etc.). Flag requests from admin/service accounts followed by immediate file-system write events on the host; prioritize requests to /etc, /var, and config-directory parents.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized File Write/Overwrite from Cisco SD-WAN Manager Process
suggestion.rationale: Article's explicit impact is 'create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem' — the actual forensic artifact post-exploitation, but zero detection use case for filesystem monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file-creation and file-write events originating from the Cisco SD-WAN Manager service process. Alert on writes to sensitive paths (/etc, /boot, /var/log, web-root parent, SSL cert stores) or high-volume overwrites of existing files in short timespan.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager Directory Enumeration via Path Traversal
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'directory or path traversal' vulnerability; attacker must probe/enumerate filesystem structure before targeting files — no detection of reconnaissance phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequences of HTTP requests from authenticated users containing directory-traversal payloads (../ chains, encoded variants, symbolic-link attacks). Correlate with 403/404 response patterns indicating directory enumeration; spike in requests during short window suggests active probing.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20262 Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entries by definition contain CVEs actively exploited in the wild. 'Known Exploited Vulnerabilities' catalog implies immediate threat. Asset exposure is the canonical baseline hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan asset inventory and vulnerability databases for Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances. Correlate against patched versions (due date 2026-06-29) and flag any unpatched systems or missing patch metadata. Cross-check against software deployment records for version lag.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Request Patterns on SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'directory or path traversal vulnerability' — HTTP requests containing traversal sequences (../, %2e%2e%2f, encoded variants) are direct attack vectors against this CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager admin consoles and APIs for path traversal payloads: relative directory traversal, double-encoding, unicode normalization, and backslash variants. Alert on any match regardless of HTTP response code.

suggestion.title: Anomalous File Write from SD-WAN Manager Process
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability permits attacker to 'create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem' — post-exploitation file operations initiated by the vulnerable process are directly observable in process and file creation events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file I/O initiated by Cisco SD-WAN Manager process (UID/GID, parent-child relationships). Flag writes to sensitive directories: /etc, /usr/bin, /var/www, cron directories, sudoers, systemd units, and any paths outside vendor-documented data directories.

suggestion.title: Authentication Abuse Against SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Exploit explicitly requires 'authenticated, remote attacker' — either credentials were compromised or authentication is weak/default. Account-based detection is essential to identify post-compromise footholds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect failed authentication spikes, successful logins from anomalous source IPs or geographies, repeated login attempts with known default credentials (admin/admin patterns), and accounts unused for 60+ days suddenly becoming active.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Command Execution via File Modification
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal + unrestricted file write permits modification of executables, scripts, cron jobs, and systemd units. 'Overwrite any file' directly enables code execution if writable system paths are targeted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate suspicious file write events from SD-WAN Manager with child process spawning, unexpected privilege escalation, or execution of newly modified system binaries. Flag execution of scripts/binaries touched by the vulnerable process within 5 minutes of write.

suggestion.title: Configuration Tampering and Policy Drift Detection
suggestion.rationale: File overwrite capability directly threatens configuration integrity. Malicious config changes enable traffic redirection, persistence, lateral movement, or VPN hijacking — all persistent and stealthy.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enable file integrity monitoring on critical SD-WAN Manager configs (routing tables, access policies, VPN certificates, authentication settings). Alert on hash mismatches, config reload events following suspicious file writes, and unauthorized changes to admin user accounts or privilege levels.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Within Compressed Timeframe
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly frames attack success as reaching exfiltration in 72 minutes ('Attackers can move from access to exfiltration in 72 minutes'), implying rapid lateral movement detection is core to closing the speed gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag multiple lateral movement attempts (same source, multiple destinations) within a 4-hour window. Correlation of logon events across different credential contexts or impossible travel times indicates reconnaissance during compression phase.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration Velocity Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article title and description center on the 72-minute window to exfiltration; this implies detection must identify unusually rapid data staging and transfer ('close the speed gap').
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect aggregated data transfer volume exceeding baseline within a 2-hour sliding window per user/asset. Flag connections to new or rare external IP ranges combined with file reads from sensitive repositories.

suggestion.title: Initial Access Indicator Correlation
suggestion.rationale: 72-minute clock starts at 'access' per the article narrative; pipeline must model entry vectors even if not campaign-specific IOCs are provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate suspicious email delivery (malware sandboxing bypass, rare attachment types) with first-time process execution and immediate credential access attempts. Short elapsed time between artifact and follow-on activity signals compressed attack.

suggestion.title: Automated Response Time Benchmark Instrumentation
suggestion.rationale: Article discusses SOC closing the speed gap via 'AI-driven automation' and 'threat hunting'—pipeline should model detection-to-response latency baselines, not just attack detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution chains that mask process lineage, use living-off-the-land binaries, or execute from temporary/system paths within the first hour of first-seen activity. Correlate with concurrent cleanup or log-deletion attempts.

suggestion.title: Child process spawn from node after Vitest config overwrite with non-standard binary
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability leads to 'RCE'—config reload executes attacker code. Pipeline/article does not detect the second-stage child process (e.g., bash, powershell, curl spawned by injected config). UC_5_6 stops at node respawn; this extends to child execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Within 5 seconds of node.exe process restart (detected via UC_5_6), detect spawning of child processes with low prevalence (not npm, not node itself) or suspicious command strings (curl, powershell, /bin/sh). Parent command should contain 'vitest' or 'vite'.

suggestion.title: Vitest API WebSocket frame inspection for CDP method payloads
suggestion.rationale: Article core claim: 'disabling write and exec does not prevent CDP' because CDP methods bypass the allowWrite/allowExec gates. No UC monitors the actual CDP protocol conversation. Network-level detection of CDP commands (e.g., 'Runtime.evaluate', 'FileSystem.write' patterns in WebSocket frames) is absent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Decode Vitest WebSocket RPC traffic on port 63315; alert on CDP method names (Runtime.evaluate, FileSystem.*, etc.) transmitted from non-browser-process source IPs or with unusual parameter payloads (e.g., config file paths, child process spawn calls).

suggestion.title: Node.js --inspect or --debug flag exposure in Vitest runner process
suggestion.rationale: Article does not mention Node debugging ports but CDI exploit can persist via config to inject inspect flags. Exposed debugging interface (port 9229+) is independent RCE vector. Should detect Vitest node processes started with debugging enabled to non-loopback.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when node.exe spawned with '--inspect', '--debug', or '--inspect-brk' flags in ProcessCommandLine AND (inspect-port is non-loopback OR process binding to 0.0.0.0). Cross-reference with Vitest in command line.

suggestion.title: Rapid succession of config file reads by node after external connection to Vitest API
suggestion.rationale: Article implies config is parsed on demand or reload. An inbound connection (UC_5_4) followed immediately by config file read (not write) could be reconnaissance before exploitation. No UC covers the pre-exploitation probing phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate inbound connection to port 63315 (non-loopback) with read access to vite.config.*, vitest.config.*, or .env files by node.exe within 10 seconds. Volume: alert if >5 config reads in 30-second window.

suggestion.title: Package.json or lock file modification by browser process
suggestion.rationale: Article states config can control execution. An advanced attack could also modify package.json's scripts or dependency list via CDP to achieve persistence or supply-chain effect. Browser-initiated file writes to package.json, package-lock.json, or yarn.lock would indicate deeper compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect browser binary (chrome.exe, firefox.exe, etc.) writing to package.json, package-lock.json, or yarn.lock in same directory as vitest project. Even single write is anomalous.

suggestion.title: Unusual environment variable passed to Vitest process from external network context
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'browser.api.host' parameter but does not specify if it can be injected via query parameters, headers, or env vars at spawn time. If Vitest config can read environment, attacker could inject VITEST_* vars over network. No detection for env-var-based config injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on node.exe or npm.exe spawning Vitest with VITEST_BROWSER_API_HOST, VITEST_ALLOW_WRITE=true, VITEST_ALLOW_EXEC=true, or other Vitest-specific env vars set to non-default values, especially if parent process is a web-tier service or inbound network listener.

suggestion.title: Google Workspace Email Forwarding Rule Creation by Anomalous Actor
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'abused Google Workspace Rules' as the attack mechanism — rule-creation audit logs are the primary detection vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Google Workspace admin audit logs for CreateForwardingAddress or filter-creation events from new/compromised service accounts. Alert on rules forwarding to external domains, rules created during off-hours or from anomalous geolocations, and rules targeting mail from research or defense-sector users.

suggestion.title: Bulk Email Exfiltration via Forwarding to External Account
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'steal Research and Defense Emails' (bulk, plural) — implies widespread rule-based forwarding detectable via traffic volume and rule scope.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on email forwarding rules that apply to high-volume distribution lists, shared mailboxes, or entire user mailboxes; rules forwarding to newly-provisioned external accounts; or multiple rules created in sequence targeting the same external destination.

suggestion.title: Compromised Credential Email Rule Creation Across Multiple Mailboxes
suggestion.rationale: Attack targeting organization-wide 'Research and Defense' operations suggests single compromised account or token with broad delegation — detect cross-mailbox rule creation patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag a single service account, admin account, or delegated user creating email forwarding rules on 5+ distinct mailboxes within 24 hours, especially if all rules forward to the same external address or share forensic timestamp patterns.

suggestion.title: Credential Abuse and Anomalous Google Workspace Admin Activity
suggestion.rationale: Email rule abuse requires valid compromised credentials; article does not detail theft method but admin activity anomalies (new geographies, service account API calls) are proxy signals.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for successful sign-ins followed immediately by email rule creation; admin activity from new IP ranges or geographies; and Gmail Settings API calls (forwardingAddresses.create, filters.create) from service accounts with long-lived or recently-rotated credentials.

suggestion.title: Google Workspace API-Driven Email Rule Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Sophisticated attackers may bypass UI and manipulate rules via Gmail Settings API — API-level rule creation is distinct from UI interactions and harder to attribute to human users.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on gmail.users.settings.forwardingAddresses.create and gmail.users.settings.filters.create API calls originating from new/anomalous service accounts, with high event frequency, or targeting forwarding addresses not previously linked to the user account.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Developer Tool Execution from Non-Standard Path
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes attacker 'turning developer tools into malware delivery channels'—direct indicator that legitimate-looking tools are weaponized and executed on developer workstations. Pipeline omitted detection for this core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor execution of downloaded developer tools (compilers, SDKs, build systems, package managers) with parent processes from web browsers or %TEMP% directories. Correlate with file properties lacking legitimate publisher signatures. Detect child processes spawning network connections or file I/O outside expected development directories.

suggestion.title: Developer Workstation C2 Beaconing to Suspicious Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Malware-laden developer tools should beacon to attacker C2. Article scenario implies post-execution command-and-control. Pipeline failed to suggest detection for anomalous outbound connections from developer machines.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound HTTPS/DNS from developer workstations to newly-registered domains, RFC1918 IPs, or IPs with no ASN reputation. Flag connection patterns consistent with malware heartbeat (regular intervals, small payload sizes). Correlate with tool execution timeframe.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain: Download of Malicious Package from Non-Official Repository
suggestion.rationale: Title references 'developer tools'—typically obtained via package managers (npm, PyPI, Maven, NuGet). Pipeline missed detection for package installs from typosquatted or malicious registry mirrors. Article phrase implies tool trojanization before download.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package manager (npm, pip, nuget, maven) downloads for: registry URLs deviating from official domains, packages with suspiciously low version counts, downloads from non-pinned or newly-created registry entries, and missing or invalid TLS certificates. Cross-reference package names against typosquatting patterns (double letters, vowel substitutions).

suggestion.title: Phishing: Developer-Targeted Spearphish with Malicious Tool Link
suggestion.rationale: To deliver trojanized tools, attacker must first social-engineer developers. Article establishes targeting of developer population. Pipeline ignored email-level detection for tool-impersonating phishing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag inbound emails to developers with: links to lookalike tool domains (e.g., npm-update[.]com vs. npmjs[.]com), urgency language around tool updates, newly-registered sender domains, and attachments claiming to be installer binaries. Correlate click/download events with subsequent tool execution.

suggestion.title: Fake Developer Tool Domain with SSL Certificate Issued in Last 30 Days
suggestion.rationale: Attacker must host malicious tool clone. Article implies web-based tool distribution. Pipeline did not surface infrastructure reconnaissance or domain registration IOCs typical of North Korean APT campaigns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Certificate Transparency logs and DNS for domains closely resembling popular developer tools (npm, pip, maven, gradle, docker, git, etc.). Flag domains registered <30 days prior, issued with Let's Encrypt (fast, cheap, unvalidated), and not belonging to official tool vendors. Correlate with proxy logs for non-standard HTTP requests.

suggestion.title: North Korean APT Infrastructure Reuse: Known Lazarus C2 IP or Domain in Developer Context
suggestion.rationale: Article attributes attack to North Korean actor. Pipeline should cross-reference article context against known Lazarus/APT38 infrastructure. Pipeline produced no actor attribution or shared IOC correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-check outbound network connections and DNS requests from developer workstations against OSINT-derived Lazarus C2 IP blocks (Shadowserver, Shodan historical data, public APT reports). Detect connections to any known NK APT infrastructure with developer-originating traffic, even at low volume.

suggestion.title: Process Execution from npm/node-gyp Build Context
suggestion.rationale: Article centers on binding.gyp's ability to execute arbitrary commands during package installation; detection should capture process spawning under npm context with suspicious child-process patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned by npm or node-gyp (e.g., cc1plus, python, sh) executing shell commands, network tools (curl, wget), or interpreters during package install phase. Baseline benign compilers and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Network Activity During npm Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Malicious binding.gyp scripts can exfiltrate data or download payload; detect outbound connections initiated by npm/node processes to non-package-registry destinations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DNS queries or HTTPS connections from npm/node-gyp processes to non-standard domains (excluding npm registry, github, and known CDNs). Flag connections to attacker-controlled infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized File Modification via binding.gyp Post-Install Hooks
suggestion.rationale: Article implies binding.gyp post-install scripts can write to arbitrary file system locations; detect unauthorized modifications to system binaries, startup scripts, or sensitive config files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on writes to /etc/profile, ~/.bashrc, cron directories, systemd units, or other persistence vectors when initiated from node_modules or npm cache contexts. Correlate with post-install script execution.

suggestion.title: Environment Variable Access in npm Build Scripts
suggestion.rationale: Binding.gyp scripts run with access to parent shell environment; malicious scripts can steal credentials, API keys, or tokens exposed as environment variables.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm/node-gyp spawned processes invoking env, printenv, or accessing $ENVIRONMENT variables, particularly in unattended/CI environments where secrets are typically injected.

suggestion.title: Elevated Privilege Execution in npm Install
suggestion.rationale: If developers run npm install with sudo, malicious binding.gyp inherits root; detect npm processes executing as uid=0 or SYSTEM in single-user installation contexts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for npm or node-gyp processes with elevated UID/SYSTEM privilege spawning child processes. Flag when elevation context (sudo/runas) originates from unprivileged user session.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance via binding.gyp System Information Gathering
suggestion.rationale: Build scripts can invoke system reconnaissance commands (uname, whoami, id) to enumerate target environment before payload execution or exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm/node-gyp context spawning system enumeration tools (uname, whoami, id, lsb_release, systeminfo, tasklist) that deviate from normal C++ compilation workflows.

suggestion.title: HTTP Path Traversal Pattern Detection — Cisco SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'directory or path traversal vulnerability.' Pipeline generated zero detection for traversal patterns (../, URL-encoded variants) in HTTP requests to Cisco endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager for path traversal indicators: '../', '..\', '%2e%2e', absolute paths, or Unicode-encoded variants. Prioritize requests from unauthenticated sources or correlate with successful credential use.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Filesystem Write Operations Post-Authentication on Cisco SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem.' Pipeline generated no detection for post-authentication file mutation events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation/modification events on Cisco SD-WAN Manager hosts within minutes of successful authentication. Flag files in /etc, /admin, /config, web root, or unexpected binary/script files as high-confidence exploitation indicators.

suggestion.title: Internet-Exposed Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Inventory
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV implies public-facing exposure; article describes remote exploitation. Pipeline generated no asset-exposure hunt despite federal agency requirement to identify and segment exposed instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager assets against WAN-side firewall rules and internet-reachable vulnerability scanner results. Flag any externally accessible instances; prioritize patching by CISA due date 2026-06-29.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20262 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes CISA KEV catalog inclusion and federal patch deadline. Pipeline generated zero scanner-based detection for the CVE signature itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Surface any vulnerability scanner detections for CVE-2026-20262 against Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager. Track instance count, network location, and patch status. Escalate per federal deadline and alert on any newly discovered instances.

suggestion.title: Typo-Squatted Package Import Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attack: 'similar to popular ones. They hope people will mistakenly download.' github.com/botdb-go/bolt vs github.com/boltdb/bolt—single-char and namespace spoofing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Go projects where go.mod/go.sum imports packages differing from canonical high-popularity modules by edit-distance ≤2 or namespace substitution. Detect imports from newly-registered namespaces (botdb-go, boltdb-mirror, etc.) that closely resemble established packages. Cross-ref against Go Module Proxy top-1000 and SLSA/OpenSSF package reputation lists.

suggestion.title: Module Cache Persistence Post-Removal
suggestion.rationale: Core evasion: 'Go Module Mirror service stored it permanently' and 'cached the backdored module' despite 'malicious Go Module Mirror's was reverted to the actual legitimate version.' Module remained exploitable for 3 years post-deletion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Go module downloads where version timestamp precedes known-removal date or module hash mismatches authoritative source. Alert on cache-hit retrievals for packages flagged in Go vulnerability database or Snyk advisories. Cross-correlate project go.mod update timestamps with package removal timelines to identify retrospective compromise windows.

suggestion.title: C2 Command Execution via Backdoored Import
suggestion.rationale: Article payload capability: 'This backdoor allows hackers to remotely control infected computers through a server that sends them commands.' Executed at package import time when 'developers to update the version.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Go runtime processes for unexpected outbound network connections during module initialization or import. Detect HTTP/HTTPS POST requests with serialized command payloads or shell-command patterns. Correlate network anomalies with recent Go dependency updates or import of packages from suspicious namespaces. Flag exfiltration patterns matching Go binary marshalling.

suggestion.title: Package Checksum Integrity Verification Failure
suggestion.rationale: Malicious v1.3.1 served via proxy despite legitimate version being available: 'when found, was reverted to the actual legitimate version however, Go Module Mirror's indefinite caching of modules kicked in.' Same package, different binaries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare module checksums in go.sum against Module Proxy responses and authoritative GitHub repo. Flag mismatches where semantic version matches but hash diverges. Alert on cache-serving of outdated/revoked module versions. Monitor for clients accepting go.mod updates that silently change dependency hashes without version bump.

suggestion.title: Supply-Chain Backdoor Activation on Dependency Update
suggestion.rationale: Article timeline: package uploaded Nov 2021, 'led developers to update the version' years later, 'stayed in the system for 3 years' before discovery Feb 2025. Detection window is bulk update events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk Go module updates within organizations, especially targeting database/utility packages. Monitor for post-update process anomalies: unexpected network connections, credential access, file modifications. Correlate update timing with known malicious package release dates. Alert if patched projects still exhibit C2-like behavior post-update.

suggestion.title: Repository Namespace Hijacking and Impersonation
suggestion.rationale: Attack exploited lax package-namespace controls: attacker registered github.com/botdb-go/bolt alongside original github.com/boltdb/bolt. Original had '80+ unresolved issues since 2015,' signaling maintenance gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag new package namespaces with >90% feature/API overlap with established high-value packages but created within 12 months of threat activity clusters. Monitor for namespace-variants appearing around maintenance gaps in legitimate packages. Detect projects importing both legitimate and typo-squatted versions simultaneously. Alert when new namespace authors have no prior publishing history.

suggestion.title: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Exposed on Internet
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'authenticated, remote attacker' can exploit; CISA KEV implies active exploitation. Detection requires first establishing which instances are internet-facing. Article explicitly references 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' but pipeline generated no detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Cisco SD-WAN Manager service (typically HTTPS on nonstandard ports, responds with Cisco banners/management interface fingerprints). Correlate external scan data or passive DNS to identify management endpoints reachable from untrusted networks. Baseline should exclude intentional VPN concentrators.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager Authentication Brute Force or Credential Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability requires 'authenticated' attacker status. Article does not state pre-auth RCE. Detection gap: how did attacker gain credentials? Brute force, reuse, or insider.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco SD-WAN Manager authentication logs for failed login attempts (esp. from external IPs), velocity spikes, or lateral login attempts across multiple manager instances. Flag successful logins from new/rare sources or outside business hours.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager Arbitrary File Write via Path Traversal
suggestion.rationale: Article core threat: 'create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem'. Pipeline provided zero filesystem detection. This is the impact phase and most direct exploit signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor filesystem writes by Cisco SD-WAN Manager processes (vmmanaged, viptela services) for path traversal sequences (../, ..\, encoded variants) in HTTP/REST API payloads. Flag file creates/overwrites in sensitive directories (/etc, /opt, /var) outside patch maintenance windows. Establish FIM baseline for critical SD-WAN config files.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20262 Vulnerability Presence in Network
suggestion.rationale: Article is CISA KEV with federal patch due 2026-06-29. Standard practice: scan asset inventory for CVE presence, compare vulnerability scan DB against known-exploited list.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability management platform for CVE-2026-20262 across all endpoints, especially Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances. Cross-reference with network discovery (shodan, internal asset DB) to identify unpatched instances. Escalate any CVE-2026-20262 findings to patch queue with CISA KEV priority.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager Configuration Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal + file write allows attacker to modify SD-WAN policies, routes, or VPN configs. Article does not specify which files but tampering with network policies is likely high-impact attack objective.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco SD-WAN Manager for configuration change events not initiated by known administrators. Correlate with authentication anomalies. Flag changes to routing tables, VPN policies, or system settings outside of change control windows. Compare running config checksums to last-known-good baseline.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager Service Disruption Detection
suggestion.rationale: File overwrite (esp. of binaries, libraries, or config) can cause service crash or hung processes. Article threat includes DoS via filesystem manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco SD-WAN Manager service availability and process health. Alert on unexpected service restarts, hung processes, or crashes correlated with unusual file activity. Baseline normal restart cadence and flag anomalous patterns.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20262 Vulnerability Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'CVE-2026-20262 — match against your vulnerability scanner.' CISA KEV entries are actively exploited and federal agencies have binding remediation timelines. Asset exposure is the foundational hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner output for CVE-2026-20262 matches against Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager deployments. If patched status is uncertain or scanner lag is suspected, cross-reference with network asset inventory for exposed Manager instances on internet-facing networks.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Creation/Overwrite on Catalyst SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability allows attacker to 'create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem of an affected system.' Post-exploitation file writes should be detectable via file system monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file creation and modification events on Catalyst SD-WAN Manager systems, especially in sensitive directories (/etc, /opt, application directories, authentication config paths). Baseline normal file operations and alert on anomalous writes outside maintenance windows. Correlate with authentication logs to identify attacker provenance.

suggestion.title: Authenticated Remote Session Followed by File System Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'authenticated, remote attacker' exploiting the vulnerability. Behavioral hunt should correlate valid authentication events with anomalous file operations in same session to catch post-exploitation activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful remote authentication to Catalyst SD-WAN Manager with subsequent file system modification events within 5-minute window. Alert on authenticated sessions that spawn processes with file write operations outside expected maintenance patterns, especially path traversal indicators ('../', '..\') in process arguments or file paths.

suggestion.title: Directory Traversal Pattern Detection in Manager API Logs
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is 'directory or path traversal' type. Application logs may capture path traversal attempts ('../', '..\') in API requests or file operation parameters before successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse Catalyst SD-WAN Manager application and HTTP access logs for path traversal sequences: ../, ..\, encoded variants (%2e%2e, %252e), or absolute path references in file operation parameters. Flag authenticated sessions with 3+ traversal attempts within 60 seconds as reconnaissance activity.

suggestion.title: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Vulnerable to CVE-2026-20262
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2026-20262 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and emphasizes CISA KEV entries are actively exploited. Pipeline generated zero vulnerability-detection use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner output for CVE-2026-20262 findings on Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances. Alert on any match within the organization's fleet, prioritizing internet-facing deployments. Correlate scanner results with patch-management records to identify unpatched systems past the federal due date (2026-06-29).

suggestion.title: Internet-Exposed Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and T1190 implies public-facing exposure is the attack vector. No asset-discovery use cases generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for inbound internet traffic to Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager management interfaces (typically TCP 830, 22, or NETCONF). Alert on any external-origin connections to affected systems. Cross-reference with inventory to identify systems not intended for external access.

suggestion.title: Unexpected File Creation/Modification on Catalyst SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states the vulnerability allows attacker to 'create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem.' Pipeline missed the file-system impact entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Catalyst SD-WAN Manager systems for file creation or modification events in sensitive directories (OS system paths, application config directories). Baseline normal file operations and alert on deviations, especially post-authentication or following failed login attempts. Correlate with application logs for evidence of exploitation.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Exploitation Attempts Against SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'directory or path traversal vulnerability' requiring HTTP-level exploitation. No network-payload or HTTP-pattern detection suggested by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests containing path traversal sequences (../, ..\ , %2e%2e) directed at Catalyst SD-WAN Manager management endpoints. Flag requests from non-whitelisted sources. Monitor for 40x/50x error spikes indicating reconnaissance or exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Authenticated Session Followed by File System Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability requires 'authenticated, remote attacker.' Pipeline should surface detection of auth-then-anomaly chains as the exploitation pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful authentication to Catalyst SD-WAN Manager with subsequent file-creation or file-modification events on the same host. Alert on short time-windows between auth and filesystem changes, especially if the user account performing file operations is not typical for that system.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20262 Cisco SD-WAN Manager Vulnerability Scan Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly specifies 'Standard asset-exposure hunt—the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in template' and 'match against your vulnerability scanner' for CVE-2026-20262, yet pipeline generated zero use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scanner detections of CVE-2026-20262 in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager deployments. Prioritize systems exposed to remote networks. Federal patch due date 2026-06-29 is enforcement deadline for alerts.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager Path Traversal File Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'allow[s] authenticated, remote attacker to create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem'—no UC generated for detection of file system exploitation post-authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation or overwrite activity on Cisco SD-WAN Manager host outside expected configuration management windows. Monitor system paths, configuration directories, and application directories for unauthorized file writes correlated with remote authentication events to the manager service.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Authentication to Cisco SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability requires 'authenticated, remote attacker' as prerequisite. This authentication requirement is the first gate in attack chain but has no corresponding detection use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco SD-WAN Manager authentication logs for successful remote logins, especially from unexpected source IPs or outside normal maintenance windows. Flag multiple failed login attempts followed by success, or authentication from untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager Directory Traversal File Write
suggestion.rationale: Article states exploit allows attacker to 'create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem' — this is the core impact and requires detection of suspicious file operations post-authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful SD-WAN Manager authentication (esp. unusual source IPs or after failed attempts) with file creation/modification events in sensitive system paths (etc/, proc/, sys/, or paths containing '..' traversal sequences). Flag writes to system binaries, config files, or web-accessible directories.

suggestion.title: Exposed Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Instance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article references checking across 'fleet' for exposed assets and mentions vulnerability requires network access. Pipeline must detect publicly-reachable SD-WAN Manager instances vulnerable to remote exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for successful connections to Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager on standard ports (443, 8443) from internet-facing endpoints. Identify instances responding with vendor-specific HTTP headers or version banners. Correlate with CVE-2026-20262 scanner matches and CVSS severity.

suggestion.title: Post-Authentication File System Traversal Indicators in SD-WAN Logs
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability explicitly requires 'authenticated, remote attacker' — need detection of abnormal file-system operations within SD-WAN Manager application logs post-login, including path-traversal attempt indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SD-WAN Manager application logs for sequences: (1) successful authentication from non-standard IP, (2) immediate file-operation API calls, (3) paths containing traversal characters (.., /etc/, /var/, absolute paths from web-root). Alert on deviation from known-good admin workflows.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager CVE-2026-20262 Signature Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title and CISA KEV listing explicitly reference CVE-2026-20262 as observable IOC; pipeline must create baseline signature detection for exploitation attempts against this specific CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to Catalyst SD-WAN Manager endpoint paths known to be vulnerable in CVE-2026-20262 (typically directory-traversal payload injection in file-upload or REST API parameters). Monitor for 40x/50x responses following abnormal query patterns; 200-OK + subsequent file-creation events are high-confidence exploitation signals.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Account Activity
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires authentication; article does not specify if default credentials exist, but any unusual account usage (password sprays, credential stuffing, dormant accounts awakening) warrant escalation given active exploitation in the wild.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for authentication anomalies: failed login attempts preceding successful login, logins from unusual geographies/IPs (if multi-site SD-WAN), service-account usage outside business hours, privilege escalation within minutes of login, credential reuse across multiple Manager instances.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20262 Patch Compliance and Vulnerability Assessment
suggestion.rationale: Article states federal due-date is 2026-06-29 and CISA KEV context emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' — pipeline should generate baseline asset inventory + patch-status use case aligned with regulatory due-dates.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner inventory for Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances with missing patches for CVE-2026-20262 (version < remediated baseline). Cross-reference against CISA KEV due-date (2026-06-29); flag any still-unpatched instances after compliance deadline. Correlate with network reachability (externally-routable IPs) to prioritize risk.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Internet-Facing
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly references asset-exposure hunt and CISA KEV status implies active exploitation against exposed instances. 'Federal patch due: 2026-06-29' signals imminent risk to unpatched internet-facing systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances accessible on WAN-facing ports (typically 443, 8443). Cross-reference against patched version inventory. Alert if internet-routable management IPs exist for CVE-2026-20262 unpatched versions.

suggestion.title: HTTP Path Traversal: CVE-2026-20262 Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is 'directory or path traversal'—classic web app attack pattern requiring detection of encoded/obfuscated traversal attempts (../, ..\, %2e%2e, etc.) against SD-WAN Manager endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager containing path traversal payloads (../, ..\, double-encoded variants, null bytes) in URI or query parameters. Baseline known legitimate paths and alert on deviation.

suggestion.title: File Creation/Modification Post-Authentication: SD-WAN Manager Filesystem
suggestion.rationale: Article describes impact: 'create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem'. Requires detection of unexpected file I/O after authentication, especially in critical directories (config, binaries, startup scripts).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SD-WAN Manager process for file-write operations to sensitive paths post-exploitation. Alert if config files, web root, startup scripts, or system executables are modified outside maintenance windows by the application process.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Configuration Tampering: SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: SD-WAN Manager stores critical network routing, VPN, and access control configs. Path traversal enabling file overwrite threatens integrity of network configuration and enables persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected modifications to SD-WAN Manager configuration files (XML, JSON, .properties) or unexpected file creation in config directories. Correlate with authentication logs to identify accounts performing unexpected changes outside change windows.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation RCE Detection: SD-WAN Manager Write-to-Executable
suggestion.rationale: File-overwrite vulnerability could enable arbitrary code execution if attacker writes to executable paths, web root, or dynamically-loaded library directories. Article impact statement does not exclude RCE as secondary outcome.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected process execution originating from SD-WAN Manager application directory or child processes, and file writes from the manager process to common RCE vectors (web app dirs, library paths, startup scripts). Cross-correlate with path traversal attempt timeline.

suggestion.title: WinRAR Archive Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'WinRAR Flaw Exploited' — vulnerability is the initial access vector. Pipeline missed the archive-based delivery and exploitation phase entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WinRAR/Unrar.exe spawning child processes (PowerShell, cmd.exe, cscript.exe) immediately after archive extraction. Alert on unusual parent processes: Outlook, Explorer instances opening files from Downloads/Temp/AppData paths.

suggestion.title: Stealer Malware Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Deploy Stealers' — execution phase is the core attack objective. No execution-phase detection suggested by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect script interpreter processes (powershell.exe, cscript.exe, cmd.exe) spawned from WinRAR-extracted content or temp directories with command-line indicators of credential/data enumeration.

suggestion.title: Credential Access — Stealer Information Collection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly targets credential theft via stealer payloads but pipeline did not map credential access techniques or detection scenarios.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes accessing credential stores: LSASS memory operations, browser profile directories (Chrome/Firefox), email client vaults, and registry hive reads (SAM/SECURITY). Correlate with WinRAR process timeline.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration to C2 Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Stolen data must reach 'Russia-aligned groups' infrastructure. Exfiltration phase absent from pipeline reconstruction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline WinRAR and child process network behavior. Alert on unexpected outbound HTTPS/HTTP to non-Microsoft destinations, particularly Russian/CIS IP space, correlating with credential access activity.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20262 HTTP Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 'authenticated, remote attacker' can 'create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem' via path traversal; pipeline generated zero UCs for detecting exploitation attempts despite this being primary detection objective.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco SD-WAN Manager endpoints for HTTP requests containing path traversal patterns (../, %2e%2e%2f) or file-read/write directives. Correlate with successful authentication logs and flag requests originating from non-corporate networks or ASNs.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager Unauthorized File System Modifications
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies post-exploitation capability to 'overwrite any file on the filesystem'; no post-exploitation file-write UC generated despite this being the primary impact vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation or modification in Cisco SD-WAN Manager directories (config, binaries, certificates) executed by SD-WAN process or children outside maintenance windows. Flag overwrites of critical system files or suspicious binary modifications.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager Internet Exposure and Baseline Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article requires 'remote attacker' access; article explicitly recommends 'asset-exposure hunt' but pipeline generated zero UCs for identifying exposed or unauthorized instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Cisco SD-WAN Manager instances reachable from untrusted networks via port enumeration or certificate discovery. Alert on authentication success from non-corporate geolocations or impossible-travel patterns to establish baseline access violations.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager Credential Compromise or Weak Authentication Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article requires 'authenticated' access as prerequisite; pipeline missed credential-access UC for detecting compromised or brute-forced credentials enabling exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SD-WAN Manager logs for credential spray patterns (failed → successful auth) or API token generation from non-standard service accounts. Alert on tokens used from geographically impossible locations or accessed via unexpected client libraries.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20262 Scanner Match Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE: CVE-2026-20262' as the matching IOC for vulnerability scanners and recommends standard asset-exposure hunting. Pipeline failed to generate this fundamental UC despite guidance to substitute the CVE into template hunts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager assets against CVE-2026-20262 in vulnerability scanner output. Flag unpatched instances post 2026-06-29 federal due date, as exploitation is actively observed in wild.

suggestion.title: SD-WAN Manager Path Traversal Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'directory or path traversal vulnerability' but pipeline surfaced no web-log detection. HTTP requests to SD-WAN Manager interface should contain traversal payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt SD-WAN Manager access logs for HTTP requests containing path-traversal sequences (../, ..\\ , Unicode variants, etc.) in URL parameters and request bodies. Baseline normal directory-access patterns and alert on anomalies targeting config, script, or system paths.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized File Creation on SD-WAN Manager Host
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could allow... to create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem'—critical post-exploitation indicator requiring filesystem monitoring. Pipeline did not surface file-integrity or file-creation detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file-creation and modification events on Catalyst SD-WAN Manager hosts for writes outside vendor installation directories and system baselines. Alert on creation of executable files (.sh, .bat, .ps1, .exe) in unexpected paths; baseline service filesystem changes.

suggestion.title: SD-WAN Manager Process Spawning Children
suggestion.rationale: Arbitrary file-write + web-app context strongly implies potential to write and execute backdoors/payloads. Article does not exclude execution pathway; process behavior analysis is critical for post-exploitation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Catalyst SD-WAN Manager service spawning unexpected child processes (shells, interpreters, scripting engines) or spawning binaries from non-standard locations. Establish baseline of expected subprocess activity per deployment.

suggestion.title: Audit Log or Configuration File Overwrite on SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article's 'overwrite any file' capability directly enables attack-log erasure (T1562) or config persistence. File-integrity monitoring should flag unexpected writes to logging and config paths.

suggestion.title: Wallpaper Engine Spawning Suspicious Child Processes
