suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor configuration file modifications on Catalyst SD-WAN Manager systems (VPN tunnel configs, peer definitions, routing rules, authentication settings). Alert on anomalous network traffic sourced from or routed through the manager. Correlate with file modification timestamps to detect tampering.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager Exposed Asset Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV implies 'active exploitation against exposed assets' — requires inventory and network exposure assessment to identify internet-facing SD-WAN Manager instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset management and vulnerability scanners to identify all Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances. Flag those with internet-facing access or accessible from untrusted networks. Cross-reference against patched versions for CVE-2026-20262.

suggestion.title: Authenticated Path Traversal Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'authenticated, remote attacker' executing 'directory or path traversal' — HTTP request logs should show path traversal patterns post-authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to Cisco SD-WAN Manager for path traversal syntax (../, ..\, URL-encoded variants) following successful authentication. Alert on requests attempting to traverse outside the application's expected directory structure.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized File Write Post-SD-WAN Manager Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers can 'create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem' — file system events correlated with remote auth indicate active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation or modification events on Cisco SD-WAN Manager hosts within 60-120 seconds of remote successful authentication. Prioritize writes to system/config directories, application binaries, or credentials stores.

suggestion.title: Failed Authentication Spike to SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires successful authentication — reconnaissance phase may involve multiple failed login attempts before successful compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track failed login attempts to Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager interfaces. Alert on >5 failed attempts from a single source IP within 10 minutes, or failed attempts followed by successful auth and suspicious file operations.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Privilege Configuration File Modifications
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal attackers can overwrite arbitrary files — compromising sudoers, SSH configs, or application config files enables persistence and escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for attempts to create or modify files in sensitive locations: /etc/sudoers*, /etc/shadow*, /root/.ssh/*, application startup scripts, or Cisco SD-WAN configuration directories. Correlate with prior remote authentication events.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20262 Patch Compliance Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Federal patch due date 2026-06-29 established — vulnerability scanner should flag vulnerable Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager versions as immediate remediation priority.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability management system for Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager version inventory. Identify systems running affected versions (pre-patch). Cross-reference with network exposure data to prioritize internet-facing instances.

suggestion.title: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Path Traversal Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability allows 'authenticated, remote attacker to create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem.' Exploitation payload delivery must be detected before impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager endpoints for path traversal patterns (../, ..\, %2e%2e, encoded variants). Flag authentication followed immediately by traversal attempts. Critical pre-2026-06-29 patch deadline.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20262 Vulnerable Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV indicates active exploitation. Article explicitly states 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' required. Must immediately identify all exposed Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances fleet-wide.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-20262 against Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager. Cross-reference with network inventory and firewall rules to identify internet-exposed instances. Escalate any findings to remediation immediately.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized File Creation/Modification on Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Core attack outcome: 'create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem of an affected system.' Post-exploitation file writes require filesystem audit detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish file write baseline on Catalyst SD-WAN Manager systems. Alert on unexpected file creation/modification in /opt, /var, /etc, or application-specific directories. Correlate with failed/successful authentication events and path traversal attempts.

suggestion.title: Authentication Anomalies to Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability requires authentication ('authenticated, remote attacker'). Monitor for auth bypass attempts or use of valid compromised credentials preceding exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on failed authentication attempts to Catalyst SD-WAN Manager immediately followed by successful logins from same source/subnet. Monitor for authentication events outside business hours or from unusual geographies. Flag if auth succeeds then path traversal payloads appear in logs.

suggestion.title: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Web Traffic Baseline Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation of management interface manifests as anomalous HTTP patterns. CISA KEV status indicates sophisticated, evasion-aware attackers may use obfuscated payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal administrative traffic to Catalyst SD-WAN Manager. Alert on traffic from unexpected source IPs, non-standard User-Agents, abnormal request rates, binary payloads in GET/POST, or connections outside maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scan: CVE-2026-20262 Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'CISA KEV entry... only adds CVEs that have been observed exploited in the wild' and 'Federal patch due: 2026-06-29' — requires baseline detection of all vulnerable Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances across fleet before active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner, asset inventory, and CMDB for Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager deployments matching CVE-2026-20262 signature. Prioritize exposed instances (internet-facing network edge). Cross-validate patch status against federal due-date 2026-06-29.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Write via Path Traversal Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem of an affected system' — requires detection of exploitation attempts that bypass path restrictions and write to unexpected locations outside normal operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager filesystem audit logs for file creation/modification in sensitive directories (system, etc, boot). Correlate with HTTP request logs showing path traversal patterns (../, double-encoded slashes, unicode bypass attempts) or unauthenticated POST/PUT requests.

suggestion.title: Authentication + File System Activity Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'authenticated, remote attacker to create a file or overwrite' — requires linking successful authentication events to subsequent unauthorized file modifications to establish exploitation timing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager systems, correlate successful remote authentication (SSH, HTTPS) with file creation/modification in system directories within 5-minute window. Flag if writes occur outside scheduled maintenance windows or by unexpected service accounts.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20262 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2026-20262 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and marks this as CISA KEV (currently exploited). No asset-exposure hunt generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all instances of Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager in the fleet and validate patch status against CVE-2026-20262. Flag any unpatched or unknown systems for remediation by federal due date 2026-06-29.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager - Path Traversal Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'authenticated, remote attacker' ability to 'create a file or overwrite any file' via path traversal, but no exploitation detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to Cisco SD-WAN Manager API endpoints containing directory traversal sequences (../, ..\ encoded variants, or path traversal bypasses) or requests to unexpected file paths. Alert on 200-OK responses following suspected traversal attempts.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager - Unauthorized File Creation/Modification
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability explicitly enables file write/overwrite on affected systems. No persistence or impact detection generated for successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco SD-WAN Manager filesystem for unexpected file creation or modification events, especially in critical directories (config, binaries, web-root). Correlate with authentication logs to identify files written by unexpected or service accounts.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Match: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager CVE-2026-20262

Cross-reference patch release date (approx. mid-June 2026) and escalate findings with missing patches on exposed assets. Correlate with federal due date 2026-06-29 for audit compliance.

suggestion.title: Exposed Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Web Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'remote attacker' exploiting 'public-facing application' (T1190); pipeline missed detection for externally accessible admin interfaces. No asset-exposure rules generated despite template reference.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/HTTPS connections to ports 22, 443, 8443 on Catalyst SD-WAN Manager appliances from non-corporate IP ranges. Catalyst typically runs on HTTPS; unexpected external access or brute-force patterns against login endpoints suggest reconnaissance or active exploit attempts.

suggestion.title: File Creation/Modification Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article core mechanic: 'create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem'; pipeline generated no detection for post-exploitation impact. File operations are the attack outcome and highest-confidence post-breach signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Catalyst SD-WAN Manager process (typically running as privileged user) for unexpected file creation/modification outside known installation and configuration directories. Flag rapid file creation in /tmp, /var, or other system paths; any write to system binaries or config files by the app user; and overwrites of web-served files (potential web shell injection).

suggestion.title: Authenticated Access to Catalyst SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'authenticated, remote attacker'; exploit requires valid credentials. Pipeline missed detection for credential use and anomalous post-auth behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Catalyst SD-WAN Manager authentication logs for successful logins followed within minutes by file operation requests or error attempts (path traversal patterns). Flag logins from unusual geographies, non-standard hours, or machine accounts; correlate with any file-system alerts.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'directory or path traversal vulnerability' as the exploitation vector; pipeline produced no rules for traversal payloads. Path patterns are signature-based and detectable at gateway/WAF.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP request logs for Catalyst SD-WAN Manager endpoints (identify via public CVSS details; typically /api/*, /admin, /settings paths) containing path traversal sequences: ../, ..\ , %2e%2e%2f, %2e%2e%5c, or nested encodings. Alert on any match even if WAF blocks it—indicates active reconnaissance or exploit delivery.

suggestion.title: Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Process Behavior Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article threat model involves application process executing file operations outside normal scope. Pipeline missed detection for privilege escalation or persistence mechanics post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Catalyst process spawning unexpected child processes (shell, bash, sh, cmd.exe, powershell) or executing system binaries (cp, mv, chmod, useradd, systemctl). Flag writes to cron jobs, systemd timers, startup scripts (/etc/init.d, /usr/lib/systemd/system, crontab), or system library paths—indicates persistence establishment.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager Asset Exposure & Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 'public-facing application' vulnerability (T1190) and references asset-exposure hunt template; requires identifying all Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances across fleet.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Fingerprint Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager by certificate, port/service signature, or HTTP banner. Correlate against patch database to identify instances running vulnerable versions < [patched version]. Flag any exposed to internet or untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized File Creation on SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'could allow...to create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem' — direct impact indicator that requires file-system auditing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file creation and modification events within Cisco SD-WAN Manager directories (config, logs, binaries). Alert on writes originating from the application's web service or API handlers to unexpected locations.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Authentication to SD-WAN Manager (Path Traversal Exploitation)
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is 'authenticated, remote attacker' — establishes baseline for login attempts and successful sessions, with post-auth file operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of successful authentications to Cisco SD-WAN Manager. Alert on: multiple failed attempts followed by success, unusual login times, geographic anomalies, or sessions followed by rapid file-system events.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20262 Patch Compliance Alert (Federal Deadline)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies federal patch due date of 2026-06-29; CISA KEV entries require time-bound remediation tracking and escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances flagged for CVE-2026-20262. Compare against approved patch list. Auto-escalate any unpatched instances approaching or past federal due date.

suggestion.title: Remote Desktop Client RCE Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article extensively covers CVE-2026-42985, CVE-2026-42992, CVE-2026-44799, CVE-2026-44801, CVE-2026-47289, CVE-2026-48563—all heap-based buffer overflows in Remote Desktop. 'An attacker who controls a Remote Desktop Server could initiate a remote code execution (RCE) on the machine when a victim connects to the attacking server using the vulnerable Remote Desktop Client.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor mstsc.exe for unexpected child process spawning (cmd, powershell, rundll32) within 5 seconds of port 3389 activity. Detect abnormal exception sequences or memory allocation patterns in RDP client processes. Correlate heap corruption indicators or abnormal thread creation within rdpclip.exe or rdpinput.exe with RDP session initiation.

suggestion.title: HTTP.sys Integer Overflow Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-47291: 'Integer overflow or wraparound in Windows HTTP Protocol Stack (http.sys). An unauthenticated attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a specially crafted packet to a targeted server utilizing the HTTP Protocol Stack (http.sys) to process packets.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect malformed HTTP requests with overflow-triggering patterns (Content-Length exceeding INT_MAX, negative sizes, protocol violations) sent to IIS. Monitor for kernel exceptions (crash dumps, unexpected http.sys termination) correlated with abnormal packets on ports 80/443.

suggestion.title: Office Email Preview Pane Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-45456, CVE-2026-45458, CVE-2026-47635 type confusion. 'The attack vector is the preview pane of Outlook (classic), and this vulnerability can be exploited when rendering emails in Outlook (classic), as the email rendering in Outlook (classic) utilizes Microsoft Word functionality.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor OUTLOOK.EXE and WINWORD.EXE for unexpected child process spawning (cmd, powershell) within 5 seconds of email preview. Detect unusual DLL injection or in-memory code execution. Alert on Office application crashes (access violations) immediately following email processing.

suggestion.title: Hyper-V Guest-to-Host Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-45607, CVE-2026-45641, CVE-2026-47652 out-of-bounds reads. 'An authenticated attacker on a guest virtual machine (VM) sends specially crafted file operation requests to hardware resources within the VM which could result in remote code execution on the host server.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In virtualized environments, detect guest VMs performing abnormal device driver interactions, direct \Device\ or \Global access, or out-of-bounds file operations via DeviceIoControl. Correlate guest exploitation with unexpected process spawning on host Hyper-V processes (vmwp.exe, vmms.exe) with SYSTEM privileges.

suggestion.title: Windows Kernel Use-After-Free Network RCE
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-45657: 'An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending specially crafted network traffic... the malicious network packets could trigger a flaw in how the Windows kernel processes certain TCP/IP data, potentially allowing the attacker to run code with system-level privileges.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate receipt of anomalous TCP/IP traffic (malformed packets, protocol violations) with kernel exception events (crash recovery, BSOD telemetry). Monitor for NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM child processes spawning immediately after network anomalies without user/service initiation.

suggestion.title: Nuance Powerscribe Unsafe Deserialization RCE
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-26142: 'remote code execution vulnerability due to deserialization of untrusted data in Nuance Powerscribe. Exploiting this vulnerability could allow an attacker to execute code over a network.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Nuance Powerscribe processes for unexpected child spawning or network communication patterns. Detect .NET deserialization payloads via network IDS. Alert on Powerscribe processing untrusted network files with immediate command interpreter spawning.

suggestion.title: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager CVE-2026-20262 Vulnerability Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2026-20262 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and references asset-exposure hunt templates; pipeline generated zero use cases despite this direct guidance and federable relevance.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Exploitation Against Cisco SD-WAN Manager

Focus on requests to file-operation or config-management endpoints. Baseline legitimate admin activity to establish FP threshold.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Creation/Modification on Cisco SD-WAN Manager Hosts

Establish baseline of legitimate admin file operations; flag deviations especially in system-critical paths (bin/, lib/, web-accessible paths).

suggestion.title: Anomalous Admin Authentication Patterns to Cisco SD-WAN Manager

Cross-reference with corporate credential breach notifications and SIEM credential-compromise alerts.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized File Creation/Modification on SD-WAN Manager Filesystem
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes exploitation outcome: 'create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem'—a direct impact indicator the pipeline omitted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager system logs for unexpected file operations (creation, modification, deletion). suggestion.title: Suspicious Authenticated Access to Catalyst SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector explicitly requires 'authenticated, remote attacker' but pipeline missed authentication anomaly detection despite this being the gateway to exploitation.

suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability type is 'directory or path traversal'; article body names this exploit vector but pipeline extracted no payload-pattern detections.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized File Write via Path Traversal (Cisco SD-WAN Manager)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability allows attacker to 'create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem of an affected system.' This is the direct impact of the exploit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected file creation or modification events on Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager systems, especially in system directories (/etc, /var, config paths, or Windows equivalents). Correlate with web access logs showing path traversal sequences or exploitation attempts. File writes from the SD-WAN Manager process or web service running under unexpected privileges are high-fidelity indicators.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Pattern Detection in SD-WAN Manager Web Logs
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability mechanism is 'directory or path traversal.' Web logs should contain malicious request patterns before file write succeeds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for path traversal sequences in HTTP requests to Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager endpoints: strings like '../', '..\\', URL-encoded variants ('%2e%2e', '%5c'), or doubled slashes in file paths. Filter on status codes indicating successful exploitation (200, 201, 204) rather than blocked attempts (400, 403). Correlate with subsequent file modification events.

suggestion.title: Configuration File Access via Path Traversal

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when SD-WAN Manager or web service processes open configuration files (e.g., passwords.conf, auth.conf, system.ini) via non-standard code paths or file handle paths that traverse parent directories. Detect unusual read-then-write patterns on sensitive configs within short time windows.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Process or Service Writing to System Directories (SD-WAN)
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability outcome is ability to 'create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem'—privileged file write is the impact.
log_sources: Windows Registry and File audit events
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On systems running Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager, alert on file creation or modification in restricted directories (system32, /bin, /etc, /var, boot directories) initiated from the web service or SD-WAN process. Baseline file write activity for the affected application and trigger on deviations. Include file integrity monitoring (FIM) alerts for unexpected changes to critical system files.

suggestion.title: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could allow an authenticated, remote attacker' and is actively exploited; requires internet-facing Manager instance. Detection should identify exposed web interfaces before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for open/responsive ports associated with Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager (typically 8443, 8888) or HTTP GET/HEAD requests to known Manager paths (e.g., /apidocs, /admin). Cross-correlate with asset inventory to identify exposed instances not previously documented as internet-facing.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Payload Detection in HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'directory or path traversal vulnerability' as attack vector; specific payload patterns should be monitored. Attackers exploit this by sending crafted requests with ../, %2e%2e%, or encoded variants.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP request logs to Catalyst SD-WAN Manager endpoints for path traversal indicators: ../, %2e%2e%, ..%2f, %252e%252e%252f, or similar directory escape sequences. Correlate with User-Agent and authentication headers to identify exploitation attempts post-authentication.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized File Creation/Modification on Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Host
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'could create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem'; post-exploitation file operations are the immediate impact. Detection should monitor filesystem activity on Manager hosts for unexpected writes.

Prioritize: (1) writes to system directories (/etc, /var, /opt outside expected paths), (2) new executable files, (3) config file modifications. Baseline normal file operations and alert on anomalies correlated with failed/successful authentications.

suggestion.title: Failed Authentication Followed by Successful Login to Catalyst SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates 'authenticated' attackers; however, successful exploitation likely preceded by reconnaissance. Detection should flag patterns of failed attempts followed by successful auth and immediate file operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In Catalyst SD-WAN Manager audit logs, identify sequences: 10+ failed login attempts to single account → successful login from same source IP → immediate file operation event. Adjust thresholds per environment baseline; flag successful logins from IPs not previously authenticated.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20262 Vulnerability Detection via Scanner/Configuration Audit
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Even if your scanners say not vulnerable... it's worth one quick check.' Detection should cross-verify vulnerability scanner results with actual Catalyst SD-WAN Manager version inventory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate vulnerability scanner reports flagging CVE-2026-20262 against CMDB version records for Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances. Alert if scanner shows 'not vulnerable' but installed version is <= patched version threshold. Include all Manager instances (exposed and internal) — lateral movement risk exists.

suggestion.title: Typo-squatting Go Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attack: 'The malicious Go Module Mirror's was named github.com/botdb-go/bolt, similar to the original one i.e. github.com/boltdb/bolt.' Detection should flag phonetically similar package names substituting legitimate ones.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Go package manager operations (go get, go mod tidy) for installation of packages with names phonetically or visually similar to known-good packages. Flag 'botdb-go/bolt' or variants deviating from canonical 'boltdb/bolt'. Cross-reference against official Go package registry.

suggestion.title: Go Module Proxy Serving Malicious Cached Version
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Go Module Mirror service stored it permanently... Go Module Mirror's indefinite caching of modules kicked in, and that cached the backdored module.' Detection should identify module proxy serving compromised versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Go dependency resolution for checksum mismatches or version anomalies between requested and served modules. Alert on go.mod/go.sum validation failures. Correlate module downloads against Go Vulnerability Database and official package source hashes.

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution from Backdoored Go Module
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'allows hackers to remotely control infected computers through a server that sends them commands i.e. via a command and control server.' Detection should identify command execution orchestrated by C2.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected process spawning from Go runtime or application processes. Correlate with outbound HTTP/DNS connections to non-whitelisted domains. Flag command execution lacking corresponding user input or code-path triggering.

suggestion.title: Bulk Dependency Auto-update to Malicious Version
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'we now wish to update our systems to the latest dependencies, which led developers to update the version that stayed in the system for 3 years.' Detection should flag automation-driven updates to compromised versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor dependency update operations (go get -u, go mod tidy) for targets matching recent vulnerability advisories. Flag updates to versions not yet widely adopted in legitimate builds. Require approval before applying updates to supply chain-critical dependencies.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Vendored Malicious Go Module
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'version...stayed in the system for 3 years,' indicating vendored persistence in git repos and build artifacts. Detection should identify malicious modules in vendor/ directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan vendor/ directories and go.sum in source control for known-malicious package names (botdb-go/bolt). Alert on presence of typosquatting packages in checked-in dependencies. Baseline legitimate packages across build pipeline.

suggestion.title: Outbound C2 Beaconing from Compromised Application
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'backdoor allows...remote control...through a server.' Detection should identify beaconing behavior from applications using backdoored Go modules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from Go application processes for regular interval, low-volume C2 patterns. Flag connections to domains not in ASN whitelist or exhibiting high entropy. Correlate beacon timing with process parent relationships.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager Internet Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article frames vulnerability as affecting 'exposed assets' (T1190 language) and explicitly recommends 'standard asset-exposure hunt.' No UC generated despite this direct guidance. This is the initial_access prerequisite.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify internet-facing Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances on standard HTTPS ports (8443, 8080 variants). Correlate inbound traffic volume and source IP diversity against asset inventory to flag exposed management interfaces.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Exploitation Attempts on SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article core attack is 'directory or path traversal'—exploit-phase reconnaissance. Pipeline skipped execution-layer detections despite vulnerability name being 'path traversal.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt HTTP request logs to SD-WAN Manager endpoints for path traversal patterns: ../ sequences, %2e%2e encodings, absolute path prefixes in file operation parameters, or suspicious directory enumeration requests.

suggestion.title: File Creation or Overwrite via SD-WAN Manager Post-Auth
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker 'could allow...to create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem.' This is the direct impact; no UC captured file I/O anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SD-WAN Manager system for unexpected file creation or modification in sensitive paths (config dirs, binary dirs, audit log locations) following remote authentication or concurrent with path-traversal-pattern HTTP traffic.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Authentication to Cisco SD-WAN Manager Pre-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'authenticated, remote attacker'—authentication is mandatory step before exploitation. No UC detects anomalous logins despite this gating requirement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track successful and failed authentication attempts to SD-WAN Manager from non-standard source IPs, bulk login patterns, or credential stuffing indicators. Correlate with subsequent file-system anomalies on same session.

suggestion.title: Code Execution via Overwritten SD-WAN Manager Binaries
suggestion.rationale: File-overwrite attacks often target executable startup scripts or plugins for RCE. Article does not exclude this escalation path; typical post-exploitation file manipulations enable command execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected process spawning from SD-WAN Manager service context or child processes of manager daemons, especially within minutes of file modification events or from suspicious session origins.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20262 Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager contains a directory or path traversal vulnerability' with active CISA KEV status. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite explicit mention of 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' template.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to Catalyst SD-WAN Manager with path traversal payloads (../, ..\ sequences) or CVE-2026-20262 exploit patterns. Alert on successful responses (200 HTTP) to admin or config paths from untrusted sources.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Filesystem Writes Post-Catalyst SD-WAN Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'authenticated, remote attacker to create a file or overwrite any file on the filesystem.' Pipeline missed the post-exploitation file modification impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful Catalyst SD-WAN Manager authentication events with abnormal file creation/modification on the same host, especially outside expected config/log directories. Flag rapid file overwrites or suspicious binary writes.

Flag requests with 401/403 responses (auth required) followed by 200/201 (exploitation success) within short time window.

suggestion.rationale: SSRF commonly targets cloud metadata services (AWS IMDSv1, GCP metadata) or internal APIs (Kubernetes, Docker, Redis, Postgres on default ports). Article describes SSRF as enabling cookie theft and proxying; exfiltration of cloud credentials via metadata is a natural escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag POST bodies to /webapi/proxy that reference 169.254.169.254, http://metadata.google.internal, or internal service endpoints (127.0.0.1:2379 for etcd, 127.0.0.1:6379 for Redis, localhost:27017 for MongoDB). Correlate to any subsequent credential exfiltration or API calls.

suggestion.title: Outbound HTTP redirection from LobeHub /webapi/proxy to attacker-controlled domain
suggestion.rationale: Article notes the proxy 'allows anyone to proxy requests.' An attacker can host a redirect that redirects the LobeHub server to an attacker site, enabling blind SSRF attacks or request injection. No UC detects the response path (where LobeHub follows the attacker's redirect).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP 302/301/307 responses returned by /webapi/proxy, then correlate the Location header to known malicious domains, newly registered domains, or out-of-policy external IPs. Flag if LobeHub server initiates a secondary connection to the redirect target.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable LobeHub version <=2.1.56 detected via HTTP banner or web content
suggestion.rationale: Article states the vulnerability affects 'LobeHub <=2.1.56.' Asset detection via vulnerability datamodel is correct, but no UC covers real-time banner grabbing or JavaScript fingerprinting to detect the running version on internet-facing instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan HTTP responses from known LobeHub instances for version strings in headers, HTML comments, or JavaScript source. Flag any version <=2.1.56 as critical. Correlate to public IPs to identify exposed instances.

suggestion.title: LobeHub /webapi/proxy POST from non-browser User-Agent or scripted tools
suggestion.rationale: The article describes direct exploitation by attackers. Legitimate traffic to /webapi/proxy (if any) would originate from the LobeHub UI (browser) or internal services. Traffic from curl, wget, Python, or PowerShell is strongly indicative of exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on POST to /webapi/proxy where User-Agent matches curl, wget, Python-requests, PowerShell, or other scripted/CLI tools. Whitelist only documented internal services. High fidelity; few FPs.

suggestion.title: POST to /webapi/proxy with response size/latency anomalies indicative of exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: SSRF attacks often result in large or long-duration responses (downloading files, querying large internal DBs). Article notes endpoint enables 'proxying requests' without auth—useful for downloading payloads or reconnaissance dumps.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track response sizes and latencies for /webapi/proxy POSTs. Baseline legitimate traffic; alert on outliers (responses >10MB or latencies >30s). Correlate to source reputation and target URL to assess exfiltration risk.

suggestion.title: Crawl4AI Frame/Generator Object Attribute Injection in POST /crawl
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Python generator and frame object attributes (gi_frame, f_back, f_builtins) do NOT start with underscore, enabling a complete sandbox escape.' This is the primary exploitation technique and should be the highest-fidelity detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to Crawl4AI /crawl endpoint for frame/generator object attribute chains: gi_frame, f_back, f_builtins, __import__, gc.get_objects(). Zero benign Crawl4AI traffic should reference these attributes; high-fidelity exploitation signature.

suggestion.title: Crawl4AI/uvicorn Process Tree Spawning Shells or Recon Tools
suggestion.rationale: RCE via 'arbitrary code execution' enables post-exploitation shell spawning and reconnaissance. Absence of this use case from pipeline despite clear narrative describing impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Crawl4AI (parent: python, uvicorn, gunicorn) spawning shells (sh, bash, dash) or recon utilities (curl, wget, nc, ncat). Suppress legitimate contexts: setup.py, pip install, pytest, jupyter.

suggestion.title: Post-RCE Environment and Credential Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1552.001 (Unsecured Credentials in Files). Post-exploitation would dump /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, cloud metadata (169.254.169.254), and process environment (/proc/self/environ, printenv).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Crawl4AI or child processes accessing credential files or environment secrets: /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, cat /proc/self/environ, printenv, metadata service queries. These are high-signal post-RCE indicators.

suggestion.title: Accessibility Service Abuse for Device Control
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Rokarolla requests Accessibility service permissions' and uses them to 'bypass standard Android security protections and obtain elevated capabilities to interact with the user interface.' Critical abuse vector enabling overlay attacks and PIN capture.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for applications requesting Accessibility Service permissions post-install, particularly those with no legitimate reason (non-assistive apps). Alert on AccessibilityService state changes following suspicious app installations, especially from sideloaded/non-Play Store sources. Correlate with overlay activity.

suggestion.title: Google Play Protect Disablement Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes evasion tactic: 'disabling Google Play Protect.' This is a high-confidence malware signal as legitimate apps never disable anti-malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on PlayProtect disable setting changes via Settings.Secure or device administration revocation. Monitor for rapid disable/enable cycling (evasion). Correlate timing with suspicious app installation or Accessibility permission grants.

suggestion.title: Phishing Overlay Credential Capture Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Core malware function: 'When the victim opens an app on the list, Rokarolla displays a fake login overlay to steal login credentials, credit card information.' Occurs against targeted banking/crypto apps (217 identified targets).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unauthorized overlay windows appearing above targeted banking/crypto applications. Correlate overlay appearance with clipboard reads, keystroke captures, and app activity in non-primary window context. Flag if overlay blocks user input to legitimate app.

suggestion.title: Keylogger and On-Screen Content Capture
suggestion.rationale: Article lists malware capabilities: 'Capture keystrokes,' 'Record on-screen content via UI logging,' 'Periodically take screenshots and upload them with timestamps.' Continuous data harvesting for credential theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for applications performing continuous AccessibilityEvent access (keystroke capture), repeated WindowState/content reads, or screenshot APIs (captureFrame, getDrawingCache). Alert on periodic high-volume file writes to cache followed by exfiltration attempts. Correlate with Accessibility permission holders.

suggestion.title: SMS and Contact Data Bulk Extraction
suggestion.rationale: Listed capabilities: 'Steal SMS messages,' 'Extract contact information and WhatsApp contacts.' Malware enumerates and exfiltrates personal data post-infection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on applications requesting READ_SMS/READ_CONTACTS followed by bulk query operations (e.g., cursor.getCount() > threshold). Monitor for exported data to temp files or network. Baseline: legitimate banking apps rarely bulk-read SMS/contacts; crypto apps never do.

suggestion.title: C2 Device Profile Enumeration and Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'Communication with the command-and-control (C2) server begins with sending a basic device profile containing details such as the phone model, installed Android version, locale...used to generate a unique identifier.' Adversary fingerprinting and C2 check-in pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections containing systematic device enumeration data (model, version, storage, RAM, battery) in first-stage beacon. Alert on TLS/HTTP POST to unknown domains with device ID derivation patterns. Correlate timing with app install + permission grants (early infection signature).

suggestion.title: GCS Bucket Squatting – Project-Name Typosquatting Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'bucket squatting' as the attack vector. Attackers create lookalike GCS bucket names to intercept legitimate model uploads. Pipeline extracted zero use cases despite the title directly stating this.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rapid creation of GCS buckets with names closely matching (Levenshtein distance <3) existing project buckets or public bucket naming conventions. Flag if created by new or anomalous service accounts, especially those without established usage history.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Model Upload to Vertex AI – Bucket Owner Mismatch
suggestion.rationale: Article describes hijacking of model uploads via bucket squatting. Pipeline missed detection for when models are uploaded to attacker-controlled buckets instead of legitimate ones. The vulnerability is in the SDK's bucket resolution logic.
log_sources: Application logs from model training pipelines
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect when Vertex AI model training jobs or uploads resolve to GCS buckets not whitelisted for that project. Alert on bucket-ownership mismatches (e.g., model destination not owned by the same GCP project/service account that initiated the job).

suggestion.title: Vertex AI SDK Dependency – Outdated / Vulnerable Version Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly flags a flaw in 'Google Vertex AI SDK.' Pipeline should identify applications or deployments still using vulnerable SDK versions (missing security patches).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag deployments or build artifacts containing google-cloud-aiplatform or google-vertex-ai SDK versions prior to the patched release. Correlate with model upload activity to identify active exploitation risk.

suggestion.title: Cross-Project GCS Access from Vertex AI Service Account
suggestion.rationale: Bucket squatting attack likely requires attackers to manipulate which GCS bucket the SDK writes to. Legitimate Vertex AI operations should respect project boundaries; cross-project writes are suspicious.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when a Vertex AI service account in project A writes to GCS buckets in project B or to buckets with weak/public ACLs. Baseline expected bucket destinations per service account and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Vertex AI Model Metadata Tampering – Unexpected Origin/Source URI
suggestion.rationale: If attackers hijack uploads via bucket squatting, the resulting model metadata will point to attacker-controlled storage. Pipeline should detect models with suspicious source URIs.
log_sources: Vertex AI model registry audit logs
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect models created/updated with source_uri or artifact_uri pointing to external/unexpected GCS buckets or public storage. Cross-reference against approved model source repositories and flag outliers.

suggestion.title: Rapid GCS Bucket + Vertex AI Model Creation – Supply Chain Staging Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Attack chain likely involves creating a bucket, uploading a malicious model, then having legitimate users or automation pull it. Pipeline should detect the dual-activity pattern suggesting staged compromise.
log_sources: Correlation across bucket and model APIs
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect patterns: new GCS bucket created → model object uploaded → Vertex AI model registered/deployed referencing that bucket, all within short timeframe (minutes to hours) by unusual principals.

suggestion.title: Fake Browser/OS Update Lure Landing Page Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Fake Update Lures' as primary vector; no detection generated for users visiting malicious update-mimicking pages. Title establishes this as core attack method.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP traffic to newly registered or typosquat domains hosting pages with 'update', 'install', 'upgrade' keywords impersonating Chrome, Windows, or Firefox. Correlate with phishing email indicators and user click events.

suggestion.title: Loader Execution via Scripted Delivery Chain
suggestion.rationale: Title mentions 'New Loaders' but pipeline surfaced zero execution-phase detections. ClickFix typically delivers via VBS, PowerShell, or batch from downloaded payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag cmd.exe or powershell.exe spawned from %TEMP% or AppData\Temp with Base64-encoded or obfuscated arguments. Monitor unsigned DLL loads immediately after process creation from temporary paths.

suggestion.title: Registry Run-Key Persistence by Loader
suggestion.rationale: ClickFix campaigns establish persistence via registry; article title 'campaigns expand' implies established persistence mechanisms entirely absent from pipeline analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run* modifications with values pointing to temporary directories or obfuscated command invocations. Alert on registry writes from temporary process contexts.

suggestion.title: Process Injection by ClickFix Payload
suggestion.rationale: Loaders characteristically perform DLL injection into legitimate processes for evasion; despite 'New Loaders' in title, pipeline missed this standard behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unsigned or suspicious DLL injection into explorer.exe, svchost.exe, rundll32.exe. Flag CreateRemoteThread, WriteProcessMemory calls originating from %TEMP% or AppData contexts.

suggestion.title: C2 Beaconing Infrastructure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Campaign-wide malware infrastructure not identified. ClickFix payloads beacon to C2 for command delivery; entire C2 phase missing from pipeline's kill-chain reconstruction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST requests to newly registered domains from infected hosts with suspicious User-Agent strings or obfuscated payloads. Monitor for repetitive beacon patterns and non-standard HTTP headers.

suggestion.title: Secondary Payload / Infostealer Execution from Update Lure
suggestion.rationale: 'New Loaders' in title implies secondary payloads; common ClickFix technique involves credential-stealing or banking malware delivered post-initial compromise. Zero collection-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for credential-stealing overlays or screen-capture utilities spawned post-infection. Flag WinAPI hooks targeting CredEnumerate, SamrQueryInformationUser. Alert on clipboard and keystroke API access patterns.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated HTTP POST to /api/v1/build_public_tmp endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states the vulnerability is 'unauthenticated' access via this endpoint: 'Shareable Playground feature works by enabling the execution of workflows by unauthenticated users, by accessing a link. Specifically, it enables the route `/api/v1/build_public_tmp`.' Initial-access detection is foundational and missing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST/GET requests to `/api/v1/build_public_tmp*` from non-authenticated sources or sources outside known administrative IP ranges. Baseline normal flow-sharing patterns (legitimate share links) to reduce FP, then alert on anomalous request rates or payloads containing shell metacharacters or encoded Python exec calls.

suggestion.title: Python subprocess execution with shell=True from Langflow runtime
suggestion.rationale: Article describes RCE within the Langflow Python runtime: 'execution of workflows by unauthenticated users' and lists T1059.006 (Python interpreter). Direct Python subprocess spawning is the execution mechanism and is not separately detected by existing UCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python subprocess calls with shell=True parameter (either via Popen/subprocess calls or direct eval/exec statements). Correlate with Langflow process parent (python/uvicorn). Look for process command-lines that contain base64 encoding, hex encoding, or shell escape sequences—indicators of obfuscated payloads.

suggestion.title: HTTP 500/error responses from /api/v1/build_public_tmp after malformed flow submission
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation attempts often fail before achieving RCE; error responses are a reliable indicator of attack probing. Article does not describe error handling or response codes, but reconnaissance activity will precede successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect clusters of HTTP 4xx/5xx responses from the `/api/v1/build_public_tmp` endpoint within a short time window, grouped by source IP. Successful exploitation may be preceded by reconnaissance requests that fail validation. Establish baseline of legitimate error rates and alert on significant deviation.

suggestion.title: Joomla Content Editor Unauthenticated Profile Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users.' This is the initial access vector—detecting profile creation without prior auth/session.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Joomla access logs for POST requests to profile creation endpoints (typically /administrator/index.php?option=com_joomckeditor or equivalent) with empty/missing authorization headers or session tokens. Flag any successful profile creation (HTTP 200) from unauthenticated clients.

suggestion.title: PHP File Upload to Web-Accessible Joomla Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could allow for upload and execution of PHP code.' Detect file uploads with .php extension or polyglot payloads to Joomla component directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST/PUT requests to Joomla upload endpoints (common: /components/com_joomckeditor/uploads/ or /media/) for PHP file creation or detection of file write events creating .php/.phtml/.phar files in web-accessible paths. Correlate with subsequent HTTP requests to those file paths.

suggestion.title: Joomla Content Editor Component Exposure (Asset Inventory)
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor' as the vulnerable product. The recommended-hunts section explicitly mentions asset-exposure template. Scan for exposed vulnerable component versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory all Joomla installations in your environment via component scanning or web fingerprinting. Identify instances with Content Editor component exposed and version <patched version (June 19, 2026 deadline implies versions prior to vendor fix). Flag as critical if accessible from untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: Unusual HTTP Methods or Parameters to Joomla Administrator Paths
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'improper access control' allowing unauthenticated access. Detect anomalous HTTP behavior targeting admin endpoints without prior authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on OPTIONS/DELETE/PATCH methods or unusual parameter combinations (e.g., _task=create&editor_profile=) to /administrator/* paths when source has no prior authenticated session cookie or Authorization header. High false-positive risk—baseline first.

suggestion.title: PHP Execution in Joomla Media/Upload Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'execution of PHP code'—uploaded files must be executed. Monitor for code execution originating from upload directories via subsequent web requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate file write events (PHP files created in /components/com_joomckeditor/uploads/) with immediate HTTP requests to those same paths, followed by process creation events (php.exe, php-cgi) or outbound connections initiated by the web server process. Time-proximity correlation is key.

suggestion.title: Joomla Database Modification Post-Upload
suggestion.rationale: Unauthenticated uploads and code execution could be used for persistence. Detect suspicious database writes (e.g., admin user creation, plugin injection) following successful uploads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Joomla database logs for INSERT/UPDATE to jos_users (user creation) or jos_extensions (plugin injection) tables when source_ip matches recent upload POST requests. Combine with code-execution indicators for higher confidence.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Editor Profile Creation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'allow[s] for upload and execution of PHP code via the creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users'—access-control bypass is the exploitation mechanism and is not being hunted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Joomla + Widget Factory Content Editor endpoints for POST requests to editor profile creation endpoints originating from unauthenticated or external sources. Flag profile creation attempts without prior authentication tokens or from IPs outside your administrative ranges.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution via Widget Editor Profile
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'upload and execution of PHP code'—code-execution detection is the critical downstream telemetry and is entirely absent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on PHP process execution (php.exe, php-cgi, php-fpm) spawned by or writing to the Widget Factory Content Editor data directories or temp upload paths, particularly with payloads or command strings indicative of web shells.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Upload to Widget Editor Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'upload and execution of PHP code'—file-write patterns to plugin/editor upload directories are observable and constitute pre-execution telemetry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect .php, .phtml, .php3, .php4, .php5 file creation in Widget Factory Content Editor upload or profile directories, especially from web-server processes (apache, www-data, iis apppool) or where file ownership changes unexpectedly.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48907 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2026-48907 — match against your vulnerability scanner'—no use case was generated for scan correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-correlate vulnerability scans detecting CVE-2026-48907 (Widget Factory Content Editor versions ≤ [EOL version]) with web server logs and process execution on the same host to confirm potential exploitation window and post-compromise activity.

suggestion.title: Joomla Widget Factory Content Editor Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Article describes a public-facing Joomla plugin; attackers will probe for its presence via version fingerprinting and endpoint enumeration (article: 'exploit public-facing application').
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests probing for Widget Factory Content Editor endpoints (e.g., /media/widgetfactory/, /plugins/editors/widgetfactory/*, /index.php?option=com_widgetfactory) from external IPs. Spike in 404 → 200 transitions on editor endpoints indicates possible scanning and successful exploitation.

suggestion.title: Joomla Content Editor — Unauthenticated Admin Access Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated users' can access editor profiles. Must detect requests to Joomla administrator endpoints lacking valid session tokens or authentication context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on requests to /administrator/index.php?option=com_joomlacontenteditor or editor-related paths where session cookie is missing, forged, or HTTP 200 is returned without valid authentication. Baseline: unauthenticated requests should receive 30x redirect or 401/403.

suggestion.title: Joomla Content Editor — PHP File Upload to Web Root
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'upload and execution of PHP code via creation of new editor profiles.' Detect POST to profile endpoints with .php/.phtml file uploads followed by file creation in web-accessible directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag multipart/form-data POST to Joomla Content Editor profile-creation endpoints containing .php, .phtml, or .php3 files. Correlate with FileCreate events in webroot, /uploads, /cache, or /tmp directories. Alert if subsequent HTTP requests execute the uploaded file.

suggestion.title: Joomla Plugin Version Scanning — CVE-2026-48907
suggestion.rationale: Article: CISA KEV with federal patch due 2026-06-19. Asset inventory must flag Widget Factory Content Editor installations to identify at-risk assets requiring immediate remediation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan Joomla instances for Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor plugin presence and version. Alert on installations of plugin in any version below the fixed build. Correlate with external exposure (public IP, port 80/443, DNS records) to prioritize high-risk targets.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution from Joomla Temporary/Upload Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article attack succeeds via 'execution of PHP code.' Detect PHP interpreter spawned with working directory in plugin upload paths, indicating exploitation success.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for php.exe, php-cgi.exe, or php spawned with CWD or document root pointing to /components/com_joomlacontenteditor, Joomla /cache, /tmp, or /uploads. Alert if process spawns child processes, connects to external IPs, or reads/writes suspicious files.

suggestion.title: Joomla Content Editor — Profile Creation Without Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability is 'improper access control' allowing profile creation by unauthenticated users. Detect profile creation events lacking valid user_id or session context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If Joomla logs profile creation (com_joomlacontenteditor profile create events), alert when event occurs without authenticated user_id, valid session token, or from an unauthenticated IP address. Baseline: all profile creation should require admin role.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise — Web Shell Activity on Exploited Joomla Server
suggestion.rationale: Successful code execution leads to web shell persistence. Detect suspicious HTTP POST/GET patterns and process spawning consistent with remote code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After successful PHP upload, detect anomalous POST requests to the uploaded file with system command parameters, unusual outbound HTTP/DNS from web server process, or httpd/apache spawning cmd.exe, bash, or sh. Correlate file access patterns (e.g., reading /etc/passwd, enumerating directories).

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Joomla Content Editor Profile Creation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'improper access control vulnerability which could allow for...creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users'—this bypass is the critical initial foothold.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST/PUT requests to Joomla Content Editor configuration or profile creation endpoints (e.g., */profile*, */editor-config*, */editor-init*) without valid session tokens or authentication headers that return 200/201. Flag rapid successive requests from single IP attempting multiple unauthenticated profile creations.

suggestion.title: Executable File Upload to Joomla Content Editor Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'upload and execution of PHP code'—successful exploitation requires uploading executable code to a web-accessible directory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor multipart form uploads targeting Content Editor directories for .php, .phtml, .php5, or .phar extensions. Alert on uploads that succeed (HTTP 200–201) followed by HTTP GET requests to the uploaded file path within 60 seconds, indicating immediate access/execution.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48907 Asset Exposure Scan
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs 'match against your vulnerability scanner' and CISA KEV is actively exploited. Federal due date 2026-06-19 creates compliance urgency; patch lag is the attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Run periodic scans to identify Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor instances matching vulnerable versions for CVE-2026-48907. Cross-reference unpatched instances with internet-facing asset inventory. Alert on any unpatched systems; flag any still unpatched after federal due date 2026-06-19.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Command Execution Post-Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'upload and execution of PHP code'—uploaded PHP executes in web server context, allowing command execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to newly created PHP files in Content Editor working directories containing command execution patterns: encoded/base64 payloads in query params, PHP functions (exec(), system(), shell_exec(), passthru()) in POST bodies, or repeated requests with different parameters suggesting command shell access.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Joomla Content Editor Instance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies CVE-2026-48907 in Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor. CISA KEV requires immediate asset inventory. Pipeline should generate baseline scan/detection use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners and network telemetry for Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor instances exposed to untrusted networks. Correlate with CVE-2026-48907 scanner results. Alert on any inbound HTTP/HTTPS to identified vulnerable endpoints.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated POST to Joomla Editor Profile Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'improper access control vulnerability...allow for upload...via the creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users.' This is the specific exploit path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to Joomla editor profile creation endpoints (/administrator/*, editor component paths) without valid session cookies/tokens. Alert on 200/201 responses. Establish baseline of legitimate admin profile creation frequency for FP filtering.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Upload to Joomla Editor Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'allow for upload and execution of PHP code.' PHP file placement in web-accessible directories post-auth-bypass indicates exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on .php/.php5/.phtml file creation in Joomla component/plugin/template directories post-POST to editor endpoints. Correlate file-write events with IIS/Apache process context. Monitor for immediate HTTP requests to newly created PHP paths.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Execution Post-Joomla Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'execution of PHP code' following upload. T1505.003 (Web Shell) describes this server-side code execution scenario.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate suspicious PHP file uploads with immediate PHP process execution (php.exe, php-cgi under w3wp.exe/apache parent). Alert if PHP execution occurs from temp/plugin/component directories post-exploit. Monitor for unexpected outbound network connections from PHP processes.

suggestion.title: Joomla Editor Endpoint Scanning/Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article vulnerability targets a specific Joomla component. Pre-exploitation reconnaissance would probe editor endpoints. Frequency-based detection for 401/403 responses on known paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on >10 sequential HTTP requests to Joomla editor-related endpoints (containing 'editor', 'profile', 'component') within 60s from single IP, primarily returning 401/403. This pattern indicates auth-bypass probing.

suggestion.title: Joomla Version/Component Fingerprinting Requests
suggestion.rationale: Attackers must identify vulnerable Widget Factory component instances. Requests to version-disclosure endpoints or manifest files are reconnaissance precursors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP GET requests to Joomla admin index, component manifest.xml paths, or version-reveal endpoints from external sources, especially when followed within minutes by exploit-attempt POST patterns.

suggestion.title: Typo-Squatting Package Installation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attack vector: 'create and upload harmful software packages...using names very similar to popular ones' (github.com/botdb-go/bolt vs github.com/boltdb/bolt). Pipeline produced no detection for this clear supply-chain initial access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Go module imports and package.mod/package.lock changes for package names that are edit-distance 1-2 from known legitimate packages. Flag installations where the imported package differs from declared dependency by character substitution (l→1, o→0, db→dd). Cross-reference against Go vulnerability database.

suggestion.title: Module Proxy Cache Poisoning Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Core persistence mechanism: 'Go Module Mirror's indefinite caching of modules kicked in, and that cached the backdored module.' This 3-year persistence was enabled by infrastructure behavior, not exploitable for detection at install-time but critical for cache integrity monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Go module proxy/registry logs for cache-hit patterns on reverted or removed packages. Alert when enterprise systems continue pulling cached versions of modules flagged in vulnerability databases after removal date. Track module.mod references to packages listed in GO-2025-3451 or equivalent.

suggestion.title: C2 Communication from Backdoored Dependencies
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'This backdoor allows hackers to remotely control infected computers through a server that sends them commands i.e. via a command and control server.' No detection hypothesis provided despite explicit C2 capability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline network egress from Go processes running BoltDB v1.3.1 or modules dependent on it. Alert on unexpected outbound connections to non-documented C2 infrastructure, particularly HTTPS connections with anomalous certificates or to uncommonly-contacted IP ranges. Correlate with module installation timestamp (Nov 2021 → Feb 2025 activation window).

suggestion.title: Dependency Update to Malicious Version
suggestion.rationale: Attack activation vector: 'we now wish to update our systems to the latest dependencies, which led developers to update the version that stayed in the system for 3 years.' Detectable as version-pull anomaly.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Go dependency management operations (go get, go mod tidy, dependency-update CI/CD runs) that target packages flagged in vulnerability advisories. Alert when updates pull versions older than current deployment, or versions that match known-compromised hashes. Correlate with Snyk/socket.dev advisory timestamps.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Package Name Pattern Matching
suggestion.rationale: Typo-squatting attack specifically exploited name similarity. Article: 'The malicious Go Module Mirror's was named github.com/botdb-go/bolt, similar to the original one i.e. github.com/boltdb/bolt.' Pattern-based detection of character-substitution squatting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Implement fuzzy-match detection on Go package imports against known-good package registry.
