suggestion.title: Widget Factory Content Editor Component Inventory
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV requires asset scan by patch due-date (2026-06-19). Pipeline must generate version-detection hunt against vulnerability scanner and package repositories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor installations with version < patched release. Confirm internet-facing exposure via network segmentation and WAF rules. Alert on any vulnerable instance not patched by federal due-date.

suggestion.title: PHP Interpreter Execution from Web Server Context
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'execution of PHP code'—post-upload execution must be detected at process level. Monitor for php.exe/php-cgi spawned by web-server user.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on php.exe or php-cgi process creation by IIS AppPool or Apache www-data user with working directory in web-accessible paths and no corresponding legitimate application activity (schedule tasks, maintenance scripts). Correlate with preceding unauthenticated web access logs.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Post-Upload Behavior Pattern
suggestion.rationale: After successful PHP upload, attacker typically tests shell with common commands (whoami, id, dir). Detect early post-exploitation reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor uploaded PHP files for rapid execution patterns: multiple distinct HTTP query parameters within 60 seconds, or unusual User-Agent combinations. Cross-reference HTTP request parameters with process creation arguments (if shell executes system commands).

suggestion.title: Joomla Unauthenticated Editor Profile Creation (CVE-2026-48907)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability allows 'creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users' — this is the direct exploit vector and must be detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP POST requests to Joomla editor profile endpoints with null or unauthenticated user context. Cross-correlate with profile creation events in Joomla audit logs showing invalid/missing credentials. High fidelity post-disclosure and for unpatched assets.

suggestion.title: Joomla PHP Code Upload and Web Execution (CVE-2026-48907)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'upload and execution of PHP code' — file writes to web-accessible directories followed by HTTP-triggered execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag .php/.phtml file creation in Joomla component/module/plugin directories with HTTP request timestamps within ±10s, or PHP execution from these paths by web-server user. Correlate with suspicious POST payloads in request logs.

suggestion.title: Widget Factory Content Editor Vulnerable Endpoint Access
suggestion.rationale: Article implies specific endpoints in the Widget Factory plugin are exploitable. Direct access to these endpoints from external sources should trigger alerts, especially POST/PUT methods.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor endpoints (URI patterns: /administrator/*, /components/com_*, /plugins/*) for POST/PUT from external IPs. Prioritize requests containing profile/config payloads or file uploads.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Joomla File System Activity Post-Exploit
suggestion.rationale: After uploading and executing PHP, attacker would persist via file modifications — article's 'execution' implies code runs with web-server privileges.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect chmod/chown on Joomla core directories, .htaccess modifications, or new .php files in administrator/tmp/ or web-root subdirectories with timestamps matching exploit request logs. Medium baseline, spike post-disclosure.

suggestion.title: Joomla Application Log Suspicious Profile/Editor Events
suggestion.rationale: Article states profiles are created by unauthenticated users — Joomla logs should record user_id=null or unauthenticated context on profile creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse Joomla logs for UserProfile or EditorProfile creation with missing/null authentication context. Match timestamps against HTTP POST attempts to /administrator/index.php. Severity bumps if profile is granted execution permissions.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scan Alert — CVE-2026-48907 Detected
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states under 'Indicators of Compromise': 'CVE-2026-48907 — match against your vulnerability scanner.' This is the primary detection gate for the CISA KEV entry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when scanners detect CVE-2026-48907 in Joomla Content Editor across the fleet. Cross-reference with asset inventory and flag unpatched instances for immediate remediation against the federal deadline (2026-06-19).

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Profile Creation Attempts in Joomla Editor
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability 'allow[s] for upload and execution of PHP code via the creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users.' Exploitation begins with profile creation from an unauthenticated context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to Joomla editor profile creation endpoints without valid session tokens or auth headers. Alert on profile creation attempts from external/untrusted IP ranges or bulk enumeration of the endpoint.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution via Malicious Editor Profile
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability enables 'upload and execution of PHP code'—this maps directly to T1059.004 code execution via script interpreter.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected PHP execution (eval, system, exec, passthru, shell_exec, include/require of user-controlled paths) originating from the Content Editor component. Cross-correlate with recent profile creation events.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Upload to Web-Accessible Directory via Editor
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation mechanism requires uploading files through the editor profile. Article states 'creation of new editor profiles' is the attack vector enabling 'upload and execution.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous file uploads through the Content Editor (especially .php, .phtml, .phar extensions) to web-accessible directories (/components/, /modules/, /plugins/). Alert on subsequent HTTP requests to newly-uploaded files.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure Hunt — Unpatched Joomla Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article instructs: 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' with template and federal deadline 2026-06-19. This is baseline detection for any CISA KEV entry—identify and prioritize exposed unpatched instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all Joomla instances via network discovery and HTTP fingerprinting (Joomla headers, /administrator/ path, version detection). Cross-check versions against patch date and correlate with vulnerability scan results to identify unpatched targets.

suggestion.title: LiteLLM: Host Header Injection Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'A crafted Host could therefore make the auth gate evaluate a different route from the one FastAPI dispatches.' Actual injection attacks manipulate Host headers; neither existing UC detects this mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor requests to `/key/*`, `/user/*`, `/team/*` endpoints for Host header anomalies: mismatches between Host header value and actual destination IP, repeated Host header mutations from single source, or Host headers containing semicolons/path-traversal patterns. Baseline legitimate proxy/load-balancer Host headers and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: LiteLLM: Auth Bypass Success Pattern (401→200)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes bypassing auth layer. Detection should look for sequences where repeated 401/403 responses are followed by 200/201 to same admin endpoint, indicating potential successful bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate failed auth attempts (401, 403 status) with subsequent successful requests (200, 201) to protected admin routes from same source within 5-minute window. Track Host header values in both request sequences; divergence suggests injection attack.

suggestion.title: LiteLLM: Rapid Admin-Route Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation of auth bypass would likely involve reconnaissance of available admin routes. Article lists 14+ protected endpoints; successful attack pattern may show sequential access attempts across multiple routes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag sources making successful requests to 3+ distinct management endpoints (across key/user/team/model/customer/spend categories) within 10 minutes. Legitimate admin activity typically targets subset of routes; broad enumeration is anomalous.

suggestion.title: LiteLLM: Unauthenticated Admin Endpoint Access
suggestion.rationale: Article core issue: 'allow unauthenticated access to protected management routes.' Detection should flag ANY successful (200/201/204) access to admin endpoints without prior auth tokens or from sources lacking admin privileges.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful (HTTP 200/201/204) requests to protected routes (key, user, team, model, customer, spend endpoints) that lack valid Authorization header, API key parameter, or session token. Correlate with source IP reputation; alert if source is external or non-whitelisted.

suggestion.title: LiteLLM Proxy Network Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Recon phase mentioned in article but not detected. Attackers must first identify exposed LiteLLM instances; banner-grab or version-enumeration attempts on common ports (8000, 8001, 4000) or `/health`, `/version` endpoints precede exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for repeated requests to `/health`, `/version`, `/docs` endpoints from external sources or requests to LiteLLM default ports from non-internal networks. Look for user-agent strings associated with scanners (curl without user-agent, Python-Requests, nmap-like patterns).

suggestion.title: LiteLLM Version-Check After Deploy
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability in versions < 1.84.0. After LiteLLM deployment or update events, confirm version via logs or config audit to ensure patched version is actually running.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate LiteLLM process startup events with version banners in application logs. Alert if startup messages or config files indicate version < 1.84.0 on internet-facing hosts. Check /etc/litellm/version or pip show litellm output post-deployment.

suggestion.title: Crawl4AI /screenshot or /pdf arbitrary output_path exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names '/screenshot and /pdf (CWE-22, CVSS 9.1)' with unvalidated output_path parameters. No detection currently monitors for suspicious path values in these endpoints, e.g., '../../../etc/passwd' or '/etc/cron.d/...'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST/GET requests to /screenshot or /pdf endpoints for output_path parameters containing path traversal patterns (../, .., encoded variants), absolute paths outside expected dirs (/tmp, /var), or suspicious file extensions (.sh, .conf, .cfg, .key). High fidelity if combined with file system create event on unvetted path.

suggestion.title: Crawl4AI JavaScript execution child process spawning
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions '/execute_js endpoint' for arbitrary JavaScript execution (T1059.007). No detection currently looks for the POST request being followed by unexpected child process creation (e.g., bash, sh, cmd spawned by Python process).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python/uvicorn/gunicorn processes spawning unexpected child processes (bash, cmd, powershell, /bin/sh) within 5 seconds of handling POST requests to /execute_js endpoint. Particularly high-fidelity if child inherits parent's network socket or writes to unexpected locations.

suggestion.title: Crawl4AI webhook endpoint data exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'webhooks' endpoint among vulnerable endpoints but no detection for outbound webhook calls or exfiltration via webhook callbacks. Attacker could craft payloads that trigger Crawl4AI to POST sensitive data to attacker-controlled servers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound HTTP POST/PUT requests initiated by Crawl4AI processes (python, uvicorn) to external IPs or non-corp domains on 80/443/8000/8080. Correlate with /webhook endpoint hits in web logs to identify potential exploitation.

suggestion.title: Crawl4AI extraction endpoint XSS or code injection payloads
suggestion.rationale: Article title lists 'XSS' vulnerability; article mentions '/markdown_extraction' and '/llm_extraction' endpoints but no detection for XSS payloads or script injection in extraction requests. Attacker could inject malicious HTML or JavaScript to poison extraction results.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect POST body payloads to /markdown_extraction and /llm_extraction endpoints for common XSS patterns (<script>, onerror=, onclick=), encoded script tags, and HTML event handlers. Flag requests with HTML/JavaScript payloads that differ from baseline content patterns (plain URLs, plain text).

suggestion.title: Crawl4AI /crawl endpoint URL exfiltration or command injection
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions '/crawl' endpoint as a vulnerable target but no use case detects suspicious URL parameters or payloads passed to it. Attackers could use /crawl to scan internal URLs (blind SSRF discovery) or inject commands via URL schemes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor /crawl endpoint for requests with RFC1918 URL targets, localhost URLs, cloud metadata URLs, or URLs containing file:// scheme. Also flag requests with command injection patterns in URL parameter (backticks, $(shell), pipe chars, semicolons in URL values).

suggestion.title: Crawl4AI kill chain: web request to file system artifact in sequence
suggestion.rationale: Kill chain reconstruction is empty. A complete sequence would be HTTP request to /screenshot (exploit) → file creation via Crawl4AI process (impact). No detection correlates the web request to subsequent file system activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate web access logs showing POST to /screenshot or /pdf endpoints (within 5-10 sec) with Filesystem events showing unexpected file creation by the Crawl4AI process. Alert if correlation count exceeds baseline or files are created in protected directories.

suggestion.title: Crawl4AI /crawl endpoint request with computed_fields or extraction_strategy attributes
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Python generator and frame object attributes (gi_frame, f_back, f_builtins) do NOT start with underscore, enabling a complete sandbox escape.' Should detect JSON payloads to POST /crawl containing computed_fields or JsonCssExtractionStrategy with chained attribute access (e.g., {"computed_fields": {"exp": "obj.gi_frame.f_back(...)"}}).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag POST requests to /crawl endpoint containing keywords 'computed_fields', 'extraction_strategy', 'JsonCssExtractionStrategy' in request body, especially when paired with frame/generator attributes (gi_frame, f_back, f_builtins, f_globals). High-confidence indicator of CVE-2026-53753 exploitation.

suggestion.title: Crawl4AI service initialized without JWT/authentication validation
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'The attack requires no authentication (JWT disabled by default).' Services without JWT validation are trivially exploitable. Should detect Crawl4AI startup with auth disabled or missing auth middleware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Crawl4AI/uvicorn process initialization with jwt_enabled=false, missing auth middleware, or absence of --auth flag in process command line. Also monitor for configuration files with auth_required: false or missing authentication_provider setting. Indicates exposed attack surface.

suggestion.title: RCE-spawned process accessing /var/run/docker.sock from Crawl4AI container
suggestion.rationale: Article title references 'Docker API' as attack vector. Post-RCE, attacker with container escape access to docker.sock can escalate to host/cluster compromise. Should detect python/sh processes from Crawl4AI runtime accessing docker.sock.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Crawl4AI container processes (python, sh, bash spawned from uvicorn/gunicorn parent) attempting open/read of /var/run/docker.sock or executing docker/docker-compose commands. Also detect container mounts that expose docker.sock at runtime.

suggestion.title: Post-RCE Kubernetes service account token exfiltration from Crawl4AI pod
suggestion.rationale: Article lists '/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io' in credential access UC and T1552.005 in techniques. Deployed Crawl4AI pods with service accounts leak K8s cluster access. Should detect reads of /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token and API calls using that token.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Crawl4AI process or shell spawned from it (post-RCE) reading /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token, certificate, or namespace files. Correlate with subsequent kubectl or curl calls to Kubernetes API endpoints using that token.

suggestion.title: Crawl4AI container process attempting library/module import of restricted modules
suggestion.rationale: Article describes sandbox escape using 'gi_frame', 'f_back' to access f_builtins and __import__. Should detect import of restricted modules (os, subprocess, socket) or use of __import__ function via ast/code evaluation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Crawl4AI Python process for runtime evaluation patterns: use of eval(), exec(), compile() with untrusted input, or __import__ calls originating from HTTP request parameters. Pair with ast_eval or similar function hooks if available in instrumentation.

suggestion.title: Crawl4AI multi-stage RCE: exploit → shell → credential/IMDS → lateral movement
suggestion.rationale: Article describes complete kill chain: exploit /crawl → RCE → credential discovery → cloud/container escalation. Should have correlation rule that chains UC_8_1 (exploit) → UC_8_2 (shell) → UC_8_3 or UC_8_4 (credential/metadata access) on same host/container within time window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlation rule: POST /crawl with sandbox-escape payload (UC_8_1) followed within 60s by process creation of shell from uvicorn parent (UC_8_2), followed within 300s by credential file access or IMDS request (UC_8_3 or UC_8_4) from same host/container. Confirms full exploitation chain.

suggestion.title: Accessibility Service Abuse via Unsolicited Request
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'Rokarolla requests Accessibility service permissions' as the mechanism to achieve 'complete administrative control.' Accessibility abuse is the single highest-signal Android threat behavior and must be detected—this is the privilege escalation fulcrum.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Android app requesting accessibility service permission without user interaction, OR requesting accessibility after presenting fake login overlay. Cross-reference app package name against known malware families. Accessibility grants to apps with SMS/notification access permissions are high-fidelity indicators.

suggestion.title: Fake Overlay Detection — Phishing and PIN Capture
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Rokarolla displays a fake login overlay to steal login credentials' and uses 'overlays…to capture the lock-screen PIN/pattern.' Overlay-based credential capture is a core attack primitive and must be detected at runtime.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for UI layer injection or window overlay creation on top of known banking/crypto apps. Flag attempts to draw translucent overlays matching phishing templates (login, PIN entry, '2FA' screens). Combine with keystroke capture hooks (T1056.004) to detect simultaneous overlays + keylogging.

suggestion.title: Google Play Protect Disablement — System Hardening Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'disabling Google Play Protect' as a core evasion tactic. Disabling device security services is a high-confidence defense evasion signal and must be detected immediately.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for disabled or suspended Google Play Protect service, OR settings changes disabling background scanning. Correlate with app installation events to detect malware disabling defenses post-installation. MDM-enrolled devices should alert on any attempt to modify Play Protect policy.

suggestion.title: SMS and Contact List Exfiltration via Unsandboxed API Access
suggestion.rationale: Article lists: 'Steal SMS messages' and 'Extract contact information and WhatsApp contacts' as core malware capabilities. Collection of SMS and contacts is a direct precursor to account takeover and fraud.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect apps with SMS or contact permission reading >100 messages/contacts within a 1-minute window (bulk extraction). Combine with network egress to unknown C2 servers. Flag combinations: (SMS permission + network exfiltration + accessibility grant + no user interaction).

suggestion.title: Keystroke Logging and Screen Recording Primitive Activation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'using keyloggers to continuously record user input' and 'Record on-screen content via UI logging' and 'Periodically take screenshots and upload them.' Continuous keystroke monitoring and screenshot collection are direct indicators of credential theft infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for input method service hooks (IME hijacking) or window manager callbacks registering on-screen touch/keystroke listeners. Detect screen capture API calls (MediaProjection, ScreenCapture) in combination with file write+network exfiltration. Establish baseline for app's historical screen capture behavior and alert on deviation.

suggestion.title: C2 Device Profile Enumeration and Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'Communication with the command-and-control (C2) server begins with sending a basic device profile containing details such as the phone model, installed Android version, locale, display characteristics, battery level, storage capacity, and available RAM.' This enumeration-then-check-against-target-list pattern is the attacker's reconnaissance phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound HTTP POST containing device metadata (Android version, locale, RAM, battery, storage, model) to C2 domain. Baseline normal app telemetry and alert on unauthenticated exfiltration to non-standard endpoints. Correlate with subsequent phishing overlay deployment to C2 to confirm check-target-list-then-download-payload flow.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Ivanti Product Version Detected
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names Ivanti critical vulnerability patches; pipeline extracted no version IOCs despite 'Ivanti' being high-priority vendor. Should monitor for vulnerable Ivanti Cloud Services, Ivanti Endpoint Manager, Ivanti Workspace Control versions in use.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag agents running Ivanti product versions in published vulnerable ranges (e.g., Ivanti Cloud Services < patched version). Cross-reference against known CVE advisories for Ivanti released this month. Correlate with failed update attempts or rollback events.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Fortinet FortiOS Version in Use
suggestion.rationale: Article names Fortinet critical patches; no Fortinet-specific IOCs extracted. Should detect FortiOS versions below patched baseline, especially on edge/perimeter devices where RCE impact is highest.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Fortinet device inventory for FortiOS version < known patch version. Monitor failed SSH/API login attempts to FortiGate devices (exploitation footprint). Alert on administrative access from non-standard IPs post-disclosure (indicates rapid scanning).

suggestion.title: SAP System Vulnerability Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions SAP critical patches but no SAP IOCs extracted. SAP vulnerabilities (e.g., in NetWeaver, Fiori, HR modules) are high-value targets; pipeline should track vulnerable versions and exploitation indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify SAP systems running vulnerable versions (extract from patch advisory). Monitor SAP audit logs for failed logons, privilege escalation attempts, or suspicious RFC calls post-disclosure. Flag any HTTP requests to known SAP CVE exploitation endpoints.

suggestion.title: Patch Deployment Failure or Rollback Post-Advisory
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates patches available but pipeline did not generate UC for monitoring deployment status. Organizations often delay or struggle with critical patches; gap detection is valuable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track patch deployment status 48-72 hours post-advisory for Ivanti, Fortinet, SAP assets. Alert on systems in vulnerable version ranges that fail patch installation or roll back patches. Correlate with high-risk asset classification (public-facing, DMZ).

suggestion.title: Joomla Content Editor Profile Creation - Unauthenticated Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability allows 'creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users'—this is the attack surface and initial access vector the pipeline should have translated into detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST requests to Joomla Content Editor profile endpoints (/components/com_contenteditor/profiles or variant) from requests without valid session tokens or authentication headers. Alert on HTTP 200-201 responses indicating successful profile creation from anonymous/unauthenticated sources.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution via Content Editor Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability enables 'upload and execution of PHP code'—execution is the weaponization phase and most critical malicious outcome to detect.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag PHP file uploads (<?php markers) to Content Editor working directories or detection of web server executing PHP from these paths immediately after suspicious POST requests. Correlate multipart/form-data with PHP code strings in request body.

suggestion.title: Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor CVE-2026-48907 Asset Scan
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends 'standard asset-exposure hunt' and explicitly applies template to CVE-2026-48907—vulnerability matching is the baseline detection the pipeline entirely omitted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for CVE-2026-48907 matches against Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor component. Cross-reference CMDB for inventory of exposed Joomla instances. Note federal patch-due date of 2026-06-19 for audit timeline correlation.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48907: Joomla Content Editor Unauthenticated Profile Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'improper access control vulnerability which could allow for upload and execution of PHP code via the creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users' — initial access vector completely undetected by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for POST requests to Joomla editor profile creation endpoints (typically /components/com_jeditor/* or similar) from sources with no prior authentication session. Alert on HTTP 200/201 responses indicating successful profile creation by unauthenticated users.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48907: Suspicious PHP File Upload via Joomla Editor
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'upload and execution of PHP code' as the exploitation method — core execution step requires dedicated detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on .php file uploads or PHP-executable content written via Joomla editor endpoints to web-accessible directories. Correlate with subsequent PHP process spawning, shell command execution, or anomalous file system activity in web-root paths.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48907: Widget Factory Content Editor Vulnerable Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV requires immediate asset visibility. Article names 'Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor' as the vulnerable product — no asset discovery or inventory use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners and asset inventory systems for all Joomla installations with Widget Factory Content Editor plugin enabled. Flag instances below the patched version. Compare deployment dates against the federal patch deadline of 2026-06-19 to prioritize remediation.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48907: Post-Exploitation PHP Webshell Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article's 'execution of PHP code' implies persistence and post-compromise activity — no post-exploitation detection logic provided despite this being the attacker's final objective.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal PHP process behavior: spawning of system shells (cmd.exe, /bin/bash), command execution from PHP interpreter context, file modifications in Joomla editor working directories, or outbound network connections initiated by PHP processes.

suggestion.title: Joomla Content Editor Unauthenticated Profile Creation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'improper access control vulnerability which could allow...creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users.' This is the root exploit step; detecting unauthenticated requests to profile creation endpoints is the highest-fidelity detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST requests to Joomla Content Editor profile endpoints (e.g., /components/com_joomlacontenteditor/...) lacking valid session tokens or admin credentials. Track requests with content-type application/x-www-form-urlencoded containing profile creation parameters (e.g., name=, type=, description=) from non-authenticated user contexts.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Upload to Joomla Editor Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'upload and execution of PHP code via the creation of new editor profiles.' This is the payload delivery and execution moment. Detecting .php files written to editor profile directories post-upload is a core TTW.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on PHP file creation in Joomla Content Editor directories (typically /components/com_joomlacontenteditor, /plugins, or /tmp derivatives) following unauthenticated requests. Correlate file-write events with subsequent PHP process spawning (php-fpm, apache, www-data) within 10 seconds, especially if the PHP file contains obfuscated or base64-encoded payloads.

suggestion.title: Suspicious PHP Execution in Web-Accessible Joomla Paths
suggestion.rationale: Article: '...could allow for upload and execution of PHP code.' Execution following upload is the attack completion. Detect PHP processes invoked from recently-created files in vulnerable component directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PHP process creation (php-fpm, php-cli, apache php handler) with a working directory or argument matching Joomla editor directories, especially when the parent process is the web server and the child PHP process references files younger than 60 seconds.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48907 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article instructs: 'match against your vulnerability scanner' and references template asset-exposure hunt for vulnerability detection. Pipeline must generate scanner-based detection rules for this CISA KEV entry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate vulnerability scanner reports flagging CVE-2026-48907 (Joomla Content Editor improper access control) against asset inventory. Prioritize any unpatched Joomla instances with the vulnerable component exposed on internet-facing ports. Cross-check patch application dates against public disclosure to identify remediation lag vs. federal due date (2026-06-19 per article).

suggestion.title: Joomla Content Editor Component Web Exposure Discovery
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry implies active exploitation; standard asset-exposure hunt is required per article. Any exposed Joomla Content Editor instance is an exploitation vector regardless of patch status.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search firewall and proxy logs for inbound HTTP requests to known Joomla Content Editor paths (/components/com_joomlacontenteditor, /index.php?option=com_joomlacontenteditor). Correlate with asset inventory to isolate exposed instances and correlate with successful admin bypass attempts or unexpected profile creation.

suggestion.title: Joomla Content Editor Unauthenticated Profile Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'allow for upload and execution of PHP code via the creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users.' Profile creation is the exploitation vector; detection of unauthorized attempts is essential.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to Joomla Content Editor profile-creation endpoints (/administrator/components/com_joomla_content_editor/*) from sources without valid session tokens. Alert on repeated attempts or rapid profile creation.

suggestion.title: Joomla Content Editor Arbitrary PHP File Upload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'upload and execution of PHP code.' Detection of PHP uploads to editor-controlled directories prevents payload staging.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on PHP file uploads to /components/com_joomla_content_editor/ and profile-storage paths. Correlate with unauthenticated access. Monitor for uploads of .php, .phtml, .php5 files regardless of initial request method or obfuscation.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure - Joomla Content Editor (CVE-2026-48907)
suggestion.rationale: Article directive: 'CVE-2026-48907 — match against your vulnerability scanner.' Federal patch due 2026-06-19 provides compliance tracking point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Vulnerability scanner must flag Joomla installations with Content Editor plugin versions vulnerable to CVE-2026-48907. Cross-reference asset database to identify unpatched systems and track remediation against federal deadline.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated PHP File Upload to Web Root
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'upload and execution of PHP code via the creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users' — core attack step requiring web server or file system detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP POST requests to Joomla editor profile endpoints from unauthenticated sessions, followed by .php file creation in web-accessible directories. Correlate with file system events showing new PHP files in web root.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution After Profile Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'upload and execution of PHP code' — successful exploitation requires runtime execution of uploaded payload, detectable via process or web server logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate recent PHP file uploads to web root with subsequent php.exe or php-cgi.exe process execution from web server context. Monitor web server logs for access to recently uploaded profile files.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48907 Vulnerability Scan Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE: CVE-2026-48907 — match against your vulnerability scanner' as primary detection method.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scan results identifying CVE-2026-48907 in Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor. Prioritize web-facing instances. Verify patches even if scanners report patched state, as patch lag is common.

suggestion.title: Administrator Interface Access by Unauthenticated User
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'improper access control vulnerability which could allow...unauthenticated users' — this access control flaw should be detectable at application authentication layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Joomla logs for administrator interface access (/administrator/index.php) without valid session authentication or with null/guest user context. Flag POST requests to create editor profiles missing authorization headers.

suggestion.title: Typosquatted Go Module Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article core: 'malicious Go Module Mirror's was named github.com/botdb-go/bolt, similar to the original one i.e. github.com/boltdb/bolt'. Phonetic/orthographic similarity is the attack vector; no detection for this high-confidence IOC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag go.mod/go.sum imports of 'github.com/botdb-go/bolt' or Levenshtein distance ≤2 matches to known-good package names (boltdb, bolt). Cross-reference Go Module Proxy resolution logs against blocklist of known typosquatted variants. Alert on module fetch from proxy.golang.org with name divergence from upstream source repository.

suggestion.title: Go Module Proxy Cache Persistence: Stale Malicious Version
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Go Module Mirror's indefinite caching of modules kicked in, and that cached the backdored module' for 3+ years (Nov 2021–Jan 2025). No detection for cache poison or stale-module serving from proxy.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Go Module Proxy requests for cache hits on versions 1.3.1 of botdb-go/bolt with request timestamps after Feb 7, 2025 (removal date). Validate returned module hash against upstream git tag. Alert if proxy serves cached content with stale Date/Last-Modified headers indicating indefinite caching policy.

suggestion.title: Remote Command Execution via Backdoored Module
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'backdoor allows hackers to remotely control infected computers through a server that sends them commands i.e. via a command and control server'. No C2 or process-execution detection for compromised Go applications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For processes or libraries built with BoltDB v1.3.1 (pre-Feb 2025): alert on unexpected outbound connections to non-standard ports or newly-seen domains. Correlate with spawning of cmd.exe, /bin/bash, or powershell without corresponding user logon or service install events. Look for regular beaconing patterns (heartbeat intervals).

suggestion.title: Malicious Go Module Supply Chain Advisory Lookup
suggestion.rationale: Article cites specific advisory: 'Snyk Open Source advisory: https://security.snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-GOLANG-GITHUBCOMBOLTDBGOBOLT-868841' and 'https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2025-3451'. These are definitive IOCs; pipeline should correlate any Go module usage against these database entries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference all go.mod/go.sum entries and compiled binary dependencies against Snyk vuln DB and Go vuln DB (pkg.go.dev/vuln). Flag exact matches on botdb-go/bolt or hash matches on v1.3.1. Query 'go list -m all' outputs for presence of malicious package.

suggestion.title: Version Constraint Relaxation Enabling Malicious Module Pull
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'we now wish to update our systems to the latest dependencies, which led developers to update the version that stayed in the system for 3 years'. Pipeline should detect when version pins are removed, allowing resolution to cached malicious versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when go.mod pin constraints (e.g., '= v1.2.0') are changed to loose ranges ('~', '^', or removed entirely). If the new constraint can resolve to botdb-go/bolt v1.3.1 or any version from a Go Module Proxy response with timestamp in [Nov 2021, Feb 7 2025], escalate. Review go.mod diffs prior to 'go get -u' commands.

suggestion.title: Typosquatting Pattern: Package Name Orthographic Distance
suggestion.rationale: Article defines typosquatting attack surface: 'bad actors create and upload harmful software packages...using names very similar to popular ones'. No detection for high-similarity package names in package managers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compute Levenshtein distance or Jaro-Winkler similarity for all package names in go.mod against a curated set of high-value targets (boltdb, bolt, redis, kafka, etc.). Alert if similarity score >0.85 and package origin is non-standard domain (not github.com/<canonical-org>). Cross-reference maintainer identity.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Joomla Content Editor Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly: 'improper access control vulnerability which could allow for upload and execution of PHP code via the creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users.' This is T1190 public-facing app exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST/GET requests to Joomla Content Editor profile creation endpoints (e.g., /component/contenteditor/profile/) originating from unauthenticated sessions or missing/invalid JWT/session tokens. Baseline legitimate editor access and alert on anomalous request volume, unusual geographic origin, or known exploit signatures.

suggestion.title: PHP File Upload to Joomla Editor Writable Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'upload...of PHP code' as the exploitation mechanism. Detect file uploads to editor-controlled paths without proper MIME validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor multipart/form-data requests uploading .php or executable files to /components/com_contenteditor/uploads/, /tmp/joomla_*, or editor cache directories. Flag uploads with mismatched MIME types (e.g., .php declared as image/jpeg). Cross-correlate uploads from unauthenticated sessions.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution from Editor Upload Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates uploaded code is 'executed'—implying T1059.001 command execution. Detect PHP interpreter spawning from editor-controlled paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on php-cgi.exe, php, or php-fpm processes spawned from Joomla editor directories (/components/com_contenteditor/, /tmp/joomla_uploads/). Correlate file uploads to the same path within 5 minutes. Flag if parent process is Apache/IIS worker thread and child process spawns shell commands (cmd.exe, /bin/sh).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Joomla Editor Profile Creation by Unauthenticated User
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users' as the core exploit vector. Profile creation is account/persistence mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST requests to profile creation endpoints from unauthenticated or low-privilege contexts. Flag rapid profile creation, profiles with escalated permissions, or profiles with non-standard names. Cross-reference database audit logs for jos_user_profiles or jos_users insertions from external IPs.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48907 Presence in Vulnerability Scan Results
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies CVE-2026-48907 as actively exploited (CISA KEV). Asset inventory and scanner output must be checked for unpatched instances; federal patch deadline is 2026-06-19.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner database (Nessus, Qualys, Rapid7) for Joomla Content Editor (Widget Factory) installations matching vulnerable version ranges for CVE-2026-48907. Flag any unpatched instance as immediate remediation target. Cross-correlate with web logs for exploitation signatures matching public POC code.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Web Access Patterns to Joomla /administrator/ Paths
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires access to protected /administrator/ endpoints. Article implies authentication is bypassed; detect unusual access patterns indicating exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to /administrator/, /administrator/index.php targeting Joomla systems from external IPs. Alert on requests with: exploit signatures in User-Agent or request body, POST requests to editor component endpoints, requests originating from known vulnerability scanner IPs, or concurrent 401/403 responses followed by successful access. Correlate with failed authentication attempts.

suggestion.title: Asset Inventory: Joomla Content Editor Instances (CVE-2026-48907)
suggestion.rationale: Article instructs: 'Even if your scanners say not vulnerable because of patches, it's worth one quick check across your fleet — patch lag is the silent killer.' Requires asset discovery before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability management and asset databases for Joomla Content Editor installations from vendor Widget Factory. Identify instances with version tags predating CVE-2026-48907 patch release. Cross-reference patch-management logs to confirm absence of remediation patches as of federal due date (2026-06-19).

suggestion.title: Web Access: Unauthenticated HTTP Requests to Joomla Editor Profile Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability: 'allows for upload and execution of PHP code via the creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users.' Unauthenticated profile creation is the exploitation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST/GET requests to Joomla editor profile creation endpoints from sessions lacking valid authentication tokens. Flag successful responses (HTTP 200-204) to profile-creation URIs. Correlate with absence of prior login events or auth-header presence.

suggestion.title: Web Application: Suspicious PHP File Upload via Editor Profiles
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation payload delivery: 'upload and execution of PHP code via the creation of new editor profiles.' File upload precedes execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect multipart/form-data POST requests to editor profile endpoints containing .php, .phtml, .php5 file payloads. Monitor file-creation events in Joomla web-accessible directories (wp-content, plugins, media) that follow HTTP uploads from unauthenticated sessions. Correlate file timestamps with HTTP POST logs.

suggestion.title: Execution: PHP Code Execution Post-Profile-Upload
suggestion.rationale: Attack outcome: 'execution of PHP code.' Post-upload code execution is the RCE indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PHP interpreter execution (php-cgi, php-fpm) initiated from Joomla editor profile directories immediately following file uploads. Detect web-server child processes spawning system commands (whoami, id, curl, wget) or establishing network connections. Look for execution patterns atypical of legitimate Joomla plugin activity.

suggestion.title: Compliance: Patch Status Against Federal Remediation Deadline
suggestion.rationale: Article provides federal context: 'Federal patch due: 2026-06-19' and 'Federal civilian agencies are required to remediate by the published due date.' Compliance check is mandatory for federal/regulated orgs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Generate daily alerts for any Joomla Content Editor instances matching CVE-2026-48907 vulnerability criteria still present in asset inventory after June 19, 2026. Flag for compliance escalation if patch status remains unresolved. Cross-reference with federal agency audit requirements.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Joomla Editor Profile Creation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'allows for... creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users'—the profile-creation endpoint is the attack surface. Detection should monitor for unauthorized profile additions without prior authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Joomla editor component for POST/PUT requests to profile creation endpoints from unauthenticated sessions or from IPs/user-agents showing no prior authentication tokens. Correlate with successful HTTP 200/201 responses indicating profile was created.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Upload via Joomla Editor Profile
suggestion.rationale: Core attack mechanism: 'upload and execution of PHP code via the creation of new editor profiles.' Detection must catch file uploads with PHP extensions or execution patterns within the editor module.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Joomla installation directory for new .php files created in editor-related paths with timestamps matching suspicious profile-creation HTTP requests. Flag if file creation occurs outside normal maintenance windows and correlates with unauthenticated access patterns.

suggestion.title: Joomla Content Editor PHP Execution by Unauthenticated Context
suggestion.rationale: The vulnerability enables 'execution of PHP code' by design; any execution of PHP from the editor component by an unauthenticated session is exploitation-indicative.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PHP interpreter execution (php-cgi, php-fpm processes) spawned by the web server with parent/context tied to editor profile uploads. Flag if execution originates from HTTP requests with no prior session authentication or from newly created profiles.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48907 Vulnerability Scanner Hit — Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry with active exploitation; scanner detection is baseline control. Article names 'CVE-2026-48907' explicitly and recommends asset-exposure hunts.

suggestion.title: Widget Factory Joomla Editor Plugin Not Patched by Due Date

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query patch-management systems and vulnerability scans for any Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor instance with version <patched build after 2026-06-19 due-date. Escalate unpatched instances as compliance/remediation risk.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanning Alert — CVE-2026-48907

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when vulnerability scanner detects CVE-2026-48907 in Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor plugin across any asset. Cross-correlate with asset inventory to identify network exposure. Prioritize instances visible from untrusted networks or lacking compensating controls (WAF blocks, network segmentation).

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Editor Profile Creation Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'could allow for upload and execution of PHP code via the creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users.' Access control bypass on sensitive administrative endpoint is the initial access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to Joomla editor profile creation endpoints (typically /index.php?option=com_contenteditor&task=editorprofiles or /administrator/index.php?...) originating from unauthenticated sessions (no valid session token, failed auth headers, or user=guest). Focus on POST requests returning 200/302 status indicating successful profile creation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious PHP File Creation in Editor Profile Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'upload and execution of PHP code.' Detection of file write activity to editor profile directories is the execution/persistence phase following the initial access exploit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for .php/.php3/.php5/.phtml file creation in Joomla editor profile directories (typically /components/com_contenteditor/profiles/ or /media/contenteditor/profiles/). Correlate file creation timestamps with HTTP POST requests to profile creation endpoints. Flag files created outside normal maintenance windows or by web server process user spawning unexpected child processes.

suggestion.title: Web Server Process Spawning Shell Commands Post-Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states impact is 'execution of PHP code' — once malicious PHP is uploaded, attackers execute commands. Detection of process creation from web server context indicates post-exploitation activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation with parent=w3wp.exe (IIS) or apache2/httpd (Linux), spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, sh, or unusual interpreters. Flag processes with command-line containing common web shell patterns (system, exec, shell_exec, passthru). Correlate with PHP file creation in editor directories within same timeframe.

suggestion.title: Repeated HTTP Requests to Uploaded PHP Files in Editor Directories
suggestion.rationale: After successful upload and initial execution, attackers maintain access by repeatedly invoking web shell. Detection of repeated access patterns to uploaded files indicates persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag repeated HTTP GET/POST requests to .php files in editor directories from same external IP across multiple sessions/timeframes. Legitimate editor profiles accessed via Joomla admin UI; malicious web shells accessed via direct URL. Look for off-hours access, requests from unexpected geographies, or unusual parameter patterns in requests to uploaded PHP files.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Langflow API Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'Unauthenticated RCE' — core attack vector is direct HTTP/REST access to Langflow endpoints without authentication. No detection UC was generated despite explicit signal in title.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Langflow API endpoints (/api/*, /flow/*, /chat/messages) for requests originating from untrusted sources that succeed despite missing or invalid authentication tokens. Flag payloads matching known CVE-2026-5027 exploitation patterns.

suggestion.title: Child Process Execution from Langflow Service
suggestion.rationale: Title confirms RCE exploitation occurs—this requires monitoring for shell spawning from the Langflow service process. Pipeline provided zero execution-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned by langflow.exe or python langflow: cmd.exe, powershell.exe, /bin/bash, sh, with focus on commands that execute remote code, wget/curl, or privilege escalation.

suggestion.title: Outbound C2 or Data Exfiltration from Langflow Process
suggestion.rationale: RCE typically leads to secondary payloads or data extraction. Article does not detail exploitation method, but post-RCE network activity is a standard detection vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound connections from Langflow service to non-whitelisted external IPs/domains, especially on high-numbered ports or known C2 infrastructure. Correlate timing with exploitation timestamps.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-5027 Vulnerability Presence in Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes vulnerability is 'unpatched'—detection must include vulnerability scanning to flag vulnerable Langflow instances before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference asset inventory against known vulnerable Langflow versions for CVE-2026-5027. Alert if vulnerable version is internet-facing or accessible from untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48907 Vulnerability Detection - Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article states Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor is 'observed exploited in the wild' per CISA KEV. Vulnerability scanner detection is the first hunt mentioned in article body.

Match CVE-2026-48907 against your vulnerability scanner to find exposed, unpatched instances. Prioritize any flagged assets for immediate patching before federal due date 2026-06-19.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Editor Profile Creation Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'allows for upload and execution...via the creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users.' This is the root access control bypass that enables the attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web access logs for POST requests to Joomla editor profile creation endpoints (typically /index.php?option=com_jckeditor or plugin-specific paths) from unauthenticated sessions (no valid session cookie/auth token). Alert on HTTP 200 responses indicating successful profile creation without prior authentication.

suggestion.title: PHP File Upload to Editor Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability enables 'upload...of PHP code.' This is the execution preparation step requiring direct log detection on the web server.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for POST/PUT requests containing .php file uploads to Joomla editor profile directories or temporary upload paths. Flag multipart/form-data requests with PHP MIME types or raw .php file content to plugin-controlled directories. Cross-reference with access logs showing unauthenticated requests (absent auth headers/cookies).

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution in Joomla Editor Paths
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability enables 'execution of PHP code.' Direct execution detection closes the attack sequence and signals active compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when PHP processes spawn with parent process php-cgi.exe or similar, where the working directory contains newly-created .php files in Joomla editor profile folders (non-standard locations for legitimate code). Correlate with prior upload activity in same session. Look for anomalous command line arguments (e.g., `php -r`, shell metacharacters) in execution context.

suggestion.title: Joomla Editor Profile Creation Abuse Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies the attack vector: profile creation is the mechanism. Behavioral pattern detection can catch variations on the base CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate editor profile creation (frequency, authenticated user source, standard parameters). Alert on spike in profile creation attempts from new/external IPs, unauthenticated requests, or concurrent creation+upload+execute chains within single session. Profile creation should be infrequent and admin-only in secure configs.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Creation in Joomla Plugin Directories
suggestion.rationale: Implied by PHP execution capability. Web shells are the canonical post-exploit artifact for code-upload vulnerabilities and warrant dedicated detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for newly-created .php files in `/components/com_jckeditor/` or similar editor plugin paths with suspicious file sizes (very small, <5KB, typical of simple shells), non-standard filenames (shell.php, admin.php, x.php), or high entropy content. Correlate file creation timestamp with prior web access logs showing upload requests.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48907 Vulnerable Joomla Content Editor Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry with active exploitation; federal remediation due 2026-06-19. Baseline asset discovery is the canonical first UC. Article: 'Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor contains an improper access control vulnerability.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for instances of Joomla Content Editor or CVE-2026-48907 signatures in vulnerability scanner output and asset management systems. Identify exposed Joomla installations accessible from untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Joomla Editor Profile Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'could allow for upload and execution of PHP code via the creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users.' POST requests to profile-creation endpoints without authentication are the exploitation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST requests to Joomla Content Editor profile/plugin endpoints returning success (HTTP 200/201) when no Authorization header, session cookie, or admin token is present. Baseline against known admin IPs first.

suggestion.title: PHP File Upload to Web-Accessible Directory

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for successful POST requests to editor endpoints followed by creation of .php files in Joomla installation directories. Windows: detect file writes to web root via filesystem auditing. Linux: auditd rules on upload paths.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution from Editor Directories
suggestion.rationale: Following successful upload, PHP payload must be invoked. Processes executing PHP from web-accessible directories indicate post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect php.exe, php-cgi.exe, or sh/bash child processes spawned by web server processes (w3wp.exe, httpd) with current working directory in Joomla install path. High fidelity if correlated with recent editor profile creation and PHP file writes.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Outbound Communication from Compromised Joomla Server
suggestion.rationale: If PHP web shell executes, attacker will likely establish C2 or data exfil. Article: 'execution of PHP code' implies payload execution and potential command handling.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline the compromised Joomla server's normal egress profile, then detect anomalous outbound HTTP/HTTPS connections to non-whitelisted external IPs/domains, particularly high-entropy domain names or residential IPs. Pair with recent editor profile creation + PHP upload timeline.

suggestion.title: JDY Botnet C2 Beacon Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes bot command infrastructure via phrase 'expands to 1,500+ devices'—implies active C2 communication. Pipeline extracted zero network indicators despite C2 being the operational spine of any botnet.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag repetitive outbound connections from endpoints to previously unseen destinations at fixed intervals. Detect beaconing signatures: fixed packet size, consistent time delta, anomalous user-agent strings. Monitor DNS for subdomains or dynamic resolution patterns typical of C2 fallback logic.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance Command Execution - Discovery Phase
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'cyber reconnaissance'—this is the explicit attack objective. Pipeline generated zero detections for T1018, T1087, or T1010. Phrase 'cyber reconnaissance' directly establishes discovery techniques as core botnet behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on rapid-fire execution of system enumeration commands (whoami, systeminfo, ipconfig, net user, net group, tasklist, Get-ADUser). Correlate multiple discovery commands executed in sequence by same process or parent. Flag LDAP or WMI queries from non-standard caller processes.

suggestion.title: Botnet Persistence via Registry/Scheduled Task Injection
suggestion.rationale: 1,500+ devices requires durable persistence to survive reboot cycles. Article mentions sustained botnet operation—implies T1053 or T1547 techniques. Pipeline captured no persistence detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for schtasks.exe or AT.exe creating scheduled tasks at off-hours. Alert on RunOnce, Run, Services registry hive modifications by unsigned/unknown processes. Track WMI event subscriptions for backdoor persistence patterns.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration to C2 Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Reconnaissance botnet collects and transmits intelligence off-host. Article phrase 'cyber reconnaissance' implies data gathering and exfil. Pipeline missed exfiltration detections entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous outbound traffic volume from endpoints to known C2 destinations. Alert on large file transfers initiated by scripting processes (wscript, powershell, cmd). Monitor for data staging patterns (temporary archive files created then deleted).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Execution from Temporary Directories
suggestion.rationale: Botnets typically execute from %Temp%, %AppData%, Downloads. Article title 'JDY Botnet' implies malware binary execution. Pipeline extracted zero execution-locus detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on executable creation and execution from %Temp%, %AppData%\Local\Temp, Downloads, or %ProgramData% directories. Flag unsigned executables or those with mismatched signing certificates. Monitor for parent-child process anomalies (cmd.exe spawning from explorer.exe).

suggestion.title: China-Linked APT Botnet Infrastructure Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'China-Linked.' Pipeline surfaced zero actor attribution, nation-state tactics, or predictive hunting correlation to known Chinese APT infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference JDY botnet C2 infrastructure, malware code patterns, and targeting scope against known China-nexus APT TTPs (APT10, APT15, APT29 subgroups). Baseline the legitimate Joomla distribution; flag hash mismatches or unexpected new files. Correlate file writes with prior unauthenticated HTTP requests to editor profile endpoints.

Flag execution initiated by the web server process (apache/nginx) with unusual parent-child relationships. Correlate with prior unauthenticated editor profile creation events.
