suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Joomla Widget Factory endpoints for POST requests creating editor profiles without valid authentication tokens or session cookies. Alert on anomalous profile creation from external IPs, suspicious user agents, or unusual volume patterns.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution via Joomla Widget Factory Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability allows 'upload and execution of PHP code'—the execution phase. No detection generated despite this being the critical post-exploitation impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on PHP file uploads to Joomla directories from unauthenticated or unprivileged sessions. Correlate with subsequent PHP execution artifacts in error logs or web server process execution.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48907 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends 'standard asset-exposure hunt' via 'vulnerability scanner'—pipeline generated no asset-exposure or scanner-based detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner output for CVE-2026-48907 matches on Joomla installations. Alert on any vulnerable status past the 2026-06-19 federal remediation deadline.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Joomla Administrator or Editor Account Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article states unauthenticated users can create editor profiles—these profiles carry elevated permissions. No detection for unexpected account creation or privilege escalation via this mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Joomla admin tables for new editor or admin accounts created from web context or low-privilege sessions. Alert on account creation without corresponding legitimate admin UI access logs.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48907 Vulnerability Scan Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states CVE-2026-48907 is a CISA KEV entry with active exploitation; explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and vulnerability scanning as the canonical detection. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this clear guidance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and asset inventory for systems running Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor or Joomla instances with the Content Editor plugin. Flag any unpatched instances against CVE-2026-48907 patch signature. Alert priority for systems not patched by federal due date 2026-06-19.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Joomla Editor Profile Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability allows 'creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users'. Pipeline missed detection for the access-control bypass mechanism that enables exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Joomla application and HTTP access logs for POST requests to editor profile endpoints (typically /administrator/index.php?option=com_content_editor or plugin config endpoints) that lack valid authentication tokens or session IDs. Flag any profile creation responses (HTTP 200/201) from unauthenticated source IPs or user agents.

suggestion.title: Suspicious PHP File Upload to Editor Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attackers can 'upload and execution of PHP code' via created profiles. This is the execution payload; pipeline provided no detection for file-upload activity or PHP writes to plugin directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP PUT/POST requests to Joomla Content Editor plugin directories for file uploads with .php, .phtml, or double-extension payloads. Correlate with unauthenticated source IPs and timestamps following editor profile creation. Flag multipart form uploads with binary or script content to web-accessible directories.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution from Uploaded Editor Artifacts
suggestion.rationale: Article chain is complete only when uploaded code executes; pipeline failed to specify detection for process spawning or code execution following successful upload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PHP interpreter execution (php.exe, php-fpm, php-cgi) spawned from Joomla web-server processes with suspicious working directories or command-line arguments pointing to Content Editor plugin or recently-uploaded artifact directories. Correlate with prior file-upload detections in the same host/timeframe.

suggestion.title: Joomla Widget Factory Plugin Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies the vulnerable component and article body references 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' template—pipeline must generate detection for internet-facing Joomla instances running Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor plugin.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and asset management systems for Joomla installations with Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor plugin installed. Flag all instances marked internet-accessible or reachable from untrusted networks. Cross-reference against patch inventory to identify systems vulnerable to CVE-2026-48907 (unpatched versions as of federal due-date 2026-06-19).

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Editor Profile Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users'—this is the core exploitation vector and must be detectable as anomalous HTTP requests without session authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to Widget Factory profile creation endpoints (typically /components/com_joomla_contenteditor/*, /administrator/index.php?option=com_joomla_contenteditor) originating from external IPs, lacking valid Joomla session tokens (_session_id), and resulting in successful (200/201) responses. Correlate multiple profile creation attempts from same source IP.

suggestion.title: PHP File Upload to Plugin Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'upload and execution of PHP code via the creation of new editor profiles'—file write to plugin directory is the execution mechanism and generates file creation/modification signals.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file system events for PHP file creation or modification under Joomla plugin directories (/components/com_joomla_contenteditor/, /plugins/*). Correlate timing and source IP with HTTP requests to profile creation endpoints to confirm upload-from-web pattern. Alert on suspicious PHP filenames or obfuscated code patterns.

suggestion.title: Web Process Execution from Plugin Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article outcome is 'execution of PHP code'—PHP interpreter spawning processes or shell access indicates successful code execution post-upload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect web server processes (apache2, httpd, php-fpm, php-cgi) spawning unusual child processes (bash, sh, python, nc, curl). Filter parent process path or command-line arguments to Joomla plugin directories. Alert on outbound network connections initiated from these child processes.

suggestion.title: Federal Patch Deadline Compliance Check
suggestion.rationale: Article states federal agencies required to remediate by 2026-06-19—pipeline should flag missed patch deadline as operational risk separate from active exploitation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query patch management and CMDB for Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor versions. Flag all systems with unfixed versions as of the federal due-date (2026-06-19). Cross-reference with asset inventory to identify unpatched internet-facing systems as high-urgency remediation queue.

suggestion.title: Clipboard Data Access Followed by Tor Egress
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'clipboard theft' combined with 'Tor-based communications.' This is high-fidelity: clipboard read + Tor connection within seconds from same process is a crypto-clipper signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when non-wallet process reads clipboard (T1115) then initiates SOCKS5 connection or Tor client activity within 60 seconds. Filter clipboard contents for crypto wallet address patterns (0x[a-fA-F0-9]{40}, legacy addresses, etc.).

suggestion.title: Wallet Binary Substitution or Registry Hijacking
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'wallet replacement.' Implies file-system swap or registry modification of wallet application paths, config, or execution entrypoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HKCU/HKLM for wallet registry keys (MetaMask, Ledger, Trezor, etc.). Alert when legitimate wallet install paths are overwritten, or when registry points to unsigned/unexpected executables.

suggestion.title: Worm-like SMB Share Self-Propagation
suggestion.rationale: Article cites 'worm-like propagation.' Distinctive pattern: malware copies itself to \\*\*\*.exe, removable media, or synced folders, then executes across multiple hosts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creating .exe on UNC paths (\\server\share\) or removable media. Correlate process execution from those paths on adjacent hosts. Alert on self-replication patterns (same binary hash appearing across multiple share roots in <1 hour).

suggestion.title: Lightweight Backdoor Tor Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'lightweight backdoor' with 'Tor-based communications' for 'persistent access' and 'follow-on activity.' Should generate C2 beaconing alerts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify processes with persistent Tor connectivity (tor.exe child or SOCKS5 API calls). Alert on regular DNS/CONNECT to .onion domains or Tor entry-node IPs at beaconing intervals (30–300s) from unexpected processes.

suggestion.title: Autostart Persistence Mechanism for Backdoor
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'establishes persistent access' via 'lightweight backdoor.' Implies Run/RunOnce registry, scheduled tasks, or WMI subscriptions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected entries in Run/RunOnce keys or scheduled tasks created by non-system processes, especially those that later exhibit clipboard access or Tor connectivity. Cross-correlate with binary hash.

suggestion.title: Clipboard Interception During Crypto Wallet Execution
suggestion.rationale: Crypto-clipper targets clipboard specifically during wallet operations. Should alert on clipboard access by non-wallet processes while wallet is running, combined with high-entropy paste patterns (hex-encoded addresses).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor clipboard read API calls from processes not in wallet whitelist. Detect when clipboard contains wallet-address patterns and is accessed by process with network capability. Alert if clipboard write precedes legitimate wallet paste within 5 seconds.

suggestion.title: Agentic Automated Vulnerability Scanning & Remediation Chains
suggestion.rationale: Article headline and schema describe 'agentic vulnerability detection system' operating 'at AI speed'—implies continuous automated discovery, exploitation testing, and remediation execution. Phrase: 'agentic vulnerability detection system, codename MDASH'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect repeated, sequential vulnerability scanning and automated remediation attempts across Windows/Azure from single orchestration source. Look for rapid-fire discovery commands (port scans, service enumeration) followed by exploitation-like payloads and privilege escalation in parent-child process chains consistent with agentic decision loops.

suggestion.title: Azure Identity Token Abuse & Service Principal Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: MDASH 'integrating into real-world workflows across Windows, Azure, and identity systems' indicates detection for credential compromise and identity-layer attacks. Article emphasizes identity systems integration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous Azure AD token requests, service principal authentication from unusual locations/times, suspicious Graph API queries for user/group enumeration, and credential spray patterns targeting high-privilege identities. Correlate with failed MFA or impossible-travel indicators.

suggestion.title: Windows Privilege Escalation & Exploitation Post-Delivery
suggestion.rationale: MDASH 'integrating into Windows' systems and described as detecting vulnerabilities implies post-exploitation privilege escalation and defense-evasion detection. Phrase: 'integrating into real-world workflows across Windows'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect UAC bypass techniques (registry modifications, token impersonation), Scheduled Task creation by non-SYSTEM processes, unusual parent-child process relationships (explorer.exe → cmd.exe → powershell.exe with system privileges), and token elevation artifacts in ETW logs.

suggestion.title: Joomla Editor Profile Creation — Unauthenticated HTTP POST
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability allows 'creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users' — the attack vector is HTTP POST to profile creation endpoints without valid session tokens.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Joomla /administrator/ endpoints for POST requests to profile/config handlers lacking valid session or CSRF tokens. Baseline legitimate admin activity; alert on off-hours or high-frequency creation attempts.

suggestion.title: PHP File Upload and Execution via Joomla Editor
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'could allow for upload and execution of PHP code' via editor profiles — successful exploitation manifests as .php file creation in web-accessible directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on .php file writes to /media/, /images/, or /templates/ directories from unauthenticated web requests. Correlate HTTP POST requests to PHP execution events (e.g., php-cgi spawned from web server process) within 2 seconds.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48907 Vulnerability Scanner Positive
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends 'asset-exposure hunt' and explicitly lists 'CVE: CVE-2026-48907' — scanner hits indicate vulnerable Widget Factory Joomla installations reachable from attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag all CVE-2026-48907 matches in vulnerability management platform. Cross-correlate with patch logs to identify systems without applied vendor updates by federal due date 2026-06-19.

suggestion.title: HTTP Access to Joomla com_joomcontenteditor Component
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor' component — HTTP requests to this component path from untrusted sources indicate scanning or exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP GET/POST to /components/com_joomcontenteditor* or similar editor component paths from external IPs. 200 responses to unauthenticated requests signal exploitable misconfiguration.

suggestion.title: Joomla Database Record Creation Without Admin Login
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates 'creation of new editor profiles' — successful attacks leave artifacts in joomla_extensions or joomla_profiles tables without corresponding admin session log entries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-correlate Joomla admin_logs for profile creation events with web_access_logs. Alert if profile is created without a corresponding authenticated admin session or if creation originates from public IP.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Editor Profile Creation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'allow[s]... creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users.' This is the canonical entry point; detecting profile creation without valid auth tokens is the primary control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP POST/PUT to Joomla Content Editor profile endpoints (e.g., /index.php?option=com_joomla_content_editor&task=profile*) where requests lack valid session cookies or authentication headers yet return 200/201 success (not 401/403). Baseline legitimate admin profile creation to tune false positives.

suggestion.title: PHP File Upload via Editor Profile Mechanism
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'allow[s] upload... of PHP code via the creation of new editor profiles.' Detecting executable file uploads is essential to prevent execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on multipart/form-data POST requests to editor profile creation endpoints containing files with .php, .phtml, .php7, or .phar extensions. Correlate with unauthenticated profile creation events. Segment alerts by authentication context to reduce false positives from legitimate admin uploads.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48907 Vulnerability Scanning Coverage
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status requires vulnerability scanning and patch compliance verification. Confirm scanners detect CVE-2026-48907 with Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor fingerprints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Validate that vulnerability scanner includes CVE-2026-48907 detection (version fingerprinting for Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor ≤ vulnerable version). Escalate any detections to high priority; correlate patch deployment against federal due date 2026-06-19 for compliance validation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious PHP Code Execution Post-Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'upload and execution of PHP code.' Detecting execution (not just upload placement) is necessary to catch active exploitation post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to newly-created editor profile file paths within 10 minutes of detected profile creation. Flag requests with high-entropy GET parameters (command injection indicators) or unusual User-Agents. Time-series correlation between creation and execution events is key to detection confidence.

suggestion.title: Rapid Multi-Profile Creation from Single Source
suggestion.rationale: Attackers exploiting the unauthenticated vulnerability may rapidly iterate or test multiple payloads. Plural 'profiles' in the article suggests enumeration/brute-force behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert if a single source IP creates >3 editor profiles within 5 minutes, especially without authentication context. Baseline normal maintenance/admin activity to tune. Unauthenticated rapid profile creation is high-fidelity indicator of exploitation attempt.

suggestion.title: Typosquatted Go Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes github.com/botdb-go/bolt as typosquatting github.com/boltdb/bolt with malicious intent. 'The malicious Go Module Mirror's was named github.com/botdb-go/bolt, similar to the original one i.e. github.com/boltdb/bolt.' No detection for suspicious Go imports resembling popular packages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Go build processes and dependency resolution (go.mod, go.sum) for package names that are homoglyphs or near-matches to well-known modules (e.g., boltdb, gorm, etc.). Alert on first-time resolutions from untrusted module proxies or GitHub accounts that don't match the canonical maintainer. Cross-reference against Go module security databases.

suggestion.title: Go Module Proxy Cache Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Go Module Mirror's indefinite caching of modules kicked in, and that cached the backdored module' and 'The Module was cached on Go Module Proxy, which continued to serve clients.' No detection for malicious modules persisting in cached proxy mirrors despite upstream removal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Log and alert on repeated Go module proxy requests (e.g., proxy.golang.org, pkg.go.dev) for package versions flagged in Go vulnerability database or recently removed from upstream repositories. Detect when developers update go.mod to pinned versions known to be backdoored (e.g., github.com/botdb-go/bolt v1.3.1).

suggestion.title: Command and Control via Compromised Go Binary
suggestion.rationale: Article states the backdoor 'allows hackers to remotely control infected computers through a server that sends them commands i.e. via a command and control server.' No detection for C2 communications initiated by Go processes or unusual outbound network activity from build/runtime environments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound network connections from Go processes (go.exe, compiled binaries from recent builds) to non-standard ports or external domains not in allowed-list. Alert on DNS resolutions to low-reputation domains or IPs from processes pulling packages from module proxies. Correlate with recent go.mod changes.

suggestion.title: Software Supply Chain Dependency Update to Backdoored Version
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'we now wish to update our systems to the latest dependencies, which led developers to update the version that stayed in the system for 3 years.' Organizations updating BoltDB to v1.3.1 (released Nov 2021, cached in proxy until Jan 2025) should be detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect changes to go.mod/go.sum or package.json that pin or upgrade to known-backdoored versions (cross-reference against Go CVE database and Snyk alerts). Alert specifically on go get github.com/botdb-go/bolt or similar typosquatted packages in build logs. Flag any organization with go.sum entries for v1.3.1 or recent updates to that version after Jan 30, 2025 discovery date.

suggestion.title: Typosquatting Package Name Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack method: 'Typo squatting attacks happen when bad actors create and upload harmful software packages to online libraries using names very similar to popular ones.' No generic detection for new package uploads with names resembling high-value targets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package repository upload events and new package registrations (Go, NPM, PyPI, Nuget) for Levenshtein distance or character-similarity matches against top-100 packages in each ecosystem. Alert on new accounts or first-time publishers uploading near-homoglyph names. Combine with reputation scoring (new account, unusual upload cadence, zero documentation).

suggestion.title: Joomla Widget Factory Editor — Unauthenticated Profile Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could allow for upload and execution of PHP code via the creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users.' Pipeline missed detection for profile creation without valid authentication tokens.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Joomla application logs and web server access logs for POST requests to the Widget Factory Content Editor profile creation endpoint (typically components/com_*/profiles endpoint patterns) that lack valid session cookies or authentication headers. Baseline legitimate profile creation IP/user patterns and alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: PHP File Upload to Joomla Plugin Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'upload and execution of PHP code.' Pipeline missed file upload detection targeting plugin directories where executable code would be placed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on .php file uploads or creation events in Joomla plugin directories (/plugins/, /components/) following requests to Widget Factory editor endpoints, especially from unauthenticated sources. Cross-reference with web server logs for subsequent GET/POST requests to newly created .php files.

suggestion.title: Public-Facing Joomla with Widget Factory Plugin
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'publicly-facing application' exploitation and notes CISA KEV is actively exploited. Pipeline missed asset inventory detection for exposed vulnerable instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan internet-facing Joomla instances for Widget Factory Content Editor plugin presence (via fingerprinting /plugins/editors/widgetfactory or component request patterns, or version disclosure in HTTP headers). Cross-reference against patch status; flag all unpatched instances as active compromise risk given CISA KEV status.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution in Joomla Plugin Upload Paths
suggestion.rationale: Article attack chain culminates in 'execution of PHP code.' Pipeline missed behavioral detection for code actually being executed post-upload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Joomla application logs for PHP execution events in plugin/component directories where recent unauthenticated uploads occurred. On Windows, monitor W3SVC IIS logs for 200/201 responses to .php requests in plugin paths. Correlate file creation timestamps with subsequent code execution within minutes.

suggestion.title: Exploit Public-Facing Application (CVE-2026-48907)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists T1190 as applicable MITRE technique and emphasizes active exploitation. Pipeline omitted structured detection for this technique applied to the specific CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Use vulnerability scanner data (Qualys, Tenable, Rapid7) to identify systems running affected Widget Factory plugin versions. Correlate scanner results with web application firewall/proxy logs and Joomla access logs for exploit attempts to the editor component endpoints in the CVE description.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Joomla Editor Profile Creation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users' as primary attack vector. Pipeline generated zero detections for this core exploitation step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on POST requests to Joomla editor profile creation endpoints (/components/com_joomla_content_editor/*, admin endpoints) from sources with missing/invalid authentication tokens, null session indicators, or missing Authorization headers. Correlate with HTTP 200–201 responses indicating successful profile creation.

suggestion.title: PHP File Creation in Joomla Editor Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'upload and execution of PHP code' as exploitation outcome. No detection covers the execution phase or file write events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation of .php files in Joomla editor plugin/profile directories following anomalous POST requests. Baseline normal editor operations, then flag writes from unexpected source IPs, timestamps outside business hours, or without corresponding authenticated admin sessions.

suggestion.title: Access Control Bypass in Editor Profile Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article's core vulnerability is 'improper access control' enabling unauthenticated exploitation. Detection should focus on auth-bypass indicators in request logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor editor-related requests for parameter injection (user_id tampering, role escalation in profile JSON/payloads), missing CSRF tokens, or requests that bypass authentication checks yet succeed. Flag requests where auth indicators are null/invalid but HTTP response is successful.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48907 Vulnerability Exposure
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry indicates active exploitation in the wild. Article specifies federal patch deadline (2026-06-19) and vulnerability in Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scanner detections of Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor < [patched version] on internet-facing assets. Prioritize by public exposure and time-to-remediate relative to federal deadline.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48907 Asset Inventory Scan
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states CISA KEV entry with 'observed exploited in the wild' status. Federal due date 2026-06-19 creates urgency. Article states: 'Anything in CISA KEV is *currently* being exploited.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory and vulnerability scanners for Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor installations. Match against CVE-2026-48907. Prioritize all matches for immediate patching. Flag any instances with patch status 'not vulnerable' for manual verification of actual applied patches per article guidance on patch lag.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Joomla Editor Profile Creation
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: 'upload and execution of PHP code via the creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users.' This is the direct exploitation mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Joomla editor profile creation endpoints (/components/com_contenteditor/*, /administrator/* profile routes) for unauthenticated POST requests (missing PHPSESSID, invalid session tokens, no Authorization headers). Correlate with successful file uploads in the same HTTP session.

suggestion.title: PHP File Upload to Joomla Plugin Directories
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation manifests as 'upload' of PHP code. File system and web server logs will capture suspicious .php file creation in Joomla component paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on .php file creation events in /components/com_contenteditor, /plugins/*, /media/* directories. Correlate with preceding unauthenticated HTTP POST requests to profile creation endpoints. Flag uploads that lack corresponding authenticated admin activity or patch/update context.

suggestion.title: PHP Interpreter Execution in Uploaded Code Context
suggestion.rationale: After uploading PHP code, attacker must execute it. Process execution logs will show php.exe/php-cgi/php-fpm spawned from web-writable directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on PHP process execution (php.exe, php-cgi, php-fpm, apache2 mod_php) sourcing from Joomla /components or /plugins directories. Establish legitimate PHP execution baseline from content editor and flag anomalies, especially chains: unauthenticated HTTP POST → file creation → PHP execution.

suggestion.title: Editor Profile Database Modifications Without Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Profile creation is a database event: 'creation of new editor profiles.' Application logs should capture INSERT/UPDATE to profile tables without matching authentication context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Joomla application logs for editor profile save/create actions (component log or database audit logs) triggered by unauthenticated sessions. Flag INSERT/UPDATE operations on editor profile tables where the user context is null, anonymous, or does not appear in authentication logs within the same session window.

suggestion.title: Recovery Partition XML File Modification Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states exploit 'Bypasses Windows BitLocker via Recovery Partition XML Files'—the core attack mechanism is XML tampering in restricted boot/recovery areas. No use case was generated for this foundational IOA.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file creation, modification, or write events targeting recovery partition paths (\Recovery\, \EFI\, System32\Recovery\) with .xml extension. Flag if process lacks system integrity or runs from user-writable directory. Correlate with subsequent boot-time behavior changes or BitLocker state queries.

suggestion.title: GreatXML Exploit Execution and Variants
suggestion.rationale: Named exploit 'GreatXML' in title provides explicit IOC foundation; pipeline should generate process-execution detection against this exploit name and related command-line patterns. Absence indicates failure to extract named-threat indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process spawning containing 'GreatXML' identifier, XML parsing utilities targeting recovery paths (msbuild.exe, powershell.exe), or scripting engines with XML/config file arguments. Flag unsigned executables or execution from %TEMP%, Downloads, or AppData user-writable paths.

suggestion.title: BitLocker Metadata and Recovery Key Unauthorized Access
suggestion.rationale: Exploit's mechanism is BitLocker bypass via recovery partition tampering—should detect unauthorized WMI queries, registry enumeration, or file reads of BitLocker recovery credentials or configuration metadata.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for WMI namespace queries (Win32_EncryptableVolume, Win32_Volume), registry reads of HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\TPM or \Security\Encryption, or file access to %SystemRoot%\System32\Recovery\*. Escalate if requestor is non-admin or scripts are involved.

suggestion.title: Boot Configuration or EFI Boot Order Modification
suggestion.rationale: Recovery partition XML files are typically parsed at boot time; successful exploitation likely results in modifications to boot sequence, EFI variables, or BCD (Boot Configuration Data). Article title implies persistence post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect modifications to BCD registry hive, EFI boot variables, or bootloader configuration files (bootmgr, winload.efi). Flag unsigned code writes to System32\hal.dll or Drivers\. Correlate temporally with recovery partition XML writes.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation or Token Impersonation for Restricted Partition Access
suggestion.rationale: Recovery partitions are access-restricted; exploiting requires privilege escalation or kernel-level access. Article doesn't detail mechanism, but UCA should detect pre-exploitation privilege-gain attempts or BYOVD/kernel exploitation patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for CreateRemoteThread or SetWindowsHookEx to system processes, UAC bypass patterns, or parent-child process chains where low-privilege process spawns token-elevated child. Flag execution of exploitation frameworks or BYOVD candidates (vulnerable drivers, WMI class loading).

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Joomla Editor Profile Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could allow for upload and execution of PHP code via the creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users'—core attack step with no detection rule generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST/GET requests to Joomla administrator user-creation endpoints (/administrator/index.php?option=com_users) from unauthenticated sessions. Flag 200/302 responses indicating successful profile creation without prior login session.

suggestion.title: PHP File Upload to Joomla Web Root
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attack involves 'upload and execution of PHP code'—no detection for unauthenticated file uploads targeting Joomla upload directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect multipart POST requests with .php file extension or application/x-php Content-Type to web-accessible Joomla paths (media/, uploads/, images/). Flag if source IP has no prior authentication records and receives 200/201 response.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution via Uploaded Web Shell
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploitation yields 'execution of PHP code' but no behavioral detection for code execution post-upload—critical for catch-post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for apache/nginx/httpd spawning child processes (bash, curl, wget, nc) or initiating unexpected outbound connections. Correlate with PHP file modifications in web directories within preceding 4 hours.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48907 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly prescribes 'match against your vulnerability scanner' but pipeline did not generate scanner-alert correlation rule. CISA KEV deadline (2026-06-19) is operationally critical.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when vulnerability scanner reports CVE-2026-48907 on internet-exposed asset. Escalate if patched=false or verification status=unknown. Flag if asset age-of-finding exceeds 48 hours post-CISA-KEV-publish (2026-06-16).

suggestion.title: Joomla Administrator Panel Access Post-Profile-Creation
suggestion.rationale: Once editor profile is created, attacker accesses /administrator endpoint for persistence. Article describes the vulnerability vector but not the post-exploitation access patterns.

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous sign-in patterns, conditional access bypass attempts, or Oauth grant abuse in Azure tenants where MDASH operates.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Detection System Fingerprinting
suggestion.rationale: Adversaries typically fingerprint defensive systems before exploitation. Article describes a detection system codename but pipeline identified no reconnaissance use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for reconnaissance queries, system enumeration commands, or scanning activity targeting MDASH system services, API endpoints, or logging infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Apache Spark ACL Authentication Bypass (CVE-2022-33891)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'if an admin had enabled an ACL authentication filter, an attacker could bypass it and execute shell commands as the Spark service user.' This describes the core exploitation pattern. CVE explicitly added to CISA KEV catalog and exploited by ZeroBot.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unauthenticated or ACL-bypassed connections to Spark instances (port 7077 default) followed by arbitrary command execution under spark user privileges. Alert on shell spawning or Java subprocess execution from Spark service context.

suggestion.title: GitPython Command Injection via Malicious Repository URLs (CVE-2022-24439)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploitation via 'clever syntax tricks' in GitPython allowing 'arbitrary command execution.' Commonly used in CI/CD pipelines and vulnerable versions existed in many environments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor git clone/pull operations for shell metacharacters (backticks, $(), pipe, semicolon) in repository URL parameters. Flag child process spawning with suspicious commands from git/python operations in CI/CD contexts.

suggestion.title: API Authorization Bypass – Unauthenticated Metadata Access
suggestion.rationale: Article describes accessing 'hidden endpoint only accessible locally' via 'specially crafted request' to 'unsafe functionality of the app's API.' Mirrors the 2023 Azure Power Apps exposure affecting 38M records.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect API requests with path traversal, parameter injection, or metadata endpoint enumeration patterns. Alert on access to admin/internal endpoints without valid authentication tokens or from unusual source IPs.

suggestion.title: ZeroBot Malware Exploitation and Propagation Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states ZeroBot exploited CVE-2022-33891 'to exploit and propagate malware through affected systems' in December 2022 and was observed by Microsoft. Active threat actor referenced by name.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for signatures of automated Spark exploitation scanning and payload delivery typical of ZeroBot campaigns. Detect malware propagation activity originating from compromised Spark instances or outbound scanning for additional vulnerable systems.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and references template—pipeline generated nothing. CISA KEV status demands quick fleet scan for vulnerable product presence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for Joomla installations with Content Editor component active, particularly matching known-vulnerable version ranges. Prioritize internet-facing instances. Cross-reference against patch inventory to identify lag.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Editor Profile Creation POST
suggestion.rationale: Article states attack vector is 'creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users'—pipeline missed this explicit access-control bypass. Logs should show admin-endpoint access without valid session.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unauthenticated POST to Joomla editor component profile-creation endpoints (e.g., /administrator/index.php?option=com_contenteditor&...) with HTTP 200-201 response. Correlate with source IP for clustering analysis.

suggestion.title: PHP File Upload to Joomla Media/Upload Paths
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'upload and execution of PHP code'—upload is the exploitation act; pipeline generated no detection for this phase, missing the intervention point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect multipart POST requests containing .php/.phtml files to Joomla /media, /images, or component upload directories from unauthenticated sources or immediately after suspicious profile-creation attempts.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution in Joomla Upload Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article describes culmination: 'execution of PHP code.' Needs post-upload detection: HTTP GETs to recently written .php files in atypical Joomla locations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate file-write events (upload) with HTTP GET/POST to PHP files in non-vendor Joomla paths within 5-minute window. Flag requests with query parameters suggesting command execution (exec, system, shell_exec patterns).

suggestion.title: Mass Reconnaissance for Joomla Content Editor Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV catalogue implies active exploitation at scale. Should hunt for scanning activity targeting the vulnerable endpoints before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for high-volume requests to Joomla /administrator endpoints and ?option=com_contenteditor parameters from external IPs across multiple internal hosts. Expect 404s/403s as attacker probes for presence.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Joomla Content Editor Profile Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could allow...upload and execution of PHP code via the creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users.' Detection of profile creation attempts without authentication is the initial exploitation step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Joomla Content Editor logs or web server access patterns for profile creation endpoints accessed without valid session tokens or authentication headers. Flag any POST/PUT requests to editor profile creation endpoints originating from IPs without prior successful authentication.

suggestion.title: PHP File Upload via Joomla Content Editor
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'upload and execution of PHP code' through editor profiles. Detection of executable code being written to web-accessible locations is critical execution indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for .php files being written to the Content Editor's upload directories, particularly those created shortly after editor profile creation events. Correlate file write events with web requests and subsequent PHP process spawning.

suggestion.title: Suspicious PHP Process Execution Post-Editor Activity
suggestion.rationale: Once PHP is uploaded, execution occurs. Article indicates code execution capability; detect processes spawned by the PHP/Joomla application after editor compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect php.exe or php-cgi spawning child processes (shells, net commands, PowerShell) with unusual parent process chains originating from web server or Joomla process contexts, particularly within minutes of Content Editor activity.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48907 Exploitation Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV indicates active exploitation. Known-bad exploit patterns or payloads for this CVE should be matched against web traffic and application logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest threat feeds (Shodan, exploit databases) for documented exploitation patterns for CVE-2026-48907. Signature-match web requests against known profile creation payloads and PHP injection patterns targeting Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor.

suggestion.title: Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor Version Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article targets specific product: Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor. Identify installations and versions in scope for this CVE via asset discovery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset management and vulnerability scanning data for Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor installations. Cross-reference version numbers against known-vulnerable builds (those pre-patch-2026-06-19). Alert on exposed instances or those behind public-facing reverse proxies.

suggestion.title: Joomla Content Editor Profile Creation by Unauthenticated Users
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'could allow for upload and execution of PHP code via the creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users' — profile creation is the exploitation pivot and primary detection point
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Joomla Content Editor API endpoints (typically /editor/profile, /index.php?option=com_editor) for POST/PUT requests creating new profiles where Authentication header is missing or session is unauthenticated. Baseline legitimate admin profile creation; alert on anomalous frequency, source IP entropy, or field manipulation.

suggestion.title: PHP File Upload to Joomla Content Editor Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'upload and execution of PHP code' — PHP files written to web-accessible Content Editor paths represent direct web shell deployment and must be detected at write time
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation or modification of .php files within Joomla Content Editor directories (/media/editor*, /plugins/editor*, /components/com_*editor*). Correlate file-write events with HTTP POST requests to upload endpoints. High-confidence signal: PHP file execution within 60 seconds of upload from Content Editor paths.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48907 Vulnerability Scanner Detection and Remediation Tracking
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry with federal patch due 2026-06-19 — scanner detection is canonical control for active-exploitation tracking; article warns 'patch lag is the silent killer'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any scanner result matching CVE-2026-48907 across all assets. Escalate to critical if not remediated by 2026-06-19. Validate scanner false-negatives: correlate 'not vulnerable' results with known Widget Factory Joomla installations. Track time-to-remediate and flag delays exceeding patch-window SLA.

suggestion.title: Joomla Content Editor Access Control Bypass — Unauthenticated API Calls
suggestion.rationale: Article root cause is 'improper access control' — the vulnerability allows unauthenticated users to reach privileged editor functions; detection must focus on authentication boundary crossing
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Joomla Content Editor API endpoints for requests lacking valid session cookies, JWT tokens, or Itemid parameters that enforce authorization. Alert when unauthenticated requests successfully reach editor profile creation, file-upload, or module-management functions. Establish baseline of legitimate (zero) unauthenticated editor access.

suggestion.title: Joomla Web Shell Execution in Content Editor Directories Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'execution of PHP code' as the impact — post-upload web shell execution confirms compromise and enables immediate response
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to .php files in Joomla Content Editor paths for payloads invoking dangerous functions (exec, system, shell_exec, passthru, eval, base64_decode). Flag high-entropy parameter values, multi-line payloads, or requests originating from external IPs to recently-written PHP files. Correlate with parent process spawning shells or outbound network connections.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48907 Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names Joomla Content Editor as a public-facing application being exploited; 'unauthenticated users' can access the vulnerable endpoint. Standard exposure hunt is the baseline for any CISA KEV.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for internet-exposed Joomla instances running Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor. Cross-reference vulnerability scanner output against firewall/proxy logs showing inbound web traffic to Joomla admin or editor components. Prioritize instances without patch date ≥ 2026-06-19.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Joomla Editor Profile Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability allows 'creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users'—this is the direct attack step. Profile creation should trigger alerts only when source is unauthenticated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Joomla application logs for profile creation events (typically in /logs or database audit tables). Trigger alert when profile creation originates from unauthenticated session or anonymous user context. Correlate with HTTP 403→200 sequences that indicate auth bypass.

suggestion.title: PHP File Upload to Joomla Web Root
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'upload and execution of PHP code'—file write followed by execution is the exploitation mechanism. Detect the upload phase before execution occurs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Joomla directory tree (/components, /plugins, /templates, /media) for new .php files created via HTTP POST requests. Correlate file creation timestamp with HTTP request logs showing profile creation or file upload endpoints. Alert on PHP uploads outside sanctioned deployment windows.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Execution in Joomla Context
suggestion.rationale: Once PHP is uploaded, 'execution' occurs—article names this as the impact. Detect process execution or system calls originating from PHP runtime in Joomla root.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process spawning (bash, sh, cmd.exe, powershell) with parent process=php-fpm or apache2 (php handler). Correlate with recent file-creation events in Joomla web root. Alert on process execution within 60s of upload-phase file writes.

suggestion.title: Joomla POST to Admin Endpoints from Untrusted Source
suggestion.rationale: Unauthenticated profile creation implies POST to an editor/admin endpoint without valid session cookie. Detect baseline-anomalous POST traffic to admin paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP POST requests to Joomla /administrator, /index.php?option=com_*, or editor profile endpoints that lack valid authenticated session cookie or include Cookie: JSESSIONID=<empty/default>. Include requests that receive 200 after prior 403.

suggestion.title: Profile Creation Parameter Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Improper access control suggests parameter tampering or missing authorization checks on profile creation API. Detect requests with suspicious profile-creation payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for POST/GET requests containing profile creation parameters (e.g., profile_name, profile_type, editor_type, permission_level) originating from IPs/users without known admin/editor role assignment. Detect requests with privilege-escalation indicators (e.g., permission=admin, role=super).

suggestion.title: Typo-squatted Go Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names the typo-squatting attack: 'similar to the original one i.e. github.com/boltdb/bolt' vs malicious 'github.com/botdb-go/bolt'. This is the initial-access vector that must be detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor go.mod and go.sum files, as well as package manager logs, for installations of github.com/botdb-go/bolt or other transposition-based package variants (bdb vs boltdb, botdb vs boltdb). Alert on any version 1.3.1 or installation timestamps between November 2021 and January 2025.

suggestion.title: Go Module Cache Poisoning Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article describes the attack mechanism: 'Go Module Mirror's indefinite caching of modules kicked in, and that cached the backdored module' — the module 'stayed in the system for 3 years'. Cache pollution is the persistence vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect when Go module proxy caches serve module github.com/botdb-go/bolt v1.3.1 across clients. Monitor for cache hit spikes on typo-squatted package variants. Alert if a cached module version predates all current security advisories for that package family.

suggestion.title: C2 Outbound Beaconing from Go Binaries
suggestion.rationale: Article states the backdoor 'allows hackers to remotely control infected computers through a server that sends them commands i.e. via a command and control server'. C2 communication is the command-and-control phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify outbound network connections from Go applications (verified via binary metadata or container inspection) to external C2 infrastructure. Focus on connections from processes loading the compromised BoltDB v1.3.1 dependency. Flag regular periodic connections to non-standard ports or known malicious domains.

suggestion.title: Bulk Dependency Update Triggering Malicious Version Install
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'we now wish to update our systems to the latest dependencies, which led developers to update the version that stayed in the system for 3 years'. Mass updating of Go modules unknowingly pulled the malicious cached version into production.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk go.mod updates that downgrade or change package source to typo-squatted variants (e.g., adding github.com/botdb-go/bolt when previous version was github.com/boltdb/bolt). Alert on updates pulling versions older than current security baseline for supply chain packages.

suggestion.title: Package Name Similarity Masquerading Detection
suggestion.rationale: Core attack mechanism: typo-squatting relies on name confusion. Article states attacker 'hope people will mistakenly download and install these dangerous versions'. Need to detect uploads of packages with transposition-distance ≤2 from popular packages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Go Module Proxy and GitHub for new package releases with names differing from established packages by single-character transpositions, dropped characters, or homograph substitutions (bdb vs boltdb, botdb vs boltdb). Flag for manual review when levenshtein distance is ≤2 from known popular packages.

suggestion.title: Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor CVE-2026-48907 Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry indicates active exploitation. Article states 'observed exploited in the wild' yet zero asset-discovery use case generated. This is the foundational hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan asset inventory and vulnerability scanner for unpatched Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor installations. Identify CVE-2026-48907 detections on assets with public-facing web exposure, prioritize by internet-facing status.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Editor Profile Creation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users'—this is the authentication bypass vector. Completely missed by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Joomla editor profile creation endpoints for requests without valid session/authentication tokens. Detect POST requests to profile management URIs (e.g., /administrator/index.php?option=com_joomlacontenteditor) with missing or tampered Authorization headers.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Upload to Web-Accessible Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'upload and execution of PHP code' but execution phase is completely absent from kill chain. Must detect malicious file write.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on .php/.phtml file writes to Joomla web-accessible directories (components, media, plugins) correlated with unauthenticated editor profile creation in preceding minutes. Flag suspicious PHP code in uploads (system(), exec(), passthru() calls).

suggestion.title: PHP Execution via Uploaded File
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'execution of PHP code'—no execution-phase detections provided. Must detect runtime command execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for php/php-cgi child processes spawned by web server (apache2, nginx, httpd) with execution of recently-written PHP files in web-accessible paths. Alert on suspicious system commands invoked from PHP context.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Persistence in Joomla Installation
suggestion.rationale: Uploaded and executed PHP code naturally persists as a web shell. Article describes execution capability but no persistence detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for newly-created PHP files in Joomla directories with timestamps matching exploitation window. Scan content for web shell indicators (eval(), base64_decode(), $_REQUEST execution, one-liner command handlers).

suggestion.title: Failed Authentication Pattern Against Joomla Admin Panel
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires accessing editor functionality without credentials. Article emphasizes 'improper access control'—detect authentication-bypass attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track successful requests to Joomla editor endpoints without prior successful administrator login. Detect rapid, automated profile-creation requests from single IP/user-agent (behavior consistent with CVE exploitation tooling).

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Joomla Editor Profile Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'improper access control vulnerability which could allow for upload and execution of PHP code via the creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users.' This is the attack entry point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST/PUT requests to Joomla profile/editor creation endpoints (administrator/index.php, plugin manager) from unauthenticated sessions (guest user, no prior login event). Alert on successful 200/302 responses to profile creation followed by file writes in the same session.

suggestion.title: PHP File Upload to Joomla Editor Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'upload and execution of PHP code via...editor profiles.' Uploaded .php files to web-accessible directories are the execution mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect .php file creation in /components/com_*/editor/*, /plugins/editors/*, /media/editors/*, or equivalent Joomla editor paths, within 5 minutes of unauthenticated profile creation POST. Correlate source IP across HTTP access logs and file change events.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Execution in Joomla Editor Context
suggestion.rationale: Article documents active wild exploitation (CISA KEV status), so uploaded PHP code must be executed. Process-level detection is critical.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for php.exe or php-cgi process spawned by web server user (www-data, apache, iis apppool) with parent/CWD referencing plugins or editors. Monitor Joomla application logs for unexpected extension activation or task execution from editor components.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48907 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly prescribes: 'CVE-2026-48907 — match against your vulnerability scanner.' Pipeline must generate scanner-driven detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag all Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor instances with versions in CVE-2026-48907 affected range. Prioritize internet-facing assets (public IP, no WAF). Cross-reference scanner match timestamp with netflow/Zeek for successful inbound remote connections.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Admin/Editor Feature Access Without Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability mechanism: 'improper access control' allows unauthenticated users to access admin/profile creation features. Authorization bypass detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Joomla logs for admin task execution (task=save, action=create, component operations) from guest/anonymous users. HTTP proxy should show direct /administrator/ access with zero prior successful authentication from that IP in the session window.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Joomla Editor Profile Creation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability allows 'creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users' — this is the primary access control bypass vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Joomla access logs for POST/PUT requests to editor profile endpoints (e.g., component=com_editors, task=profile operations) arriving without valid session tokens or authentication headers. Alert on profile creation attempts originating from external IP ranges or non-administrative user contexts.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Upload to Joomla Web Root
suggestion.rationale: Attack explicitly includes 'upload and execution of PHP code via the creation of new editor profiles' — file upload to web-accessible directories is the execution mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web application logs for multipart file uploads to Joomla plugin/editor directories (e.g., /plugins, /components/com_editors/). Alert on .php, .phtml files written to web root with timestamps outside maintenance windows. Track file size anomalies in profile uploads (large binaries in profile data).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48907 Widget Factory Component Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry with federal due date 2026-06-19; vulnerability scanning is baseline detection for known-exploited vulnerabilities regardless of patch claims, due to industry patch lag.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor presence and version matching CVE-2026-48907 signature. Cross-reference asset inventory to flag public-facing Joomla instances. Generate high-priority alerts for unpatched instances with internet-routable IPs; escalate based on federal timeline.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Unauthenticated Requests to Joomla Administrator Functions
suggestion.rationale: Improper access control means attackers bypass authentication; monitor for abnormal request patterns to normally-restricted endpoints as described in 'unauthenticated' profile creation capability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline HTTP request patterns to /administrator, editor profile endpoints, and component configuration pages — establish threshold for authenticated-only traffic. Alert on sustained requests from external/untrusted sources lacking authentication context. Correlate with failed login logs and IP reputation data.

suggestion.title: Recovery Partition XML File Access and Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'Recovery Partition XML Files' as attack surface: 'Bypasses Windows BitLocker via Recovery Partition XML Files'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file-system access to Windows recovery/EFI partitions (\Recovery, \EFI, \BOOT, \BIOS) by non-system processes, or CREATE/MODIFY operations on .xml files within those paths. Alert on process elevation followed by XML file access in recovery contexts, or on attempts to mount recovery partitions via diskpart, SetupAPI, or direct partition access.

suggestion.title: BitLocker Metadata Enumeration and Key Extraction
suggestion.rationale: Core attack: 'Bypasses Windows BitLocker'. Recovery partition XML files store BitLocker metadata and key material. Article: 'GreatXML Exploit Bypasses Windows BitLocker'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process calls to manage-bde.exe, WMI BitLocker methods (win32_encryptablevolume), or direct reads of BitLocker configuration registry hives (HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\BitLocker). Flag recovery key export or enumeration attempts, or access to recovery XML files by processes not signed by Microsoft.

suggestion.title: Privileged XML Processing in Pre-OS/Recovery Context
suggestion.rationale: Threat name 'GreatXML' and attack chain require XML parsing during recovery/pre-OS execution with elevated privilege. Article: 'GreatXML Exploit ... XML Files'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execution of XML parsers (powershell.exe, cscript.exe, mshta.exe, msxml3-6 library loads) with SYSTEM or TrustedInstaller privileges when processing files from recovery partitions or boot-time execution contexts. Flag unusual XML parser invocations from System32 that read recovery-related paths.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Recovery Partition Mount and Direct Access
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires access to recovery partition normally sealed from user-mode code. 'Recovery Partition XML Files' implies partition enumeration, mounting, or direct access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on non-OS processes invoking volume/partition APIs (SetupAPI, VDS/VSS, diskpart.exe, ioctl calls), attempting to enumerate or mount recovery partitions, or accessing raw partition tables. Flag processes acquiring SeSystemtimePrivilege or SeLoadDriverPrivilege that interact with recovery partition paths.

suggestion.title: XML External Entity (XXE) Attack on BitLocker Configuration
suggestion.rationale: Recovery partition XML files likely encode BitLocker configuration, key material, or encryption metadata. XXE or XML bomb exploitation is congruent with 'GreatXML' naming.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for XML parsing exceptions or resource exhaustion (billion laughs attacks, entity expansion loops) when XML parsers consume files from recovery/boot partitions. Alert on external entity (DOCTYPE/ENTITY) declarations in XML files recovered from recovery partitions, or on parser errors indicative of XXE attempts.

suggestion.title: Widget Factory Joomla Editor — Unauthenticated Profile Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'allow[s] upload and execution of PHP code via the creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users.' This is the exploitation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to Joomla editor profile creation endpoints (e.g., /administrator/index.php?option=com_contenteditor) from unauthenticated sessions or sessions lacking admin privileges. Baseline: legitimate profile creation should be rare or nonexistent in typical environments.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Upload via Joomla Editor Profiles
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'upload and execution of PHP code.' This is the payload delivery and T1505.004 (Web Shell) execution mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for multipart/form-data HTTP requests with .php, .phtml, or executable extensions being written to web-accessible directories via the editor profile creation endpoint. Flag unexpected executable file uploads to /media, /images, or web root followed by HTTP requests to execute the uploaded file.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48907 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV requires federal remediation by 2026-06-19 (same-day deadline). Scanner detection is primary IOC for asset prioritization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any CVE-2026-48907 match in vulnerability scanner results for Joomla instances, especially those with internet-facing administrative interfaces. Prioritize for emergency patching ahead of 2026-06-19 deadline.

suggestion.title: Widget Factory Plugin Presence on Joomla Instances
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires the vulnerable plugin to be installed. Asset discovery of affected software is prerequisite for hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Joomla installations running Widget Factory Content Editor via plugin manifest enumeration (HTTP GET to plugin paths, plugin XML responses, HTTP headers). Flag unpatched versions in asset inventory for immediate remediation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious PHP Execution Post-Upload to Joomla
suggestion.rationale: After PHP file is uploaded via unauthenticated editor profile creation, attacker executes it. Correlation between upload and execution signals exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP POST requests to editor profile endpoints with subsequent HTTP requests to newly-created PHP files. Look for .php files in web root with recent creation timestamps matching upload requests, then accessed via HTTP GET/POST within seconds. This signals web shell execution.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes vulnerability affects 'public-facing application' and CISA KEV only lists actively exploited flaws. Standard first-line hunt for exposed Joomla + Content Editor installations. Article: 'public-facing application'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Joomla installations with Content Editor plugin active. Use asset discovery scanners (e.g., Shodan, Censys) for 'Joomla' + 'Content Editor' headers, HTTP fingerprints, or plugin signatures. Correlate with internal vulnerability scanner CVE-2026-48907 findings. Prioritize publicly routable assets.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Unauthenticated Editor Profile Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability allows 'creation of new editor profiles for unauthenticated users' — this is the attack entry point. Detection should flag profile creation from non-authenticated sessions before successful login.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST requests to Joomla editor profile creation endpoints (typically /administrator/index.php or /component/contenteditor/profiles). Alert when requests originate from unauthenticated sessions (no valid session token, IP not in whitelist, user-agent anomalies). High FP risk from legitimate admin use — baseline typical profile creation patterns first.

suggestion.title: PHP File Upload via Joomla Editor Profile
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'upload and execution of PHP code via the creation of new editor profiles.' Detection must capture the actual payload delivery (PHP file upload) separate from profile creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file write events to Joomla Content Editor upload directories for .php extensions. Cross-correlate with process execution of PHP interpreter (php-cgi, php-fpm) immediately after upload. Baseline expected PHP uploads from admin users; flag all others. Watch for polyglot uploads (.php.jpg) as bypass.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48907 Exploitation Pattern — Joomla Content Editor
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV catalog entry requires active threat hunting for this specific CVE. Article: 'Federal civilian agencies are required to remediate by the published due date.' Standard practice is cross-fleet scanner correlation + intrusion attempt detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag all hosts in vulnerability scanner output with CVE-2026-48907 present. Cross-correlate with patch management system to identify unpatched instances. Secondary: hunt logs for exploitation signatures (malformed profile creation requests, PHP error logs from editor component, unexpected PHP execution from web-accessible paths).

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution via Joomla Editor — Post-Exploit Behavior
suggestion.rationale: Article describes successful exploitation results in 'execution of PHP code' on server. Post-exploitation detection must cover attacker activity post-upload (webshell runtime, reverse shell, data exfil).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PHP process spawning unexpected child processes (bash, cmd.exe, powershell) immediately after Content Editor uploads. Alert on outbound network connections from php-cgi/php-fpm to non-whitelisted external IPs. Look for PHP sessions with abnormally long runtimes or memory allocation anomalies in application logs.

suggestion.title: Scanner/WAF Detection: CVE-2026-48907 Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation flow can be detected at ingress before profile creation succeeds. Article: 'improper access control' is the vulnerability class — WAF rules should detect unauthenticated attempts to access restricted endpoints.
